problem: Existing tokenizers face performance trade-off between understanding and generation due to conflict between semantic abstraction and pixel reconstruction.
approach: UniFlow adapts visual encoders via layer-wise adaptive self-distillation and uses lightweight patch-wise pixel flow decoder for semantic-conditioned reconstruction.
contribution: 7B UniFlow-XL surpasses 14B TokenFlow-XL by 6.05% on understanding benchmarks while achieving competitive visual reconstruction and generation.

problem: MLLMs struggle with high-level physics reasoning, particularly understanding dynamics of continuum objects despite improvements in image and video understanding.
approach: Introduces Scene Dynamic Field (SDF) leveraging physics simulators within multi-task fine-tuning framework to improve intuitive physics understanding on NFS and TCV tasks.
contribution: Achieves up to 20.7% gains on fluid tasks with strong generalization to unseen physical domains, addressing critical gap in physics grounding.

problem: Open world segmentation requires precise segmentation and semantic understanding of infinitely open object categories where foundation models like SAM show weak semantic understanding.
approach: WOW-Seg introduces Mask2Token visual prompt module aligning masks with VLLM features and Cascade Attention Mask to decouple information across instances.
contribution: On 7,662-class Region Recognition Dataset achieves 89.7 semantic similarity and 82.4 semantic IoU with one-eighth parameter count of previous SOTA.

problem: Fluorescence microscopy imaging requires scanning through cell volumes while minimizing phototoxicity, resulting in sparse anisotropic volumes with high noise.
approach: Reformulates FM tensor completion as mathematically equivalent score-based generative model with structural consistency priors to guide toward denoised reconstructions.
contribution: Demonstrates state-of-the-art on SR-CACO-2 and four real in vivo cellular datasets with substantial improvements in signal-to-noise ratio and structural fidelity.

problem: Federated bilevel optimization is susceptible to Byzantine failures but existing resilient approaches are restricted to single-level or use inefficient sub-loop updates.
approach: BR-FedBi operates in single-loop with auxiliary variable for efficient hypergradient estimation, extended with momentum and probabilistic gradient estimator (PAGE).
contribution: Achieves optimal Byzantine resilience and optimal sample complexity with single-loop efficiency.

problem: Layer-wise pruning of LLMs depends on static heuristics and fails to account for layer interdependencies, limiting effectiveness.
approach: Formulates layer pruning as cooperative game where layers are players; uses lightweight surrogate network to estimate Shapley values and identify critical layers.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent superiority in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, achieving more efficient and effective layer-wise pruning.

problem: Efficient 3D mesh compression requires effective representation of mesh data; existing methods often exhibit suboptimal compression due to inefficient representations.
approach: Proposes Sparse Implicit Representation (SIR) recording signed distance field values only near surface on regular grids, with lightweight Sparse Neural Compression network.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art mesh and point cloud compression approaches in both performance and computational efficiency.

problem: Quantization-aware training for reasoning LLMs degrades reasoning capability because complex knowledge structures introduced during post-training are affected by quantization.
approach: Two-stage QAT pipeline: first quantizes with mixed-domain calibration to preserve capabilities, then fine-tunes quantized model with teacher-guided reward-rectification loss.
contribution: 2-bit Qwen3-8B outperforms PTQ baselines by 50.45% on average; achieves 2% higher reasoning accuracy than BitNet-2B4T using only 40K sequences.

problem: Comparing dynamical systems estimated from trajectory data lacks a principled metric accounting for sampling frequency invariance and spectral geometry.
approach: Represents each system as distribution of joint operator eigenvalues and spectral projectors, defines metric via optimal transport (Spectral-Grassmann Wasserstein).
contribution: Metric is invariant to sampling frequency, computationally efficient with convergence guarantees, enables Fréchet means for system interpolation.

problem: Standard transformer design is assumed optimal but may be suboptimal for specific datasets; understanding task-specific inductive biases is unclear.
approach: Optimizes transformer architecture for given datasets by learning most important non-linearities (GeLU, softmax) on held-out data, evaluates compatibility across tasks.
contribution: Identifies task-specific architectures with dramatic improvements in learning speed and generalization; standard transformers rarely local optima but task-specific designs sacrifice universality.

problem: Decentralized nonconvex stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise lacks theoretical guarantees, particularly for realistic gradient noise in attention models.
approach: GT-NSGDm combines gradient tracking, normalization, and momentum to handle heavy-tailed noise on distributed nodes, guaranteeing optimal convergence rate.
contribution: Achieves first optimal non-asymptotic rate O(1/T^{(p-1)/(3p-2)}) matching centralized lower bound; demonstrates topology-independent speedup.

problem: Model editing via task arithmetic enables parameter updates but fairness impacts remain unexplored despite growing concern over biased outcomes in high-stakes applications.
approach: Systematically studies group fairness in task arithmetic comparing against full fine-tuning and LoRA, provides theoretical bound linking task vector scaling to fairness.
contribution: Establishes task arithmetic as fairness-aware alternative with tunable subgroup-specific task vectors achieving competitive accuracy while reducing disparities.

problem: Large vision-language models expand KV cache creating memory bottleneck; existing compression methods focus on importance but overlook modality-specific semantic redundancy.
approach: MixKV mixes importance with diversity for compression, adapting to head-wise semantic redundancy and selectively balancing diversity and importance when compressing.
contribution: Consistently enhances existing methods across LVLMs with 5.1% average improvement under extreme compression and 8.0-9.0% gains on GUI grounding tasks.

problem: Standard GPT architecture is not provably optimal; energy-based models offer alternative paradigm viewing inference as exploration of energy landscape.
approach: NRGPT modifies GPT to unify with EBM framework by conceptualizing inference as token exploration on energy landscape, proving this becomes gradient descent under conditions.
contribution: Performs well on Shakespeare, ListOPS, and OpenWebText; exhibits potential robustness to overfitting during extended training.

problem: Autoregressive image generation models produce errors in early predictions that accumulate through the sequence, limiting final image quality.
approach: TensorAR shifts from predicting discrete tokens to predicting overlapping tensor windows, enabling refinement of earlier outputs while preserving autoregressive causality. It uses a discrete tensor noising mechanism inspired by diffusion to prevent information leakage.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent gains in generation quality and instruction-following ability with superior balance between quality and latency in both class-to-image and text-to-image tasks.

problem: Reconstructing a floorplan from movement trajectories is ill-posed since many layouts can explain the same trajectories, and path planning is non-invertible and non-differentiable.
approach: CoGuide uses a diffusion-based posterior sampler with a contrastive embedding space to reformulate the likelihood score in a smoother space, enabling stable optimization during denoising.
contribution: Produces more consistent floorplans from trajectories and is more robust than differentiable-planner baselines and guided-diffusion methods.

problem: Q-learning for risk-sensitive objectives under the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) criterion lacks sample efficiency and proper theoretical foundations.
approach: The algorithm uses a novel predictive tail value function formulation that admits a recursive Bellman structure, enabling efficient use of entire sample trajectories rather than only worst-case outcomes.
contribution: Improves CVaR performance while maintaining stable and interpretable learning dynamics, with consistency proofs via Bellman optimality equation.

problem: When deep ReLU networks are initialized with small weights, gradient descent escapes a saddle point at the origin, but the escape dynamics and structure are poorly understood.
approach: The paper analyzes escape directions and their properties, discovering that deeper layers exhibit a low-rank bias where the first singular value is at least ℓ^(1/4) larger than others.
contribution: Reveals that deep ReLU networks exhibit saddle-to-saddle dynamics with GD visiting a sequence of saddles with increasing bottleneck rank.

problem: Existing counterfactual explanation methods inherit ambiguity in distance metrics and rely on flat geometries, leading to off-manifold artifacts and adversarial collapse.
approach: PCG traces geodesics under a perceptually Riemannian metric induced from robust vision features, ensuring smooth on-manifold transitions aligned with human perception.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on three vision datasets and reveals failure modes hidden under standard metrics.

problem: RAG systems introduce privacy vulnerabilities because existing attacks fail to accurately isolate knowledge base content within mixed responses across heterogeneous domains.
approach: A black-box attack exploits knowledge asymmetry by decomposing queries to maximize information divergence, using semantic relationship scoring and a neural classifier to identify private segments.
contribution: Achieves over 90% extraction accuracy in single-domain and 80% in multi-domain settings, outperforming baselines by over 30%.

problem: Current protein models either capture sequence semantics without structural grounding or rely on MSAs which fail in alignment-sparse regimes.
approach: FlexProtein jointly learns from sequences and 3D structures using masked language modeling and diffusion-based denoising without requiring MSAs.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art on 12 tasks with particularly strong gains in mutation-rich settings where MSA-based methods struggle.

problem: Prompt-based continual learning either uses task-specific prompts (computational overhead, linear memory scaling) or shared prompts (knowledge interference).
approach: SMoPE organizes a shared prompt into prompt experts within a sparse MoE architecture with prompt-attention score aggregation for dynamic activation and adaptive noise for balanced expert utilization.
contribution: Outperforms task-specific prompt methods while achieving efficiency comparable to single-prompt approaches across multiple CL benchmarks.

problem: Prediction with expert advice under local differential privacy (LDP) constraints lacks effective methods that balance privacy and utility.
approach: RW-AdaBatch and RW-Meta leverage limited-switching behavior induced by LDP to provide privacy amplification that grows stronger on easier data, plus a general method for privately selecting non-trivial learning algorithm experts.
contribution: Outperforms classical baselines and state-of-the-art central DP algorithms by 1.5-3x on COVID-19 hospital prediction tasks.

problem: Bridge diffusion models for image restoration rely on predefined trajectories that limit both sampling efficiency and quality.
approach: CGB constructs a lower-action geodesic trajectory with entropy-regularized mixing of degraded image and noise, using a pretrained denoiser as guidance and learning a single-step consistency mapping.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art across image restoration tasks with high-quality recovery using single or fewer sampling steps.

problem: Offline multi-agent imitation learning lacks characterizations of distance to Nash equilibrium, and even exact measure matching can fail.
approach: The paper proves impossibility and hardness results, then shows how strategic dominance assumptions enable Nash imitation guarantees via best-response continuity.
contribution: Provides Nash imitation gap of O(nε_BC/(1-γ)^2) for dominant strategy expert equilibria under BC error ε_BC.

problem: Neural network training complexity is understudied in quantized settings despite quantization's practical benefits for speed and energy efficiency.
approach: Initiates complexity-theoretic study of ReLU network training under full quantization with fixed-parameter tractable cases parameterized by input dimensionality, width, output dimensionality or error bound.
contribution: Establishes strong lower bounds showing hardness in binary and restrictive settings, while identifying tractable cases via input dimensionality combined with width and output parameters.

problem: Test-time verification for LLMs involves interactions between generator coverage, verifier region of convergence, and sampling algorithm sub-optimality that lack unified characterization.
approach: Frames verifiable test-time scaling as a transport problem identifying three regimes: transport, policy improvement, and saturation, analyzing both sequential and batched sampling algorithms.
contribution: Empirically validates theoretical findings on Qwen, Llama, and Gemma models, uncovering trade-offs between coverage and sub-optimality.

problem: Understanding how frozen-weight transformers can emulate algorithms via in-context prompting lacks formal characterization.
approach: Proves that minimal transformers with frozen weights emulate algorithms by encoding algorithm parameters into token representations creating sharp dot-product gaps that force softmax attention.
contribution: Demonstrates universality: a single fixed-weight two-layer softmax attention module emulates all algorithms from task-specific class via prompt alone, with no parameter updates.

problem: Existing GPS trajectory generation is limited to small urban areas, lacks transportation-mode diversity, and requires numerous sampling steps for diffusion-based approaches.
approach: TrajFlow uses flow-matching with a trajectory harmonization & reconstruction strategy to improve robustness across geospatial scales while maintaining scalability and diversity.
contribution: Consistently outperforms diffusion and deep generative baselines at urban, metropolitan, and nationwide levels on a nationwide Japanese mobile phone dataset.

problem: Pixel-space diffusion requires complex cascade pipelines and high token complexity due to VAE compressed latent training paradigms.
approach: PixNerd models pixel-space diffusion using large-patch diffusion transformers with neural field decoding, creating a streamlined single-stage end-to-end solution.
contribution: Achieves 1.93 FID on ImageNet 256x256 with 8x lower latency and competitive scores on GenEval and DPG benchmarks for text-to-image.

problem: Safe reinforcement learning faces a safety paradox where improving policy safety reduces constraint-violating samples, impairing feasibility estimation.
approach: FDPI employs an additional policy that strategically maximizes constraint violations while staying close to the original policy, combining samples with importance sampling correction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Safety-Gymnasium with lowest violation and competitive-to-best return simultaneously.

problem: Detecting AI risks and alignment-faking behaviors becomes harder as models scale, yet existing detection attempts lack early warning systems based on value detection.
approach: LitmusValues evaluates AI value prioritization via AIRiskDilemmas that pit values against one another in scenarios relevant to AI safety, revealing self-consistent value priorities.
contribution: Shows that values including Care predict both seen risky behaviors in AIRiskDilemmas and unseen behaviors in HarmBench.

problem: Generating physically stable and novel metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for inverse design requires exploring vast chemical and structural spaces without mode collapse.
approach: PRO-MOF uses a hierarchical RL framework with high-level block selection and low-level 3D assembly policies, optimized via high-fidelity physical rewards from a universal atomistic model.
contribution: Outperforms diffusion-based and genetic algorithm baselines on multiple inverse design tasks including CO2 capacity and pore diameter targeting.

problem: MLLM-based GUI agents lack robustness for complex long-horizon tasks in dynamic environments despite proficiency in short-term tasks.
approach: LongHorizonUI introduces a Multimodal Enhanced Perceiver for state representation, Deep Reflection Decider for multi-level feedback validation, and Compensatory Action Executor with rollback strategy.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements on LongGUIBench (tasks >15 steps) while retaining competitive performance on diverse public benchmarks.

problem: Verifying whether sequence models trained on samples capture the true world model structure remains largely unexplored despite theoretical soundness guarantees.
approach: Proposes adversarial sequence generation for chess to verify soundness by forcing invalid next-move predictions, analyzing failure modes across different training recipes.
contribution: Finds no model is sound but identifies training techniques and dataset choices that remarkably improve soundness, and demonstrates board state probes benefit both training and attacks.

problem: Complex vehicle routing problems demand substantial expert effort for intent interpretation, algorithm design, and external intervention throughout execution.
approach: AFL decomposes the VRP pipeline into three manageable subtasks with four specialized LLM agents whose coordinated interactions enforce consistency and logical soundness.
contribution: Achieves comparable performance to meticulously designed algorithms on 20 complex VRPs with code reliability and solution feasibility close to 100%.

problem: Constraint-based causal discovery for partially observed systems faces challenges with multiple testing and error propagation despite recent advances.
approach: LGES is a score-based greedy search method for structure identification with latent variables, establishing global consistency guarantees via Generalized N Factor Model.
contribution: Enables identification of structure including latent variables up to Markov equivalence class with well-defined operators for efficient graph space search.

problem: Existing LLM benchmarks for network applications risk contamination from static design, show high variance from limited datasets, and fail to reflect production complexity.
approach: NetArena provides dynamic benchmark generation with abstraction generalizing across applications, runtime integration with network emulators for execution-time feedback.
contribution: Improves statistical reliability with confidence interval overlap reduced from 85% to 0, reveals agents achieve only 13-38% average performance on realistic large-scale queries.

problem: Fine-tuning large vision and language models under differentially private federated learning faces privacy-utility trade-offs, especially with LoRA methods.
approach: LA-LoRA decouples gradient interactions by alternating low-rank matrix updates and aligns update directions across clients to enhance robustness under privacy constraints.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on Swin Transformer and RoBERTa models with 16.83% improvement over RoLoRA on Swin-B under strict privacy budget.

problem: Visualization-of-thought multimodal reasoning accumulates lengthy and redundant tokens, increasing computation and memory costs substantially.
approach: DARE adaptively prunes multimodal tokens across depths, reasoning hops, and modalities via intra- and inter-hop-aware retention and asymmetric compression by modality-specific redundancy.
contribution: Achieves 40.37% FLOPs reduction and 46.07% KV-cache reduction while preserving or improving performance across seven spatial reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Controlling linear dynamical systems under adversarial disturbances requires efficient algorithms that scale with the stability margin.
approach: Proposes a novel convex relaxation using spectral filters constructed from eigenvectors of a Hankel matrix to approximate linear control policies.
contribution: Achieves runtime scaling polylogarithmically with inverse stability margin, improving upon prior polynomial dependence while maintaining regret guarantees.

problem: LLMs suffer from unexpected code-switching (language mixing) which degrades readability and usability of multilingual responses.
approach: SASFT uses sparse autoencoders to identify code-switching mechanisms and fine-tunes to maintain appropriate pre-activation values of specific language features.
contribution: Reduces unexpected code-switching by over 50% with complete elimination in four cases, while maintaining or improving performance on six multilingual benchmarks.

problem: Injecting camera parameters into transformers for implicit rendering lacks a way to generalize across diverse sensing conditions and modalities.
approach: RoRE embeds image patches as rays using learning-based rotary positional embeddings, providing unified representation robust to unconventional camera geometries and modalities.
contribution: Demonstrates improved generalization on perspective, fisheye, and RGB-thermal setups with single network flexibly integrating arbitrary cameras and modalities.

problem: Binning functions for event-based vision are discontinuous, truncating gradients at frame level and forcing reliance on frame-based features alone.
approach: Uses functional backpropagation to synthesize weak derivatives during backpropagation via integration by parts, reconstructing cotangent functions from sampled vectors.
contribution: Improves egomotion with 3.2% lower RMS error, achieves 9.4% lower EPE in optical flow and 5.1% lower error in SLAM.

problem: 3D anime character generation requires handling exaggerated proportions, stylized details, and artistically consistent garments with animation-ready skeleton and expression control.
approach: Extends Anime-SMPL with unified skeleton generation and blendshape facial control, introduces body-aligned component-wise garment generation pipeline.
contribution: Generates high-quality animation-ready 3D characters with expressive faces, bodies, and detailed textures across garments, skin, and faces.

problem: Point cloud generation typically treats shape as holistic or only supports part composition without enforcing symmetry and part priors throughout generation.
approach: Quartet of Diffusions leverages four coordinated diffusion models for global latents, symmetries, semantic parts, and spatial assembly with central global latent reinforcing coherence.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance as the first 3D point cloud framework fully integrating and enforcing both symmetry and part priors throughout generation.

problem: Conventional flow matching and diffusion policies require visual conditioning during iterative denoising, incurring substantial time and memory overhead.
approach: VITA bridges visual representations to latent actions via noise-free flow matching with an action autoencoder aligned to visual latents and flow latent decoding.
contribution: Achieves 1.5x-2x faster inference while outperforming or matching SOTA on 9 simulation and 5 real-world robotic tasks.

problem: Featurizing odorants for robust olfactory prediction is difficult due to complex activation patterns and lack of universally accepted feature design.
approach: LORAX uses LoRA fine-tuning of chemical foundation models with cross-attention to create olfaction-specific representations aligned with olfactory neural representation.
contribution: Outperforms existing models on predictive tasks by identifying information overlap between foundation models and hand-designed features, demonstrating necessity of fine-tuning.

problem: Post-training LLMs with RL often improves performance while reducing output diversity, leading to narrow and canonical responses.
approach: DQO uses determinantal point processes to jointly optimize for quality and semantic diversity by measuring diversity as the volume spanned by response embeddings.
contribution: Substantially improves semantic diversity without sacrificing quality across instruction-following, summarization, story generation, and reasoning tasks.

problem: Existing knowledge editing methods target dense architectures, limiting applicability to sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs which introduce routing distribution shifts.
approach: MoEEdit reparameterizes expert updates through per-expert null-space projections to keep router inputs invariant, solving block-structured optimization with efficient BCD solver.
contribution: Achieves SOTA efficacy and generalization with high specificity, routing stability, and superior computational and memory efficiency.

problem: Understanding the computational and reasoning capabilities of masked diffusion models relative to autoregressive models remains largely unexplored.
approach: Connects masked diffusion models to chain-of-thought and padded looped transformers, proving equivalence to polynomially-padded PLTs in finite-precision setting.
contribution: Shows MDMs can solve all problems CoT-augmented transformers can, with inherent efficiency advantages for certain classes like regular languages.

problem: ML-based combinatorial optimization solvers rely on small-scale synthetic benchmarks that fail to capture real-world structure and extreme scale.
approach: FrontierCO spans eight CO problems with instances from competitions and public repositories, providing easy and hard sets alongside standardized training resources.
contribution: Evaluates 16 ML solvers against classical solvers, finding persistent performance gaps that widen under structural challenges and large scales like TSP up to 10M nodes.

problem: Identifiability of sparse linear ODEs from data is poorly characterized despite its practical relevance and contrast with the dense case.
approach: Characterizes identifiability of sparse linear ODEs, showing unidentifiability occurs with positive probability in practically relevant sparsity regimes.
contribution: Provides lower bounds for unidentifiability probability and empirically corroborates theoretical unidentifiability persists in practice despite inductive biases.

problem: Existing medical vision benchmarks lack expert curation and realistic clinical diagnostic workflows, failing to reflect stepwise recognition and reasoning processes.
approach: MedLesionVQA constructs a benchmark from 10k+ real patient visits with expert verification, 12K volunteer images, and 19K expert-verified QA pairs with fine-grained annotations.
contribution: Exposes persistent gap with best MLLM at 56.2% versus primary physicians at 61.4% and specialists at 73.2%, underscoring need for trustworthy medical AI.

problem: Spatio-temporal point process models struggle to capture complex nonlinear dependencies between events in space and time when using traditional kernel-based methods or methods that process space and time independently.
approach: TEN-DM combines spatio-temporal graph construction with multimodal topological feature learning and temporal query techniques to effectively model periodic patterns and spatio-temporal dependencies together.
contribution: TEN-DM demonstrates improved effectiveness on multiple STPP datasets compared to state-of-the-art methods by jointly modeling spatio-temporal dependencies.

problem: Machine unlearning requires removing specific information from trained models while maintaining performance on retained data, but unlearning signals can interfere with learning signals in complex ways.
approach: Sharp MinMax splits the model into two branches: one uses sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) to learn retain signals, and the other uses sharpness maximization to unlearn forget signals, achieving better signal separation.
contribution: Sharp MinMax achieves better unlearning performance with decreased feature entanglement, stronger resistance to membership inference attacks, and flatter loss landscapes compared to baseline methods.

problem: Distribution shift in biomedical applications across different subjects, institutions, and recording devices degrades model performance, and existing normalization layers ignore temporal dependencies in signal data.
approach: PSDNorm leverages Monge mapping and temporal context to normalize feature maps while preserving auto-correlation in time-series signals, trained on 10K subjects across 10 datasets.
contribution: PSDNorm achieves state-of-the-art performance on unseen datasets while being 4-times more data-efficient than BatchNorm on sleep staging tasks.

problem: Using approximate AI4S models as simulators for RL introduces modeling errors that degrade policy quality, and the computational costs needed for safe RL are unclear.
approach: An ε-N framework quantifies the minimal computational cost N*(ε) required for an AI4S model to ensure unbiased value function estimation in tabular RL, connecting surrogate accuracy, grid resolution, and policy quality through spectral theory and Sobolev estimates.
contribution: The framework reveals that different systems (ODE vs PDE environments) require different allocations of computational effort between simulation and RL optimization for cost-efficient, scalable AI4S-RL systems with provable guarantees.

problem: LLM unlearning effectiveness depends on how knowledge is encoded during training, but prior work assumes fixed training and models, missing opportunities to improve unlearning by modifying encoding strategies.
approach: Two empirical studies examine how paraphrased descriptions and chunking of multiple facts into single training texts influence unlearning performance.
contribution: Learning-time encoding choices significantly impact unlearning effectiveness, providing practical strategies for improving LLM unlearning through encoding-aware design.

problem: RL research needs scalable, diverse environments that are computationally tractable, but traditional CPU-bound video game emulators like Atari are expensive and poorly suited for large-scale GPU-based experimentation.
approach: Octax implements classic arcade games (CHIP-8 based) entirely in JAX, creating GPU-native environments with orders-of-magnitude speedups and modular design for easy extension via LLMs.
contribution: Octax enables massive-scale RL training on GPUs while demonstrating significant improvements in training speed and scalability compared to CPU emulators like traditional Atari.

problem: Standard k-means clustering is computationally expensive on large datasets, and existing acceleration techniques often introduce hyperparameters that complicate tuning.
approach: Angle k-means leverages angular relationships between data points and cluster centers to reduce computation while maintaining compatibility with standard k-means through no new hyperparameters.
contribution: Angle k-means achieves significant speedup over ball k-means and Exp-ns while maintaining linear time complexity in sample size and dimensionality.

problem: Submodular function minimization typically requires exact function value queries, but in practice only noisy pairwise comparisons may be available through dueling oracles.
approach: An algorithm uses a dueling oracle with responses governed by a transfer function to minimize submodular functions, with analysis for both linear and sigmoid transfer functions.
contribution: For linear transfer functions, achieves O(n^(3/2)/√T) error rate with matching lower bounds for constrained algorithms; for sigmoid transfer functions achieves O(n^(7/5)/T^(2/5)) error rate.

problem: Universal dexterous grasping requires learning policies for diverse objects and hand poses, but existing RL approaches need complex reward design and curriculum learning, leading to suboptimal solutions.
approach: DemoGrasp starts from a single successful grasping demonstration and formulates trajectory editing as a single-step MDP, where wrist pose edits determine where to grasp and hand joint angles determine how to grasp.
contribution: DemoGrasp achieves 95% success on Shadow Hand simulation across hundreds of objects, 84.6% success on unseen dexterous embodiments, and successfully grasps 110 real-world objects via vision-based imitation.

problem: DNNs suffer severe performance degradation on tabular data under distribution shift, and prior test-time adaptation methods designed for images fail on tabular modality and often depend on source domain access.
approach: PFT3A addresses label and feature shift without source access through: (1) class prior estimation for calibration, (2) robust feature learning via alignment of source-like and target-like features.
contribution: PFT3A enables prior-free tabular test-time adaptation addressing both label and feature shifts without requiring source domain or prior knowledge.

problem: Bayesian optimization addresses scalar-output functions, but many applications produce tensor-valued outputs with internal structural dependencies not captured by existing methods.
approach: A tensor-output Gaussian process (TOGP) with specialized kernels captures structural dependencies, paired with UCB acquisition and CMAB-UCB2 criterion for selecting both queried points and output subsets in combinatorial settings.
contribution: Tensor-output BO methods achieve sublinear regret bounds; on real-world experiments, CBBO demonstrates superiority by handling partially observed tensor outputs and optimizing over output subsets.

problem: Fine-tuning large neural networks within strict memory constraints is challenging, and static channel selection lacks awareness of data-specific importance patterns.
approach: TraDy combines architecture-dependent layer selection with dynamic stochastic channel resampling between epochs, optimizing both memory use and gradient approximation quality.
contribution: TraDy achieves up to 99% activation sparsity, 95% weight derivative sparsity, and 97% FLOPs reduction for weight derivatives while maintaining state-of-the-art performance on downstream tasks.

problem: Medical-domain knowledge representation in LLMs is poorly understood, making it difficult to target fine-tuning, unlearning, or debiasing at the right model layers.
approach: Four interpretability techniques (UMAP, gradient-based saliency, layer lesioning, activation patching) analyze how five LLMs represent medical knowledge (ages, symptoms, diseases, drugs) across layers.
contribution: Medical knowledge maps reveal that most medical knowledge in Llama3.3-70B is processed in the first half of layers; age is encoded non-linearly, disease progression is non-monotonic and circular, and drugs cluster by specialty rather than mechanism.

problem: Score-based generative models are difficult to integrate into ADMM optimization for inverse problems due to manifold mismatch between training noise and algorithm iterates, and convergence is not guaranteed.
approach: ADMM-PnP with AC-DC denoiser uses: (1) auto-correction via additive Gaussian noise, (2) directional correction via conditional Langevin dynamics, (3) score-based denoising; convergence is proven under proper parameter settings.
contribution: AC-DC denoiser achieves high-probability fixed-point convergence under weakly nonexpansive operator conditions; experiments show consistent improvements in solution quality on inverse problems.

problem: Offline multi-agent RL with multi-task datasets faces variable input structures due to different agent counts, and transformer-based methods compress history into single tokens, losing long-range dependencies critical for partially observable MARL.
approach: STAIRS-Former augments transformers with spatial and temporal hierarchies plus token dropout to properly attend to critical tokens while leveraging long history across varying agent populations.
contribution: STAIRS-Former achieves new state-of-the-art on StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge with diverse multi-task datasets, consistently outperforming prior algorithms.

problem: Instance and panoptic segmentation rely on expensive dense annotations (masks, boxes, points), and unsupervised/weakly-supervised methods are constrained by semantic backbone limitations.
approach: TRACE shows that text-to-image diffusion models encode instance boundary priors; it identifies the Instance Emergence Point in self-attention maps and extracts boundaries via Attention Boundary Divergence, distilling into a one-step decoder.
contribution: TRACE achieves +5.1 AP improvement on unsupervised instance segmentation and +1.7 PQ on tag-supervised panoptic segmentation while being 81x faster than per-image diffusion inversion.

problem: Contrastive objectives power multimodal models but training is slow due to reliance on long stochastic optimization with minibatch back-propagation.
approach: UniCon introduces a contrastive similarity weight matrix that enables closed-form global solutions replacing minibatch back-propagation with exact updates; RKHS kernelization unifies contrastive alignment with spectral methods.
contribution: UniCon achieves substantial efficiency gains while preserving generality and strong empirical performance on synthetic, unimodal, multimodal, and zero-shot tasks.

problem: LLMs memorize sensitive data during pretraining, creating compliance risks under GDPR and EU AI Act, and existing unlearning methods leak data, sacrifice fluency, or require expensive reward models.
approach: PURGE uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with an intrinsic reward penalizing forbidden concepts, enabling safe unlearning without external reward models.
contribution: PURGE achieves up to 46x lower token usage than state-of-the-art, improves fluency by +5.48% and robustness by +12.02%, reaching 11% unlearning effectiveness while preserving 98% utility.

problem: Contrastive learning produces embeddings with unclear distributional properties, making it difficult to derive analytical expressions for likelihood, entropy, and mutual information.
approach: Analysis shows that InfoNCE-trained embeddings are well-approximated by multivariate Gaussian distributions under alignment and concentration assumptions; added regularization promotes low norm and high entropy.
contribution: Features from InfoNCE training follow near-precise Gaussian distributions, enabling analytic expressions in the representation space and applications in likelihood-based inference.

problem: Reconstructing complete 3D assets requires separate pipelines for geometry, materials, and illumination with distinct limitations, and single-image methods suffer from fundamental ill-posedness in disentanglement.
approach: MIDR-3D unifies reconstruction in one end-to-end pipeline using transformer cross-conditioning and a dual-path strategy: one path predicts structure/appearance, the other predicts environment illumination; differentiable Monte Carlo renderer enables training.
contribution: MIDR-3D reconstructs complete relightable 3D assets from sparse multi-view images in under one second with physically-based materials and environment illumination.

problem: RAG systems incur substantial overhead from processing frequently repeated text chunks and apply uniform retrieval depth regardless of query complexity, wasting computation.
approach: AdaCache uses cache-aware partial recomputation profiling attention patterns for selective cache variants, and adaptive context augmentation dynamically determines optimal retrieval depth via lightweight confidence estimation.
contribution: AdaCache delivers substantial improvements in Time-To-First-Token compared to state-of-the-art RAG caching systems while preserving generation quality.

problem: Model inversion attacks reconstruct training data from models, but the prevailing explanation that rote memorization drives exposure is incomplete.
approach: Analysis shows that privacy under model inversion arises from adversarially non-robust features (generalizable but unstable features), not information dependency; Anti-Adversarial Training learns these features intentionally.
contribution: Anti-Adversarial Training achieves superior reconstruction defense and higher accuracy than state-of-the-art defenses, revealing that non-robust features drive privacy exposure.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering faces distribution shifts when views are partially missing, and existing methods either increase computational complexity through imputation or ignore inter-view bias.
approach: PDD uses unbiased projections learned from complete views to refine biased projections from incomplete data, plus robust contrastive learning for consensus projection to mitigate cluster collapse.
contribution: PDD achieves superior incomplete multi-view clustering performance compared to state-of-the-art methods while avoiding imputation overhead.

problem: Vision tokenizers trained for reconstruction excel at low-level appearance but lack semantic representations for understanding, while contrastive encoders capture semantics but cannot decode to pixels.
approach: DualToken disentangles reconstruction and semantic objectives into separate codebooks for high-level semantics and low-level details, unifying representations for both understanding and generation.
contribution: DualToken sets new records: 0.25 rFID and 82.0% zero-shot ImageNet accuracy; surpasses VILA-U by 5.8 points on visual understanding and 13% improvement on GenAI-Bench.

problem: AI control mechanisms impose operational and financial costs that limit practical adoption of oversight systems for agentic AI in high-stakes applications.
approach: A theoretical framework quantifies Control Tax (cost of control measures) and maps classifier performance to safety assurances; evaluates backdoor detection against adversarial code insertion and optimizes monitoring strategies under budget constraints.
contribution: Framework enables practitioners to make informed decisions by connecting safety guarantees with costs, advancing AI Control through principled economic feasibility assessment.

problem: Open-set text classification must classify known labels while reliably rejecting OOD inputs, but existing methods train on closed-set ID data with biased representations, yielding overconfident OOD predictions.
approach: UnLLM reformulates classification as subset-conditioned text generation: the LLM is prompted with sampled subsets of known labels, automatically assigning unknowns, transforming OOD detection into an intrinsic capability.
contribution: UnLLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across six benchmarks by explicitly incorporating unknowns through unified representation-logits-inference optimization.

problem: Representing epistemic uncertainty via credal sets (convex sets of probability distributions) requires training complex ensemble models, limiting application to foundation models and multimodal systems.
approach: An efficient method grounded in relative likelihood uses decalibration to predict probability intervals (credal sets) for each class without ensemble training.
contribution: Decalibration enables credal prediction on TabPFN and CLIP architectures (previously infeasible), with strong coverage-efficiency performance, OOD detection, and in-context learning capabilities.

problem: Building 4D video representations typically requires additional estimators (depth, flow, tracking) or heavy per-scene optimization, making methods brittle and hard to generalize.
approach: Trace Anything represents video as a Trajectory Field: a dense mapping assigning each pixel to a parametric 3D trajectory; a neural network predicts trajectory fields in a single forward pass.
contribution: Trace Anything surpasses existing methods on trajectory field benchmarks and point tracking with significant efficiency gains, enabling applications in goal-conditioned manipulation and motion extrapolation.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts routing mechanisms in LLMs lack clear understanding from a mechanistic interpretability perspective, hindering insights for model design and analysis.
approach: A lightweight decomposition methodology recursively breaks down routing decisions by model components, studying contributions of attention and MoE layers to routing across different LLMs.
contribution: Analysis reveals MoE entanglement patterns (consistent layer-to-layer firing correlation), persistent cross-layer influence of components, and different long/short-range promoting/inhibiting effects across models.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs incurs high training memory costs dominated by activations, and existing data-agnostic optimization strategies are ineffective and unstable.
approach: TokenSeek performs instance-aware token seeking and ditching to dynamically identify and remove less important tokens per example, reducing activation memory across transformer layers.
contribution: TokenSeek requires only 14.8% of memory on Llama3.2 1B while achieving on-par or better fine-tuning performance; interpretable token seeking reveals insights for future token efficiency research.

problem: Autoregressive language models train efficiently but overfit easily, while masked-diffusion models resist overfitting but train slowly; combining objectives requires understanding optimal ratios.
approach: Dual Language Models combine autoregressive and masked-diffusion objectives without architectural changes; analysis of 50 models under varying data repetition derives optimal objective ratios.
contribution: Dual-objective training achieves the best of both worlds: autoregressive sample-efficiency and masked-diffusion overfitting resilience, with optimal ratio similar across different performance targets.

problem: Speculative decoding is constrained by serialized execution causing mutual waiting between draft and target models, limiting parallelism and efficiency.
approach: SpecBranch adapts branch prediction mechanisms from CPUs: parallel speculative branches hedge against rejections, with adaptive draft lengths combining implicit draft confidence and explicit target feature reuse.
contribution: SpecBranch achieves 1.8x-4.5x speedups over auto-regressive decoding and reduces rollback tokens by 50% on poorly-aligned models while maintaining identical sampling distribution.

problem: Pose estimation from limited body sensors generalizes poorly across users because location measurements are highly influenced by body size differences.
approach: InPose formulates pose estimation as an inverse problem using a pre-trained diffusion model conditioned on rotational measurements alone, guided by a likelihood term from measured locations.
contribution: InPose achieves zero-shot generalization across users by leveraging diffusion priors to infer pose sequences compatible with sparse on-body rotation measurements.

problem: Single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics analysis requires extensive manual programming and complex tool integration, hindering accessibility for researchers.
approach: CellAgent is an LLM-driven multi-agent framework using hierarchical decision-making to perform end-to-end analysis via natural language; sc-Omni toolkit consolidates essential analysis tools with self-reflective optimization for iterative refinement.
contribution: CellAgent significantly improves efficiency in scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics analysis while maintaining performance comparable to existing approaches and human expert standards.

problem: Continual unlearning in text-to-image models fails due to cumulative parameter drift, causing utility collapse after few unlearning requests, and existing methods struggle with sequential vs batch scenarios.
approach: Study of regularization strategies plus gradient-projection method that constrains parameter drift orthogonal to important subspaces, maintaining semantic awareness of concepts near unlearning targets.
contribution: Systematic study establishes continual unlearning as a fundamental challenge; gradient-projection regularization substantially improves performance and is complementary to other regularizers.

problem: Mask-based diffusion language models struggle to revise incorrect tokens once generated, limiting refinement capability and generation quality.
approach: RemeDi (Remasking-enabled Diffusion LM) jointly predicts token distributions and per-token confidence scores; low-confidence tokens are remasked and resampled with richer context in later steps.
contribution: RemeDi achieves state-of-the-art results among open-source diffusion language models on multiple datasets through confidence-aware remasking.

problem: LLM-based search agents suffer efficiency bottlenecks: exact search incurs overhead, coarse retrieval requires extra reasoning, and system design inefficiencies cause cascading latency.
approach: SearchAgent-X uses high-recall approximate retrieval with priority-aware scheduling and non-stall retrieval to eliminate waiting and scheduling inefficiencies.
contribution: SearchAgent-X achieves up to 3.4x higher throughput and 5x lower latency compared to vLLM and HNSW-based systems without sacrificing generation quality.

problem: Learning from constrained demonstrations (e.g., joystick control limiting dimensions) results in suboptimal policies because experts cannot demonstrate optimal behavior.
approach: The method infers a state-only reward signal from demonstrations to measure task progress, self-labels rewards for unknown states via temporal interpolation, enabling exploration of shorter trajectories.
contribution: Outperforms behavioral cloning in sample efficiency and task completion; on WidowX arm, achieves 11-second task completion, 10x faster than behavioral cloning.

problem: Knowledge distillation from LLMs via synthetic data lacks pedagogical awareness, treating it as one-off synthesis rather than systematic learning.
approach: IOA (Knowledge Identifier, Organizer, Adapter) pipeline systematically identifies deficiencies, organizes delivery through progressive curricula, and adapts to student capacity using Bloom's Mastery and Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development.
contribution: IOA achieves 94.7% teacher performance retention on DollyEval using <1/10 parameters; shows 19.2% improvement on MATH and 22.3% on HumanEval vs baselines.

problem: Data curation for private machine learning assumes curated-model training on public data is privacy-preserving, but curation pipelines can leak private information through scores, selections, and trained models.
approach: Novel attacks target every curation stage: score computation, subset selection, and trained model inference; demonstrates membership information leakage despite models never seeing private data.
contribution: Reveals privacy risks in data curation previously overlooked; shows models trained on curated public data leak membership about private guidance data, requiring formal privacy guarantees in curation design.

problem: Fine-grained visual classification struggles to distinguish visually similar subcategories within a broad category due to subtle inter-class differences, large intra-class variations, and data scarcity.
approach: PSCL integrates text-controllable part localization using clearCLIP, multi-scale multi-part feature extraction to reduce redundancy, and visual-language contrastive learning with intermediate-granularity text features to improve alignment and separability.
contribution: The framework demonstrates superior performance and generalization ability on five publicly available FGVC datasets through modular design and synergy between vision and language.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from visual hallucinations and language shortcuts, learning to rely on text priors rather than visual perception because existing post-training methods only supervise final outputs without explicit visual reasoning guidance.
approach: Vision-SR1 decomposes VLM reasoning into visual perception and language reasoning stages: first generating self-contained visual descriptions, then validating these with language-only reasoning, combining self-rewards with output supervision through reinforcement learning.
contribution: The method improves visual reasoning without external supervisions and provides balanced training signals through self-rewarding multi-reward policy optimization.

problem: Large Reasoning Models generate verbose chains of thought with much redundant or truncated content, and supervised finetuning propagates these uninformative patterns, degrading performance and efficiency.
approach: The framework uses integrated gradient attribution to identify segment-level metrics (attribution strength and direction consistency) that indicate reflective versus shallow reasoning, then applies selective supervised finetuning while masking loss for unimportant segments.
contribution: Segment-level selective learning improves accuracy and output efficiency by enabling more effective learning from long reasoning traces across multiple models and datasets.

problem: Diffusion and flow-based models require expensive integration during inference for sampling, and existing consistency training methods have computational challenges such as requiring model inverses or backpropagation through iterations.
approach: CurlFlow trains a model to compute both ODE solutions and implied velocity by following non-conservative dynamics with curl, achieving this without explicit invertibility constraints or expensive differentiation through model iteration.
contribution: On CIFAR, CurlFlow attains a favorable relationship of FID to step count, relative to flow matching, MeanFlow, and other flow map learning methods.

problem: Model merging overlooks the role of the fine-tuning process, focusing only on parameter conflicts at merging stage, leading to significant post-merge performance degradation and instability.
approach: MergOPT formulates model merging as distributionally robust optimization where parameters of other experts are viewed as adversarial merge-offsets, injecting merge-induced parameter shifts into fine-tuning weight updates to stabilize the loss landscape.
contribution: Across four LLMs and one vision model, MergOPT consistently outperforms standard fine-tuning with average relative gain of 3.5% and maximum gain of 9.5% across merging strategies when merging seven experts.

problem: Developing effective mobile GUI agents with reinforcement learning remains challenging due to heavy-tailed task difficulty distribution and inefficient large-scale environment sampling.
approach: MOBILERL introduces Difficulty-Adaptive GRPO (ADAGRPO) with difficulty-adaptive positive replay and failure curriculum filtering to handle varying task difficulties, plus shortest-path reward adjustment for multi-turn tasks.
contribution: MOBILERL-9B achieves state-of-the-art success rates on AndroidWorld (80.2%) and Android-Lab (53.6%), demonstrating strong performance across diverse mobile apps and tasks.

problem: Differential privacy under add/remove adjacency overstates attribute privacy when the protection goal is per-record attributes rather than membership, as it ignores the substitute adjacency relation.
approach: The work develops novel attacks to audit DP under substitute adjacency and shows that audit results are inconsistent with DP guarantees reported under add/remove but consistent with substitute-based accounting.
contribution: Empirical results demonstrate a critical gap between add/remove and substitute adjacency audit findings, highlighting that the choice of adjacency is essential when protecting per-record attributes.

problem: Large Language Models used in high-stakes legal decisions lack systematic evaluation for judicial fairness, which is necessary to ensure trustworthiness in resolving judicial issues.
approach: The framework measures LLM fairness based on judicial fairness theories using 65 labels and 161 values, and develops three evaluation metrics—inconsistency, bias, and imbalanced inaccuracy—assessed on 16 LLMs using the JudiFair dataset of 177,100 unique case facts.
contribution: Experiments uncover pervasive inconsistency, bias, and imbalanced inaccuracy across models, revealing severe LLM judicial unfairness with pronounced biases on demographic labels.

problem: DNA language models designed for functional DNA sequence and genome design possess generative power that creates biosafety concerns about designing human viruses.
approach: GeneBreaker is a jailbreak framework integrating an LLM agent with bioinformatics tools to design high-homology non-pathogenic prompts, beam search guided by PathoLM, and BLAST-based evaluation to identify successful pathogenic sequence generation.
contribution: GeneBreaker successfully jailbreaks Evo series models across 6 viral categories with up to 60% Attack Success Rate for Evo2-40B, with generated sequences showing structural fidelity.

problem: The relationship between Graph Neural Network expressivity and predictive performance remains unclear, particularly whether increased expressivity improves or harms generalization.
approach: The work introduces pseudometrics capturing structural similarity between graphs and derives generalization bounds depending on distance between training and test graphs, model complexity, and training set size.
contribution: Generalization bounds reveal that more expressive GNNs may generalize worse unless increased complexity is balanced by sufficiently large training sets or reduced distance between training and test graphs.

problem: Large language models lack elementary safety features against prompt injection attacks due to the absence of intrinsic separation between instructions and data at the token level.
approach: ASIDE applies orthogonal rotation to embeddings of data tokens, creating clearly distinct representations of instructions and data without additional parameters.
contribution: Instruction-tuned LLMs with ASIDE achieve substantially higher instruction-data separation without performance loss and show increased robustness to prompt injection benchmarks even without dedicated safety training.

problem: Much long-text training data does not genuinely require extended context, as most spans can be predicted with short-range context while only a fraction depends on long-distance dependencies.
approach: LongFilter measures information gain from extended context by contrasting model predictions under long-context versus short-context settings, identifying samples where long-range dependencies are essential.
contribution: Extending LLaMA-3-8B context from 8K to 64K with LongFilter-selected data yields substantial improvements on HELMET, LongBench, and RULER benchmarks.

problem: Vision token pruning in efficient VLMs achieves good performance on VQA tasks but suffers substantial degradation on visual grounding tasks due to loss of global spatial reference frames.
approach: Nuwa is a two-stage token pruning framework: first applying separation, alignment, and aggregation operations inspired by swarm intelligence to retain global spatial anchors, then text-guided pruning within the LLM.
contribution: Nuwa achieves state-of-the-art VQA performance (94% to 95%) and substantial improvements on visual grounding tasks (7% to 47%), demonstrating effective spatial integrity preservation.

problem: Deploying reasoning language models involves a performance-cost tradeoff at model size and reasoning budget levels, requiring optimal routing of queries to model-budget pairs.
approach: RADAR learns an item response model from model responses to different queries with different budgets, using interpretable parameters of query difficulties and model-budget abilities to route queries appropriately.
contribution: RADAR demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art routing methods on 8 reasoning benchmarks with strong generalization to out-of-distribution queries.

problem: Training methods like GRPO for search agents discard rich entity information from synthetic data, relying on sparse outcome-based rewards and unable to distinguish informative near-miss samples from complete failures.
approach: E-GRPO formulates a dense entity-aware reward function that assigns partial rewards to incorrect samples proportional to their entity match rate, enabling learning from near-miss samples.
contribution: E-GRPO consistently outperforms GRPO baseline on QA and deep research benchmarks with superior accuracy and more efficient reasoning policies requiring fewer tool calls.

problem: LLM-as-a-judge reliability in open-ended tasks with dynamic environments and complex interactions remains unexplored, with significant gaps between LLM judges and human experts.
approach: WebDevJudge is a systematic benchmark with human preference labels over paired web implementations, evaluating LLMs, MLLMs, and agentic workflows through non-interactive and interactive dynamic evaluation.
contribution: Experiments reveal a significant gap between LLM judges and human experts, with failures in recognizing functional equivalence, verifying task feasibility, and mitigating bias.

problem: Existing PBR texture generation methods fail to address materials decomposition from image prompts under limited illumination cues and seamless view-consistent texture completion.
approach: LumiTex comprises multi-branch generation for disentangling albedo and metallic-roughness under shared illumination priors, lighting-aware material attention for physically grounded generation, and geometry-guided inpainting for seamless UV completion.
contribution: LumiTex achieves state-of-the-art texture quality, surpassing both existing open-source and commercial methods in PBR texture generation.

problem: Understanding robustness of Text-Attributed Graphs to textual and structural perturbations remains fragmented, with no systematic evaluation across diverse models and attack scenarios.
approach: A unified framework evaluates robustness of classical GNNs, robust GNNs, and GraphLLMs across ten datasets under text-based, structure-based, and hybrid perturbations in poisoning and evasion scenarios.
contribution: Analysis reveals inherent robustness trade-offs between text and structure, performance dependence on text encoders and attack types, and introduces SFT-auto for superior balanced robustness.

problem: Federated clustering when the total number of clusters is unknown and clients have heterogeneous overlapping cluster sets lacks principled approaches.
approach: FedGEM is a federated generalized expectation-maximization algorithm where clients perform local EM steps and construct uncertainty sets around local components; the server learns cluster overlaps and infers global clusters via closed-form computations.
contribution: FedGEM achieves probabilistic convergence guarantees and comparable performance to centralized EM while outperforming existing federated clustering methods.

problem: Efficient design of genomic perturbation experiments is constrained by vast search spaces and experimental limitations, making exhaustive genome perturbation infeasible.
approach: BioBO integrates Bayesian optimization with multimodal gene embeddings and enrichment analysis, using biologically grounded priors with acquisition functions to bias search toward promising genes while maintaining exploration.
contribution: BioBO improves labeling efficiency by 25-40% compared to conventional BO and yields pathway-level explanations linking designs to biologically coherent regulatory circuits.

problem: Activation steering for LLM alignment lacks a unified theoretical framework and relies on one-step steering that fails to capture complex activation distribution patterns.
approach: BODES provides a unified ODE-based framework for activation steering, interpreting conventional activation addition as first-order approximation to ODE solution; identifies steering directions via barrier functions and employs multi-step adaptive steering.
contribution: BODES achieves consistent empirical improvements with 7% gain on TruthfulQA, 2% on RealToxicityPrompts, and 2% on UltraFeedback compared to state-of-the-art activation steering methods.

problem: The objectives that large language models implicitly optimize remain dangerously opaque, making trustworthy alignment and auditing a grand challenge.
approach: The framework reframes reward inference from estimation to verification by leveraging Bayesian IRL to recover a distribution over objectives, enabling quantifying non-identifiability, providing uncertainty-aware diagnostics, and validating policy-level utility.
contribution: Successfully audits a detoxified LLM yielding a well-calibrated interpretable objective that strengthens alignment guarantees and achieves comparable toxicity reductions to ground-truth alignment.

problem: Sequential editing that updates LLM knowledge through multiple edits destabilizes representations and induces catastrophic forgetting.
approach: SPHERE uses Hyperspherical Energy to quantify neuron uniformity during editing and employs HE-driven regularization to stabilize weight distributions; identifies a sparse space complementary to principal hyperspherical directions.
contribution: SPHERE preserves prior knowledge while enabling reliable sequential updates, with strong correlation between Hyperspherical Energy dynamics and editing performance.

problem: It remains unclear whether LLMs can acquire genuinely new reasoning strategies beyond skills encoded during pre-training, particularly for algorithmic coding tasks.
approach: DELTA-Code is a controlled benchmark using templated problem generators to probe learnability (can RL solve problems with zero pretrained pass rate?) and transferrability (do learned skills generalize to OOD problems?).
contribution: Experiments reveal grokking phase transitions enabling learnability on previously unsolvable problems; results show solid gains within families and for recomposed skills but persistent transfer limitations.

problem: Most LLM-based theorem provers are constrained by needing expert-written formal statements as inputs, limiting applicability to real-world problems expressed in natural language.
approach: Mathesis proposes an autoformalizer trained with reinforcement learning integrating syntactic, semantic, and prover feedback; introduces LeanScorer for evaluating semantic correctness and Gaokao-Formal benchmark.
contribution: The autoformalizer improves pass rates by 45% on Gaokao-Formal and 6% on MiniF2F; paired with provers achieves 42% gain for DeepSeek-Prover-V2 on Gaokao-Formal.

problem: Image personalization enables customizing Text-to-Image models but suffers from concept coupling, where models create spurious associations between subjects and their contexts.
approach: ACCORD formalizes concept coupling as a statistical dependency problem with two regularization losses: Denoising Decouple Loss minimizing dependency changes across denoising steps and Prior Decouple Loss aligning relational priors with superclasses.
contribution: ACCORD achieves superior balance between personalization fidelity and text control across subject, style, and face personalization benchmarks.

problem: Task vectors for accelerating in-context learning inference remain poorly understood in terms of their emergence, functionality, and limitations.
approach: The work proposes that task vectors encode single in-context demonstrations distilled from original ones, providing theoretical and empirical support through loss landscape analysis and practical LLM experiments.
contribution: Findings predict task vector failure in representing high-rank mappings and suggest enhancement by injecting multiple task vectors into few-shot prompts.

problem: VLM-based autonomous driving systems suffer from either bypassing perception and prediction stages or employing fragmented decision-making where these modules operate separately.
approach: AutoDrive-P3 integrates Perception, Prediction, and Planning through structured reasoning with P3-CoT dataset and P3-GRPO hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm providing progressive supervision.
contribution: AutoDrive-P3 enables safer and more interpretable autonomous driving through coherent reasoning that progressively generates answers for perception, prediction, and planning.

problem: EEG-based brain-computer interfaces suffer from poor generalization due to distribution shifts across domains, with most methods relying on Euclidean embeddings unsuited for hierarchical structures.
approach: HEEGNet uses hybrid hyperbolic network architecture combining Euclidean and hyperbolic encoders with coarse-to-fine domain adaptation to capture hierarchical structure in EEG.
contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate HEEGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple EEG datasets covering visual evoked potentials, emotion recognition, and intracranial EEG.

problem: Attention-based methods for capturing global cross-variate dependencies in multivariate time series suffer from quadratic complexity limiting scalability.
approach: VPNet proposes that modeling local cross-variate interactions is sufficient and efficient; uses patch-level autoencoder with VarTCNBlock applying depthwise 2D convolutions across a variates-by-patches grid for linear complexity scaling.
contribution: VPNet excels in both accuracy and efficiency with computational complexity scaling linearly with the number of variates.

problem: Trajectory Optimization models remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks, with existing backdoor methods ineffective due to TO models' sequence modeling nature and existing backdoor defenses lack action-level attacks.
approach: TrojanTO is a post-training action-level backdoor attack employing alternating training to forge trigger-target action connections, trajectory filtering for stealthiness, and batch poisoning for consistency.
contribution: TrojanTO effectively implants backdoors across diverse tasks and TO architectures (DT, GDT, DC) with low attack budget (0.3% of trajectories).

problem: Parallel Tempering for MCMC sampling is limited by minimal overlap between adjacent distributions in challenging problems, requiring increased computational resources.
approach: The framework accelerates Parallel Tempering by leveraging neural samplers including normalising flows, diffusion models, and controlled diffusions to reduce required overlap.
contribution: Theoretically and empirically demonstrates improved sample quality, reduced computational cost compared to classical PT, and efficient free energy estimation on multimodal problems.

problem: Video diffusion models struggle to balance semantic understanding with fine-grained visual details for manipulation videos, which require capturing subtle contact-rich dynamics.
approach: MIMIC is a two-stage image-to-video diffusion framework using an Interaction-Motion-Aware module to fuse reference video features and produce semantic masks, with Pair Prompt Control to disentangle object and camera motion.
contribution: MIMIC significantly outperforms existing methods, effectively preserving manipulation intent and motion details for diverse and deformable objects.

problem: Training with stochastic gradient descent at moderately large learning rates improves robustness against spurious correlations, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear.
approach: The work identifies batch size as critical and shows robustness gains arise from implicit regularization of SGD intensifying with larger learning rates and smaller batch sizes.
contribution: Theoretically establishes the phenomenon in linear models and empirically demonstrates SGD systematically suppresses spurious feature dependence across multiple deep neural network benchmarks.

problem: Auto-formalization of theorem statements remains a bottleneck for LLMs due to hallucinations, semantic mismatches, and inability to synthesize new definitions.
approach: Aria emulates expert reasoning via Graph-of-Thought by recursively decomposing statements into dependency graphs and constructing formalizations from grounded concepts; introduces AriaScorer for verification.
contribution: Achieves 91.6% compilation success rate and 68.5% final accuracy on ProofNet; on FATE-X reaches 44.0% accuracy (vs. baseline 24.0%); reaches 42.9% on homological conjectures while others score 0%.

problem: Existing image restoration methods treat mixed compound degradations by iteratively removing fixed categories, lacking compositionality and introducing cascading artifacts, overcorrection, or signal loss.
approach: PRISM is a prompted conditional diffusion framework using compound-aware supervision on degradation mixtures and weighted contrastive disentanglement to align compound distortions with primitives.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on unseen complex real-world degradations including underwater visibility and under-display camera effects; enables selective restoration for expert guidance.

problem: Frontier language models appear strong at reasoning but performance is often inflated by shortcuts such as memorisation and knowledge rather than genuine reasoning.
approach: LingOLY-TOO applies expert-designed obfuscations to Linguistics Olympiad problems preserving solution logic while removing orthographic clues that trigger memorisation patterns.
contribution: Model performance markedly drops upon obfuscation (best reasoning models drop from 0.60 to 0.48), effectively disentangling reasoning from knowledge.

problem: Task vectors often fail to transfer across different pre-trained models because their parameter spaces are misaligned.
approach: GradFix approximates ideal sign structure using only a handful of labeled samples without fine-tuning; computes target-model gradients to mask source task vector creating locally aligned updates.
contribution: Significant performance gains on vision and language benchmarks; outperforms naive task vector addition and few-shot fine-tuning; improves multi-task and multi-source model merging.

problem: Existing model merging methods fail to match full accuracy of separately fine-tuned endpoints when combining multiple fine-tuned models.
approach: MASS stores only the most salient singular components for each task based on low-rank decomposition and merges them into a shared model; at inference, a data-free router identifies best-fit subspaces.
contribution: Recovers up to 98% of average accuracy of individual fine-tuned models on CLIP-based image classification with 2x storage factor and two-pass inference overhead.

problem: Existing reward shaping methods for RL in reasoning models rely on hand-crafted directional penalties (higher/lower-is-better) that are often biased and require careful tuning.
approach: CANON amplifies impact of target metrics without presuming direction by regrouping responses based on metric values, measuring which trends correlate with performance, and identifying better responses within groups.
contribution: CANON with entropy consistently outperforms prior methods on math reasoning and logic tasks; when applied to response length improves token efficiency and performance-cost tradeoff.

problem: Reinforcement learning after next-token prediction works well in reasoning domains, but the optimization mechanisms enabling this success are not theoretically understood.
approach: They study a theoretical framework where autoregressive transformers are first trained on next-token prediction over a mixture of short and long chain-of-thought sequences, then fine-tuned with RL. For the parity prediction task, they prove RL enables generalization when the proportion of long demonstrations is not exponentially small.
contribution: They expose optimization mechanisms by which RL improves over next-token prediction, showing RL leverages longer responses to facilitate learning and deriving theoretical bounds for linear models on parity tasks.

problem: Human-Object Interaction detection with vision-language models suffers from sparse supervision and lacks a unified architecture that performs well in both fully supervised and zero-shot scenarios.
approach: They propose LINK, which decouples from detector-specific features via a Human-Object Geometrical Encoder and VLM Linking Decoder, then applies a Progressive Learning Strategy under a teacher-student paradigm to deliver dense supervision through contrastive learning.
contribution: LINK achieves state-of-the-art results on SWiG-HOI, HICO-DET, and V-COCO, showing strong performance in both zero-shot and fully supervised settings with open-vocabulary capability.

problem: Dense embeddings are extremely high-dimensional (e.g., 4096), incurring substantial costs in storage and inference latency, and existing sparse embedding methods suffer severe degradation in the ultra-sparse regime (k ≤ 4).
approach: CSRv2 introduces progressive k-annealing to stabilize sparsity learning, enhances quality via supervised contrastive objectives, and enables full backbone fine-tuning to reduce dead neurons and improve ultra-sparse representations.
contribution: CSRv2 reduces dead neurons from 80% to 20% and delivers 14% accuracy gain at k=2, achieving 7x speedup over Matryoshka Representation Learning and up to 300x improvements in compute and memory efficiency.

problem: Existing diffusion preference alignment methods focus only on positive preferences and maintain two distinct models, increasing computational cost and diluting learned negative alignment through weight merging.
approach: Diff-SNPO introduces a single-network framework that jointly learns from both positive and negative preferences using a bounded preference objective to prevent winner-likelihood collapse.
contribution: Diff-SNPO delivers strong alignment performance with significantly lower computational overhead than prior two-model approaches, showing that explicit negative preference modeling can be simple, stable, and efficient.

problem: While MLLM-based universal multimodal retrieval methods adopt contrastive learning, the mechanisms underlying their retrieval capabilities remain largely unexplored, potentially resulting in suboptimal performance.
approach: U-MARVEL systematically analyzes primary contributors to effective embedding learning by implementing a general MLLM-based embedding pipeline and exploring progressive transition, hard negative mining, and re-ranker distillation.
contribution: U-MARVEL outperforms state-of-the-art competitors on M-BEIR by a large margin in supervised settings and exhibits strong zero-shot performance on composed image retrieval and text-to-video retrieval.

problem: Estimating causal quantities typically requires large datasets, which can be expensive when measuring outcomes is costly, and prior work focuses narrowly on conditional average treatment effects.
