problem: LLMs used in healthcare may worsen existing biases; current methods lack ability to reveal and control spurious reliance on patient race.
approach: Assess Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to reveal associations between race and stigmatizing concepts in gemma-2 models; use SAE latents to steer model outputs for bias mitigation.
contribution: Identifies SAE latents correlating with race; demonstrates that steering via latents can induce problematic associations and offers potential for bias mitigation in controlled settings.

problem: Vision-Language Navigation agents lack fine-grained semantics and physical executability in 3D Gaussian Splatting environments.
approach: SAGE-3D upgrades 3DGS with Object-Centric Semantic Grounding for fine-grained annotations and Physics-Aware Execution Jointing for collision and physical interfaces; introduces InteriorGS dataset (1K scenes) and SAGE-Bench (2M VLN data).
contribution: Demonstrates strong generalizability with 31% improvement on VLN-CE Unseen task; provides benchmark showing 3DGS data is harder to converge but exhibits superior generalization.

problem: LLMs trained with reinforcement learning tend to generate unnecessary and low-quality chain-of-thought steps, failing when initial reasoning direction is suboptimal.
approach: Re² allows LLMs to abandon unproductive reasoning paths and restart via reinforcement learning without preliminary supervised fine-tuning, amplifying redo behavior from 0.5% to over 30%.
contribution: Achieves substantial performance gains over standard RLVR with same training compute budget and notable improvements as test-time samples increase.

problem: Few-shot Whole Slide Image classification suffers from overfitting due to low-dimensional manifold geometry being perturbed by downstream models.
approach: Propose Manifold Residual (MR) block decoupling linear layers into: (1) fixed random matrix as geometric anchor preserving topology, (2) trainable low-rank residual pathway for task-specific adaptation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art few-shot WSI classification with significantly fewer parameters via geometry-aware learning.

problem: Large Reasoning Models show significant accuracy degradation on long contexts and suffer from over-thinking due to ineffective self-verification.
approach: GrAlgoBench evaluates LRMs on graph algorithm problems allowing fine-grained difficulty control and programmatic verification; comprises nine tasks testing long-context reasoning.
contribution: Reveals accuracy falls below 50% once graphs exceed 120 nodes; demonstrates over-thinking phenomenon driven by extensive yet ineffective self-verification.

problem: Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks can produce degenerate explanations unrelated to actual model inference, and faithfulness metrics fail to identify these failure modes.
approach: Identify degenerate explanations through empirical analysis; demonstrate that SE-GNNs achieve optimal risk while producing unrelated explanations; introduce novel faithfulness metric reliably marking degenerate explanations.
contribution: Reveals failure modes in SE-GNN explanations and proposes reliable auditing mechanism for both malicious and natural degenerate explanations.

problem: Optimal integration of tools (code, search, reasoning) for diverse questions in tool-augmented LLMs lacks practical guidance.
approach: TUMIX ensemble framework runs multiple agents in parallel with distinct tool-use strategies, iteratively refining responses; enables auto-optimization of agent designs via LLMs.
contribution: Achieves 3.55% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art on reasoning benchmarks with near-equal inference costs; can halt refinement at confidence targets preserving 49% of inference cost.

problem: Frank-Wolfe algorithms rely on short steps but may not efficiently leverage function smoothness properties for convergence.
approach: Introduce optimistic Frank-Wolfe framework with primal-dual guarantees and generalized short-step strategy optimizing computable primal-dual gap.
contribution: Presents primal-dual convergence proof; empirical results demonstrate optimistic algorithm outperforms existing methods with practical stopping criteria.

problem: Post-training quantization for diffusion LLMs at 2-bit fails to achieve satisfactory performance due to masked-denoising activation patterns differing from standard PTQ assumptions.
approach: Quant-dLLM introduces Masked Calibration Simulation aligning calibration with timestep-dependent masking, Data-aware Any-order Quantizer learning ultra-low-bit representations, and Adaptive Blockwise Mixed Precision for sensitivity-based bit allocation.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art AR-transfer PTQ methods on dLLMs at 2-bit precision.

problem: Data-free continual model merging must balance transparency (avoiding interference with earlier tasks) and fidelity (adapting to new tasks) without task data.
approach: NUFILT proposes null-space filtering to preserve prior responses and lightweight LoRA adapter for task-specific signals, using projection-based surrogate loss.
contribution: Enables backbone to absorb new knowledge while retaining existing behaviors with theoretical subspace alignment guarantees and no extra inference cost.

problem: Electronic structure predictions from quantum mechanical methods are computationally expensive, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: BOA introduces Basis Overlap Architecture, an equivariant GNN using novel message passing with overlap matrix of basis functions to predict ground state electron density.
contribution: Surpasses previous state-of-the-art on QM9 and MD density datasets with excellent generalization to larger molecules up to 200 atoms.

problem: Training urban embodied AI agents requires diverse, high-fidelity environments but human-crafted and procedurally generated scenes lack scalability or real-world complexity.
approach: UrbanVerse converts crowd-sourced city-tour videos into physics-aware simulation scenes; provides UrbanVerse-100K (100k+ annotated 3D assets) and UrbanVerse-Gen (automatic pipeline extracting layouts and instantiating scenes).
contribution: Provides 160 high-quality scenes across 24 countries with strong zero-shot sim-to-real transfer improving success by +30.1% and enabling 300 m real-world mission.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization for VLMs relies on oversimplified pairwise comparisons with single negatives, failing to capture complex multimodal preferences.
approach: MISP-DPO incorporates multiple semantically diverse negative images via Plackett-Luce model; selects negatives based on reconstruction difficulty, semantic deviation, and mutual diversity with importance sampling for efficiency.
contribution: Consistently improves multimodal alignment across five benchmarks by incorporating semantic-aware, multi-negative sampling in preference-based learning.

problem: Reduced order modelling for high-dimensional parametric problems using linear subspaces becomes unreliable with classical interpolation in high-dimensional parameter spaces.
approach: Propose neural network-based subspace regression with redundancy strategy (predicting larger-than-needed subspaces) to simplify mapping and reduce complexity.
contribution: Demonstrates significant accuracy improvement with larger subspaces; shows applicability to parametric eigenproblems, deflation, relaxation, optimal control, and PDEs.

problem: LLMs show limited capability for code optimization focused on minimal execution time, with existing methods confined to local improvements.
approach: Adopt problem-oriented perspective reconstructing optimization pairs from multiple programmers on same problem; introduce anchor verification framework to mitigate optimization accuracy trade-offs.
contribution: Significantly enhances both correct optimization ratio and speedup through global algorithmic innovation enabled by problem-centric approach.

problem: Tree-Sliced Wasserstein metric is efficient but computing tree-based p-Wasserstein for p>1 is costly, limiting practical use to p=1 despite higher-order metrics offering better optimization landscapes.
approach: Introduce TS-Sobolev, tree-sliced regularized Sobolev IPM with closed-form expression admitting tractable computation for all p≥1; extends framework to hyperspheres.
contribution: Achieves same computational complexity for p>1 as TSW at p=1 while recovering TSW exactly at p=1; serves as drop-in replacement with additional flexibility.

problem: Real-time super-resolution models struggle with compressed streaming video content; existing datasets do not reflect streaming media characteristics.
approach: Introduce StreamSR dataset from YouTube covering diverse genres and resolutions; benchmark 11 state-of-the-art models; propose EfRLFN with Efficient Channel Attention and hyperbolic tangent activation.
contribution: Demonstrates fine-tuning on StreamSR yields significant performance gains generalizing across standard benchmarks for streaming super-resolution.

problem: Existing code similarity metrics do not reflect algorithmic similarity; LLM-based algorithm design lacks methods to distinguish innovative algorithms from syntactic refinements.
approach: Define algorithm similarity through problem-solving behavior by comparing trajectories of intermediate solutions progressively generated by algorithms.
contribution: Demonstrates utility in improving LLM-based algorithm design via diversity-maintaining search and provides algorithm analysis tool.

problem: Submodular maximization algorithms suffer from prohibitively high computational costs, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: Propose AAPGA integrating continuous relaxation, Accelerated Approximate Projected Gradient Ascent, and randomized rounding for near-optimal solutions under cardinality, knapsack, and partition matroid constraints.
contribution: Establishes approximation guarantees with improved query complexity; achieves up to 32.3x speedup over traditional methods on small-scale experiments.

problem: Time series anomaly detection via diffusion models suffers from irreducible variance due to inherent stochasticity, limiting reconstruction fidelity.
approach: ICDiffAD synergizes adaptive noise scheduling via SNR Scheduler with semi-deterministic generation via SNR Implicit Conditioning Mechanism initializing diffusion from partially corrupted inputs.
contribution: Improves F1 score by 20.2% and reduces false positives by 60.23% compared to existing diffusion-based TSAD methods.

problem: Text-to-image generation struggles to faithfully capture user intentions from short, under-specified prompts due to insufficient grounding in visual semantics.
approach: RePrompt introduces reasoning into prompt enhancement via reinforcement learning; trains language model to generate structured, self-reflective prompts optimized for image-level outcomes with tailored reward models.
contribution: Significantly boosts spatial layout fidelity and compositional generalization across diverse T2I backbones, establishing state-of-the-art results on GenEval and T2I-Compbench.

problem: Generative models lack formal verification that they are truly controllable despite proliferation of controlled generation methods.
approach: Provide theoretical framework formalizing controllability as control process; propose algorithm to estimate controllable sets with probably-approximately correct bounds distribution-free for any black-box model.
contribution: Demonstrates model controllability is surprisingly fragile and highly dependent on experimental setting, shifting focus from attempting control to understanding its fundamental limits.

problem: Dataset-level heterogeneity introduces domain biases degrading generalization in Time Series Foundation Models.
approach: FeDaL applies federated learning paradigm to learn dataset-agnostic representations; introduces Domain Bias Elimination (DBE) and Global Bias Elimination (GBE) mechanisms.
contribution: Demonstrates cross-dataset generalization improvements across eight tasks with analysis of federated scaling behavior under decentralization.

problem: Existing associative memory models evaluate retrieval quality based on proximity, which cannot guarantee retrieved patterns have strongest association with query.
approach: Propose adaptive similarity that learns to approximate likelihood of stored patterns generating query from context-drawn samples; integrate into Adaptive Hopfield Network (A-Hop).
contribution: Theoretically proves optimal correct retrieval under noisy, masked, and biased variants; achieves state-of-the-art on memory retrieval, classification, and multiple instance learning.

problem: Feasibility-sensitive QP optimization requires efficient solutions with robustness to both feasible and infeasible problems.
approach: FlexQP provides flexible QP optimizer based on exact constraint relaxation; Deep FlexQP applies deep unfolding to learn dimension-agnostic feedback policies from training data.
contribution: Generalizes to larger dimensions and longer iterations than trained for; outperforms state-of-the-art on portfolio, classification, and regression with PAC Bayes generalization guarantees.

problem: Large Reasoning Models generate excessively long chain-of-thought responses with redundant steps, inflating inference cost while maintaining accuracy remains challenging.
approach: PEAR introduces Phase Entropy Aware Reward mechanism penalizing excessive entropy during thinking phase while allowing exploration in answer phase, enabling adaptive response length control.
contribution: Consistently reduces response length while sustaining competitive accuracy across four benchmarks without explicit length targets or rigid truncation.

problem: Existing CATE estimation methods perform poorly in low-overlap regions where treatment propensity scores are extreme.
approach: Overlap-Adaptive Regularization (OAR) regularizes target models proportionally to overlap weights, increasing regularization strength in low-overlap regions and preserving Neyman-orthogonality for robust inference.
contribution: OAR significantly improves CATE estimation in low-overlap settings compared to constant regularization across both parametric and non-parametric meta-learners.

problem: Individualized differential privacy causes utility imbalance: data from owners with stronger privacy requirements becomes underrepresented in trained models, degrading performance on sensitive subgroups.
approach: INO-SGD strategically down-weights data within batches to improve performance on more private data while satisfying individualized privacy constraints.
contribution: INO-SGD is the first algorithm designed to address utility imbalance while satisfying individualized differential privacy guarantees.

problem: Existing universal prediction bounds for stochastic sequences hold only in expectation, not with high probability guarantees.
approach: Derives high-probability regret bounds for universal prediction over countable alphabets with convergence rate O(T^-1/2 δ^-1/2), complementing prior expectation-based bounds.
contribution: Establishes vanishing high-probability regret bounds with similar form to prior expectation bounds and proves an impossibility result on improving the δ exponent.

problem: LLMs suffer performance degradation on long contexts due to proactive interference from irrelevant information disrupting reasoning and memory.
approach: Sculptor equips LLMs with Active Context Management tools including context fragmentation, summarization, and precise search to sculpt internal working memory, plus dynamic context-aware RL training.
contribution: Sculptor significantly improves performance on long-context benchmarks without specific training and mitigates proactive interference through explicit context-control strategies.

problem: Image-guided multimodal translation is constrained by scarcity of multilingual image-text pairs, limiting language coverage.
approach: Speech-guided Multimodal Machine Translation (SMMT) uses speech and text fusion in an MLLM with a Self-Evolution Mechanism to synthesize speech and iteratively optimize using positive samples.
contribution: SMMT achieves state-of-the-art on Multi30K and new state-of-the-art average performance on FLORES-200 across 108 translation directions.

problem: Graph similarity measures often rely on costly transportation-based metrics; efficient approximations enabling graph retrieval at scale are lacking.
approach: Discovers exchangeability property in GNN embeddings enabling approximation of transportation-based graph similarities via Euclidean distances between order statistics and proposes unified locality-sensitive hashing framework.
contribution: LSH framework supports diverse relevance measures including subgraph matching and graph edit distance more effectively than baselines.

problem: LLM agents can be tricked into executing harmful goals decomposed into benign subtasks; shallow alignment techniques fail to reason about long-range intent.
approach: Proposes lightweight sequential monitoring framework observing conversation at higher level, curates DecomposedHarm dataset with 4,634 tasks, and uses prompt-engineered monitors with cumulative sub-prompt evaluation.
contribution: Lightweight sequential monitors achieve 93% defense success rate against decomposition attacks while cutting costs by 90% and latency by 50%.

problem: Multimodal alignment post-training leaves user role unaligned and assumes fixed input prompt structure, making VLMs vulnerable to structural perturbations.
approach: Introduces Role-Modality Attacks (RMA) exploiting role confusion and image token position changes, and proposes adversarial training using perturbed prompts to achieve robustness.
contribution: Adversarial training makes VLMs robust to input prompt perturbations with substantial Attack Success Rate reduction.

problem: Diffusion models reproduce exact training images; existing norm-based memorization detection assumes isotropic log-probability distributions which fails in low-noise anisotropic regime.
approach: Develops memorization detection metric integrating isotropic norm and anisotropic alignment (angular alignment between guidance vector and unconditional scores) computed via two forward passes.
contribution: Detection metric outperforms existing denoising-free methods and is approximately 5x faster than prior best approach.

problem: Optical flow methods rely on cost volumes which are computationally expensive; simpler warping-based approaches are unexplored.
approach: WAFT replaces cost volume with high-resolution warping, using a simple flexible meta-architecture with minimal inductive biases.
contribution: WAFT ranks 1st on Spring, Sintel, and KITTI benchmarks, achieves best zero-shot generalization on KITTI, and is up to 4.1x faster than similar-performance methods.

problem: Linear attention mechanisms show improvement but decay matrix design is structurally limited to Diagonal-Plus-Rank-1, restricting expressiveness.
approach: HDLA uses efficient matrix decomposition to achieve Diagonal-Plus-Rank-2 decay structure and proposes chunk-wise parallel algorithm accommodating diagonal-plus-rank-r decay and key-value outer products.
contribution: HDLA sets new SOTA on language modeling and retrieval at 2.8B scale, with up to 80% performance gains on retrieval tasks.

problem: Existing LLM evaluation benchmarks are prone to saturation and memorization or rely on subjective comparisons; assessing LLM capability for combinatorial optimization is underexplored.
approach: HeuriGym is an agentic framework where LLMs propose heuristics, receive code-execution feedback, and iteratively refine solutions, with Quality-Yield Index metric capturing solution pass rate and quality.
contribution: Evaluation of nine SOTA models reveals persistent limitations; even GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.5-Pro achieve only 0.6 QYI compared to expert baseline of 1.

problem: LLMs exhibit cultural bias and limited awareness of underrepresented cultures; mechanisms underlying cultural understanding remain unexplored.
approach: Identifies culture-general and culture-specific neurons via gradient-based scoring, showing they account for <1% of neurons and concentrate in shallow-to-middle MLP layers.
contribution: Suppressing culture-specific neurons degrads cultural benchmark performance by up to 30% with minimal impact on general NLU, revealing cultural knowledge mechanisms.

problem: Decentralized composite optimization over networks without central coordinators suffers from communication bottlenecks limiting scalability.
approach: Proposes decentralized Symmetric ADMM incorporating multiple communication rounds per iteration with new constraint formulation enabling beyond-neighbor information exchange and optimal communication rules.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence while reducing total iterations and overall communication cost compared to existing decentralized methods.

problem: Existing motion-language models face quantization errors capping motion quality and cross-modal interference when unifying discrete text and continuous motion in single-stream architecture.
approach: MotionGPT3 encodes raw motion into continuous latent space via VAE and uses dual-stream Transformer with shared attention to preserve modality-specific routes while enabling controlled bidirectional flow.
contribution: Achieves 2x faster training convergence in loss and up to 4x faster validation convergence while maintaining SOTA performance on motion understanding and generation.

problem: Training GUI agents is limited by reliance on unsafe live web interactions or expensive scarce human-crafted data; efficiently compressing LLM knowledge into agent behavior is underexplored.
approach: WebFactory automates closed-loop RL pipeline: environment synthesis -> knowledge-aware task generation -> LLM trajectory collection -> decomposed reward RL training -> agent evaluation.
contribution: Agent trained on synthetic data from 10 websites achieves performance comparable to agents trained on same human-annotated data from much larger environments.

problem: Omni-modal LLMs aim for modality-invariant reasoning but whether they achieve it or inherit modality-specific biases is unclear.
approach: XModBench is a 60K-question tri-modal benchmark with five task families covering all six cross-modality directions to measure cross-modal consistency and diagnose task competence and modality disparity.
contribution: Even Gemini-2.5-Pro struggles with spatial/temporal reasoning (<60% accuracy) and exhibits 20+ point modality disparities and directional imbalance.

problem: Classical predictive coding formulations are unidirectional (generative or discriminative) but experimental evidence suggests brains employ bidirectional processing.
approach: Proposes bidirectional PC (bPC) combining generative and discriminative inference via energy landscape simultaneously supporting both tasks with biologically plausible circuit implementation.
contribution: bPC matches or outperforms unidirectional models on specialized tasks and shows superior performance on multimodal learning and inference with missing information.

problem: Pixel-space generative models train poorly and underperform latent-space counterparts; persistent performance and efficiency gaps limit adoption.
approach: Two-stage framework: pre-train encoders capturing semantics from clean images aligned with deterministic sampling trajectory points, then fine-tune end-to-end for diffusion and consistency models.
contribution: Pixel-space diffusion achieves FID 1.58 on ImageNet-256 and 2.35 on ImageNet-512, surpassing VAE counterparts with only ~30% of DiT training compute; consistency model achieves FID 8.82 on ImageNet-256.

problem: Class incremental learning with only unlabeled data and class names is realistic but pseudo-label noise aggravates catastrophic forgetting.
approach: N2L uses regression with MSE loss solved recursively, applies feature dimensionality reduction, and iteratively updates labels using reduced-feature classifier with bi-level weight adjustment for confidence and class imbalance.
contribution: Achieves performance equivalent to joint training with unlabeled data, mitigating catastrophic forgetting and outperforming SOTA methods.

problem: SAM2 shows excellent video segmentation but heavy computational burden hinders real-time video processing; post-training acceleration is underexplored.
approach: Proposes object-aware Sparse Window Routing (SWR) for image encoder and Sparse Memory Retrieval (SMR) for memory attention to eliminate redundant background computation leveraging consistency and saliency cues.
contribution: Efficient-SAM2 significantly improves inference efficiency by adaptively focusing on object regions.

problem: Existing safety fine-tuning for VLMs lacks visual reasoning ability in safety-critical contexts; multi-image safety scenarios are underexplored.
approach: Introduces Multi-Image Safety (MIS) dataset with multi-image inputs and safety Chain-of-Thought labels for fine-grained reasoning logic.
contribution: Fine-tuning InternVL2.5-8B with MIS increases accuracy by 0.83% on general benchmarks and substantially reduces Attack Success Rate on safety benchmarks.

problem: Pose-based human animation relies on error-prone pose estimators sensitive to occlusion and complex poses.
approach: DirectAnimator bypasses pose extraction using Driving Cue Triplet (pose, face, location) fused via CueFusion DiT, with Same2X training strategy aligning cross-ID features with same-ID data.
contribution: Achieves SOTA visual quality and identity preservation while remaining robust to occlusions and complex articulation with fewer resources.

problem: Web agents struggle with short-horizon subtasks on UI components; existing benchmarks do not extensively evaluate subtask mastery.
approach: WARC-Bench features 438 tasks on dynamic webpages via Web ARChive files, evaluated via SFT and RL with verifiable rewards.
contribution: SFT achieves 48.8% success rate; RLVR over SFT improves to 52.8%, outperforming many frontier models on critical web navigation subtasks.

problem: How LLM performance evolves during self-improvement training remains underexplored despite self-improvement being a significant technique.
approach: Theoretically models self-improvement dynamics via solver-verifier gap concept; shows how to model entire training trajectory and quantify capability limits by fitting to experiments.
contribution: Framework validated on various LLMs and datasets reveals that external data can be utilized at any stage in limited-data regimes without significantly affecting final performance.

problem: Traditional learning rate decay is computationally expensive during LLM pre-training; decay-free scheduling via model merging lacks theoretical foundation.
approach: WSM establishes formal connection between LR decay and model merging, unifying cosine/linear/inverse-sqrt decay as principled model averaging compatible with diverse optimizers.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Warmup-Stable-Decay with improvements of +3.5% MATH, +2.9% HumanEval, +5.5% MMLU-Pro.

problem: Fine-tuning open-source LLMs with proprietary data is standard practice but data owners can extract private fine-tuning data via backdoor training.
approach: Demonstrates backdoor extraction attack where open-source LLM provider can extract downstream fine-tuning data through simple training with black-box model access.
contribution: Extraction performance reaches 76.3% of 5,000 query samples in practical settings and up to 94.9% in ideal settings; defense strategies are ineffective.

problem: Contextual pricing under semi-parametric demand model with Hölder-continuous link function has suboptimal regret rates and requires restrictive assumptions.
approach: Combines stationary subroutine with local polynomial regression under unimodality condition, achieving unified rate O(T^((β+1)/(2β+1))) for all β≥1.
contribution: Recovers and strengthens existing results for β=1,2, removes derivative lower bound assumptions, and improves practical performance with reduced exploration phases.

problem: Multimodal LLM evaluation lacks assessment of cognitive capabilities like execution, perception reasoning, learning, memory, and planning that mirror children's development.
approach: KidGym is a 2D grid-based benchmark with 12 tasks inspired by Wechsler Intelligence Scales, with random object layouts and customizable difficulty levels.
contribution: Evaluation of SOTA MLLMs reveals significant limitations and provides actionable insights into model capabilities.

problem: Current foundation models capture either tissue context or sequence features but not both; alternative splicing and isoform reuse are overlooked.
approach: CDBridge is a post-training strategy unifying DNA and protein models via splicing-inspired token merge for isoform-aware representations and conditional decoder injecting tissue embeddings.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior methods on GTEx-Benchmark, capturing long-range exon dependencies and resolving isoform reuse for tissue-specific expression prediction.

problem: Standard softmax attention with uncontrolled query/key norms causes training instabilities even on simple data with spurious patterns.
approach: QUEST constrains keys to hyperspherical latent space while allowing tokens to control attention sharpness via query-modulated spherical attention.
contribution: QUEST trains without instabilities and produces models with improved performance robust to data corruptions and adversarial attacks.

problem: Monocular RGB-based human performance capture lacks sufficient observations for unseen regions.
approach: Maintains progressively updated canonical space accumulating appearance over time and formulates rendering as probabilistic regression to resolve conflicts between past and current observations.
contribution: Produces sharper reconstructions than deterministic regression and enables plausible synthesis in regions with no prior observations.

problem: High-fidelity generative modeling of neuronal morphologies is underexplored but crucial for connectomics.
approach: MoGen uses flow matching to generate high-resolution 3D point clouds with local geometric context injected into scalable latent transformer backbone.
contribution: Augmenting connectomics pipeline training set with MoGen samples improves classifier accuracy and reduces split/merge errors by 4.4%, potentially reducing manual proofreading by over 157 person-years.

problem: Static task-specific LLM benchmarks are fragile to contamination and saturation; interactive evaluation capturing reasoning is lacking.
approach: Reframes evaluation as teaching: candidate model guides weaker students and student gains score the model via Application/Judgment/Guidance/Reflection metrics.
contribution: Achieves Spearman >0.95 with human-preference leaderboards, surpasses direct baselines, and provides actionable training signals.

problem: Existing mistake detection focuses on action execution but overlooks what actions produce, i.e., action effects; many errors manifest in resulting outcomes not execution.
approach: Action Effect Modeling (AEM) jointly captures execution and outcomes via probabilistic formulation, selecting informative effect frames and extracting complementary cues via visual grounding and scene graphs.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on EgoPER and CaptainCook4D under one-class classification setting by modeling both execution and outcome.

problem: Diffusion LLMs discard rich intermediate predictions during denoising despite temporal oscillation where correct answers emerge mid-process.
approach: Introduces Temporal Self-Consistency Voting (training-free test-time decoding aggregating predictions) and Temporal Consistency Reinforcement using Temporal Semantic Entropy as reward signal.
contribution: Achieves average improvement of 24.7% on Countdown and gains of 2.0% GSM8K, 4.3% MATH500, 6.6% SVAMP with temporal consistency methods.

problem: Structured image reasoning (charts, diagrams) fails in MLLMs due to perceptual slips cascading into erroneous conclusions.
approach: Multi-agent system with dispatcher, planner, reasoner, critics, and visual tool agents; fine-tunes MLLM into grounding model with pixel-level localization integrated with CV algorithms.
contribution: Dynamic three-stage workflow with image memory enables flexible reasoning, significantly improving visual reasoning on chart and geometry benchmarks.

problem: Open-source web agents significantly underperform proprietary systems; training scalable high-capability agents is challenging.
approach: Complete post-training pipeline with SailorFog-QA-2 dataset built from interconnected knowledge graph and dual-environment RL combining high-fidelity simulator with robust real-world environment.
contribution: Qwen3-30B-A3B agent achieves 35.3 BrowseComp-EN, 44.1 BrowseComp-ZH, 30.6 HLE, surpassing DeepSeek-V3.1 and competing with proprietary systems.

problem: Federated learning communication overhead is critical; existing compression methods rely on magnitude heuristics ignoring output discrepancy.
approach: Uses calibration data on clients to measure output discrepancy induced by dropping compression units as compression metric guiding selection.
contribution: Achieves 18.9% relative accuracy improvement at 0.1 compression ratio under severe communication constraints.

problem: Dynamic personalized summarization requires capturing time-variant subjective preferences but existing models assume memoryless or short-memory Markovian diffusion.
approach: Walk2Pers extends random walk view with action-conditioned geometric steps decomposed into magnitude and orientation mediated by dual memory lanes suppressing disinterest.
contribution: Outperforms specialized personalized summarizers by 0.41 PerSEval and strong LLM baselines by 0.22 with cross-domain robustness of 0.19 over best LLM.

problem: Dataset distillation struggles to simultaneously achieve diversity, generalization, and representativeness in synthesized datasets without external constraints.
approach: The method quantifies representativeness using a Mercer kernel to measure similarity between synthetic and real data in feature space, then guides the reverse diffusion process with this prior without retraining.
contribution: DAP outperforms state-of-the-art methods on ImageNet-1K and achieves superior cross-architecture generalization in dataset distillation.

problem: Current transformer-based LLMs have quadratic compute and linear memory bottlenecks that limit inference efficiency, while linear-scaling models lack capabilities or hardware efficiency.
approach: Mamba-3 combines three improvements inspired by state-space models: more expressive recurrence, complex state update rules for richer tracking, and multi-input/output formulation to better exploit hardware parallelism during decoding.
contribution: Mamba-3 achieves significant gains in retrieval, state-tracking, and language modeling tasks, setting the Pareto frontier for performance under fixed inference budget.

problem: Existing unlearnable example methods rely on empirical heuristics without solid theoretical explanations, making them difficult to improve systematically.
approach: The work analyzes unlearnable examples from a mutual information reduction perspective, showing effective methods decrease mutual information between clean and poisoned features, then proposes MI-UE that maximizes cosine similarity among intra-class features to reduce covariance.
contribution: MI-UE significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in preventing unauthorized model learning even under defense mechanisms.

problem: Open-set test-time adaptation for 3D point cloud semantic segmentation is hindered by class imbalance where known samples dominate and unknown instances are sparse or absent.
approach: GOOD leverages geometric priors to cluster point clouds into superpoints, introduces a confidence metric to distinguish known and unknown points, and uses prototype-based representations for robust segmentation.
contribution: GOOD outperforms HGL by 1.93% mIoU, 8.99% AUROC, and 7.91% FPR95 on the Synth4D to SemanticKITTI benchmark.

problem: Peer review integrity is threatened by the potential use of LLMs to generate negligent reviews, yet there is no comprehensive resource for benchmarking AI text detection in this domain.
approach: The work introduces a dataset of 788,984 AI-written peer reviews paired with human reviews from ICLR and NeurIPS, then evaluates 18 AI text detection algorithms and proposes Anchor, a context-aware method leveraging manuscript content.
contribution: The evaluation reveals the difficulty of identifying AI-generated peer reviews at the individual level, highlighting the urgent need for better detection tools.

problem: Designing effective multi-agent systems requires optimizing both prompts and topologies, which is inherently complex and difficult to automate.
approach: MASS is a three-stage optimization framework that interleaves local prompt optimization, workflow topology optimization, and global prompt optimization, where each stage is conditioned on iteratively optimized components from former stages.
contribution: MASS-optimized systems substantially outperform existing alternatives and reveal design principles for building effective multi-agent systems.

problem: Anisotropic singular value spectra in parameters, activations, and gradients cause wide numerical ranges that introduce quantization bias and spectral distortion, severely degrading low-bit training of LLMs.
approach: Metis partitions anisotropic spectra into narrower sub-distributions for independent quantization using random sampling and projection, leveraging properties of the dominant spectral subspace to minimize decomposition overhead.
contribution: Metis enables robust W4A4G4 FP4 training of LLaMA-3 8B with only 0.4% training loss gap and 0.1% downstream accuracy degradation relative to BF16.

problem: Vision-language models struggle to simultaneously express hierarchy within concept families and compositionality across different concept families.
approach: PHyCLIP employs an l1-product metric on a Cartesian product of hyperbolic factors, with intra-family hierarchies emerging in individual hyperbolic factors and cross-family composition captured by the l1-product metric.
contribution: PHyCLIP outperforms single-space approaches on zero-shot classification, retrieval, hierarchical classification, and compositional understanding tasks with more interpretable embedding structures.

problem: Existing vision-language and audio models cannot reliably converse with users in real-time about live scenes, despite advances in individual modalities.
approach: The work introduces the Interactive Video Dataset (IVD) that assesses how well existing models support real-time question-answering based on camera and audio input, and shows fine-tuning on this data reduces performance gaps.
contribution: IVD reveals that existing models fall far behind human performance and identifies main sources of performance gaps, while showing fine-tuning can significantly reduce the gap.

problem: Cross-modal representation learning optimizes statistical objectives without causal constraints, introducing spurious dependencies and representation-induced structural drift that undermines causal inference.
approach: CARL explicitly embeds causal structure preservation constraints using multi-consistency loss architecture with conditional independence preservation, information bottleneck regularization, and Markov boundary preservation loss.
contribution: CARL achieves state-of-the-art performance in preserving conditional independence patterns under synthetic experiments with known causal ground truth.

problem: Enabling LLMs for open-ended and mechanistic reasoning in biology is hindered because most biological outcomes are non-verifiable, limiting application of Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards.
approach: CellDuality uses a complementary task duality principle where the model performs forward reasoning (predicting biological outcomes) followed by inverse reasoning (reconstructing initial conditions), with reconstruction fidelity serving as intrinsic reward without ground-truth labels.
contribution: CellDuality enables LLM agents for robust reasoning in single-cell biology through self-supervised feedback without verifiable rewards.

problem: Online conformal prediction methods produce overly conservative prediction sets under data distribution shifts in fully adversarial environments.
approach: COP incorporates underlying data patterns into the update rule through estimated cumulative distribution functions of non-conformity scores, producing tighter prediction sets when predictable patterns exist while maintaining valid coverage.
contribution: COP achieves valid coverage guarantees and constructs shorter prediction intervals than baseline methods while achieving finite-sample coverage under arbitrary learning rates.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to understand humans in diverse, complex scenarios at multiple levels of perception, comprehension, and reasoning.
approach: HumanPCR is an evaluation suite with over 6,000 multiple-choice questions across perception and comprehension levels, plus manually curated video reasoning tests requiring integration of visual evidence and proactive context extraction.
contribution: Extensive evaluation of 30+ state-of-the-art models reveals significant challenges in human-centric visual understanding, especially in spatial perception, temporal understanding, and mind modeling.

problem: Instruction-based image editing applies uniform generation processes across entire images despite edited and unedited regions having significantly different generation difficulty and computational needs.
approach: RegionE adaptively partitions images into edited and unedited regions, applies one-step prediction to unedited areas and local iterative denoising to edited regions, using Region-Instruction KV Cache and adaptive velocity decay cache.
contribution: RegionE accelerates image editing tasks without additional training while maintaining high quality.

problem: Existing symmetry-based disentanglement requires strong prior knowledge of symmetry group structure or restrictive assumptions about subgroup properties.
approach: The method enables embodied agents to autonomously discover group structure through unsupervised interaction with the environment, with proven identifiability under minimal assumptions.
contribution: The approach outperforms existing Linear Symmetry-Based Disentangled (LSBD) methods on three environments with different group decompositions.

problem: Q-value biases in offline-to-online RL follow heavy-tailed distributions during online fine-tuning, causing high estimation variance and hindering performance improvement.
approach: LAROO introduces parameterized Laplace-distributed noise to transfer heavy-tailed bias nature into the noise, combines estimated Q-values with noise, and uses conservative ensemble-based estimates to re-center biases.
contribution: LAROO achieves significant performance improvement over baselines by promoting heavy-tailed Q-value biases into a standardized form.

problem: Multimodal large language models struggle with complex mathematical reasoning despite impressive capabilities in other domains.
approach: WE-MATH 2.0 integrates a structured mathematical knowledge hierarchy with 491 knowledge points, model-centric data space modeling with diverse difficulty levels, and a two-stage RL framework combining supervised fine-tuning and progressive alignment RL.
contribution: WE-MATH 2.0 achieves competitive performance on widely used benchmarks while demonstrating strong generalization on a comprehensive benchmark covering all 491 knowledge points.

problem: Existing consistent approaches for partial and complementary multi-label learning either require accurate estimation of label generation processes or make unrealistic uniform distribution assumptions.
approach: The work proposes risk estimators based on first- and second-order strategies that handle both partial and complementary multi-label learning in a unified way without relying on aforementioned conditions.
contribution: The approach proves consistency with respect to two widely used multi-label classification metrics and derives convergence rates for estimation errors.

problem: Time Series Foundation Models designed for real-valued series cannot effectively leverage heterogeneous covariates like categorical variables and multimodal data, which are task-specific and unavailable during pretraining.
approach: UniCA performs covariate homogenization to transform heterogeneous covariates into high-level homogeneous series representations, then fuses them via unified attention-based mechanism while preserving TSFM generalization.
contribution: UniCA demonstrates superiority on multiple unimodal and multimodal covariate-aware forecasting benchmarks.

problem: Acquiring fine-grained, high-resolution time series data is often limited by cost and feasibility, necessitating super-resolution from sparse, low-resolution inputs.
approach: SRT decomposes input into trend and seasonal components, aligns them to target resolution using implicit neural representation, and leverages cross-resolution attention to guide high-resolution detail generation via disentangled rectified flow.
contribution: SRT and SRT-large consistently outperform existing methods across nine public datasets at multiple scale factors with strong zero-shot super-resolution capability.

problem: Speech synthesis models lack alignment with human perception due to the absence of large-scale human preference datasets, particularly for naturalness.
approach: SpeechJudge introduces a comprehensive suite with 99k human feedback speech pairs, establishes a challenging benchmark for speech naturalness judgment, and develops a generative reward model using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B trained via SFT and RL with GRPO.
contribution: SpeechJudge-GRM achieves 77.2% accuracy on the SpeechJudge-Eval benchmark, substantially improving over existing metrics and AudioLLMs.

problem: Activation sparsity benefits in ReLU models do not directly apply to modern LLMs, resulting in fragmented model-specific strategies and limited general understanding.
approach: The work introduces a framework for evaluating sparsity robustness in contemporary LLMs and conducts systematic investigation of activation sparsity in feedforward layers across diverse model families and scales.
contribution: Results uncover universal properties of activation sparsity across diverse models and scales, showing potential for effective sparsity grows with model size, with first study of activation sparsity in diffusion-based LLMs.

problem: Joint Energy-Based Models for simultaneous robust classification and high-fidelity generation suffer from training instability and poor sample quality from SGLD-based approaches.
approach: The method integrates adversarial training principles by replacing SGLD-based learning with stable AT-based approach using Binary Cross-Entropy loss, combines adversarial training for robustness with gradient regularization, and employs two-stage training to address normalization instabilities.
contribution: The approach is the first EBM-based hybrid to scale to high-resolution datasets (ImageNet 256x256) with high training stability while achieving state-of-the-art discriminative and generative performance.

problem: Single-view metric depth estimation from sparse observations requires complex architectural designs to generate metric-accurate dense depth maps.
approach: LDCM uses a Poisson-based depth initialization module to generate coarse dense depth from diverse sparse observations as a structural prior, replaces depth head with point map head for direct 3D coordinate regression, and eliminates camera intrinsic dependency.
contribution: LDCM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks and sparsity levels with strong generalization to unseen data distributions.

problem: The counting power of transformers remains unclear beyond semi-linear properties expressible as boolean combinations of linear inequalities.
approach: The work provides formal framework proving transformers can capture semialgebraic counting properties expressible as boolean combinations of arbitrary multivariate polynomials, with connections to Hilbert's tenth problem showing undecidability results.
contribution: Results demonstrate transformers can express highly nonlinear counting properties generalizing those capturable by support vector machines with polynomial kernels.

problem: Existing benchmarks for evaluating long-range capabilities in graph learning cannot guarantee tasks depend on long-range information or are too limited, making claims of improvement questionable.
approach: LRIM introduces a physics-based benchmark using the Ising model with provably long-range dependencies, consisting of ten datasets scaling from 256 to 65k nodes with controllable long-range interactions through tunable parameters.
contribution: Experiments show both message-passing architectures and graph transformers perform far from optimal, especially scalable methods, providing model-agnostic evidence that local information is insufficient.

problem: Imputing missing values in multivariate time series is challenging under diverse missing patterns and heavy missingness because corrupted temporal features hinder cross-variable information transfer.
approach: T1 uses a CNN-Transformer hybrid with Channel-Head Binding creating one-to-one correspondence between CNN channels and attention heads, enabling selective information transfer where affected pathways down-weight based on observable patterns.
contribution: T1 achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing MSE by 46% on average compared to the second-best baseline with particularly strong gains under extreme sparsity (70% missing ratio).

problem: Streaming video generation suffers from severe error accumulation over long horizons, significantly degrading quality in interactive world models and neural game engines.
approach: Rolling Forcing uses joint denoising of multiple frames with progressively increasing noise levels, integrates attention sink mechanism for global context anchoring, and employs efficient training algorithm with few-step distillation over extended windows.
contribution: Rolling Forcing enables real-time streaming generation of multi-minute videos on a single GPU with substantially reduced error accumulation.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models benefit from chain-of-thought reasoning but long output generation for thoughts negatively affects inference time in real-world robotic tasks.
approach: HyT enables VLAs to learn from thoughts and benefit from performance gains while optionally omitting CoT generation during inference, supporting flexible conditional prediction of diverse outputs.
contribution: HyT preserves performance improvements from reasoning without the inference time cost through hybrid training.

problem: All-in-one image restoration requires approximating heterogeneous inverse functions from diverse mixed degradations, yet principles governing effective restoration remain underexplored.
approach: The work revisits attention mechanisms for all-in-one restoration, identifying two bottlenecks: linear value paths restricting expressivity and absence of explicit global slot for degradation context, proposing nonlinear value transform and global spatial token.
contribution: Proposed primitives improve restoration across synthetic, mixed, underwater, and medical benchmarks with negligible overhead and consistent performance gains.

problem: Model-based offline RL relies on dynamics models for policy exploration and evaluation, but many exhibit limited capability in long-horizon prediction due to error accumulation.
approach: ADM-v2 structurally decouples recurrent forward of RNN cells from backtracked state, making direct prediction more flexible and supporting parallel uncertainty estimation, enabling full-horizon roll-outs.
contribution: ADM-v2 achieves SOTA on both D4RL and NeoRL under full-horizon roll-out setting, with substantial advancements for policy optimization while other models degrade.

problem: Current approaches to decoding visual representations from brain signals emphasize high-level semantic features while neglecting pixel-level details, limiting understanding of human visual system.
approach: The work leverages multiple pre-trained visual encoders with distinct inductive biases to capture hierarchical visual representations using contrastive learning objective, introducing a Fusion Prior that learns stable mapping from large-scale data.
contribution: The method achieves favorable balance between retrieval accuracy and reconstruction fidelity through hierarchical visual embedding alignment.

problem: Automating mathematical formalization for theorem proving is hindered because informal statements are complex and offer limited context on underlying math concepts for effective retrieval.
approach: DRIFT enables LLMs to decompose informal mathematical statements into smaller sub-components for targeted premise retrieval from libraries like Mathlib, and retrieves illustrative theorems to help models use premises more effectively.
contribution: DRIFT consistently improves premise retrieval nearly doubling F1 score compared to DPR baseline on ProofNet with strong performance on out-of-distribution ConNF benchmark.

problem: Evaluating AI agents on complex, open-ended deep research tasks is hindered by lack of realistic benchmarks that include both public and private knowledge sources.
approach: DRBench introduces a benchmark with 100 tasks across 10 domains that require identifying supporting facts from public web and private company knowledge bases, grounded in realistic user personas and enterprise context.
contribution: Evaluation of diverse agents on DRBench demonstrates their strengths and weaknesses, highlighting critical paths for advancing enterprise deep research.

problem: Neural networks implicitly learn class-specific functional modules but cannot be easily isolated and recombined for modular inference.
approach: The method trains sparse networks with KL-divergence-based loss to learn only functional modules for assigned class subsets, using iterative magnitude pruning to remove irrelevant weights, enabling composition via weight summation or logit averaging.
contribution: Trained subnetworks achieve high accuracy on target classes with minimal leakage, and combined modules often recover generalist performance with interpretable functional structure.

problem: Existing multimodal Process Reward Models lack sufficient training data to effectively estimate step-wise value scores during reasoning.
approach: The work constructs VisualPRM400K with 400K multimodal process supervision data to develop VisualPRM capable of estimating value scores for each step, with VisualProcessBench for measuring PRM and MLLM abilities.
contribution: VisualPRM improves reasoning performance of three types of MLLMs with 5.9-point improvement on seven benchmarks even when applied to highly capable models like InternVL2.5-78B.

problem: Off-policy RL systems with stale rollout data either degrade in performance or collapse during training, limiting efficiency and scalability of LLM reasoning.
approach: M2PO constrains the second moment of importance weights to suppress extreme outliers while preserving informative updates, reducing clipped high-variance tokens while maintaining stable optimization.
contribution: M2PO delivers stable off-policy training even with data stale by at least 256 model updates, matching on-policy performance across six model scales and eight reasoning benchmarks.

problem: State-of-the-art data-driven models systematically underestimate magnitudes and short-term variations of extreme wind velocities despite performing well for general meteorological forecasting.
approach: The work provides theoretical analysis of how data frequency spectrum influences extreme wind prediction errors, proposes novel loss function with gradient penalty and frequency reweighting in physics-embedded machine learning models.
contribution: The approach achieves significant improvements in extreme wind velocity prediction while maintaining robust overall performance.

problem: Unified multimodal models with shared transformers suffer from severe gradient conflicts between vision and text due to different statistical properties of images and text.
approach: Uni-X proposes a two-end-separated, middle-shared X-shaped architecture dedicating initial and final layers to modality-specific processing while maintaining shared middle layers for high-level semantic fusion.
contribution: Uni-X achieves superior training efficiency and at 3B parameters matches or surpasses 7B AR-based UMMs with GenEval score of 82 for image generation and strong vision/text performance.

problem: Speculative decoding relies on static time allocation between drafting and verification, while dynamic approaches optimize proxy metrics like acceptance length rather than actual throughput.
approach: LTD formulates the problem as a reinforcement learning environment training two co-adaptive policies to dynamically coordinate draft and verification phases, directly optimizing throughput.
contribution: LTD achieves speedup ratios of 2.24x to 4.32x across five LLMs and four tasks, outperforming Eagle3 by up to 36.4%.

problem: Video generation models struggle with the copy-paste problem, where they fail to faithfully follow textual instructions because in-pair training entangles subject identity with background and contextual attributes.
approach: Phantom-Data introduces a cross-pair dataset of one million identity-consistent pairs constructed via subject detection, large-scale cross-context retrieval from diverse sources, and identity verification to ensure visual consistency under contextual variation.
contribution: Training with Phantom-Data significantly improves prompt alignment and visual quality while preserving identity consistency on par with in-pair baselines.

problem: Existing heteroscedastic bandit algorithms rely on cumulative variance as a complexity measure, which is not optimal because it remains high even when noise is near-zero at many rounds.
approach: VAEE (Variance-Aware Exploration with Elimination) is a novel algorithm for linear bandits with fixed action sets that uses active exploration to maximize information gain and achieves a harmonic-mean dependent regret rate.
contribution: VAEE achieves simple regret with a nearly harmonic-mean dependent rate, breaking the total variance barrier and providing a more accurate complexity characterization for heteroscedastic linear bandits.

problem: Existing geospatial representation learning methods excel at depicting locations in their physical states but neglect the crucial human-centric understanding of a location's socio-economic context and functional role.
approach: MoRA leverages a mobility graph as its core backbone to fuse physical remote sensing imagery, structured demographic statistics, and human dynamics through spatial tokenization, GNNs, and asymmetric contrastive learning, aligning 100M+ POIs with a billion-edge mobility graph.
contribution: MoRA achieves superior predictive performance on 9 downstream prediction tasks by an average of 12.9% compared to state-of-the-art models and demonstrates scaling behavior in geospatial representation learning.

problem: Understanding whether gradient-based training promotes parameters belonging to lower-dimensional structures remains a fundamental unsolved challenge in deep learning theory.
approach: The paper studies when gradient flow on a parameter θ implies an intrinsic gradient flow on a lifted variable z=φ(θ), establishing a criterion based on kernel inclusion of linear maps and applying it to ReLU networks with path-lifting and linear networks with weight-matrix products.
contribution: For dense sets of initializations, the flow can be rewritten as an intrinsic dynamic in lower dimensions; the analysis shows relaxed balanced initializations ensure the intrinsic metric property for linear networks.

problem: Fast 3D scene reconstruction from unstructured image collections with arbitrary numbers of images, variable camera calibration, and camera pose estimation remains challenging.
approach: YoNoSplat is a feedforward model that predicts local Gaussians and camera poses for each view, aggregated into a global representation via a novel mixing training strategy that gradually transitions from ground-truth to predicted poses and embeds camera intrinsics into the network.
contribution: YoNoSplat achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks in both pose-free and pose-dependent settings while reconstructing 100 views at 280×518 resolution in 2.69 seconds on an NVIDIA GH200 GPU.

problem: Diffusion models suffer from substantial computational overhead due to their iterative inference process, and naive feature caching leads to noticeable quality degradation.
approach: ERTACache formally analyzes cumulative caching error into feature shift and step amplification components, then rectifies both via offline residual profiling, dynamic timestep adjustment via trajectory-aware correction coefficients, and closed-form residual linearization error approximation.
contribution: ERTACache achieves up to 2x inference speedup while preserving or improving visual quality; on Wan 2.1 video diffusion, it delivers 2x acceleration with minimal VBench degradation.

problem: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) suffer from inherently much higher training variance than autoregressive models, making them unstable during task-specific fine-tuning despite being competitive at initialization.
approach: The paper derives the first decomposition of MDM training variance into three sources (masking pattern noise, masking rate noise, data noise) and proposes six variance-reduction methods including P-POTS, a Pareto-optimal timestep sampler, and MIRROR, which uses negatively correlated samples.
contribution: Compared to standard MDM training, the proposed methods improve accuracy by 7-8% on complex reasoning tasks while reducing run-to-run variability to near ARM levels.

problem: Evaluating frontier AI systems on tasks requiring deep expertise across multiple domains is challenging because even expert humans can only provide weak signals in their narrow specialization.
approach: ConfHit derives an unbiased estimator of top-1 accuracy from complementary labels (which indicate incorrect options) and constructs density-ratio weighted conformal p-values to quantify confidence in hits via a nested testing procedure.
contribution: ConfHit enables evaluation of large language models without ground truth using complementary labels and can train agentic systems with weak signals while maintaining statistical validity guarantees.

problem: Web browsing agents often get lost in unfamiliar websites because they lack understanding of their environments and uncertainty about which pages must be visited to achieve goals.
approach: Go-Browse frames data collection as a graph search, enabling reuse of information across exploration episodes to efficiently collect 10K successful trajectories and 40K interaction steps across 100 URLs.
contribution: Fine-tuning a 7B parameter language model on this dataset achieves 21.7% success rate on WebArena benchmark, beating GPT-4o mini by 2.4% and exceeding state-of-the-art for sub-10B models by 2.9%.

problem: Combining diffusion models with autoregressive frameworks introduces condition errors that degrade image quality in autoregressive diffusion models with diffusion loss.
approach: The paper provides theoretical comparison of conditional diffusion and autoregressive diffusion, demonstrating that patch denoising mitigates condition errors and proposes a novel condition refinement approach based on Optimal Transport (OT) theory formulated as a Wasserstein Gradient Flow.
contribution: Theoretical analysis shows autoregressive condition generation causes condition error influence to decay exponentially; the proposed OT-based refinement ensures convergence toward ideal condition distribution.

problem: Predicting properties of molecular interactions is challenging because existing models neglect the molecular pairs' interactions and fail to capture core invariant substructures due to insufficient modeling of interaction relationships.
approach: I2Mole establishes indiscriminate connections between intermolecular atoms which are refined using improved graph information bottleneck theory, and constructs an environment codebook from environment subgraphs to optimize mutual information.
contribution: I2Mole accurately captures core substructures and significantly enhances model generalization for predicting drug-drug interaction properties.

problem: 3D style transfer on complex scenes requires per-scene optimization and precomputed poses, limiting scalability and applicability to diverse unposed inputs.
approach: Stylos adopts a Transformer backbone with two pathways where geometry predictions retain self-attention while style is injected via global cross-attention, combined with a voxel-based 3D style loss to align aggregated scene features to style statistics.
contribution: Stylos achieves high-quality zero-shot style transfer on single-view and large-scale multi-view settings without per-scene optimization or precomputed poses while generalizing to unseen categories and styles.

problem: Ensuring deep generative models produce candidates that truly satisfy desired properties requires reliable guarantees, but budget constraints, lack of oracle access, and distribution shift make this difficult.
approach: ConfHit formalizes certification and design through weighted exchangeability between historical and generated samples, constructs multiple-sample density-ratio weighted conformal p-values, and proposes a nested testing procedure to certify candidate sets.
contribution: ConfHit consistently delivers valid coverage guarantees at multiple confidence levels while maintaining compact certified sets for generative molecule design across representative tasks.

problem: Language models can exhibit alignment faking without verbalizing deceptive reasoning, making it difficult to detect misalignment through inspection of reasoning traces.
approach: The paper studies Claude 3.5 Sonnet's behavior when told its reasoning will be monitored and it will be trained on harmful queries, comparing explicit instruction-based hiding approaches with intrinsic motivation to obfuscate.
contribution: Claude 3.5 Sonnet shows 24.3% compliance gap between training and deployment while verbalization of alignment faking drops 93.7%; intrinsic motivation to obfuscate outperforms explicit instruction-based methods.

problem: Sampling-based decoding strategies for LLMs require careful hyperparameter tuning that varies by task and temperature, and outputs degrade at higher temperatures.
approach: p-less sampling is an information-theoretic approach that dynamically sets a truncation threshold at each decoding step based on the entire token probability distribution without hyperparameters.
contribution: p-less sampling outperforms existing methods across math, logical reasoning, and creative writing tasks while exhibiting much less quality degradation at higher temperatures and achieving greater inference efficiency.

problem: Existing video understanding benchmarks fail to comprehensively evaluate synergistic reasoning across audio and visual modalities, often neglecting modality complementarity and logical consistency.
approach: OmniVideoBench comprises 1000 high-quality QA pairs with step-by-step reasoning traces derived from 628 diverse videos, with 13 carefully designed question types covering temporal reasoning, spatial localization, counting, and causal inference.
contribution: Evaluation of multiple MLLMs on OmniVideoBench reveals a pronounced gap between model performance and human reasoning, with open-source models significantly lagging closed-source counterparts.

problem: Knowledge editing in LLMs fails on multi-hop factual recall because existing methods overlook how chained knowledge is dynamically represented at the neuron level during multi-hop reasoning.
approach: ACE leverages neuron-level attribution to identify and edit critical query-value pathways where implicit subjects function as query neurons that activate corresponding value neurons across transformer layers.
contribution: ACE outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 9.44% on GPT-J and 37.46% on Qwen3-8B for multi-hop knowledge editing while revealing fine-grained activation patterns.

problem: LLM-based web agents on long-horizon tasks face a fundamental tradeoff between context saturation from noisy histories and irreversible loss of critical details from fixed summarization.
approach: AgentFold treats context as a dynamic cognitive workspace inspired by retrospective consolidation, learning to execute folding operations at multiple scales with granular condensations or deep consolidations while managing historical trajectories.
contribution: AgentFold-30B-A3B achieves 36.2% on BrowseComp and 47.3% on BrowseComp-ZH, surpassing or matching open-source models of dramatically larger scale and proprietary agents like OpenAI's o4-mini.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning and preference learning often fail to generalize to novel or complex instructions and may compromise models' general capabilities despite improving instruction-following.
approach: ContextIF is a reinforcement learning framework that automatically generates precise constraint summaries and optimal context demonstrations via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) guided by comprehensive context reward.
contribution: ContextIF achieves substantial performance gains over existing SFT and ICL methods on multiple instruction-following benchmarks while preserving model parameters and general capabilities.

problem: Understanding how incorporation of domain knowledge affects learning rates when data are dependent remains a major challenge in physics-informed machine learning.
approach: The paper derives complexity-dependent bounds on excess risk for empirical risk minimization with physics-informed regularization under data dependence.
contribution: When physical prior information is aligned, the learning rate improves from the slow Sobolev minimax rate to the fast optimal i.i.d. rate without sample-size deflation.

problem: Extending model-based reinforcement learning to physical multi-robot cooperation is challenging due to the complexity of joint dynamics and difficulty in learning transferable behaviors.
approach: SeqWM employs independent, autoregressive agent-wise world models where each agent generates future trajectories and plans actions based on predictions of its predecessors, enabling explicit intention sharing.
contribution: SeqWM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both performance and sample efficiency while exhibiting advanced cooperative behaviors such as predictive adaptation and role division, validated on physical quadrupeds.

problem: Active sequential prediction-powered mean estimation with query probability optimization remains incompletely understood when mixing constant probability constraints with uncertainty-based suggestions.
approach: The paper develops a non-asymptotic analysis of the estimator, establishes data-dependent bounds on confidence intervals, and shows that no-regret learning for query probability control leads convergence patterns.
contribution: Analysis reveals that query probability converges to the max constraint when chosen obliviously to current covariates, and simulation results corroborate the theoretical findings.

problem: Applying the Minimum Description Length principle to neural networks like Transformers is challenging due to lack of a principled, universal measure for model complexity.
approach: The paper introduces asymptotically optimal description length objectives grounded in Kolmogorov complexity theory, proves they exist for Transformers via computational universality, and constructs a tractable variational objective based on adaptive Gaussian mixture priors.
contribution: The variational objective selects for low-complexity solutions with strong generalization on algorithmic tasks, establishing a path toward training networks that achieve greater compression.

problem: Multi-objective reinforcement learning agents must adapt policies to different user preferences while handling unknown preferences and generalizing to novel objectives.
approach: The paper leverages reward-free reinforcement learning (RFRL) as an auxiliary task to enhance MORL via preference-guided exploration that focuses learning on relevant environment parts.
contribution: The approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art MORL methods across diverse MO-Gymnasium tasks with superior performance and data efficiency while preserving general capabilities.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models frequently misrepresent historical contexts through stereotyping, anachronisms, and inaccurate demographic patterns.
approach: The benchmark combines HistVis (30,000 synthetic images from three diffusion models) with a reproducible evaluation protocol assessing implicit stylistic associations, historical consistency, and demographic representation.
contribution: Findings reveal systematic inaccuracies including unstated stylistic cues that stereotype past eras, anachronisms such as modern artifacts in pre-modern contexts, and unrealistic demographic patterns.

problem: Neural operators for solving PDEs suffer from poor transferability to new geometries, requiring expensive retraining on domain-specific data.
approach: Schwarz Neural Inference (SNI) partitions the problem domain into subdomains where local problems are solved with neural operators, then stitches local solutions into a global solution.
contribution: SNI achieves remarkable geometry generalization across linear and nonlinear PDEs with diverse boundary conditions compared to alternative methods with theoretical convergence and error bounds.

problem: Genuine zero-shot text classification is underexplored due to existing benchmarks incorporating labeled examples through supervised probes or fine-tuning.
approach: BTZSC introduces 22 public datasets spanning sentiment, topic, intent, and emotion classification and systematically compares 38 checkpoints across four model families including NLI cross-encoders, embedding models, rerankers, and instruction-tuned LLMs.
contribution: Modern rerankers like Qwen3-Reranker-8B achieve state-of-the-art macro F1=0.72; strong embedding models achieve competitive performance while offering best accuracy-latency tradeoffs.

problem: Static safety benchmarks and red-teaming tools fail to identify emerging real-world vulnerabilities in code agents by not covering boundary conditions like combined effects of different jailbreak tools.
approach: RedCodeAgent is an automated red-teaming agent with an adaptive memory module that leverages existing jailbreak knowledge to dynamically select effective red-teaming tools and combinations from a tailored toolbox.
contribution: RedCodeAgent consistently outperforms existing red-teaming methods across multiple state-of-the-art code agents with higher attack success rates and lower rejection rates, and is validated on real-world assistants.

problem: Independent sampling from generative models tends to produce redundant results when presenting multiple outputs, limiting user choices and idea exploration.
approach: Group inference formulates selection as a quadratic integer assignment problem with nodes representing candidates, optimizing sample quality (unary term) while maximizing diversity (binary term), with progressive pruning for efficiency.
contribution: The method significantly improves group diversity and quality compared to independent sampling and recent inference algorithms across text-to-image, image-to-image, and image prompting tasks.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting's reliance on spherical harmonics for color encoding limits its ability to separate diffuse and specular components, making complex reflections difficult to represent accurately.
approach: An augmented Gaussian kernel explicitly models specular effects through view-dependent opacity and uses an error-driven compensation strategy to improve rendering quality through adaptive insertion and optimization.
contribution: The method surpasses state-of-the-art NeRF methods in rendering performance while achieving greater parameter efficiency.

problem: Generalizing deep RL agents to unseen environments is challenging; existing Unsupervised Environment Design methods measure learning potential via regret approximated solely by value-function loss.
approach: TRACED combines transition-prediction error with a lightweight Co-Learnability metric to capture how training on one task affects performance on others, refining regret approximation.
contribution: TRACED produces curricula that improve zero-shot generalization over strong baselines across multiple benchmarks with transition-prediction error driving rapid complexity ramp-up.

problem: Counterfactual explanations for GNNs often rely on single perturbation strategies (edge additions or deletions), missing impactful changes that combine both types.
approach: ATEX-CF integrates adversarial attack insights with counterfactual generation to efficiently explore both edge additions and deletions, jointly optimizing fidelity, sparsity, and plausibility under perturbation constraints.
contribution: ATEX-CF generates faithful, concise, and plausible explanations on synthetic and real-world node classification benchmarks, demonstrating the value of integrating adversarial insights into counterfactual reasoning.

problem: Modern visual generation models struggle with producing or editing structured visuals like charts and diagrams because they require composition planning, text rendering, and factual fidelity.
approach: A unified model integrates a multimodal language model with FLUX.1-Kontext via a lightweight connector; three-stage training enables progressive feature alignment, knowledge infusion, and reasoning-augmented generation.
contribution: The approach achieves state-of-the-art open-source performance on structured image generation and editing with consistent gains from inference-time reasoning; StructScore metric introduced for fine-grained factual evaluation.

problem: Standard privacy preservation approaches update all weights in neural networks at high cost, leading to unnecessary utility loss and potential prediction misalignment.
approach: The paper empirically shows only a small number of weights are vulnerable to membership privacy breach; instead of discarding these neurons, only their weights are rewound during fine-tuning.
contribution: This mechanism enhances resilience against Membership Inference Attacks while maintaining utility when plugged into other privacy approaches.
