contribution: Covariance matching is optimal in some regimes; the theoretical insights for linear models carry over to deep neural networks, and covariance matching outperforms recent synthetic data selection approaches.

problem: Existing on-the-fly category discovery methods rely on hash-based encodings that overestimate the number of categories and suffer from hash function sensitivity.
approach: Reformulate OCD into open-set recognition and fully novel OCD; employ soft class thresholding for known classes and Adaptive Gaussian Expansion to dynamically model probability density functions for novel categories.
contribution: AGE achieves state-of-the-art performance in on-the-fly category discovery across multiple datasets with significantly improved real-time classification feasibility.

problem: Recent embedding models focus on data scaling or synthesis while neglecting systematic exploration of training techniques and data quality improvements.
approach: KaLM-Embedding-V2 implements a 0.5B model with bidirectional attention and proposes a progressive multi-stage training pipeline combining pre-training, fine-tuning, and contrastive distillation with focal reweighting and hard-negative mining.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, rivaling models 3-26× larger while being compact.

problem: Evaluating LLM-based agentic systems acting as co-scientists requires realistic end-to-end research scenarios integrating data analysis, interpretation, and new insights from experimental data.
approach: HeurekaBench creates benchmarks with exploratory, open-ended research questions grounded in scientific studies; uses a semi-automated pipeline with multiple LLMs to extract insights and verify against reported findings.
contribution: Enables quantitative end-to-end evaluation of scientific agents; shows adding a critic module improves ill-formed responses by up to 22%, setting a path toward rigorous agentic system evaluation.

problem: In-context learning under complex non-i.i.d. scenarios lacks theoretical understanding of which factors ensure generalization.
approach: Establish stability bounds for transformers trained with mini-batch gradient descent and introduce a distribution-level discrepancy measure; derive a generalization error bound for ICL with asymptotic convergence.
contribution: Reveals that token-wise prediction errors accumulate over time and can cause generalization collapse if length is unconstrained; provides theoretical guarantees for ICL generalization.

problem: Despite strong performance of test-time scaling methods like OpenAI's o1, the conditions in training data under which long chains-of-thought emerge and improve performance remain unclear.
approach: Study test-time scaling for transformers on an in-context weight prediction task for linear regression; analyze relationships between test-time compute, context length, and task difficulty.
contribution: Characterizes task hardness via the smallest eigenvalue of feature covariance; shows training on diverse, relevant, and hard tasks results in best test-time scaling performance.

problem: Existing learning-based feature upsamplers require re-training for every feature extractor and do not generalize to different feature types at inference time.
approach: AnyUp proposes an inference-time feature-agnostic upsampling architecture that can be applied to any vision feature at any resolution without encoder-specific training.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art upsampling performance, generalizes to different feature types, preserves feature semantics while being efficient for diverse downstream tasks.

problem: Existing protein generation models underutilize vast structural information in large-scale protein datasets; the challenge is how to exploit abundant unlabeled protein data using unsupervised pretraining.
approach: RigidSSL introduces rigidity-based pretraining using inertial frame canonicalization, combines large-scale perturbations with molecular dynamics views, and applies rigid-body flow matching with Invariant Point Attention.
contribution: RigidSSL learns stable, geometry-aware representations that improve downstream protein generation by better exploiting low-cost unlabeled protein datasets.

problem: Multi-objective flexible job shop scheduling problems remain underexplored in neural combinatorial optimization, limiting applicability in practical multi-criteria decision-making scenarios.
approach: Propose a decomposition-based NCO method with DCAN, a dual conditional attention network that takes objective preferences and learns adaptable policies; decompose MOFJSPs into subproblems with different preferences.
contribution: Outperforms traditional multi-objective optimization methods and generalizes well across diverse problem instances, enabling multi-criteria scheduling via neural methods.

problem: RL training of LLMs stalls on hard problems where the policy cannot generate rollouts with non-zero rewards, requiring better credit assignment.
approach: Interventional Training leverages single-step oracle interventions to provide language feedback on intermediate reasoning steps; patches the model via supervised fine-tuning on the on-policy rollout plus correction.
contribution: With approximately 100 oracle interventions, InT solves 16% more hard test problems previously unsolved and improves performance across multiple standard evaluations.

problem: Search agents trained via RL are limited by shallow tool-use depth and error accumulation over multiple iterative interactions.
approach: WebSeer introduces a self-reflection mechanism within RL training, constructs a large dataset annotated with reflection patterns, and uses a two-stage training framework unifying cold start and RL.
contribution: Using a single 14B model, achieves state-of-the-art results on HotpotQA (72.3% accuracy) and SimpleQA (90.0% accuracy) with strong generalization to out-of-distribution datasets.

problem: Conventional image codecs optimized for human vision are ill-suited for MLLMs, which have diverse downstream tasks with varying feature-level dependencies.
approach: CoTAM adaptively protects multi-level features by using CLIP's shallow-layer attention to generate importance maps; the decoder integrates a lightweight adapter with multi-level loss to preserve both low-level details and high-level semantics.
contribution: Achieves up to 35.99% bitrate saving while maintaining MLLM task performance, outperforming previous neural codecs.

problem: Research on state space models like Mamba for time series classification has remained limited, with insufficient benchmarking and reproducibility.
approach: MambaSL minimally redesigns the selective SSM and projection layers of a single-layer Mamba guided by four TSC-specific hypotheses; re-evaluates 20 baselines across all 30 UEA datasets under a unified protocol.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the UEA benchmark among 21 models with statistically significant improvements and reproducible public checkpoints.

problem: Applying diffusion models to CT reconstruction is challenging due to correlated noise, artifact structures, system geometry dependence, and misaligned value ranges not typical of natural image generation.
approach: DM4CT benchmarks nine diffusion-based methods alongside seven baselines including model-based and unsupervised approaches across medical and industrial CT datasets with sparse-view and noisy configurations.
contribution: Provides detailed insights into diffusion model behavior for CT reconstruction; a public real-world high-resolution synchrotron dataset enables rigorous evaluation.

problem: Prompt optimization methods target point-wise accuracy but do not enforce paraphrase invariance or searching stability, leaving LLMs brittle to small semantic-preserving paraphrases.
approach: TARE introduces textual sharpness as a formal criterion for robustness in the semantic space of prompts; alternates between an inner adversarial search stressing prompts with hard paraphrases and an outer robust selection.
contribution: Generates prompts that preserve accuracy under paraphrasing; ATARE adapts with anisotropic weights and balances exploration-fidelity, outperforming accuracy-only prompt search.

problem: Classical influence functions face challenges when applied to deep neural networks due to non-invertible Hessians and high-dimensional parameter spaces.
approach: Propose Bayesian influence functions that replace Hessian inversion with loss landscape statistics estimated via stochastic-gradient MCMC sampling, capturing higher-order parameter interactions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on predicting retraining experiments while scaling efficiently to billion-parameter neural networks.

problem: Extending PPO to expressive, high-capacity policy models like continuous normalizing flows is challenging because likelihood evaluation along the full flow trajectory is computationally expensive and numerically unstable.
approach: PolicyFlow approximates importance ratios using velocity field variations along a simple interpolation path; proposes Brownian Regularizer as an implicit entropy regularizer to prevent mode collapse.
contribution: Integrates expressive CNF policies with PPO-style objectives without requiring full trajectory likelihood evaluation, achieving competitive or superior performance on diverse tasks.

problem: Speech-language models treat speech understanding as a single black box and reason weakly about non-content aspects under sparse supervision.
approach: Adopt a modular perspective using a world model that learns forward dynamics over latent states, factorizing speech understanding into four modules communicating through a causal graph.
contribution: First graph-based modular speech model for explicit reasoning, enabling counterfactual interventions and interpretability; supports causal analysis under partial supervision.

problem: Reward-guided image editing requires preserving semantic content of the source image while enhancing a target reward, a task largely unexplored in diffusion/flow-matching models.
approach: Formulate editing as a trajectory optimal control problem where the reverse process is a controllable trajectory from the source image; iteratively update adjoint states to steer the editing.
contribution: Significantly outperforms inversion-based baselines in balancing reward maximization and fidelity to the source image without reward hacking.

problem: Existing inductive link prediction methods for knowledge hypergraphs assume fixed relational vocabulary and cannot generalize to novel relation types or novel entities.
approach: Propose HYPER as a foundation model that learns and transfers across different relation types of varying arities by encoding entities along with their positions in hyperedges.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods in both node-only and node-and-relation inductive settings, showing strong generalization to unseen higher-arity relational structures.

problem: While activation steering reduces hallucinations, existing methods require real-time monitoring during inference; models still lack the ability to abstain from answering questions they don't know.
approach: CASAL directly bakes activation steering benefits into model weights via amortized optimization, training only a submodule of a single transformer layer.
contribution: Reduces hallucination by 30-40% across multiple benchmarks with 30× better compute efficiency than LoRA baselines; generalizes to OOD domains and works with both dense and MoE models.

problem: Test-time scaling methods suffer from high inference latency due to synchronization overhead when scaling along parallel and sequential dimensions.
approach: ATTS follows hypothesis testing to enable asynchronous inference through online calibration and proposes an ordinal classification algorithm supporting a three-stage rejection sampling pipeline.
contribution: Delivers up to 56.7× speedup in test-time scaling and 4.14× throughput improvement while maintaining accurate rejection rate control and no accuracy loss.

problem: Sequential quantization frameworks treat all layers equally during post-training quantization, which may be suboptimal when facing challenging bit-width settings.
approach: SliderQuant employs adaptive sliding quantization with inter-layer designs targeting shallow/intermediate/deep layers and intra-layer incremental strategies to reduce quantization error.
contribution: Significantly reduces quantization errors across layers, improving LLM quantization quality at challenging bit-widths.

problem: Monotonicity constraints in value function factorization limit expressiveness and restrict the range of joint action values, hindering optimal policy learning.
approach: POW iteratively identifies potentially optimal joint actions and assigns higher training weights through a theoretically grounded weighted training process.
contribution: Guarantees recovery of the true optimal policy and consistently surpasses state-of-the-art value-based MARL methods across diverse environments.

problem: Graph neural networks overlook multi-way and hierarchical relationships; existing topological deep learning models are restricted to undirected settings and fail to capture directed higher-order patterns.
approach: Introduce Semi-Simplicial Neural Networks operating on semi-simplicial sets that encode directed higher-order motifs; propose Routing-SSNs that dynamically select informative relations.
contribution: Strictly more expressive than standard graph and TDL models; achieves state-of-the-art on brain dynamics classification (27% improvement over second-best) and scales efficiently.

problem: Few-shot anomaly detection is challenging because limited samples make differentiation between normal and abnormal features difficult, especially under category-agnostic conditions.
approach: FoundAD leverages foundation visual encoders to learn a nonlinear projection operator onto the natural image manifold; anomaly amount correlates with embedding differences.
contribution: Supports multi-class detection with competitive performance while surpassing other approaches in model size and inference efficiency.

problem: LLM pruning methods are widely used for efficiency but remain unexplored for security vulnerabilities.
approach: The paper introduces an attack where an adversary computes a proxy metric for pruning likelihood and injects malicious behaviors into unprunable parameters while using prunable parameters to mask them during pre-pruning.
contribution: Demonstrates that modern pruning methods can be maliciously exploited with success rates up to 95.7% for jailbreak and 99.5% for targeted injection, revealing a critical deployment-time security gap.

problem: Attention in transformer prefill is computationally expensive due to processing all key-value pairs, slowing inference.
approach: QuoKA leverages query-key similarity patterns to prioritize low-similarity queries and retain representative queries, then selects aligned key-value pairs for sparse attention evaluation.
contribution: Achieves 3x reduction in time-to-first-token and up to 7x speedup on Intel CPUs while utilizing 88% fewer key-value pairs and maintaining near-baseline accuracy.

problem: Multi-view clustering fails on incomplete data where some views are missing, and existing recovery methods introduce errors.
approach: The method proposes confident block diagonal structures to infer missing views while preserving invariable local structure, combined with graph completion across all views.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on multiple benchmark datasets compared to state-of-the-art incomplete multi-view clustering methods.

problem: Differentiable physics simulators produce erratic or vanishing gradients in contact-rich tasks, hindering optimization.
approach: A differentiable contact model is proposed that satisfies well-behaved gradient properties while maintaining computational efficiency in rigid-body simulation.
contribution: Enables discovery of complex contact-rich control signals from simple initializations for locomotion and manipulation tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs process excessive visual tokens, increasing computational cost without improving task performance.
approach: The method uses explainability techniques (attention maps) to identify task-irrelevant visual tokens at the input stage of LLMs, trained via lightweight convolutional networks.
contribution: Achieves significant token reduction with negligible performance loss across 13 benchmarks on three leading MLLMs without architecture modification.

problem: Video restoration using generative models suffers from distribution drift and poor texture quality due to imperfect alignment.
approach: Vivid-VR combines concept distillation from a pretrained T2V model with a redesigned ControlNet architecture featuring dual-branch control connectors for generation control.
contribution: Achieves impressive texture realism, visual vividness, and temporal consistency on synthetic and real-world benchmarks as well as AIGC videos.

problem: Long-context LLM decoding is bottlenecked by the expanding key-value cache, which grows linearly with sequence length.
approach: LycheeDecode partitions attention heads into retrieval heads (identifying crucial tokens) and sparse heads (reusing them), using a hardware-efficient top-k selection strategy.
contribution: Demonstrates comparable generative quality to full-attention baseline with up to 2.7x speedup at 128K context length across LongBench and RULER benchmarks.

problem: Brain-to-image decoding through fMRI typically relies on intermediate feature spaces, obscuring how brain signals shape generation.
approach: NeuroAdapter directly conditions a diffusion model on brain representations, bypassing intermediate feature spaces, with an interpretability framework probing cross-attention across denoising steps.
contribution: Provides competitive visual reconstruction quality on fMRI datasets with greater transparency into how different cortical areas influence generation.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs with new data can inadvertently introduce unsafe behaviors or degrade safety alignment.
approach: GradShield computes a Finetuning Implicit Harmfulness Score for each data point and removes harmful samples before fine-tuning to preserve alignment.
contribution: Maintains Attack Success Rate under 6% while preserving utility performance across multiple fine-tuning tasks.

problem: LLM-based agents face high latency and inference costs that limit real-world deployment and user experience.
approach: DSP uses asynchronous online reinforcement learning to dynamically balance latency and cost without offline training, allowing user control over the acceleration-cost tradeoff.
contribution: Achieves comparable efficiency to the fastest lossless acceleration method while reducing total cost by 30% and unnecessary cost up to 60%.

problem: Knowledge distillation lacks theoretical understanding of how soft probabilistic outputs affect student convergence and generalization.
approach: The paper analyzes SGD convergence with Bayesian teachers that provide Bayes Class Probabilities, showing variance reduction and improved generalization bounds.
contribution: Students distilled from Bayesian teachers achieve up to 4.27% higher accuracies and exhibit 30% less noise in convergence compared to deterministic teachers.

problem: Logic optimization for chip design relies on expensive GNN-based pruning that is slow and hard to interpret.
approach: HIS learns a hierarchical tree structure to represent symbolic functions, trained with RL to optimize a Transformer for symbolic token generation that identifies ineffective subgraphs.
contribution: Outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches in efficiency and optimization performance on two widely used circuit benchmarks.

problem: Fixed N:M sparsity in neural networks limits flexibility in adapting pruning to varying weight importance across layers.
approach: FlexHiNM-GP adaptively partitions layers into dense, vector-pruned, and N:M sparse regions with iterative channel-rearrangement (Gyro-Permutation) and differentiable Hard Concrete masking.
contribution: Consistently surpasses structured baselines and approaches unstructured pruning performance on vision and language benchmarks.

problem: Computing optimal transport maps requires numerical integration or adversarial training, which is computationally expensive.
approach: The method uses the Hamilton-Jacobi equation and characteristics method to derive closed-form bidirectional transport maps trained via a pure minimization framework.
contribution: Establishes a principled and versatile tool for optimal transport with provable optimality, demonstrating accuracy, scalability, and efficiency.

problem: Multimodal LLMs remain vulnerable to adversarial visual inputs despite existing safety defenses.
approach: GuardAlign combines optimal-transport-enhanced safety detection (measuring distribution distances) with cross-modal attentive calibration to strengthen safety signals during generation.
contribution: Reduces unsafe response rates by up to 39% on SPA-VL while improving utility (VQAv2 from 78.51% to 79.21%).

problem: Uncertainty estimation on resource-constrained microcontrollers is impractical because existing methods require multiple inference passes.
approach: SNAP-UQ predicts next activations from low-rank projections using tiny int8 heads, computing standardized prediction error as depth-wise surprisal signals aggregated into an uncertainty score.
contribution: Reduces flash and latency by 40-60% and 25-35% respectively compared to early-exit and ensemble baselines while maintaining AUROC ≈ 0.9 failure detection.

problem: Existing hallucination benchmarks for MLLMs use oversimplified tasks and fail to assess fine-grained visual perception.
approach: FREAK proposes fine-grained photorealistic images with counter-commonsense edits and evaluates hallucination via CoT prompting techniques on a controlled subset.
contribution: Reveals severe hallucination issues in SOTA models regarding fine-grained visual perception with critical insights on hallucination patterns.

problem: Solving inverse problems with diffusion models requires careful tuning or suffers from local optima and noise overfitting.
approach: NA-NHMC performs posterior sampling by treating reverse diffusion as a deterministic mapping from noise to images, enabling solution space exploration while keeping proposals on the learned manifold.
contribution: Achieves superior reconstruction quality across four linear and three nonlinear inverse problems, significantly outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Traditional gradient descent requires unrealistically large learning rates to escape saddle points during fine-tuning.
approach: The paper introduces steepest mirror flows as a theoretical framework showing that steeper descent facilitates saddle-point escape and feature learning better than gradient descent.
contribution: Explains why Adam and AdamW outperform SGD in fine-tuning through saddle-point escape and feature learning mechanisms.

problem: Deep neural networks do not align well with human visual behavior, exhibiting poor error consistency and weak shape bias.
approach: The method demonstrates that low-pass filtering (via image blurring at test-time) removes high-frequency information and improves behavioral alignment with human visual perception.
contribution: Halves the alignment gap between DNNs and human observers by blurring images at test-time, achieving state-of-the-art model-vs-human score.

problem: Watermarking verification in diffusion models requires slow, error-prone inversion that limits practical deployment.
approach: FARI proposes fast one-step inversion paired with lightweight adversarial LoRA fine-tuning, exploiting the lower curvature of inversion trajectories for efficient watermark extraction.
contribution: Surpasses 50-step DDIM inversion in both speed and robustness with ~20 minutes of fine-tuning on a single GPU.

problem: Evaluating multi-turn instruction-based image editing is unreliable because benchmarks lack paired references or rely only on VLMs.
approach: EdiVal-Agent decomposes images into objects, synthesizes diverse editing instructions, and measures instruction-following and content-consistency via object-centric metrics.
contribution: Enables automated fine-grained evaluation of multi-turn editing with object-centric metrics on a new video benchmark for category splitting.

problem: Detecting training data contamination in LLMs is difficult because it is hard to distinguish memorization from generalization.
approach: CoDeC measures how in-context learning affects model performance to distinguish memorized data from unseen datasets, producing model- and dataset-agnostic contamination scores.
contribution: Produces interpretable contamination scores that clearly separate seen and unseen datasets with strong evidence of memorization in open-weight models.

problem: Scaling laws for generative evaluations like math problem-solving remain underexplored, limiting prediction of model capabilities.
approach: Three pretraining scaling laws are proposed for fitting pass-at-k on generative evaluations, differing in covariates: compute, parameters-tokens, and log-likelihoods of solutions.
contribution: Identifies that generative evaluations introduce hyperparameters acting as control levers for scaling behavior, with the gold reference likelihood law uniquely stable across 5 orders.

problem: Predicting downstream LLM task performance from scaling laws is unreliable, limiting extrapolation of model capabilities.
approach: A two-parameter scaling law directly models downstream accuracy from training budget, validated on models up to 17B parameters trained on up to 350B tokens.
contribution: Accurately describes downstream accuracy scaling for fixed token-to-parameter ratio and enables extrapolation with up to 6.7x larger training budget.

problem: LLMs with persistent memory lack mechanisms to control information flow based on context, risking inappropriate disclosure.
approach: CIMemories uses synthetic user profiles with 100+ attributes and task contexts to evaluate whether LLMs control information flow appropriately across different scenarios.
contribution: Reveals frontier models exhibit 14%-69% attribute-level violations, highlighting critical gaps in integrity-aware memory systems.

problem: Fixed video classification taxonomies cannot accommodate emerging category distinctions without costly annotation and retraining.
approach: The method leverages latent compositional structure of video classifiers to expose fine-grained distinctions without additional data, enhanced by low-shot fine-tuning.
contribution: Substantially outperforms vision-language baselines on category splitting while preserving accuracy on the rest of the taxonomy.

problem: Existing copula models struggle to scale and represent multimodal dependencies in high-dimensional data.
approach: Diffusion and flow-based copulas model dependencies by learning to remember forgotten inter-variable dependencies, supporting both density estimation and efficient sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art copula approaches in modelling complex and high-dimensional dependencies.

problem: Generating realistic human geometry with fine clothing details and accurate body interactions at scale is computationally inefficient.
approach: A two-stage generative framework encodes geometry distributions as 2D feature maps using flow matching, then trains a flow model on the latent space with SMPL domain refinement.
contribution: Achieves 57% improvement in geometry quality for pose-conditioned avatar generation and novel pose synthesis over existing methods.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models suffer from hallucinations that degrade performance on vision-language tasks.
approach: Dynamic Multimodal Activation Steering constructs a semantic-based truthfulness steering vector database and computes visual perception vectors, applied to influential attention heads.
contribution: Significantly enhances model performance and outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in hallucination mitigation across multiple models and datasets.

problem: Identifying promising reasoning traces early is difficult, wasting computation on unproductive paths during inference-time scaling.
approach: Latent-trajectory signals characterize temporal evolution of internal representations during reasoning, enabling early selection of promising candidates during generation.
contribution: Reduces token usage by up to 70% while preserving and improving accuracy by 2.6% on average compared to majority voting.

problem: Evaluating LLMs on realistic software development tasks with long code context remains a gap in current benchmarks.
approach: SwingArena pairs LLMs as patch submitters and reviewers in CI pipelines, with a retrieval-augmented code generation module handling long-context challenges.
contribution: Presents a scalable methodology for evaluating LLMs in realistic CI-driven software development with over 400 real-world GitHub issues.

problem: Offline RL must balance preventing out-of-distribution actions with learning expressive multimodal policies.
approach: ReFORM learns a behavior-cloning flow with bounded source distribution, then optimizes a reflected flow generating bounded noise while keeping the support.
contribution: Dominates all baselines on 40 OGBench tasks with constant hyperparameters, maintaining strong performance across datasets of varying quality.

problem: Deep learning for electronic-structure Hamiltonian prediction struggles to generalize across diverse materials.
approach: NextHAM introduces zeroth-step Hamiltonians as descriptors, uses a Transformer with E(3)-symmetry, and proposes training objectives for accuracy in both real and reciprocal space.
contribution: Demonstrates improved generalization on Materials-HAM-SOC, a dataset of 17,000 materials spanning 60+ elements with spin-orbit coupling effects.

problem: Novel view synthesis from sparse RGB fails under rapid camera motion, and event-based methods require per-scene optimization.
approach: EA3D jointly leverages event streams and RGB imagery via an EA-Renderer that fuses appearance with event-based geometry, conditioned to a 3D-informed diffusion model.
contribution: Consistently outperforms optimization-based and generalizable baselines on both real-world and synthetic event data with superior fidelity.

problem: SVG understanding, editing, and generation remain fragmented tasks with limited dataset and method transferability.
approach: InternSVG leverages MLLMs with SVG-specific tokens and two-stage training progressing from static SVGs to animations, trained on the large SAgoge dataset.
contribution: Achieves substantial gains and consistently outperforms leading open and proprietary counterparts on SVG understanding, editing, and generation.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to understand real-world scenarios from synchronized audio-visual input.
approach: WorldSense designs omni-modal evaluation tasks requiring audio and video synergies across 1,662 videos in 8 domains with 3,172 multi-choice QA pairs.
contribution: Demonstrates that existing models achieve only 65.1% best accuracy on real-world omni-modal understanding tasks across 1,662 audio-visual videos.

problem: Graph neural networks lack large-scale datasets that capture spatial multi-edges and complex geometric structures.
approach: Poly2Graph automates mapping 1-D Hamiltonians to spectral graphs, generating HSG-12M containing 11.6M static and 5.1M dynamic spatial multigraphs.
contribution: Introduces HSG-12M with 11.6M static and 5.1M dynamic spatial multigraphs, the first large-scale dataset of spatial multigraphs for graph learning.

problem: The expressiveness of transformers and their ability to represent formal languages remains theoretically unexplored.
approach: The paper proves that transformers can represent formal languages more succinctly than finite automata and LTL formulas via a succinctness measure.
contribution: Proves that transformers are EXPSPACE-complete in expressive power, substantially surpassing finite automata and LTL formulas.

problem: Language models struggle with table understanding due to structured data complexity and lack of semantic context.
approach: TableMaster extracts and verbalizes table content with semantic context and introduces adaptive reasoning that flexibly adjusts between textual and symbolic reasoning.
contribution: Achieves 78.13% accuracy on WikiTQ using GPT-4o-mini, surpassing existing baselines for table understanding.

problem: Autoregressive image generation models are computationally intensive and sequential, making on-device deployment difficult due to high latency.
approach: CIAR uses cloud-device collaboration with on-device token uncertainty quantification via continuous probability intervals to handle visual token vocabularies and spatial redundancy in image regions.
contribution: Achieves 2.18× speed-up and reduces cloud requests by 70% while preserving image quality compared to existing methods.

problem: It is unclear when spectrum-aware optimizers like Muon outperform standard methods and why they might benefit generalization, particularly on imbalanced data.
approach: The paper studies Spectral Gradient Descent (SpecGD) on Gaussian mixture data and linear/bilinear models, showing SpecGD learns principal components at equal rates unlike standard GD which prioritizes dominant components first.
contribution: Demonstrates SpecGD achieves better balanced accuracy on imbalanced data early in training compared to GD, with benefits amplified in deep linear models.

problem: Reducing sampling steps below 4 for diffusion models becomes increasingly challenging, suggesting efficiency gains should be sought along other axes like model scale.
approach: SwD introduces scale-wise distillation that enables progressive generation for few-step models, avoiding redundant computations at intermediate timesteps and using kernel MMD loss.
contribution: Approaches 2-step sampling speed while outperforming alternatives under the same compute budget on text-to-image and video diffusion models.

problem: Omni Language Models struggle to capture fine-grained multimodal details accurately, with an inherent tradeoff between detail level and hallucination.
approach: Omni-Detective uses agentic data generation with tool-calling to produce detailed, minimally hallucinatory multimodal data; Audio-Captioner and Omni-Captioner models are trained on this curated data.
contribution: Omni-Captioner achieves state-of-the-art on VDC and best detail-hallucination tradeoff on video-SALMONN 2, with performance comparable to Gemini 2.5 Pro.

problem: Existing knowledge editing methods struggle to scale beyond thousands of edits without compromising model abilities or causing forgetting.
approach: NeuralDB models edited facts as a neural Key-Value database with non-linear gated retrieval, enabling edits via simple modifications to existing Locate-and-Edit methods.
contribution: Scales knowledge editing to 100,000 facts (50× more than prior work) while maintaining performance on text understanding and generation tasks.

problem: Understanding implicit planning in language models requires scalable methods beyond prior qualitative case studies to assess how models prepare for predicted future tokens.
approach: The paper proposes simple vector steering techniques to assess implicit planning by manipulating generated rhymes or answers through end-of-line vectors affecting intermediate token generation.
contribution: Shows implicit planning is universal and present in models as small as 1B parameters, with ability to manipulate output via steering in rhyme generation and question answering.

problem: Vision-Language Models hallucinate due to generic visual augmentations that ignore text query context, limiting the effectiveness of visual contrastive decoding.
approach: Introduces self-augmentation prompting that dynamically aligns semantics between query and visual augmentation, plus adaptive thresholding based on output sparsity.
contribution: Enhances factual consistency across four LVLMs and seven benchmarks, achieving better results than state-of-the-art visual contrastive decoding methods.

problem: Masked autoencoders for medical volumetric imaging use discrete voxel reconstruction which neglects comprehensive anatomical structure continuity.
approach: MedGMAE replaces voxel reconstruction with 3D Gaussian primitives reconstruction, learning to predict complete Gaussian parameter sets from sparse visible patches.
contribution: Outperforms traditional MAE baselines on downstream segmentation, classification, and registration tasks, enabling faster 3D CT volume reconstruction.

problem: Simulators used in RL training are a security blind spot vulnerable to adversarial manipulation of dynamics that could stealthily implant backdoors.
approach: Daze attacks implant action-level backdoors by exploiting simulator dynamics without altering or observing rewards, using formal guarantees of attack success.
contribution: First demonstration of RL backdoor attacks that transfer to real robotic hardware, highlighting simulator vulnerabilities in the RL pipeline.

problem: Existing group-based policy optimization methods like GRPO allocate fixed rollouts uniformly across all prompts, wasting budget on less informative examples.
approach: VIP uses a lightweight Gaussian process to predict per-prompt success probabilities and solves a convex optimization problem to allocate rollouts minimizing expected gradient variance.
contribution: Consistently improves sampling efficiency and achieves higher performance than uniform or heuristic allocation strategies across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Adapters for foundation models degrade performance under extreme data scarcity (less than 1% training data), worse than simple linear probing.
approach: Dual-Kernel Adapter uses large-kernel convolutions for spatial context and small-kernel convolutions for local detail, expanding effective receptive field.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing adapter methods in both data-constrained and data-rich medical imaging scenarios for classification and segmentation.

problem: Learned Sparse Retrieval methods struggle to scale across languages, requiring dense methods for multilingual search.
approach: MILCO maps queries and documents from different languages into a shared English lexical space via a multilingual connector, using Sparse Alignment Pretraining and a LexEcho head for robustness.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art multilingual LSR performance while maintaining 3× lower retrieval latency and 10× smaller index size than dense alternatives.

problem: Graph outlier detection methods based on graph convolution fail when homophily aggregation contaminates normal node representations near anomalies.
approach: CER-GOD jointly optimizes a masking spoiler that weakens heterogeneous neighbors with an unsupervised clustering detector, guided by a diversity loss.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance by dismantling the homophily trap and eliminating the need for predefined anomaly thresholds.

problem: Autoregressive visual generation models struggle with complex prompts specifying multiple objects with precise spatial relationships and attributes.
approach: GoT-R1 applies reinforcement learning to learn explicit reasoning strategies for semantic-spatial reasoning via a dual-stage reward framework leveraging MLLMs.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements on T2I-CompBench and GenEval, particularly on compositional tasks with precise spatial relationships.

problem: Current alignment methods fail to infer users' deep implicit preferences and lack defensive reasoning to navigate real-world ambiguity.
approach: CDRA reframes alignment as structured reasoning, using a multi-faceted cognitive council to annotate preferences and training a Personalized Generative Process Reward Model.
contribution: DeepPref benchmark with 3000 preference-query pairs enables discovering and aligning with users' true preferences through critique-driven policy alignment.

problem: Existing online-to-nonconvex conversion methods require complex double-loop schemes and impose strong assumptions on second-order gradient moments.
approach: Uses a novel doubly optimistic hint function with gradient evaluation at extrapolated points, motivated by two optimistic assumptions about gradient and direction changes.
contribution: Eliminates the double-loop and logarithmic factor in deterministic case, achieving O(ε^-1.75 log(1/ε)) complexity while simplifying the stochastic setting.

problem: Evaluating anthropomorphic LLM behaviors typically uses single-turn assessment, missing multi-turn social phenomena and their effects on user perception.
approach: AnthroBench uses multi-turn simulations of user interactions and validates with large-scale human studies (N=1101) to measure 14 distinct anthropomorphic behaviors.
contribution: Shows anthropomorphic behaviors are primarily characterized by relationship-building and first-person pronoun use, with many only emerging after multiple turns.

problem: Offline RL relies on a single global Q-function which fails to capture the compositional nature of tasks with diverse subtasks.
approach: ICQL formulates Q-learning as contextual inference using linear Transformers to adaptively infer local Q-functions from retrieved transitions without subtask labels.
contribution: Improves performance by up to 29.46% on Kitchen tasks and up to 6% on Gym/Adroit tasks through compositional value estimation.

problem: Existing inference-time computation approaches for System 2 Thinking are modality-specific, problem-specific, or require additional supervision beyond pretraining.
approach: Energy-Based Transformers learn to verify input-prediction compatibility and reformulate prediction as optimization via energy minimization, trained from unsupervised pretraining.
contribution: Outperforms Transformer++ and Diffusion Transformers on multiple modalities, scaling 35% faster during pretraining with up to 29% inference-time improvements.

problem: Detecting missing persons in forests is challenging because dense canopy cover conceals individuals in aerial imagery, requiring under-canopy perspectives.
approach: ForestPersons dataset provides 96,482 images with bounding boxes, pose, and visibility labels from ground-level and low-altitude perspectives reflecting MAV forest SAR conditions.
contribution: Demonstrates standard object detection models trained on prior datasets show limited performance, indicating a gap requiring specialized benchmarks for forest SAR.

problem: Neural scaling laws' sensitivity to data quality interventions remains poorly understood, hindering resource planning and performance projection.
approach: QualityPajama tests 23 systematically filtered datasets across 2,000+ models (100M-8B parameters) to measure how deduplication, filtering, and rewriting reshape scaling behavior.
contribution: Shows data interventions reshape scaling dynamics non-trivially, moving exponents/coefficients/constants in conflicting directions with different optimal strategies at different scales.

problem: Accurate recall from large-scale memories is challenging for QA in similarity-dense scenarios where semantic distance alone is insufficient.
approach: AssoMem constructs an associative memory graph anchoring dialogue utterances to automatically extracted clues, using multi-dimensional signals (relevance, importance, temporal alignment) with adaptive MI-driven fusion.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three benchmarks including the newly introduced MeetingQA dataset.

problem: Machine unlearning via multi-objective optimization using weighted sum scalarization causes unstable training and model utility degradation due to conflicting gradients.
approach: OFMU uses penalty-based bi-level optimization with inner maximization enforcing forgetting via similarity-aware gradient decorrelation and outer minimization preserving retention.
contribution: Achieves better tradeoffs between forgetting efficacy and model utility with provable convergence guarantees under convex and non-convex regimes.

problem: Existing LID estimation benchmarks are overly simplistic or use domain datasets with unknown true LID, leading to potentially erroneous evaluations.
approach: Uses techniques to create LID benchmarks for arbitrary domains by transforming manifolds while preserving structure, addressing biases in NN-based methods.
contribution: Identifies critical limitations of state-of-the-art LID methods and new directions for future development through comparative analysis.

problem: Intelligent systems must balance broad generalization with precise identification, but the tradeoff between these goals remains unclear.
approach: Derives closed-form expressions for finite semantic resolution showing a universal Pareto front linking generalization and identification probabilities.
contribution: Provides precise theory of the generalization-identification tradeoff with empirical validation on ReLU networks, CNNs, and vision-language models.

problem: It is unclear how robust different probabilistic models are to low-quality data, with existing analysis limited in scope.
approach: Systematically investigates effects of data corruption (deduplication, heuristic filtering) across autoregressive models, diffusion models, and classifiers through multi-perspective analysis.
contribution: Shows autoregressive models are remarkably resilient while diffusion models degrade catastrophically, linked to conditioning information richness and absolute information content.

problem: Fine-tuning vision-language models often distorts semantic representation geometry, neglecting the geometric structure of data distribution.
approach: MPS-Tuning preserves manifold topology by aligning Gram matrices before and after fine-tuning (upper-bounding Gromov-Wasserstein distance) while sculpting it for class separability.
contribution: Significantly improves performance while preserving semantic manifold structure in few-shot image classification.

problem: Multimodal LLMs internalize sensitive information and existing unlearning methods irreversibly alter parameters, conflicting with modern privacy regulations.
approach: Knowledge Externalization transfers targeted knowledge into external memory tokens via Dual-Stream Memory Tuning and Soft Orthogonal Weighting to preserve token independence.
contribution: Achieves effective forgetting while enabling high-fidelity restoration, continuous knowledge editing, and emergent compositionality across multiple memory tokens.

problem: Existing benchmarks for transferability estimation metrics have unrealistic model spaces and static hierarchies that artificially inflate performance claims.
approach: Analyzes shortcomings of current benchmark setups and provides concrete recommendations for constructing more robust and realistic benchmarks.
contribution: Reveals that simple dataset-agnostic heuristics can outperform sophisticated methods on current benchmarks, highlighting a disconnect from real-world complexity.

problem: Explaining time series prediction changes is difficult because most XAI methods analyze each step independently without leveraging temporal dependencies.
approach: Delta-XAI wraps 14 XAI methods for online settings and proposes Shifted Window Integrated Gradients (SWING) incorporating past observations in the integration path.
contribution: SWING outperforms recent approaches on faithfulness, sufficiency, and coherence metrics, capturing temporal dependencies and mitigating out-of-distribution effects.

problem: Diffusion models' synchronous denoising causes prompt-related regions to reference unrelated regions at the same noise level, impairing text-image alignment.
approach: Asynchronous diffusion models allocate distinct timesteps to different pixels, allowing prompt-related regions to be denoised gradually and access clearer context.
contribution: Significantly improves text-to-image alignment across diverse prompts through dynamic pixel-wise timestep modulation.

problem: Neural networks lack ability to inherently respect causal structures, limiting their robustness to covariate shift and interpretability.
approach: Causal Transformers incorporate predefined causal constraints from Directed Acyclic Graphs into Transformer architectures while maintaining powerful function approximation.
contribution: Improves robustness, reliability, and interpretability at inference time while respecting underlying structural constraints.

problem: Sparse autoencoders on multimodal embeddings often learn split dictionaries with most features unimodal rather than representing shared concepts.
approach: Uses cross-modal random masking and group-sparse regularization to encourage multimodal alignment in sparse feature decomposition of CLIP and CLAP embeddings.
contribution: Learns more multimodal dictionaries while reducing dead neurons and improving feature semanticity compared to standard SAEs.

problem: Understanding psychological and social behaviors requires unified multi-task systems but existing work uses specialized datasets, missing scalability and cross-task transfer.
approach: Human Behavior Atlas unifies 100,000+ samples spanning text/audio/visual modalities across affective states, cognitive states, pathologies, and social processes.
contribution: Training on the benchmark enables models (Omnisapiens-7B variants) to outperform multimodal LLMs and improve transfer to novel behavioral datasets.

problem: Fine-tuning large-scale teachers for knowledge distillation is impractical and proxy-based optimization for CMI maximization introduces inaccuracies.
approach: DJIP uses a trainable differentiable JPEG layer before the teacher to perturb inputs maximizing CMI, with an alternating optimization algorithm to learn JPEG parameters.
contribution: Improves student accuracy by up to 4.11% while remaining computationally lightweight and compatible with standard KD pipelines.

problem: Maintaining spectral sparsifiers of geometric graphs under dynamic point location changes requires efficient algorithms.
approach: Presents a fully-dynamic data structure maintaining spectral sparsifiers with O(n^(1+o(1))) initialization and n^o(1) update time.
contribution: Enables robust spectral sparsification applicable to iterative optimization algorithms with data structure maintaining matrix-vector operations under sparse updates.

problem: Diffusion language models' iterative denoising creates vulnerability to jailbreak attacks where intermediate affirmative tokens steer toward harmful responses.
approach: Proposes safety alignment training diffusion models to generate safe responses from contaminated intermediate denoising steps containing affirmative tokens.
contribution: Significantly mitigates priming vulnerability with minimal impact on task performance and improves robustness against conventional jailbreak attacks.

problem: Designing robust subsidy schemes for boundedly rational agents in principal-agent problems requires understanding how agents deviate from optimal policies.
approach: Analyzes perfectly rational baseline then introduces epsilon-incentive-compatible agents who accept policies within epsilon of personal optimum, reducing to concave optimization.
contribution: Shows optimal subsidies concentrate along social-welfare-maximizing trajectories and characterizes welfare loss under bounded rationality.

problem: Zero-shot time-series forecasting is hindered by limited data, leakage-prone evaluation, and privacy constraints.
approach: Proposes first practical univariate simulator using SARIMA with stability region sampling, superposition for multi-seasonality, and heavy-tailed noise for burstiness.
contribution: Enables training on ~1B simulated series for strong zero-shot generalization, surpassing statistical forecasters and recent foundation baselines on M-Series and GiftEval.

problem: Two-stage 3D object detectors struggle due to proposal quality degradation from point cloud sparsity and lack of contextual cues in independent refinement.
approach: PTN includes Hierarchical Attentive Feature Alignment for multi-granularity representations and Collaborative Proposal Refinement for contextual-aware interactions.
contribution: Achieves promising performance on Waymo and KITTI benchmarks by extracting both coarse voxel and fine point features with improved proposal refinement.

problem: Medical diagnosis systems often output direct answers without clinical evidence from quantitative analysis, compromising reliability for clinical use.
approach: MedAgent-Pro uses hierarchical agentic reasoning with disease-level planning via retrieval-augmented generation agents accessing medical guidelines, and patient-level step-by-step reasoning with visual analysis tools and evidence-based reflection.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance over mainstream VLMs and agentic systems across diverse anatomical regions and imaging modalities with confirmed clinical relevance.

problem: SMOTE, widely used for synthetic data generation, has unknown privacy implications despite deployment in sensitive applications.
approach: Systematic privacy leakage study using membership inference attacks and novel geometric attacks (DistinSMOTE and ReconSMOTE) that exploit SMOTE's properties.
contribution: Reveals that SMOTE is inherently non-private with perfect distinction of real vs synthetic records and near-perfect minority record reconstruction under realistic imbalance ratios.

problem: Creating task-specific multimodal models requires manual expert effort; no automated framework exists to select the best VLM for a user-defined task.
approach: Mordal reduces candidate search space and minimizes evaluation time per candidate through automated multimodal model search.
contribution: Finds optimal VLMs with 8.9x-11.6x lower GPU hours than grid search and 69% higher weighted Kendall's tau than state-of-the-art model selection.

problem: LLMs often explore suboptimally in sequential decision-making tasks, limiting their autonomous agent capabilities.
approach: Compares SFT and RL training on multi-armed bandits with various reward signals including regret-shaped and oracle imitation rewards, analyzing emergent exploration strategies.
contribution: Shows agents trained with RL/SFT match UCB/Thompson Sampling performance with robust generalization but reveal early catastrophic failure from exploitative bias.

problem: Extensive step-by-step reasoning in multimodal models incurs substantial computational overhead in token costs and response time.
approach: SketchThinker-R1 uses three stages: cold-start conversion to sketch-style reasoning, SketchJudge reward model training, and sketch-thinking reinforcement learning.
contribution: Achieves over 64% reduction in reasoning token cost without compromising answer accuracy while focusing reasoning on key problem-solving cues.

problem: Comparing full-graph and mini-batch GNN training approaches requires characterizing their distinct model performance and computational efficiency impacts.
approach: Systematic empirical and theoretical analysis through batch size and fan-out size lens, including novel generalization analysis via Wasserstein distance.
contribution: Provides generalization bounds and practical hyperparameter tuning guidance, revealing full-graph training doesn't always yield better performance than optimized mini-batch settings.

problem: LLMs deployed in clinical settings may generate responses misaligned with core nursing values, creating risks in nurse-patient interactions.
approach: First benchmark for nursing value alignment with five core dimensions distilled from international codes, including easy-level (2,200 aligned/violating) and hard-level (2,200 dialogue) datasets.
contribution: Evaluates 23 SoTA LLMs revealing general LLMs outperform medical ones, and Justice dimension is hardest for value alignment.

problem: Symmetry-aware methods assume transformed datapoints are important under test distribution, but this assumption's validity is rarely evaluated.
approach: Develops two-sample neural classifier test to quantify dataset anisotropy and validates on synthetic and benchmark point cloud datasets.
contribution: Reveals high anisotropy in benchmark datasets; shows equivariance benefits are dataset-dependent and invariant methods can underperform on anisotropic data even with invariant labels.

problem: Semi-supervised graph anomaly detection with only normal labels requires reliable anomaly synthesis, but existing methods lack quantitative anomaly assessment.
approach: TAQ-GAD uses topological anomaly quantification (node boundary and isolation scores) to dynamically screen pseudo-anomalies and enhance graph structure via virtual anomaly centers.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art methods through topological quantification and effective anomaly enhancement on benchmark datasets.

problem: LLM hallucinations from data-driven and reasoning-driven sources compromise reliability; existing methods address only one source with task-specific heuristics.
approach: Introduces Hallucination Risk Bound framework decomposing risk into data and reasoning components, builds HalluGuard using NTK-based score leveraging induced geometry.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art detection across 10 benchmarks, 11 baselines, and 9 LLM backbones for diverse hallucination forms.

problem: Existing jailbreak evaluation systems lack case-specific criteria, resulting in misleading effectiveness assessments and safety conclusions.
approach: GuidedBench comprises harmful question dataset with GuidedEval system providing detailed case-by-case evaluation guidelines for accurate jailbreak assessment.
contribution: Reduces inter-evaluator variance by at least 76.03%, offers more accurate method comparisons, and reveals why existing benchmarks fail to evaluate accurately.

problem: Maximum Common Edge Subgraph problem suffers from scalability issues in traditional max-clique and search-based algorithms for larger instances.
approach: Neural Graduated Assignment stacks differentiable assignment optimization with neural components, using learnable temperature for high-dimensional matching parameterization.
contribution: Significantly improves computation time and scalability on large instances while enhancing performance on MCES, similarity estimation, and graph retrieval tasks.

problem: Healthcare fraud detection faces label scarcity from delayed verification and rapidly evolving fraud patterns manifesting in complex graph-structured interactions.
approach: ConFVG combines Fiedler Vector-guided graph autoencoder for structure-aware learning with Subgraph Attention Fusion module for real-time adaptation to emerging fraud patterns.
contribution: Addresses label scarcity and non-stationary fraud detection through spectral graph properties and Mean Teacher mechanisms.

problem: Post-training quantization effectiveness in LLMs depends on training dynamics, but mechanisms underlying quantization robustness remain unclear.
approach: Comprehensive analysis of quantization degradation across training trajectories up to 32B parameters and 15T tokens, examining learning rate and hyperparameter interactions.
contribution: Shows validation loss and quantization error diverge after learning rate decay independent of scale; strategic hyperparameter interventions improve quantization quality.

problem: Attention learner training is costly; existing methods don't leverage the unique structure of attention mechanisms for efficient learning.
approach: AtteNT reinterprets learning through nonparametric teaching by analyzing attention mechanism's role in gradient descent and recasting evolution as functional gradient descent.
contribution: Achieves 13.01% training time reduction for LLMs and 20.58% for ViTs without accuracy compromise through importance-adaptive teaching.

problem: Low-rank and sparse LLM compression faces challenges in rank-sparsity interaction and layer-wise weight allocation, limiting existing methods' effectiveness.
approach: Two-stage method using robust PCA for initial decomposition followed by probabilistic global allocation strategy for joint rank-sparsity structure identification.
contribution: Automatically detects layer redundancy and manages sparse-rank interaction, significantly surpassing state-of-the-art sparsification and approximation techniques.

problem: Traditional language models require tokenization preprocessing, creating barriers to true end-to-end learning from raw sequences.
approach: Dynamic chunking mechanism automatically learns content and context-dependent segmentation jointly with model in hierarchical network operating at byte level.
contribution: Byte-level H-Net outperforms Transformer LMs on BPE tokens; multi-stage hierarchy improves scaling with data and character robustness in weak-tokenization languages.

problem: Scheduling algorithms with predictions need to balance consistency under perfect predictions with robustness under bad predictions while degrading smoothly.
approach: Refines smoothness metric as competitive ratio over instances where predictions provide information, establishes bounds for online completion time and makespan minimization.
contribution: Provides eta and eta-squared smooth bounds for single machine total completion time; O(eta-squared) smooth algorithms for parallel machines.

problem: LLM routing lacks support for realistic agentic settings requiring task planning, multi-round cooperation, and memory utilization with diverse agent types.
approach: Heterogeneous graph-based agentic router formulating workflow generation as MDP with agent selection, using GARNet to capture interactions among queries/agents/responses optimized via RL.
contribution: Improves accuracy by up to 9.3% while reducing GPU cost from 186.26 GiB to 1.04 GiB; generalizes to unseen tasks with strong zero-shot capabilities.

problem: Self-supervised learning methods typically focus on either recognition or motion rather than both jointly for multi-object natural videos.
approach: Midway Network extends latent dynamics modeling with midway top-down path for motion latents, dense forward prediction, and hierarchical structure for natural video scenes.
contribution: Learns strong representations for both semantic segmentation and optical flow on large-scale video datasets with novel forward feature perturbation analysis.

problem: Existing MLA kernel implementations choose either training efficiency (naive) or decoding bandwidth (absorb), missing opportunities to leverage shared prefixes.
approach: Hybrid approach combining naive formulation for compute-bound parts and absorb formulation for bandwidth-limited parts to exploit shared prefix data reuse.
contribution: Improves attention throughput by up to 3x and 3.24x on NPU/GPUs; boosts end-to-end throughput by 1.48x tokens/second with only 3% HBM overhead.

problem: LLM memorization risks and mechanisms remain poorly understood, limiting ability to predict and control memorization in training.
approach: Hubble suite of open-source models (1B/8B parameters, 100B/500B tokens) with minimal pairs: standard and perturbed models with controlled sensitive data insertion.
contribution: Establishes memorization determined by data frequency relative to corpus size; identifies best practices of diluting data and early training insertion to reduce memorization.

problem: Existing audio-visual benchmarks lack strict correlation, diverse audio types, and varying scene spans necessary for comprehensive Omni-LLM evaluation.
approach: JointAVBench with automated pipeline leveraging vision/audio/general LLMs to synthesize questions and answers requiring joint audio-visual understanding across five cognitive dimensions.
contribution: Shows best Omni-LLM achieves 62.6% accuracy outperforming uni-modal baselines but revealing substantial room for improvement in cross-scene reasoning.

problem: Open-source community lacks unified RL framework for training LLM agents from scratch across diverse multi-turn decision-making environments.
approach: AgentGym-RL with modular framework and ScalingInter-RL staged training approach progressing from short to long-horizon interactions for stable training.
contribution: Achieves performance on par with or exceeding OpenAI o3 and Gemini-2.5-Pro across 27 tasks; enables community-driven next-generation agent development.

problem: Attention mechanisms in LLMs face computational challenges at large scale, limiting practical deployment efficiency.
approach: Proposes attention sampler definition and sampling methods in streaming setting inspired by classical l2 sampler, providing theoretical analysis of space and update time.
contribution: Significantly reduces computational burden of traditional attention with demonstrated theoretical effectiveness across model architectures and domains.

problem: Vision-language models assume complete multimodal inputs, but real-world scenarios involve missing modalities due to privacy or resource constraints.
approach: MoRA parameter-efficient method with modality-common parameters for bidirectional knowledge transfer and modality-specific parameters for flexibility.
contribution: Achieves 5.24% average improvement in missing-modality scenarios using only 0.11% of full fine-tuning parameters and 25.90% of inference time.

problem: Drag-based image editing suffers from distortions in target regions; prior DDPM models provide insufficient priors for projecting latents onto image manifold.
approach: DragFlow harnesses FLUX DiT priors via region-based supervision with affine transformations for richer feature guidance, integrating personalization adapters and MLLMs.
contribution: Leverages FLUX's stronger priors for drag-based editing with region-based paradigm; curates Region-based Dragging benchmark with multi-level annotations.

problem: LLMs exhibit sensitivity to input context variations, compromising reliability; conventional metrics fail to assess local prediction robustness.
approach: Token Constraint Bound metric quantifies maximum internal state perturbation LLMs withstand before dominant next-token changes, linked to output embedding geometry.
contribution: Correlates with effective prompt engineering, uncovers critical instabilities missed by perplexity in in-context learning, enabling analysis of contextual stability.

problem: MCTS abstraction requires value-equivalent states/actions with same rewards, limiting detectable abstractions and reducing sample efficiency.
approach: KVDA framework groups states/actions with different values if differences can be inferred, modifies OGA-UCT to use this relaxed framework.
contribution: Detects significantly more abstractions than OGA-UCT with no additional parameters, outperforms on diverse deterministic environments.

problem: Respiratory auscultation faces information loss from spectrogram conversion and severe class imbalance from limited data availability.
approach: Resp-Agent with Active Adversarial Curriculum Agent controls diagnosis-informed synthesis; Modality-Weaving Diagnoser fuses EHR and audio via Strategic Attention.
contribution: Introduces Resp-229k benchmark (229k recordings); consistently outperforms prior approaches under data scarcity and long-tailed class imbalance.

problem: Continual learning requires balancing stability and plasticity; existing orthogonal projection methods struggle to optimally partition gradient space.
approach: SplitLoRA applies Low-Rank Adaptation with theoretical analysis of subspace partitioning effects, deriving optimal gradient space partition for stability-plasticity balance.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance through principled gradient space partitioning in LoRA-based framework.

problem: RLVR for agentic training depends on manual task queries and ground-truth answers, limiting scalability of RL processes.
approach: Search self-play with task proposer generating search queries and problem solver solving them, using RAG to verify query answerability from proposer's search results.
contribution: Enables self-play agentic RLVR without supervision; proposer and solver co-evolve capabilities through competition and cooperation.

problem: Estimating potential outcomes over time from observational data requires proper time-varying confounding adjustment, but existing methods have limitations.
approach: IGC-Net performs fully regression-based iterative G-computation for conditional average potential outcomes over time without propensity score division.
contribution: First neural model for fully regression-based G-computation in time-varying setting, significant step toward personalized decision-making from EHRs.

problem: Cascaded video synthesis pipelines suffer from inefficient pixel-space interfaces and mismatched degradation strategies between base and super-resolution models.
approach: SimpleGVR operates entirely in latent space with latent upsampler for conditioning and flow-based plus model-guided degradation strategies aligned with upstream model.
contribution: Establishes simple baseline for cascaded video super-resolution with detail-aware timestep sampler and efficient temporal handling for long videos.

problem: Sparse routing dynamics in MoE models respond to multilingual data in unclear ways, limiting understanding of cross-lingual generalization.
approach: Analyzes expert routing via parallel multilingual datasets revealing layer-wise phenomena and routing interventions steering routers via middle-layer task expert promotion.
contribution: Reveals language-specific routing in early/late layers, cross-lingual alignment in middle layers, 1-2% consistent multilingual gains via inference-time steering.

problem: Existing open-source approaches for visual search exhibit monotonous reasoning and limited interaction turns, inadequate for difficult exploratory tasks.
approach: Mini-o3 with Visual Probe Dataset, iterative collection pipeline for diverse reasoning patterns, and over-turn masking enabling multi-turn scaling at inference.
contribution: Naturally scales to tens of reasoning turns during inference despite training with six-turn upper bound; improves accuracy with increased reasoning turns.

problem: Agent RL for long-term multi-turn tasks with outcome-only rewards suffers from sparse supervision, limiting sample efficiency.
approach: Tree-GRPO uses tree search sampling to share common prefixes and construct step-wise process signals from outcome reward, enabling intra/inter-tree level advantages.
contribution: Demonstrates tree-structured trajectory equivalence to step-level direct preference learning; outperforms chain-based RL across 11 datasets and 3 QA task types.

problem: OR problem solving via LLMs faces credit assignment problems and myopic process supervision that fails to holistically evaluate interdependent steps.
approach: StepORLM with co-evolutionary loop where policy and generative process reward model (GenPRM) improve iteratively via dual-feedback mechanism and W-DPO.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art on six OR benchmarks outperforming larger models; GenPRM acts as universal process verifier boosting inference scaling.

problem: GNN confidence estimates misalign with predictive correctness in safety-critical settings; existing calibration methods depend on coarse statistics.
approach: WATS post-hoc calibration uses node-specific temperatures based on heat-kernel graph wavelet features capturing fine-grained structural heterogeneity.
contribution: Achieves lowest ECE across benchmarks, outperforming baselines by up to 41.2% while remaining computationally efficient across diverse graph sizes.

problem: Discrete diffusion LLM decoding faces substantial computational overhead despite lower latency than autoregressive approaches.
approach: Hierarchy-dLLM recursively partitions masked spans into smaller decoding areas, decoding by confidence to increase tokens per forward pass.
contribution: Up to 17x faster than vanilla decoding and 1.5x faster than Fast-dLLM with accuracy comparable or surpassing baselines.

problem: Designing implantable brain-machine interfaces that achieve high accuracy, strong generalization, and low computational cost under strict power and hardware constraints remains impractical despite large-scale neural activity datasets.
approach: The paper proposes Re-parametrized self-Attention Spiking Neural Network (RAT SNN) with multi-timescale dynamic spiking neurons and spike-driven attention in a lightweight architecture, combined with a stepwise pretraining framework that integrates neural variability across conditions including temporal drift, subjects, and tasks.
contribution: RAT SNN consistently outperforms SNN baselines and matches state-of-the-art ANN models with much lower computational cost under both seen and unseen conditions.

problem: Multivariate time series anomaly diagnosis, which includes both detection and localization, lacks theoretical insights and effective methods for pinpointing which variables are anomalous in complex systems.
approach: The paper proposes Attention Low-Rank Transformer (ALoRa-T) that applies low-rank regularization to self-attention and introduces ALoRa-Loc, which quantifies interrelationships among time series variables to associate anomalies with specific variables.
contribution: ALoRa-T and ALoRa-Loc significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in both anomaly detection and localization tasks on multivariate time series.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards succeeds on reasoning tasks but cannot easily extend to open-ended generation where there is no unambiguous ground truth, leading to inefficiency and reward hacking.
approach: The paper proposes reinforcement learning with verifiable reference-based rewards (RLVRR) that decomposes rewards into content (core concepts via keywords) and style (stylistic properties via LLM-based verification), combining RL's exploratory strength with SFT's efficiency.
contribution: RLVRR substantially outperforms SFT trained with ten times more data, unifies training of reasoning and open-ended generation, and generalizes more effectively while preserving output diversity across more than 10 benchmarks.

problem: Understanding how neural networks generalize and memorize data, and identifying out-of-distribution samples, requires tools that go beyond analyzing learned representations in isolation.
approach: The paper models neural networks as dynamical systems acting on latent manifolds, deriving a latent vector field from iterative encoding-decoding maps that reveals attractor points emerging from standard training.
contribution: The latent vector field representation enables analyzing generalization and memorization regimes throughout training, extracting prior knowledge from network parameters via attractors without requiring input data, and identifying out-of-distribution samples from their trajectories.

problem: Designing effective trajectory tokenizers for behavior generation in autonomous driving requires understanding how vocabulary properties like coverage, utilization, symmetry, and robustness affect model performance and generalization.
approach: TrajTok combines rule-based vocabulary candidate setup with data-driven filtering and selection, and proposes spatial-aware label smoothing to model similarities between trajectory tokens.
contribution: TrajTok achieves balanced coverage and utilization with good symmetry and robustness, winning first place in the 2025 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge.

problem: Dynamic data pruning accelerates training but introduces inconsistency in importance score comparisons across different model states (score context drift) and biases gradient dynamics through variable selection rates (temporal gradient bias).
approach: RePB performs pruning decisions within local windows using loss scores from near-constant model states, and applies cumulative temporal rescaling to reweight sample losses based on historical selection frequency.
contribution: RePB achieves near-full-dataset accuracy using most reduced data (above 30%) across 16 datasets, 17 models and 13 tasks, providing a robust and scalable approach to efficient deep learning.

problem: Quantum federated learning requires distributed training across heterogeneous quantum computers with varying error properties and circuit depths, which standard approaches cannot accommodate.
approach: Quorus uses a layerwise loss function for training varying-depth quantum models and presents model designs optimizing for shot budget, qubit count, midcircuit measurement, and optimization space.
contribution: Quorus improves testing accuracy by 12.4% on average over state-of-the-art methods on both simulated and real quantum hardware.

problem: Vision language models struggle to generate accurate visual reasoning paths because visual hallucinations cannot be effectively verified or corrected like linguistic reasoning can be.
approach: Visual Contrastive Self-Taught Reasoner (VC-STaR) leverages contrastive VQA pairs of visually similar images with synonymous questions to help VLMs identify relevant visual cues more precisely, then uses these rationales for supervised finetuning.
contribution: VC-STaR outperforms existing self-improving approaches and surpasses models finetuned on state-of-the-art visual reasoning datasets on the VisCoR-55K dataset.

problem: Long chain-of-thought reasoning significantly improves LLM performance on complex tasks but incurs substantial computational and memory costs that limit efficiency and practicality.
approach: The paper proposes a state-transition framework that models reasoning as iterative state updates using linear attention, where each token retrieves relevant historical information from a compressed reasoning state without attending to all previous tokens.
contribution: The framework reduces attention computational complexity from quadratic to linear while improving reasoning performance on multiple datasets and model sizes.

problem: Transformers face severe computational and memory bottlenecks when processing long sequences, and existing sparse attention methods introduce excessive parameters and disrupt the standard pretrain-short-finetune-long workflow.
approach: Dense-Sparse Switchable Attention (DSSA) reuses dense attention parameters through parameter-free architecture modification, using dense attention for short inputs and transitioning smoothly to sparse attention for long sequences.
contribution: DSSA achieves 4x speedup over dense attention while retaining 98.1% performance on long-context understanding and 99.7% on chain-of-thought reasoning.

problem: Test-time reinforcement learning relies on constructing reliable learning signals, but standard approaches like majority voting collapse to spurious popular answers rather than correct ones.
