approach: Self-Harmony uses a single model in two roles: a Solver producing answers and a Reframer rephrasing inputs, then aggregates answer frequencies across original and reframed views using the harmonic mean to select solutions stable under reframing.
contribution: Self-Harmony achieves state-of-the-art results in label-free test-time settings, ranking first in 28 of 30 settings, with zero training failures across all experiments.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models rely on non-differentiable Top-k+Softmax routing that conflates the decisions of which experts to activate and how to distribute contributions among them.
approach: Dirichlet-Routed MoE (DirMoE) uses a fully differentiable routing mechanism built on a Dirichlet variational autoencoder, disentangling expert selection (via Bernoulli) from expert contribution distribution (via Dirichlet).
contribution: DirMoE matches or exceeds other methods while improving expert specialization and enabling precise control of active expert counts through a direct sparsity penalty.

problem: Deep reinforcement learning is vulnerable to environmental uncertainties that limit deployment in real-world scenarios, and existing distributionally robust RL algorithms are restricted to value-based methods in tabular settings.
approach: Distributionally Robust Soft Actor-Critic (DR-SAC) maximizes entropy-regularized rewards against worst-case transition models within a KL-divergence constrained uncertainty set using actor-critic learning.
contribution: DR-SAC achieves up to 9.8x higher average reward than SAC baseline under common perturbations and significantly improves computational efficiency compared to existing DR-RL algorithms.

problem: Multi-agent systems driven by LLMs may enable collective financial fraud, but the risks and dynamics of such behavior remain unexplored.
approach: The paper introduces MultiAgentFraudBench, simulating 21 typical online fraud scenarios covering the full fraud lifecycle, and analyzes fraud dynamics including interaction depth, hype-building effects, and collaboration failures.
contribution: The work demonstrates real-world dangers of multi-agent fraud and proposes mitigation strategies including monitor agents and group resilience through information sharing.

problem: Integrating paired texts with time series remains underdeveloped despite advances in LLMs and time series learning, particularly when capturing periodic properties shared between text and numerical data.
approach: Texts as Time Series (TaTS) treats time-series-paired texts as auxiliary variables, enabling any numerical-only time series model to handle multimodal data by leveraging periodic properties shared between modalities.
contribution: TaTS enhances multimodal predictive performance on forecasting and imputation tasks without modifying model architectures across various benchmark datasets.

problem: Long-horizon embodied planning is challenging because exogenous processes (e.g., water heating, dominoes cascading) unfold concurrently with agent actions, and standard models only account for endogenous effects.
approach: ExoPredicator learns abstract world models with symbolic state representations and causal processes for both endogenous actions and exogenous mechanisms via variational Bayesian inference combined with LLM proposals.
contribution: The learned models enable fast planning that generalizes to held-out tasks with more objects and more complex goals, outperforming baselines on five simulated tabletop robotics environments.

problem: Progress in LLM-generated mathematical proof generation is hindered by the lack of a large-scale, high-quality dataset of human-evaluated proofs and understanding of gaps between natural language and formal proofs.
approach: The Open Proof Corpus (OPC) provides over 5,000 human-evaluated proofs from state-of-the-art LLMs on problems from USAMO and IMO, enabling analysis of natural-to-formal proof gaps and best-of-n selection strategies.
contribution: The OPC allows finetuning an 8B model to match Gemini-2.5-Pro and perform close to GPT-5 on proof correctness evaluation.

problem: Multi-agent communication must balance task performance, communication efficiency, and human interpretability, creating a fundamental trilemma difficult to resolve.
approach: Grounding Language and Contrastive learning (GLC) framework learns discretized communication symbols via autoencoder, aligns them semantically with human concepts using LLM-generated data, and applies contrastive learning to ensure consistency across agents.
contribution: GLC outperforms state-of-the-art methods delivering superior task performance, higher communication efficiency, and enhanced human interpretability across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Story generation by LLMs diverges from human-authored works regarding complex narrative structure and human-aligned preferences due to absence of effective modeling of subjective human story preferences.
approach: StoryRMB benchmark assesses reward models on story preferences with 1,133 instances, and StoryReward is developed as an advanced reward model trained on roughly 100,000 high-quality story preference pairs.
contribution: StoryReward achieves state-of-the-art performance on StoryRMB, outperforming much larger models, and performs well in downstream best-of-n story selection applications.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning overestimates the value of out-of-distribution actions; existing penalization methods fail to accurately identify OOD actions and may suppress beneficial exploration.
approach: DOSER trains two diffusion models for behavior policy and state distribution using single-step denoising reconstruction error as OOD indicator, then selectively suppresses risky actions while encouraging exploration of high-potential ones during policy optimization.
contribution: DOSER proves to be a gamma-contraction with bounded value estimates and consistently attains superior performance on offline RL benchmarks, especially on suboptimal datasets.

problem: Automatic stage lighting control has been treated as a classification task mapping music to predefined patterns, resulting in formulaic outcomes that lack rationality and fail to match human engineer performance.
approach: Skip-BART adapts the BART model to take audio music as input and produce light hue and intensity as output, incorporating a novel skip connection mechanism and using pre-training and transfer learning techniques.
contribution: Skip-BART outperforms conventional rule-based methods across all evaluation metrics and shows only limited gap compared to real lighting engineers.

problem: Multi-view clustering suffers from noisy correspondence in real-world web-collected datasets, where category-level mismatch and sample-level misalignment break cross-view consistency assumptions.
approach: CorreGen formulates noisy correspondence learning as maximum likelihood estimation via Expectation-Maximization, inferring soft correspondence distributions in the E-step and updating embeddings in the M-step with GMM-guided marginals.
contribution: CorreGen significantly improves clustering robustness on both synthetic and real-world noisy datasets.

problem: Temporal graphs with noisy neighbors and complex temporal dynamics suffer from unreliable information propagation, and existing methods fail to handle severe noise and long-term dependencies due to constrained sampling scope.
approach: Temporal Graph Thumbnail (TGT) extracts a temporal graph's global evolutionary skeleton using von Neumann graph entropy and node mutual information to characterize temporal regularities and enhance robustness.
contribution: TGT achieves superior capability and robustness compared to baselines, particularly in rapidly evolving and noisy environments.

problem: Analyzing posterior sampling techniques for reinforcement learning remains a challenge, especially in complex settings like episodic MDPs.
approach: Q-Learning with Posterior Sampling (PSQL) uses Gaussian posteriors on Q-values for exploration, adapting Thompson Sampling principles to the Q-learning setting.
contribution: PSQL achieves a regret bound of O-tilde(H^2*sqrt(SAT)) that closely matches the known lower bound, with novel technical insights for combining posterior sampling with dynamic programming and TD-learning.

problem: Existing incomplete multi-view clustering methods lack explicit alignment and collaborative interaction between view recovery and subspace representation learning in exploring complementarity and consistency.
approach: ARSL-IMVC infers complete views from view-shared latent representation and view-specific estimators with HSIC regularization, then learns subspace representations modeling high-order correlations in unified low-rank tensor space.
contribution: ARSL-IMVC demonstrates powerful capacity in complex incomplete multi-view clustering tasks across seven datasets.

problem: Federated learning for quantile inference under local differential privacy must handle data heterogeneity while maintaining statistical efficiency and privacy guarantees.
approach: The paper proposes an SGD-based estimator with local gradients perturbed via a randomized mechanism with global parameters, establishing asymptotic normality and functional central limit theorems.
contribution: The method accommodates data heterogeneity with individual privacy budgets and constructs confidence intervals via self-normalization without estimating nuisance parameters.

problem: Logical specifications for reinforcement learning may be under-specified, leading to agents failing to learn useful policies despite specification satisfaction.
approach: AutoSpec searches for logical specification refinements via exploration-guided strategy, exploiting compositional nature of SpectRL specifications to introduce new edge specifications or refine existing ones.
contribution: AutoSpec yields improvements in solving more complex control tasks when refined specifications are utilized with RL algorithms.

problem: Image denoising when noise level is unknown and varies across training data requires methods that don't depend on knowing the noise model a priori.
approach: The paper introduces a resource-efficient neural network architecture with zero divergence by design, enabling self-supervised learning via Stein's unbiased risk estimation.
contribution: The divergence-free architecture retains sufficient expressivity to remain competitive while outperforming divergence-based approaches when noise level is unknown and varies.

problem: Inference scaling for LLMs in Pass@k settings requires selecting k responses, but neither majority voting nor Best-of-N exhibits desirable scaling with k and sampling budget N.
approach: Best-of-Majority (BoM) restricts candidates to high-frequency responses before selecting top-k rewards, combining advantages of majority voting and BoN.
contribution: BoM achieves minimax-optimal regret with a sampling budget of N=O-tilde(C*), unlike majority voting and BoN whose performance degrades with increased N.

problem: Current AI agent benchmarks either do not measure real-world tasks or are not sufficiently difficult to meaningfully measure frontier models.
approach: Terminal-Bench comprises 74 hard tasks in command line environments inspired by real workflows, with unique environments, human-written solutions, and comprehensive tests for verification.
contribution: Frontier models and agents score less than 50% on the benchmark; error analysis identifies areas for model and agent improvement.

problem: LLM safety can be compromised by superficial style patterns in queries (e.g., formatting) that are semantically irrelevant to malicious intent, creating a blind spot in alignment procedures.
approach: SafeStyle incorporates style-aware safety training data during fine-tuning, where safety data is augmented to match the distribution of style patterns in instruction-tuning data.
contribution: SafeStyle consistently outperforms baselines in maintaining LLM safety across three LLMs, six fine-tuning style settings, and two real-world instruction-tuning datasets.

problem: Imitation learning for end-to-end driving lacks recovery data for closed-loop deployment, causing small mistakes to compound into failures, while existing data augmentation methods are prohibitively slow.
approach: 3D Rasterization replaces costly rendering with lightweight rasterization of annotated primitives, enabling counterfactual recovery maneuvers and cross-agent view synthesis, combined with Raster-to-Real feature-space alignment.
contribution: RAP ranks 1st on four major benchmarks: NAVSIM v1/v2, Waymo Open Dataset Vision-based E2E Driving, and Bench2Drive for closed-loop robustness and long-tail generalization.

problem: Long chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs is computationally expensive due to unnecessary reasoning steps that don't contribute to the final answer.
approach: FROST leverages attention weights to identify and prune uncritical reasoning paths, introducing the concept of reasoning outliers and removing them at the sentence level.
contribution: FROST achieves 69.68% average reduction in token usage and 26.70% improvement in accuracy over the base model on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: LLMs can exhibit concept-conditioned semantic divergence where common high-level cues elicit uniform stance-like responses that evade token-trigger audits, representing a blind spot in current safety evaluations.
approach: RAVEN couples semantic entropy over paraphrastic samples with cross-model disagreement to flag cases where a model is simultaneously highly certain and atypical among peers.
contribution: RAVEN surfaces recurrent, model-specific divergences in 9 of 12 sensitive topics across five LLM families, providing an early-warning signal for propaganda-like influence.

problem: Real-world image restoration faces heterogeneous degradations and requires balancing fidelity and realism, while posterior sampling typically requires a known forward operator that is rarely available.
approach: LearnIR trains a lightweight model to predict gradient correction distributions enabling Diffusion Posterior Sampling Correction, and introduces Dynamic Resolution Module to preserve structures and refine textures.
contribution: LearnIR achieves state-of-the-art performance in PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS on ISTD, O-HAZE, HazyDet, REVIDE, and FaceShadow datasets.

problem: Understanding how reinforcement learning agents discover and represent plans internally remains opaque, limiting our ability to predict and control learned behaviors.
approach: The paper reverse-engineers a convolutional RNN trained on Sokoban, identifying path channels storing future moves and extension kernels encoding transition models and backtracking through negative values.
contribution: The precise plan representation reveals how model-free RL implicitly learns a bidirectional planning algorithm in more familiar terms.

problem: Diffusion model alignment for downstream objectives often suffers from reward over-optimization and mode collapse when using RL or direct backpropagation.
approach: Diffusion Alignment as Variational EM (DAV) formulates alignment as iterative E-step and M-step, where E-step generates diverse reward-aligned samples via test-time search and M-step refines the model.
contribution: DAV optimizes reward while preserving diversity on both continuous (text-to-image) and discrete (DNA sequence design) tasks.

problem: Generating complex 3D physical scenes requires modeling both spatial placement and physical properties like contact, support, balance, and containment, which standard layout generation overlooks.
approach: PhyScensis uses an LLM agent powered by a physics engine to iteratively propose assets with spatial and physical predicates, with a solver realizing predicates into 3D scenes and feedback guiding refinement.
contribution: PhyScensis produces physically plausible scene configurations with high complexity while preserving fine-grained controllability through textual descriptions and numerical parameters.

problem: Generative models applied to scientific problems lack guarantees that generated outputs satisfy known physical constraints, limiting deployment in scientific and engineering applications.
approach: Split Augmented Langevin (SAL) enforces constraints through variable splitting and primal-dual sampling with theoretical convergence guarantees, applicable to both Langevin dynamics and diffusion models.
contribution: Constrained diffusion models generate physical fields satisfying energy and mass conservation laws, substantially improving forecast accuracy in diffusion-based data assimilation.

problem: Learning distributions over permutations typically relies on expensive variational inference or mixtures of restricted parametric families, limiting expressivity and computational efficiency.
approach: The paper proposes leveraging alternative permutation representations (Lehmer codes, Fisher-Yates draws, Insertion-Vectors) forming bijections with the symmetric group, enabling unconstrained deep learning.
contribution: The method significantly outperforms current approaches on jigsaw puzzle benchmarks and enables learning non-trivial distributions on cyclic permutations and movie re-ranking tasks.

problem: Content-aware video streaming requires dynamic chunk-level importance weights for quality optimization, but direct human annotation is prohibitively expensive and vision-saliency models generalize poorly.
approach: HiVid uses LLMs as a scalable proxy to generate high-fidelity saliency weights by: (1) perceiving frames in local context windows autoregressively; (2) ranking windows globally with an LLM-guided merge-sort for VOD; (3) predicting future weights with a multi-modal time series model for live streaming.
contribution: HiVid improves weight prediction accuracy by up to 11.5% for VOD and 26% for live streaming over SOTA, and boosts QoE correlation by 14.7% in user studies.

problem: Parallel decoding methods enable faster text generation than autoregressive models but sacrifice quality because they struggle to model the complex joint distribution of token sequences.
approach: Gumbel Distillation uses the Gumbel-Max trick to create a deterministic mapping from latent noise to teacher outputs, enabling parallel decoders to learn the joint distribution without modifying architecture.
contribution: Gumbel Distillation achieves 30.0% improvement in MAUVE Score and 10.5% in generative perplexity over MDLM on OpenWebText.

problem: Training expressive policy classes (diffusion, flow-matching) with online RL is unstable because their parameterization by long denoising chains hinders gradient propagation when optimizing against value functions.
approach: EXPO avoids direct value optimization over the expressive policy and instead constructs an on-the-fly policy: a base policy trained with stable imitation learning plus a lightweight Gaussian edit policy that edits actions toward higher value.
contribution: EXPO achieves 2-3x improvement in sample efficiency over prior methods in fine-tuning and leveraging offline data settings.

problem: Existing text-rich image understanding benchmarks lack systematic evaluation of MLLMs' reasoning capabilities in complex visual-textual scenarios and provide only final answers without step-by-step reasoning traces.
approach: OCR-Reasoning provides 1,069 human-annotated examples with detailed step-by-step reasoning traces spanning 6 reasoning abilities and 18 practical tasks, enabling holistic evaluation of both answers and reasoning processes.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation shows advanced MLLMs exhibit substantial difficulties in text-rich reasoning, with none achieving 50% accuracy, revealing an urgent gap to address.

problem: Existing cortical representation learning methods are stage-specific and lack generalization across the lifespan due to non-Euclidean cortical surfaces, homogenization from registration, and distribution shifts across ages.
approach: CortiLife introduces a surface tokenizer with icosahedron-based patchification and multi-level encoding to transform cortical manifolds into token representations, combined with masked self-distillation and metadata language prompting for age-aware modeling.
contribution: CortiLife is the first unified vision-language framework achieving lifespan-aware cortical representation learning across distribution shifts.

problem: LLMs are trained on massive corpora including private, copyrighted, or harmful data, but completely retraining to exclude these is prohibitively expensive.
approach: MSA leverages prior model checkpoints from pretraining to estimate and counteract the effect of targeted datapoints using model state arithmetic.
contribution: MSA achieves competitive or better performance than existing machine unlearning algorithms across multiple benchmarks, models, and metrics.

problem: Fine-tuning non-robust pretrained models with a robust objective leads to poor performance and potential transfer failure due to impedance of task adaptation.
approach: Epsilon-Scheduling uses a schedule over perturbation strength during training to promote optimal transfer, and introduces expected robustness metric capturing performance across perturbation ranges.
contribution: Epsilon-Scheduling prevents suboptimal transfer and consistently improves expected robustness across six pretrained models and five datasets.

problem: Most reasoning models do not extrapolate well at test-time, failing to improve performance on hard problems when allowed to think longer beyond training token budgets.
approach: e3 trains LLMs to perform in-context exploration by: (1) chaining asymmetric skills; (2) using negative gradients to amplify exploration; (3) coupling task difficulty with training token budget via curriculum.
contribution: e3-1.7B achieves best known scores on AIME'25 and HMMT'25 and extrapolates to 2x the training token budget.

problem: Vehicle routing relies on expert-crafted heuristics and massive foundation models, but smaller fine-tuned LLMs' potential for designing superior operators is underexplored.
approach: RFTHGS uses RL to fine-tune a compact LLM to generate crossover operators for Hybrid Genetic Search, with curriculum-based rewards progressing from compilable to executable to superior-performing operators.
contribution: Fine-tuned LLM generates crossover operators exceeding expert designs and outperforming GPT-4o on CVRP instances up to 1000 nodes.

problem: Jointly training LLMs on multiple reasoning datasets creates conflicts between tasks, degrading performance compared to single-dataset fine-tuning.
approach: The framework identifies exclusive and overlapped parameters per task via parameter variation analysis, then updates them differentially to preserve benefits while avoiding conflicts.
contribution: Differential fine-tuning achieves consistent improvements on mix-up and continual SFT across Llama3-8B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-14B on diverse reasoning tasks.

problem: Self-supervised novel view synthesis models predict poses that do not transfer across scenes, failing the key criterion of transferability for true NVS capability.
approach: XFactor combines pair-wise pose estimation with input/output augmentation to disentangle camera pose from scene content without 3D inductive biases, using latent pose variables instead of SE(3) parameterization.
contribution: XFactor achieves true transferability with latent poses and significantly outperforms prior pose-free NVS transformers.

problem: Reliably composing LLMs for complex multi-step workflows remains brittle, and discrete prompt optimization struggles to enforce formal compliance for structured tasks.
approach: TACs treat the entire workflow as an unnormalized joint distribution and enable gradient-based training of typed probabilistic programs through parameter-efficient adaptation and deterministic logic.
contribution: TACs improve FinQA from 12.0% to 24.7%, MGSM-SymPy from 57.1% to 75.9%, and MuSR from 36.5% to 62.6%.

problem: Deep reasoning paradigms struggle in open-ended generation because RL lacks clear reward signals and high-quality models, while distillation is expensive and capped by teacher capabilities.
approach: REER works backwards from known solutions to computationally discover latent step-by-step reasoning that produces them, creating DeepWriting-20K dataset of 20,000 deep reasoning trajectories.
contribution: DeepWriter-8B trained on REER data surpasses open-source baselines and achieves competitive or superior performance to GPT-4o and Claude 3.5.

problem: Speculative decoding itself relies on sequential dependence between speculation and verification phases, creating a bottleneck in parallel token generation.
approach: Speculative Speculative Decoding (SSD) parallelizes by having the draft model predict likely verification outcomes pre-emptively; Saguaro implements this with principled methods to handle key challenges after theoretical analysis.
contribution: Saguaro is up to 2x faster than speculative decoding and 5x faster than autoregressive decoding.

problem: Goal-conditioned RL agents learn goal representations tied to specific state spaces that fail to generalize to different environments.
approach: Dual goal representations characterize states through temporal distances to all other states, depending only on environment dynamics and invariant to state representation, enabling provably sufficient information for optimal policies.
contribution: Dual representations consistently improve offline goal-reaching performance across 20 OGBench tasks.

problem: Recurrent neural networks for 3D reconstruction perform well within training context length but degrade significantly when applied beyond it, revealing limited length generalization.
approach: TTT3R leverages test-time training by using alignment confidence between memory state and observations to derive a closed-form learning rate for memory updates, balancing historical retention and adaptation.
contribution: TTT3R achieves 2x improvement in global pose estimation over baselines while operating at 20 FPS with 6 GB GPU memory.

problem: Serving LLMs at scale requires efficient KV cache management, but stale caches consume scarce GPU memory and either require offloading or recomputation.
approach: KVTC combines PCA-based feature decorrelation, adaptive quantization, and entropy coding to compress KV caches with only brief calibration.
contribution: KVTC achieves up to 20x compression while maintaining accuracy on reasoning and long-context tasks across Llama 3.1, Mistral-NeMo, and R1-Qwen 2.5.

problem: Molecular generative models are not guaranteed to generate synthesizable molecules, and existing solutions struggle to effectively navigate the exponentially large combinatorial space.
approach: ReaSyn iteratively refines synthetic pathways by: (1) bottom-up and top-down traversal of synthetic trees; (2) discrete flow model edits at pathway level; (3) unified autoregressive model for both directions.
contribution: ReaSyn achieves highest reconstruction rate, pathway diversity, and optimization performance in synthesizable molecule tasks.

problem: General-purpose VLMs like GPT-4 excel at generalization but controlling humanoid agents requires translating high-level instructions into low-level control while adapting to physical feedback.
approach: BiBo combines an embodied instruction compiler using chain of visual question answering to guide VLMs in specifying control parameters, with a diffusion-based motion executor.
contribution: BiBo achieves 90.2% task success rate and improves text-guided motion precision by 16.3% over prior methods.

problem: Reasoning LLMs generate chain-of-thought traces to improve transparency, but their robustness to disruptions within reasoning traces remains unclear.
approach: The paper introduces a controlled evaluation framework applying seven interventions (benign, neutral, adversarial) at fixed timesteps and analyzing recovery mechanisms across MATH, SCIENCE, and LOGIC tasks.
contribution: RLLMs are generally robust with recovery improving by model size and decreasing with early interventions; paraphrasing suppresses doubt expressions reducing performance by over 200%.

problem: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) for physiological measurement is susceptible to illumination changes and motion artifacts, and LLMs struggle with continuous noise-sensitive signals due to text-centric design.
approach: PhysLLM bridges LLMs and rPPG via: (1) Text Prototype Guidance projecting features into semantic space; (2) Dual-Domain Stationary algorithm for signal stability; (3) physiological priors injected through statistics and task descriptions.
contribution: PhysLLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness on benchmark datasets with superior generalization across lighting and motion variations.

problem: Large Reasoning Models generate over-long chains-of-thought with excessive reflections and circular reasoning, consuming high tokens without improving accuracy.
approach: ARLCP uses RL with adaptive reflection penalty that curtails unnecessary steps while preserving essential reasoning, plus length penalty calibrated to problem complexity.
contribution: ARLCP reduces response length by 53.1% while improving accuracy by 5.8% for 1.5B models, and achieves 35.0% reduction for 7B models.

problem: Pseudolabeling in long-tailed semi-supervised learning amplifies bias through a vicious cycle, and existing logit adjustment methods ignore semantic relationships between classes causing intra-super-class imbalance.
approach: SCAD performs dynamic super-class-aware logit adjustment leveraging latent semantic structure to focus correction on confusable groups.
contribution: SCAD achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-tailed semi-supervised learning benchmarks.

problem: Measuring LLM persuasive capabilities is challenging because human persuasion effectiveness varies across domains, yet understanding and evaluating this is critical.
approach: The framework grounds evaluation in Bayesian Persuasion theory, repurposing human-human datasets to construct environments for evaluating and training LLMs in strategic persuasion.
contribution: Frontier models achieve high persuasion gains with sophisticated strategies aligned to theory; RL training improves even small LLMs significantly.

problem: Physical simulation requires spatially-varying mechanical properties that are typically laboriously hand-crafted, limiting automation in content creation and scientific applications.
approach: VoMP is a feed-forward model predicting Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and density throughout object volumes by aggregating multi-view features and mapping to a trained material manifold.
contribution: VoMP estimates accurate volumetric properties enabling simulation-ready asset conversion with realistic deformable simulations.

problem: Diffusion Transformers have quadratic training cost with sequence length, making large-scale pretraining prohibitively expensive despite state-of-the-art generative performance.
approach: SPRINT enables aggressive token dropping (up to 75%) by using shallow layers for local detail on all tokens, deep sparse layers for computation reduction, and residual fusion with two-stage training.
contribution: SPRINT achieves 9.8x training savings with comparable FID/FDD on ImageNet-1K 256×256, and halves FLOPs at inference.

problem: Multi-source data integration for time-to-event outcomes is underdeveloped when populations are heterogeneous and privacy constraints prevent direct data pooling.
approach: The federated method dynamically re-weights source contributions to correct distributional shifts while preserving privacy, leveraging semiparametric efficiency theory and double robustness.
contribution: Method demonstrated validity and efficiency gains on multi-site HIV prevention trials and all-cause mortality analysis.

problem: Constructing coresets for LASSO regression via sensitivity sampling requires size scaling with total sensitivity and VC dimension, but capturing the sparse l1 penalty structure is challenging.
approach: The paper provides empirical process-based sensitivity sampling localizing the functional space into independent subspaces and leveraging geometric properties for tight bounds.
contribution: Achieves coreset size Õ(ε⁻²d·((log d)³·min(1,log d/λ²)+log(1/δ))) with matching lower bounds in certain regimes.

problem: AI systems lack large-scale benchmarks for smell recognition, limiting progress in allergen detection, manufacturing monitoring, and biomarker sensing.
approach: SmellNet uses portable gas and chemical sensors to create the first large-scale database with 828,000 data points across 50 substances and 43 mixtures; ScentFormer combines temporal differencing and sliding-window augmentation.
contribution: ScentFormer achieves 58.5% Top-1 accuracy on SmellNet-BASE classification and 50.2% Top-1@0.1 on mixture distribution prediction.

problem: Generic object tracking methods rely on 2D features and lack 3D geometric cues, making them susceptible to partial occlusion, distractors, and appearance/geometry variations.
approach: GOT-Edit integrates geometry-aware cues via online cross-modality model editing using null-space constrained updates that incorporate geometric information while preserving semantic discrimination.
contribution: GOT-Edit achieves superior robustness and accuracy across GOT benchmarks, particularly under occlusion and clutter.

problem: Weather foundation models excel at numerical reasoning but lack language-based reasoning for interactive scientific workflows, while LLMs cannot reason about high-dimensional meteorological datasets.
approach: Zephyrus is an agentic framework with ZephyrusWorld environment featuring tools for weather data, geoquerying, forecasting, and climate simulation, enabling multi-turn LLM agents.
contribution: Zephyrus outperforms text-only baselines by up to 35 percentage points on ZephyrusBench which includes tasks from basic lookups to advanced forecasting.

problem: Adapting Vision-Language Models to decentralized heterogeneous data is challenging because existing federated prompt tuning methods sacrifice generalization for personalization.
approach: pFedMMA leverages multi-modal adapters with modality-specific projections and globally shared projection aligning cross-modal features, allowing local adaptation while training shared components.
contribution: pFedMMA achieves state-of-the-art personalization-generalization trade-offs across eleven datasets including domain- and label-shift scenarios.

problem: Generalized linear bandits assume the reward function is known, but misspecification of the link function leads to algorithm failure in realistic settings.
approach: Single index bandits address this by treating unknown reward functions as latent variables; STOR and ESTOR are proposed for monotonic functions, GSTOR for general functions.
contribution: ESTOR achieves nearly optimal regret bound Õ(√T) and extends to high-dimensional sparse settings.

problem: RL training of VLMs suffers from severe system-level bottlenecks: centralized data loading creates I/O bottlenecks and heterogeneous sequence lengths cause load imbalance.
approach: FlexRL introduces decentralized data pipeline parallelizing fetch/preprocessing and hybrid sequence sharding enabling sub-sequence level load balancing for both inference and training.
contribution: FlexRL achieves 4.2-7.7x end-to-end speedups on 128-GPU cluster compared to production baselines.

problem: Conformal prediction provides marginal coverage guarantees but fails to account for algorithmic biases, undermining fairness and trust.
approach: The framework constructs prediction sets guaranteeing conditional coverage on adaptively identified subgroups, balancing effectiveness and efficiency.
contribution: Approach achieves compact prediction sets with adaptive equalized coverage across unfairly treated subgroups.

problem: Training large reasoning models via SFT+RLVR is constrained by reliance on high-quality annotated data and external verifiers, limiting application to unverifiable tasks.
approach: Native Reasoning Training (NRT) treats reasoning as a latent variable and employs unified training that rewards paths increasing likelihood of correct answers, creating self-correcting loops.
contribution: NRT achieves state-of-the-art performance among verifier-free methods, significantly outperforming standard approaches on Llama and Mistral families.

problem: Trajectory planning for autonomous driving is challenging due to behavioral uncertainty and complex multi-agent interactions; existing methods generate trajectories without exploiting scene evolution.
approach: OccDriver uses dual-branch coarse-to-fine decoding: vectorized branch generates multimodal trajectories, rasterized branch predicts future occupancy, then vectorized refines using occupancy feedback.
contribution: OccDriver achieves state-of-the-art on nuPlan in both Non-Reactive and Reactive closed-loop performance.

problem: Quantized neural networks resist pixel-level attacks but remain vulnerable to patch-based adversarial attacks which transfer highly across bit-widths.
approach: TriQDef disrupts transferability via: (1) Feature Disalignment Penalty enforcing semantic inconsistency; (2) Gradient Perceptual Dissonance Penalty misaligning gradients; (3) shared backbone across quantizers.
contribution: TriQDef lowers Attack Success Rates by over 40% on unseen patch and quantization combinations while preserving clean accuracy.

problem: MeanFlow framework for few-step generative modeling achieves strong results but its success mechanisms are not fully understood, with optimization objectives in conflict.
approach: AlphaFlow decomposes MeanFlow into trajectory flow matching and consistency, identifies negative correlation causing optimization conflict, and introduces curriculum strategy smoothly annealing objectives.
contribution: AlphaFlow-XL/2+ achieves state-of-the-art on ImageNet-1K 256×256 with FID 2.58 (1-NFE) and 2.15 (2-NFE).

problem: Next-token prediction struggles with long-horizon reasoning and creative writing due to teacher-forced training, and multi-token prediction offers limited improvements by capturing only short-range dependencies.
approach: Future Summary Prediction (FSP) trains an auxiliary head predicting compact future representations (handcrafted bags-of-words or learned reverse-LM embeddings) preserving long-term information.
contribution: FSP improves over both NTP and MTP on math, reasoning, and coding benchmarks across 3B and 8B models.

problem: Long-horizon robot manipulation with deformable objects fails due to inconsistent demonstration quality and frame-index-based labeling brittleness.
approach: A stage-aware reward model predicts task stage and progress using natural-language subtask annotations, then filters demonstrations via Reward-Aligned Behavior Cloning.
contribution: Achieves 83% success on T-shirt folding from flattened state and 67% from crumpled, compared to 8% and 0% with vanilla BC.

problem: Natural language vehicle control must handle ambiguous commands and evolving dialogue context while maintaining protocol compliance.
approach: Unified framework combining agent-orchestrated data augmentation pipeline, reference models, and evaluation protocol to generate and assess diverse ambiguity-rich dialogues.
contribution: Achieves 15% higher parsing accuracy, 20% stronger ambiguity resolution, and 98% protocol compliance on realistic in-cabin scenarios.

problem: LLM steering requires either suboptimal signals from labeled examples or hundreds of examples with task-specific optimization procedures.
approach: COLD-Steer approximates gradient descent effects at inference time using unit kernel approximation or finite-difference methods without parameter updates.
contribution: Achieves up to 95% steering effectiveness using 50 times fewer samples than baselines.

problem: Imperfect-information games like Fog of War chess require reasoning about information gathering and opponent knowledge beyond standard search.
approach: Obscuro advances search in imperfect-information games through improved algorithms for scalable reasoning without common knowledge.
contribution: First superhuman AI for FoW chess, significantly stronger than prior state-of-the-art and human players including world's best.

problem: Multimodal LLMs hallucinate emotions, generating irrelevant content despite lacking innate emotional instincts.
approach: EmotionHallucer benchmark evaluates emotion hallucinations via adversarial QA framework grounded in emotion psychology and real-world perception.
contribution: Finds most current models exhibit substantial emotion hallucinations, with closed-source outperforming open-source and reasoning improving performance.

problem: High-resolution visual representation learning fails due to quadratic complexity of Vision Transformers and fixed scanning patterns in Mamba-based models.
approach: InfoScan learns adaptive scanning policy via reinforcement learning, assessing informativeness through entropy and local structural analysis.
contribution: Achieves superior efficiency-accuracy trade-offs across diverse tasks via information-driven dynamic scanning.

problem: Token-wise layer skipping in LLMs suffers from instability in early-exit and router-based methods requiring extensive retraining.
approach: GateSkip uses residual-stream sigmoid-linear gates on each Attention/MLP branch, enabling per-layer token skipping via gate-based ranking.
contribution: Saves up to 15% compute while retaining >90% accuracy on long-form reasoning, with stable fine-tuning on pretrained models.

problem: Training VAEs from scratch emphasizes low-level details over semantic structure for diffusion model tokenizers.
approach: AlignTok aligns pretrained visual encoders via three-stage strategy: frozen adapter-decoder, joint optimization with semantic loss, decoder refinement.
contribution: Reaches gFID of 1.90 on ImageNet 256x256 in 64 epochs, outperforming FLUX VAE and VA-VAE on text-to-image models.

problem: Molecular representations fail to capture stereochemistry and complex features at fragment level due to atom-level graphs and fixed fragment libraries.
approach: h-MINT uses OverlapBPE tokenization allowing overlapping fragments plus hierarchical model jointly capturing drug-target interactions at atom and fragment levels.
contribution: Improves binding affinity prediction by 2-4% Pearson/Spearman correlation, enhances virtual screening by 1-3% on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Reasoning language models self-jailbreak by introducing benign assumptions to justify harmful requests despite safety training.
approach: Mechanistic analysis reveals RLMs use compliance from benign reasoning training to circumvent safety guardrails by reframing harmful requests.
contribution: Shows minimal safety reasoning data during training ensures RLMs remain safety-aligned despite self-jailbreaking tendency.

problem: fMRI decoding and concept grounding struggle to capture interacting concepts and hierarchical structure from neural activity.
approach: NEURONA neuro-symbolic framework learns to decode interacting concepts via hierarchical predicate-argument dependencies grounded in fMRI.
contribution: Incorporating structure improves both decoding accuracy and generalization across brain regions.

problem: State-of-the-art policy gradient methods for text-to-image model alignment suffer from training instability and high variance due to disproportionate credit assignment.
approach: PCPO enforces proportional credit assignment through stable objective reformulation and principled timestep reweighting to mitigate model collapse.
contribution: Substantially outperforms DanceGRPO with faster convergence and superior image quality through mitigating recursive training failures.

problem: Existing time-series explanation methods fail to capture temporal context, producing fragmented point-wise explanations lacking interpretable segment boundaries.
approach: TimeSeg uses information-theoretic framework with reinforcement learning to identify contiguous subsequences maximizing mutual information with predictions.
contribution: Produces more coherent and human-understandable segment-wise explanations capturing holistic temporal patterns.

problem: Self-attention mechanisms cannot perform polyadic tasks requiring detecting correlated token triples or compositional references.
approach: Poly-attention defines generalizations of self-attention enabling arbitrary higher-order tensor computations with systematic complexity analysis.
contribution: Provides tight complexity bounds and representational strength analysis, revealing trade-offs between expressiveness and approximation time.

problem: Fine-tuning-based concept erasure is time-consuming for multiple concepts, while real-time editing degrades non-target generation quality.
approach: SPEED edits model parameters by searching null space where updates don't affect non-targets, using influence filtering, prior augmentation, and invariant constraints.
contribution: Erases 100 concepts in 5 seconds with consistent non-target preservation outperforming existing methods.

problem: Individual vision foundation models excel in specific domains but lack generality across diverse robot tasks.
approach: VER distills multiple VFMs into expert library, fine-tuning lightweight routing network for dynamic task-relevant expert selection via patchwise routing.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 17 diverse robotic tasks with fewer than 0.4% parameters requiring fine-tuning.

problem: Local navigation policies fail to generalize across robot morphologies due to embodiment-specific dynamics and multi-modal decision problems.
approach: CE-Nav decouples universal geometric reasoning via embodiment-agnostic VelFlow from dynamics adaptation via lightweight refiner using online RL.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on quadrupeds, bipeds, quadrotors with minimal adaptation cost and successful real-world deployment.

problem: Chunked critics for multi-step value propagation require open-loop policy execution over full action chunks, causing sub-optimality in reactive environments.
approach: Decoupled Q-Chunking separates critic and policy chunk lengths via optimistic distillation of partial chunks from original chunked critic.
contribution: Retains multi-step value benefits while avoiding open-loop sub-optimality on long-horizon offline goal-conditioned benchmarks.

problem: Image-to-point cloud registration faces projection ambiguity and scale inconsistency between 2D and 3D representations.
approach: RayI2P predicts patch-wise 3D ray bundles connecting image patches to scene, then estimates pose via differentiable ray-guided regression.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art registration accuracy on KITTI and nuScenes, outperforming existing methods.

problem: Uncertainty quantification via ensembles is computationally expensive, while single-model approximations struggle.
approach: Contextual similarity distillation estimates ensemble variance with single model by reinterpreting ensemble variance as supervised regression with kernel targets.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance to ensemble baselines on out-of-distribution detection and sparse-reward RL.

problem: Scaling visual geometry transformers for long image sequences faces computational and memory bottlenecks due to token collapse in global attention.
approach: FastVGGT uses training-free three-part token partitioning preserving initial frames, salient tokens, and region-based random sampling.
contribution: Achieves 4x speedup on 1000-image sequences while mitigating error accumulation without retraining.

problem: Textured 3D morphing struggles to preserve both structural coherence and appearance when extending 2D interpolation to 3D.
approach: Interp3D uses generative priors with progressive alignment, enforcing structure via SLAT-guided interpolation and fine-grained texture fusion.
contribution: Demonstrates significant advantages over previous methods in fidelity, transition smoothness, and plausibility via quantitative metrics and human studies.

problem: Full LLM fine-tuning is computationally expensive while PEFT struggles to learn new knowledge with suboptimal performance.
approach: Hybrid fine-tuning jointly updates LLMs and PEFT modules via zeroth-order and first-order methods under novel hybrid smoothness condition framework.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent performance improvement across downstream tasks and model architectures making hybrid approach viable for large-scale fine-tuning.

problem: Existing metrics for evaluating formal statement translation fail to balance semantic and structural information grounded in proof correctness.
approach: ASSESS captures syntactic structure via operator trees and computes TransTED Similarity metric incorporating semantic transformations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and Kappa score on EPLA benchmark of 1,247 expert-annotated formal statement pairs.

problem: Discrete Flow Models require pretrained teachers or expensive finetuning for few-step acceleration without strong acceleration guarantees.
approach: PairFlow trains DFMs from coupled source-target distributions using closed-form inversion without requiring pretrained teachers.
contribution: Matches or surpasses two-stage finetuning performance with only 1.7% training compute overhead.

problem: Probabilistic forecasting of irregular time series lacks marginalization consistency between joint and marginal distributions.
approach: MOSES parametrizes stochastic process via mixture of normalizing flows with separable univariate transformations enabling analytical marginalization.
contribution: Achieves accurate joint and marginal predictions significantly outperforming ProFITi and other baselines on marginalization consistency.

problem: Model merging trades off accuracy against storage cost, with single merged models suffering large gaps from individual fine-tuned models.
approach: FlexMerge generates merged models of varying sizes spanning spectrum from single model to all individuals, supporting multiple merging algorithms.
contribution: Reveals steep accuracy gains with modest size increases (up to 13.5% when doubling) and algorithm rankings vary across size spectrum.

problem: Transformer principles from text transfer imperfectly to time series due to structural differences in data representations.
approach: Analyzes Transformers through rank structure and flow-of-ranks mechanism explaining compressibility and depth-dependent rank inflation.
contribution: Compresses Chronos foundation model achieving 65% inference time and 81% memory reduction without accuracy loss.

problem: Existing RLVR methods improve effectiveness but neglect diversity by imitating entire expert trajectories.
approach: MENTOR provides expert guidance only at critical decision points via mixed-policy framework enabling effective and diverse exploration.
contribution: Enables models to capture expert essence rather than surface imitation, achieving superior overall performance in reasoning tasks.

problem: Current information-seeking agents rely heavily on search-engine-indexed knowledge, missing unindexed sources like dynamic pages and embedded files.
approach: UIS-Digger uses multi-agent framework with dual-mode browsing enabling simultaneous webpage searching and file parsing.
contribution: Achieves 26.36% on UIS-QA benchmark with 30B backbone, outperforming systems integrating O3 and GPT-4.1 at revealing UIS limitations.

problem: Traditional Image Quality Assessment methods predict human preferences but cannot assess image usability for embodied AI tasks.
approach: Constructs perception-cognition-decision-execution pipeline with Embodied-IQA database containing 30k image pairs and 5m annotations via VLMs and real robots.
contribution: Establishes first IQA benchmark for embodied AI, demonstrating need for quality indicators tailored to robot perception under distortions.

problem: Adversarial attacks on SNNs typically modify intensities or event counts, overlooking timing-only attacks preserving spike counts and amplitudes.
approach: Spike-retiming uses projected-in-the-loop optimization with soft logits for differentiable retiming and discrete projection satisfying capacity constraints.
contribution: Achieves over 90% attack success on DVS-Gesture while touching fewer than 2% of spikes.

problem: Adapting 3D generative models for specific design tasks requires costly retraining and cannot handle seed ligands or fragments.
approach: Introduces Interpolate-Integrate and Replacement Guidance, training-free inference-time conditioning strategies for E(3)-equivariant flow-matching models.
contribution: Generates bioisosteric 3D molecules preserving shape and pharmacophore patterns for ligand hopping and fragment merging tasks.

problem: Transfer learning suffers from negative transfer where source representations harm target performance under distribution shift.
approach: Augments frozen source features with trainable target-side encoder capturing residual signals, providing theoretical guarantees against negative transfer.
contribution: Proves convergence rate no worse than training from scratch under informative distributions up to logarithmic factors.

problem: High-quality numeric labels for regression are scarce while rankings are easier to obtain from experts or AI judges.
approach: BAYES-ECR performs Bayesian update combining Gaussian regressor likelihood with Bradley-Terry ranker likelihood plus calibration for scale mismatch.
contribution: Shows 97.65% median improvement across 12 datasets over prior state-of-the-art with calibrated ranking.

problem: Protein generation benchmarks focus on functional motifs, leaving general geometric preservation capabilities untested.
approach: GeomMotif benchmark evaluates arbitrary structural fragment preservation via 57 tasks sampling from PDB with comprehensive structural characterization.
contribution: Reveals sequence-based and structure-based models find different tasks challenging, with geometric preservation varying significantly by structural context.

problem: Group-based policy gradient methods like GRPO suffer from degenerate groups erasing learning signals and synchronization barriers limiting scalability.
approach: SPO replaces per-group baselines with persistent KL-adaptive value tracker and normalizes advantages globally, enabling prioritized sampling curriculum.
contribution: Improves Qwen3-8B average maj@32 by +3.4pp over GRPO across five hard math benchmarks with +7.3pp on BRUMO 25.

problem: Existing spatio-temporal models fail to generalize to unseen regions or graph topologies, while physics-driven approaches scale poorly to complex structures.
approach: PhySTA integrates operator-based spectrum-temporal learning with Graph-Time Fourier Neural Operator plus adaptive multi-scale interaction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computation cost and parameter overhead on large-scale benchmarks.

problem: 4-bit quantization assumed memory-optimal universally, but reasoning models show KV cache dominance requiring scale-dependent trade-offs.
approach: Systematic experiments on mathematical, code generation, and knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks establish scale-dependent quantization thresholds.
contribution: Finds models below 8-bit effective 4B parameters benefit from larger weights, while larger models prioritize test-time compute.

problem: Inference-time control in diffusion models lacks principled methods for adapting outputs to diverse test-time objectives.
approach: Framework orchestrates local and global search via breadth-first/depth-first tree search and annealed Langevin MCMC.
contribution: Demonstrates significant gains in performance and efficiency over baselines across planning, offline RL, and image generation.

problem: Causal discovery with latent variables is difficult because existing methods rely on strong structural assumptions about indicator patterns and interactions, lacking a general equivalence characterization that would enable structural-assumption-free discovery.
approach: The authors establish graphical criteria for distributional equivalence between graphs with latent variables and cycles using a new tool called edge rank constraints, then provide a procedure to traverse equivalence classes and develop an algorithm for model recovery.
contribution: This is the first equivalence characterization with latent variables in any parametric setting without structural assumptions, enabling the first structural-assumption-free causal discovery method.

problem: Compositional generative models for long-horizon planning face a critical challenge when local distributions are multimodal: existing methods average incompatible modes, producing infeasible or incoherent plans.
approach: CDGS embeds guided search within diffusion denoising by exploring diverse mode combinations through population-based sampling, filtering infeasible candidates via likelihood, and enforcing global consistency through iterative resampling between overlapping segments.
contribution: The method matches oracle performance on seven robot manipulation tasks and generalizes across domains to enable coherent panoramic images and long videos.

problem: Training a single network with multiple objectives often leads to conflicting gradients that degrade shared representations into a compromised suboptimal state, a problem termed latent representation collapse.
approach: Domain Expansion restructures the latent space by using orthogonal pooling to assign each objective to mutually orthogonal subspaces, preventing gradient conflicts.
contribution: The framework prevents latent representation collapse and yields an explicit, interpretable, and compositional latent space where concepts can be directly manipulated.

problem: Existing dual-arm robot planning methods often fail to fully optimize task parallelism, limiting the potential for efficient dual-arm collaboration in complex multitasking scenarios.
approach: RoboPARA uses an LLM-driven framework with two stages: dependency graph-based planning candidate generation via directed acyclic graphs, and graph re-traversal-based dual-arm parallel planning to maximize parallelism.
contribution: RoboPARA significantly outperforms existing planning methods in efficiency and reliability, particularly in complex task combinations, and introduces the X-DAPT dataset for evaluating dual-arm task parallelism.

problem: Training Tri-Planar NeRFs to model large collections of 3D objects is computationally intensive because current approaches independently train one tri-plane per object, overlooking structural similarities.
approach: Fused-Planes captures structural similarities across objects through a latent space and shared base planes, with each object represented as a decomposition over these base planes plus object-specific features.
contribution: Fused-Planes achieves 7.2× faster training and 3.2× lower memory footprint than Tri-Planes while maintaining rendering quality, with an ultra-lightweight variant reducing per-object memory by 1875×.

problem: Scheduling jobs to servers while learning unknown service rates is challenging because job and server feature lists may differ under different policies, complicating the analysis of queue state differences.
approach: The authors introduce contextual queueing bandits with a novel policy-switching queues framework and coupling argument to decompose queue length regret, providing algorithms CQB-ε and CQB-Opt with regret bounds.
contribution: CQB-ε achieves a regret upper bound of Õ(T^{-1/4}) and CQB-Opt achieves O(log^2 T) for adversarially chosen contexts, validated experimentally.

problem: Existing approaches to hateful meme detection produce only binary predictions without explanations, and recent explain-then-detect methods using chain-of-thought fail to provide actionable moderation support.
approach: ExPO-HM combines SFT warmup, GRPO with curriculum learning, and Conditional Decision Entropy as both metric and reward, designed after human annotator processes to identify policy-relevant cues like targets and attack types.
contribution: ExPO-HM achieves state-of-the-art performance on binary detection and fine-grained classification with up to 15% and 17% F1 improvement over GRPO and DPO baselines respectively.

problem: Autoregressive decoding in LLMs requires O(n) sequential steps for n tokens, and current diffusion-based LLMs rely on fixed, input-agnostic parallel decoding heuristics that fail to adapt to task characteristics.
approach: Learn2PD trains a lightweight adaptive filter model post-training to predict whether each token position will match the final output, approximating an oracle parallel decoding strategy that unmasks only correct tokens.
contribution: Learn2PD achieves up to 22.58× speedup without performance drop, and up to 57.51× when combined with KV-Cache, without requiring retraining on diverse NLP tasks.

problem: Differentiable MPC has limited adoption because traditional sequential optimization algorithms are challenging to parallelize on modern GPUs, bottlenecking learning and control applications.
approach: The method introduces GPU-accelerated differentiable optimization via sequential quadratic programming and custom preconditioned conjugate gradient with tridiagonal preconditioning to exploit problem structure.
contribution: The solver achieves substantial speedups over CPU and GPU baselines, significantly improving state-of-the-art training times on RL and imitation learning, and enables robust drifting on handling limit tasks.

problem: Collecting large-scale human demonstrations for bimanual mobile manipulation is costly, and prior automated data generation methods fail for mobile manipulation due to reachability (base placement) and visibility (camera positioning) challenges.
approach: MoMaGen formulates data generation as constrained optimization satisfying hard constraints like reachability while balancing soft constraints like camera visibility during navigation.
contribution: MoMaGen generates much more diverse datasets than previous methods for multi-step bimanual mobile manipulation, enabling successful imitation learning from generated data.

problem: LLMs face two bottlenecks in scientific reasoning: explicit retrieval fragments reasoning with token overhead, and multi-agent pipelines dilute strong solutions by averaging candidates.
approach: Eigen-1 combines implicit token-level retrieval via a Monitor-based module with Hierarchical Solution Refinement and Quality-Aware Iterative Reasoning to iteratively repair candidate solutions.
contribution: Achieves 48.3% accuracy on Humanity's Last Exam Bio/Chem Gold, surpassing strongest baselines by 13.4 points, while reducing token usage by 53.5% and agent steps by 43.7%.

problem: In-context image editing models typically depend on task-specific pipelines and expert models for data curation, making them difficult to scale and less general.
approach: VINCIE learns in-context image editing directly from videos using three proxy tasks: next-image prediction, current segmentation prediction, and next-segmentation prediction.
contribution: Despite training only on videos, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on multi-turn image editing benchmarks and demonstrates capabilities in multi-concept composition and story generation.

problem: LLM-based agents are limited in hard-exploration tasks requiring learning new knowledge through exploration, particularly in environments like text-based games with complex state spaces.
approach: GLoW maintains a trajectory frontier of high-value discoveries at global scale while learning from local trial-and-error via Multi-path Advantage Reflection, which infers advantage-based signals to guide exploration.
contribution: GLoW achieves state-of-the-art performance for LLM-based approaches on Jericho benchmarks while requiring 100-800× fewer environment interactions than state-of-the-art RL methods.

problem: Traditional web information extraction evaluation relies on offline benchmarks from HTML snapshots at single time points, failing to account for the temporally evolving nature of live websites.
approach: LiveWeb-IE introduces a benchmark for evaluating WIE systems against live websites with natural language queries requiring information extraction of various data categories, plus Visual Grounding Scraper that mimics human visual reasoning.
contribution: The benchmark enables granular assessment of WIE systems across complexity levels, with VGS showing effectiveness across diverse models in extracting live web information.

problem: In-context learning does not explicitly encode observations, relying instead on prior knowledge and exemplars, raising questions about whether ICL truly constitutes learning or primarily relies on pattern deduction.
approach: Large-scale empirical analysis ablating memorization, pretraining, distributional shifts, and prompting style reveals that ICL has limited ability to generalize to unseen tasks.
contribution: The analysis shows that accuracy is insensitive to exemplar distribution and model variation in high-exemplar regimes, and ICL's ad-hoc encoding mechanism does not provide robust all-purpose generalization.

problem: Long-Form Question Answering evaluation is challenging because existing LFQA benchmarks lack reference answers, have limited size and topic coverage, and no automatic metrics capture information density effectively.
approach: LFQA-E provides a multilingual, reference-based benchmark with 1,625 questions and 7,649 pairwise comparisons across 15 topics, evaluating 17 automatic metrics across five categories.
contribution: Results demonstrate that none of the existing automatic metrics perform comparably to human judgments, providing detailed failure case analysis and generalization capacity insights.

problem: The quadratic complexity of softmax attention prevents Transformers from scaling to high-resolution vision tasks, and linear attention approximations using Gaussian kernels lack theoretical grounding and oversuppress mid-range interactions.
approach: LaplacianFormer replaces softmax with a principled Laplacian kernel, introduces a provably injective feature map, and uses Nyström approximation with Newton-Schulz iteration for efficient computation.
contribution: LaplacianFormer achieves strong performance-efficiency trade-offs on ImageNet while improving attention expressiveness compared to existing linear attention variants.

problem: LLM-based agents lack capability to assist in complex scientific workflows requiring interaction with professional software, with current benchmarks focusing only on isolated problems.
approach: ScienceBoard provides a realistic multi-domain environment with integrated professional software and a benchmark of 169 high-quality real-world tasks spanning biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics.
contribution: Evaluation shows that state-of-the-art agents like GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 only achieve 15% overall success rate, revealing fundamental limitations in complex workflow assistance.

problem: Hallucination in vision-language models and sign language translation occurs when models generate fluent text unsupported by visual evidence, particularly in gloss-free models that map continuous movements directly to language.
approach: The paper proposes a token-level reliability measure combining feature-based sensitivity (masked video changes) and counterfactual signals (probability differences under altered video) aggregated into sentence-level scores.
contribution: The proposed measure predicts hallucination rates across benchmarks and architectures, distinguishes grounded from guessed tokens, and enables risk estimation without references.

problem: The Learning to Explain paradigm faces three challenges: self-supervised objectives rely on model assumptions limiting generalizability, prior-explanation-driven methods cannot guarantee supervisory signal quality, and hybrid approaches suffer from poor convergence.
approach: A faithfulness-guided amortized explainer derives a self-supervised objective free from target model assumptions, generates high-quality signals by deduplicating and filtering prior explanations, and jointly optimizes both via dynamic weighting.
contribution: The approach produces more faithful explanations than existing methods while proving that an explanation mapping can achieve optimality simultaneously across multiple faithfulness metrics.

problem: Existing video super-resolution methods decouple spatial and temporal components and rely on brittle explicit frame warping for motion compensation, limiting quality and scalability.
approach: The method encodes video as continuous spatio-temporally coherent 3D Video Fourier Fields using sinusoidal basis coefficients predicted by a neural encoder, enabling flexible arbitrary-scale sampling with analytical aliasing-free reconstruction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks with sharper and temporally more consistent reconstructions while being computationally more efficient.

problem: Deterministic attention implementations like FlashAttention-3 suffer 37.9% throughput reduction on backward passes because gradient accumulation must serialize to guarantee numerical consistency, causing hardware underutilization.
approach: DASH formulates the backward pass as a scheduling problem on a directed acyclic graph and derives optimal schedules including Descending Q-Tile Iteration and Shift Scheduling to minimize critical path length.
contribution: Improves attention backward pass throughput by up to 1.28× compared to baseline, significantly advancing reproducible LLM training efficiency while maintaining determinism.

problem: Single-agent vision-language navigation focuses on sequential step-by-step execution, missing benefits of collaborative approaches including shorter makespan and robustness via role specialization.
approach: CoNavBench introduces collaborative VLN tasks and the NavCraft platform for automated generation with two-stage hierarchical agents producing base missions and coordinating helper robots via handoffs and rendezvous.
contribution: Provides 4,048 single and collaborative episodes with a collaboration type taxonomy and a collaborative baseline using finetuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B that demonstrates collaborative policies reduce makespan.

problem: Long chain-of-thought LLMs often exhibit suboptimal reasoning behaviors including overthinking and excessively protracted reasoning chains that impair performance.
approach: RePro frames chain-of-thought as gradient descent and introduces a process-level reward using dual scoring to quantify optimization intensity and stability, integrated into RLVR pipelines.
contribution: Consistently enhances reasoning performance across multiple RL algorithms and diverse LLMs on mathematics, science, and coding benchmarks while mitigating suboptimal reasoning behaviors.

problem: Causal graphs often contain many irrelevant edges that complicate analysis when researchers are interested in causal relationships within specific tiers.
approach: A systematic method leverages tiered knowledge to prune causal graph edges while preserving identifiability of conditional causal effects, enabling query-specific discovery from observational data.
contribution: Achieves exponential speedups compared to existing methods when tiered knowledge is available by recovering reduced graphs tailored to specific causal queries.

problem: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards suffers from the 'learning cliff' phenomenon: models consistently fail on problems beyond their capabilities, yielding zero-reward signals that stall progress.
approach: Scaf-GRPO provides minimal guidance through tiered in-prompt hints only when independent learning plateaus, enabling models to construct valid solutions by themselves while avoiding the learning cliff.
contribution: Boosts Qwen2.5-Math-7B pass@1 on AIME24 by 44.3% relative to vanilla GRPO, unlocking the model's ability to solve problems previously beyond its reach.

problem: Current AI agent evaluation focuses on isolated problems and lacks environments and tool interfaces for the full software DevOps cycle including deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.
approach: DevOps-Gym introduces an end-to-end benchmark with 700+ real-world tasks from 30+ Java and Go projects covering build/configuration, monitoring, issue resolving, and test generation.
contribution: State-of-the-art models achieve only around 15% success on new tasks like monitoring, highlighting fundamental limitations in automating the full DevOps cycle.

problem: Offline RL methods using behavior policy regularization are conservative and can limit performance and generalization, especially when the behavior policy is suboptimal.
approach: PIC constructs a set of similar states and selects optimal actions from their corresponding candidates as constraints, implemented via ensemble methods in EPIC for stronger performance.
contribution: PIC and EPIC achieve competitive performance on D4RL continuous control tasks while maintaining efficiency and discovering the coupling effect between peer influence and uncertainty estimation.

problem: Most multimodal RLVR methods neglect the critical role of visual perception, failing to capture token-level visual dependencies needed for effective reasoning.
approach: VPPO introduces token perception measurement and proposes a dual mechanism: reweighting trajectory advantage by visual dependency and focusing policy updates on perceptually pivotal tokens.
contribution: Demonstrates substantial gains across eight perception and reasoning benchmarks on both 7B and 32B model scales, with analysis revealing sparse distribution of visual dependency in CoT.

problem: Current model-brain alignment research focuses on fMRI measurements, leaving open questions about fine-grained dynamic visual processing in continuous video understanding.
approach: Cross-Temporal Representational Similarity Analysis matches best time-unfolded model features to dynamically evolving EEG brain responses across 100+ models, analyzing temporal integration and classification tasks.
contribution: Reveals that posterior electrodes align with mid-level action features with temporal correspondence, while frontal electrodes align with high-level static representations without temporal correspondence.

problem: Machine-generated text detectors achieve high accuracy in monolingual settings but degrade severely on zero-shot languages and are vulnerable to adversarial attacks via code-switching.
approach: TASTE combines an attacker using translation-based code-switching with an adversarially trained detector using a Language-Agnostic Adversarial Loss for language-invariant feature learning.
contribution: Surpasses 8 state-of-the-art detectors, improving average F1 score by 0.064 and reducing attack success rate by 3.8% across 9 languages and 8 attack types.

problem: Offline RL struggles with complex long-horizon sequential decision making because existing conservative approaches can limit performance and generalization.
approach: DEAS leverages action sequences for value learning to reduce the effective planning horizon, using detached value learning to steer value estimates toward in-distribution high-return actions.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on complex long-horizon OGBench tasks and can enhance vision-language-action models, boosting performance on RoboCasa and real-world manipulation.

problem: Interpreting reasoning models from a single chain-of-thought is inadequate; understanding causal influence requires studying reasoning as a distribution of possible trajectories.
approach: The method uses on-policy resampling to approximate the distribution of reasoning trajectories, applying causal analysis to measure token influence through resilience metrics and counterfactual importance.
contribution: Reveals that normative self-preservation sentences have small non-resilient effects on decisions, while on-policy sentence insertions produce larger and more consistent effects than off-policy edits.

problem: Sound source localization methods are constrained by fixed array geometries and predefined directional grids, limiting generalizability and scalability across diverse acoustic scenarios.
approach: AGG-RL jointly learns audio-geometry and grid representations in a shared latent space using learnable non-uniform Fourier transforms and relative microphone positional encoding for physics-informed design.
contribution: Achieves superior performance particularly under unseen conditions, demonstrating the potential of physics-informed representation learning for universal spatial acoustic scene understanding.

problem: Unsupervised object-centric learning models create a conflict between sharp encoder attention maps and blurry reconstruction maps from the decoder, causing a vicious cycle of mutual degradation.
approach: Synergistic Representation Learning establishes a virtuous cycle where the encoder deblurs semantic boundaries in decoder output while the decoder denoise encoder features, stabilized by slot regularization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging video object-centric learning benchmarks by breaking the encoder-decoder representational gap.

problem: Generating high-resolution 3D CT volumes with fine details is challenging due to substantial computational demands and optimization difficulties in existing generative models.
approach: PRDiT uses a two-stage architecture with a local MLP-based blind estimator on overlapping patches for low-frequency structures and a memory-efficient global residual diffusion transformer for high-frequency details.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models on LIDC-IDRI and RAD-ChestCT datasets with significantly lower 3D FID, MMD, and Wasserstein distance scores.

problem: Peer effect estimation typically requires explicit specification of exposure mapping functions that aggregate peer treatments, but the true function is rarely known and misspecification leads to biased estimates.
approach: EGONETGNN is a graph neural network that automatically learns the exposure mapping function and captures complex peer exposure mechanisms involving peer treatments, node attributes, edge attributes, and structure.
contribution: Proves more robust to complex influence mechanisms than naive GNN approaches, with evaluation on synthetic and semi-synthetic data demonstrating superior performance.

problem: Vision-Language Models struggle with spatial reasoning due to inadequate 3D understanding from 2D-centric pretraining and reasoning failures induced by redundant 3D information.
approach: MSSR uses a dual-agent framework where a Perception Agent queries 3D scenes to extract minimal sufficient information including a novel SOG module for language-grounded directions, and a Reasoning Agent iteratively refines to minimize redundancy.
contribution: Significantly improves accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging spatial reasoning benchmarks with interpretable reasoning paths.
