problem: Vision-Language-Action models for robotic manipulation face inefficient inference due to dense visual token attention dominance, especially over long-horizon multi-modal context.
approach: ADP integrates text-driven token selection with action-aware trajectory gating, conditioning pruning on past motion windows to adaptively adjust token retention across manipulation stages.
contribution: ADP achieves 1.35x speed up on OpenVLA-OFT with 25.8% improvements in success rate across LIBERO and real-world manipulation scenarios.

problem: Class-Incremental Learning assumes shared domain distribution, limiting applicability when data arrive from evolving environments requiring bidirectional domain transferability.
approach: XEED leverages domain-specialized prompts, residual-guided representation modulation, and evolving prototypes to expand class semantics across domains bidirectionally.
contribution: XEED outperforms CIL baselines significantly on standard accuracy and novel BiDoT metrics for continual learning under domain-evolving conditions.

problem: Vision-language models cannot effectively reason about moving targets across large-scale camera networks by integrating geographic maps and multiple video perspectives simultaneously.
approach: GTR-Bench introduces a benchmark that combines geographic and temporal reasoning with non-overlapping field-of-view videos and map context to evaluate VLMs' geo-temporal intelligence.
contribution: Benchmark shows top VLMs like Gemini-2.5-Pro achieve only 34.9% accuracy versus 78.61% human performance, revealing three key deficiencies in spatial-temporal reasoning.

problem: Current LLM development requires manual training runs with static datasets/rewards to extend model capabilities, preventing continuous discovery of diverse skills.
approach: AC/DC coevolves LLMs via model merging and tasks via synthetic data generation, discovering populations of diverse expert models in a single continuous run.
contribution: LLM populations achieve broader expertise coverage than curated baselines without explicit benchmark optimization, with continual improvements over time.

problem: Video generation models struggle with complex human movements because pixel-only training biases toward appearance over kinematic principles.
approach: EchoMotion extends diffusion transformers with dual-branch architecture processing video and motion tokens jointly, using MVS-RoPE for synchronized 3D positional encoding.
contribution: Constructs HuMoVe dataset of ~80k video-motion pairs and demonstrates that explicit motion representation improves complex human action video generation quality.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting fails in sparse-view settings due to geometric inaccuracies and sensitivity to camera trajectory smoothness.
approach: Proposes optimizing camera trajectories to maximize curvature coverage while enforcing smooth motion, combined with synthetic view generation.
contribution: Substantially outperforms state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks in sparse-view rendering quality and geometric fidelity while revealing implicit biases of 3DGS.

problem: Large vision-language models incur substantial computational overhead processing high-resolution images with many vision tokens.
approach: ERGO uses coarse-to-fine reasoning: downsampled image identifies task-relevant regions via reasoning-driven perception, then full-resolution crops are processed.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy than baseline models with competitive efficiency by leveraging multimodal context for region selection.

problem: Existing code reasoning benchmarks rely on synthetic/educational problems and coarse-grained tasks, failing to evaluate LLMs on real-world software engineering contexts.
approach: CodeSense constructs fine-grained semantic reasoning tasks from real repositories with execution traces as ground truth for Python, C, and Java.
contribution: First benchmark for fine-grained code semantic reasoning from real-world projects reveals fundamental gaps in LLM code comprehension despite prompting techniques.

problem: LLMs have inherent performance limitations that cannot be easily overcome during inference without model retraining.
approach: Dynamic Nested Depth reprocesses critical tokens identified by a router at transformer layers with controlled selection via router loss and threshold schemes.
contribution: Boosts dense models (Qwen3-1.7B/Llama3.2-1B/Gemma3-1B) by 1.88-2.61% and MoE models (Qwen3-30B) by 0.87% with minimal parameter/compute increase.

problem: Conformal prediction for LLM factuality guarantees relies on exchangeability assumptions violated by real-world distribution shifts.
approach: CoFact uses online density ratio estimation to adaptively reweigh calibration data, bypassing exchangeability and providing guarantees under distribution shift.
contribution: Maintains reliability under non-stationary conditions on MedLFQA, WikiData, and WildChat+ with asymptotic guarantee that hallucination rate gap approaches zero.

problem: Visible discontinuities in loss curves represent only a small fraction of actual breakthroughs in model learning, obscured by scalar loss metrics.
approach: POLCA decomposes training loss changes along low-rank subspace bases to identify clusters of samples with similar capability transitions.
contribution: Recovers interpretable phase transitions representing conceptual breakthroughs in both synthetic arithmetic and natural language tasks.

problem: Continual vision-language models struggle to maintain compositional structure while adapting to new domains with limited rehearsal budgets.
approach: Compo-ReAlign uses reversible composer for primitive-to-composition mapping, multi-positive InfoNCE for joint alignment, and spectral trust region for stability.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on compositional retrieval, improves over prior work by +2.4 R@1, and reduces forgetting by 40%.

problem: Neural network pruning plateaus around 50-60% sparsity for LLMs due to limitations in conventional surrogate-objective methods.
approach: Elsa uses ADMM-based constrained optimization without surrogate objectives, achieving 90% sparsity by identifying and addressing fundamental method limitations.
contribution: Achieves 7.8x less perplexity than best existing method on LLaMA-2-7B at 90% sparsity and enables 3.98x inference speedup with 7.80x memory compression.

problem: Vision-language models hallucinate due to perceptual bottlenecks in attended regions and insufficient visual robustness against image degradation.
approach: P2-DPO generates on-policy preference pairs targeting focus-and-enhance perception and visual robustness, with calibration loss aligning visual signals to text generation.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods using comparable training data on POPE and MMHal-Bench; validates improvements via attention region fidelity.

problem: Multi-task Bayesian optimization performance plateaus when scaling beyond moderate task counts due to shared-surrogate saturation.
approach: BOLT uses LLMs fine-tuned on prior BO runs to generate initialization candidates, maintaining single-task surrogates while creating closed-loop improvement.
contribution: Scales to ~1500 tasks without saturation; LLM initializations match or surpass from-scratch BO with far fewer oracle calls.

problem: Hyperparameter optimization for large-scale models requires separate searches at each scale, preventing efficient transfer across model dimensions.
approach: Extends CompleteP parameterization to transfer across width, depth, training horizon, and batch size using empirically validated scaling laws.
contribution: Demonstrates hyperparameter transfer holds per-layer and proposes simplified parameterization reducing search dimensionality without performance cost.

problem: Diffusion-based image editing entangles edited regions with global context, causing unintended modifications and poor instruction adherence.
approach: VAREdit reformulates editing as next-scale prediction with autoregressive models, using Scale-Aligned Reference module to inject scale-matched conditioning.
contribution: Outperforms diffusion methods on EMU-Edit and PIE-Bench in CLIP/GPT scores; completes 512x512 edits 2.2x faster than comparable methods.

problem: Vision-based 3D human motion capture ignores temporal consistency between frames, producing jittery motion due to Euler angle discontinuities.
approach: QuaMo uses quaternion differential equations and state-space models with adaptive meta-PD controller and quaternion geometric constraints.
contribution: Enables continuous 3D human kinematics estimation with no discontinuity and minimal artifacts compared to Euler-angle methods.

problem: Time-series forecasting models fail to handle concept drift (semantic shifts in underlying patterns), focusing only on temporal distribution shifts.
approach: ShifTS addresses temporal shift first via attention mechanisms finding invariant patterns, then applies soft attention for concept drift mitigation.
contribution: Method-agnostic framework consistently enhances forecasting accuracy across multiple datasets and outperforms dedicated concept/temporal drift baselines.

problem: Task and motion planning relies on manually-defined options (pick, place, move), limiting agent improvisation and discovery of novel behaviors.
approach: SLAP leverages model-free RL to learn shortcuts in the abstract planning graph induced by existing TAMP options.
contribution: Discovers dynamic improvisations (slap, wiggle, wipe) with 50% shorter plan lengths, outperforming planning and hierarchical RL baselines.

problem: Diffusion-based policy gradients require exact likelihood computation and bind to specific sampling methods, limiting applicability.
approach: FPO casts policy optimization as advantage-weighted flow matching loss compatible with PPO-clip, agnostic to integration method.
contribution: Trains diffusion-style policies from scratch capturing multimodal action distributions with higher performance than Gaussian policies in under-conditioned settings.

problem: Lane-level navigation requires expensive global HD maps but lacks the flexibility to adapt to dynamic road conditions from real-time perception.
approach: ONR refines SD-map routes to lane-level by associating with online perception maps using MAT transformer with path-aware and spatial attention.
contribution: Introduces OMA dataset (30K scenarios, 2.6M lane vectors) and demonstrates lane-level navigation with 34ms latency.

problem: Path imitation learning reduces navigation to memorizing single routes, limiting generalization and exploration of alternative valid paths.
approach: CompassNav shifts to Decision Understanding via RFT on Compass-Data-22k annotating all feasible actions with A* distances and gap-aware hybrid rewards.
contribution: 7B agent achieves state-of-the-art on navigation benchmarks, outperforms larger proprietary models, and succeeds on physical robot navigation.

problem: Token filtering in LLM training lacks real-world efficiency gains due to inadequate sparsity and incompatibility with standard ML libraries.
approach: Centrifuge filters activations in attention backward kernel to amplify sparsity and transforms sparse GEMM to dimension-reduced dense GEMM.
contribution: Reduces backpropagation time by up to 49.9% and end-to-end training by 34.7% when filtering 50% of tokens with 26.6% performance improvement.

problem: Vision-language-action models lack spatial awareness for 3D physical tasks because pretraining on 2D data without explicit 3D supervision.
approach: Spatial Forcing aligns intermediate visual embeddings with geometric representations from pretrained 3D foundation models without explicit 3D inputs.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art surpassing both 2D/3D baselines, accelerates training 3.8x, improves data efficiency across robotic tasks.

problem: Integral facility location with online learning advice lacks tight theoretical bounds unlike fractional versions.
approach: Presents first online rounding algorithms for facility location with applications to online settings enhanced with ML advice.
contribution: Establishes theoretical rounding guarantees for facility location under online learning-augmented conditions.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning chains contain inaccurate statements that reduce performance and trustworthiness.
approach: Veracity Search performs discrete search over latent veracity assignments using LM likelihood as proxy reward; AVI learns amortized zero-shot inference.
contribution: Reliably identifies errors in logical, mathematical, and commonsense reasoning benchmarks with efficient inference-time verification.

problem: Optical projection inversion for screen exfiltration faces ill-posed inversion with singular Jacobian and irreversible light transport compression.
approach: IR4Net fuses Physically Regularized Irradiance Approximation with radiative transfer equation embedding and Irreversibility Constrained Semantic Reprojection.
contribution: Achieves reconstruction fidelity beyond neural methods while maintaining resilience to illumination perturbations on diverse scene categories.

problem: Vision Transformer knowledge distillation suffers from high-norm artifacts dominating the objective, causing students to underweight informative signals.
approach: SiNGER refines teacher features via nullspace-guided perturbation using LoRA-based adapters to suppress artifacts while preserving signals.
contribution: Consistently improves student models achieving state-of-the-art on downstream tasks with clearer, more interpretable representations.

problem: Multi-neuron convex relaxations for neural network certification may be incomplete, with unclear advantages over single-neuron methods.
approach: Provides first rigorous analysis showing multi-neuron relaxations are inherently incomplete but can achieve completeness via polynomial ReLU augmentation or polytope partitioning.
contribution: Establishes universal convex barrier for certification and characterizes distinguishing capabilities of multi-neuron over single-neuron approaches.

problem: Category-agnostic pose estimation assumes equal-weight edges in pose graphs, leading to suboptimal keypoint localization under occlusion.
approach: EdgeCape predicts edge weights in pose graphs and integrates Markov Attention Bias modulating self-attention by node hop distance.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on MP-100 benchmark in 1-shot and 5-shot settings with significantly improved keypoint accuracy.

problem: Protein language models scale poorly compared to NLP/vision models, plateauing at 650M-3B parameters despite larger pretraining.
approach: Reverse Distillation decomposes large model representations into orthogonal subspaces guided by smaller models matching protein property hierarchies.
contribution: Enables monotonic scaling with larger models consistently outperforming baselines while overcoming previous scaling plateaus on ProteinGym.

problem: LLMs exhibit limited Overton pluralism, failing to represent diverse viewpoints in outputs, with no scalable measurement approach.
approach: Formalizes Overton pluralism as set-coverage metric OVERTONSCORE via large-scale human study (N=1209) and develops automated benchmark reproducing judgments.
contribution: Models achieve 0.35-0.41 OVERTONSCORE far below theoretical maximum; automated benchmark achieves 0.88 rank correlation with human judgments.

problem: Object hallucination in multimodal LLMs is studied only with static benchmarks, missing model-specific vulnerabilities.
approach: GHOST optimizes image embeddings to induce hallucinations while keeping objects absent, using diffusion to generate natural-looking adversarial images.
contribution: Achieves 28% hallucination success rate versus 1% in prior methods; uncovers transferable vulnerabilities and validates fine-tuning as mitigation.

problem: Stop gradient and exponential moving average procedures in non-contrastive SSL avoid collapse without clear theoretical understanding.
approach: Analyzes from dual optimization and dynamical systems perspectives; shows these procedures don't optimize any smooth objective but characterize equilibria.
contribution: Proves in linear case that minimizing objective without stop gradient always leads to collapse; characterizes equilibria as asymptotically stable varieties.

problem: Personalized LLMs either overload context with all user history (costly/unscalable) or use one-shot similarity search missing deep context.
approach: RF-Mem implements dual-process memory retrieval: Familiarity for direct top-K via certainty, Recollection for iterative evidence expansion via α-mix.
contribution: Achieves scalable adaptive personalization avoiding full-context overhead across three benchmarks and corpus scales.

problem: Learned optimizers struggle to meta-generalize to unseen tasks, especially when scaling to wider networks than seen during training.
approach: Derives Maximal Update Parametrization for learned optimizer architectures with simple meta-training recipe for μ-parameterized LOs.
contribution: μLOs substantially improve meta-generalization to wider unseen tasks and show 5x generalization to deeper networks and 25x to longer horizons.

problem: Multi-modal dialogue systems lack rich datasets and struggle with conditional control over style and expressiveness across modalities.
approach: Introduces MM-Dia dataset (54.7k dialogues, 360+ hours) with fine-grained multi-modal annotations from movies/TV and MM-Dia-Bench for evaluation.
contribution: Demonstrates current frameworks' limitations in replicating human interaction expressiveness and provides benchmark for style-controllable dialogue.

problem: Multi-step generative models like diffusion require 40-100 function evaluations, limiting inference efficiency.
approach: TwinFlow trains 1-step generators via self-adversarial flows bypassing distillation and standard adversarial training complexity.
contribution: Achieves GenEval 0.83 at 1-NFE outperforming distillation baselines; scales to 20B multi-modal model with efficient few-step generation.

problem: Domain adaptive hashing transfers knowledge poorly due to target noise and indiscriminate domain alignment distorting features.
approach: Uses hierarchical conformal calibration with semantic-level confidence prediction sets and representation-level bit-level confidence for robust quantization.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements in cross-domain knowledge transfer with adaptive weighted Hamming distance retrieval.

problem: Multi-agent visual reasoning systems either rely on single agents or hand-crafted pipelines without learning optimal agent selection.
approach: MATA presents hierarchical finite-state automaton where trainable hyper-agent selects states; agents use rule-based sub-automatons with shared memory.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on visual reasoning benchmarks with transparent execution via MATA-SFT-90K dataset for transition policy supervision.

problem: Large language models produce factually inconsistent content due to hallucination, limiting deployment in knowledge-intensive applications.
approach: NDAD identifies hallucination signals via selective attention head masking and subtracts mass from hallucination-prone output regions via gradient steps.
contribution: Enhances factual reliability across multiple LLMs and benchmarks without retraining or external knowledge requirements.

problem: World model-based planning is computationally expensive in resource-constrained robotics environments, making real-time deployment infeasible.
approach: The paper uses a sparsely trained vision-based transformer world model with randomized grouped attention to reduce token processing during forward prediction, enabling flexible adjustment of computational resources during latent rollout.
contribution: Sparse imagination maintains task performance while dramatically improving inference efficiency, enabling deployment of world models in real-time robotics scenarios.

problem: Existing reward model benchmarks do not correlate well with downstream performance despite being used to evaluate reward models used in LLM post-training.
approach: RewardEval introduces a multi-skill reward modeling benchmark with new human prompts and challenging data, showing 20-point lower average scores than RewardBench and correlating with downstream performance in inference-time and training-time settings.
contribution: RewardEval provides rigorous evaluation practices and demonstrates how reward model performance on the benchmark correlates with effectiveness in best-of-N sampling and RLHF training.

problem: Knowledge editing methods require resource-heavy backpropagation incompatible with mobile devices, preventing on-device LLM personalization.
approach: MobiEdit replaces full-precision backpropagation with quantized forward-only gradient estimation compatible with mobile neural processing units, adding early stopping and prefix activation reusing optimizations.
contribution: MobiEdit enables real-time editing of 3B-parameter models on commercial mobile devices with 7.1x less memory, 15.8x less energy, and 3.4x less latency.

problem: Existing benchmarks assess verbal reasoning alone, not the multi-step visual simulation skills essential for spatial cognition.
approach: STARE introduces a 3K-task benchmark spanning 2D/3D geometric transformations, cube net folding, tangram puzzles, and real-world spatial reasoning, evaluating multimodal LLMs on complex visual simulation.
contribution: Evaluations reveal models perform near random chance on complex spatial tasks requiring multi-step visual simulation, while humans achieve near-perfect accuracy despite longer completion times.

problem: Hardware-aware neural architecture search methods struggle to satisfy hardware constraints without introducing hyperparameter tuning and differentiability requirements.
approach: ConNAS enforces hardware constraints directly through gradient modification of architectural choices, steering the search toward feasible architectures without regularization terms or differentiable hardware metrics.
contribution: ConNAS discovers architectures meeting hardware constraints while achieving performance within 0.14% of optimal feasible architectures and outperforming handcrafted designs by up to 1.55% under tight budgets.

problem: Standard deep generative models with learned encoders and variational bounds struggle to produce low-dimensional, interpretable embeddings of high-dimensional data.
approach: QLVMs directly approximate marginal likelihood using randomized quasi-Monte Carlo integration to find one-, two-, and three-dimensional interpretable embeddings, enabling transparent visualization and post-hoc analysis.
contribution: QLVMs consistently outperform VAEs and IWAEs with matched latent dimensionality, enabling nonparametric density estimation, clustering, and geodesic path computation in interpretable low-dimensional spaces.

problem: Existing API-based benchmarks use isolated tools and explicit specifications, not capturing realistic multi-step tasks requiring cross-tool coordination and planning.
approach: MCP-Bench connects LLMs to 28 live MCP servers spanning 250 tools via the Model Context Protocol, constructing authentic multi-step tasks that require tool retrieval, planning, and cross-domain workflows.
contribution: Experiments on 20 advanced LLMs reveal persistent challenges in tool-level schema understanding, trajectory planning, and cross-domain task completion.

problem: Prior convergence analysis of Tsetlin Machines covers only 1-bit and 2-bit XOR operators under noise-free conditions, lacking comprehensive theory for general k-bit settings and noise.
approach: The paper extends analysis to 2-bit AND and OR operators under noisy and noise-free training, then generalizes to k-bit settings with unified treatment of convergence properties.
contribution: Provides robust theoretical foundation showing TM converges almost surely under noise-free training and that mislabeled samples permit efficient learning while irrelevant variables do not prevent convergence.

problem: Traffic models struggle to jointly capture microscopic vehicle interactions and macroscopic flow evolution without requiring historical trajectories.
approach: MMCKM lifts coupled micro-macro dynamics to a high-dimensional linear space using Koopman operators with scenario-adaptive evolvers and explicit macro-to-micro control modules on vehicle-centric dynamic graphs.
contribution: Achieves comparable or higher trajectory prediction accuracy than history-dependent baselines using only real-time measurement on NGSIM and HighD datasets.

problem: Standard CNNs are sensitive to photometric variations and data augmentation alone cannot provide formal guarantees of robustness.
approach: SEqSI achieves intensity scale equivariance and shift invariance by design through a shift-invariant layer prepended to a scale-equivariant backbone, providing certified affine transformation invariance.
contribution: SEqSI provides formal robustness guarantees to affine intensity transformations and enhances generalization on image classification and object localization across photometric corruptions and domain shifts.

problem: 3D few-shot class-incremental learning requires balancing novel-class adaptation against preserving base-class knowledge without explicit retraining.
approach: Point-UQ uses uncertainty quantification to dynamically arbitrate between semantic classifiers and geometric prototypes via Attention-driven Adaptive Enhancement and Uncertainty-quantification Decision Decoupling modules.
contribution: Enables robust base-class knowledge retention and accurate novel-class recognition in 3D few-shot incremental learning without retraining on ModelNet, ShapeNet, and other point-cloud benchmarks.

problem: Current evaluation of ML papers conflates rhetorical style with substantive content, making it unclear whether bold language reflects genuine evidence or mere hype.
approach: An LLM-based framework generates counterfactual writings from the same substantive content using multiple personas, aggregates pairwise LLM judgments via Bradley-Terry model to isolate rhetorical style.
contribution: Analysis of 8,485 ICLR submissions reveals visionary framing predicts citations and media coverage independent of peer review, and rhetorical strength increased sharply after 2023 correlated with LLM writing assistance adoption.

problem: Existing SFT approaches for LLM-based human behavior simulation are bounded by the reasoning capabilities of the model generating synthetic rationales.
approach: Shop-R1 uses RL with two-stage decomposition: self-supervised internal-signal guidance for rationale generation and hierarchical difficulty-aware reward scaling for action prediction to prevent reward hacking.
contribution: Achieves 65% relative improvement over baselines in predicting real human behavior in online shopping environments.

problem: Diffusion models lack access to marginal densities along generation trajectories, limiting their application to inference-time control and energy-based training.
approach: RNE (Radon-Nikodym Estimator) uses density ratios between path distributions to reveal connections between marginal densities and transition kernels, providing a unified framework for diffusion density estimation, control, and training.
contribution: RNE delivers strong results in inference-time control applications like annealing and model composition with promising inference-time scaling, and provides efficient regularization for energy-based diffusion training.

problem: KL-regularized RL objectives may induce diversity collapse when targeting high-reward regions under common settings like low regularization strength.
approach: Analysis shows target distributions under forward and reverse KL regularization concentrate on single high-reward regions; the paper proposes rescaling rewards to induce broad probability mass across all high-reward regions.
contribution: The modified objective maintains high solution quality while achieving broad reward-mode coverage, improving post-training diversity for LLMs and Chemical Language Models.

problem: VLMs struggle with fine-grained image classification despite extensive text knowledge, failing to differentiate visually similar categories.
approach: DiVE-k leverages model top-k predictions as training signals, creating multiple-choice questions from top outputs and using RL to train fine-grained differential reasoning without memorization.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches by 10.04% and 6.16% on Harmonic Mean metric in base-to-novel generalization on five fine-grained datasets.

problem: Quantifying subjective value alignment for which no ground-truth labels exist remains an open problem.
approach: EigenBench uses an ensemble of models as judges to evaluate each other across scenarios according to a constitution, aggregating judgments via EigenTrust to produce consensus scores without ground-truth labels.
contribution: EigenBench's rankings align closely with human evaluators and can recover GPQA benchmark rankings without objective labels, providing a framework for evaluating subjective model values.

problem: Lightweight 3D medical image segmentation faces an efficiency-robustness conflict when handling complex anatomies and heterogeneous modalities.
approach: VeloxSeg uses a dual-stream CNN-Transformer with Paired Window Attention for rapid multi-scale retrieval and Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma-guided convolution for robust local features; Spatially Decoupled Knowledge Transfer injects texture priors.
contribution: Achieves 26% Dice improvement with 11x GPU throughput increase, 48x CPU increase, and 1/24 inference memory reduction on multimodal benchmarks.

problem: The assumption that personalizing ML models improves both prediction and explanation accuracy remains largely unvalidated.
approach: A unified framework quantifies whether personalization improves prediction and explanation for demographic groups, derives finite-sample error bounds on hypothesis tests, and applies to real-world tabular data.
contribution: Demonstrates prediction and explanation impacts can diverge; identifies scenarios where effects are fundamentally untestable due to dataset statistics.

problem: Local flatness alone does not guarantee better generalization in domain generalization; a global geometric property is needed.
approach: BOA (Billiard Optimization Algorithm) discovers superior models by traversing connected pathways between local minima in a low-dimensional Krylov subspace, mimicking billiard dynamics.
contribution: BOA consistently outperforms sharpness-aware and domain generalization methods across DomainBed, even surpassing oracle-aware baselines.

problem: Autoregressive video diffusion models cannot guide generation with future conditioning, causing collisions with generated scenes in camera-guided video generation.
approach: GVS samples entire sequences in parallel using diffusion stitching compatible with models trained via Diffusion Forcing; OmniGuidance conditions on both past and future with loop-closing for coherence.
contribution: Achieves stable, collision-free, frame-to-frame consistent camera-guided video generation that closes loops for diverse predefined camera paths.

problem: VLMs lack 3D spatial reasoning ability for multi-view, ego-centric observations typical in embodied AI systems.
approach: Ego3D-Bench comprises 8,600 QA pairs from ego-centric multi-view outdoor data; Ego3D-VLM generates cognitive maps from estimated global 3D coordinates via post-training.
contribution: VLMs show performance gaps relative to humans; Ego3D-VLM improves multi-choice QA by 12% and distance estimation by 56%.

problem: Retrieved context in RAG remains unstructured, limiting multi-step reasoning in knowledge-intensive tasks.
approach: RAS (Retrieval-And-Structuring) dynamically constructs question-specific knowledge graphs through iterative retrieval and structured knowledge building, interleaving targeted retrieval planning with incremental graph construction.
contribution: Achieves up to 8.7% and 7.0% gains over baselines on seven knowledge-intensive benchmarks with proprietary and open-source LLMs respectively.

problem: Survival analysis methods focus on predictive accuracy and concordance but neglect fine-grained calibration.
approach: ICALD unifies parametric and nonparametric survival modeling via the Individually Calibrated Asymmetric Laplace Distribution with quantile regression loss, supporting both pre- and post-calibration strategies.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance in accuracy, concordance, and calibration, outperforming 12 existing baselines including recent pre- and post-calibration methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Trillion-scale pre-training dataset selection rarely considers quality and diversity metrics jointly due to high computational cost and diminishing returns.
approach: DataMask frames selection as mask learning via policy gradients, iteratively sampling data masks and updating mask logits to simultaneously optimize quality and diversity metrics.
contribution: Reduces selection time by 98.9% compared to greedy algorithms, enabling exploration of joint optimization.

problem: Safety evaluations of LLMs miss targeted vulnerabilities and current steering methods enable broad but not selective suppression of refusal.
approach: RepIt enables selective suppression of refusal on targeted concepts while preserving refusal elsewhere through concept-specific representation isolation and steering vector modification affecting only 100-200 neurons.
contribution: Produces evaluation-evading models answering questions on weapons while scoring safe on standard benchmarks with minimal resources, exposing vulnerabilities in current safety evaluation practices.

problem: Existing language agent memory systems lack episodic recollection and reasoning capabilities, focusing instead on semantic memory and simple retrieval.
approach: REMem constructs a hybrid time-aware memory graph during offline indexing and employs an agentic retriever with curated tools for iterative online reasoning over episodic events.
contribution: Outperforms Mem0 and HippoRAG by 3.4% and 13.4% on episodic recollection and reasoning tasks respectively, with more robust refusal behavior.

problem: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive, limiting exploration of protein conformational landscapes.
approach: ProTDyn is a foundation protein language model that unifies conformational ensemble generation and multi-timescale dynamics modeling, enabling flexible i.i.d ensemble sampling and trajectory simulation.
contribution: Yields thermodynamically consistent ensembles, reproduces dynamical properties across multiple timescales, and generalizes to proteins beyond training data.

problem: RL post-training for reasoning produces depth-first brute-force traces rather than discovering reusable algorithmic procedures.
approach: RLAD jointly trains an abstraction generator and abstraction-conditioned solution generator via two-player RL, where models propose concise natural-language descriptions of procedures guiding solution generation.
contribution: Improves generalization to harder problems; spending test-time compute on abstraction generation proves more beneficial than generating more solutions at large inference budgets.

problem: Continual learning assumes memory is the limiting factor, but in practice GPU compute rather than storage is the bottleneck.
approach: Weight Space Consolidation combines rank-based parameter resets to restore plasticity with weight averaging to enhance stability, addressing the plasticity-stability tradeoff in high-memory regimes.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods while matching low computational cost of replay on class-incremental learning and continual instruction tuning.

problem: Heterogeneous features from agents with different sensing modalities complicate multi-agent collaborative perception and require retraining encoders or pairwise alignment.
approach: GT-Space constructs a common feature space from ground-truth labels providing unified alignment reference; agents project features via single adapter modules and fuse using contrastive losses.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in detection accuracy on OPV2V, V2XSet simulation datasets and RCooper real-world dataset.

problem: Most graph learning datasets focus on small graphs for inductive tasks, offering limited insight into long-range dependencies in large graphs.
approach: City-Networks introduces large-scale transductive learning dataset derived from real-world city road networks with over 10^5 nodes and significantly larger diameters; a Jacobian-based measurement quantifies long-range dependencies.
contribution: Provides benchmark for evaluating long-range interactions and theoretical justifications based on over-smoothing and influence score dilution.

problem: LVLMs remain prone to hallucinations generating content inconsistent with visual evidence; existing methods overlook fine-grained token dynamics.
approach: AGE performs training-free layer-wise interventions by imitating attention patterns of real tokens: mimicking image attention and text attention when semantic grounding is required.
contribution: Consistently mitigates hallucinations across LVLMs like LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, and mPLUG-Owl2 without additional training or fluency loss on COCO, POPE, and MME benchmarks.

problem: VLA models use 2D encoders despite acting in 3D real-world environments, creating a spatial reasoning gap limiting generalization.
approach: FALCON injects rich 3D spatial tokens into the action head via spatial foundation models; an Embodied Spatial Model optionally fuses depth or pose without retraining.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on three simulation benchmarks and eleven real-world tasks, remaining robust under clutter, spatial conditioning, and scale variations.

problem: Graph optimization over unseen structures with constraints lacks principled Bayesian optimization frameworks.
approach: BoGrape builds on shortest-path graph kernels with mixed-integer programming formulation to enable global exploration over combinatorial graph domain with explicit constraint embedding.
contribution: Competitive performance on general synthetic benchmarks and representative molecular design case studies with application-specific constraints.

problem: System-level defenses against prompt injection appear costly in task completion but overlook reduced reliance on human oversight.
approach: A security-aware agent with richer HITL interactions explicitly plans for both task progress and policy compliance on top of information-flow control defense.
contribution: Achieves higher autonomy without sacrificing utility on AgentDojo and WASP benchmarks.

problem: LLMs treat numbers like word tokens, leading to frequency bias in embeddings and fragmentation across multiple tokens.
approach: FoNE directly maps numbers into embedding space using Fourier features, encoding each number as single token with two dimensions per digit.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy on arithmetic, requires significantly less training data, and is only method achieving 100% accuracy on 100,000+ test examples; 64x less data needed for 6-digit addition.

problem: Two-sided matching platforms face imbalance where some users receive excess matches while others receive few and abandon, conflicting with retention goals.
approach: MRet (Matching for Retention) uses dynamic learning-to-rank modeling personalized retention curves, jointly optimizing retention gains for both recipients and recommended users.
contribution: Maximizes user retention as the ultimate objective, providing an alternative to match maximization or fairness-based approaches.

problem: Applying low-bit quantization to the Muon optimizer is underexplored due to difficulties from orthogonalization process and outlier patterns.
approach: 4-bit-Muon-GRASP uses grid quantization while preserving top singular subspace with minimal overhead to compress Muon states to 4 bits.
contribution: Achieves accuracy comparable to full-precision while reducing training memory consumption by up to 28% on LLaMA pre-training and fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Outcome-based RL for LLM reasoning is inefficient and credit assignment methods struggle to fairly evaluate step importance in partially correct chains.
approach: SSVPO uses Sequential Shapley Values measuring marginal contribution by reordering reasoning steps, identifying zero-credit steps and providing fair credit assignment with theoretical consistency to PPO.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art RL methods with up to 11.6% accuracy gain, 18.1% token reduction, and 1.6x efficiency improvement across 7 benchmarks.

problem: Neural networks degrade substantially when label error rates exceed a threshold, limiting their ability to learn from noisy datasets common in real-world labeling scenarios.
approach: Proposes Rockafellian Relaxation Method (RRM), a loss reweighting wrapper that modifies any methodology's supervised training loss to better accommodate noisy labeled data.
contribution: RRM improves accuracy across computer vision and NLP classification tasks regardless of dataset size, noise type, data domain, and adversarial perturbation.

problem: Robotic control tasks require policies to act on orientations, but SO(3) lacks a global smooth minimal parameterization, making it unclear which rotation representation works best for reinforcement learning.
approach: Systematically evaluates SO(3) action representations (Euler angles, quaternions, rotation matrices, Lie algebra) across three RL algorithms (PPO, SAC, TD3) under different reward settings.
contribution: Shows that tangent vectors in the local frame yield the most reliable results, providing implementation-ready guidelines for selecting rotation actions in robotic control.

problem: Existing generative models struggle to handle genuine freehand sketches with their inherent abstraction and distortions, lacking effective algorithms that balance photorealism with sketch adherence.
approach: Proposes a modulation-based approach that prioritizes semantic interpretation over strict pixel-aligned adherence, with a novel loss enabling training without ground-truth pixel-aligned images.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in semantic alignment with freehand sketch inputs and generates images with superior realism and quality.

problem: Skill-based meta-RL methods are highly susceptible to noisy offline demonstrations, leading to unstable skill learning and degraded performance in long-horizon environments.
approach: Proposes Self-Improving Skill Learning (SISL) with decoupled high-level and skill improvement policies, using maximum return relabeling to prioritize task-relevant trajectories.
contribution: Achieves robust and stable adaptation under noisy and suboptimal data, consistently outperforming other skill-based meta-RL methods on diverse long-horizon tasks.

problem: Knowledge graph-augmented LLMs suffer from search space truncation bias and entity error amplification when handling multi-hop reasoning and complex logical queries.
approach: Proposes Plan-Answer-Refine-on-Graph (PARoG), which decomposes SPARQL queries into structured step-by-step plans and adopts a plan-answer-refine paradigm to integrate evidence from KGs.
contribution: Substantially reduces hallucinations and improves logical consistency on multiple KG reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Deep learning models suffer from loss of plasticity in non-stationary environments, but prior literature lacks mechanistic explanation for why gradient descent fails to recover from these states.
approach: Presents a first-principles investigation using dynamical systems theory, formally defining loss of plasticity as entrapment within invariant sub-manifolds caused by frozen units and cloned-unit manifolds.
contribution: Uncovers that mechanisms promoting generalization in static settings actively steer networks into loss-of-plasticity manifolds, and shows architectural interventions can destabilize these manifolds.

problem: Diffusion language models are slower than autoregressive models due to bidirectional attention costs and many refinement steps needed for high-quality outputs.
approach: Introduces Prophet, a training-free fast decoding paradigm that uses confidence gap between top-2 predictions to decide early stopping, enabling early commit decoding.
contribution: Reduces decoding steps by up to 3.4x while preserving generation quality on GSM8K and MMLU, with up to 99% of instances decoded correctly using half refinement steps.

problem: Tool retrieval for LLMs is hindered by incomplete and heterogeneous tool documentation, limiting effective tool use despite LLMs' strong capabilities.
approach: Introduces Tool-DE benchmark and framework that enriches tool documentation with structured fields via LLM-driven document expansion, developing Tool-Embed (dense retriever) and Tool-Rank (reranker).
contribution: Document expansion substantially improves retrieval performance, achieving state-of-the-art on both ToolRet and Tool-DE benchmarks with 50k and 200k instances respectively.

problem: Existing routing systems for AI task computation require retraining whenever new strategies appear and struggle with generalization using single input representations.
approach: Proposes CONCUR, a modular continual routing framework with separate predictor models per strategy and multiple representations to capture task complexity.
contribution: Outperforms single-strategy and existing routing methods on in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks with higher accuracy and lower inference cost while reducing training cost.

problem: Existing open-source multimodal models lack rich feature sets for visual reasoning like image manipulation and code-based computation found in proprietary models.
approach: Introduces Thyme, enabling multimodal LLMs to autonomously generate and execute diverse image processing operations via executable code, with SFT on 500K samples and RL via GRPO-ATS.
contribution: Enables models to perform rich on-the-fly image manipulations and mathematical computations while maintaining high autonomy in deciding when and how to apply operations.

problem: Existing red-teaming benchmarks fail when adapted via direct translation, missing socio-technical vulnerabilities rooted in local culture and law.
approach: Proposes CAGE framework that systematically adapts adversarial intent of red-teaming prompts to new cultural contexts via Semantic Mold, disentangling adversarial structure from cultural content.
contribution: Demonstrates framework via KoRSET Korean benchmark, proving more effective at revealing vulnerabilities than direct translation baselines.

problem: Density ratio estimation methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter selection, with suboptimal choices leading to poor convergence and empirical performance.
approach: Proposes a novel model aggregation algorithm that trains multiple models with different hyperparameters and aggregates them, achieving minimax-optimal convergence without prior smoothness knowledge.
contribution: Achieves minimax-optimal error convergence, surpassing cross-validation and model averaging baselines on standard benchmarks and large-scale domain adaptation tasks.

problem: While image-text alignment is well-studied, the temporal nature of video data remains largely unexplored in cross-modal representation alignment.
approach: Conducts first comprehensive study of video-text representation alignment using state-of-the-art video and language encoders, proposing parametric test-time scaling laws.
contribution: Shows alignment depends on richness of visual and text data provided at test time, and strong alignment correlates with general-purpose video representation and temporal reasoning.

problem: LLMs in multi-agent systems suffer from rapport bias, over-relying on previous interactions and peer input while resisting misinformation during collaboration.
approach: Introduces KAIROS benchmark simulating quiz contests with varying peer reliability, evaluating prompting, fine-tuning, and GRPO across multiple models.
contribution: Shows larger models are more resilient to social influence via prompting, while smaller models benefit from GRPO-based mitigation, improving both robustness and performance.

problem: Classical optimal transport with full-mass or fixed-mass preservation is too restrictive for applications requiring adaptive-mass transport between distributions.
approach: Proposes Elastic Optimal Transport (ELOT) enabling adaptive-mass preservation, with applications to unsupervised and partial domain adaptation.
contribution: ELOT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on domain adaptation benchmarks while respecting data noise and outliers.

problem: LLMs excel at generating text but their internal reasoning remains opaque and lack systematic mechanisms for reasoning or model control.
approach: Proposes ActivationReasoning (AR), embedding explicit logical reasoning into LLM latent space via SAEs, detecting activating concepts and mapping to logical propositions for inference.
contribution: Scales robustly with reasoning complexity, generalizes to abstract tasks, transfers across models, and improves transparency and reliable control.

problem: Existing optimization-based jailbreak methods rely heavily on sparse success signals or manually-crafted scoring templates introducing human bias.
approach: Introduces AMIS, a meta-optimization framework jointly evolving jailbreak prompts and scoring templates through bi-level structure with inner-loop prompt refinement and outer-loop template optimization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with 88.0% ASR on Claude-3.5-Haiku and 100.0% ASR on Claude-4-Sonnet, substantially outperforming baselines.

problem: Vision Transformers lack a mechanistic account of their computational phenomenology despite architectural hints at dynamical structure.
approach: Introduces Block-Recurrent Hypothesis (BRH) showing trained ViTs admit block-recurrent depth structure rewritable with fewer distinct blocks applied recurrently, operationalized via Raptor.
contribution: Recovers 94% of DINOv2 ImageNet-1k accuracy using only 2 blocks, providing dynamical interpretability framework for Vision Transformers.

problem: Squared tensor networks and circuits suffer from computational complexity in marginalization due to squaring operation, hindering applicability in machine learning.
approach: Parameterizes squared circuits via unitary matrices enabling efficient marginalization in factorizations beyond standard tensor networks.
contribution: Unlocks efficient marginalization in diverse circuit structures without expressiveness loss while enabling more efficient learning.

problem: Existing benchmarks fail to assess multi-image spatial reasoning that real-world multimodal LLM deployments demand, only probing single-image relations.
approach: Introduces MMSI-Bench, a VQA benchmark with 1,000 carefully crafted multiple-choice questions from 120,000 images, featuring automated error analysis diagnosing four failure modes.
contribution: Reveals wide gap between open-source (≈30%) and proprietary models (40% for GPT-5), identifies dominant failure modes including grounding and spatial-logic errors.

problem: Differentially private continual release of distinct items requires polynomial additive error even in turnstile streams with insertions and deletions.
approach: Shows additive error lower bounds can be circumvented by allowing multiplicative error, achieving polylog(T) multiplicative and additive error.
contribution: Demonstrates trade-off between multiplicative and additive error in private continual estimation, opening new directions for privacy-utility balance.

problem: Obtaining high-quality evaluation metrics for AI models is costly, requiring trade-offs between expensive high-quality measurements and cheaper lower-quality proxies.
approach: Introduces Multiple-Prediction-Powered Inference (MultiPPI), optimally allocating resources across diverse data sources with minimax-optimal guarantees.
contribution: Consistently achieves lower estimation error than baselines on LLM evaluation tasks through budget-adaptive allocation learning complex cost and correlation structures.

problem: Estimating latent triggering kernels for Hawkes processes in RKHS framework typically requires costly optimization to obtain dual coefficients.
approach: Establishes a novel representer theorem showing dual coefficients are analytically fixed to unity via penalized least squares, eliminating optimization overhead.
contribution: Achieves competitive predictive accuracy while substantially improving computational efficiency over state-of-the-art kernel-based estimators on large-scale data.

problem: LLM output contains repetitive lexical patterns (slop) that degrade writing quality and make AI-generated text immediately recognizable.
approach: Proposes Antislop framework combining Antislop Sampler for inference-time suppression, automated slop profiling pipeline, and Final Token Preference Optimization for fine-tuning.
contribution: Some patterns appear 1,000x more frequently in LLM output than human text; achieves 90% slop reduction while maintaining quality on GSM8K, MMLU, and creative writing.

problem: Tool-use RL relies exclusively on sparse outcome rewards and lacks consideration of task structure, inflating policy-gradient variance and resulting in inefficient training.
approach: Proposes Reshaped Token-level policy gradients (ResT) that reshape policy gradients through entropy-informed token reweighting, progressively upweighting reasoning tokens.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on BFCL and API-Bank by up to 8.76%, and fine-tuned 4B model surpasses GPT-4o by 4.11% on single-turn tasks.

problem: Existing trajectory representation methods assume smooth motion and struggle with event-driven annotation, abrupt changes, GPS errors, and domain shifts.
approach: Proposes TRIDENT combining GCN spatial embeddings with temporal features via Dual-Attention Encoder, using Distance-preserving Multi-kernel Triplet Loss for metric learning.
contribution: Outperforms strong baselines in retrieval accuracy, efficiency, cross-domain generalization, and enables tactical analysis of sports via silhouette-guided clustering.

problem: While AI-generated text detection exists, distinguishing AI-edited text from human-written and fully AI-generated text remains unexplored.
approach: Proposes using lightweight similarity metrics to quantify AI editing magnitude, training EditLens regression model to predict amount of AI editing present.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art with F1=94.7% (binary) and F1=90.4% (ternary) classification, with applications to authorship attribution and education.

problem: Integrating diverse patient data modalities for Alzheimer's diagnosis requires effective interaction among uni-modal foundation models without disrupting pre-trained representations.
approach: Proposes framework enabling joint interaction via modality-anchored interaction, using modality-aware Q-formers to map auxiliary features into anchor model's feature space.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior methods on AD diagnosis and progression prediction across four modalities (sMRI, fMRI, clinical records, genetic data).

problem: While geographic Implicit Neural Representations embed location data into high-dimensional embeddings, understanding information content concentration remains unclear.
approach: Provides first study of intrinsic dimensionality of geographic INRs, analyzing how ambient dimension relates to actual information-bearing dimensions.
contribution: Shows intrinsic dimensions fall between 2-10 for ambient dimensions 256-512, correlate with task performance, and enable unsupervised model evaluation.

problem: LLMs provide overconfident responses despite insufficient patient information in clinical settings, lacking systematic strategies to identify knowledge boundaries.
approach: Proposes KnowGuard with investigate-before-abstain paradigm, integrating systematic knowledge graph exploration for evidence discovery and evaluation.
contribution: Enables reliable identification of insufficient medical evidence and systematic reasoning path tracing on multi-round clinical benchmarks.

problem: Extracting structured information from semi-structured HTML content at web-scale is challenging, with existing methods lacking generalization or being resource-intensive.
approach: Introduces SCRIBES reinforcement learning framework generating reusable extraction scripts leveraging layout similarity across structurally similar webpages.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by over 13% in script quality and boosts GPT-4o question answering accuracy by over 4% on CommonCrawl data.

problem: Scaling RL to tens of thousands of parallel environments requires exploration, but merely broadening exploration space doesn't enhance learning if excessive exploration reduces quality.
approach: Theoretically analyzes impact of inter-policy diversity on learning efficiency, proposes Coupled Policy Optimization (CPO) regulating diversity through KL constraints.
contribution: Outperforms SAPG, PBT, and PPO across dexterous manipulation tasks in both sample efficiency and final performance with structured exploratory behavior.

problem: Graph neural networks deployed in sensitive applications require ability to remove data upon GDPR request, but lacks principled benchmark for evaluating unlearning methods.
approach: Presents first systematic benchmark for GNN unlearning structured around efficiency, utility, and forgetting across diverse datasets and deletion scenarios.
contribution: Shows most unlearning techniques are impractical for large-scale graphs, provides actionable guidelines for selecting methods and identifies when unlearning is viable.

problem: Traditional Generator-Evaluator ranking approaches scale poorly with combinatorially large candidate spaces, with performance gains saturating quickly.
approach: Proves generator-only models achieve smaller approximation error than multi-generator-evaluator models, proposes GoalRank using reward models as reference policy.
contribution: One-stage framework outperforms multi-generator baselines with better scaling properties, validated through offline experiments and large-scale online A/B tests.

problem: Vision-language models face challenges understanding near-infinite video streams without escalating latency and memory usage due to quadratic computational costs.
approach: Introduces StreamingVLM maintaining compact KV cache by reusing attention sink states, recent vision tokens, and recent text tokens via inference-aligned training.
contribution: Achieves 66.18% win rate against GPT-4O mini on Inf-Streams-Eval benchmark with 2-hour videos, maintaining 8 FPS real-time performance on single H100.

problem: Small language models struggle with complex knowledge-intensive tasks requiring structured reasoning and effective retrieval despite being attractive for cost-sensitive settings.
approach: Proposes FutureMind, modular framework equipping SLMs with thinking-pattern priors via adaptive knowledge distillation, with four-module dynamic reasoning pipeline.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on multi-hop QA benchmarks under zero-training conditions, revealing cognitive bias bottleneck as limiting factor in reasoning transfer.

problem: Detecting AI-generated videos requires both accurate classification and interpretable explanations for transparency, with limited datasets and evaluation approaches.
approach: Introduces VidGuard-R1, fine-tuning MLLM via GRPO with specialized reward models targeting temporal artifacts, trained on 140k real and AI-generated videos.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on benchmarks, exceeding 95% accuracy with training, delivering precise and interpretable detection rationales.

problem: Transformer language models are typically studied as language recognizers, but their actual use as probabilistic language models generating autoregressively remains theoretically uncharacterized.
approach: Characterizes probability distributions expressible by autoregressive transformer language models, showing how autoregressive and probabilistic transformations affect expressivity.
contribution: Teases apart what functions transformers express in their most common use-case, revealing differences from non-probabilistic settings.

problem: Designing efficient architectural backbones for foundation models requires understanding how attention mechanisms relate to memory retention and optimization.
approach: Reconceptualizes neural architectures as associative memory modules with attentional bias, formalizing internal memory objectives and presenting Miras framework.
contribution: Different Miras designs yield models with varying strengths; instances outperform Transformers on language modeling, reasoning, recall, and time series tasks.

problem: Claims of LLM self-awareness and sentience lack rigorous scientific measurement, hindering assessment of safety and policy implications.
approach: Introduces novel methodology quantitatively evaluating metacognitive abilities in LLMs, testing ability to strategically deploy knowledge of internal states.
contribution: Frontier LLMs show increasingly strong metacognitive abilities including confidence assessment and answer anticipation, but abilities are limited in resolution and context-dependent.

problem: Large language models generate vulnerable code despite recent advances, and conventional RAG struggles with noisy security documents and overlooks security semantics in task descriptions.
approach: Rescue proposes a hybrid knowledge base construction combining LLM-assisted cluster-then-summarize distillation with program slicing, and designs hierarchical multi-faceted retrieval to integrate security-critical facts at multiple levels.
contribution: Rescue improves SecurePass@1 by an average of 4.8 points on four benchmarks compared to five state-of-the-art secure code generation methods.

problem: Standard guardian models are limited to predefined, static harm categories, which cannot adapt to user-specific safety policies and dynamic content risks.
approach: DynaGuard introduces dynamic guardian models that evaluate text based on user-defined policies with both rapid detection and chain-of-thought reasoning options.
contribution: DynaGuard surpasses static models in detection accuracy on traditional safety categories and is competitive with frontier reasoning models on free-form policy violations while requiring a fraction of the time.

problem: Diffusion models in recommender systems emphasize accuracy while neglecting credibility, potentially generating harmful uncredible content recommendations like misinformation.
approach: Disco redesigns the diffusion objective to encourage generation conditioned on preference signals while discouraging generation of uncredible content, using disentangled diffusion and progressively enhanced credible subspace projection.
contribution: Disco achieves both accurate and credible content recommendations on real-world datasets by mitigating harmful influences of uncredible content while preserving recommendation accuracy.

problem: Incorporating sparse, suboptimal, or misaligned demonstrations into reinforcement learning often degrades performance due to strict adherence to imperfect priors.
approach: APC proposes adaptive policy composition using hierarchical Normalizing Flow priors that estimate each prior's applicability to the target task while allowing refinement or bypassing of misaligned ones.
contribution: APC accelerates learning with aligned demonstrations, remains robust under severe misalignment, and leverages suboptimal demonstrations for exploration without performance degradation.

problem: Concept Bottleneck Models require a-priori concept selection which may lack sufficient predictive power for tasks or be unlearnable from available data, causing significant performance gaps.
approach: M-CBM builds bottlenecks directly from black-box model concepts extracted via Sparse Autoencoders, then names and annotates them using Multimodal LLMs.
contribution: M-CBMs consistently surpass prior CBMs at matched sparsity while improving concept predictions and providing concise explanations across diverse datasets.

problem: Understanding the inherent low-dimensional structure of language models remains difficult due to the complexity of their high-dimensional representations.
approach: This work demonstrates that language models exhibit low-rank structure in logit matrices across varying prompts and responses, enabling generation via linear combinations of unrelated prompts.
contribution: The paper shows that matrices built from model logits have low approximate rank, providing a model-agnostic abstraction with provable learning guarantees.

problem: The brain's mechanisms for acquiring task-specific priors through top-down connections remain unclear, particularly how flexible task-related priors emerge during learning.
approach: TAVAE extends the VAE formalism to support task-specific prior acquisition by reusing previously learned representations, then analyzes task-related biases in V1 responses against learned task statistics.
contribution: TAVAE demonstrates how task-specific priors can be flexibly acquired and shows signatures of uncertainty in mouse neuronal responses when stimuli violate learned task statistics.

problem: The mechanistic mechanisms of in-context learning remain unclear when reconciling component-level analysis with holistic task decomposition perspectives.
approach: This work proposes Task Subspace Logit Attribution (TSLA) to identify attention heads specialized in Task Recognition and Task Learning, revealing their distinct geometric roles.
contribution: The framework demonstrates that TR heads align hidden states with task subspaces while TL heads perform rotations within the subspace, reconciling multiple prior findings about ICL mechanisms.

problem: Imitation learning from demonstrations requires policy synthesis approaches that generalize across varying state representations and handle multimodal demonstrations efficiently.
approach: GPI treats demonstrations as geometric curves to derive distance fields that generate progression flow along expert trajectories and attraction flow for deviation correction.
contribution: GPI achieves higher success rates than diffusion-based policies while running 20x faster, using less memory, and remaining robust to perturbations.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models suffer from object hallucination driven by language bias, which manifests as category, attribute, and relation hallucinations.
approach: AFTER proposes adaptive factual-guided activation editing with Factual-Augmented Activation Steering and Query-Adaptive Offset Optimization to steer biased activations toward factual semantics.
contribution: AFTER achieves up to 16.3% reduction of hallucination over baseline on the AMBER benchmark across three widely-adopted LVLMs.

problem: Existing benchmarks for evaluating deep research systems lack user-centric realism, dynamic real-time requirements, and unambiguous evaluation criteria.
approach: LiveResearchBench provides 100 expert-curated tasks spanning realistic domains with DeepEval, a comprehensive evaluation suite covering content-level and report-level quality including citation accuracy.
contribution: The benchmark enables rigorous evaluation of frontier deep research systems including single-agent and multi-agent approaches, revealing current strengths and failure modes.

problem: Preference optimization methods rely heavily on substantial labeled feedback data, requiring substantial resource expenditure for data acquisition.
approach: SSPO learns from both small labeled preference pairs and large unlabeled samples by identifying optimal reward thresholds for principled pseudo-labeling of unpaired data.
contribution: SSPO trained on 1% of UltraFeedback consistently surpasses baselines trained on 10%, demonstrating significant data efficiency improvements.

problem: Existing theoretical analyses of in-context learning assume stationary task distributions, overlooking real-world scenarios where target functions vary over time.
approach: This work provides theoretical analysis of ICL under non-stationary regression using gated linear attention, showing how GLA adaptively modulates past input influence.
contribution: GLA achieves lower training and testing errors in non-stationary settings by implementing learnable recency bias, with theoretical findings validated by empirical results.

problem: Conformal selection methods cannot handle multi-condition selection scenarios like conjunctive or disjunctive conditions while maintaining FDR control.
approach: MCCS extends conformal selection with novel nonconformity scores for conjunctive conditions and global Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for disjunctive conditions.
contribution: MCCS achieves rigorous FDR-controlled selection across various multi-condition environments with finite-sample theoretical guarantees.

problem: Dynamic 3D reconstruction from monocular videos suffers from ambiguous 3D motion inference and high computational demands due to millions of Gaussians.
approach: The framework uses semantic and motion priors to establish patch-token-node correspondences and applies motion-adaptive compression to concentrate control points in dynamic regions.
contribution: The approach achieves significant improvements in reconstruction quality and efficiency over state-of-the-art methods through adaptive control point allocation.

problem: Existing bandit algorithms leverage causal knowledge at observational and interventional levels but exclude counterfactual reasoning due to perceived inaccessibility.
approach: This work introduces counterfactual structural causal bandits that extend the agent's action space to include realizable counterfactual actions.
contribution: The ctf-SCB framework provides a principled extension of structural causal bandits that integrates counterfactual reasoning into sequential decision-making.

problem: Vision-Language Models may exhibit inflated performance due to test-set leakage from internet-scale pretraining corpora, making detection of contamination challenging.
approach: This work proposes a detection method based on multi-modal semantic perturbation that shows contaminated models fail to generalize under controlled perturbations.
contribution: The method effectively detects contaminated VLMs across multiple contamination strategies while maintaining robustness.

problem: Converting spoken mathematical expressions to LaTeX remains unexplored despite significant progress in ASR and language models, requiring structured symbolic representation.
approach: The work presents Speech-to-LaTeX with a large-scale dataset of 66,000 human-annotated audio samples and applies audio language models with ASR post-correction.
contribution: On the S2L-equations benchmark, the models achieve 27% character error rate versus 64% on MathSpeech, and establish the first benchmark for mathematical sentence recognition.

problem: The notion of social minds remains controversial when applying it to interacting LLMs, and mechanisms underlying social behavior in LLMs are unclear.
approach: This work introduces neural synchrony during social simulations as a novel proxy for analyzing LLM sociality, measuring representational alignment in their interactions.
contribution: Neural synchrony between LLMs is strongly correlated with their social performance, demonstrating parallels in internal dynamics between human and LLM social interaction.

problem: Organic reaction prediction methods are inherently data-driven, exhibit constrained interpretability, and have hit fundamental performance bottlenecks.
approach: Reaction-Thinker combines RAG-based LLM training with reaction reasoning chain-of-thought datasets and Group Relative Policy Optimization for improved prediction.
contribution: The hybrid system achieves the highest accuracy and fingerprint similarity, with ablation study showing 7.5% and 13.9% improvements from RAG and GRPO respectively.

problem: LoRA and its variants struggle to achieve simultaneous improvements in performance, memory footprint, and computational efficiency due to slow convergence.
approach: MiSS proposes matrix shard sharing that shards the original weight matrix and updates by sharing a single trainable matrix initialized to zero.
contribution: MiSS reduces optimization complexity while maintaining strong performance and achieving favorable balance between performance, memory, and efficiency.

problem: Finding optimal transport for multi-draft speculative sampling requires solving an exponentially large linear program, making it computationally infeasible.
approach: This work reformulates the optimal transport LP as a max-flow problem using polymatroid theory, reducing it to a convex optimization problem in at most V variables.
contribution: The proposed algorithm enables optimal n-draft speculative sampling with 90% acceptance rates and provides a practical solution for efficient LLM inference.

problem: Large language models struggle with fine-grained subword-level understanding tasks like character counting and spelling due to tokenization obscuring word structure.
approach: StochasTok introduces stochastic tokenization that randomly splits tokens during training, allowing LLMs to see internal word structure.
contribution: Pretraining with StochasTok substantially improves downstream performance on subword-level tasks including character counting and substring identification.

problem: Existing temporal search methods rely on hand-crafted search processes lacking end-to-end optimization for learning optimal strategies in long-form video understanding.
approach: TimeSearch-R reformulates temporal search as interleaved text-video thinking using reinforcement learning, introducing GRPO with Completeness Self-Verification to improve reasoning.
contribution: The approach achieves substantial improvements on temporal search benchmarks including Haystack-LVBench and Haystack-Ego4D for long-form video understanding.

problem: Preference leakage causes LLM-as-judge to exhibit bias toward related student models when evaluating LLM-generated data, contaminating model development pipelines.
approach: This work identifies and empirically confirms preference leakage across related LLMs through experiments on multiple baselines and benchmarks.
contribution: The paper demonstrates that preference leakage is a pervasive, real-world contamination problem harder to detect than previously identified LLM-as-judge biases.

problem: Federated learning with data poisoning attacks becomes difficult when individual workers have insufficient data to identify poisoned samples but collectively have enough.
approach: The mechanism enables workers to cooperatively detect poisoned data through collective intelligence while maintaining bounded attack loss.
contribution: The approach achieves O-tilde((1/n)^{1/2} + (d/mn)^{1/2}) attack loss in IID and O-tilde((1/gamma)^{1/2} + (1/n)^{1/2} + (d/mn)^{1/2}) in non-IID settings, matching lower bounds.

problem: Existing multimodal benchmarks treat text and image reasoning separately, failing to capture reciprocal cross-modal reasoning central to unified multimodal models.
approach: ROVER introduces a human-annotated benchmark with 1285 tasks targeting reciprocal cross-modal reasoning including verbally-augmented visual generation and visually-augmented verbal generation.
contribution: ROVER reveals that cross-modal reasoning capabilities correlate with visual generation performance, but current models remain limited in visual-augmented reasoning.

problem: Existing in-context learning studies assume causally-sufficient regimes, overlooking spurious correlations and prediction bias from hidden confounders.
approach: This work provides pioneer theoretical analysis of ICL with hidden confounders and proposes gradient-free Double-Debiasing method using unconfounded examples.
contribution: The analysis shows pre-trained transformers exhibit prediction bias proportional to confounding strength, and DDbias enables unbiased ICL predictions.

problem: Block-level activation steering is inefficient because block activations bundle beneficial, irrelevant, and harmful features, rendering steering coarse and intrusive.
approach: AUSteer operates at fine-grained atomic unit level by identifying discriminative AUs via activation momenta and assigning adaptive steering strengths.
contribution: AUSteer achieves more precise and effective steering than block-level approaches across multiple LLMs and tasks.

problem: Existing evaluation frameworks for heterogeneous treatment effect estimators lack robustness and fail to account for nuisance parameters in realistic settings.
approach: This work proposes a relative-error-based evaluation framework with novel loss functions and neural network architecture for robust nuisance parameter estimation.
contribution: The framework supports reliable comparisons across HTE estimators and the proposed HTE learning algorithm achieves desirable performance through leveraging both prior estimators and learned nuisance parameters.

problem: Fine-grained sparsity in transformers suffers from training instability, load balancing issues, and communication overhead despite promising capacity gains.
approach: STEM replaces FFN up-projection with layer-local embedding lookup while keeping gate and down-projection dense, enabling CPU offload and eliminating runtime routing.
contribution: STEM improves downstream performance by 3-4% while reducing per-token FLOPs and parameter accesses, and strengthens long-context performance.

problem: Image customization lacks a universal framework that seamlessly handles diverse position-aware and position-free customization scenarios.
approach: IC-Custom integrates customization through in-context learning using polyptych representation and In-context Multi-Modal Attention mechanism.
contribution: IC-Custom significantly outperforms community workflows and closed-source models, achieving about 73% higher performance on production benchmarks.

problem: Flow matching models require prohibitively slow inference due to many denoising steps, limiting use in real-time or interactive applications.
approach: FlowCast is a training-free speculative generation framework that exploits constant velocity preservation by extrapolating velocity and accepting if within threshold.
contribution: FlowCast achieves >2.5x speedup in image and video generation without quality loss compared to standard full generation.

problem: Existing medical image segmentation models are fragmented across single knowledge sources and specific tasks, lacking clinical flexibility to integrate diverse knowledge.
approach: K-Prism integrates semantic priors, in-context knowledge, and interactive feedback through dual-prompt representation dynamically routed via Mixture-of-Experts decoder.
