approach: Present OmniCT, a unified slice-volume LVLM with spatial consistency enhancement via volumetric composition and tri-axial encoding, organ-level semantic enhancement via segmentation, and MedEval-CT benchmark.
contribution: First unified slice-volume LVLM for CT enabling comprehensive analysis of both sub-centimeter details and inter-organ relationships.

problem: Long video reasoning in LVLMs is hindered by uniform frame sampling and static reasoning, unable to handle visually intensive tasks efficiently.
approach: Introduce FrameThinker with iterative frame interrogation via two-phase training: supervised fine-tuning for action learning followed by reinforcement learning with comprehensive reward design.
contribution: Achieves +10.4% average improvement on reasoning benchmarks while drastically reducing processed frames; establishes state-of-the-art on LongVideo-Reason at 76.1%.

problem: Audio-visual knowledge distillation struggles to match feature dimensions between teacher-student or trades accuracy for flexibility in teacher-student pairing.
approach: Propose Entropy-Monitored Kernelized Token Distillation (EM-KTD), which distills pairwise relationships between embeddings via Gram matrices with adaptive entropy-based modulation.
contribution: Uses 94% fewer parameters while preserving 96.9% performance on audio-visual event recognition and 96.5% on audio-visual segmentation.

problem: Monocular 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM suffers from time-consuming per-frame optimization, geometric inaccuracy, and multi-view inconsistency.
approach: Present Flash-Mono using feed-forward prediction to directly forecast camera poses and Gaussian properties from multi-frame context via recurrent cross-attention, with 2D Gaussian surfels replacing 3D ellipsoids.
contribution: Achieves 10× speedup compared to optimization-based methods while ensuring high-quality rendering and robust loop closure via hidden-state submap descriptors.

problem: Egocentric 3D hand reconstruction faces depth ambiguity, self-occlusion, and complex hand-object interactions that unseen contexts challenge.
approach: Introduce EgoHandICL, the first in-context learning framework for 3D hand reconstruction using complementary exemplar retrieval via VLMs, ICL-tailored tokenizer with multimodal context, and MAE-based architecture.
contribution: Demonstrates significant improvements on ARCTIC and EgoExo4D benchmarks with applicability to real-world egocentric scenarios and integration with EgoVLMs.

problem: Minimizing polarization in opinion dynamics requires learning unknown innate opinions from scalar feedback in online settings, a challenge absent in prior static-setting work.
approach: Formulate polarization minimization as regret minimization under opinion dynamics with unknown parameters, propose two-stage low-rank matrix bandit algorithm with subspace estimation.
contribution: Achieves Õ(√T) cumulative regret over horizon T, establishing connection between social media interventions and multi-armed bandits.

problem: Plain Vision Transformers are slow and impractical for efficiency-critical applications, while existing acceleration methods sacrifice generality or accuracy.
approach: Introduce Jumbo token with wider processing via efficient shared FFN, maintaining plain-ViT compatibility while increasing global context.
contribution: Improves ViT baselines at Nano-Large scales while maintaining speed; gains 4.9% on MAE pre-training, 5.2% on test-time adaptation, compatible with ViT methods.

problem: Inversion-free flow-based image editing exhibits unstable trajectories and poor source consistency despite theoretical advantages.
approach: Propose FlowAlign, adding flow-matching loss as regularization to promote smooth, stable editing trajectories that balance semantic alignment with source preservation.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in source preservation and editing controllability; naturally supports reversible editing via trajectory reversal.

problem: Malicious LLM agents can probe others in multi-turn interactions to extract sensitive information, but evolving vulnerabilities are hard to anticipate.
approach: Present a search-based framework alternating between attack and defense strategy improvement through simulation, using LLMs as optimizers to propose new instructions with parallel search.
contribution: Discovers escalating attack tactics from direct requests to impersonation and consent forgery; defenses evolve from rules to robust identity-verification; strategies transfer across scenarios.

problem: Training LLM agents on complex tool-use tasks suffers from extreme data scarcity, with supervised fine-tuning overfitting and standard RL cold-start and instability.
approach: Introduce Environment Tuning, a paradigm learning directly from problem instances via structured curriculum, actionable environment augmentation with corrective feedback, and fine-grained progress rewards.
contribution: Achieves competitive in-distribution performance and superior out-of-distribution generalization using only 400 BFCL problem instances, overcoming SFT performance collapse.

problem: Predicting biomolecular binding affinity is challenging due to limited high-quality data and existing methods specialized for specific interaction types.
approach: Repurpose AlphaFold 3 for representation learning introducing Atom-level Diffusion Transformer (ADiT), unified tokenization, diffusion transformers, and removal of MSA/template dependencies.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on protein-ligand, drug-target, protein-protein, and antibody-antigen interactions; identifies wet-lab validated affinity-enhancing mutations.

problem: Feedforward 3D reconstruction from sparse images often produces discrete, color-biased point clouds lacking surface continuity.
approach: Present SurfSplat using 2D Gaussian Splatting with surface continuity priors and forced alpha blending, introducing High-Resolution Rendering Consistency (HRRC) for evaluation.
contribution: Reconstructs coherent geometry with faithful textures outperforming prior methods on RealEstate10K, DL3DV, and ScanNet.

problem: Reasoning over long contexts requires advanced thinking patterns but high-difficulty RL data for long-context reasoning is scarce.
approach: Introduce LoongRL with KeyChain, a synthesis approach transforming short multi-hop QA into high-difficulty long-context tasks via UUID chains hiding questions among distracting documents.
contribution: Models trained at 16K effectively solve 128K tasks; LoongRL-14B reaches 74.2 on long-context multi-hop QA, rivaling o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1; improves retrieval and preserves short-context reasoning.

problem: Temporal knowledge graph reasoning fails for emerging entities without historical interactions, though similar entities exhibit transferable temporal patterns.
approach: Propose TransFIR, which categorizes emerging entities into latent semantic clusters using codebook-based classifier, allowing them to adopt reasoning patterns from similar known entities.
contribution: Achieves average 28.6% improvement in Mean Reciprocal Rank on emerging entity reasoning across multiple datasets.

problem: Cross-entropy scaling law breaks down at very large model scales, with loss decreasing slower than expected, complicating large language model development.
approach: Decompose cross-entropy into Error-Entropy, Self-Alignment, and Confidence; show error-entropy alone follows power-law scaling while other components remain invariant.
contribution: Establishes error-entropy scaling law as more accurate descriptor of model behavior across 32 models spanning five orders of magnitude in size.

problem: Leveraging offline non-curated data (reward-free, mixed quality, multi-embodiment) for offline-to-online RL fails due to distributional shift during fine-tuning.
approach: Apply experience rehearsal and execution guidance techniques to address distributional shift, enabling effective world model fine-tuning on offline data.
contribution: Achieves 102.8% relative improvement in aggregate score across 72 visuomotor tasks on limited sample budgets; outperforms prior offline RL methods on manipulation and locomotion.

problem: Training LLM-based agents for complex desktop automation via end-to-end RL is challenging due to environmental inefficiency and training instability over extended runs.
approach: Introduce ComputerRL framework with API-GUI paradigm unifying APIs and GUI interaction, distributed RL infrastructure orchestrating thousands of parallel virtual desktops, and Entropulse strategy alternating RL with SFT.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art 48.9% accuracy on OSWorld benchmark with GLM-ComputerRL-9B; demonstrates significant improvements for general desktop automation agents.

problem: Federated learning in Riemannian settings faces challenges from partial participation and data heterogeneity with limited theoretical analysis.
approach: Present RFedAGS, a Riemannian FL algorithm based on averaging gradient streams server aggregation, handling partial participation and heterogeneity.
contribution: Achieves global convergence and sublinear/linear convergence rates under decaying and fixed step sizes with performance validated on synthetic and real-world data.

problem: Extracting morphological traits from biological images remains slow and expert-driven, limiting large-scale ecological studies due to lack of trait-level annotated datasets.
approach: Use sparse autoencoders on foundation-model features to identify monosemantic neurons, then localize salient regions and prompt vision-language models to generate trait descriptions.
contribution: Constructs Bioscan-Traits with 80K trait annotations from 19K insect images; improves BioCLIP zero-shot species classification on in-the-wild Insects benchmark.

problem: Reconstructing high-fidelity 3D clothed portraits from unconstrained in-the-wild photos varies significantly in pose, viewpoint, cropping, and occlusion.
approach: Introduce UP2You, a tuning-free solution using data rectifier paradigm to convert unconstrained inputs into clean orthogonal multi-view images, with pose-correlated feature aggregation (PCFA) module.
contribution: Surpasses prior methods in geometric accuracy (15% Chamfer reduction, 18% P2S on PuzzleIOI) and texture fidelity; efficient at 1.5 minutes per person with multi-garment virtual try-on support.

problem: Zero-shot human-object interaction detection couples interaction recognition tightly to specific detectors and relies on coarse-grained VLM features, limiting generalization.
approach: Propose decoupled framework separating object detection from interaction recognition via MLLMs for zero-shot IR, introducing deterministic generation formulated as VQA and spatial-aware pooling.
contribution: Achieves superior zero-shot performance with strong cross-dataset generalization and flexibility to integrate with any object detectors without retraining.

problem: Alignment of LLMs with human preferences is undermined by noisy labels, but existing robust methods rely on narrow single heuristics missing diverse noise.
approach: Introduce diagnostic-driven meta-learning paradigm where models learn to fuse multiple intrinsic feedback streams (preference consistency, learning difficulty, generation confidence) for holistic reliability assessment.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art across various noise conditions; provides first quantitative analysis showing fusion of diagnostics essential vs. any single heuristic.

problem: Can Mixture-of-Experts surpass dense architectures under strictly equal resource constraints including parameter count, compute, and data?
approach: Comprehensively investigate MoE architecture and find optimal design; demonstrate MoE with optimal activation rate outperforms dense counterparts under same total resources.
contribution: Validates through nearly 200 models at 2B scale and 50+ at 7B scale on 50 trillion tokens; shows data reuse resolves performance-data tradeoff; all code and models released.

problem: Two-stage framework combining reward-free behavioral cloning with online preference-based feedback lacks principled analysis connecting offline data to online efficiency.
approach: Provide first principled analysis of offline-to-online approach; introduce BRIDGE algorithm integrating both signals via uncertainty-weighted objective with derived regret bounds.
contribution: Derives regret bounds shrinking with offline demonstration quantity; validates lower regret than standalone behavioral cloning or online preference-based RL.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with reasoning across modalities, with conflicting reports on whether additional modalities help or harm, due to lack of controlled evaluation frameworks.
approach: Introduce logic-grounded evaluation framework categorizing reasoning into six interaction patterns; identify two core failures: task-composition bottleneck and fusion bottleneck.
contribution: Reveals additional modalities enhance reasoning only with independent sufficient paths; proposes two-step prompting (recognize then reason) addressing failures.

problem: Existing multimodal agents specialize in either 2D GUI or 3D embodied environments but cannot seamlessly handle tasks requiring interactions across both types of environments.
approach: OmniActor uses a Layer-heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts architecture that separates parameters at deep layers to eliminate data conflicts while sharing parameters at shallow layers to leverage synergy, paired with unified action spaces and large-scale diverse datasets.
contribution: OmniActor outperforms agents trained solely on GUI or embodied data in their respective tasks, particularly excelling at GUI tasks with the unified framework.

problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems still hallucinate despite having correct and sufficient context, due to imbalance between how models use external context versus internal knowledge.
approach: LUMINA detects hallucinations through context-knowledge signals by quantifying external context utilization via distributional distance and measuring internal knowledge utilization via token evolution across transformer layers, with statistical validation.
contribution: LUMINA achieves consistently high AUROC and AUPRC scores on RAG hallucination benchmarks, outperforming prior methods by up to +13% AUROC on HalluRAG.

problem: Spiking neural networks promise energy efficiency with time-to-first-spike encoding but require costly evaluation of temporal decay functions and multiplications with synaptic weights.
approach: Otters repurposes natural signal decay in optoelectronic devices as the core computation of TTFS, treating the device's analog output as fused synaptic weight and temporal decay, combined with a quantized neural network-to-SNN conversion algorithm for transformers.
contribution: Otters achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on seven GLUE benchmark datasets with 1.77x improvement in energy efficiency over previous leading SNNs.

problem: Conventional video LLMs fail to respond at the precise moment when sufficient evidence first appears in a streaming video, lacking decision transparency and temporal alignment with visual evidence.
approach: Thinking-QwenVL decouples reasoning control from memory integration using an Active Thinking Decision Maker for transparent response timing and a Hierarchical Progressive Semantic Integration module for efficient memory management across streaming clips.
contribution: Thinking-QwenVL improves accuracy on StreamingBench from 67.63% to 71.60%, enabling precise response timing aligned with visual evidence.

problem: Cross-domain offline RL handles limited single-domain data but exhibits fragility under dynamics perturbations during deployment, particularly when target domain data is limited.
approach: DROCO introduces a robust cross-domain Bellman operator that enhances test-time robustness against dynamics perturbations while maintaining train-time robustness, augmented with dynamic value penalty and Huber loss.
contribution: DROCO outperforms strong baselines and exhibits enhanced robustness to dynamics perturbations across various dynamics shift scenarios.

problem: Black-box LLMs produce generic outputs overlook individual user preferences, with personalization methods limited to matching final outputs without modeling underlying reasoning.
approach: RPM constructs structured user behavior models from response-influential features to create personalized reasoning paths and retrieves beneficial examples via feature-based retrieval to guide inference.
contribution: RPM consistently outperforms existing response-level methods across four diverse tasks while enhancing both personalization performance and interpretability.

problem: Text-to-CAD generation is fragile because direct code generation without explicit assembly hierarchy or geometric constraints expands the search space, causing minor early errors to propagate.
approach: The method learns an intermediate hierarchical and geometry-aware graph representation that predicts assembly decomposition and constraints before sequencing operations, with structure-aware progressive curriculum learning.
contribution: The approach improves geometric fidelity and constraint satisfaction by narrowing the search space and enabling the model to handle more complex assemblies.

problem: Current MLLM-SAM integration fails to exploit SAM's ability for iterative mask refinement through interactive segmentation, mimicking human interaction.
approach: SAM-Veteran uses a multi-task reinforcement learning framework with Group Relative Policy Optimization to enable mask-aware SAM agents that generate bounding boxes, propose refinement points, and adaptively terminate.
contribution: SAM-Veteran achieves state-of-the-art performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain segmentation benchmarks with human-like SAM interaction.

problem: SFT-based cold start for MLLM-RL approaches adopts reasoning and output format paradigms that induce instruction-style overfitting and weaken out-of-distribution generalization.
approach: SPECS performs preference-based training instead of SFT for cold start via self-distilled preference data, focusing on shallow transferable surface-form criteria before handing off to RL with verifiable rewards.
contribution: SPECS yields consistent performance gains over strong baselines across multiple multimodal benchmarks through decoupled learning.

problem: Existing code retrieval benchmarks focus on Python and rarely stress-test robustness, particularly for C/C++ code where semantic understanding beyond lexical cues is critical.
approach: CLARC is a C/C++ benchmark built from real GitHub repositories with 1,245 query-code pairs for evaluation and 5,472 for training, incorporating LLM-generated validated queries and challenging settings like identifier anonymization and assembly compilation.
contribution: Evaluation of six state-of-the-art models reveals sharp drops in retrieval effectiveness under challenging conditions, highlighting reliance on lexical features.

problem: Uniform LLM-GNN fusion strategies provide only small overall performance gains because aggregate metrics obscure when LLMs benefit, inhibiting signals for selective strategies.
approach: GLANCE frames LLM-GNN fusion around nodes where GNNs falter, using a lightweight router trained with advantage-based objectives to decide per-node whether to query the LLM.
contribution: GLANCE achieves significant gains on heterophilous nodes (up to +5.8%) while maintaining top overall performance (up to +1.1%), with best performance balance across node subgroups.

problem: Reward models suffer from reward hacking by latching onto superficial attributes like response length, mistaking correlated cues for true causal drivers of quality.
approach: CROME uses an oracle LLM to identify causally relevant rubrics, then applies causal augmentations enforcing sensitivity along causal attributes and neutral augmentations enforcing invariance along spurious attributes.
contribution: CROME outperforms standard baselines on RewardBench by up to 5.3% average accuracy, achieving gains of up to 7.1% at specific evaluation conditions.

problem: Large language models fail to retain reasoning from previous tasks and apply it in future contexts, losing the ability to learn and adapt.
approach: LAG reuses prior computation and reasoning from past logs at test time by representing task logs as key-value caches that encode full reasoning context, retrieving relevant KV values to augment generation.
contribution: LAG significantly outperforms standard agentic systems and existing reflection-based memory approaches on knowledge- and reasoning-intensive datasets.

problem: Quadratic attention complexity poses a bottleneck for video diffusion models generating long-duration, high-resolution videos, and existing sparse attention methods don't optimally capture video's spatio-temporal characteristics.
approach: VMoBA introduces sparse attention specifically adapted for VDMs with layer-wise recurrent block partition (1D-2D-3D), global block selection, and threshold-based selection to dynamically attend salient blocks.
contribution: VMoBA achieves 2.92x FLOPs and 1.48x latency speedup during VDM training on longer sequences while attaining comparable or superior generation quality.

problem: Retrofitting LLMs with new behaviors requires full finetuning or distillation, costly steps that must be repeated for every architecture.
approach: Command-V copies residual representation adapters from donor models and pastes their effect into recipient models by deriving linear converters between layers and applying interventions in activation space without backpropagation.
contribution: Command-V matches finetuning performance on safety-refusal, jailbreak, and chain-of-thought tasks while using orders of magnitude less resources.

problem: Triangle-to-quad conversion pipelines generate quad meshes with poor topology, lacking an end-to-end generative approach for native quad-mesh production.
approach: QuadGPT formulates quad-mesh generation as sequence prediction using a unified tokenization for mixed topologies and reinforcement learning fine-tuning via topology-aware dPO.
contribution: QuadGPT significantly surpasses triangle-to-quad conversion pipelines in both geometric accuracy and topological quality.

problem: Current emotional intelligence benchmarks for MLLMs are limited, with unknown generalization abilities across distinct scenarios and reasoning capabilities to identify emotional state triggers.
approach: MME-Emotion provides a systematic benchmark with over 6,000 curated video clips and task-specific QA pairs spanning eight emotional tasks, evaluated through hybrid metrics and multi-agent framework.
contribution: Evaluation of 20 advanced MLLMs reveals unsatisfactory emotional intelligence with the best achieving only 39.3% recognition and 56.0% Chain-of-Thought scores.

problem: Abductive reasoning over knowledge graphs lacks controllability, yielding numerous plausible but redundant or irrelevant hypotheses, limiting practical utility.
approach: CtrlHGen introduces controllable hypothesis generation with dataset augmentation via sub-logical decomposition and smoothed semantic rewards including Dice/Overlap scores plus condition-adherence reward.
contribution: CtrlHGen better adheres to control conditions while achieving superior semantic similarity on three benchmark datasets.

problem: EEG foundation models adapted from CV/NLP overlook that neural activity exhibits diverse sparse coding across complex geometric topological cortex.
approach: Uni-NTFM designs a heterogeneous feature projection module encoding time and frequency domains, a topological embedding mechanism aligning sensor configs to unified functional topography, and a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer with 1.9B parameters.
contribution: Uni-NTFM outperforms existing EEG models across nine distinct benchmarks after pretraining on 28,000 hours of EEG data.

problem: Best-of-N selection for LLM generations is inherently zero-sum, discarding diverse and potentially useful information from the candidate pool.
approach: FusioN uses an LLM judge to synthesize informative elements from all N candidates into a single winning generation, tested in test-time scaling and synthetic data generation.
contribution: FusioN consistently outperforms Best-of-N across 11 languages, 3 diverse benchmarks, and varying model scales in both test-time scaling and downstream synthetic data generation.

problem: Membership inference attack vulnerabilities in Diffusion Language Models remain unexplored despite their multiple maskable configurations exponentially increasing attack opportunities.
approach: SAMA performs subset-aggregated membership attacks by sampling masked subsets at progressive densities and applying sign-based statistics with inverse-weighted aggregation prioritizing sparse masks' cleaner signals.
contribution: SAMA achieves 30% relative AUC improvement over baselines with up to 8x improvement at low false positive rates.

problem: Question answering with context struggles to balance reasoning quality against response efficiency, lacking principled difficulty assessment.
approach: MoL introduces adaptive mixture-of-length reasoning with information-theoretic difficulty assessment and dual-objective reward mechanism that modulates response length based on query complexity.
contribution: MoL exhibits intelligent brevity by producing shorter responses for simpler queries and longer ones for complex inputs, achieving competitive accuracy while substantially reducing tokens.

problem: RL agents face high sample complexity in sparse/delayed reward settings, while heavy LLM guidance introduces scalability issues and risks dependence on unreliable signals.
approach: MIRA incorporates a structured, evolving memory graph storing high-return trajectory segments and LLM subgoals, deriving utility signals that softly adjust advantage estimation without altering rewards.
contribution: MIRA outperforms RL baselines and reaches returns comparable to methods with frequent LLM supervision while requiring substantially fewer LLM queries.

problem: Offline multi-agent RL requires effective collaboration among heterogeneous agents under dataset constraints, but uniform conservatism over-constrains critical agents and under-constrains others.
approach: OMCDA dynamically adjusts conservatism per agent using a decomposed Q-function architecture to disentangle return computation from policy deviation assessment and scale constraint strength by agent importance.
contribution: OMCDA outperforms existing offline MARL methods on MuJoCo and SMAC, effectively balancing flexibility and conservatism while ensuring fair credit assignment.

problem: Conventional data-fidelity loss functions seek pointwise agreement with noisy measurements, leading to overfitting to noise in inverse problems.
approach: Distributional Consistency loss evaluates data-fidelity collectively by testing whether observed measurements are statistically consistent with noise distributions implied by the current estimate.
contribution: DC loss acts as a direct plug-in replacement for standard data consistency terms, avoiding overfitting to measurement noise without early stopping.

problem: SFT-then-RL two-stage pipeline suffers from inconsistency where SFT enforces rigid imitation that suppresses exploration, limiting RL's improvement potential.
approach: TRAPO interleaves SFT and RL within training by optimizing SFT loss on expert prefixes and RL loss on model completions, introducing Trust-Region SFT that minimizes forward KL inside trust region with adaptive prefix selection.
contribution: TRAPO consistently surpasses SFT, RL, and SFT-then-RL baselines plus recent state-of-the-art on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Transformers designed for CV/NLP struggle with medical time series because MedTS signals are inherently centralized while Transformer attention is decentralized, failing to capture global synchronization.
approach: CoTAR replaces decentralized attention with a centralized MLP-based module using a global core token as proxy to facilitate inter-token interaction, enforcing centralized aggregation-redistribution.
contribution: CoTAR achieves up to 12.13% improvement on APAVA dataset with merely 33% memory usage and 20% inference time compared to attention-based approaches.

problem: Computing Wasserstein distances for multiple pairs of distributions is expensive, requiring efficient approximation methods.
approach: The method regresses Wasserstein distance on sliced Wasserstein distances using both standard SW (lower bounds) and lifted SW (upper bounds) as predictors via linear models.
contribution: The approach provides better Wasserstein distance approximation than state-of-the-art Wasserstein Wormhole, particularly in low-data regimes, and can accelerate Wormhole training.

problem: 3DGS optimization suffers from overlooked details: update step coupling inducing optimizer state rescaling and gradient coupling in moments leading to under/over-effective regularization.
approach: The work decouples 3DGS optimization into Sparse Adam, Re-State Regularization, and Decoupled Attribute Regularization, re-coupling beneficial components into AdamW-GS.
contribution: AdamW-GS achieves better optimization efficiency and representation effectiveness simultaneously under 3DGS and 3DGS-MCMC frameworks.

problem: AI-generated image detectors exhibit Few-Patch Bias due to Lazy Learner effect, relying disproportionately on minority patches while neglecting distributed cues.
approach: Panoptic Patch Learning integrates randomized patch reconstruction injecting synthetic cues into random patches and patch-wise contrastive learning enforcing consistent discriminative capability across patches.
contribution: PPL enhances generalization and robustness of AIGI detection across datasets by ensuring uniform patch utilization.

problem: Existing multimodal models constrained by autoregressive architectures prevent balanced integration of understanding and generation capabilities with task-decoupled designs limiting cross-modal applications.
approach: NExT-OMNI achieves unified modeling through discrete flow paradigms using metric-induced probability paths and kinetic optimal velocities, enabling any-to-any understanding and generation natively.
contribution: NExT-OMNI delivers competitive performance on multimodal benchmarks while outperforming prior unified models in multi-turn interaction and cross-modal retrieval.

problem: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization requires tailored surrogate and acquisition choices per problem, is myopic, and adds refitting overhead.
approach: TAMO uses a transformer that operates across varying input/objective dimensions and is pretrained with RL to maximize cumulative hypervolume, enabling plug-and-play transfer without retraining.
contribution: TAMO reduces proposal time by 50-1000x versus alternatives while matching or improving Pareto quality under tight evaluation budgets.

problem: Zero-shot semantic segmentation struggles because CLIP vision encoder patch representations lack object-centric structure for coherent semantic region localization.
approach: OC-ZSS introduces self-supervision-guided object prompts attending to coarse regions via unsupervised clustering, refined through dual-stage Object Refinement Attention module with granular attention across receptive fields.
contribution: OC-ZSS achieves state-of-the-art performance on zero-shot segmentation benchmarks across inductive, transductive, and cross-domain settings.

problem: Existing methods for neural data alignment neglect temporal structure or capture it while conflating shared and private signals across multiple brain regions.
approach: CTAE employs Transformer encoders/decoders to capture non-stationary non-linear dynamics while explicitly partitioning latent space into orthogonal shared and private subspaces.
contribution: CTAE extracts meaningful representations that better decode behavior variables compared to existing approaches on high-density electrophysiology datasets.

problem: Test-time scaling with extended Chain-of-Thought reasoning incurs significant decoding overhead due to large language models generating redundant thinking with clear structured over/underthinking patterns.
approach: TrimR employs a lightweight pretrained verifier to detect and truncate redundant intermediate thoughts without LLM or verifier fine-tuning, engineered for high-throughput asynchronous deployment.
contribution: TrimR improves reasoning runtime by up to 70% on MATH500, AIME24/25, and GPQA benchmarks with negligible accuracy impact.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that generate harmful content, with existing detection methods limited to specific attack types or too time-consuming.
approach: JDJN detects JailNeurons (key neurons enabling jailbreak) at each model layer via neuron localization algorithm, aggregating them across layers to train a generalizable detector.
contribution: The approach achieves the highest detection success rate with exceptionally low false positive rates and strong generalizability across unseen benign datasets and attack types.

problem: Data augmentation parameter selection is typically left to trial-and-error or expensive validation-based optimization, lacking principled methods.
approach: The framework interprets augmentation parameters as model hyperparameters and optimizes the marginal likelihood via tractable ELBO, enabling joint optimization of augmentation and model parameters.
contribution: The approach improves calibration and yields robust performance over fixed or no augmentation across computer vision and NLP tasks with theoretical generalization guarantees.

problem: Existing preference datasets for reward model training are narrowly scoped, synthetically labeled, or lack rigorous quality control, limiting RM generalization.
approach: A large-scale preference dataset of 40 million pairs is created via human-AI synergistic pipeline where humans provide verified annotations and LLMs perform automatic curation, training Bradley-Terry models on 26 million curated pairs.
contribution: The reward models achieve state-of-the-art performance across seven reward model benchmarks, outperforming generative reward models and demonstrating versatility across alignment, correctness, safety, and robustness.

problem: Standard masked diffusion models use factorized predictions over masked positions, requiring many simulation steps because sampling too many positions at once degrades sample quality.
approach: Self-speculative masked diffusions generate non-factorized predictions by modifying transformer attention from non-causal to causal, enabling draft token generation and parallel validation via model-integrated speculative sampling.
contribution: The method achieves approximately 2x reduction in required network forward passes on GPT2-scale text modeling and protein sequence generation.

problem: Existing generative music models lack intuitive frequency-domain controls for manipulating musical patterns and structure at desired timescales.
approach: LatentFT combines diffusion autoencoder with latent-space Fourier transform to separate musical patterns by timescale, enabling coherent manipulation through latent-frequency masking during training.
contribution: LatentFT improves condition adherence and quality compared to baselines, paralleling equalizers in music production but operating on latent-space frequencies to shape structure.

problem: Symbolic regression suffers from exponential search space growth, with redundant exploration of syntactically different expressions that define the same function, slowing training.
approach: Introduces EGG-SR, which embeds symbolic equivalence into regression methods (MCTS, DRL, LLM) using equality graphs to compactly represent equivalent expressions, pruning redundancy and accelerating learning.
contribution: Demonstrates that EGG-SR consistently enhances symbolic regression across benchmarks, discovering more accurate expressions within the same time limit while tightening regret bounds for MCTS and reducing DRL gradient variance.

problem: LLMs used for tabular feature engineering act as black-box optimizers that lack calibrated utility estimates, leading to repeated exploration of low-yield operations without principled prioritization.
approach: Proposes a human-LLM collaborative framework that decouples proposal (LLM-generated candidates) from selection (guided by explicit utility modeling) and incorporates human preference feedback to identify more promising operations.
contribution: Improves feature engineering performance across tabular datasets and reduces user cognitive load, validated on both synthetic and real user studies.

problem: Multimodal editing large models fail to preserve facial identity consistency during portrait editing due to cross-source distribution bias and feature contamination, hindering practical deployment.
approach: Introduces EditedID, an alignment-disentanglement-entanglement framework using adaptive mixing for latent alignment, hybrid solvers for identity attribute disentanglement, and attentional gating for selective element entanglement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in preserving facial ID and edited element consistency as a training-free, plug-and-play solution for single/multi-person editing in open-world settings.

problem: Hierarchical federated learning topology selection remains open, as optimal configurations depend on complex interactions between data heterogeneity, network conditions, and client participation patterns.
approach: Establishes a unified convergence framework analyzing all four HFL topologies (Star-Star, Star-Ring, Ring-Star, Ring-Ring) under non-convex objectives with varying intra/inter-group data heterogeneity and full/partial client participation.
contribution: Reveals three fundamental topology selection principles: top-tier aggregation dominance, dependency on client grouping, and inter-group heterogeneity primacy, validated on CIFAR-10/CINIC-10/Fashion-MNIST/SST-2.

problem: LLM-based embeddings use encoder-only approaches that overlook generative strengths and miss latent concepts implicit in semantic representations.
approach: Introduces GIRCSE, which leverages autoregressive generation with iterative contrastive refinement to produce soft-token sequences optimized under contrastive objectives, capturing implicit semantics.
contribution: Outperforms strong LLM-based embedding baselines on MTEB benchmarks and exhibits emergent test-time scaling where generating more tokens steadily improves embedding quality.

problem: Frozen multimodal LLMs for video anomaly detection inherit pre-training biases and cannot adapt internal representations to specific contexts, limiting ability to handle subtle anomalies.
approach: Proposes SteerVAD, which identifies latent anomaly experts via gradient-free representational separability analysis and uses a hierarchical meta-controller to generate dynamic rectification signals that amplify anomaly-relevant dimensions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among tuning-free approaches while requiring only 1% of training data, establishing active representation steering as a new direction for VAD.

problem: Multimodal ecological learning from heterogeneous data sources (satellite, time series, tabular, bioacoustics) suffers from incomplete data and modality imbalance, where dominant modalities hinder optimization of others.
approach: Introduces MIAM, a dynamic masking strategy that explores full input combinations, prioritizes informative/challenging subsets, and adaptively increases masking of dominant modalities based on relative performance and learning dynamics.
contribution: Significantly improves robustness and predictive performance on GeoPlant and TaxaBench while enabling fine-grained contribution analysis revealing which variables and regions most strongly drive performance.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards fails in long-context scenarios because sparse outcome-only rewards provide insufficient gradient signal for the model to learn contextual grounding from external information.
approach: Proposes LongRLVR, augmenting sparse answer rewards with dense, verifiable context rewards that directly incentivize correct information selection, providing robust learning gradients for long-context reasoning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard RLVR across models (Qwen, LLaMA), boosting 14B model RULER-QA scores from 73.17 to 88.90 and LongBench v2 from 39.8 to 46.5.

problem: Quantum machine learning advantages have been proven for evaluation hardness but remain poorly understood for the learning process itself, especially for quantum functions without random-generation capability.
approach: Proves identification learning advantages for quantum functions under complexity-theoretic assumptions by developing a new proof strategy showing exponential advantage for broad quantum identification tasks.
contribution: Establishes first proofs of quantum identification learning advantages and conjecturally shows quantum functions are not random-generatable under plausible complexity assumptions.

problem: Masked diffusion models for language generation rely on ad hoc rule-based unmasking schedules (max-confidence, max-margin) that do not effectively adapt to data distributions or task requirements.
approach: Replaces heuristic schedules with a learned scheduler formulated as a KL-regularized MDP with explicit reference policy, optimizing a regularized objective with policy-improvement and convergence guarantees.
contribution: Proves learned policy generates samples closer to data distribution than heuristics, achieving 22% gain over random and 12% gain over max-confidence on SUDOKU with critical unmasking order.

problem: Training LLM agents via reinforcement learning faces sparse, unverifiable rewards and high-variance credit assignment when using explicit step labels or additional rollouts.
approach: Introduces iStar, which optimizes an implicit process reward model alongside policy using multi-turn DPO objective to generate implicit step rewards for each action, combining step-level with trajectory-level advantages.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on WebShop, VisualSokoban, and SOTOPIA benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance over frontier LLMs with higher sample efficiency.

problem: Learning dynamic causal structures is challenging because both instantaneous and lagged causal dependencies change over time, violating stationarity assumptions and destabilizing discovery methods.
approach: Introduces DyCausal, leveraging convolutional networks to model causal structures within coarse-grained time windows and linear interpolation to refine to each time step, with matrix-norm-based acyclic constraints.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on synthetic and real-world datasets, effectively identifying fully dynamic causal structures from coarse to fine temporal scales.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models inherit cultural biases from training data and fail to faithfully depict underrepresented regions, with existing benchmarks focusing on object-centric categories rather than cultural activities.
approach: Introduces CULTIVate, a benchmark of 576 cross-cultural activity prompts spanning 16 countries with descriptor-based evaluation across cultural dimensions (background, attire, objects, interactions).
contribution: Proposes four metrics measuring cultural alignment, hallucination, exaggerated elements, and diversity, revealing systematic disparities favoring global north and enabling cultural faithfulness measurement.

problem: Ensuring factuality of LLM outputs is essential for safety in high-stakes domains, but existing conformal inference approaches are either overly conservative or rely on simple models that fail to capture complex group structures.
approach: Reformulates conformal inference in multiplicative filtering, modeling factuality as product of claim-level scores, and uses ensemble methods with group-conditional calibration for more accurate factuality scoring.
contribution: MACI consistently achieves user-specified coverage with substantially higher retention and lower time cost than baselines, providing distribution-free factuality guarantees.

problem: Euclidean space embeddings of hierarchical code structures cause significant distortion, especially for deep or highly branched ASTs, limiting models' ability to capture deep program semantics.
approach: Proposes HypeCodeNet, a geometric deep learning framework operating natively in hyperbolic space with manifold-aware components including hyperbolic embedding, tangent-space message-passing, and geodesic-based attention.
contribution: Significantly outperforms Euclidean models (GraphCodeBERT) on code clone detection, completion, and link prediction, especially on tasks requiring deep structural understanding.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with aesthetic assessment due to scarcity of aesthetic reasoning data and inherent subjectivity, making it difficult to generate accurate judgments with interpretable rationales.
approach: Proposes Aes-R1, integrating AesCoT pipeline for high-quality chain-of-thought aesthetic reasoning data with Relative-Absolute Policy Optimization (RAPO) jointly optimizing absolute score regression and relative ranking.
contribution: Improves backbone PLCC/SRCC metrics by 47.9%/34.8%, surpassing similar-scale baselines and enabling grounded aesthetic scoring and reasoning in unified framework.

problem: Signal integrity analysis in IC design requires expensive SPICE simulation to evaluate crosstalk-induced delay and transient glitches, becoming prohibitive for large-scale designs.
approach: Proposes Si-GT, a graph transformer with virtual NET tokens, mesh pattern encoding, and intra-inter net attention to efficiently model signal propagation and coupling in interconnects.
contribution: Outperforms GNN and transformer baselines on 200k delay and 187k glitch examples with substantially reduced computation compared to SPICE, enabling scalable IC verification.

problem: The expressive power of linear attention layers for in-context learning of linear dynamical systems in non-i.i.d. settings remains poorly understood.
approach: Provides optimal weight construction for single linear-attention layer and proves equivalence to one gradient descent step with autoregression objective; uncovers relation to Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient for larger window sizes.
contribution: Adds to understanding of transformer expressivity as in-context learners and offers plausible hypotheses for observations where they compete with Kalman filters in LDS settings.

problem: Existing neural rendering methods achieve high fidelity but suffer from low rendering speeds or only support pinhole camera models, lacking support for complex lenses and LiDAR data needed for autonomous driving simulation.
approach: Proposes SimULi, extending 3DGS with LiDAR support via automated tiling for arbitrary spinning LiDARs, ray-based culling, and factorized Gaussian representation for cross-sensor consistency.
contribution: Renders 10-20x faster than ray tracing and 1.5-14x faster than prior rasterization while matching or exceeding fidelity, handling wide camera model range on autonomous driving datasets.

problem: AI-based film generation systems generate videos but struggle with expressive camera language and cinematic rhythm, producing templated visuals and unengaging narratives.
approach: Introduces FilMaster, integrating real-world cinematic principles through scene-level retrieval-augmented generation for coherent camera planning and audience-aware post-production rhythm control.
contribution: Generates professional-grade, editable films by learning cinematography from 440,000 real film clips and emulating professional post-production workflows for coherent visual storytelling.

problem: Graph neural networks struggle with heterophilic graphs where connected nodes have dissimilar features, with existing approaches focusing on architecture without addressing root causes and performing worse than MLPs.
approach: Proposes GRAPHITE, directly transforming the graph by creating feature nodes to facilitate homophilic message passing between nodes sharing similar features, based on exact homophily definition.
contribution: First method explicitly transforming graphs to improve homophily, significantly outperforming 23 latest GNNs on heterophilic datasets where even MLPs surpass traditional graph methods.

problem: Adapting multiple pretrained medical foundation models to joint diagnosis across heterogeneous domains (radiology and pathology) remains an open challenge for multi-modal clinical workflows.
approach: Proposes CTF, using clinically grounded concepts as shared semantic interface for cross-modal co-adaptation before fusion, with Global-Context-Shared Prompt mechanism capturing domain-specific priors and cross-domain context.
contribution: Outperforms unimodal and fusion baselines (AUC 0.903 on TCGA-GBMLGG) while requiring only 0.15% additional parameters, enabling parameter-efficient multi-modal medical analysis.

problem: Diffusion models lack ability to interpret and follow numeric instructions for continuous semantic attribute control, as text encoders are designed for discrete tokens and existing methods overlook compositional nature of aesthetics.
approach: Introduces AttriCtrl, decomposing aesthetic attributes and quantifying via hybrid strategy mapping dimensions to [0,1] scale, then transforming user values to embeddings via plug-and-play value encoder.
contribution: Achieves accurate and continuous control over single and multiple aesthetic attributes in diffusion-based generation with generalizable framework.

problem: SE(p)-invariant alignment methods face high computational costs or lack metric guarantees when comparing distributions on measured Banach spaces.
approach: Introduces SEINT, using polar transport discrepancy with distance convolution to extract SE(p)-invariant representations for optimal-transport-based distribution alignment with O(n log n) to O(n²) complexity.
contribution: Proves SEINT is well-defined metric with SE(p)-invariance, outperforms existing methods in classification and cross-space tasks, and enhances molecular generation as regularizer.

problem: Mean flow enables 1-NFE generation but results are often not compelling enough for practical applications requiring higher quality outputs.
approach: Proposes RMFlow, integrating coarse 1-NFE MeanFlow transport with tailored noise-injection refinement, training via new loss balancing Wasserstein distance and sample likelihood.
contribution: Achieves near state-of-the-art results on text-to-image, context-to-molecule, and time-series generation using only 1-NFE at computational cost comparable to baseline MeanFlow.

problem: Video reasoning with reinforcement learning relies on coarse sequence-level rewards and single-factor token selection, neglecting fine-grained links among visual inputs, temporal dynamics, and outputs.
approach: Proposes Video-KTR, performing selective token-level RL using three attribution signals: visual-aware tokens via counterfactual masking, temporal-aware via frame shuffling, and high-entropy tokens for uncertainty.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Video-Holmes (42.7%, surpassing GPT-4o) with consistent gains on reasoning and general tasks, improving accuracy and interpretability via modality-sensitive token-level updates.

problem: LLMs perform well on single-language code generation but their ability to generate cross-programming-language interoperating code remains underexplored and poorly benchmarked.
approach: Introduces CrossPL, a benchmark covering 2534 cross-programming-language tasks across IPC (six languages) and Python-C FFI modes, with LLM-based workflows for benchmark construction and evaluation.
contribution: Evaluates 20 state-of-the-art LLMs, revealing clear limitations with best model achieving only 19.5% Pass@1 on FFI subset, underscoring urgent need to improve cross-language code generation.

problem: Guidance of generative flow models typically requires modifying probability flow vector field, which restricts flexibility and may introduce errors through field approximation.
approach: Proposes SGFM, modifying source distribution directly while keeping pre-trained vector field intact, reducing guidance to sampling from source distribution with flexibility in sampling method choice.
contribution: Theoretically recovers desired target distribution exactly with Wasserstein error bounds for approximate sampling/field, demonstrates effectiveness on 2D benchmarks, physics tasks, and imaging inverse problems.

problem: Large foundation models have substantial memory requirements, but linear low-rank approximation suffers significant information loss from rank truncation and struggles with adaptive compression across heterogeneous layers.
approach: Proposes NLA, using piecewise-linear kernels with forward-pass optimization to approximate weights and cubic sparsity scheduling to adaptively allocate compression across layers with different sensitivities.
contribution: Demonstrates superior compression performance on LLMs and vision models across datasets while achieving higher compression ratios than existing methods.

problem: Neural network layer widths are typically selected manually or via expensive hyperparameter search, which is infeasible for foundation models with billions of parameters.
approach: Introduces technique to learn unbounded width during training via standard backpropagation, jointly optimizing layer width and parameters across diverse data domains.
contribution: Shows width adapts to task difficulty with easy truncation at zero cost, enabling smooth performance-compute trade-off or dynamic compression without performance degradation.

problem: Existing learning-based data augmentation methods rely on learning latent representations with generative models, lacking intuitive construction and fine-grained controllability.
approach: Proposes data augmentation based on energy-based modeling and information geometry principles, enabling geometrically aware latent space construction with efficient encoding/decoding.
contribution: Achieves competitive downstream performance while offering fine-grained controllability lacking in existing augmentation literature.

problem: Vision-language models are evaluated on comparative reasoning with large, salient differences, but ability to distinguish subtle variations across diverse domains (industrial, medical, aerial) remains unexplored.
approach: Introduces VLM-SubtleBench, evaluating subtle comparative reasoning across ten difference types and diverse domains, with controlled analyses revealing performance degradation patterns.
contribution: Reveals systematic gaps between VLM and human performance on subtle differences, establishing foundation for advancing toward human-level comparative reasoning.

problem: Reinforcement fine-tuning suffers from reward over-optimization where models hack reward signals to achieve high scores without producing quality outputs, particularly in high-reward region.
approach: Proposes rubric-based rewards that leverage off-policy exemplars while remaining insensitive to their artifacts, with workflow to distinguish great and diverse responses capturing high-reward tail.
contribution: Demonstrates rubric-based rewards substantially mitigate reward over-optimization and deliver effective LLM post-training improvements.

problem: Extending unified multimodal understanding and generation to 3D scenes from multiview images, with unclear principles for how generation facilitates understanding.
approach: Presents Omni-View, jointly modeling scene understanding, novel view synthesis, and geometry estimation via understanding model, texture module for appearance, and geometry module for explicit constraints.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art score of 55.4 on VSI-Bench while simultaneously delivering strong performance in novel view synthesis and 3D scene generation.

problem: Existing inference-time scaling for LLMs relies on inefficient discrete search or trial-and-error prompting, missing opportunity for continuous gradient-based optimization.
approach: Proposes ∇-Reasoner, integrating differentiable optimization over token logits during decoding via Differentiable Textual Optimization (DTO), leveraging gradients from LLM likelihood and reward model.
contribution: Achieves over 20% accuracy improvement on mathematical reasoning benchmarks while reducing model calls by 10-40%, shifting from zeroth-order to first-order optimization at test time.

problem: Training diffusion models typically requires clean ground-truth images unavailable in many applications, limiting practical applicability to real-world noisy settings.
approach: Introduces MSM, learning partial measurement scores directly from noisy and subsampled measurements, aggregating scores to synthesize fully sampled measurements without clean images.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on unconditional generation and inverse problems using only degraded measurements, with stochastic sampling variant efficiently approximating exact formulation.

problem: Vision-and-language navigation agents suffer from catastrophic forgetting across environments, limiting practical use in continual learning scenarios where agents must adapt to new domains.
approach: Proposes M³E, mixture of macro and micro experts with dual-router architecture separating scene-level reasoning from local perceptual alignment, using dynamic momentum updates to preserve knowledge.
contribution: Consistently outperforms fine-tuning and continual learning baselines on R2R and REVERIE domain-incremental settings, offering parameter-efficient solution for adapting to new environments.

problem: Existing world models require extensive domain-specific training and produce low-fidelity predictions, while video diffusion models on internet data lack action controllability for sequential decision-making.
approach: Presents Vid2World, leveraging pre-trained video diffusion models through video diffusion causalization (reshaping for autoregressive generation) and causal action guidance for interactive world modeling.
contribution: Demonstrates scalable pathway for repurposing video diffusion models into interactive world models across robot manipulation, 3D games, and open-world navigation.

problem: Autoregressive unified models suffer from slow inference due to sequential decoding, while non-autoregressive models suffer from weak generalization due to limited pretrained backbones.
approach: Introduces Muddit, unified discrete diffusion transformer enabling fast parallel generation across text and image via token-level discrete denoising, strong visual priors, and lightweight text decoder.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance to significantly larger AR models in both quality and speed, highlighting pure discrete diffusion's potential as scalable multimodal backbone.

problem: Confidence scores from segmentation models are heuristic and lack rigorous uncertainty estimates, and applying conformal prediction directly ignores crucial spatial correlations between pixels.
approach: Proposes CONSIGN, incorporating spatial correlations into conformal prediction via decomposition to generate meaningful prediction sets with user-specified error guarantees.
contribution: Generates prediction sets with high-probability error guarantees across medical and COCO datasets, significantly improving performance and uncertainty quality versus CP baselines.

problem: Transfer learning in Neyman-Pearson classification must control both Type-I and Type-II errors simultaneously, which is difficult when distribution shifts occur in both the null and alternative distributions.
approach: Derive an adaptive procedure that uses source data to improve both error types while automatically detecting and avoiding negative transfer when the source is uninformative.
contribution: Provides statistical and computational guarantees for improved Type-I and Type-II errors under simultaneous distribution shifts in both distributions.

problem: Long-tailed semi-supervised learning suffers from confirmation bias where skewed pseudo-labeling progressively marginalizes tail classes, exacerbated by distribution mismatch between labeled and unlabeled data.
approach: Co-design class-wise and overall logit adjustment components using effective rank estimation for class sample sizes and meta-learning to optimize overall adjustment strength.
contribution: Co-Calibrated Logit Adjustment (CoLA) framework addresses limitations of prior Logit Adjustment methods by treating overall adjustment as a learnable parameter optimized via meta-learning.

problem: Uncertainty quantification via ensembles like Deep Ensembles achieves strong performance but has prohibitively high computational and memory costs for large models.
approach: Prune attention heads to create diverse ensemble members and merge them via new multi-head attention with grouped fully-connected layers, achieving efficiency close to a single network.
contribution: Hydra Ensembles matches or surpasses Deep Ensembles in uncertainty quantification performance with inference speed near a single network, including state-of-the-art results on ImageNet-1k zero-shot classification.

problem: It is unclear whether LLMs contain a small subset of critical neurons essential for core language abilities, as found in the human brain.
approach: Propose Perturbation-based Causal Identification of Critical Neurons method to systematically locate such critical neurons and analyze their distribution and effects across model layers.
contribution: Reveals that LLMs contain ultra-sparse critical neuron sets concentrated in outer layers (particularly MLP down_proj), whose disruption can collapse a 72B-parameter model with perplexity increasing by up to 20 orders of magnitude.

problem: Omni-modal large language models excel at perception but lack the complex reasoning abilities of recent large reasoning models, and enhancing them requires costly training.
approach: Introduce ThinkOmni, a training-free framework using off-the-shelf reasoning models to guide omni-modal model decoding and adaptively balance perception and reasoning signals without hyperparameter tuning.
contribution: Achieves 70.2 on MathVista and 75.5 on MMAU, demonstrating consistent performance improvements on six multi-modal reasoning benchmarks without additional training data or retraining.

problem: Iterative heuristics for vehicle routing waste computation by repeatedly searching stable solution segments that rarely change across iterations, particularly in large-scale problems with long subtours.
approach: Introduce Learning-to-Segment (L2Seg), a neural framework that identifies stable and unstable solution portions to enable First-Segment-Then-Aggregate decomposition, preserving stable segments as fixed hypernodes.
contribution: L2Seg accelerates state-of-the-art iterative solvers by 2x to 7x on CVRP and VRPTW, with a synergistic variant combining global and local approaches for best performance.

problem: Bayesian experimental design approaches cannot scale to high-dimensional design spaces because they require a likelihood model that remains accurate throughout the space, which fails in practice.
approach: Introduce DiffBED, which uses a generative prior via diffusion model guided by information-theoretic design objectives to ensure realistic and informative designs.
contribution: Successfully scales Bayesian experimental design to high-dimensional problems like high-resolution image design, whereas prior BED applications were restricted to only handful-dimensional design spaces.

problem: LLMs require balancing two competing objectives: injecting stochasticity to explore multiple reasoning chains while ensuring accuracy in each path, but existing methods conflate different sources of uncertainty.
approach: Calibrate decoding by correctness rather than confidence alone: sample from tokens with higher estimated correctness and reduce sampling where expected correctness is low via Greedy-Threshold and Calibrated-TopK/Epsilon.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains across math and general reasoning benchmarks by showing low-confidence steps should be greedy and correctness-ranked truncation improves over confidence-based methods.

problem: Hierarchical-causal frameworks for understanding neural representation fail to explain misrepresentation and how systems can abstract details while maintaining fine-grained information for downstream functions.
approach: Propose readout representation that defines representation by recoverable information rather than causal origin, introducing representation size metric linked to robustness and redundancy.
contribution: Shows inputs can be accurately reconstructed from heavily perturbed mid-level features, challenging causal mapping perspectives and offering new lens for analyzing biological and artificial neural systems.

problem: Finding globally optimal solutions for empirical risk minimization of two-layer neural networks was unsolved, limiting exact optimization to small problems.
approach: Introduce Deep-ICE algorithm achieving global optimality for two-layer maxout and ReLU networks with worst-case time complexity O(N^{DK+1}), with heuristic extension for larger datasets.
contribution: First globally optimal algorithm for two-layer network training with provably exact solutions on small-scale datasets and significantly improved performance on larger datasets compared to gradient descent and SVMs.

problem: Multimodal large language models' fine-grained action understanding ability has not been fully examined, and their performance on complex action recognition is unclear.
approach: Reformulate EPIC-KITCHENS-100 into MLLM benchmark with hard negatives, then finetune models with supervised dataset including hard action recognition, temporal detection, and captioning.
contribution: LLaVAction achieves 21-point accuracy improvement over GPT-4o on the new EPIC-KITCHENS-100-MQA benchmark and strong improvements on action recognition benchmarks.

problem: Reinforcement learning for tuning LLMs achieves good performance but causes significant loss in output diversity by implicitly optimizing reverse KL divergence.
approach: Start from explicit target distribution obtained by filtering incorrect answers while preserving correct ones, then approximate using Amari's alpha-divergence family to control precision-diversity trade-off.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Lean theorem-proving along the coverage-precision Pareto frontier, with superior coverage compared to other methods.

problem: Shampoo and SOAP optimizer variants require memory overhead from Adam integration and rely on Adam for good performance, limiting their effectiveness.
approach: Reinterpret Shampoo and SOAP estimation procedures as covariance estimation via Kullback-Leibler divergence minimization, then propose KL-Shampoo and KL-SOAP with practical estimation schemes.
contribution: KL-Shampoo and KL-SOAP match or exceed Shampoo/SOAP performance while maintaining SOAP-level runtime, with KL-Shampoo avoiding Adam overhead while consistently outperforming other methods.

problem: Representation-learning methods from vision and NLP have not been widely adopted in modern time series forecasters despite showing promise, with a frequency mismatch between historical inputs and future targets.
approach: Introduce TimaAlign, a lightweight plug-and-play framework that aligns auxiliary features via reconstruction task, feeding corrected features into any base forecaster.
contribution: Extensive experiments across eight benchmarks show TimaAlign provides superior performance by correcting frequency mismatches, with theoretical justifications for how reconstruction improves generalization.

problem: LLMs solve drill-style math exercises but fail when problems require genuine concept understanding, as outcome-based RL reinforces pattern reuse rather than concept selection.
approach: Introduce CORE, which synthesizes concept-aligned quizzes, injects concept snippets into rollouts, and reinforces trajectories that correctly apply injected concepts with divergence penalty.
contribution: Yields consistent gains on 7B-class model across in-domain and diverse out-of-domain math benchmarks (GSM8K, SVAMP, MAWPS, SAT-Math, OlympiadBench, Gaokao, etc.) with largest improvements on concept-heavy categories.

problem: Today's AI systems have fixed, human-designed architectures and cannot autonomously improve themselves continuously, unlike the cumulative scientific method.
approach: Introduce Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM), which iteratively modifies its own code and empirically validates changes using coding benchmarks, sampling agents from an archive and self-modifying to create diverse versions.
contribution: Demonstrates open-ended evolution of self-improving agents that grows an archive of diverse, high-quality agents through Darwinian evolution and validation.

problem: Squared L2 distance in continuous-time graph representation violates triangle inequality, causing distortion in node positions and poor performance on social and collaboration networks.
approach: Propose L1 latent distance based continuous-time graph representation (L1LD-CTGR) using L1 norm as true latent metric with closed-form piecewise exponential hazard integral for efficient computation.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on synthetic and real-world data with true latent metric space, solved gradient intractability via descent direction enabling mainstream learning architectures.

problem: Understanding how neural populations in higher visual areas encode object-centered visual information and whether feature-specific information is organized into structured, semantically meaningful subspaces remains unclear.
approach: Introduce MIG-Vis, which uses VAE for group-wise disentangled neural latent subspace inference, then applies mutual information-guided diffusion to visualize visual-semantic features encoded by each latent group.
contribution: Identifies neural latent groups with clear semantic selectivity to diverse visual features including object pose, inter-category transformations, and other attributes in IT cortex.

problem: Evaluation of LLMs on advanced research-level problems in hard sciences like condensed matter theory is scarce, limiting understanding of their reasoning capabilities.
approach: Create CMT-Benchmark with 50 original research-level problems in condensed matter theory covering analytical and computational approaches, designed and verified by expert researchers.
contribution: Shows frontier models like OpenAI-o3 struggle with complex tasks, establishing a comprehensive benchmark while providing insights that performance declines significantly with task complexity.

problem: Clinical ML models trained at one hospital often degrade under distribution shifts at other hospitals, and portable patient representations that transfer across sites are needed.
approach: Map irregular ICU time series to concise natural language summaries using frozen LLM, then embed summaries with frozen text embedding model to obtain fixed-length portable vectors.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance in-distribution while exhibiting smaller relative performance drops when transferring to new hospitals across MIMIC-IV, HIRID, and PPICU datasets.

problem: Due to confounders, treated and control groups have imbalanced distributions, and outcome prediction models trained on one group generalize poorly to the other group.
approach: Adjust the outcome prediction model rather than confounders via Wasserstein geodesic to smoothly connect control and treated groups, gradually adjusting the model between consecutive groups.
contribution: Avoids over-balancing issues and demonstrates effectiveness across benchmark datasets in terms of multiple evaluation metrics with theoretical analysis.

problem: Weight regularization techniques like EWC remain underexplored in parameter-efficient continual learning paradigms with pre-trained models and task-specific low-rank modules.
approach: Revisit weight regularization by regularizing shared low-rank updates through EWC, keeping storage constant regardless of task count, and propose EWC-LoRA for efficient practical deployment.
contribution: Achieves better stability-plasticity trade-off than other low-rank methods across various benchmarks while maintaining constant memory requirement independent of task count.

problem: LLM-generated verbalized confidence scores are miscalibrated, reporting high confidence on low-accuracy instances, harming trust and safety in deployment.
approach: Introduce Distractor-Normalized Coherence (DINCO), which has models verbalize confidence across self-generated distractors and normalizes by total confidence, augmented with generator-validator disagreement.
contribution: Provides less saturated, more usable confidence estimates that better calibrate LLM outputs by leveraging coherence across validations on incompatible claims.

problem: Pre-training world models on action-free video data typically train models to predict single deterministic futures, which is ill-posed for stochastic environments with unknown actions.
approach: Introduce HAUWM (Horizon-Calibrated Uncertainty World Model) using probabilistic ensemble predicting frames at random future horizons with HCU loss to shape predictive variance growth over time.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on MetaWorld, DeepMind Control Suite, and RoboDesk by learning reliable temporal confidence in latent dynamics.

problem: DINOv2 foundation model shows strong performance on downstream tasks but its internal representational structure and concept organization remain unclear.
approach: Conduct comprehensive analysis using overcomplete dictionary learning to extract 32,000+ visual concepts, analyzing how downstream tasks recruit concepts and examining concept geometry and statistics.
contribution: Reveals functional specialization in task recruitment (classification uses learned negations, segmentation uses boundary detectors, depth uses monocular cues), antipodal concept pairs, and distributed encoding.

problem: Learning effective cutting plane selection for branch-and-cut algorithms requires unclear sample complexity, with two scoring functions (tree size and gap closed) having unknown relative difficulty.
approach: Present new sample complexity lower bounds for both scoring functions showing they require similar samples as learning any generic target function, and provide empirical evidence that gap closed is effective proxy.
contribution: Establishes first lower bounds for learning-to-cut framework, showing bounds are nearly tight for neural networks and suggesting gap closed and tree size are of comparable learning difficulty.

problem: Current evaluations of geometric reasoning in vision-language models face limitations including test contamination, emphasis on final answers over processes, and insufficient diagnostic granularity.
approach: Present GeoBench, a hierarchical benchmark with four reasoning levels (Visual Perception, Goal-Oriented Planning, Rigorous Theorem Application, Self-Reflective Backtracking) with formally verified tasks.
contribution: Reveals reasoning models like OpenAI-o3 outperform general MLLMs but performance declines with complexity; shows sub-goal decomposition and premise filtering critically influence accuracy.

problem: The reversal curse (inability to infer 'B is A' from learned 'A is B') is considered fundamental, and model editing causes logical inconsistencies across dependent facts.
approach: Train LMs from scratch on synthetic knowledge graphs showing bilinear relational structure emerges in hidden representations, enabling reversal inference and consistent model editing.
contribution: Demonstrates bilinear structure enables alleviating the reversal curse and causes edits to correctly propagate to reverse facts and logically dependent facts without inconsistencies.

problem: Representational similarity metrics that force all units to be matched are susceptible to noise and outliers, leading to unreliable neural correspondence estimates.
approach: Extend soft-matching distance to partial optimal transport setting allowing some neurons to remain unmatched, yielding rotation-sensitive robust correspondences via unbalanced soft-matching distance.
contribution: Provides theoretical advantages and practical benefits: preserves correct matches under outliers, achieves higher alignment precision on fMRI data, enables quality-based analyses of network partitions.

problem: PAC-Bayes generalization bounds typically produce vacuous results and are not tight, limiting their practical utility for understanding model generalization.
approach: Present family of block-sample MAC-Bayes bounds where divergence terms depend only on training data subsets, with expectation rather than high-probability bounds.
contribution: Proposed MAC-Bayes bounds show promise of significantly improving PAC-Bayes tightness, with numerical examples showing finite bounds when original PAC-Bayes is vacuous.

problem: LLMs trained on text alone surprisingly develop visual priors enabling unlocking of latent visual capabilities and symbolic visual generation, but their composition and origin remain unclear.
approach: Systematically analyze visual priors revealing separable perception and reasoning components with unique scaling trends; show reasoning scales from reasoning-centric data and perception emerges diffusely.
contribution: Grounded in 100+ controlled experiments consuming 500,000 GPU-hours, revealing that visual reasoning is transferable, perception is vision-encoder sensitive, and proposes data-centric recipe for vision-aware LLMs.

problem: Forward-Forward algorithm remains largely confined to supervised settings, with limited application to reinforcement learning where learning signals arise more naturally.
approach: Introduce Action-conditioned Root mean squared Q-Functions (ARQ), applying goodness function and action conditioning for local RL using temporal difference learning.
contribution: Achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art local backprop-free RL methods on MinAtar and DeepMind Control Suite while outperforming backpropagation-trained algorithms on most tasks.

problem: Structured State Space Duality (SSD) in Mamba-2 substantially increases memory and latency overhead, requiring efficient compression strategies tailored to SSD architecture.
approach: Present SSDi8, the first post-training quantization framework for SSD maintaining INT8 path with reformulation decoupling multiplications, adaptive channel-varying quantization, and error correction.
contribution: Achieves accuracy comparable to FP16 with up to 1.4X speedup in W4A8 and W8A8 settings, with robustness validated on resource-constrained Orin Nano device.
