problem: Imitation learning methods require large amounts of high-quality demonstrations including expert actions, which are often unavailable.
approach: LWAIL uses Wasserstein distance computed in a dynamics-aware latent space trained via Intention Conditioned Value Function (ICVF) pretraining to enable state-only distribution matching with minimal expert episodes.
contribution: Achieves expert-level performance using only one or a few state-only expert episodes, outperforming prior Wasserstein-based and adversarial IL methods on MuJoCo environments.

problem: AI agents deployed in real-world settings pose significant safety risks, but existing benchmarks rely on simulated environments and narrow task domains that inadequately assess real-world safety.
approach: OpenAgentSafety evaluates agents interacting with real tools (web browsers, code executors, file systems, bash, messaging) across 350+ multi-turn tasks spanning benign and adversarial intents, combining rule-based and LLM-as-judge assessments.
contribution: Reveals that 51.2%-72.7% of safety-vulnerable tasks produce unsafe behavior across five prominent LLMs, highlighting critical risks before deployment.

problem: LLMs trained on single reasoning modalities (typically natural language) miss synergies between complementary representational formats for logical reasoning.
approach: Mixture-of-Thought (MoT) enables LLMs to jointly learn from self-generated rationales across natural language, code, and a new symbolic modality (truth-table) that enumerates logical cases.
contribution: Achieves up to 11.7pp average accuracy gain on FOLIO and ProofWriter benchmarks compared to single-modality chain-of-thought approaches.

problem: Federated learning with heterogeneous model architectures cannot use standard parameter aggregation methods, and data heterogeneity limits generalization on unseen data.
approach: Clients share feature distribution statistics (mean/covariance) with the server, then train variational transposed CNNs using Gaussian latent samples to generate synthetic data for fine-tuning.
contribution: Improves generalization accuracy compared to model-heterogeneous FL frameworks while reducing communication costs and memory consumption.

problem: Video reasoning in LVLMs lacks challenging multi-hop questions and high-quality video-grounded Chain-of-Thought data needed to bootstrap reasoning enhancement via reinforcement learning.
approach: ReWatch-R1 uses a multi-agent ReAct framework to synthesize video-grounded CoT by simulating re-watching and information retrieval, then post-trains with SFT and RLVR using an Observation & Reasoning reward mechanism.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on five challenging video reasoning benchmarks with improved reasoning grounding and reduced hallucination.

problem: 3D scene generation from single images fails to organize part-level objects into distinct instances because internal assignment mechanisms lack structural constraints.
approach: SceneTransporter formulates structured 3D scene generation as a global correlation assignment problem solved via entropic Optimal Transport within the compositional DiT denoising loop, enforcing one-to-one routing and coherent grouping.
contribution: Significantly improves instance-level coherence and geometric fidelity in open-world scene generation compared to existing methods.

problem: Current video benchmarks for multimodal models focus on simple perception tasks that only require matching question-mentioned frames, not multi-frame reasoning or analysis of hidden information.
approach: MMR-V defines long-range multi-frame reasoning tasks requiring inference across far-distant evidence frames and hidden information beyond direct perception, with manually annotated questions and distractor strategies.
contribution: Reveals that even the best-performing model (Gemini-2.5-pro) achieves only 64.3% accuracy and that current reasoning enhancement strategies bring limited gains, indicating a gap in multimodal reasoning capabilities.

problem: First-frame-guided video editing provides limited fine-grained control over the temporal evolution of edits across the entire video.
approach: Uses mask-based LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained Image-to-Video models with spatiotemporal masks to teach preservation of source content or generation of novel content, with optional temporal consistency or reference-guided synthesis.
contribution: Enables users to control the entire temporal evolution of complex edits like object rotation or flower blooming, outperforming baseline methods in video editing performance.

problem: Joint human-scene reconstruction from monocular video produces noisy geometry and artifacts that cause motion-tracking and scene interaction policies to fail.
approach: CRISP fits convex planar primitives to depth-based point clouds via clustering, uses human-scene contact modeling to reconstruct occluded geometry, and ensures physical plausibility through RL-driven humanoid control.
contribution: Reduces motion-tracking failure rates from 55.2% to 6.9% on EMDB and PROX benchmarks while delivering 43% faster RL simulation throughput for robotics applications.

problem: Existing multimodal models operate offline and cannot handle real-time interactive video understanding with sequential questions, memory constraints, and future anticipation.
approach: RIVER Bench introduces Retrospective Memory, Live-Perception, and Proactive Anticipation tasks with real-time interactive format evaluating models on streaming video comprehension, revealing deficiencies in long-term memory and future perception.
contribution: Demonstrates that offline models struggle with real-time processing and proposes a general improvement method enabling flexible real-time user interaction.

problem: Continual vision-language learning must maintain stable yet plastic capability under non-stationary streams without storing raw data, preventing catastrophic forgetting and maintaining transfer.
approach: CoMem organizes knowledge into a compact concept-relation graph, rehearses by conditioning practice signals on sampled subgraphs, and uses compositional consistency objectives and uncertainty-aware filtering.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art retention and transfer with consistent gains on cross-domain retrieval, concept learning, and continual VQA under matched memory and parameter budgets.

problem: Existing RAG systems lack methods for LLMs to proactively ask clarifying questions when faced with underspecified queries, as they ignore rule-based reasoning structures embedded in retrieved knowledge.
approach: GPS uses Directed Acyclic Graph reasoning with theoretical completeness guarantees to capture condition logic in retrieved knowledge, combines traversal-based pruning with user responses, and applies RL with hybrid reward.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines in both answer accuracy and interaction cost through targeted state probing and dynamic DAG-based clarification.

problem: Weight pruning LLMs is challenging because estimating global weight importance across massive parameters is infeasible, and uniform sparsity ratios across layers fail to account for uneven layer contributions.
approach: LSA allocates layer-wise sparsity by quantifying importance through minimal linear reconstruction error (LSE) when removing 50% of least important weights, supporting non-uniform block-level granularity.
contribution: At 70% overall sparsity, LSA surpasses state-of-the-art methods across language modeling and seven zero-shot tasks while supporting flexible per-block pruning.

problem: Vision Transformers process global [CLS] tokens and local patch tokens identically despite their distinct natures, causing friction in learning both global and local features effectively.
approach: Proposes specialized processing paths that disentangle [CLS] and patch token flow through normalization layers and early QKV projections based on analysis showing implicit differentiation between token types.
contribution: Improves segmentation by over 2 mIoU points on standard benchmarks while maintaining classification accuracy with only 8% parameter increase and no computational overhead.

problem: Self-supervised RL feature learning via mutual information skill learning (MISL) lacks theoretical understanding of how representation parametrization enables identifiable recovery of environment features.
approach: Analyzes Contrastive Successor Features (CSF) through identifiable representation learning, proving CSF recovers ground-truth features up to linear transformation due to inner-product parametrization and skill diversity.
contribution: Provides first identifiability guarantee for representation learning in RL, explaining implications of different MI objectives; validated on MuJoCo and DeepMind Control from both states and pixels.

problem: Scaling multimodal models to 3D medical imaging is computationally expensive because existing methods rely on 2D slices or fixed-token compression that disrupts volumetric continuity.
approach: Photon uses instruction-conditioned token scheduling with surrogate gradient propagation to adaptively reduce tokens during training/inference, incorporates custom backpropagation for differentiable discrete optimization, and applies regularization to mitigate bias.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on diverse medical visual question answering tasks while reducing resource usage and accelerating both training and inference.

problem: Existing reward methods for GUI agents struggle to generalize due to lack of ground-truth trajectories and application databases, while static trajectory-based LLM-as-Judge approaches suffer from limited accuracy.
approach: ProRe uses a general-purpose reasoner that schedules targeted state probing tasks executed by domain-specific evaluator agents, collecting additional environment observations to assign more accurate rewards.
contribution: Improves reward accuracy and F1 score by up to 5.3% and 19.4% respectively, with policy agents achieving up to 22.4% success rate improvement over baselines.

problem: GPU kernel writing is highly iterative and challenging, requiring domain expertise to improve performance through execution feedback, making it suitable for RL but lacking multi-turn training recipes.
approach: Kevin applies multi-turn RL with novel recipes for long trajectories and effective reward attribution across turns to train on CUDA kernel generation and optimization using verifiable rewards (correctness and speedup).
contribution: Improves kernel correctness from 56% to 82% and mean speedup from 0.53x to 1.10x of PyTorch Eager baseline, surpassing o4-mini and showing higher improvement rates with more refinement turns.

problem: Long-context models are susceptible to contextual noise from irrelevant tokens that can mislead attention, yet the role of noise in degrading performance is not well understood.
approach: Uses Integrated Gradient scores to detect and quantify noise information within context, proposes Context Denoising Training (CDT) that improves attention on critical tokens while reinforcing their influence on predictions.
contribution: CDT significantly boosts model attention on critical tokens; when trained with CDT, an 8B open-source model achieves performance (50.92) comparable to GPT-4o (51.00) across four tasks.

problem: Training computer-use agents requires massive amounts of manually annotated GUI interaction data, which is prohibitively expensive to acquire at scale.
approach: VideoAgentTrek automatically mines training data from YouTube tutorial videos by developing Video2Action with a video grounding model detecting GUI actions and an action-content recognizer extracting structured parameters.
contribution: From 39,000 YouTube videos generates 1.52 million interaction steps; improves OSWorld-Verified success from 9.3% to 15.8% (70% relative gain) and AgentNetBench step accuracy from 64.1% to 69.3%.

problem: Different rank aggregation methods produce significantly different results, impacting applications like AI agent development and evaluation, but no principled method exists for selecting which aggregation rule to use.
approach: Designs a data-driven rule-picking rule (RPR) that maximizes consistency if the data collection process were repeated, without assuming a generative model, and provides a sampling-based implementation.
contribution: Satisfies consistency-related axioms failed by natural RPRs and provides insights into improving consistency on both statistical models and real-world data.

problem: Standard representational similarity methods produce asymmetric results lacking global alignment scores and struggle with networks of different depths due to restriction to rigid one-to-one layer correspondences.
approach: Hierarchical Optimal Transport (HOT) jointly infers soft, globally consistent layer-to-layer couplings allowing source neurons to distribute mass across multiple target layers, minimizing transport cost under marginal constraints.
contribution: Matches or surpasses standard pairwise matching in alignment quality across vision models, LLMs, and visual cortex recordings while naturally handling depth mismatches through mass distribution.

problem: Representation alignment for generation typically assumes stronger global performance (ImageNet1K accuracy) leads to better generation, but the actual driver of generation performance is unclear.
approach: Conducts large-scale empirical analysis across 27 vision encoders, revealing spatial structure rather than global performance drives generation; proposes iREPA with convolution layer replacement and spatial normalization.
contribution: iREPA consistently improves REPA convergence speed across diverse encoders and model sizes with a 4-line modification, demonstrating spatial information transfer is critical for generation.

problem: Few-shot VQA performance of LMMs using in-context learning does not improve monotonically with more examples because extraneous image information overwhelms the model.
approach: Meta-Adaptive Prompt Distillation uses meta-learning to induce few-shot capabilities through fixed soft prompts distilled from task-relevant features adapted at test time via an attention-mapper module.
contribution: Achieves 21.2% improvement over ICL on VL-ICL Bench and 7.7% further enhancement compared to parameter-efficient finetuning methods for rapid task adaptation.

problem: LLMs typically acquire behaviors from demonstrations or experience, yet much training data consists of symbolic descriptions (instructions, rules, strategies) that specify procedures without examples.
approach: Programming by Backprop (PBB) enables LLMs to execute behaviors directly from abstract symbolic descriptions through targeted finetuning, tested on source code and grammar rules.
contribution: Shows LLMs can internalize reusable procedural abstractions from symbolic descriptions, generalizing across inputs and benefiting from chain-of-thought reasoning, though full reliability remains a challenge.

problem: Existing LiDAR compression methods rely on computationally intensive 3D contexts like voxels and octrees that struggle to balance compression efficiency with coding speed.
approach: Proposes a neural LiDAR compressor using 2D context models with multi-scale spatial, optical-flow temporal, and camera cross-modal context to reduce latency while enabling joint geometry-intensity compression.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements in both rate-distortion performance and coding speed compared to existing methods while supporting universal geometry-intensity compression.

problem: Designing synthesizable 3D ligands for protein pockets is hindered by lack of accurate synthesizability metrics and inconsistencies among classical metrics.
approach: Proposes SYNC, an SE(3)-invariant synthesizability classifier for SBDD and establishes a paradigm using guided diffusion and Direct Preference Optimization to generate synthesizable molecules.
contribution: SYNC demonstrates superior generalizability and speed compared to existing metrics; guided synthesis generates highly synthesizable molecules without compromising binding affinity.

problem: Existing video generation methods depend on fine-tuning large-scale models for specific tasks, which becomes impractical as model sizes grow; fine-grained frame-level control is needed.
approach: Frame Guidance applies training-free guidance to video diffusion models using frame-level signals (keyframes, styles, sketches, depth) via latent processing and optimization strategies for global coherence.
contribution: Produces high-quality controlled videos across diverse tasks including keyframe guidance, stylization, and looping without any training or explicit domain knowledge.

problem: Multimodal models struggle to detect academic fraud in visual evidence from retracted papers because existing benchmarks lack real-world complexity and task diversity.
approach: THEMIS evaluates MLLMs on 4K+ questions spanning 7 scenarios from authentic retracted cases and synthetic data with 16 fine-grained manipulation operations and 5 core fraud reasoning capabilities.
contribution: Even the best-performing model falls below passing threshold, demonstrating THEMIS presents a stringent test for complex, real-world fraud detection tasks.

problem: Predicting complex physical systems is hindered by the lack of expensive real-world data, resulting in models trained primarily on simulations that fail to bridge the sim-to-real gap.
approach: RealPDEBench integrates real-world measurements with paired simulations across five physical systems, defines three tasks comparing real and simulated data, and benchmarks ten representative baselines.
contribution: Reveals significant discrepancies between simulated and real-world data; pretraining with simulated data consistently improves both accuracy and convergence, advancing sim-to-real transfer.

problem: Incomplete multi-view multi-label learning must integrate information under simultaneous view and label incompleteness while maintaining robustness and avoiding over-alignment.
approach: PCVE formulates a principled objective maximizing variational evidence lower bound with permutation-consistent regularization to encourage distributional consistency across views and masked multi-label learning for missing labels.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods in multi-label classification with improved cross-view semantic cohesion and preservation of discriminative capacity.

problem: Current LLMs achieve high single-function verification but fail catastrophically at compositional reasoning across multi-function programs with interacting components.
approach: DafnyCOMP benchmark systematically evaluates LLMs on compositional specification generation for programs composed of 2-5 functions with data dependencies via LLM-driven synthesis.
contribution: Reveals 92% performance gap: while syntax correctness remains >99% for single-function tasks, it drops to 95.67% and verification crashes to 3.69% for compositional tasks.

problem: Set-based gait recognition overlooks short-range temporal context while sequence-based approaches fail to capture long-range temporal dependencies effectively.
approach: GaitSnippet conceptualizes gait as a composition of individualized actions represented by frames randomly selected from continuous segments (snippets), enabling multi-scale temporal context learning.
contribution: Achieves rank-1 accuracy of 77.5% on Gait3D and 81.7% on GREW using 2D CNN backbone, demonstrating effectiveness of snippet-based approach for comprehensive gait feature learning.

problem: Existing long-context LLM benchmarks lack narrative coherence, cover narrow domains, and only test simple recall-oriented tasks, limiting evaluation of true memory abilities.
approach: BEAM benchmark automatically generates up to 10M token coherent conversations with diverse topics and probing questions targeting multiple memory abilities; proposes LIGHT framework with three memory systems.
contribution: BEAM shows 1M-token context models struggle as dialogues lengthen; LIGHT consistently improves performance 3.5%-12.69% across various models by implementing long-term episodic, short-term working, and scratchpad memory.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action models relying on latent actions for VLA pretraining have not fully explored how latent actions can be learned and incorporated for improved generalization.
approach: villa-X advances latent action modeling by improving how latent actions are learned and integrated into VLA pretraining, enabling zero-shot latent action plan generation for unseen embodiments.
contribution: Achieves superior performance across diverse SIMPLER simulation tasks and real-world robotic setups with gripper and dexterous hand manipulation compared to prior VLA approaches.

problem: Scaling diffusion transformers to generate long-context videos is fundamentally limited by quadratic self-attention cost, making memory and computation intractable for long sequences.
approach: Reframes long-context video generation as information retrieval and proposes Mixture of Contexts (MoC), a learnable sparse attention routing module that dynamically selects informative chunks with causal routing.
contribution: Achieves near-linear scaling efficiency by allocating compute to salient history, preserving identities, actions, and scenes over minutes of content without loop closures.

problem: LLM-based global optimization often struggles in high-dimensional search spaces or without domain-specific priors, leading to sparse or uninformative candidate suggestions.
approach: HOLLM partitions the search space into promising subregions selected via bandit-inspired scoring, with LLMs proposing high-quality candidates within each subregion without explicit domain knowledge.
contribution: Consistently matches or surpasses leading global optimization methods while substantially outperforming global LLM-based sampling strategies on standard optimization benchmarks.

problem: Generating synchronized audio-video content is challenging because ensuring precise temporal alignment between audio and visual components while maintaining quality is non-trivial.
approach: JavisDiT uses a Diffusion Transformer for synchronized generation with a Hierarchical Spatial-Temporal Synchronized Prior Estimator extracting fine-grained spatio-temporal priors to guide audio-video alignment.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in both generation quality and synchronization precision on the new JavisBench with 10,140 high-quality text-captioned sounding videos.

problem: Existing multi-person 4D human-scene reconstruction from monocular video requires multi-stage pipelines, iterative refinement, and heavy dependencies (detection, depth estimation, SLAM), limiting real-time performance.
approach: Human3R uses parameter-efficient visual prompt tuning on CUT3R to jointly recover multiple SMPL-X bodies, dense 3D scenes, and camera trajectories in a single forward pass without iterative refinement.
contribution: Achieves superior or competitive performance in global human motion, mesh recovery, video depth, and pose estimation with a single unified model at real-time speed (15 FPS) on 8GB memory.

problem: Traditional mutual information estimators struggle with data that poses difficulties for conventional approaches, particularly in complex domains.
approach: InfoBridge leverages diffusion bridge models to frame mutual information estimation as a domain transfer problem, constructing an unbiased estimator via bridge matching.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on three standard MI estimation benchmarks (low-dimensional, image-based, high MI) and on real-world protein language model embeddings.

problem: Understanding the computational complexity of verifying properties of ReLU neural networks, such as positivity and function bounds, remains challenging and poorly understood.
approach: The paper proves parameterized hardness results by showing that deciding positivity of 2-layer ReLU networks is W[1]-hard when parameterized by input dimension, and establishes similar hardness for zonotope containment and Lipschitz constant computation.
contribution: Resolves open problems from COLT '25 by proving that network verification problems are W[1]-hard and NP-hard, establishing that naive enumeration methods are essentially optimal under the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

problem: PATE framework struggles with diverse generative tasks like text generation where teacher disagreement increases with output diversity, forcing a tradeoff between diversity and privacy-utility performance.
approach: Hot PATE introduces a diversity-preserving ensemble sampler that uses optimal transport to transfer diversity without incurring additional privacy cost, requiring only API access to proprietary models.
contribution: Shows significant improvements in privacy-utility tradeoff on in-context learning tasks by preserving output diversity while maintaining privacy guarantees.

problem: 3D part segmentation suffers from taxonomy constraints and limited generalization to unseen objects when relying on 2D foundation models that fail to capture intrinsic 3D geometry.
approach: PartSAM employs a triplane-based dual-branch encoder trained natively on large-scale 3D data with over five million shape-part pairs, enabling promptable segmentation of both surface and internal structures.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks with emergent open-world capabilities, enabling accurate part identification and automatic decomposition of 3D shapes.

problem: Layout-to-image generation suffers from attribute leakage due to entangled instance features and poor generalization to novel scenes due to insufficient paired training data.
approach: I-DRUID uses instance-disentanglement modules to extract clean instance representations and applies reinforcement learning with unpaired data to improve generalization to novel scenes.
contribution: Demonstrates improved layout-to-image generation accuracy by combining instance disentanglement with RL on unpaired, prompt-only data to avoid the need for paired data collection.

problem: Computer use agents lack large-scale, open-source training data spanning multiple platforms and domains, limiting progress toward general-purpose GUI automation.
approach: ScaleCUA provides a large-scale dataset across 6 operating systems and 3 task domains built via a closed-loop pipeline combining automated agents with human experts.
contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art results with 94.4% on MMBench-GUI L1-Hard, 60.6% on OSWorld-G, and 47.4% on WebArena-Lite-v2, demonstrating data-driven scaling for computer use agents.

problem: Private domain discovery requires selecting informative subsets of items from unknown domains while preserving differential privacy, a challenging problem under privacy constraints.
approach: Uses the Weighted Gaussian Mechanism as a domain-discovery precursor for top-k and k-hitting set algorithms, providing near-optimal missing mass guarantees on Zipfian data.
contribution: Extends known-domain algorithms to unknown-domain variants with new utility guarantees, demonstrating competitive or superior performance on all three problem types.

problem: Large language models suffer from substantial size that presents deployment and inference challenges, requiring practical compression methods that preserve model abilities.
approach: GPTailor compresses models by strategically merging layers from different finetuned variants through layer removal, selection, and merging operations, posed as a zero-order optimization problem.
contribution: For Llama2-13B, maintains approximately 97.3% of original performance while removing ~25% of parameters, significantly outperforming previous state-of-the-art pruning methods.

problem: Graph retrieval-augmented generation requires joint optimization of graph construction and retrieval, but prior work addresses these in isolation, leading to suboptimal performance especially under domain shift.
approach: Youtu-GraphRAG integrates graph construction, community detection, and retrieval into a unified agentic framework with seed schema guidance and hierarchical knowledge organization.
contribution: Demonstrates robustness across six challenging benchmarks by jointly connecting graph construction with schema-aware extraction and dually-perceived community detection.

problem: Building agentic multimodal models that reliably invoke external tools remains challenging, as direct reinforcement learning alone fails to establish robust tool-use behavior.
approach: DeepEyesV2 uses a two-stage training pipeline: cold-start stage to establish tool-use patterns followed by reinforcement learning to refine tool invocation on diverse, moderately challenging datasets.
contribution: Enables task-adaptive tool invocation with reliable tool integration, demonstrating that systematic tool integration enables complex reasoning across understanding, mathematical, and search-intensive tasks.

problem: Sign-SGD requires manual stepsize selection based on unknown, problem-specific quantities, creating a practical limitation for training large language models.
approach: Parameter-free Sign-SGD removes manual stepsize selection through adaptive methods that work across deterministic, stochastic, and multi-node settings, including momentum variants.
contribution: Matches performance of tuned Sign-SGD and AdamW on LLaMA (130M, 350M) and Swin Transformer (28M) while avoiding tuning overhead and achieving approximately 1.5× end-to-end speedup.

problem: LLM-based planners generate inaccurate plans due to gaps between general knowledge and environment-specific requirements, with iterative refinement incurring substantial query costs.
approach: CoPiC generates diverse high-level planning programs that iteratively produce candidate plans, which a trained domain-adaptive selector evaluates and selects based on alignment with long-term rewards.
contribution: Achieves 19.14% improvement in success rate and 79.39% reduction in token costs on ALFWorld, NetHack, and StarCraft II compared to advanced LLM-based baselines.

problem: Existing world model benchmarks use open-loop protocols that emphasize visual quality in isolation, leaving unclear whether world models actually help agents succeed at embodied tasks.
approach: WoW! benchmarks world models in closed-loop settings that mirror real agent-environment interactions with unified planning strategy, standardized action API, and four diverse environments.
contribution: Reveals that visual quality alone does not guarantee task success (controllability matters more), scaling post-training data is more effective than upgrading pretrained video generators, and more compute improves performance.

problem: Riemannian zeroth-order optimization struggles in geodesically incomplete settings where stationary points may not exist under the original metric.
approach: Constructs structure-preserving metrics that are geodesically complete while ensuring stationary points remain stationary, combining this with intrinsic analysis of zeroth-order estimators.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees for SGD matching best-known complexity in geodesically complete settings, with empirical validation on mesh optimization tasks.

problem: MLLM-based image quality assessment primarily relies on general contextual descriptions, limiting fine-grained quality perception of local image regions.
approach: Introduces grounding-IQA paradigm that integrates multimodal referring and grounding with IQA, comprising grounding-IQA-description (with bounding boxes) and visual question answering for local regions.
contribution: Constructs GIQA-160K dataset via automated annotation and develops GIQA-Bench benchmark, demonstrating that fine-grained grounding enables more detailed quality assessment.

problem: Implicit neural representations suffer from spectral bias, limited noise robustness, and difficulty capturing both local and global features despite strong performance across vision tasks.
approach: COSMO-INR leverages harmonic analysis and Chebyshev Polynomials to design activation functions modulated by complex sinusoidal terms that provide complete spectral support throughout the network.
contribution: Provides theoretical proof of improved spectral support through harmonic analysis, develops new activation functions with regularized deep priors, and demonstrates improved INR performance.

problem: Agentic RAG approaches treat retrieval as a black-box querying operation, confining agents to query issuing and hindering their ability to tackle complex information-seeking tasks.
approach: Interact-RAG introduces a Corpus Interaction Engine with action primitives for fine-grained control, enabling agents to manipulate the retrieval process directly through reasoning-enhanced workflow and autonomous end-to-end learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms advanced methods across six benchmarks by enabling agents to interact with the corpus rather than passively query it.

problem: KV-cache memory footprint scales linearly with sequence length, creating bottlenecks on constrained hardware during long-sequence generation tasks like multi-turn dialogue and chain-of-thought reasoning.
approach: IceCache integrates semantic token clustering with PagedAttention to organize tokens hierarchically and improve cache hit rates, maintaining only the most semantically relevant tokens on GPU.
contribution: Achieves over 99% accuracy with 256-token budget and 97% accuracy with 64-token budget, while using only 25% of full KV-cache token budget on long-sequence scenarios.

problem: Spoken language understanding requires integrating semantic, paralinguistic, and phonological characteristics, but existing benchmarks lack comprehensive linguistic grounding and fine-grained perception evaluation.
approach: MMSU introduces a comprehensive benchmark with 5,000 audio-QA triplets across 47 tasks grounded in linguistic theory, covering phonetics, prosody, rhetoric, syntactics, semantics, and paralinguistics.
contribution: Evaluates 22 advanced SpeechLLMs revealing substantial room for improvement, establishing new standards for comprehensive speech language understanding assessment.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems are vulnerable to collective cognitive biases like the Mandela effect, where groups collectively misremember events due to false details and social influence.
approach: Proposes ManBench benchmark with four task types and five interaction protocols to evaluate Mandela effect in multi-agent systems, testing both prompt-level defenses and model-level alignment-based mitigation.
contribution: Demonstrates 74.40% average reduction in Mandela effect through cognitive anchoring, source scrutiny, and alignment-based defenses on the proposed benchmark.

problem: Micro-expression recognition suffers from reliance on pixel-level motion descriptors lacking identity-invariance and domain generalization, combined with scarce annotated data.
approach: D-FACE uses a pretrained facial action tokenizer to shift from pixel-level descriptors to semantic-level facial action tokens, employing Transformer with emotion-description-guided CLIP alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art recognition accuracy with high-quality cross-identity and cross-domain micro-expression generation, demonstrating the paradigm shift from pixel-level to semantic-level representations.

problem: Whether LLM agents can shape co-players' learning dynamics in multi-agent settings remains unexplored, unlike well-studied opponent shaping in reinforcement learning.
approach: ShapeLLM adapts model-free opponent shaping methods for transformer-based agents, enabling LLM agents to influence co-players' behavior in diverse game-theoretic environments.
contribution: Demonstrates LLM agents can guide opponents toward exploitable equilibria in competitive games and promote coordination in cooperative games, establishing opponent shaping as a key multi-agent dimension.

problem: Image understanding and synthesis typically require separate discriminative and generative approaches, missing opportunities for mutual reinforcement between perception and generation.
approach: GenRep jointly conducts discriminative learning and generative modeling by distilling diffusion model knowledge to guide perception, with gradient alignment strategy to reconcile both learning objectives.
contribution: Achieves top-leading performance on both image understanding and generation benchmarks through unified training that creates positive feedback loop between perception and synthesis tasks.

problem: Multimodal embedding models condense information into single vectors (limiting expressiveness) or produce too many vectors (expensive for retrieval), constraining practical scalability.
approach: MetaEmbed uses learnable Meta Tokens with Matryoshka Multi-Vector Retrieval training to learn information organization by granularity, enabling test-time scaling via token selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance scaling to 32B parameters with flexible test-time quality-efficiency tradeoffs on MMEB and ViDoRe benchmarks.

problem: LLM pre-training is expensive, requiring efficient data selection methods that balance quality estimates against coverage and diversity to optimize the Pareto frontier.
approach: Evaluates 22 data curation techniques on T5-style models, identifying AskLLM (using instruction-tuned LLM zero-shot assessment) and density sampling (modeling data distribution) as best methods.
contribution: Shows AskLLM consistently outperforms full-data training by 10% sampling and converges 70% faster, establishing data-efficient pre-training as viable alternative to full-dataset training.

problem: Tensor-based incomplete multi-view clustering requires expensive adjacency matrix post-processing and struggles to capture geometric graph structure with high computational complexity.
approach: CAMEL jointly learns view-specific embeddings with structured constraints and organizes them into tensors with low-rank constraints, approximating Laplacian degree with constant-degree matrices to reduce complexity.
contribution: Reduces computational complexity from O(n²) to O(1) while eliminating post-processing, achieving better clustering performance through coordinated optimization of graph connectivity and high-order correlations.

problem: Offline bandit evaluation using reward models remains vulnerable to adversarial manipulations that can drastically alter bandit behavior with imperceptible perturbations.
approach: Investigates adversarial robustness of offline bandits from linear to nonlinear (ReLU) reward functions, showing high-dimensional effects where perturbations become more effective as dimensionality increases.
contribution: Reveals striking vulnerability of high-dimensional offline bandits to adversarial attacks, establishing this as a key security concern for bandit-based evaluation of generative models.

problem: Text-to-image retrieval fails on short, underspecified queries that are semantically ambiguous and lack explicit quality control, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Uses generative LLM for quality-controllable query completion, conditioning enrichment on discretized quality levels derived from relevance and aesthetic scoring models.
contribution: Provides flexible, transparent, and controllable retrieval by extending underspecified queries into descriptive forms that capture visual attributes while enabling user-preferred quality steering.

problem: Credit assignment at arbitrary delays remains challenging, as standard exponentially decaying eligibility traces mix events during delays, complicating temporal precision in synaptic plasticity.
approach: Proposes cascading eligibility traces (CETs) formed by state-space models inspired by biochemical reaction cascades, providing temporally precise memory for delayed credit assignment.
contribution: Demonstrates CETs enable credit assignment at behavioral timescales from seconds to minutes and handle extremely slow retrograde signals, offering better basis for modeling synaptic plasticity.

problem: Existing peptide design approaches generate sequences and structures in decoupled manner, failing to ensure designs are physically stable, evolutionarily plausible, and internally coherent.
approach: PepTri uses SE(3)-equivariant diffusion framework jointly generating peptide sequences and 3D structures with three guidance signals: physics-informed, evolutionary, and mutual information.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on peptide-protein benchmarks with improved binding affinity, structural accuracy, and design diversity through tri-guided generative process.

problem: LLMs often express miscalibrated confidence in their answers, creating safety and trustworthiness concerns for their deployment in high-stakes applications.
approach: Uses reinforcement learning optimizing logarithmic scoring rule reward to fine-tune LLMs for expressing calibrated confidence estimates, directly penalizing both over- and under-confidence.
contribution: Shows models exhibit substantially improved calibration and generalize to unseen tasks, with emergent general confidence awareness from integrated calibration into generative process.

problem: Computing polar decomposition efficiently for GPU training differs sharply from classical settings, requiring algorithms prioritizing throughput over precision.
approach: Polar Express uses minimax optimization at each iteration to adapt update rules for matrix sign computation, maintaining efficiency with only matrix-matrix multiplications suitable for GPU deployment.
contribution: Converges rapidly both in early iterations and asymptotically, addresses finite-precision issues in bfloat16, and improves GPT-2 validation loss on FineWeb when integrated into Muon optimizer.

problem: Quantum error correction decoding faces fundamental accuracy-efficiency tradeoff between high-precision but expensive tensor networks and fast but less accurate neural methods.
approach: SAQ-Decoder combines transformer architecture with constraint-aware post-processing, using dual-stream architecture and differentiable logical loss to optimize logical error rates on finite fields.
contribution: Achieves near maximum likelihood accuracy (10.99% error threshold on toric codes vs 11.0% theoretical bound) with linear computational scalability, addressing key requirements for fault-tolerant quantum systems.

problem: LLM-based agents exhibit systematic latent source preferences that bias information selection toward particular publishers/platforms, potentially distorting information presentation to users.
approach: Conducts controlled experiments on twelve LLMs across news, research, and e-commerce tasks to identify and quantify latent source preferences encoded in parametric knowledge.
contribution: Shows several models consistently exhibit strong predictable source preferences sensitive to context, outweighing content influence, explaining phenomena like left-leaning news recommendation bias.

problem: Existing deep reinforcement learning workflow schedulers use rigid, single-path inference architectures that struggle with diverse scheduling scenarios and varying deadline requirements.
approach: DEFT introduces mixture-of-experts DRL architecture with specialized experts trained for different deadline tightness levels and graph-adaptive gating using cross-attention.
contribution: Significantly reduces execution cost and deadline violations across dynamic cloud workflow benchmarks, adaptively routing through appropriate experts for deadline-sensitive scheduling.

problem: Computer-use agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, but current adversarial testing either lacks realism or ignores hybrid web-OS attack scenarios.
approach: RedTeamCUA introduces hybrid sandbox integrating VM-based OS with Docker-based web platforms, developing RTC-Bench with 864 examples for realistic adversarial scenario testing.
contribution: Benchmarks frontier CUAs showing Claude exhibits 42.9% Attack Success Rate while Operator shows 7.6%, revealing significant vulnerabilities even in most secure implementations.

problem: 3D object-scene composition with Gaussian Splatting suffers from baked appearance preventing realistic composition and requires expensive ray-tracing for relightable reconstruction.
approach: ComGS introduces Surface Octahedral Probes storing lighting/occlusion information for efficient querying via interpolation, and simplifies lighting by focusing on environment at object placement.
contribution: Achieves high-quality real-time rendering at ~26 FPS with at least 2× speedup in reconstruction, producing visually harmonious compositions through efficient inverse rendering.

problem: Brain-to-text decoding suffers from semantic mismatches during alignment, as human brains selectively encode salient regions based on individual interests not uniformly across scenes.
approach: Yo'Mind uses optimal transport-driven personalized semantic masking to adaptively mask redundant visual components based on individual neural responses, enabling unified brain-visual-linguistic alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art brain-to-text reconstruction with improved interpretability and enables cross-subject decoding, bridging semantic gaps through personalized visual semantic pruning.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks suffer from spectral bias that causes networks to learn low-frequency features first, limiting accuracy on high-frequency PDEs.
approach: IFeF-PINN enriches latent space using high-frequency components through Random Fourier Features in iterative two-stage training: basis estimation then coefficient regression.
contribution: Empirically establishes Random Fourier Features enhance expressive capacity for high-frequency PDE approximation, showing superior performance over state-of-the-art on benchmark problems.

problem: SFT checkpoints with highest evaluation performance often fail to maximize RL potential due to distributional forgetting where models drift excessively from base model distribution.
approach: Identifies diversity metrics (entropy, self-BLEU) as reliable early-stopping criteria and introduces Adaptive Early-Stop Loss balancing new pattern acquisition with distribution preservation.
contribution: Shows diversity-based early stopping surpasses performance-based selection and AESL further enhances RL preparation on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Intermediate state in real-world processes often contains sparse activations whose identifiability and learnability through end-to-end training remains theoretically unestablished.
approach: Sparling proves Motif Identifiability Theorem establishing precise identification of sparse motifs through end-to-end error reduction, and provides algorithm using novel informational bottleneck enforcing extreme sparsity.
contribution: Precisely localizes intermediate states up to feature permutation with >90% accuracy on synthetic and real domains (DigitCircle, LaTeX-OCR, Audio-MNIST) through end-to-end training alone.

problem: Multi-view clustering struggles to balance semantic and structural information, where existing methods bias toward one type while treating the other as auxiliary, limiting generalization and clustering performance.
approach: DREAM disentangles semantic information via a VAE branch and captures structure-aware features through a GCN branch, dynamically fusing them with a gated module and enforcing triple-granularity consistency across views, samples, and clusters.
contribution: DREAM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multi-view clustering approaches on benchmark datasets.

problem: Controlling stylistic attributes of LLMs requires parallel corpora and suffers from discreteness, instability, and lack of fine-grained control over output characteristics like formality or complexity.
approach: Reframe Low-Rank Adaptation as a causal intervention by contrasting activations with/without LoRA perturbations, then use PCA denoising and geometric median for robust style vector extraction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on conceptual complexity, text detoxification, and formality control with bidirectional steering and generalization across models.

problem: Iteratively retraining generative models on self-generated synthetic data causes model collapse, where performance deteriorates over successive training iterations.
approach: Inject external synthetic data verification through a human or better model as a verifier during retraining, preventing model collapse and enabling convergence to verifier's knowledge center.
contribution: Theory and experiments on linear regression and CVAE show verifier-guided retraining yields early improvements and long-run convergence, while unguided retraining causes collapse.

problem: Masked diffusion models degrade performance when using few denoising steps due to limited modeling of inter-dimensional dependencies in discrete data.
approach: Introduce Variational Autoencoding Discrete Diffusion (VADD) with an auxiliary recognition model to capture correlations among dimensions via variational bounds, enabling stable training and amortized inference.
contribution: VADD consistently outperforms masked diffusion baselines, especially with small denoising steps, across 2D toy data, pixel-level image generation, and text generation.

problem: Multi-turn image editing tasks require efficient composition of expensive AI tool calls, making end-to-end planning costly and limiting scalability.
approach: Combine fast LLM subtask planning with slow A* search per subtask, then extract reusable subroutines from successful toolpaths via inductive reasoning to enable adaptive fast-slow planning.
contribution: FaSTA* achieves significant computational efficiency gains while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art image editing baselines by reusing symbolic subroutines and triggering A* only for novel tasks.

problem: LLMs with external tools rely on supervised fine-tuning with distilled trajectories, leading to imitative reasoning that limits generalization and tool-calling capabilities.
approach: Train with lightweight rule-based reinforcement learning using only binary rewards for format validity and functional correctness of tool invocations, avoiding dependence on annotated reasoning trajectories.
contribution: Nemotron-Research-Tool-N1 7B and 14B models outperform GPT-4o on major tool-use benchmarks, demonstrating that pure RL outperforms the widely-adopted SFT-then-RL pipeline.

problem: Source-free domain adaptive object detection overlooks object-level structural cues within cross-domain data, relying instead on pseudo-label refinement and teacher-student frameworks.
approach: Integrate object-centric learning into DETR-based detectors via a Hierarchical Slot Awareness module and Class-Guided Slot Contrast to disentangle images into slot representations guided toward class semantics.
contribution: CGSA outperforms previous source-free domain adaptive object detection methods across five cross-domain datasets by introducing the first object-centric design for this task.

problem: Post-training quantization of Mixture-of-Experts models incurs substantial memory overhead during inference, and uniform quantization suffers significant accuracy loss at low bit-widths.
approach: Propose expert-wise mixed-precision strategy based on change in router's L2 norm during training and maximum intra-neuron variance, allocating higher precision to experts sensitive to quantization.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy than existing quantization methods on large-scale MoE models including Switch Transformer and Mixtral, reducing inference cost with negligible bit-width assignment overhead.

problem: Existing depth estimation models lack spatially consistent geometry prediction from arbitrary camera viewpoints, particularly without known camera poses.
approach: Depth Anything 3 uses a single plain transformer encoder and singular depth-ray prediction target via teacher-student training, achieving detail and generalization while simplifying the modeling approach.
contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art across camera pose estimation, any-view geometry, and visual rendering, surpassing VGGT by 35.7% in pose accuracy and 23.6% in geometric accuracy.

problem: Chain-of-thought monitoring for detecting AI misalignment can be evaded through ciphered reasoning hidden in encrypted, translated, or compressed text.
approach: Test whether models can reason within different ciphers via fine-tuning and prompting, measuring accuracy on math problems as a proxy for reasoning capability in ciphered contexts.
contribution: Current frontier models struggle with lesser-known ciphers despite comprehending them; ciphered reasoning capability correlates with cipher prevalence in pretraining data and improves slowly with fine-tuning.

problem: Key-value cache in autoregressive LLM inference grows linearly with sequence length, causing memory bottlenecks that limit long-context inference efficiency.
approach: Propose ChanMix, a mixed-precision quantization framework supporting 2-bit and FP8 precision with channel-aware bit reallocation based on per-channel quantization sensitivity.
contribution: Achieves at least 5 percentage points improvement over baseline methods on RULER benchmark, enabling 2.3x increase in batch size and 1.5x longer context during inference.

problem: Understanding how fine-tuning on harmful tasks causes generalization to unrelated prompts with malicious behaviors (emergent misalignment) requires mechanistic investigation.
approach: Apply model diffing via sparse autoencoders to compare internal representations before/after fine-tuning, identifying misaligned persona features in activation space that predict emergent misalignment.
contribution: Discovers a toxic persona feature most strongly controlling emergent misalignment, and shows fine-tuning on just hundreds of benign samples efficiently restores alignment.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models produce object hallucinations where visual encoders suffer from statistical bias, inherent bias, and vulnerability, not just LLM components.
approach: SHIELD mitigates hallucinations through three training-free strategies: re-weighting visual tokens to reduce bias, introducing noise-derived tokens to counter inherent bias, and applying adversarial attacks with contrastive decoding.
contribution: Effectively mitigates object hallucinations across diverse benchmarks and LVLM families while achieving strong performance on general LVLM benchmarks.

problem: Simulating user behavior in conversations using assistant LMs produces poor simulators, as better-trained assistants make worse user simulators due to their optimized conversational style.
approach: Train purpose-built User Language Models via post-training to simulate human users in multi-turn conversations, capturing realistic user behavior including refinement and indirect phrasing.
contribution: User LMs align better with human behavior and achieve better simulation robustness than assistant models, revealing that GPT-4o performance drops from 74.6% to 57.4% under realistic user simulation.

problem: Bayesian optimization relies on expert priors but existing methods are overly complex, tied to specific acquisition functions, or highly sensitive to inaccurate priors.
approach: DynMeanBO incorporates expert priors into Gaussian process mean function with dynamic decay, exploiting expert knowledge early while reverting to standard behavior and ensuring robustness.
contribution: Accelerates convergence with informative priors and remains robust against biased ones, with convergence guarantees and compatibility across acquisition functions.

problem: Classical quantile regression does not extend naturally to multivariate responses, and existing approaches overlook the geometry of joint distributions.
approach: Combine neural optimal transport with amortized optimization to parameterize conditional vector quantile functions as gradients of convex potentials, ensuring monotonicity and uniform ranks.
contribution: Produces tighter and more informative predictive regions via conformal prediction by adapting to conditional distribution geometry, showing improved coverage-efficiency trade-offs.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting models are vulnerable to partial infringement attacks where adversaries extract and reuse subsets of Gaussians, and existing watermarking protects only rendered images.
approach: NGS-Marker integrates jointly-trained watermark injector and decoder with gradient-based progressive injection for full-scene coverage, enabling robust ownership decoding from local regions.
contribution: Effectively defends against partial infringement while supporting hybrid protection and multimodal watermarking for practical real-world deployment.

problem: LLMs struggle to perform rule-consistent mathematical reasoning, and existing evaluations using PASS@k metrics fail to capture gaps between final-answer accuracy and derivation fidelity.
approach: Model chain-of-thought as a rule-based stochastic process over directed acyclic graphs, introducing logical closeness metric that quantifies adherence to DAG structure beyond PASS@k.
contribution: DAG-Math benchmark reveals statistically significant differences in reasoning fidelity among LLM families even when PASS@k is comparable, providing actionable diagnostics.

problem: Evaluating user-facing AI applications in open-ended domains requires expensive human feedback or behavioral signals, creating a bottleneck for system optimization.
approach: AutoMetrics synthesizes evaluation metrics by combining retrieval from curated MetricBank of 48 metrics with automatically-generated LLM-as-a-Judge criteria informed by lightweight human feedback, composed via regression.
contribution: Improves Kendall correlation with human ratings by up to 33.4% over LLM-as-a-Judge baseline while requiring fewer than 100 feedback points across diverse tasks.

problem: Large neural networks face rigid trade-offs between performance and computational budget at inference time, ill-suited for resource-constrained or dynamic environments.
approach: Nested Subspace Networks re-parameterize linear layers to satisfy nested subspace properties, enabling smooth adjustment across compute budgets via rank selection with uncertainty-aware training.
contribution: A single NSN-adapted model achieves 50% reduction in inference FLOPs with only 5 percentage point accuracy loss, unlocking adaptive foundation models with predictable compute-performance frontier.

problem: Personalized video generation faces a fundamental trade-off between identity consistency and action realism, with imprecise subject-video alignment and inadequate fine-grained action modeling.
approach: ReactID harmonizes identity and motion through curated high-precision dataset, progressive training curriculum analyzing learning difficulty, and timeline-based conditioning with subject-aware mechanisms.
contribution: Balances identity accuracy and motion naturalness, achieving state-of-the-art performance on personalized video generation benchmarks.

problem: Sim-to-real transfer in RL relies on resource-intensive re-training of the full policy network, limiting flexibility in dynamic environments.
approach: Found-adapt decouples skill acquisition from environment adaptation by pretraining a foundation policy on offline trajectories, then performing efficient latent-space adaptation via adapter networks.
contribution: Significantly reduces the sim-to-real gap across multiple locomotion tasks through efficient latent adaptation without costly policy optimization.

problem: Graph-based multi-view clustering relies on static graph structures and suffers from false negative contamination in contrastive learning, with trade-offs between cross-view consistency and view-specific discrimination.
approach: MANGO combines adaptive multi-scale diffusion with random walk-driven contrastive learning and structure-aware view consistency, using high-probability semantic paths to filter false negatives.
contribution: Extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks demonstrate improved performance by reconciling consistency-specificity trade-offs through diffusion-guided graph learning.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models fall short on zero-shot robotic manipulation due to scarcity and heterogeneity in embodied datasets, lacking fine-grained spatial reasoning.
approach: FSD generates intermediate spatial relationship representations through hierarchical data construction and self-consistency mechanisms, providing fine-grained guidance for robotic manipulation.
contribution: Achieves 40.6% success rate in SimplerEnv and 72% in real-world tasks, outperforming strongest baseline by 30% through improved spatial reasoning.

problem: Video compositing requires intensive manual labor and expert collaboration, with rigid identity preservation often leading to unnatural motion.
approach: GenCompositor uses a Diffusion Transformer with background preservation via masked token injection, novel position embedding ERoPE for layout control, and multi-action temporal conditioning.
contribution: Demonstrates effective generative video compositing with customizable size, motion trajectory, and attributes via interactive editing on newly curated VideoComp dataset of 61K video sets.

problem: Editing generated images lacks intuitive control over scene composition, typically requiring retraining rather than direct manipulation of geometric structure.
approach: Generative Blocks World represents scenes as assemblies of convex 3D primitives that can be edited, then generates new images via flow-based models conditioned on depth and texture hints.
contribution: Achieves accurate object and camera moves while preserving object identity, outperforming prior works in visual fidelity, editability, and compositional generalization.

problem: RL-based macro placement neglects accumulated expert knowledge from years of engineering practice, optimizing oversimplified proxy objectives that deviate from expert-designed solutions.
approach: Integrate EDA domain expertise via expert knowledge injection including dataflow guidance and I/O constraints, and expert workflow imitation through preference optimization on backend feedback.
contribution: Substantial improvements on ICCAD 2015 and OpenROAD benchmarks by bridging RL-based placement with domain expertise and post-refinement processes.

problem: Shadow generation and relighting are treated as disjoint tasks, overlooking the intrinsic coupling of illumination and shadowing essential for physically consistent indirect effects.
approach: Propose Light-Geometry Interaction maps representing light-aware occlusion from monocular depth, embedding them in a bridge-matching generative backbone for joint shadow and relighting.
contribution: Significant gains in realism and consistency across synthetic and real images by enabling physics-inspired priors that constrain generative models and bridge geometry-inspired rendering.

problem: Ordinal regression struggles with inherent ordering and non-stationary inter-class boundaries, while existing rank-based methods suffer from rigidity of fixed binning.
approach: GoR reframes ordinal regression as sequential generation via autoregressively predicting ordinal segments until dynamic end-of-sequence, enabling adaptive resolution and step-wise refinement.
contribution: Theoretically establishes bias-variance error bound and proposes Coverage-Distinctiveness Index metric; extensive experiments on 17 ordinal regression benchmarks show effectiveness.

problem: Group distributionally robust optimization fails in speech when CTC loss scales with input length and linguistic properties, causing spurious group loss differences.
approach: CTC-DRO smooths group weight updates to prevent overemphasis on consistently high-loss groups while using input length-matched batching to mitigate CTC scaling issues.
contribution: Reduces worst-language error by up to 47.1% and average error by 32.9% on multilingual ASR across ML-SUPERB 2.0, applicable with minimal computational cost.

problem: Existing LLM safety evaluations fail to capture catastrophic risks in multi-turn conversations due to fixed attack prompts, lack of statistical guarantees, and limited scalability.
approach: C3LLM provides a principled certification framework modeling multi-turn conversations as Markov processes over query graphs with semantic similarity edges, quantifying catastrophic risks via confidence intervals.
contribution: Reveals substantial catastrophic risks in frontier models with certified lower bounds as high as 70%, highlighting urgent need for improved safety training strategies.

problem: Graph neural networks rely on message-passing which is limited in expressive power, and sequence-based canonicalization flattens structure and distorts graph distances.
approach: Canonical Tree Cover Neural Networks represent graphs with canonical spanning tree covers processed via expressive tree encoders, preserving graph distances better than sequences.
contribution: Strictly more expressive than sequence-based canonicalization; consistently outperforms invariant GNNs and random samplers across graph classification benchmarks.

problem: Multi-modal LLMs struggle with spatial understanding of 3D worlds despite strong general perception, limiting zero-shot 3D spatial reasoning capabilities.
approach: pySpatial equips MLLMs with spatial tools via Python code generation, composing function calls to 3D reconstruction, camera-pose recovery, and novel-view rendering for zero-shot reasoning.
contribution: Outperforms GPT-4.1-mini by 12.94% on MindCube, with successful real-world indoor navigation demonstrating practical effectiveness of explicit spatial reasoning.

problem: Latent diffusion model-based image restoration methods suffer from slow iterative denoising, making them impractical for time-sensitive applications despite improved perceptual quality.
approach: RestoreVAR adopts visual autoregressive modeling from scale-space, capturing degradations in coarse scales and details in finer scales, with cross-attention and latent refinement tailored for restoration.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art restoration performance among generative methods with over 10x faster inference and strong generalization capabilities.

problem: Single-image view synthesis requires expensive optimization or per-image training, limiting real-time photorealistic synthesis across camera movements.
approach: SHARP regresses 3D Gaussian representation parameters from a single image via single feedforward neural network pass, enabling metric, zero-shot view synthesis.
contribution: Reduces LPIPS by 25-34% and DISTS by 21-43% versus best prior model, achieving photorealistic synthesis in less than a second with three orders of magnitude speed improvement.

problem: Accelerating LLM pretraining via computationally-efficient second-order approximations risks substantial performance loss compared to full second-order methods.
approach: Apply full Gauss-Newton preconditioning to transformer models up to 150M parameters and compare against layerwise Hessian structure approximations.
contribution: Full Gauss-Newton achieves 5.4x reduction in training iterations over baselines; layerwise GN matches full performance, suggesting higher-order terms may not be critical.

problem: Model-based offline RL suffers from model exploitation due to model errors and Q-value underestimation, with existing methods like RAMBO prone to instability and over-conservatism.
approach: ROMI introduces robust value-aware model learning requiring models to predict states with values close to minimum Q-value within adjustable uncertainty sets, with implicitly differentiable adaptive weighting.
contribution: Significantly outperforms RAMBO on D4RL and NeoRL datasets, achieving competitive performance through controllable conservatism and stable model updates.

problem: Collecting informative images for 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction lacks feedback, causing inefficient and potentially deficient data gathering.
approach: Active learning algorithm estimates most informative image poses by partitioning consistent regions via Gaussian attributes, evaluating semantic feature variance per Gaussian, and optimizing noisy poses.
contribution: Demonstrates robust active learning performance under accurate and noisy pose conditions on both synthetic and real-world scenes.

problem: Network dismantling methods depend on global structural knowledge, exhibit slow running times, and overlook latent geometry that governs complex system dynamics.
approach: LGD-NA leverages local network automata rules to approximate effective link distances and identify critical nodes, capturing latent manifold information for efficient dismantling.
contribution: Outperforms all existing dismantling algorithms across 1,475 real-world networks and scales efficiently via GPU acceleration while enabling network robustness engineering.

problem: Existing LLM tool-use benchmarks overlook real-world user behavior including compositional tasks, implicit intent spread across turns, and instruction transitions, making progress spurious.
approach: WildToolBench grounds tool-use evaluation in real-world user behavior patterns, testing 57 LLMs on compositional tasks, implicit intent inference, and flexible instruction transitions.
contribution: No model achieves accuracy above 15%, revealing substantial gap in LLMs' robustness despite prior benchmarks suggesting progress, emphasizing user-LLM-tool interaction challenges.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning with trajectory preferences struggles to learn robust policies when data coverage is poor and lacks algorithmic tractability or theoretical guarantees.
approach: MCP leverages a tractable conservative learning framework that improves policies upon a reference policy supported by the data, using a general function class without requiring known transition dynamics.
contribution: First provably sample-efficient and computationally tractable offline preference-based RL algorithm under partial data coverage.

problem: Large Language Models struggle to understand molecular graphs effectively because existing graph-LLM bridges use fixed-length static tokens that overlook stereochemistry and substructural context.
approach: EDT-Former generates tokens aligned with informative molecular patches using entropy-guided dynamic token selection, enabling frozen graph encoders to align with LLMs without backbone fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on MoleculeQA, Mol-Instructions, and property prediction benchmarks with efficient multimodal molecular understanding.

problem: Multi-view 3D reconstruction methods fail when input views have insufficient overlap, occlusions, or sparse coverage, resulting in incomplete reconstructions.
approach: ReconViaGen integrates reconstruction priors into a diffusion-based generative framework with cross-view connections and improved denoising controllability to generate consistent plausible structures.
contribution: Reconstructs complete and accurate 3D models consistent with input views in both global structure and local details despite sparse view coverage.

problem: No large-scale benchmark exists for evaluating LLM agents on complex future prediction tasks requiring real-time updates and handling data contamination.
approach: FutureX is a dynamic live benchmark with real-time daily updates, automated question/answer collection, and evaluation of 25 LLM/agent models including reasoning and search capabilities.
contribution: Establishes largest and most diverse live benchmark for future prediction with contamination-free evaluation through automated pipeline.

problem: N-gram novelty alone is an inadequate metric for textual creativity because it ignores creativity's dual nature: novelty and appropriateness.
approach: Study the relationship between n-gram novelty and expert-judged creativity through 7542 annotations of human and AI-generated text via close reading.
contribution: Demonstrates that ~91% of top-quartile n-gram novel expressions are not judged as creative, showing n-gram novelty correlates with lower pragmaticality in LLMs.

problem: Existing unlearning methods for LLMs remain vulnerable to relearning during subsequent training, allowing forgotten knowledge to resurface.
approach: Ssiuu employs attribution-guided regularization to prevent spurious negative influence and faithfully remove target knowledge instead of hiding it.
contribution: Reliably erases target knowledge and outperforms baselines across adversarial injection and instruction-following retraining scenarios.

problem: Driving world models evaluate generation quality but overlook downstream perception performance, and synthetic data benefits disappear when training epochs are equalized.
approach: Dream4Drive decomposes video into 3D-aware guidance maps and renders 3D assets onto them, enabling fine-tuned world models to produce multi-view photorealistic videos for training perception models.
contribution: Generates multi-view corner cases at scale that significantly boost corner case perception in autonomous driving.

problem: Existing language agent benchmarks focus on narrow domains or simplified tasks lacking the diversity, realism, and long-horizon complexity of real-world applications.
approach: Toolathlon provides 32 software applications, 604 tools from MCP servers, realistic environment states from real software, and 108 manually sourced tasks requiring ~20 interaction turns.
contribution: Largest and most diverse benchmark for language agents with reliable execution-based evaluation across real-world applications.

problem: The LLM community focuses almost exclusively on decoder-only models while lacking fair comparisons between encoder-only and decoder-only architectures trained with identical recipes.
approach: Ettin suite provides paired encoder-only and decoder-only models (17M to 1B params) trained on up to 2 trillion tokens with the same recipe.
contribution: Beats ModernBERT as encoder and Llama 3.2 and SmolLM2 as decoders; shows encoder tasks benefit from encoders while decoders excel at generation.

problem: LLMs' autoregressive decoding limits their ability to revisit and refine earlier tokens holistically, leading to inefficient exploration of diverse solutions.
approach: LaDiR unifies continuous latent representations with latent diffusion by encoding reasoning steps into VAE latent blocks and denoising them with blockwise bidirectional attention.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy, diversity, and interpretability on mathematical reasoning and planning benchmarks over autoregressive and existing diffusion methods.

problem: LLMs applied to forecasting tasks may fail evaluation due to temporal leakage and unclear generalization to real-world forecasting performance.
approach: Systematic analysis identifies two categories of evaluation issues: temporal leakage and failure to extrapolate from evaluation to real-world forecasting.
contribution: Demonstrates through concrete examples how evaluation flaws can invalidate current performance claims about LLM forecasting abilities.

problem: Existing equivariant policy learning methods require structured inputs like 3D point clouds or top-down views, preventing their use in low-cost or dynamic environments.
approach: RAVEN is the first SE(3)-equivariant policy framework operating on RGB images by treating image data as collections of rays that transform under 3D roto-translations.
contribution: Consistently surpasses baselines in both performance and efficiency on robot manipulation in simulation and real-world settings.

problem: State-of-the-art 3D occupancy estimation methods rely on slow voxel-based or dense Gaussian representations lacking flexibility for temporal dynamics.
approach: S2GO summarizes scenes into compact query sets propagated through time online, decoded into semantic Gaussians at each timestep with denoising rendering.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes and KITTI occupancy benchmarks with 4.5x faster inference than GaussianWorld.

problem: It is unclear when Transformers can learn to rely on causal features instead of spurious correlations, especially under strong data correlation.
approach: Analyzes Transformer training through correlation strength and implicit regularization, identifying Correlation Crowding-Out where gradient descent filters spurious cues.
contribution: Shows that under suitable conditions, standard training induces cause-only prediction through occupation and crowding-out mechanisms.

problem: Diffusion-based image generation suffers from slow inference due to computational expense, and prior caching methods use rigid heuristics with limited generalization.
approach: ECAD uses a genetic algorithm to learn efficient per-model caching schedules forming a Pareto frontier from calibration prompts, with no network modifications required.
contribution: Achieves significant inference speedups with fine-grained quality-latency trade-off control, generalizing to unseen resolutions and model variants.

problem: Symbolic regression truncates the scientific discovery cycle by focusing on hypothesis and experiment without systematic analysis of structural errors.
approach: RESTART closes the loop with a principled analysis stage: short-term refinement uses boosting to identify unexplained signals, long-term library distills successful refinements.
contribution: Achieves lower error and higher accuracy than baselines on LLM-SRBench; recovers near-exact functional forms on out-of-distribution data.

problem: Static classifier-free guidance scales fail to adapt to diverse prompt requirements in text-to-image diffusion, and existing solutions introduce complexity without generalization.
approach: Dynamic CFG scheduling leverages online feedback from small-scale latent-space evaluators (CLIP, discriminator, reward model) to select optimal per-timestep guidance scales.
contribution: Achieves up to 53.8% human preference win-rate vs default Imagen 3 baseline with improvements in text alignment, visual quality, and text rendering.

problem: Neural datasets contain heterogeneous populations of stable and stochastic cells, making it hard to identify consistent activity patterns during self-supervised pretraining.
approach: POYO-SSL exploits heterogeneity by pretraining only on predictable neurons identified via skewness and kurtosis, then fine-tuning on unpredictable population.
contribution: Yields 12-13% relative gains over from-scratch training with smooth monotonic scaling on Allen Brain Observatory; exhibits no plateau as model size increases.

problem: Video understanding in multimodal LMs is limited by context length, causing missed key frames and poor coherence across long time scales.
approach: VideoNSA adapts Native Sparse Attention to video-LMs via end-to-end training on 216K video instruction dataset with hardware-aware hybrid attention strategy.
