contribution: Reliably scales to 128K tokens with improved long-video understanding, temporal reasoning, and spatial performance over token-compression baselines.

problem: AdamW is the default optimizer for transformer pretraining but the community has struggled to find faster, more stable alternatives.
approach: Single-line modification to any momentum-based optimizer creates cautious optimizers (C-AdamW, C-Lion) that preserve Adam's Hamiltonian and convergence guarantees.
contribution: Consistent speed-up on LLM pretraining and post-training with better results on MAE pretraining and minimal hyperparameter tuning required.

problem: Diffusion LLMs introduce unprecedented vulnerabilities distinct from autoregressive LLMs due to iterative and parallel generation mechanisms.
approach: DiffuGuard uses stochastic annealing remasking to mitigate greedy selection bias and block-level audit-repair that exploits internal representations for risk detection.
contribution: Reduces attack success rate from 47.9% to 14.7% across six jailbreak methods while preserving model utility and efficiency.

problem: Recent hardware-accelerated FP4 formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) promise efficiency gains but their practical benefits remain unproven due to format-specific challenges.
approach: MR-GPTQ tailors GPTQ quantization to FP4 using block-wise Hadamard transforms and format-specific optimizations supported by high-performance GPU kernels.
contribution: Achieves speedups up to 3.6x layer-wise on NVIDIA B200 and 6x on RTX5090 with accuracy matching or outperforming state-of-the-art.

problem: Vision-language model evaluation relies mainly on English benchmarks and translations of English datasets that fail to capture cultural nuances.
approach: Kaleidoscope is a large-scale in-language benchmark covering 18 languages and 14 subjects with 20,911 multiple-choice questions built through open science collaboration.
contribution: Demonstrates that multilingual VLMs perform poorly on low-resource languages and complex multimodal scenarios, highlighting need for culturally inclusive evaluation.

problem: Continual learning suffers from catastrophic forgetting; existing approaches like replay and EWC have limitations in data generation and task optimization.
approach: Leverages rank-1 Fisher structure of diffusion models to propose rank-1 EWC variant paired with replay for parameter sharing while mitigating drift.
contribution: Consistently improves average FID and reduces forgetting; nearly eliminates on MNIST/FashionMNIST and roughly halves on ImageNet-1k.

problem: Cache-affinity scheduling for KV cache reuse conflicts with load-balancing requirements in distributed LLM serving, forcing suboptimal routing choices.
approach: DualMap maps each request to two candidate instances using independent hash functions, then intelligently selects the better candidate based on system state.
contribution: Simultaneously enables cache affinity and load balancing with SLO-aware routing and hotspot-aware rebalancing for dynamic workloads.

problem: Conformal prediction relies on softmax-derived nonconformity scores that unreliably indicate model certainty, limiting prediction set adaptiveness.
approach: Leverages Helmholtz Free Energy as uncertainty measure and reweights nonconformity scores with monotonic transformation of energy score for each sample.
contribution: Improves adaptiveness of prediction sets with notable increase in both efficiency and adaptiveness compared to baseline nonconformity scores.

problem: In-context learning is effective but incurs high inference costs as context length grows, limiting practical applications.
approach: Prompt-MII uses RL-based framework to meta-learn instruction induction that reduces training examples to compact descriptive prompts achieving comparable ICL performance.
contribution: Improves downstream model quality by 4-9 F1 points while requiring 3-13x fewer tokens, trained on 3,000+ diverse classification datasets.

problem: Evaluating diffusion posterior sampling algorithms lacks distribution-level comparisons and gold-standard reference methods for inverse problems.
approach: Proposes statistical benchmark using discretized Lévy processes with efficient Gibbs sampling methods that provide gold-standard posterior samples for DPS evaluation.
contribution: Enables arbitrary-precision Monte Carlo estimation and isolation of algorithmic errors from learned component errors across multiple inverse problems.

problem: Semantic caches using static similarity thresholds lack formal correctness guarantees, resulting in unexpected error rates and suboptimal cache hit rates.
approach: vCache employs online learning algorithm to estimate optimal threshold for each cached prompt, enabling reliable cache responses with user-defined error bounds.
contribution: Consistently meets specified error bounds while achieving up to 12.5x higher cache hit and 26x lower error rates vs static-threshold baselines.

problem: Text-image manipulation methods struggle with text removal, lack style control, and tend to generate duplicated letters despite advances in inpainting.
approach: OmniText leverages cross- and self-attention mechanisms to enable text removal via inversion and style control via redistributed attention, using latent optimization.
contribution: Training-free generalist for diverse text image manipulation tasks with novel loss functions and OmniText-Bench dataset for evaluation.

problem: Generative classifiers using diffusion-based approaches suffer from substantial computational costs, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: Investigates VAR-based generative classifiers which offer tractable likelihood, proposes Adaptive VAR Classifier+ for improved accuracy and efficiency.
contribution: Achieves significantly more efficient inference than diffusion-based counterparts with improved accuracy; enables visual explainability via token-wise mutual information.

problem: RL-based scaling approaches for tool use struggle to scale thinking length sufficiently for complex problems and waste tokens on simple problems through overthinking.
approach: Uses warm-up supervised fine-tuning to distinguish simple/complex problems, then applies entropy-based optimization objectives to enable automatic reasoning-length scaling.
contribution: Achieves auto-scaling for efficient tool use with 9.8% accuracy improvements while reducing computational overhead by ~81%.

problem: Existing navigation models struggle to provide unified solutions across heterogeneous paradigms like instruct-goal, object-goal, point-goal navigation, and exploration.
approach: OmniNav proposes fast-slow system design: fast module generates waypoints from short-horizon context, slow module conducts deliberative planning over long-horizon observations.
contribution: Handles multiple navigation paradigms within single architecture with high precision waypoint prediction supporting real-world deployment up to 5 Hz.

problem: Conventional RNNs collapse temporal dynamics into fixed-dimensional hidden states, limiting adaptability and context learning for sequence modeling.
approach: WARP parametrizes hidden state as weights and biases of auxiliary network driven by input differences, enabling gradient-free test-time adaptation and physics-informed priors.
contribution: Matches or surpasses state-of-the-art on diverse tasks; physics-informed variant outperforms baseline by >10x on dynamical system reconstruction.

problem: LLMs perform multi-step reasoning but cannot reliably verify their own logic, with flawed reasoning undermining trust in high-stakes scenarios.
approach: VeriCoT extracts formal logical arguments from CoT, formalizes steps into first-order logic, identifies premises, and uses automated solvers to verify validity.
contribution: Effectively identifies flawed reasoning and serves as strong predictor of answer correctness; improves reasoning via self-reflection and preference fine-tuning.

problem: LLMs have limited parametric knowledge and existing RAGs struggle with knowledge-intensive tasks due to fragmented information and weak graph structure modeling.
approach: G-reasoner integrates graph and language foundation models with QuadGraph, a standardized four-layer abstraction unifying heterogeneous knowledge into common representation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on six benchmarks with scalable 34M-parameter graph foundation model integrated with LLMs.

problem: MLLMs often struggle with fine-grained visual understanding and hallucinations due to over-reliance on linguistic priors that distract from actual visual information.
approach: MMGrounded-PostAlign introduces dual grounding with visual module identifying referred objects and textual module generating rationale, plus negative rejection and selective reasoning.
contribution: Significant improvements on POPE, HaloQuest, ReasonSeg, MME, and MMBench benchmarks with enhanced visual-textual alignment and reduced hallucinations.

problem: Existing variance-dependent lower bounds for linear contextual bandits have gaps with upper bounds and only consider fixed total variance budgets, not general variance sequences.
approach: Establishes variance-dependent lower bounds for both prefixed and adaptive variance sequences using novel analysis techniques.
contribution: Overcomes limitations of prior work with improved lower bound of Ω(d√(Σσ²_k)/log K) that closes gap with existing upper bounds.

problem: Diffusion-based image compositing struggles to preserve coherent spatial relations in pairwise or sequential edits, with subsequent insertions overwriting previous content.
approach: PICS uses self-supervised composition-by-decomposition with Interaction Transformer employing Mixture-of-Experts and adaptive α-blending for compatibility-aware fusion.
contribution: Delivers superior pairwise compositing quality and substantially improved stability across virtual try-on, indoor, and street scene settings.

problem: Weighting methods in federated learning operate efficiently but fail to address the main obstacle: communication bottleneck in heterogeneous data scenarios.
approach: Incorporates compression into the weighting scheme with convergence analysis under convexity for both exact and stochastic oracles.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees while addressing communication bottleneck in federated learning with heterogeneous data.

problem: Audio large language models lack fine-grained spatial reasoning ability, relying on coarse binaural cues that limit accuracy in direction and distance estimation.
approach: The paper introduces SAGE, a geometry-aware audio encoder that aligns binaural acoustic features with 3D spatial structure using panoramic depth images and room-impulse responses at training time, then integrates it into OWL, an ALLM with spatially grounded chain-of-thought reasoning over direction-of-arrival and distance estimates.
contribution: OWL reduces mean direction-of-arrival error by 11 degrees and achieves o'clock-level azimuth estimation while supporting multi-step spatial reasoning.

problem: Existing mathematical reasoning benchmarks are limited in scale, language coverage, and task diversity, leaving mathematical retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation underexplored.
approach: MathNet provides 17,512 expert-authored Olympiad-level problems spanning 40 countries and 10 languages, supporting three tasks: mathematical comprehension, mathematical retrieval with 39K equivalence pairs, and Math RAG evaluation.
contribution: MathNet is the largest high-quality Olympiad dataset with the first retrieval benchmark for problem equivalence; state-of-the-art reasoning models achieve 76.8% (GPT-5) and 46.8% (Claude 4.5 Opus), showing significant remaining challenges.

problem: Automated alpha mining in quantitative finance is hindered by reward sparsity, inadequate sequential representations of formulas, and the inability to generate diverse portfolios of non-correlated alphas.
approach: AlphaSAGE combines a structure-aware encoder using Relational Graph Convolutional Networks with Generative Flow Networks and a dense multi-faceted reward structure to mine alphas via a novel generative flow network framework.
contribution: AlphaSAGE outperforms existing baselines in mining more diverse, novel, and highly predictive alpha portfolios, establishing a new paradigm for automated alpha mining.

problem: Predictive training using Koopman operator theory to accelerate SGD suffers from gradient explosion, especially for complex network structures.
approach: Predictive Differential Training (PDT) incorporates differential learning with an effective masking strategy based on dynamic consistency analysis to select high-fidelity weight predictions, and uses an acceleration scheduler to adjust prediction intervals.
contribution: PDT integrates seamlessly with existing optimizers (SGD, Adam, RMSprop, LAMB) and shows consistent performance improvement with reduced gradient explosion.

problem: The interaction between structured compressibility and adversarial robustness is poorly understood, hindering the design of models that are both efficient and robust.
approach: A principled framework analyzes how neuron-level sparsity and spectral compressibility affect robustness by examining their effects on learned representations and sensitivity directions.
contribution: The analysis reveals that compressibility induces sensitive directions exploitable by adversaries, with robustness bounds showing how compressibility impacts l-infinity and l-2 robustness; vulnerabilities persist under adversarial training and transfer learning.

problem: Exploiting symmetries in Bayesian Optimization is limited because the max kernel, which captures maximum similarity across group orbits, is not positive semidefinite.
approach: The paper revisits the max kernel idea by using a positive semidefinite projection of the max kernel to capture symmetries in expensive black-box function optimization.
contribution: The projected max kernel achieves significantly lower regret on synthetic and real-world BO benchmarks without increasing computational complexity compared to existing invariant and non-invariant kernels.

problem: Existing multimodal masked diffusion models support only simple image-level understanding and low-resolution generation, lacking unified capabilities for grounding, editing, and high-resolution synthesis.
approach: Lavida-O introduces Elastic Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that couples lightweight generation and larger understanding branches with token compression, universal text conditioning, and stratified sampling for efficient multimodal understanding and generation.
contribution: Lavida-O achieves state-of-the-art performance on RefCOCO grounding, GenEval text-to-image, and ImgEdit benchmarks while supporting 1024px synthesis and outperforming Qwen2.5-VL and Flux models with considerable speedup.

problem: Understanding how data geometry controls implicit bias and generalization in overparameterized neural networks trained below the edge of stability remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Theoretical analysis for two-layer ReLU networks examines how data geometry affects generalization through intrinsic dimension adaptation and concentration of probability mass toward the unit sphere.
contribution: For data on low-dimensional balls, generalization bounds adapt to intrinsic dimension; for isotropic distributions, mass concentration toward the sphere leads to memorization while dispersed mass enables learning shared patterns.

problem: Scaling laws and compute-optimal performance of signSGD under realistic data distributions with power-law feature and target decay are not well understood.
approach: Analysis of signSGD under power-law random features model characterizes population risk as a function of model size, training steps, and learning rate, identifying drift-normalization and noise-reshaping effects unique to signSGD.
contribution: signSGD can achieve steeper compute-optimal slopes than SGD in noise-dominant regimes, and the warmup-stable-decay schedule further reduces noise and sharpens the optimal slope.

problem: Current search-augmented language models struggle with fact-seeking questions where web search yields conflicting, noisy, or unhelpful results, especially in long-context reasoning.
approach: SealQA provides a three-flavor benchmark (SEAL-0 for near-zero accuracy questions, SEAL-HARD for challenging cases, LongSeal for long-context multi-document reasoning) to evaluate reasoning and factual accuracy with conflicting web results.
contribution: Even frontier reasoning models like GPT-5 achieve only 43.2% on SEAL-0, and test-time compute increases often plateau or decline; models struggle with document selection in long-context scenarios.

problem: The data processing inequality suggests no benefit to low-level preprocessing before classification, yet practitioners routinely perform enhancement and encoding steps.
approach: Theoretical analysis of binary classification with classifiers converging to Bayes optimal as training samples increase examines when low-level processing improves accuracy.
contribution: For finite training samples, preprocessing always exists that improves classification accuracy; the gain depends on class separation, training set size, and class balance, consistent with empirical observations on benchmark datasets.

problem: Concept Bottleneck Models enable interpretable predictions and test-time intervention on concepts, but interventions fail when the model exhibits systemic misalignment with expert reasoning due to data bias.
approach: CBDebug introduces a two-step Removal and Retraining framework where experts identify undesired concepts and the system converts concept-level feedback into sample-level auxiliary labels for supervised bias mitigation and targeted augmentation.
contribution: CBDebug significantly outperforms prior retraining methods across PIP-Net and Post-hoc CBM architectures on datasets with known spurious correlations.

problem: Training expressive flow-based policies with off-policy reinforcement learning is unstable due to gradient pathologies in multi-step action sampling, analogous to RNN vanishing/exploding gradients.
approach: SAC Flow reparameterizes velocity networks using gated and decoded variants inspired by modern sequential models, enabling end-to-end training of flow policies via noise-augmented rollouts.
contribution: SAC Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on continuous control and robotic manipulation benchmarks while eliminating the need for policy distillation or surrogate objectives.

problem: MIP solvers generate thousands of cuts consuming gigabytes of memory while providing minimal benefit, making traditional approaches computationally expensive and memory-intensive.
approach: MIRACLE uses reinforcement learning with PPO to learn a cut-selection policy via curriculum learning and imitation learning on expert solver decisions, enabling adaptive inference with dynamic computational budgets.
contribution: MIRACLE achieves 98.1% memory reduction with 0.08% objective gap, 3.78x average speedup on MIPLIB problems, and 100% success rate on instances where SCIP fails 47-53% of the time.

problem: Text-to-motion models trained on generic text corpora lack explicit alignment between motion-related words and skeletal movements, limiting fine-grained motion understanding.
approach: Motion-Aligned Text Encoding (MATE) incorporates motion semantics into LLM word embeddings through motion localization (soft attention guidance between sub-texts and motion segments) and motion disentanglement (contrastive kinematic prototypes).
contribution: LLMs enhanced with MATE significantly surpass state-of-the-art T2M performance on two benchmarks when integrated into existing methods with minimal modifications.

problem: RL controllers struggle to satisfy trajectory-level safety and reliability constraints; formal specifications like LTL offer correct-by-construction objectives but produce sparse rewards.
approach: The paper integrates LTL with differentiable simulators by relaxing discrete automaton transitions via soft state labeling to produce differentiable rewards, enabling gradient-based learning directly from formal specifications.
contribution: The framework preserves objective soundness while achieving up to twice the returns of discrete baselines on complex nonlinear contact-rich continuous-control tasks.

problem: Existing Process Reward Models struggle with table-specific operations like sub-table retrieval and schema interaction, limiting performance in tabular reasoning for test-time scaling.
approach: TaTToo integrates tool-based verification with a dual-stage paradigm combining supervised fine-tuning on step-level annotations with reinforcement learning using tool-grounded reward shaping.
contribution: TaTToo improves downstream LRMs by 30.9% on five tabular reasoning benchmarks covering numerical reasoning, fact-checking, and data analysis.

problem: Existing methods fail to capture the complex physics of extreme collisions, producing non-physical artifacts and material adhesion at fracture interfaces.
approach: Fracture-GS enhances Collision Material Point Method with momentum-conserving interface forces and integrates it with fracture-aware 3D Gaussian continuum representation through implicit reconstruction, collision resolution, and dynamic fracture tracking.
contribution: The framework demonstrates superior physical accuracy and computational efficiency in handling homogeneous materials, heterogeneous composites, and multi-body collisions compared to existing methods.

problem: Existing protein function prediction models lack fine-grained intra-protein understanding of critical structural and functional features.
approach: VenusX is a benchmark with 878,000 samples from InterPro, BioLiP, and SAbDab covering six annotation types: residue-level binary classification, fragment-level multi-class classification, and pairwise functional similarity for active sites, binding sites, conserved sites, motifs, domains, and epitopes.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of diverse models (protein language models, sequence-structure hybrids, structure-based, alignment-based) reveals performance gaps across in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios.

problem: Generating counterfactual explanations that are robust to input and model perturbations while maintaining plausibility and diversity remains challenging in a unified, model-agnostic manner.
approach: LAPACE uses Label-conditional Gaussian Mixture VAE to learn structured latent space with class-specific Gaussian components and generates counterfactual paths by interpolating from input latents to learned centroids.
contribution: The method ensures robustness to input changes as paths converge to fixed centroids, provides diverse recourse options, and supports user-specified actionability constraints via gradient optimization.

problem: Open-set graph anomaly detection with limited labeled normal and abnormal nodes is challenging due to data scarcity for unseen anomalies and label scarcity for training.
approach: DEMO adaptively fuses multiple seen nodes to simulate unseen anomalies while dynamically adjusting sample weights based on energy gradients to prioritize informative nodes and maintain a memory bank for pseudo-labeling.
contribution: DEMO outperforms baselines on various benchmarks for detecting unseen anomalies different from training anomalies.

problem: Scaling Vision-Language Models in multi-agent systems is economically unsustainable due to high coordination costs under information asymmetry and heuristic proxies that ignore costs.
approach: Agora reframes coordination as a decentralized market for uncertainty, formalizing epistemic uncertainty as a tradable asset with market-aware Thompson Sampling extended as broker to guide cost-efficient equilibria.
contribution: Agora achieves +8.5% accuracy over baselines on MMMU while reducing cost by over 3x across five multimodal benchmarks (MMMU, MMBench, MathVision, InfoVQA, CC-OCR).

problem: Existing resting-state fMRI models trained on limited data struggle to generalize across diverse populations and scanning protocols.
approach: MnemoDyn uses a dynamical-systems based model with multi-resolution temporal modeling on 40K rs-fMRI sequences across public and permission-based datasets, trained without transformer backbones.
contribution: MnemoDyn delivers superior reconstruction quality compared to state-of-the-art transformer-based approaches and generalizes well across populations and protocols while being compute efficient.

problem: RAG systems expose external knowledge bases to extraction attacks via malicious inputs, but detection is easy; extraction via benign queries remains understudied.
approach: IKEA uses anchor concepts (knowledge-related keywords) to generate natural queries, then applies Experience Reflection Sampling and Trust Region Directed Mutation to exhaustively explore RAG's embedding space.
contribution: IKEA surpasses baselines by over 80% in extraction efficiency and 90% in attack success rate; substitute RAG systems built from IKEA extractions show close performance to originals.

problem: World models for autonomous driving suffer from identity drift, where objects change appearance or category across frames due to lack of instance-level temporal constraints.
approach: ConsisDrive introduces Instance-Masked Attention and Instance-Masked Loss to enforce temporal consistency at the instance level, ensuring visual tokens interact only with corresponding instance features.
contribution: ConsisDrive achieves state-of-the-art driving video generation quality and demonstrates significant improvements in downstream autonomous driving tasks on nuScenes.

problem: Discrete Level-of-Detail rendering requires significant storage for model copies and causes jarring visual popping artifacts during transitions.
approach: CLoD-GS introduces a continuous LoD mechanism directly into 3D Gaussian Splatting with learnable distance-dependent decay parameters that adjust Gaussian opacity based on viewpoint proximity.
contribution: CLoD-GS enables smooth quality scaling within a single unified model while reducing primitive count and memory footprint compared to discrete methods.

problem: Traditional CFD and graphics pipelines for fire effects require handcrafted geometry and expert-tuned parameters, limiting scalability to real-world scenes.
approach: FieryGS integrates multimodal LLM-based material reasoning, efficient volumetric combustion simulation, and unified rendering of fire and 3DGS through three modules: implicit reconstruction, combustion simulation, and dynamic fracture tracking.
contribution: FieryGS enables realistic, controllable fire synthesis in real scenes with precise user control over intensity, airflow, ignition location, and other combustion parameters.

problem: Standard preference elicitation methods fail to capture true cognitive processes behind human decision-making, such as use of heuristics and simplifying thought patterns.
approach: An axiomatic approach learns cognitively faithful decision processes from pairwise comparisons where features are processed with learned rules then aggregated via fixed rules like Bradley-Terry.
contribution: The method learns interpretable models of human decision-making in kidney allocation tasks matching or surpassing prior accuracy on pairwise decision-making.

problem: Existing machine-generated text detectors struggle to identify task-specific MGT on real-world platforms like Wikipedia, where tasks like summarization produce text resembling human writing.
approach: TSM-Bench provides a multilingual, multi-generator, multi-task benchmark for evaluating MGT detectors on common Wikipedia editing tasks, revealing generalization asymmetries.
contribution: Average detection accuracy drops 10-40% compared to prior benchmarks; fine-tuning on task-specific data enables cross-domain generalization but not vice versa.

problem: Cascaded speech systems transcribe and resynthesize, discarding paralinguistic cues and creating a text bottleneck; text-guided systems still rely on text intermediates.
approach: A true speech-to-speech LLM uses modality-based layer-splitting architecture with frozen pre-training to preserve reasoning while adding native speech capabilities without text guidance.
contribution: The model achieves state-of-the-art spoken question answering and comparable speech-to-speech performance relative to text-guided systems while maintaining competitive text performance.

problem: Academic rebuttal is a complex strategic communication task under information asymmetry requiring perspective-taking, but current approaches miss this and imitate surface-level linguistics.
approach: RebuttalAgent grounds rebuttal in Theory of Mind (ToM) via ToM-Strategy-Response framework, trained with supervised fine-tuning on synthetic RebuttalBench (9,533 trajectories) followed by RL with self-reward.
contribution: RebuttalAgent significantly outperforms the base model by 18.3% average; Rebuttal-RM specialized evaluator achieves scoring consistency with human preferences surpassing GPT-4.1.

problem: Diffusion LLMs recompute all QKV at every denoising step and layer despite minimal KV state changes, creating substantial redundancy and high decoding latency.
approach: Elastic-Cache performs adaptive layer-aware KV cache updates by deciding when to refresh via attention-aware drift test on most-attended tokens and where via depth-aware schedule.
contribution: Elastic-Cache achieves 8.7x speedup on GSM8K (256 tokens), 45.1x on longer sequences, and 4.8x on HumanEval with negligible generation quality loss.

problem: Generating short movies from textual descriptions while maintaining long-range coherence in both storyline and visual appearance is challenging.
approach: Captain Cinema uses top-down keyframe planning to generate narrative keyframes ensuring coherence, then bottom-up video synthesis conditioned on keyframes; includes interleaved training strategy for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers.
contribution: Captain Cinema demonstrates favorable performance in automated creation of visually coherent and narratively consistent short films.

problem: Explaining RL agent policies in natural language requires handling pluralistic and probabilistic human judgments about explanation quality, not captured by point estimates.
approach: The framework trains LLMs for explanation generation via RL from AI feedback using rewards from continuous normalizing flows that capture probabilistic human reward distributions.
contribution: CNF-based rewards yield explanations enabling more accurate agent decision predictions, greater logical soundness and actionability, and lower cognitive load than prior RLHF/RLAIF methods.

problem: Knowledge editing and unlearning mechanisms in LLMs remain largely unexplored due to insufficient, isolated, small-scale evaluation.
approach: KnowledgeSmith proposes a unified framework casting editing and unlearning as constrained optimization, with automatic dataset generator providing structured interventions across graph levels and data scales.
contribution: Results show LLMs do not exhibit similar updating as humans for different knowledge levels, and there exists consistency-capacity trade-off between editing reliability and model performance.

problem: LoRA fine-tuning faces generalization challenges, and applying Sharpness-Aware Minimization to LoRA is computationally expensive due to sequential QKV computation.
approach: Bi-LoRA introduces auxiliary adversarial LoRA module that decouples sharpness optimization from task adaptation, enabling parallel computation while providing perturbations outside the primary module's optimization subspace.
contribution: Bi-LoRA roughly halves SAM application time for LoRA while achieving both efficiency and effectiveness across diverse architectures and tasks.

problem: Knowledge distillation typically forces students to mimic teacher distributions over entire outputs, causing distribution mismatch especially in complex reasoning tasks with limited student capacity.
approach: Token-Selective Dual Knowledge Distillation combines indirect distillation (teacher re-ranks student-proposed responses) and direct distillation (selective token-level distribution matching based on confidence difference) with entropy regularization.
contribution: TSD-KD achieves state-of-the-art performance on 10 challenging reasoning benchmarks, outperforming baselines by up to 54.4% and runner-up by 40.3%.

problem: Computing worst-case robust real-time pursuit strategies for graph-based pursuit-evasion games under partial observability (imperfect information) is currently missing from the literature.
approach: R2PS proves dynamic programming maintains optimality under asynchronous evader moves, extends it with belief preservation for partial observability, and embeds into EPG framework for learning robust cross-graph policies.
contribution: R2PS achieves robust zero-shot generalization to unseen real-world graph structures against asynchronous-move DP evasion strategies with policy learning via RL.

problem: RL training convergence for post-training LLMs is sensitive to batching and prompt selection; optimal strategies remain unclear.
approach: Prompt Curriculum Learning uses a learned value model to select intermediate-difficulty prompts (50% model success rate) without costly rollouts, focusing on most sample-efficient prompts.
contribution: PCL achieves highest performance or significantly less training time to reach comparable performance; PCL is 12.1x and 16.9x faster at identifying intermediate-difficulty prompts on MATH and DeepScaleR.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems lack scalable reliability due to structural fragility and the scarcity of large-scale datasets for error attribution and debugging.
approach: Aegis constructs 9,533 annotated failure trajectories via LLM-based error injection into successful executions, supporting three learning paradigms: supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and contrastive learning.
contribution: Fine-tuned LLMs achieve error attribution performance competitive with proprietary models an order of magnitude larger, validating automated data generation for reliable multi-agent systems.

problem: Machine learning researchers often miss that popular molecular datasets contain orientational bias because atomic geometries are not randomly rotated, which can lead to spurious model performance.
approach: The paper demonstrates the bias empirically by training classifiers to separate original molecules from rotated ones with high accuracy, and by training models that use only molecular orientation to predict chemical properties.
contribution: Documented and validated that QM9, QMugs, and OMol25 datasets contain systematic orientational bias that neural networks exploit, providing a cautionary insight for molecular machine learning practitioners.

problem: Decentralized learning performs poorly under high data heterogeneity and limited communication because peer-to-peer synchronization strategies are not well optimized for generalization.
approach: The paper studies how to schedule communication over time in decentralized training, finding that concentrating communication in later stages and performing a single global merge at the final step surprisingly improves generalization.
contribution: Showed theoretically that a fully connected final merge in decentralized SGD can match parallel SGD convergence rates, reinterpreting model discrepancies as beneficial rather than detrimental.

problem: GUI visual grounding for agent systems has relied on expensive supervised fine-tuning of multimodal models despite advances in foundation models, making scaling impractical.
approach: GuirlVG applies reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning to GUI grounding with empirical component analysis and an Adversarial KL Factor to stabilize training against reward over-optimization.
contribution: Achieved +7.7% improvement on ScreenSpot and +17.2% on ScreenSpotPro using only 5.2K training samples versus 10M+ for supervised methods.

problem: Deep learning approaches for PDE forecasting struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution scenarios without test-time adaptation data, limiting zero-shot deployment.
approach: iMOOE captures two-fold PDE invariance (ingredient operators and their compositions) through an Invariance-aligned Mixture Of Operator Expert architecture with frequency-enriched learning.
contribution: Achieved superior zero-shot generalization across diverse OOD PDE forecasting scenarios while maintaining in-distribution performance on simulated and real-world benchmarks.

problem: Applying SVD to reduce Vision Language Model computation traditionally achieves limited real-world latency improvement despite theoretical benefits.
approach: WSVD applies SVD at finer granularity with adaptive weighting of parameter importance and quantization of weights and activations to preserve accuracy during compression.
contribution: Achieved over 1.8x decoding speedup on VLMs while preserving accuracy performance through weighted, quantized SVD.

problem: Solving constrained routing problems with neural networks is challenging because complex feasibility constraints make high-quality solution generation difficult.
approach: LMask employs dynamic masking with lazy refinement and backtracking, using refinement intensity embeddings and constraint violation penalties during training.
contribution: Achieved state-of-the-art feasibility rates and solution quality on TSPTW and TSPDL with theoretical guarantees for validity and probabilistic optimality.

problem: Scaling concept unlearning in diffusion models to large numbers of concepts faces conflicts in weight updates, collateral damage to similar content, and efficiency bottlenecks.
approach: ScaPre uses conflict-aware stabilization via spectral trace regularization and the Informax Decoupler to identify concept-relevant parameters and adaptively reweight updates.
contribution: Enabled scalable and precise large-scale unlearning without auxiliary data or modules, effectively removing target concepts while maintaining generation quality.

problem: Conformal prediction's validity assumptions break when training data have corrupted or missing labels, requiring robustness to distribution shifts.
approach: Proposes uncertain imputation to preserve label uncertainty without weight estimation, complementing privileged information approaches in a triply robust framework.
contribution: Showed PCP remains valid even with poorly estimated weights and introduced UI method that provides statistically valid predictions through careful label imputation.

problem: Group relative policy optimization for LLM reasoning is slow because generating multiple responses per query creates a computational bottleneck in the autoregressive generation phase.
approach: FastGRPO applies concurrency-aware speculative decoding that dynamically adjusts drafting strategy based on real-time concurrency and introduces online draft learning to adapt to evolving target models.
contribution: Achieved 2.35x to 2.72x end-to-end speedup on mathematical reasoning datasets, making GRPO training practical.

problem: Spatial-temporal video grounding suffers from hallucinations due to misalignment between textual descriptions and visual coordinates, worsened by the need for dense coordinate prediction.
approach: STVG-R1 reformulates coordinate prediction as instance identification with temporally consistent IDs embedded as visual prompts, then applies reinforcement learning with task-driven rewards.
contribution: Achieved 20.9% improvement on m_IoU on HCSTVG-v2 over Qwen2.5-VL-7B and SOTA 47.3% J&F on zero-shot multi-object video segmentation.

problem: Dataset distillation needs efficient algorithms with theoretical guarantees for both supervised learning and offline RL without requiring model training.
approach: Matches losses on training and synthetic datasets using randomly sampled regressors, then extends via Bellman loss matching to offline RL.
contribution: Proved O(d^2) regressor complexity suffices for supervised distillation with matching lower bounds, and extended the approach to offline RL without policy optimization.

problem: Diffusion Language Models suffer from slow inference because scattered token acceptance creates fragmented KV caches requiring repeated repairs.
approach: Prefix Absorption uses Longest Stable Prefix scheduling to commit high-margin, temporally stable tokens as atomic blocks aligned with structural delimiters.
contribution: Reduced end-to-end latency while maintaining or improving task quality on code generation and reasoning with geometric decay in active sequence length.

problem: RL training of LLMs is resource-intensive, requiring substantial GPU memory and long rollout durations that limit practical deployment.
approach: QeRL combines NVFP4 quantization with LoRA and adds Adaptive Quantization Noise to increase policy entropy and enable dynamic noise adjustment during training.
contribution: Achieved 1.2x-1.5x speedup over BF16 LoRA and 1.5x-2.0x over QLoRA while reducing memory, enabling 32B LLM training on single H100 GPU.

problem: Vision-language models hallucinate on visually degraded document images, producing fluent yet incorrect OCR without signaling uncertainty.
approach: TreeVGR uses GRPO to train models that bracket uncertain spans with uncertainty tags while balancing accuracy and uncertainty coverage with multi-objective rewards.
contribution: Maintained transcription accuracy while achieving 0.685 F1 score on uncertainty tagging in degraded OCR and introduced TreeBench, a diagnostic benchmark.

problem: Event sensor understanding lacks semantic-aware approaches for open-vocabulary instance segmentation despite advances in other visual modalities.
approach: SEAL provides a unified framework for semantic-aware event segmentation at multiple granularities using visual prompts for both instance and part-level understanding.
contribution: Outperformed proposed baselines in performance and inference speed with parameter-efficient architecture and curated benchmarks across granularity levels.

problem: Single-cell RNA clustering is difficult because measurement noise and biological variability cause different cell types to project close together in standard latent spaces.
approach: A latent plug-and-play diffusion framework uses Gibbs sampling with Doob-bridged diffusion, applying denoising in latent space while steering with noise reintroduction in observation space.
contribution: Improved clustering accuracy on synthetic data under varied noise and dataset shifts while enabling generalization via clean reference data.

problem: EEG classification needs interpretable, lightweight models that can efficiently differentiate epilepsy from healthy subjects.
approach: Constructs lightweight transformers by unrolling a spectral denoising algorithm for balanced signed graphs with learned optimal cutoff frequencies.
contribution: Achieved classification performance comparable to deep learning with dramatically fewer parameters through algorithm unrolling.

problem: Vision-language models hallucinate on degraded documents in OCR tasks, producing fluent but incorrect text without uncertainty signals.
approach: Uses GRPO to train uncertainty-aware OCR that brackets unreliable spans with uncertainty tags while balancing transcription accuracy and tag coverage.
contribution: Maintained accuracy while achieving 0.685 F1 on uncertainty tags and introduced Blur-OCR benchmark for evaluating uncertainty-aware OCR.

problem: Offline RL struggles with generalization to unseen state-action pairs because value functions become overly optimistic about poorly represented regions.
approach: Uses contrastive preference learning to train policies by contrasting successful demonstrations with failure behaviors and synthetic out-of-distribution behaviors.
contribution: Substantially outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in learning efficiency and final performance on challenging sparse-reward offline RL benchmarks.

problem: Deep Gaussian process posterior inference over inducing variables is inefficient because DDVI starts from a simple prior far from the true posterior.
approach: Diffusion Bridge Variational Inference initiates reverse diffusion from a learnable data-dependent distribution parameterized via amortized networks and progressively adapted.
contribution: Consistently outperformed DDVI in predictive accuracy, convergence speed, and sample efficiency across regression, classification, and reconstruction tasks.

problem: Sparse attention mechanisms for reducing decoding latency lack guarantees on approximation quality and fail to provide consistent approximations across heads.
approach: vAttention unifies top-k and sampling with statistical guarantees, providing user-specified (ε,δ) approximation accuracy bounds and leveraging complementary strengths.
contribution: Improved sparse attention quality by ~4.5 percentage points and bridged the gap between full and sparse attention at 10x-20x sparsity.

problem: Reinforcement learning fine-tuning of pretrained policies causes mode collapse where policies lose diversity and rely on easily exploitable outputs.
approach: Introduces a polychromic objective that explicitly enforces exploration and refinement of diverse generations using vine sampling and modified advantage functions.
contribution: Improved success rates on BabyAI and Minigrid by reliably solving more environment configurations and achieving higher coverage in pass@n experiments.

problem: Adapting LLM behavior typically requires external knowledge or fine-tuning, but it is unclear if models already contain specialized subnetworks for different personas.
approach: Identifies persona-specialized subnetworks via small calibration datasets and activation signatures, using masking to isolate lightweight subnetworks.
contribution: Demonstrated that LLMs contain distinct persona subnetworks enabling training-free, parameter-efficient persona adaptation with stronger alignment than external methods.

problem: Test-time scaling strategies for autoregressive LLMs may not transfer well to masked diffusion language models due to their fundamentally different generation process.
approach: UnMaskFork formulates unmasking as a search tree and applies Monte Carlo Tree Search with deterministic partial unmasking actions from multiple MDLMs.
contribution: Consistently outperformed test-time scaling baselines on complex coding benchmarks and showed strong scalability on mathematical reasoning.

problem: Decoder-only LLMs struggle with table reasoning because serialization obscures row and column structure, and external graph approaches show inconsistent gains.
approach: HInT injects hypergraph-derived structural features directly into layers where row-column relations are concentrated using gated fusion.
contribution: Showed consistent improvements across diverse table reasoning tasks over text-only baselines and prior graph-based methods.

problem: RL training of multi-turn LLM agents is unstable and reasoning quality is hard to monitor because entropy metrics only measure within-input diversity.
approach: Identifies template collapse via mutual-information proxies and explains it through signal-to-noise ratio mechanisms, proposing SNR-Aware Filtering to prioritize high-variance prompts.
contribution: Consistently improved input dependence and task performance across planning, math, navigation, and code execution through monitoring and mitigating template collapse.

problem: Removing semantic watermarks from images requires balancing removal success, perceptual quality, and computational cost, but no approach achieves all three.
approach: DAWN is a lightweight training-free attack projecting watermarked images onto natural-image priors in frequency and semantic spaces with decoupled perceptual alignment.
contribution: Reduced detectability while preserving structural and semantic fidelity across diverse watermarking schemes with low computational cost.

problem: Public health reasoning at scale lacks structured machine learning formulations with sufficient supervised signals and appropriate evaluation.
approach: Introduces GlobalHealthAtlas dataset of 280,210 multilingual instances with LLM-assisted construction and domain-aligned evaluator assessing six dimensions.
contribution: Provided large-scale multilingual public health dataset with rigorous quality control and reproducible evaluation enabling safety-critical health reasoning research.

problem: Applying continuous diffusion to discrete data underperforms pure discrete formulations because Gaussian noise corrupts data through two mechanisms with different scales.
approach: CANDI introduces token identifiability framework and proposes hybrid approach that decouples discrete and continuous corruption for joint learning.
contribution: Enabled classifier-based guidance with off-the-shelf classifiers and outperformed masked diffusion on text at low NFE.

problem: Maximum entropy RL has performance bottlenecks from non-stationary Q-value estimation and short-sighted local entropy tuning without accounting for cumulative entropy.
approach: TECRL introduces reward-entropy separation to decouple value targets and trajectory entropy constraints to govern long-term stochasticity.
contribution: DSAC-E consistently outperformed baselines in cumulative returns and training stability across locomotion, manipulation, and vision-based driving tasks.

problem: Gaze perception models trained on one domain fail to generalize across domains because they miss underlying 3D geometry and motion dynamics.
approach: SG-Gaze learns Structurally and Geometrically Consistent representations via dual-branch adversarial learning with View-Consistent Regularization using synthetic perturbations.
contribution: Achieved state-of-the-art accuracy and strong generalization across 12 challenging cross-domain transfers through enforcing structural and geometric consistency.

problem: Understanding layer-wise reasoning dynamics in LLMs lacks a principled model-intrinsic signal that captures how reasoning intensity varies.
approach: Establishes formal link between reasoning intensity and L2 norm of hidden states using SAE diagnostics and introduces three test-time techniques guided by L2 norms.
contribution: Proved L2 norm bounds SAE reasoning feature activations and showed norm-based techniques significantly improve reasoning across architectures and benchmarks.

problem: Inferring unobserved mechanistic latent states from indirect observations is hard because classical methods don't scale and deep learning methods learn artificial states.
approach: GReinSS uses policy learning with dynamically rescaled rewards to maximize observed data likelihood and accurately reconstruct latent sets and graphs.
contribution: Accurately reconstructed simulated latent sets and RNA isoforms, outperforming VAE baselines and matching orthogonal sequencing better than RSEM.

problem: Activation steering methods often underperform prompt steering despite theoretical promise, making it unclear how to bridge the gap.
approach: PSR models learn to mimic prompt-steering interventions through position-specific steering coefficients trained to imitate prompt-based behavior.
contribution: Achieved performance close to or exceeding prompt steering while maintaining interpretability on persona steering and instruction following.

problem: Understanding bias mechanisms in observational studies remains challenging despite methods for detecting and mitigating biases.
approach: Shows that bias magnitude and nuisance function estimator performance correlation can distinguish among common bias sources.
contribution: Validated methodology through synthetic experiments and case studies, offering a framework for revealing bias mechanisms in observational studies.

problem: Discovering symbolic differential equations from observational data typically uses only quantitative metrics, missing domain knowledge and physical plausibility.
approach: DoLQ uses multi-agent architecture with LLM-based Scientist Agent conducting both qualitative and quantitative evaluations to guide symbolic regression.
contribution: Achieved superior performance in success rates and accurately recovering correct symbolic terms of ground-truth equations.

problem: Agentic LLM pipelines assume models evaluate outputs the same way they generate them, but this assumption may not hold leading to deployment failures.
approach: Proposes generator-evaluator self-consistency metric and tests it across 10 models on 491 concepts, examining relationship to mistakes in clinical settings.
contribution: Found substantial self-consistency variation and that higher consistency paradoxically links to greater vulnerability to mistakes.

problem: RL with combinatorial action spaces is challenging because feasible sets are exponentially large with complex constraints, making direct policy parameterization impractical.
approach: LSFlow learns a stochastic policy in latent space via spherical flow matching with a combinatorial solver delegating feasibility, using smoothed Bellman operator.
contribution: Outperformed state-of-the-art baselines by average 20.6% across combinatorial RL tasks while guaranteeing feasibility.

problem: Protein structure generation needs scalable approaches that learn true mechanistic distributions rather than artificial latent states.
approach: PAR uses multi-scale autoregressive generation with coarse-to-fine prediction and flow-based decoder, addressing exposure bias via noisy context learning.
contribution: Demonstrated strong zero-shot generalization for conditional generation and motif scaffolding, with favorable scaling behavior on unconditional benchmarks.

problem: LLM watermarking must balance robustness to edits and detectability, but the fundamental trade-offs governing these objectives remain unclear.
approach: Presents information-theoretic framework using KL divergence to capture trade-off between robustness and detectability, proposing hybrid strategy selecting Pareto-optimal schemes.
contribution: Established bounds on the trilemma among robustness, stealth, and reliable verification, with experimental validation on paraphrasing attacks.

problem: Reinforcement learning methods designed for autoregressive LLMs are not suitable for diffusion LLMs, which have fundamentally different generation mechanisms.
approach: Proposes Distribution Matching Policy Optimization (DMPO), which fine-tunes diffusion LLMs by matching their policy distribution to an optimal, reward-tilted distribution via cross-entropy optimization, with a novel weight baseline subtraction technique to handle small batch sizes.
contribution: Achieves 39.63 percentage-point improvement in accuracy over prior RL baselines and 67.97 percentage points over the base model on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Relational reasoning methods using convex coordinate-wise region-based embeddings lack clear characterization of their expressive limitations for capturing symbolic rules.
approach: Provides theoretical analysis of region-based embeddings, establishing both limitations and opportunities for pushing the expressivity of convex coordinate-wise models for relational reasoning.
contribution: Characterizes fundamental limitations of convex coordinate-wise models while showing there is still room to improve their expressivity for symbolic rule capture.

problem: Single monolithic models for fake image detection across multiple forensic subdomains consistently underperform compared to ensemble approaches due to artifact feature space collapse.
approach: Proposes SICA, which uses high-level semantics as a structural prior to reconstruct a unified-yet-discriminative artifact feature space, enabling the first practical monolithic detection paradigm.
contribution: Outperforms 15 state-of-the-art methods and reconstructs artifact feature space in near-orthogonal manner across the OpenMMSec dataset.

problem: Out-of-distribution generalization lacks theoretical understanding, particularly regarding lower bounds on generalization error under distribution shift.
approach: Establishes both lower and upper bounds on OOD generalization error from a statistical learning theory perspective, analyzing when simple empirical risk minimization over source domains is nearly optimal.
contribution: Shows that under RCS and empirical-RCS conditions, ERM can achieve nearly optimal error rates without knowledge of distributional parameters or domain discrepancy.

problem: Scaling introspection training for LLMs is limited by lack of ground-truth labels for what behaviors a model has learned.
approach: Trains LoRA introspection adapters by fine-tuning models with implanted behaviors to create labeled pairs, then transfers the adapter to audit other fine-tunes and the base model without retraining.
contribution: Successfully audits misaligned models and detects fine-tuning API attacks, with effectiveness increasing for larger models.

problem: Current machine-text detectors can be evaded by attacks that manipulate text while standard style-based defenses are believed to be universal against such attacks.
approach: Develops a paraphrasing attack that jointly optimizes for both undetectability and adherence to specific human writing styles, while showing multi-document analysis can still distinguish human and machine text.
contribution: Demonstrates that no single-document style defense is universal, as sophisticated attacks can evade all detectors, though distributional differences emerge with multiple documents.

problem: Generating conceptual engineering designs that satisfy physical constraints and optimize over both discrete topologies and continuous parameters is computationally expensive.
approach: Uses hierarchical diffusion models with Riemannian Diffusion Language Modeling for discrete topology sampling and masked diffusion for continuous parameter sampling conditioned on topology.
contribution: Rediscovers known physical laws in aircraft design while significantly accelerating design generation via simulation-based inference.

problem: Pre-trained image-to-3D models struggle with spatial fidelity in multi-instance generation, and fine-tuning approaches incur substantial training overhead.
approach: Proposes a training-free framework that leverages spatial priors in pre-trained models via instance-aware separation guidance during denoising and geometry-adaptive spatial stabilization.
contribution: Achieves better performance in global layout and local instances compared to multi-instance methods without requiring training.

problem: Existing concept erasing methods for text-to-image models excessively suppress unsafe concepts while damaging the model's ability to interpret safe semantics, reducing overall utility.
approach: Optimizes concept erasing reward using reinforcement learning with a safe adapter that regulates embeddings in cross-attention layers to achieve precise concept elimination.
contribution: Alleviates unsafe content generation while preserving benign image fidelity, with better robustness against red-teaming and effectiveness in image-to-image scenarios.

problem: Multimodal large language models require heavy post-hoc training to be converted into effective retrieval systems, limiting their practical deployment.
approach: Presents a training-free framework that extracts semantically grounded embeddings directly from MLLMs for candidate search, then uses their reasoning ability for precise reranking.
contribution: Substantially outperforms models trained on millions of retrieval pairs on MMEB and MMEB-V2 benchmarks while preserving generative abilities.

problem: Existing optimal transport methods for short text clustering neglect semantic consistency between samples, leading to inconsistent pseudo-labels for similar texts.
approach: Integrates instance-level attention mechanisms to capture semantic relationships into the optimal transport formulation, generating pseudo-labels that account for both local consistency and global structure.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods by generating reliable pseudo-labels that incorporate semantic awareness.

problem: Learning optimal contract parameters in hidden-action principal-agent settings suffers from exponential dependence on problem instance size, making online learning approaches impractical.
approach: Shows that assuming knowledge of possible agent actions while remaining unaware of which are actually available allows sublinear regret without exponential dependence on problem size.
contribution: Enables practical online learning algorithms for contract design by avoiding exponential scaling in problem instance size.

problem: KL regularization in alignment methods can cause LLMs to inherit biases from base policies that conflict with user preferences, reducing utility.
approach: Formulates reward model design as a Stackelberg game and proposes a simple reward shaping scheme that optimally balances KL regularization with user preference maximization.
contribution: Consistently improves average reward with win-tie rates exceeding 66% against baselines in inference-time alignment with minimal overhead.

problem: Heterogeneity in tactile sensor designs prevents learning unified tactile representations that generalize across different sensors in robotic applications.
approach: Proposes a two-stage framework using cross-sensor modulators to eliminate sensor biases, synthetic data for cross-sensor self-supervised learning, and real data for sim-to-real semantic alignment.
contribution: Demonstrates strong multi-sensor generalization and significantly improves sensor-agnostic representation learning.

problem: Real-world execution environments contain common corruptions like pop-ups and resolution changes that severely degrade MLLM-based agent performance, but robustness is not evaluated.
approach: Introduces a benchmark with 9 configurable common corruptions and proposes AgentHijack-Agent framework combining enhanced grounding with behavior summarization for robust execution.
contribution: Reveals fragility of current agents to minor corruptions and demonstrates effectiveness of robustness-aware approach.

problem: Certified machine unlearning requires prohibitive noise levels that destroy model utility, especially for large-scale deletion requests.
approach: Proposes Asymmetric Langevin Unlearning that leverages public data to suppress unlearning cost, enabling distribution mismatch analysis and mass unlearning scenarios.
contribution: Achieves strict computational advantage over retraining while maintaining utility under reasonable distribution shifts through public data injection.

problem: Determining mixture order and estimating parameters from limited moment information is challenging, especially in high dimensions.
approach: Introduces a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations for approximating target measures by parametric mixtures, with finite convergence under rank conditions.
contribution: Provides both the number of clusters and strong initialization for clustering algorithms, with asymptotic convergence guarantees.

problem: Code generation methods that verify solutions against sparse public test cases suffer from pseudo-correctness, where solutions pass visible tests but fail hidden ones.
approach: Proposes adversarial Monte Carlo tree search where a solver generates code and an attacker evolves targeted test cases to exploit logical gaps, creating a dynamic filter.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines by reducing false positive rates and forcing generalization beyond initial test constraints.

problem: Speculative decoding under sampling (temperature > 0) shows worse speedups than greedy decoding because verification rules over-reject low-risk drafts.
approach: Proposes ARC-Decode with risk-bounded acceptance using Jensen-Shannon divergence to identify drafts that preserve target model distributions while maintaining tractability.
contribution: Achieves up to 1.6x end-to-end speedup over EAGLE-3 under sampling with negligible quality degradation.

problem: Preference optimization methods like DPO treat all annotated pairs equally, forcing models to overfit to inconsistent human feedback rather than learning robust preferences.
approach: Estimates annotator reliability and infers latent ground truth from noisy feedback, then uses reliability-aware consistency optimization to prioritize high-consensus signals.
contribution: Reduces overfitting to inconsistent supervision and achieves superior performance compared to RLHF baselines.

problem: Continuous knowledge updating for pre-trained LLMs is challenging, and parametric approaches like LoRA lack fundamental characterization of capacity and composability.
approach: Provides the first systematic empirical study mapping the design space of LoRA-based memory, from storage capacity to long-context reasoning and multi-module scaling.
contribution: Positions LoRA as a complementary memory axis alongside RAG and ICL with distinct practical advantages.

problem: Current benchmarks overlook agents' ability to orchestrate domain-specific tools for complex scientific workflows, and state-of-the-art models struggle with extended interactions.
approach: Introduces SciAgentGym with 1,780 domain-specific tools and SciAgentBench for tiered evaluation, plus SciForge data synthesis that models tool dependencies as a graph to generate logic-aware trajectories.
contribution: Demonstrates that fine-tuned SciAgent-8B outperforms Qwen3-VL-235B-Instruct with positive cross-domain transfer of scientific tool-use capabilities.

problem: Evaluating algorithm discovery systems is limited by existing task suites that are contaminated, saturated, or too simple to reflect real algorithm development challenges.
approach: Introduces DiscoGen, a procedural generator that creates billions of algorithm discovery tasks spanning multiple machine learning fields, with DiscoBench for principled evaluation.
contribution: Enables large-scale optimization of algorithm discovery agents and exposes failure modes invisible at toy scale.

problem: Key-value cache memory demands limit LLM inference efficiency, and existing eviction heuristics rely on indirect proxies for token utility without theoretical grounding.
approach: Reframes KV cache eviction as an RL problem with lightweight per-head agents trained on generation traces to predict future token utility without LLM modifications.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on long-context benchmarks (up to 128K tokens) with zero-shot generalization to longer sequences.

problem: Existing snapshot compressive imaging methods are restricted to discrete spectral outputs, preventing continuous spectral reconstruction and super-resolution.
approach: Synergizes deep unfolding networks with implicit neural representations, using continuous spectral fields to generate spectral intensities at arbitrary wavelengths.
contribution: Achieves continuous spectral modeling at arbitrary resolutions while outperforming state-of-the-art in reconstruction fidelity and spectral preservation.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering under heavy missingness and view imbalance leads to unreliable cross-view correspondences and poor semantic convergence.
approach: Proposes MAGIC with masked multi-path contrastive learning for calibrated cluster semantics before reconstruction, using confidence-gated semantic transfer with geometry-preserving fallback.
contribution: Shows consistent gains over prior methods across benchmarks with different missing ratios through masked consensus and confidence-aware imputation.

problem: Cross-domain anomaly detection in logs faces challenges with geometric proximity alone being insufficient for normality and distribution alignment causing negative transfer.
approach: Uses shared-private prototype systems to disentangle cross-domain patterns, applies domain-conditioned flow matching for anomaly detection, and performs prototype-drift-driven hard example mining.
contribution: Delivers substantial gains on HDFS, BGL, Thunderbird, and Spirit datasets under multi-domain joint training.

problem: Translating natural language requirements into optimization formulations is labor-intensive, and evaluation is dominated by toy benchmarks that hide industrial-scale challenges.
approach: Constructs MIPLIB-NL through structure-aware reverse engineering of real mixed-integer programs, with iterative validation via expert review and human-LLM interaction.
contribution: Provides 223 industrial-scale benchmarks revealing substantial performance degradation in systems that perform well on existing benchmarks.

problem: Sampling from bounded-support distributions via reflective HMC lacks non-asymptotic mixing-time bounds and relies on restrictive convexity assumptions.
approach: Proposes a convex-container plus thinning framework applicable to arbitrary bounded-support densities, establishing first non-asymptotic total-variation mixing bounds.
contribution: Achieves polynomial dimension dependence O(d^2) for smooth targets, with sharper bounds under strong convexity, and improves sampling on Stiefel manifolds.

problem: Local self-supervised learning algorithms struggle to match performance of global backpropagation-based SSL, and the theoretical connection between them is unclear.
approach: Develops theory for linear networks showing conditions when local-SSL implements global BP-SSL weight updates, then extends with variants for nonlinear networks.
contribution: Best local-SSL with CLAPP loss matches comparable BP-SSL performance and improves state-of-the-art layer-wise SSL on multiple image datasets.

problem: State-of-the-art multi-class unsupervised anomaly detection requires task-specific training which is costly under distribution shifts and faces a fidelity-stability tradeoff.
approach: Proposes Retrieval-based Anomaly Detection that stores anomaly-free features and detects anomalies through multi-level retrieval matching without task-specific training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks including 96.7% Pixel AUROC on MVTec-AD with just a single anomaly-free image.

problem: Knowledge distillation designed for supervised learning suffers from distribution mismatch and objective interference when combined with RL, requiring careful loss balancing.
approach: Proposes RL-aware distillation with Trust Region Ratio Distillation, using PPO-style likelihood-ratio objectives to guide students toward teachers only when improving policy updates.
contribution: Consistently outperforms offline distillation, standard GRPO, and KL-based on-policy baselines on logic reasoning and math benchmarks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs fine-tuned via FTaaS face backdoor risks from poisoned data, and existing defenses fail to generalize across diverse trigger types and modalities.
approach: Uncovers universal backdoor fingerprint in attention allocation divergence and proposes TCAP using Gaussian Mixture Models to identify trigger-responsive attention heads.
contribution: Achieves consistently strong unsupervised backdoor detection performance across diverse MLLM architectures and attack methods.

problem: Incomplete multimodal learning under training-time missing modalities is challenging as it prevents reliance on complete data for reconstruction or cross-modal priors.
approach: Reformulates as sequence reasoning task using LLMs for prompt-guided context-aware imputation and multidimensional fusion, with mask-aware dual-path aggregation to calibrate uncertainty.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on Action Quality Assessment datasets without complete training data.

problem: Efficient retrieval requires balancing computational cost of exact relevance models against quality loss from approximate nearest neighbor search.
approach: Describes queries and items by their relevance to support sets to obtain embeddings, theoretically proving they can approximate complex similarity models.
contribution: Demonstrates power of relevance-based embeddings on diverse academic and production datasets for improved candidate retrieval.

problem: Clustered federated learning requires identifying client clusters based on data distribution, but client assignments are unknown and algorithms often require near-optimal initialization.
approach: Proposes CLoVE that embeds clients using model losses and clusters them via patterns in loss values, enabling iterative cluster identification and cluster-specific optimization.
contribution: Achieves accurate cluster recovery with high probability and exponentially fast convergence with applicability to supervised and unsupervised settings.

problem: Explanation consistency in time series classifiers is treated as evidence of robustness, but predictions and explanations can be adversarially decoupled.
approach: Proposes TSEF, a dual-target attack that jointly manipulates classifier and explainer outputs to achieve targeted misclassification while keeping explanations consistent.
contribution: Reveals that explanation stability is a misleading proxy for robustness, motivating coupling-aware robustness evaluation.

problem: Retrieval agents for scientific research fail to understand complex relational networks among papers, such as corroborating/conflicting studies and technological lineages.
approach: Introduces SciNet dataset with 8,940 tasks across three relational understanding levels: ego-centric retrieval, pairwise relationships, and scientific evolution paths.
contribution: Shows current retrieval agents achieve below 20% accuracy on relation-aware tasks, while agents with SciNet achieve 25.3% improvement in downstream review quality.

problem: Compositional entropic risk objectives suffer from non-convergence, numerical instability, and slow convergence when applied to problems with expensive loss functions.
approach: Proposes SCENT using stochastic proximal mirror descent on the dual formulation with Bregman divergence from negative exponential functions to capture geometry.
contribution: Achieves O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate for convex problems with demonstrated effectiveness on extreme classification, AUC maximization, and robust optimization.

problem: Real-world networks have heterogeneous communication delays, making node assignment optimization crucial for minimizing bottleneck communication delay in decentralized learning.
approach: Proposes BTSP-MSR that bounds bottleneck communication delay on circulant digraphs by combining ring-graph BCD and deviation terms, solving sequentially.
contribution: Consistently reduces bottleneck communication delay across circulant digraphs with large node counts under heterogeneous delay settings.

problem: Maximum inner product search over large databases is computationally expensive, requiring fast lookup of database vectors most similar to a query.
approach: Train neural networks to directly predict MIPS solutions by learning the convex value function using Input Convex Neural Networks (ICNNs) or VectorICNNs, amortizing the cost across a query distribution.
contribution: Demonstrates that convexity provides an effective inductive bias, achieving high match rates with only a single forward pass at inference.

problem: Molecular representation learning fails to generalize out-of-distribution when training data covers only limited chemical space and models rely on environment-dependent factors.
approach: Propose MoSIR framework that decomposes molecular embeddings into semantic invariant and environment-sensitive components via prototype constraint and bi-level min-max optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on molecular OOD benchmarks across diverse distribution shifts.

problem: De novo ligand design lacks flexibility in modeling real docking interactions, relies on pseudo objectives rather than true de novo generation, and cannot generate diverse ligand types.
approach: Introduce MagicDock framework using gradient inversion where reverse gradients from binding prediction guide ligand generation, with differentiable 3D point-cloud representations capturing docking details.
contribution: Achieves average improvements across 9 scenarios with theoretical guarantees.

problem: Audio foundation models struggle to process complex multi-source acoustic scenes with multiple speakers and background/foreground sound effects.
approach: AudioChat framework uses LLM-based tool-calling agents to simulate user-system interactions for training data, with Audio Transfusion Forcing objective for structured reasoning and interactive multi-turn understanding.
contribution: Enables unified generation, editing, and understanding of audio stories with three new metrics measuring task performance.

problem: Federated class-incremental learning must balance exemplar effectiveness with privacy while learning new classes without forgetting old ones in distributed settings.
approach: Propose CLIF method using cross-view Lewis weight fusion to compute importance scores from multiple feature perspectives and frequency-based weighted training.
contribution: Consistently improves baselines by 1-6% with theoretical guarantees for soundness.

problem: Graph contrastive learning with artificial perturbations diverges from biological reality when applied to gene regulatory networks, and most methods avoid structural changes entirely.
approach: Propose SupGCL that incorporates biological perturbations from gene knockdown experiments as explicit supervision, linking artificial augmentations with real perturbations.
contribution: Yields clearer disease-subtype structure and improves clustering on patient-derived GRNs from three cancer types.

problem: Traditional TDDE solvers require time discretization, forcing a latency-accuracy trade-off where high fidelity requires prohibitive runtime.
approach: Introduce DS-TS using Dynamical System Machines with excitatory-inhibitory coupling, state-aware nonlinearity, and hierarchical temporal integration for continuous physical evolution.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity solutions with ~10³× speed and ~10⁵× energy efficiency improvements over baseline solvers.

problem: Static fine-tuning of foundation models like SAM2 imposes rigid structural constraints, limiting adaptability to varying complexity in specialized downstream tasks.
approach: Propose ACO-MoE-LoRA combining Ant Colony Optimization with mixture-of-experts to dynamically evolve expert selection and LoRA ranks during training via pheromone-guided routing.
contribution: Consistently outperforms static adapters on 16 datasets while addressing local optimality limitations of recent dynamic heuristics.

problem: Training-free video anomaly detection suffers from computational inefficiency due to complex memory retrieval or high-latency visual-language models.
approach: Propose PRISM framework using differential amplification and whitening mechanisms to suppress common-mode background noise in embedding space from pre-trained multimodal models.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods with real-time inference capability.
