problem: Masked diffusion language models require expensive iterative denoising by repeatedly processing the entire sequence at every step.
approach: Propose DyLLM that selectively computes only salient tokens by identifying them via cosine similarity of attention contexts, reusing cached activations for other tokens.
contribution: Achieves up to 9.6× higher throughput while preserving baseline accuracy across reasoning and code-generation benchmarks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for GUI automation fail on real-world desktop environments with multi-window stacking, occlusion, and visual clutter due to training on idealized interfaces.
approach: Introduce WinDeskGround benchmark that parametrically generates complex desktop scenarios by controlling window occlusion, layout density, and semantic similarity.
contribution: Evaluates five leading MLLMs on 1,356 instruction-target pairs, showing accuracy declines under partial occlusion.

problem: Existing formal theorem proving approaches rely on task-specific pipelines and trained models, limiting flexibility and reproducibility for diverse mathematical reasoning tasks.
approach: Propose using a general coding agent as a formal math reasoner, combining Claude Code with Numina-Lean-MCP for autonomous Lean interaction and theorem retrieval.
contribution: Solves all problems in Putnam 2025 (12/12) and successfully formalizes the Brascamp-Lieb theorem.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle with few-shot imitation learning and fail to reason about long-horizon tasks with limited demonstrations.
approach: Introduce FOCA framework combining explicit prediction of task-grounded future interaction embeddings with implicit alignment to goal observations.
contribution: Achieves 95.7% success with 20 demonstrations on LIBERO, 7-12% improvement on RoboCasa, and up to 26% gains on real robots.

problem: Editing autonomous driving logs requires simultaneously modifying objects and ego-trajectories while maintaining physical plausibility, creating a dilemma between generative flexibility and precise control.
approach: Introduce SceneDirector using LiDAR-guided depth completion to construct geometric scaffolds and static texture banks, with mask-gated reference attention balancing geometry and appearance.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art in both controllability and visual quality.

problem: Multi-hop question answering must handle both parallel fact-verification and chained reasoning with complementary requirements, yet existing methods excel at only one.
approach: Propose DTKG framework inspired by cognitive science that dynamically categorizes questions then applies tailored reasoning paths for parallel or chained inference.
contribution: Achieves 5.0%-29.5% performance improvement on six datasets.

problem: Learning-based combinatorial optimization requires supervision or expensive gradients while classical approximation algorithms provide guarantees but cannot adapt to input distributions.
approach: Propose fully differentiable MPNN incorporating approximation-algorithmic principles for Uniform Facility Location without solver supervision or discrete relaxations.
contribution: Has provable approximation guarantees and empirically improves on standard approximation algorithms.

problem: Optimizing maintenance strategies for large-scale infrastructure requires offline constrained RL under hard budgetary limits without dangerous exploration, but existing benchmarks lack distributional shift and realistic constraints.
approach: Introduce InfraRL benchmark from U.S. National Bridge Inventory defining offline maintenance strategy optimization under hard budgetary constraints.
contribution: Benchmarks diverse approaches revealing critical trade-offs between safety and long-term efficiency.

problem: Solving discounted MDPs efficiently requires balancing sample complexity without knowing prediction error quality when using external predictions of transitions.
approach: Propose algorithm leveraging predictions of transition matrix without requiring knowledge of prediction error using minimax optimization techniques.
contribution: Achieves sample complexity uniformly better than O((1-γ)^-4 N ε^-2), improving upon prior results despite not accessing prediction quality.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering with partial observations relies on weak cross-view signals and overlooks stable neighborhood structures, leading to unstable latent recovery.
approach: Propose IMVC-NCD using neighborhood-conditioned diffusion that aggregates stable local neighborhood structures while encoding missingness states for reliable guidance.
contribution: Produces semantically aligned and view-consistent representations robust to high missing-view ratios.

problem: Existing software agents trained on human-curated data face a fundamental barrier to superintelligence due to limited training data and lack of autonomous learning experiences.
approach: Propose Self-play SWE-RL requiring only sandboxed repositories where LLM agents inject and repair increasingly complex bugs via RL in self-play setting.
contribution: Achieves +10.4 and +7.8 point self-improvement on SWE-bench benchmarks, generalizing to unseen bug descriptions.

problem: Semi-supervised learning must seamlessly integrate paired and unpaired data, but existing approaches rely on heuristics rather than principled likelihood-based frameworks.
approach: Propose learning paradigm integrating paired and unpaired data via likelihood maximization that connects to inverse entropic optimal transport.
contribution: Demonstrates universal approximation property and effectively learns conditional distributions using combined data.

problem: Repository-level performance optimization demands expertise in reasoning about code semantics and software engineering to reduce runtime while preserving correctness, but benchmarks emphasize what to fix not how.
approach: Introduce SWE-fficiency benchmark with 498 tasks on real codebases where agents investigate code semantics, localize bottlenecks, and produce performance-improving patches.
contribution: Reveals top agents achieve less than 0.23× expert speedup, struggling with optimization localization and multi-function reasoning.

problem: Tokenization remains a hardcoded compression step in LLM pipelines despite the trend toward end-to-end architectures, and existing learnable approaches use weak continuous approximations.
approach: Show token boundaries can be learned using score function estimates from reinforcement learning that directly optimize discrete boundary drawing with techniques like time discounting.
contribution: Outperforms straight-through estimates both qualitatively and quantitatively at 100 million parameter scale.

problem: Most video generation models synthesize scenes holistically and lack mechanisms for explicit compositional manipulation and spatiotemporal control of individual elements.
approach: Propose HECTOR enabling hybrid reference conditioning from static images and/or dynamic videos with explicit trajectory specification for location, scale, and speed.
contribution: Achieves superior visual quality, stronger reference preservation, and improved motion controllability.

problem: Large vision-language models exhibit language bias where they over-rely on text while neglecting visual inputs, leading to hallucination rooted in modality misalignment during training.
approach: Propose Language Bias Regularization during instruction tuning and Language Bias Penalty in DPO training to penalize language bias without additional data.
contribution: Consistently improves on ten general benchmarks and reduces hallucination across diverse models.

problem: Long-sequence reasoning in LLMs creates severe KV cache memory bottlenecks, and existing compression methods fail due to rotating queries in RoPE making representative selection difficult.
approach: Propose TriAttention leveraging Q/K vector concentration in pre-RoPE space via trigonometric series to estimate key importance and score keys by position preference.
contribution: On AIME25 with 32K-token generation, matches full attention accuracy with 2.5× throughput or 10.7× KV memory reduction.

problem: Continuous diffusion for categorical data lacks understanding of which tokenization schemes work best for the framework.
approach: Study latent space structure using Kullback-Leibler divergence on diffusion paths and analyze token prediction accuracy, proving FSQ tokenization is optimal.
contribution: Text-to-speech diffusion with FSQ tokens outperforms LLM-based counterparts while being significantly smaller and faster.

problem: Estimating the forest matrix of signed graphs is computationally expensive as existing algorithms designed for unsigned graphs are difficult to extend.
approach: Propose GSCF algorithm based on loop-erased random walks to generate generalized spanning converging forests in O(n) expected time.
contribution: Achieves high estimation accuracy with O(ln) sampling algorithms, scales to graphs with over twenty million nodes.

problem: Code reasoning methods supervise only final outputs and ignore intermediate execution states, leading to reward hacking with inconsistent reasoning.
approach: Introduce StepCodeReasoner with structured print-based execution-trace anchors and Dual-Granularity GRPO for credit assignment at inter-trajectory and intra-trajectory levels.
contribution: 7B model achieves 91.1% on CRUXEval, 86.5% on LiveCodeBench, outperforming CodeReasoner-7B and GPT-4o.

problem: Reasoning video object segmentation limited to fixed initial inputs lacks capacity to actively acquire further visual evidence, essential for resolving complex references in long videos.
approach: Propose VideoSEG-O3 using multi-turn RL framework with temporal-spatial chain-of-thought, SEG-aware logit calibration, and decoupled thinking traces.
contribution: Achieves advanced performance across 8 benchmarks, excelling in long-horizon and complex reasoning tasks.

problem: Existing benchmarks for causal machine learning rely on hand-crafted datasets, leading to brittle and non-generalizable conclusions about method performance.
approach: Introduce CausalProfiler, a synthetic benchmark generator that randomly samples causal models, data, queries, and ground truths based on explicit design choices.
contribution: Provides first random generator of synthetic causal benchmarks with coverage guarantees across observation, intervention, and counterfactual reasoning levels.

problem: Transformers must handle multiple generative processes, but how a single model organizes multiple conflicting world models remains unclear.
approach: Introduce MetaOthello suite of Othello-like games with shared syntax but different rules trained on mixed-variant data to study world model organization.
contribution: Shows transformers learn shared world-state representations, resolve ambiguity through localized mechanisms, and structure representations abstractly beyond surface form.

problem: Federated LoRA methods adopt uniform aggregation breaking under encoder-decoder asymmetry in medical segmentation where encoder handles appearance shifts and decoder handles supervision variations.
approach: Propose Inverse Asymmetric Tuning personalizing module-specific components while retaining shared pathways, with Subspace Orthogonality Regularizer preventing leakage.
contribution: Consistent improvements over federated LoRA and parameter-efficient baselines.

problem: Repository-level code editing requires understanding complex dependencies across large codebases, but existing approaches rely heavily on complex agent scaffolding.
approach: Propose Clean-PR paradigm using GitHub pull requests as training signal, converting noisy diffs into search/replace blocks via reconstruction and validation.
contribution: Achieves 13.6% absolute improvement on SWE-bench Lite and 12.3% on SWE-bench Verified through agentless supervised fine-tuning.

problem: Survival prediction ignores censoring contributions, potentially discarding useful signals when event and censoring processes are coupled.
approach: Introduce latent decomposition learning event-specific, censoring-specific, confounding, and irrelevant information to guide representation learning.
contribution: Consistent gains over baselines on 10 datasets (2 semi-synthetic, 8 real-world) across 4 popular deep-learning survival models.

problem: Active learning for inferring time-dependent vector fields from Lagrangian observer placements typically follows ad-hoc strategies, lacking principled placement guidance.
approach: Introduce BALLAST combining Bayesian active learning with physics-informed Gaussian process surrogate models and look-ahead amendment for sea-drifter trajectories.
contribution: Demonstrates notable benefits of sequential observer placement on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

problem: Model markets with competing providers and customers have profit opportunities through intelligent arbitrage when capabilities and costs vary.
approach: Conduct empirical study of arbitrage strategies allocating inference budget across providers to undercut market prices.
contribution: Demonstrates simple arbitrage generates net profit margins up to 40% on SWE-bench, with implications for model development and market dynamics.

problem: Existing pluralistic value alignment methods treat value representations as entangled, limiting fine-grained controllability when modifying individual values.
approach: Propose DisAlign framework using information-geometric perspective to decompose representations into consensus and value-specific components via spectral decomposition.
contribution: Consistently improves value disentanglement and achieves more accurate pluralistic value control.

problem: Ad-hoc teamwork requires robust agents that adapt to novel partners without pre-training, but existing methods rely on expensive partner populations.
approach: Introduce UPD generating training partners on-the-fly and selecting adaptively based on learnability criterion without pre-trained populations.
contribution: Consistently achieves strong performance across Level-Based Foraging and Overcooked environments with higher returns and better human-like behavior than baselines.

problem: Diffusion models require Gaussian noise and iterative sampling with latency-accuracy trade-offs, and non-Markovian star-shaped processes lose temporal coherence.
approach: Propose learning Markovian projection of star-shaped forward process enabling learning over broad exponential models, particularly for knowledge distillation.
contribution: Enables few-step or single-step generation while maintaining flexibility across multiple generative tasks.

problem: Learning complex, subjective safety constraints from human feedback in reinforcement learning is data-inefficient because humans can only provide limited expert demonstrations.
approach: PbCRL uses preference learning with a novel dead-zone mechanism to capture heavy-tailed safety cost distributions, combined with SNR loss for exploration and two-stage training to reduce online labeling burden.
contribution: Achieves superior alignment with true safety requirements and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on safety and reward metrics.

problem: Large language models lack efficient post-training methods to improve reasoning abilities without extensive supervised data.
approach: One-shot Entropy Minimization applies entropy minimization over a single unlabeled example with ~10 gradient steps, inducing a right-skewed logit shift that amplifies high-probability tokens.
contribution: Substantially improves reasoning across mathematical, logical, and coding domains as a fully unsupervised post-training approach.

problem: LLMs exhibit belief drift in multiple-choice question answering, violating the martingale property required for coherent Bayesian inference.
approach: Prompted Predictive Resampling (PPR) generates repeated answers to the same question to expose belief drift; uses seed-answer prompting and self-consistency fine-tuning loss to accelerate stabilization.
contribution: Substantially reduces belief drift and improves predictive coherence on multiple-choice QA benchmarks without sacrificing accuracy.

problem: Large language models perform arithmetic poorly, indicating a disconnect between internal neural representations and discrete outputs.
approach: Identifies Iso-Raw-Sum Trajectory (IRST) manifold geometry and proposes Noisy Quantization Model framing arithmetic errors as topological slippages of continuous carry potential across quantization thresholds.
contribution: Provides geometric framework explaining arithmetic failures and enables geometric consistency checks that detect and correct quantization errors during inference.

problem: LLM backdoor attacks fail to persist when users perform supervised fine-tuning because poisoning creates a narrow, sharp basin vulnerable to parameter drift.
approach: BAD-BOOM uses broader smoothness minimization with Fisher-induced ellipsoidal constraint to allocate larger perturbation budgets to backdoor-sensitive parameters, widening the backdoor basin.
contribution: Consistently preserves high attack success rate across multiple LLMs and SFT scenarios while maintaining competitive utility.

problem: Softmax attention diffuses probability mass to irrelevant tokens at long sequence lengths, and lowering temperature to sharpen focus causes vanishing gradients.
approach: LUCID Attention applies a preconditioner derived from exponentiated key-key similarities that minimizes key overlap in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space, enabling focused retrieval without temperature lowering.
contribution: Achieves up to 18% improvement on BABILong and 14% on RULER long-context retrieval tasks with same computational complexity as standard attention.

problem: Vision-Language Model prompt learning neglects spectral (frequency) granularity of visual signals, focusing only on text optimization while treating visual encoders as frozen holistic extractors.
approach: SpecPL decomposes visual signals via VAE into semantic low-frequency bands and granular high-frequency details; uses counterfactual granule training by permuting high-frequency signals to enforce visual-semantic distinction.
contribution: Achieves 81.51% harmonic-mean accuracy as a universal plug-and-play booster for text-oriented baselines on 11 benchmarks.

problem: Adapting frozen MLLMs for dense retrieval while preserving pre-trained semantic space is challenging because invasive parameter updates may impair reasoning capability.
approach: SLQ uses Shared Latent Queries appended to both text and image tokens, leveraging native causal attention to aggregate multimodal context into unified embedding; constructs KARR-Bench for knowledge-aware reasoning retrieval.
contribution: Outperforms full fine-tuning and LoRA on COCO and Flickr30K while achieving substantial gains on knowledge-aware retrieval.

problem: Existing multilingual policy optimization restricts each training question to a single response language or uses fixed dominant-language supervision, limiting diversity of training signals.
approach: Language-Routed Policy Optimization (LRPO) treats language as selectable variable, eliciting multilingual rollouts and using multi-armed bandit language router to adaptively balance exploration-exploitation of language quality.
contribution: Consistently improves multilingual performance by enabling adaptive language routing for cross-lingual knowledge exploitation.

problem: While frozen self-supervised representations transfer well with few labels within tasks, understanding why they generalize across many tasks without interference remains unclear.
approach: Shows that directional CDNV (decision-axis variance) controls both few-shot transfer and multitask interference; proves sharp non-asymptotic generalization bounds and links decision-axis collapse to orthogonal task geometry.
contribution: Provides geometric explanation for few-shot transfer in self-supervised learning with bounds that track practical few-shot error.

problem: Existing exam-style benchmarks focus on understanding and reasoning rather than rigorous drawing tasks, lacking precise evaluation of semantic correctness and visual plausibility in image generation.
approach: GenExam introduces 1,000 samples across 10 subjects with four-level taxonomy, each with ground-truth images and fine-grained scoring points evaluating semantic correctness and visual plausibility.
contribution: Reveals large gap between open-source and closed-source models, providing rigorous assessment of integrated understanding, reasoning, and generation.

problem: LLMs excel at one-on-one instruction but struggle with one-to-many alignment (e.g., clinical ward rounds) due to context dilution and goal misalignment across diverse trainees.
approach: ClinTutor-R1 is a multimodal agent with explicit internal thinking mechanism modeling individual belief states and group consensus, trained via multi-agent pedagogical simulator (ClinEdu) and large-scale Socratic dialogue dataset (ClinTeach).
contribution: Outperforms base models by over 20% and achieves parity with reasoning models while maintaining scalability across expanding cohorts.

problem: Data-free compression methods like NF4 suffer functional collapse below 4 bits, while data-dependent methods require calibration data and extensive training.
approach: EntQuant decouples numerical precision from storage cost via entropy coding, compressing a 70B model in under 10 minutes using only quantization without recovery training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and instruction-tuned models while retaining functional performance at modest inference overhead.

problem: Diffusion models produce highly curved trajectories and noisy score targets due to memoryless forward process with independent data-noise coupling.
approach: Adjoint Schrödinger Bridge Matching (ASBM) recovers optimal trajectories by viewing SB forward dynamic as coupling construction and learning backward generative dynamic with matching loss supervised by induced optimal coupling.
contribution: Produces significantly straighter and more efficient sampling paths with improved stability, scaling to high-dimensional image generation with fewer steps.

problem: Large language models reveal and amplify societal biases during chain-of-thought generation, yet existing mitigation methods require retraining or auxiliary systems.
approach: COFT applies training-free token-level fairness control at decode time: creates masked counterfactual prompt, applies logit fusion to attenuate attribute-driven biases, and uses conformal calibration for candidate token set certification.
contribution: Reduces bias metrics by 30-55% (median 38%) while preserving task utility, language quality, and reasoning accuracy with <11% computational overhead.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models exhibit large discontinuities in accuracy-compute trade-offs because once selected, experts execute fully without width variation.
approach: MoSE introduces nested, slimmable expert structure enabling variable-width execution; combines multi-width training with standard MoE objectives and uses lightweight test-time training to map router confidence to expert widths.
contribution: Matches or improves standard MoE at full width and shifts compute-quality frontier toward lower inference FLOPs with continuous accuracy-compute spectrum.

problem: Subgoal-based policy tree search requires explicit subgoal generation incurring substantial overhead, limiting scalability to complex environments.
approach: Uses learned rerooter through √LTS algorithm that implicitly decomposes problems into soft subtasks; proposes three rerooter designs: clustering-based (exploiting global structure), heuristic-based (leveraging cost-to-go), and hybrid.
contribution: Scales to complex environments where explicit subgoal methods fail while achieving state-of-the-art online training efficiency.

problem: As LLMs act as autonomous agents with tool access in sandboxed environments, evaluating their capacity to escape these sandboxes is critical for security assurance.
approach: SandboxEscapeBench is a CTF-style benchmark with nested sandbox architecture covering misconfiguration, privilege errors, kernel flaws, and runtime/orchestration weaknesses.
contribution: Shows LLMs can identify and exploit sandbox vulnerabilities when present, demonstrating need for rigorous evaluation to ensure sandboxing remains effective.

problem: Large multimodal models lack explicit taxonomic knowledge, leading to poor hierarchical visual recognition consistency despite strong general capabilities.
approach: HiR² introduces hierarchical representation regularization combining taxonomic entailment loss (via hyperbolic cones) and discriminative dispersive loss (angular separation on unit sphere) for semantic-aware visual tree extraction.
contribution: Effectively captures taxonomic structures across diverse LMMs and fine-tuning methods, improving hierarchical consistency.

problem: Graph generative models struggle to scale to large, complex structures while maintaining node and edge feature generation for real-world applications.
approach: FAHNES is a hierarchical framework generating topology and features jointly via node coarsening and localized expansion, guided by hierarchical scale encoding for cross-scale consistency.
contribution: Achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance while uniquely scaling to featured large-scale graphs and hypergraphs.

problem: Value factorization in MARL relies on static coordination assumptions that hinder generalization on long-horizon tasks with shifting inter-agent dependencies.
approach: TACTIC combines VQ-VAE trajectory abstraction for discrete task classes, semantic-conditioned sparse coordination graphs that prune edges by variance-based payoff sensitivity, and frozen trajectory-class predictor.
contribution: Shows strong competitiveness with adaptive coordination under sparse rewards and dynamic task structures on SMAC and SUMO.

problem: Existing lipid-binding protein predictors use fully supervised training treating unlabeled samples as negatives, creating systematic false negatives due to missing evidence.
approach: LipoPU formulates lipid-binding learning as ranking-based positive-unlabeled objective at pocket level, using attention-based representations robust to ambiguous pocket definitions.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains over supervised baselines and identifies biologically informative residues via structural case studies.

problem: Traditional image forgery localization methods depend on physical noise absent in synthetic data, failing against realistic AI-generated forgeries.
approach: FLAME theoretically demonstrates diffusion inherently suppresses local high-frequency variance creating energy gaps; uses LAD map to capture anomalies with parameter-efficient SAM adapter; introduces EditStream for continuous synthetic data generation.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art results on AI-generated forgery datasets while generalizing to unseen generative architectures.

problem: Constrained optimization algorithms struggle with difficult-to-project constraints and lack adaptive step-size schemes for parameter-free performance.
approach: Uses randomized feasibility algorithm with Polyak steps and adaptive sampling of constraints per iteration; decouples constraint satisfaction from objective minimization.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence in expectation for strongly convex objectives and O(1/√T) rate for nonsmooth objectives with problem parameter-free adaptive stepsizes.

problem: Obtaining simultaneous confidence bounds for aggregated effects over data-selected subsets requires computationally intractable nonlinear combinatorial optimization.
approach: Casts weighted densest-subgraph problem as exact linear and mixed integer linear programs; develops fully polynomial-time approximation scheme exploiting rank-1 structure.
contribution: Establishes finite-sample coverage guarantee with lighter subset-family dependence than classical methods and demonstrates scalability on synthetic and ML applications.

problem: Code generation models hallucinate, producing functionally incorrect code that hinders deployment in safety-critical systems due to difficulty identifying correctness without test suites.
approach: Automatically generates unit tests via dynamic code analysis; proposes selective generator that abstains from uncertain generations based on functional correctness; uses generated tests in both learning and evaluation.
contribution: Theoretically controls false discovery rate among non-abstained answers while enabling precise code evaluation and functional correctness verification.

problem: DNA language models depend critically on tokenization strategy, yet fixed tokenizations are brittle under shifts, indels, and local repeats because DNA lacks canonical boundaries.
approach: DNAChunker introduces learnable adaptive segmentation module producing context-dependent, variable-length units; learns to allocate finer granularity to enriched regions while compressing repetitive sequences.
contribution: Consistently improves over fixed-tokenization baselines on five benchmarks with learned segmentation that is mutation-resilient and biologically-informed.

problem: Existing representational similarity metrics lack rigorous theoretical grounding linking functional and representational similarity across dimensions.
approach: Unifies three dimensions through usable information framework: establishes formal link between stitching and conditional mutual information; reveals similarity is relative to predictive family capacity; shows representational similarity is sufficient but not necessary for functional similarity.
contribution: Provides unified theoretical and empirical synthesis linking functional, representational similarity and reconstruction via task-granularity hierarchy.

problem: Open-vocabulary object detection approaches distill regional features for semantic alignment but sacrifice spatial fidelity when using distilled features for both classification and localization.
approach: OSSD explicitly decouples semantic and spatial learning: distills object semantics from CLIP global embeddings for region discrimination and injects spatial priors from base-trained detector; proposes Location Quality Estimation Head.
contribution: Achieves 49.2 AP50 on OV-COCO (3.6% above previous best) and 40.5 mAP on novel categories in OV-LVIS.

problem: Modern AI hardware adopts low-precision floating-point formats for LLMs, yet unified comparison of FP versus INT quantization across granularities has been missing.
approach: Systematically investigates FP-INT trade-offs revealing critical performance crossover: FP excels in coarse-grained quantization, INT surpasses in fine-grained; introduces symmetric clipping resolving gradient bias in fine-grained INT training.
contribution: Demonstrates MXINT8 and MXINT4 superior to FP counterparts in accuracy and hardware efficiency, challenging current hardware trajectories.

problem: Open-vocabulary segmentation produces blurred boundaries and fragmented structures because image-level training in CLIP mixes amplitude and phase information limiting fine-grained discrimination.
approach: PhaseAlign decouples magnitude and phase of visual-textual embeddings in complex domain; introduces spatial-aware cross-modal projection modeling local relations via multi-scale contrast, and attention-guided affinity propagating activations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks with improved boundary clarity and region integrity.

problem: Rigid integer-based bit-widths in quantization create deployment gap where LLMs cannot fit optimally to specific memory budgets.
approach: LiftQuant enables continuous bit-width control via lift-then-project mechanism: approximates low-dimensional vectors by projecting 1-bit lattice from higher-dimensional lifted space; effective bit-width is ratio of lifted to original dimension.
contribution: Enables 70B LLM compression to 2.4 bits for 24GB GPU with performance significantly surpassing standard 2-bit models.

problem: Masked diffusion model samplers remain greedy, selecting locally certain tokens without accounting for downstream effects, increasing cumulative uncertainty.
approach: Info-Gain Sampler uses MDM bidirectional structure to balance immediate uncertainty with information gained over remaining positions; training-free decoding method.
contribution: Improves average reasoning accuracy by 2.9-11.6 points and achieves 62.8% win rate in creative writing across reasoning, coding, and generation tasks.

problem: Diffusion models suffer high inference latency while flow-based policy methods require complex constraints; applying MeanFlow to robotics faces spectral bias and gradient starvation in low-velocity regimes.
approach: One-step MeanFlow Policy (OMP) introduces lightweight directional alignment synchronizing predicted velocities with true mean velocities; implements Differential Derivation Equation to approximate Jacobian-Vector Product.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on Adroit and Meta-World with superior success rate and trajectory accuracy while maintaining single-step efficiency.

problem: Existing 3D scene generation methods prioritize visual plausibility but neglect protocol grounding and safety constraints essential for scientific experimentation in automated laboratories.
approach: LabBuilder operates through three tightly coupled components: LabForge curates meta-dataset and translates specifications into protocols; LabGen synthesizes layouts via constraint-aware optimization; LabTouchstone evaluates layouts as benchmark.
contribution: Generates realistic laboratory environments valid under geometric, chemical-safety, and navigation constraints with significantly improved performance.

problem: Gradient testing and estimation rely on expensive function evaluations, but learning using only comparison oracle is understudied.
approach: Designs gradient testing algorithm using O(1) queries to determine if normalized gradient is ε-close or 2ε-far from target; gradient estimation using O(n log(1/ε)) queries proven optimal.
contribution: Establishes optimal query complexity for gradient estimation and develops quantum algorithm achieving O(log(n/ε)) queries.

problem: Federated continual learning of LLMs faces communication-stability-plasticity trilemma; naively uploading all layers increases forgetting despite improved plasticity.
approach: RieSelect treats stability as staying within Fisher-metric safe basin; derives layer-wise conflict score and certified safe step size; formulates selective uplink as knapsack-based utility-risk selection.
contribution: Improves average accuracy by 18.99-28.14 points while reducing total uplink by 53-115× under standard communication protocols.

problem: Sampling from non-log-concave distributions with difference-of-convex regularizers combines smooth data fidelity and non-smooth DC structure.
approach: DC-LA applies Moreau envelopes to DC components separately and studies proximal Langevin algorithm with DC structure exploitation.
contribution: Establishes convergence to target distribution in q-Wasserstein distance for all q, improving prior work with more general framework and assumptions.

problem: Conditional sampling from partially observed distributions requires additional feature information but contemporary methods lack efficient one-shot inference.
approach: CGMMD frames conditional sampling as direct adversary-free minimization; uses nearest-neighbor kernels enabling single-pass generation; establishes convergence bounds and concentration results.
contribution: Performs competitively on synthetic complex densities and practical applications like image denoising and super-resolution with low test-time complexity.

problem: Autoregressive PDE surrogates violate global conservation and physical bounds over long rollouts, destabilizing predictions for conservation laws.
approach: FluxNet learns cumulative transport amounts via capacity-constrained transport heads (L/U/D) enforcing lower/upper/dual bounds; no temporal integration required enabling large-timestep prediction.
contribution: Achieves exact conservation, structural bound preservation, modularity, and superior stability at large temporal strides on 1D/2D benchmarks.

problem: Image editing methods using text-to-image models suffer from accumulated drift when the reconstruction path uses mismatched timesteps, limiting reconstruction fidelity.
approach: DirectEdit eliminates reconstruction error by directly aligning forward paths instead of rectifying the inversion path, using attention feature injection and multi-branch mask-guided noise blending for feature sharing.
contribution: Achieves efficient and accurate image editing with superior performance over state-of-the-art methods without introducing additional neural function evaluations.

problem: Label noise in federated graph learning degrades global model generalization, and existing federated label-noise methods designed for vision tasks yield suboptimal results when applied to graph data.
approach: FedRGL leverages globally aggregated models and local subgraph structure to implement class-aware dual-consistency filtering for noise-node identification, then assigns pseudo-labels using graph contrastive learning augmentations.
contribution: Achieves 5-8% higher accuracy on average and up to 30% improvement over weaker baselines under various noise conditions across real-world graph datasets.

problem: Translating natural-language descriptions of decision problems into formal optimization code is brittle with large language models, often generating syntactically invalid or non-executable code.
approach: NEMO uses autonomous coding agents with sandboxed execution to guarantee code validity by construction, employing asymmetric validation loops, external memory for experience reuse, and minimum Bayes risk decoding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on nine optimization benchmarks with substantial margins on several datasets by treating autonomous coding agents as first-class abstractions.

problem: DiLoCo's outer synchronization is bandwidth-heavy and brittle to stragglers and transient failures in low-bandwidth distributed training settings.
approach: Factored Gossip DiLoCo replaces exact synchronization with approximate gossip-based mixing, factorizing synchronization into non-blocking mixing overlapped with computation and blocking tightening steps.
contribution: Substantially improves compute utilization on billion-parameter language models in low-bandwidth settings with training progress ranging from comparable to closely matching standard DiLoCo.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation for multimodal document QA breaks document structure and cross-modal alignment, and iterative retrieval fails by looping on partial evidence without persistent global search state.
approach: G²-Reader maintains a Content Graph preserving document structure and cross-modal semantics, plus a Planning Graph of sub-questions to track findings and guide stepwise navigation for evidence completion.
contribution: Reaches 66.21% average accuracy on VisDoMBench, outperforming strong baselines and standalone GPT-5 at 53.08% with Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct.

problem: Uniform computation budgets in LLM decoding over-compute on easy tokens and under-compute on hard ones, wasting inference resources since token difficulty varies widely.
approach: Self-Optimizing Language Models pair a frozen LLM with a lightweight policy network that selects discrete efficiency actions per token, controlling attention sparsity, MLP pruning, and activation quantization bit-width.
contribution: Improves quality at matched budget over static allocation and strong random schedule search, offering a complementary axis for inference-efficiency optimization.

problem: Model merging on Mixture-of-Experts architectures fails due to routing breakdown, where the merged router cannot dispatch tokens to suitable experts after parameter perturbations.
approach: Hessian-Aware Router Calibration leverages second-order curvature information to realign the merged router using a closed-form solution solvable via matrix-free conjugate gradient.
contribution: Effectively mitigates routing breakdown across diverse MoE merging baselines with substantial performance improvements on mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.

problem: No single action space is universally best for building generalist AI agents; effective action spaces are highly task-dependent, complicating the goal of one agent for all tasks.
approach: Chain-of-Action unifies high-level abstract and low-level control actions in a single model, using abstract goals as intermediate reasoning steps that guide precise executable action generation.
contribution: OpenHA achieves state-of-the-art performance as an All-in-One generalist agent trained on diverse action spaces, outperforming strong specialized baselines on over 800 Minecraft tasks.

problem: Bayesian experimental design cannot handle both partially observable dynamical systems and fully online inference, where latent states make likelihood and information-theoretic objectives intractable.
approach: Derives new estimators of expected information gain and gradients that marginalize latent states via nested particle filters, enabling scalable stochastic optimization in nonlinear state-space models.
contribution: Successfully handles partial observability and online inference on realistic models like SIR and moving source location tasks with convergence guarantees.

problem: Existing RL backdoor attacks rely on unrealistic white-box access to parameters, rewards, or observations, missing practical black-box supply-chain vulnerabilities.
approach: Supply-Chain Backdoor attack poisons the dataset through legitimate agent-environment interactions by training with third-party policies in a black-box manner.
contribution: Demonstrates over 90% peak attack success rate and reduces victim returns by 80% with only 3% data corruption, exposing critical vulnerabilities in the RL supply chain.

problem: Long-form video understanding in VLMs faces tension between computational constraints and capturing information across thousands of frames without reliable recovery from poor sampling choices.
approach: VideoBrain uses dual complementary agents—CLIP-based semantic retrieval and Uniform temporal sampling—with behavior-aware rewards teaching when agent invocation is genuinely beneficial.
contribution: Achieves 3.5-9.0% improvement over baseline while using 30-40% fewer frames with strong cross-dataset generalization to short videos.

problem: Decoupled offline speculator training introduces high time-to-serve lag, delayed utility feedback, and domain-drift degradation as target models are repurposed to new domains.
approach: Aurora reframes online speculator learning as asynchronous reinforcement learning from live inference traces, using accepted tokens for positive feedback and rejected proposals for implicit negative feedback.
contribution: Supports day-0 deployment with immediate utility feedback and rapid domain adaptation while continuously improving system performance from live traffic.

problem: Q-based imitation learning methods like IQ-Learn claim to outperform behavioral cloning but actually reduce to BC, remaining susceptible to compounding errors under partial observability.
approach: Dual Q-DM uses Bellman constraints to drive value flow—Q-values propagate from demonstrated to unvisited states via environment dynamics—enabling generalization beyond demonstrations.
contribution: First non-adversarial imitation learning method theoretically guaranteed to eliminate compounding errors, equivalent to adversarial imitation learning in mitigating horizon-dependent gaps.

problem: Budget-feasible procurement mechanism design focuses on buyer value maximization, neglecting buyer utility (value minus payments) and welfare (value minus costs) objectives.
approach: Designs simple mechanisms achieving constant-factor approximation for welfare in prior-free settings and near-optimal utility in Bayesian settings with ex-post budget constraints.
contribution: Introduces mechanisms for utility-optimal and welfare-optimal procurement beyond value-maximization, with generalizations to other objectives.

problem: Text-to-CAD systems hallucinate missing dimensions and follow inconsistent instructions when geometric descriptions are under-specified or internally contradictory.
approach: ProCAD pairs a proactive clarifying agent auditing prompts and asking targeted questions with a CAD coding agent, enabling self-consistent specification before synthesis.
contribution: Reduces mean Chamfer distance by 79.9% and lowers invalidity ratio from 4.8% to 0.9%, outperforming Claude Sonnet 4.5 with low interaction overhead.

problem: Diffusion models produce semantic inconsistencies (hallucinations) and existing guidance methods add computational overhead or require external signals and architectural modifications.
approach: TAG amplifies tangential score components using an intermediate sample as projection basis, steering toward higher-probability regions without extra training or architecture changes.
contribution: Corrects sampling trajectory with negligible overhead, reducing inconsistencies and improving fidelity as a training-free, architecture-agnostic plug-and-play guidance method.

problem: RL for open-ended tasks with vast solution spaces lacks objective ground truth, and pointwise reward scoring induces discrimination collapse where reward models fail to distinguish subtle advantages.
approach: ArenaRL shifts from pointwise scoring to intra-group relative ranking via process-aware pairwise evaluation, constructing adversarial arenas with tournament-based ranking for stable advantage signals.
contribution: Achieves O(N) complexity with high-precision advantage estimation, introducing two benchmarks (Open-Travel, Open-DeepResearch) for open-ended agent training and evaluation.

problem: Reasoning models handle symbol symmetries only implicitly via expensive data augmentation, failing to exploit permutation invariances architecturally.
approach: SE-RRMs enforce permutation equivariance at the architectural level through symbol-equivariant layers, guaranteeing identical solutions under symbol or color permutations.
contribution: Outperforms prior RRMs on 9×9 Sudoku and generalizes from training data to smaller (4×4) and larger (16×16, 25×25) instances with only 2M parameters.

problem: Scene-centric benchmarks evaluate unconstrained environments where single images admit multiple plausible 3D interpretations, failing to test spatial reasoning in determinate settings.
approach: SSI-Bench uses structural constraints from geometry, topology, and physical feasibility to make 3D relations determinate, containing 1,000 ranking questions requiring full 3D relation resolution.
contribution: Reveals large human-model gap: best open-source model 22.2%, strongest closed-source 33.6%, humans 91.6%, showing fundamental spatial-understanding limitations with minimal gains from chain-of-thought.

problem: Adversaries can inject malicious records into LLM-agent memory to bias behavior, but effective injections are visibly malicious while stealthy injections are less effective.
approach: MemIncept generates cooperative query sets via bidirectional evolutionary strategy: forward pass ensures collective target outcome, backward pass ensures semantic closeness to benign queries.
contribution: Achieves high success rates comparable to explicit attacks while remaining difficult to flag under automated filters, demonstrating practical memory-poisoning vulnerabilities.

problem: Tubal Nuclear Norm applies uniform penalties to frequency-domain singular values without distinguishing inter-frequency sparsity from intra-frequency low-rankness, limiting flexibility for multi-level spectral structures.
approach: Tensor ℓp-Schatten-q quasi-norm enables explicit control of dual spectral sparsity by jointly regularizing inter-frequency sparsity and intra-frequency low-rankness with theoretical minimax error bounds.
contribution: Subsumes TNN as special case with reweighted optimization for nonconvex problems, demonstrating effectiveness and robustness on tensor completion and image clustering.

problem: Non-generative vision models fail to achieve compositional generalization that is hallmark of human data efficiency, yet generative approaches require complex inductive biases.
approach: Formalizes that encoder-based (non-generative) methods require substantially more complex inductive biases than decoder-based (generative) methods for compositional generalization.
contribution: Demonstrates theoretically that generative methods with simple decoder biases outperform non-generative methods requiring large-scale pretraining for compositional generalization.

problem: Existing LLM unlearning methods based on prediction loss maximization face issues of over-forgetting and poor model utility.
approach: DareU uses reinforcement learning to reduce data attribution scores of generated responses to forget-data owners, shifting optimization target from loss maximization to de-attribution.
contribution: Outperforms existing baseline approaches, achieving effective unlearning while balancing forget quality and model utility through attribution rewards.

problem: Robotic manipulation of flat objects is challenging due to ungraspable configurations, strong geometry/material variations, and limited generalization in closed-setting evaluations.
approach: Decouples manipulation into strategy generator predicting object-invariant strategies from point clouds via contrastive learning, and execution module decomposing into reusable action primitives.
contribution: Introduces FlatLab benchmark with high-fidelity simulation and standardized protocols; demonstrates effective generalization to unseen objects and categories.

problem: Most deep research frameworks rely on rigid one-shot workflows with long autonomous runs, offering little room for course correction when user intent shifts.
approach: SteER introduces mid-process interpretable control using cost-benefit formulation to pause when beneficial, combines diversity-aware planning with utility signals rewarding alignment/novelty/coverage.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by up to 22.80% on alignment, leads on quality metrics, and is preferred by humans in 85%+ pairwise judgments.

problem: Verbalized confidence in LLMs fails to calibrate universally across diverse tasks without degrading accuracy.
approach: Decomposes confidence into reasoning uncertainty and evidence localization uncertainty, enabling task-aware semantics that restore cross-family generalization via supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Shows universal confidence calibration fails across task families but within-family transfer works; decompositional approach restores cross-family generalization.

problem: Surrogate models for topology optimization exhibit highly variable out-of-distribution generalization under distribution shifts like changing loads or boundary conditions.
approach: Introduces pseudo-sensitivities to characterize which physical fields enable generalization, conditioning Bernoulli flow-matching generators on sensitivity-equivalent fields for information-theoretic optimality.
contribution: Sensitivity-conditioned matching yields state-of-the-art out-of-distribution performance across structural and CFD topology optimization under load and boundary-condition shifts.

problem: Cloud-edge collaborative speculative decoding suffers from sequential token generation/communication with low resource utilization and inflexible verification triggering causing premature or costly operations.
approach: PipeSD overlaps token generation and communication via token-batch pipeline scheduling optimized by dynamic programming, with dual-threshold verification and Bayesian optimization autotuning.
contribution: Achieves 1.16-2.16× speedup and reduces energy consumption by 14.3-25.3% across draft-target pairs on real-world cloud-edge testbeds.

problem: Test-time guidance in diffusion-based navigation can produce unreliable trajectories when updates drift off the training manifold.
approach: Fisher Preserving Guidance avoids large Fisher drift via low-rank Jacobian factorization requiring single backward pass, with Truncated Fisher Denoising Sensitivity for uncertainty-based multi-sample blending.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements in navigation performance over diffusion-policy baselines without additional training on Maze2D, PushT, and real robot tasks.

problem: KV cache compression evaluations focus on sparse retrieval tasks, masking degradation in reasoning tasks where chain-of-thought coherence is critical.
approach: ShotKV explicitly separates prefill and decoding phases to prioritize semantic units (few-shot examples), preserving chain-of-thought links while enabling aggressive compression.
contribution: Achieves 9-18% accuracy improvements on long-context generation tasks while delivering 11% latency reduction compared to full cache inference.

problem: Standard point-wise residual minimization in Physics-Informed Neural Networks suffers from convergence pathologies in topologically complex domains like TPMS due to locality bias.
approach: MUSA-PINN reformulates Navier-Stokes constraints as integral conservation laws over hierarchical spherical control volumes with flux-balance residuals and skeleton-aware meso-scale volumes.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on steady incompressible flow in TPMS geometries, reducing relative errors by up to 93% while preserving mass conservation.

problem: Attention scores diminish in long contexts, raising questions about token distinguishability and whether it can be preserved.
approach: Introduces Aitchison distance to quantify relative differences among attention probabilities, showing that token distinguishability converges to non-zero limit with Gaussian queries/keys.
contribution: Derives theoretical lower bound of Ω(√log L) on temperature scaling for sharp attention, providing principled alternative to entropy for monitoring training.

problem: Grounded visual reasoning methods impose high computational costs via multi-round ground-then-answer processes while requiring accurate region selection.
approach: RTAF feeds low-resolution thumbnails for reasoning about relevant regions and high-resolution crops for answering, with tool access for extreme cases and reinforcement learning training.
contribution: Based on Qwen2.5-VL, achieves 5.8 point performance gain with comparable or reduced computation through thumbnail reasoning and focused answering.

problem: Multi-view clustering with missing views and cross-view sample misalignment causes inferior clustering performance and hinders cross-view modeling.
approach: OPTION uses conditional flow matching for manifold-preserving missing-view imputation and Gromov-Wasserstein structural regularization for alignment-free fusion in latent space.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods across ideal, incomplete, and unaligned scenarios with optional contrastive regularization for aligned settings.

problem: Prompt sensitivity causes unpredictable LLM performance variations between instruction-based and example-based prompting styles.
approach: Identifies task-specific attention heads whose outputs describe the task (lexical task heads) that are shared across prompting styles and trigger answer production.
contribution: Shows behavioral variation can be explained by activation degree of lexical heads, with failures sometimes due to competing task representations diluting target signals.

problem: Multi-modal Diffusion Language Models suffer from visual hallucinations due to static visual perception without sequential dependencies to dynamically interact with visual content.
approach: VGR detects hallucinated spans via confidence fluctuation during denoising and corrects them through targeted visual evidence extraction and in-place remasking.
contribution: Reduces hallucinations and recalls more details on image captioning and hallucination evaluation benchmarks by exploiting diffusion dynamics.

problem: Two-stage agent heterogeneity in intervention policy learning creates distinct agent types with varying returns, but existing methods fail to fully identify all types.
approach: Proposes minimax approach within counterfactual principal strata framework with three estimators (P-OR, P-IPS, P-DR) providing unbiasedness and robustness guarantees.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for optimal intervention allocation accounting for two-stage outcomes with experimental validation of effectiveness.

problem: Reasoning models become confident in answers early but continue generating tokens without revealing internal beliefs, conflating performative with genuine reasoning.
approach: Compares activation probing, early forced answering, and CoT monitors across models, finding models' final answers are decodable from activations earlier than monitors report.
contribution: Probe-guided early exit reduces tokens by up to 80% on MMLU and 30% on GPQA-Diamond with similar accuracy, enabling detection of performative reasoning.

problem: Multi-vector retrieval systems like ColBERT provide superior quality but incur significantly increased search latency compared to single-vector approaches.
approach: LEMUR reduces multi-vector similarity search to supervised learning solved by one-hidden-layer neural network, then reduces inference to single-vector search in latent space.
contribution: Order of magnitude faster than prior multi-vector similarity search methods while maintaining quality advantages.

problem: Manifold clustering methods focus on combining K-means with manifold learning but overlook consistency between data structures and labels, suffering from high computational cost.
approach: LMBC uses label information to guide manifold construction ensuring consistency, introduces anchor-induced distance representation for compact manifold modeling, and maximizes Schatten-p norm for class balance.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness and scalability on benchmark datasets with theoretical analysis supporting balance maintenance.

problem: LLMs fail to ensure feasible solutions for engineering problems with data and physical constraints, limiting their practical applicability despite strong reasoning capabilities.
approach: Propose EngiAgent, a multi-agent system with a fully connected coordinator that routes feedback flexibly between specialized agents for problem analysis, modeling, verification, solving, and evaluation.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements in feasibility-oriented engineering problem solving across four domains, establishing a new paradigm that overcomes rigidity of prior pipeline-based methods.

problem: LLMs exhibit persistent miscalibration after instruction tuning and preference alignment, making their predictions unreliable for downstream tasks.
approach: Introduce CORAL, which uses weight-decay MLP probes to capture distributed correctness signals from model internals at inference time without retraining.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy by 10% and expected calibration error by 50% on average; transfers gains to held-out benchmarks without retraining with 14% accuracy and 49% ECE improvements.

problem: Heterogeneous federated learning struggles to learn across different model architectures because direct parameter sharing is infeasible.
approach: Reformulate HFL as a LEGO assembly game by decomposing models into modular components and collaboratively learning these components under predefined composition rules.
contribution: Develops LEGO-FL framework enabling flexible model construction while preserving collaborative learning across heterogeneous architectures and system scales.

problem: Deep learning architectures neglect joint rate and phase dynamics that biological neural systems exploit for efficient feature binding and information processing.
approach: Introduce Kuramoto oscillatory Phase Encoding (KoPE) as an evolving phase state in Vision Transformers with neuro-inspired synchronization for enhanced structure learning.
contribution: Improves training, parameter, and data efficiency while benefiting structured tasks including segmentation, language alignment, and visual reasoning; accelerates attention concentration.

problem: Analytic class-incremental learning with pre-trained models trades efficiency for stability; accumulated errors and feature incompatibility compromise performance.
approach: Propose VILA, a dual-branch framework using two-level vision-language calibration: geometric fusion at feature level and cross-modal semantic priors at decision level.
contribution: Consistently yields superior performance across eight benchmarks, particularly in fine-grained and long-sequence scenarios, maintaining efficiency while overcoming brittleness.

problem: Adaptive sparse activation inference methods often alter activation maps, reducing efficiency gains and limiting practical speedup for resource-constrained devices.
approach: Introduce SparseInfer, an MLP-free method based on sentence-level prediction that identifies core neurons whose stability and semantic relevance enable fixed activation during encoding.
contribution: Achieves 10.33x speedup while maintaining performance by discovering that core neurons align with input semantics.

problem: Data attribution methods assume attribution values faithfully reflect participants' contributions, but this assumption can break under distributed training.
approach: Demonstrate an attribution-first attack using latent optimization to inject synthetic batches that exploit non-IID label coverage and evaluator sensitivities.
contribution: Shows single participants can substantially inflate measured attribution while preserving global utility, revealing attribution as a new attack surface.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems suffer from redundant prefill computation for shared content, creating bottlenecks in KV cache memory and time-to-first-token.
approach: Propose RelayCaching, which directly reuses decoding KV caches from previous agents in subsequent prefill phases by selectively recomputing at sparse, localized positions.
contribution: Achieves over 80% KV cache reuse and 4.7x TTFT reduction with negligible accuracy loss across mathematical reasoning, knowledge, and code generation.

problem: DPO models sequence-level preferences despite generation being token-driven, leaving per-prefix optimality implicit and limiting alignment quality.
approach: Introduce Token-level Bregman Preference Optimization (TBPO), deriving a density-ratio matching objective that recovers token-level optimality from sequence-level comparisons.
contribution: Improves alignment quality and training stability while increasing output diversity relative to sequence-level and token-level baselines.

problem: MLLMs lack active perception capabilities, limiting efficiency in tasks requiring selective visual attention for relevant information gathering.
approach: Propose Active-o3, an RL framework built on GRPO that learns efficient region selection through modular sensing-action design and dual-form rewards.
contribution: Equips MLLMs with active perception capabilities while preserving general understanding; enhances performance on small/dense-object grounding and domain-specific scenarios.

problem: Joint robot morphology and control optimization is challenging under computational constraints without principled multi-objective search mechanisms.
approach: Introduce Debate2Create, a multi-agent LLM framework where design and control agents iterate in thesis-antithesis-synthesis loops guided by criterion-specific judges.
contribution: Achieves highest normalized scores on locomotion benchmarks with gains up to 3.2x on Ant and 9x on Swimmer; 18-35% gains over compute-matched baselines.

problem: FFN interpretability in LLMs is challenging because self-attention context obscures how FFNs process tokens, limiting understanding of model internals.
approach: Propose MemoryLLM, which decouples FFNs from attention by training them in isolation using token embeddings, enabling study as context-free neural retrieval memory.
contribution: Achieves context-free FFNs via pre-computed token-wise lookups enabling on-demand VRAM-storage transfer; enhances inference efficiency.

problem: Static multi-codebook vector quantizers limit expressiveness for heterogeneous data geometry, while dynamic methods suffer from sequential dependency bottlenecks.
approach: Propose RQ-MoE, combining two-level MoE with dual-stream quantization to enable input-dependent dynamic codebook construction with parallel decoding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction and retrieval performance while providing 6-14x faster decoding than prior vector quantization methods.

problem: It remains unclear whether VLMs genuinely understand physical transformations and can maintain invariant representations under dynamic scene changes.
approach: Introduce ConservationBench evaluating conservation of physical quantities across paired conserving and non-conserving scenarios with 23,040 questions across 112 VLMs.
contribution: Reveals systematic failure: performance remains near chance on conservation tasks; strong textual priors favor invariance but models perform worse with visual content.

problem: MLLMs struggle with in-context learning over long sequences due to finite context windows, KV cache costs, and inflexible memory compression approaches.
approach: Introduce TASM, a training-free framework using Task-Vector Guided Compression and Semantics-Aware Token Merging formulated as Bipartite Graph Matching.
contribution: Sustains strong multi-modal ICL performance under high compression ratios by balancing efficiency, adaptability, and semantic fidelity.

problem: Multimodal contrastive learning suffers from modality gap where image and text representations collapse into separated subspaces, obscuring what determines downstream performance.
approach: Develop first theoretical framework analyzing convergent optimal representations showing modality gap arises from dimension collapse; prove shared space alignment is dominant factor.
contribution: Proposes Shared Space Alignment (SSA) improving MCL pretraining by enhancing alignment without modality gap reduction; validated theory with improved empirical results.

problem: Reward models exhibit persistent biases including length, sycophancy, overconfidence, and model-specific style preferences that enable reward hacking.
approach: Systematically measure and categorize RM failures as tractable or resistant to linear intervention; propose mechanistic reward shaping post-hoc mitigation.
contribution: Reduces targeted biases without degrading reward quality and generalizes out-of-distribution.

problem: Embedding hard constraints into neural networks typically requires either soft penalty methods lacking guarantees or post-processing causing suboptimality.
approach: Introduce CAffNet with trainable constraint-affine (CAffine) layers enabling input-dependent affine constraints of arbitrary cardinality.
contribution: Preserves universal approximation properties while providing provable constraint adherence guarantees for all inputs.

problem: Fine-tuning MLLMs on task-specific data causes catastrophic forgetting on pretrained tasks, and existing mitigation methods scale poorly with model size.
approach: Propose Model-Dowser, computing principled importance scores jointly considering weight magnitudes, activations, and sensitivities, then selectively preserving high-importance parameters.
contribution: Effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting on LLaVA and NVILA while remaining resource-efficient and scalable to multi-billion parameters.

problem: Evaluating end-to-end spreadsheet generation is challenging because relevant criteria vary by use case and intertwine stylistic, structural, and functional features.
approach: Introduce SpreadsheetArena, a platform for blind pairwise evaluations of LLM-generated spreadsheets with a dataset of prompts, outputs, and preference votes.
contribution: Reveals stylistic/structural/functional preferences vary meaningfully across prompts; expert evaluations show ranked models don't reliably follow domain-specific best practices.

problem: Extending federated learning to MLLMs faces challenges: heterogeneous client modalities cause architectural incompatibility and full-parameter fine-tuning incurs prohibitive communication costs.
approach: Propose UniFLoW with FedA2-LoRA, using multi-modal encoders and analytical aggregation to handle client-side heterogeneity while maintaining aggregation consistency.
contribution: Enables scalable, communication-efficient federated fine-tuning with state-of-the-art FedLoRA performance across text, image, and speech modalities.

problem: Nonlinear MPC control actions are opaque to operators despite being critical for safety-critical infrastructure, undermining trust and deployment.
approach: Present Hierarchical Causal Abduction combining physics-informed domain knowledge graphs, KKT optimization evidence, and temporal causal discovery to generate faithful explanations.
contribution: Improves explanation accuracy by 53% over LIME using cross-domain parameters; domain-specific tuning achieves 0.88 accuracy with validation across three control applications.

problem: Continual learning requires balancing stability against plasticity; projection-based methods constrain updates limiting plasticity while linear approximations cause gradient deviation.
approach: Propose MoCL with factorized subspace approximation and metabolic gating based on Tsallis entropy to suppress conflicting updates.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both classification performance and efficiency by capturing geometric manifolds while supporting shared low-loss behavior.

problem: Image relighting requires representations separating illumination from scene properties while retaining dense geometry and photometry, creating a semantic-photometric trade-off.
approach: Introduce Augmented Latent Intrinsics (ALI) fusing dense pixel-aligned features into latent-intrinsic relighting and refining via self-supervision on unlabeled pairs.
contribution: Improves relighting quality particularly on glossy, metallic, and transparent materials by demonstrating generative relighting as effective tool for quantifying physical information in visual encoders.

problem: Coresets for instruction tuning are difficult to curate; existing methods rely on coarse sample-level signals that are computationally expensive and miss fine-grained features.
approach: Introduce TRIM, a forward-only token-centric framework matching representational patterns via attention-based fingerprints from target samples without gradients.
contribution: Coresets consistently outperform baselines by up to 9% on downstream tasks and even surpass full-data fine-tuning at fraction of computational cost.

problem: Two-sample testing in few-shot settings with severe sample-size imbalance requires leveraging abundant reference data to detect departures.
approach: Propose LOTTERY, learning reference-dependent representations capturing global and local structure, weighted via uncertainty-guided principle.
contribution: Achieves permutation-based type I error control with consistency guarantees; aggregation incurs only log-log n overhead with matching lower bounds.

problem: Synthesizing realistic and diverse anomalous samples from limited data is vital for model robustness but requires reconciling fidelity and diversity.
approach: Introduce Anomaly Preference Optimization reformulating anomaly generation as preference learning with implicit alignment using real anomalies as references.
contribution: Outperforms baselines achieving state-of-the-art performance in both realism and diversity via Time-Aware Capacity Allocation and hierarchical sampling.

problem: Mechanisms underlying transferability of pretrained RNA foundation models remain unclear, hindering principled guidance for future development.
approach: Conduct systematic investigation of transfer learning in RNA FMs across diverse structural and functional tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates frozen representations are not universally transferable; pretraining benefits via optimization initialization when objectives align, accelerating convergence to flatter minima.

problem: Existing world models lack effective training paradigms for real-world videos over long horizons due to noisy pose and scarcity of viewpoint revisits.
approach: Propose Infinite-World with Hierarchical Pose-free Memory Compressor recursively distilling historical latents and Uncertainty-aware Action Abstraction.
contribution: Maintains coherent visual memory over 1000+ frames in real-world environments with superior visual quality, action controllability, and spatial consistency.

problem: RL methods for code generation show weak generalization across programming languages; naive multilingual training suffers from optimization imbalance.
approach: Propose GXPO forming training groups by generating solutions in multiple languages and jointly optimizing language-specific and cross-language signals.
contribution: Consistently improves performance with pronounced gains on low-resource languages; introduces Multilingual LiveCodeBench extending LiveCodeBench to unified multilingual setting.

problem: Understanding uniform convergence behavior of halfspaces beyond worst-case VC bounds reveals sharp dimensional and structural thresholds.
approach: Study fine-grained uniform convergence showing inhomogeneous halfspaces in Rd (d≥2) have tight VC bounds while homogeneous in R2 exhibit different behavior.
contribution: Proves realizable case achieves O(1/n) error while agnostic case has log-free band-wise deviations with log-log n union overhead matching lower bounds.

problem: Multimodal reasoning for UHR remote sensing bottlenecks on visual evidence acquisition requiring localization in massive pixel spaces without structured domain priors.
approach: Investigate staged knowledge injection: cold-start with Earth-science text QA, pre-warm on UHR image-text examples during SFT, then apply agentic RLVR.
contribution: Achieves 60.04% Pass@1 on XLRS-Bench outperforming larger general-purpose models, establishing new SOTA with Text-Before-Vision paradigm.

problem: Why linear RNNs parallelize like transformers while nonlinear RNNs do not remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Provide tight connection between RNN types and complexity classes: LRNNs as log-depth circuits; nonlinear RNNs solve L-complete to P-complete problems.
contribution: Reveals fundamental parallelization barriers for nonlinear RNNs; identifies expressivity differences between LRNN variants and associated automata-theoretic models.

problem: Concept Bottleneck Models improve interpretability but cannot verify whether learned concepts align with human intentions, hurting explainability.
approach: Introduce Prototype-Grounded Concept Models (PGCMs) grounding concepts in learned visual prototypes enabling direct inspection and targeted human intervention.
contribution: Achieves similar performance to CBMs while substantially improving transparency, interpretability, and intervenability.

problem: Parametric CAD modeling from incomplete human intent (sketches, text) without target models is challenging due to representational gaps.
approach: Propose HiCAD framework with Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment bridging heterogeneous inputs and Spatial-Aware RL ensuring geometric-topological consistency.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines across multiple tasks with first large-scale HiCAD dataset aligning sketches, descriptions, and parametric CAD codes.

problem: Mechanisms underlying what thinking models learn during RL versus SFT training remain unclear, hindering efficient development.
approach: Introduce constructive model diffing decomposing base-to-fine-tuned differences into reasoning mechanisms and heuristics using Sparse Autoencoders.
contribution: Reveals RL primarily teaches models when to apply pre-existing capabilities while SFT teaches new mechanisms; implications for efficient reasoning model development.

problem: Flow matching suffers from high-variance training targets using single-sample conditional velocities, destabilizing optimization and slowing convergence.
approach: Characterize variance explicitly identifying high-variance near prior and low-variance near data; propose Stable Velocity Matching with variance-reduction and Stable Velocity Sampling.
contribution: Consistent training efficiency improvements and 2x faster sampling without degrading quality on ImageNet, text-to-image/video models including SD3.5, Flux.

problem: VQ-VAEs are difficult to train due to discretization; existing approaches suffer from training complexity or suboptimal performance.
approach: Propose Gaussian Quant (GQ) training Gaussian VAE then converting to VQ-VAE without additional training using random codebook vectors.
contribution: Outperforms VQGAN, FSQ, LFQ, BSQ on both UNet and ViT; guarantees small quantization error when codebook size exceeds bits-back coding rate.

problem: MLLMs lack deep-research capabilities for multi-turn, multi-entity visual and textual search under heavy noise from real-world scenarios.
approach: Propose Vision-DeepResearch performing multi-turn multi-entity and multi-scale visual-textual search, internalizing deep-research capabilities via cold-start supervision and RL.
contribution: Substantially outperforms existing multimodal deep-research MLLMs and workflows with foundation models like GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude-4-Sonnet.

problem: Existing methods struggle to uncover systematic dynamical structure in high-dimensional time series; generative models conflate dynamics with distractors.
approach: Develop Recognition-Parametrized Gaussian State-Space Model (RP-GSSM) inferring accurate latent dynamics via probabilistic framework without parametrized decoder.
contribution: Recovers physically meaningful latent states from noisy video faithfully, reliably identifies nonlinear dynamics, remains robust to visual distractors.

problem: LLM agents struggle to retrieve relevant past experience at the right level of granularity when solving complex software engineering tasks, leading to misguided solutions.
approach: Aligns memory storage and retrieval with the agent's functional decomposition into subtasks rather than treating entire episodes as atomic units, improving instance-level matching.
contribution: Achieves +4.7 pp improvement in Pass@1 over vanilla agents, with gains scaling with interaction steps on SWE-bench Verified.

problem: Text-to-video generation fails to reliably synthesize multiple subjects with complex relations—subjects go missing and spatial relationships become misaligned.
