approach: Decouples presence and alignment challenges via composition-aware attention: uses Subject-aware Condition Interpolation to enforce presence and Layout-forcing Attention Modulation to align spatial relations dynamically.
contribution: Boosts T2V-CompBench scores by 15.7% and 11.7% on two baselines with only 5% inference overhead, scaling to general T2V and compositional T2I.

problem: Agent benchmarks contain hidden validity flaws from interactions among user instructions, environments, tools, and evaluation protocols that confound model errors with benchmark artifacts.
approach: Decomposes tasks into four standardized components (User, Environment, Ground Truth, Evaluation) and applies hybrid rule-based and LLM-guided auditing to detect validity issues.
contribution: Achieves F1 scores 0.791-0.874 aligning with expert judgments and identifies missed issues in tau-bench; released AgentSuite platform.

problem: Test-time adaptation for vision-language models like CLIP suffers from optimization and inference stage mismatch when learning from pseudo labels generated by augmentations.
approach: Proposes self-ensembling strategy that adaptively emphasizes the test image itself over augmented views during both optimization and inference to obtain reliable pseudo labels.
contribution: USE framework and lightweight SE method outperform Test-Time Prompt Tuning; SE integrates as consistent booster with existing TTA methods.

problem: Dataset distillation compresses data but fails to preserve predictive patterns equally across demographic groups, causing fairness gaps independent of group imbalance.
approach: Identifies group-imbalance-agnostic barycenter of predictive information that induces similar representations across subgroups through cross-group alignment.
contribution: Reduces bias introduced by dataset distillation; method is compatible with existing distillation approaches and substantially improves fairness.

problem: Action chunking in vision-language-action models faces an inherent trade-off: longer horizons enable global foresight but impair fine-grained control, and vice versa.
approach: Mixture of Horizons segments action chunks into parallel streams with different horizons processed by a shared transformer, then fuses via a learned linear gate.
contribution: Enables adaptive dynamic inference with 2.5× higher throughput; achieves consistent gains on both simulated and real-world robotic tasks.

problem: Gradient-based optimization in class-incremental learning distorts decision boundaries from earlier tasks as new classes are added, creating a plasticity-stability dilemma.
approach: Externalizes plasticity into a binary synaptic matrix evolved via stochastic bit-flip updates with eligibility traces and collision signals that suppress cross-class interference.
contribution: Rivals gradient-based methods in exemplar-free settings; consistently boosts SOTA baselines as a lightweight plugin with mechanistic validation of geometric theory.

problem: Music-to-motion systems trained offline degrade in streaming where audio conditioning history becomes stale or unreliable and conditions change abruptly.
approach: Combines causal music encoder capturing rhythmic structure with diffusion-forcing sequence model trained under heterogeneous noise; hybrid schedule and history-guided sampler balance responsiveness and consistency.
contribution: Delivers stable long-horizon rollouts and sharper audio-motion alignment in real-time interactive system while maintaining causality and latency constraints.

problem: Masked Diffusion Models lack reliable self-correction mechanisms during inference—existing approaches require major architectural changes or imprecise quality proxies.
approach: PRISM applies lightweight plug-in remasking at inference: defines self-correction loss that provably learns per-token quality scores without RL or verifier.
contribution: Advances MDM inference across domains and scales (Sudoku, text-170M, code-8B); provides open-source implementation.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models degrade under distribution shifts because behavior representations suffer from short-horizon temporal fragmentation and static execution alignment.
approach: BehaviorVLA uses causal Mamba to encode long-horizon trajectories into unified behavior representation and phase-conditioned decoder to align actions with task progress.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on RoboTwin 2.0 (58%), LIBERO (98%), CALVIN (4.36); sim-to-real transfer matches OpenVLA-OFT with only 50% of data.

problem: Time series forecasting loss functions use point-wise Euclidean metrics that ignore the geometric structure of probability distributions, leading to suboptimal uncertainty quantification.
approach: InfoGeo Loss grounds loss in information geometry with three components: distribution parameterization with learnable statistics, Fisher information metric on manifolds, and Bregman divergence for asymmetry.
contribution: Achieves 6.8% MSE and 5.3% MAE improvement on average across seven datasets with five architectures; includes theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: 3D assembly methods treat the problem as pure pose estimation without leveraging holistic shape context, failing to handle missing geometry or infer plausible completions.
approach: Reformulates assembly as joint assembly-and-generation problem: generation informs structure via shape context while assembly provides part-level priors to generation.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance on in-the-wild objects with diverse geometries, varying part counts, and missing pieces; synthesizes complete shapes.

problem: Online link recommendation is performative—recommended links change future feedback and fairness estimates from logged outcomes become unreliable after policy updates.
approach: COPF defines group opportunity gaps over exposure counterfactuals, makes them estimable via explicit exploration and propensity logging, and audits with graph-aware doubly-robust estimators.
contribution: Reduces worst-case spikes in exposure-counterfactual disparities with modest ranking impact; includes residual outcome indistinguishability bounds under temporal mixing.

problem: Discovering causal structure in time series is difficult when systems have endogenous context variables that both drive dynamics and are influenced by system state.
approach: Introduces PCMCI-based algorithms for Structural Causal Models with endogenous discrete context variables, leveraging either context persistence or sparsity of dependencies.
contribution: Theoretically sound algorithms with proof of correctness; systematic evaluation on benchmarks and land-atmosphere feedback application demonstrates effectiveness.

problem: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction produces heuristic confidence scores lacking probabilistic grounding, failing to indicate where and how much predicted geometry can be trusted.
approach: Trust3R combines gated residual mean refinement with Normal-Inverse-Wishart evidential head to yield multivariate Student-t distribution for per-point uncertainty.
contribution: Achieves 25% lower AURC and 41% lower AUSE on ScanNet++; improves risk-coverage and sparsification across diverse indoor/outdoor benchmarks.

problem: Full-duplex voice agents are deployed to production but existing evaluations address conversational dynamics and task completion in isolation, not grounded complexity.
approach: tau-Voice extends tau-bench with voice agent evaluation combining verifiable task completion, full-duplex interaction, realistic audio, and controllable voice simulator.
contribution: Voice agents retain only 30-45% of text performance under realistic conditions; 79-90% of failures stem from agent behavior; provides reproducible testbed.

problem: Model-based RL world models either prioritize reconstruction fidelity without task relevance or focus on decision-critical features at the cost of dynamics quality.
approach: Value-Aligned World Model adds intrinsic latent-space value-alignment regularization with adaptive weighting that balances reconstruction fidelity and decision-making utility.
contribution: Consistently boosts existing methods on Atari 100k and DeepMind Control with minimal code overhead; provides unified framework with negligible computational cost.

problem: Learning dynamics of high-dimensional probability densities over time without trajectory information requires solving complex optimal transport couplings at each step.
approach: Two-parameter flows learn sampling-time transports from base to marginals, then extract physics-time velocity by regressing on synthetic trajectories; uniqueness guaranteed.
contribution: Scales to high dimensions while avoiding per-step transport couplings; naturally explains rotational or circulating physics phenomena.

problem: Learning optimal intervention sequences from offline data for online adaptive deployment remains challenging in domains like personalized medicine.
approach: GIFT learns goal-conditioned policy from observational data by rescaling rewards with clipped importance weights; converges to unique fixed point under standard assumptions.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in creating goal-conditioned policies; includes bias bounds from clipping and approximation.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks for time-dependent PDEs reuse a single network across all times, forcing same features to handle markedly different dynamics and destabilizing training.
approach: Time-Induced Neural Networks (TINNs) parameterizes network weights as learned functions of time, allowing spatial representation to evolve while maintaining shared structure.
contribution: Achieves up to 4× improved relative L2 error and 10× faster convergence compared to PINNs and baselines on various time-dependent PDEs.

problem: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning routing relies on sample-to-task similarity and equal cross-modal weighting, missing intra-task diversity and modality-specific reliability variation.
approach: Hyper-LLaVA models task matching in hyperbolic space to leverage intra-task diversity and quantifies per-modality matching ambiguity for adaptive cross-modal balancing.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA approaches by large margins on continual multimodal learning; addresses both intra- and inter-modality routing challenges.

problem: Aligning LLMs to serve heterogeneous, conflicting preferences while leveraging test-time compute through multi-sample generation remains theoretically uncharted.
approach: Formalizes universal alignment through test-time scaling and derives optimal convergence rates; shows symmetric multi-player alignment games preserve output diversity.
contribution: Characterizes optimal rate f(k)=k/(k+1) for k-sample policies; demonstrates methods like NLHF fundamentally underutilize test-time scaling due to diversity collapse.

problem: Rare events in LLMs—behavior far from typical but highly significant—are hard to observe during development yet likely to surface at scale during deployment.
approach: Develops end-to-end framework for systematic rare event analysis spanning theory, efficient generation strategies, probability estimation, and error analysis.
contribution: Provides practical implementation for analyzing rare events; generalizes to other models and contexts with concrete examples and extensions.

problem: Optimizing complex systems like LLM prompts and multi-turn agents requires labor-intensive manual iteration and struggles with stochastic feedback and solution space expansion.
approach: POLCA maintains priority queue for exploration-exploitation, uses epsilon-net for parameter diversity, and LLM Summarizer for meta-learning across trials.
contribution: Converges to near-optimal solutions under stochasticity; outperforms SOTA on tau-bench, HotpotQA, VeriBench, KernelBench with robust performance.

problem: Diffusion LLMs use fixed-size action blocks, creating rigidity that breaks logical reasoning flow and ignores task-specific optimal block size variation.
approach: b1 framework learns dynamic-size blocks via Monotonic Entropy Descent objective with RL, enforcing consistent descent across block entropies to ensure coherent reasoning.
contribution: Consistent improvement over fixed-size baselines on reasoning benchmarks; plug-and-play module for dLLM post-training with released code.

problem: Mamba-based 3D pose estimation struggles with forced sequence flattening confusion and depth modeling ambiguity from single-view observation.
approach: StructMamPose adds Identity Anchoring Mechanism to enforce valid topological dependencies and View Transformation Hub to transform depth inference into observable features.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on most datasets by addressing spatiotemporal modeling and explicit spatial understanding challenges.

problem: Grounding benchmark performance in human task completion time requires costly, noisy annotations that don't scale; pre-hoc prediction of this metric remains unexplored.
approach: BRIDGE uses Item Response Theory to jointly estimate latent task difficulty and model capability from performance data; aligns difficulty linearly with log(human time).
contribution: Infers human task completion time for new benchmarks from model performance; reproduces METR's exponential scaling with 50% horizon doubling every 6 months.

problem: Context-entangled content segmentation (camouflaged object detection) requires robust learning from data with unclear boundaries, where objects share patterns with surroundings.
approach: CurriSeg uses curriculum selection to distinguish hard-but-informative from noisy samples, then anti-curriculum fine-tuning via spectral-blindness and sharpness-aware minimization.
contribution: Consistent improvements across CECS benchmarks without added parameters or training time; unifies curriculum and anti-curriculum principles for robust segmentation.

problem: Coding agents excel at single GitHub issues but struggle to generalize across diverse real-world tasks requiring codebase exploration, testing, and architecture design.
approach: Hybrid-Gym provides scalable synthetic training tasks (function localization, dependency search) designed via decomposition of transferable skills across diverse coding tasks.
contribution: Improves base model by 25.4% on SWE-Bench Verified, 7.9% on SWT-Bench, 5.1% on Commit-0; complementary gains with downstream task datasets.

problem: LLM annealing phase relies on empirical heuristics for data selection that lack principled grounding in optimization theory.
approach: DiReCT characterizes annealing via loss landscape spectral geometry and formulates selection as constrained optimization with directional constraints on per-sample gradients.
contribution: Consistently achieves SOTA across model scales; identifies samples aligning with optimal curvature-aware descent path.

problem: Multimodal LLM self-improvement training suffers from data imbalance (simple samples over-trained, hard ones under-trained) and language prior bias neglecting visual cues.
approach: VISTA introduces prefix resampling to reuse partial correct traces and vision-aware attention scoring to quantify focus on visual information.
contribution: Brings up to +13.66% average gains across MLLMs and tasks; enhances both supervised fine-tuning and preference learning scenarios.

problem: Fixed-dimensional E(3)-equivariant latent spaces for 3D molecules are geometrically precise but semantically shallow for comprehensive representation learning.
approach: MolAlign3D anchors manipulable latents from MolFLAE with embeddings from pre-trained molecular encoder to create semantically dense and geometrically precise manifold.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and comparable property prediction; significantly enhances zero-shot molecular manipulation including atom-count editing.

problem: Feature-map knowledge distillation fails for ViT compression despite per-image compressibility—revealed through spectral analysis as an encoding mismatch.
approach: Identifies bandwidth mismatch where tokens spread energy across modes even in low-rank subspace; proposes Lift (lightweight inference projector) or WideLast (wider last block).
contribution: Revives feature KD for ViT compression, improving DeiT-Tiny distilled from CaiT-S24 from 74.86% to 77.53%/78.23% top-1 accuracy.

problem: Video diffusion model adversarial attacks via image-to-video conditioning fail because robust spatio-temporal priors suppress motion artifact injection.
approach: MEDUSA targets temporal attention matrix rank collapse via nuclear norm minimization, inducing degenerate rank-1 state to freeze video motion.
contribution: Achieves effective motion elimination validated by mathematical analysis; circumvents gradient vanishing in direct temporal mapping.

problem: LLM-based CAD generation lacks high-quality datasets, fine-grained evaluation, and doesn't adequately decompose geometric vs. spatial reasoning in multi-step modeling.
approach: Op-CAD introduces largest operation-oriented CAD dataset with parsing module and geometry-guided annotation; proposes Chamfer/Fillet IoU metric and Chain-of-Operation prompting.
contribution: Establishes benchmark across eight LLMs; Chain-of-Operation strategy improves results by emulating human-engineer step-by-step reasoning.

problem: Pre-hoc performance prediction for fine-tuning remains theoretically ungrounded; understanding fundamental prediction limits is unclear.
approach: Decomposes risk into intrinsic limit (static compatibility) and reducible optimization variance; proves variance admits necessary decay-rate bound and derives budget-optimal probing.
contribution: Derives predictability phase diagram organizing tasks into Static-Sufficient, Dynamic-Critical, and Noise-Dominant regimes; validates on synthetic and real benchmarks.

problem: Best-of-N selection in LLMs relies on unreliable verification—logit confidence suffers calibration collapse while sample agreement is costly and brittle.
approach: Analyzes latent dynamics during inference and introduces Latent Velocity Entropy (LVE), a training-free metric quantifying temporal concentration of representation updates.
contribution: On MATH500, LogNorm-LVE reaches 92.2% Pass@1 at N=10 with only 3 samples; remains informative when logit-confidence fails on reasoning tasks.

problem: Formal mathematics in Lean lacks many folklore lemmas that mathematicians take for granted, limiting usability for everyday mathematical work.
approach: MathlibLemma mines missing connective tissue via modular LLM pipeline: discovery, formalization, and proving of reusable intermediate facts.
contribution: Produces 1,506 Lean-checked proofs with 4,028-statement benchmark; curated subset merged into Mathlib; transforms LLMs from passive to active library contributors.

problem: Data science agent benchmarks have fragmented interfaces, narrow coverage, and lack rigorous data grounding—many tasks solvable without using actual data.
approach: DSGym provides standardized modular framework with quality-filtered tasks, adds DSBio (expert bioinformatics) and DSPredict (challenging prediction), and execution-verified synthesis.
contribution: Enables end-to-end measurement of agent planning, implementation, and validation; training on 2,000 examples substantially improves 4B model on benchmarks.

problem: Federated LoRA suffers from rotational misalignment—semantically equivalent updates represented in different latent subspaces across clients interfere destructively when averaged.
approach: FedRot-LoRA aligns client updates via orthogonal transformations before aggregation to reduce cross-client subspace mismatch without communication cost.
contribution: Convergence analysis shows alignment yields tighter aggregation error bounds; consistently outperforms baselines across heterogeneity levels without restricting expressivity.

problem: Online fair division with many items, few copies, and unknown utility functions makes it difficult to estimate utilities for all item-agent pairs accurately.
approach: Model online fair division as a contextual bandit problem with utility as an unknown function of item-agent features, achieving sub-linear regret.
contribution: Proposes algorithms for online fair division that achieve provable sub-linear regret without requiring large item copy counts.

problem: Fairness methods for continuous protected attributes and regression tasks are scarce, with existing null-space projection approaches limited to linear models.
approach: Extend iterative null-space projection to kernel methods via empirical feature spaces, applying the method to Support Vector Regression for continuous fairness.
contribution: Theoretically derives kernel-based fairness projection applicable to continuous protected attributes with competitive performance against contemporary methods.

problem: Implicit Neural Representations based on vanilla MLPs are believed to have inherent low-frequency bias preventing high-frequency signal representation.
approach: Regulate network rank during training using high-rank-preserving optimizers like Muon, improving activation distributions for high-frequency content.
contribution: Demonstrates that rank degradation, not architecture, causes low-frequency bias, achieving up to +9 dB PSNR improvement with simple MLPs.

problem: Analog and Mixed-Signal circuit sizing requires expert knowledge and faces high dimensionality, nonlinearity, and strict performance constraints without efficient automation.
approach: Use LLM agents in a reflective meta-optimization framework with two-loop optimization: inner loop for sizing, outer loop for adaptive search-space refinement via simulation feedback.
contribution: Proposes AutoSizer achieving higher solution quality, faster convergence, and higher success rates than traditional optimization and LLM-based agents on AMS-SizingBench.

problem: Optimizing pretraining data composition requires balancing computational efficiency with sample efficiency and flexibility across diverse pipeline architectures.
approach: Approach data mixing as reinforcement learning with a parameterized policy that maximizes constructive gradient interference, supporting both proxy and non-proxy modes.
contribution: AC-ODM reaches optimal validation perplexity on Pythia-1B with 66% fewer training steps and achieves 27.5% improvement in MMLU accuracy with negligible overhead.

problem: ML-based surrogate models for aerodynamic simulations require mesh input, making deployment costly for new geometries despite mesh providing lower errors.
approach: Develop SMART, a neural surrogate using point-cloud geometry without mesh, with cross-layer attention between encoder and physics decoder for joint feature-field updating.
contribution: Demonstrates that mesh-free models can match or exceed mesh-dependent methods, enabling efficient surrogate modeling for industry-level aerodynamic simulations.

problem: Auto-regressive mesh generation requires thousands of predictions per inference, creating substantial latency despite high-quality outputs.
approach: Employ lightweight multi-head speculative decoding with verification and resampling, using distillation to align prediction distributions.
contribution: XSpecMesh achieves 1.7× speedup for auto-regressive mesh generation without sacrificing generation quality.

problem: KV cache eviction for long-context LLM inference relies on heuristics without rigorous theoretical foundation, wasting memory and affecting fidelity.
approach: Rethink eviction via Information Bottleneck principle, deriving closed-form mutual information objective and using statistical leverage scores for capacity-aware selection.
contribution: CapKV consistently outperforms prior eviction methods, preserving maximum predictive signal while improving memory-fidelity trade-off.

problem: Evaluation of unsafe content in spoken dialogues is text-centric, missing prosodic evidence and transcription failures critical for audio safety.
approach: Introduce LALM-as-a-Judge benchmark with 24,000 multi-turn dialogues spanning 8 unsafe categories and 5 severity levels, evaluating 6 LALMs across modality configurations.
contribution: Shows audio contributes non-lexical evidence beyond transcripts; multimodal gains vary with audio-pathway bottlenecks; derives practitioner guidance for LALM deployment.

problem: Understanding how syntactic and semantic information is encoded in LLM representations, particularly at scale, remains unclear.
approach: Average hidden representations of sentences sharing syntactic structure or meaning to obtain centroids, measure information loss via similarity metrics.
contribution: Finds syntax and semantics are partially linearly encoded in DeepSeek-V3 with different cross-layer profiles, enabling selective decoupling of linguistic signals.

problem: Long chain-of-thought reasoning with multiple attempts needs RL methods that properly weight per-attempt rewards to optimize multi-attempt success.
approach: Introduce Calibrated Attempt-Level GRPO with unbiased gradient weighting to handle per-attempt feedback while maintaining low variance.
contribution: Theory reveals how per-attempt rewards influence training; CAL-GRPO outperforms vanilla GRPO on multi-attempt chain-of-thought problems.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning of LLMs defaults to negative log-likelihood loss, which violates optimality assumptions during post-training with pre-trained priors and noisy supervision.
approach: Systematically study probability-based objectives across 8 model backbones and 27 benchmarks, characterizing behavior along model-capability continuum.
contribution: Prior-leaning objectives outperform NLL near model-strong end while NLL dominates model-weak end, enabling adapted objectives per capability level.

problem: Why multimodal learning outperforms unimodal approaches lacks rigorous theoretical explanation despite widespread empirical evidence.
approach: Link multimodal advantage to smoother loss landscape via convolutional smoothing theory; introduce stochastic modality pairing during training.
contribution: Shows multimodal models achieve smoother loss landscapes with better robustness and generalization; stochastic pairing further promotes flatness.

problem: LLM-driven multi-agent systems lack systematic organization of inference-time parallelism strategies, missing how replica and structural parallelism interact.
approach: Model two-tier parallelism: Replica (multiple solution paths) and Structural (concurrent task decomposition), proposing TIPEX framework for unified coordination.
contribution: TIPEX demonstrates complementary effects of parallelism levels across task complexities, with intermediate difficulty benefiting most from coordination.

problem: Large Audio-Language Models easily elicit harmful responses from audio inputs compared to text, lacking effective safety alignment mechanisms.
approach: Propose SARSteer with text-derived refusal steering and decomposed safe-space ablation to mitigate over-refusal while maintaining benign-query robustness.
contribution: SARSteer significantly improves harmful-query refusal in LALMs while preserving benign responses, establishing principled safety alignment for audio modality.

problem: Standard Subsampled Natural Gradient Descent analyses using stochastic preconditioning lack insight into realistic small-sample settings.
approach: Analyze SNG as sketch-and-project method with squared volume sampling proxy, enabling single mini-batch convergence and explicit rate characterization.
contribution: Provides global convergence guarantees for any mini-batch size and reveals how SNG exploits spectral decay in model Jacobian better than SGD.

problem: AI agents need systematic evaluation on realistic bioinformatics tasks with robustness testing and local deployment for privacy-sensitive workflows.
approach: Introduce BioAgent Bench with manually curated end-to-end bioinformatics tasks, LLM-based grading, and perturbation robustness tests.
contribution: Shows frontier LLMs can complete pipelines reliably but fail under perturbations; identifies need for local agents to preserve patient data privacy.

problem: High dynamic range novel view synthesis suffers from geometric artifacts and radiometric distortions under multi-exposure conditions due to exposure and structure not being jointly addressed.
approach: Decompose HDR-NVS into Irradiance and Geometry fields with exposure-aware signed distance function that reweights supervision by local exposure reliability.
contribution: Expo-GS achieves peak PSNR of 39.06 dB under HDR and 41.38 dB in LDR-OE, preserving high-frequency textures and maintaining structural consistency.

problem: Agentic multimodal models experience premature interaction collapse due to terminal reward design preventing advantage distinction and redundant context hindering feedback absorption.
approach: Derive advantage signals from whole rollout trajectories; use differentiated Gaussian rewards to dynamically calibrate interaction tolerance and reduce redundancy.
contribution: DR-MMSearchAgent achieves state-of-the-art on FVQA-test with 8.4% improvement over MMSearch-R1 through trajectory-level advantage estimation.

problem: Large Reasoning Models post-trained via RL exhibit exploration collapse where temperature sampling fails to improve pass@n accuracy.
approach: Diagnose entropy asymmetry between final and intermediate layers; propose Latent Exploration Decoding to aggregate intermediate posteriors with maximal entropy.
contribution: LED improves pass@1 and pass@16 accuracy by 0.61 and 1.03 percentage points without training, restoring exploration post-RL fine-tuning.

problem: Personalized federated LoRA assumes homogeneous client needs and dual LoRA creates conflicting optimization objectives, limiting scalability across heterogeneous scenarios.
approach: Decouple LoRA into generalized and personalized subspaces via single adapter, integrate cross-client knowledge via SVD compression, use OOD-oriented weighting at inference.
contribution: Het-CPFLoRA outperforms state-of-art in both personalization and generalization across heterogeneous client data distributions.

problem: Naive quantization of LLMs degrades performance due to large magnitude outliers in activations, making naive INT4 quantization impractical.
approach: Introduce three lightweight function-preserving transforms: pre-RoPE transform, value transform, and dynamic scaling; train end-to-end matching full-precision outputs.
contribution: FPTQuant enables static INT4 quantization with 3.9× speedup over FP and performance matching most prior work without custom kernels.

problem: Differentiating through quadratic program solutions via KKT systems incurs high computational cost and numerical robustness issues at scale.
approach: Decouple QP solving from differentiation using penalty-based framework; map to smooth approximate penalty problem and implicitly differentiate.
contribution: dXPP achieves substantial speedups on large-scale problems while maintaining robustness, avoiding explicit KKT differentiation difficulties.

problem: Vision-language models generate fluent causal explanations but lack evaluation distinguishing linguistic plausibility from faithful causal reasoning.
approach: Introduce dual-probe methodology: Text-Only and Chain-Text probes; define Abstraction Gap metric quantifying normalized performance difference across Pearl's hierarchy.
contribution: CAGE benchmark reveals 7 of 8 VLMs exhibit large abstraction gaps despite high text scores, showing causal reasoning and fluency are dissociable.

problem: Unclear to what extent transformers can implement exact algorithmic computations like clustering beyond statistical modeling.
approach: Specify transformer implementation from first principles executing Lloyd's k-means algorithm using attention, residuals, and feed-forward blocks.
contribution: k-means transformer exactly implements Lloyd's algorithm; trained models generalize beyond Lloyd's, achieving better clustering quality.

problem: SAM3D enables 3D reconstruction but deployment is hindered by prohibitive inference latency due to pipeline heterogeneity.
approach: Conduct systematic investigation revealing multi-level heterogeneity; propose Fast-SAM3D with modality-aware caching, spatiotemporal token carving, and spectral-aware aggregation.
contribution: Fast-SAM3D delivers up to 2.67× end-to-end speedup with negligible fidelity loss on single-view 3D generation.

problem: Understanding implicit bias in deep networks through gradient-based training lacks tractable singular-value dynamics beyond balanced deep linear models.
approach: Propose signatures of deep Jacobians: depth-induced exponential scaling and strong spectral separation; prove Lyapunov exponents govern singular values in piecewise-linear networks.
contribution: Shows singular-value dynamics decouple under sufficient separation, mirroring balanced deep-linear analyses and mechanistically explaining implicit bias.

problem: Linearized fine-tuning produces disentangled task vectors but suffers limited expressivity and higher inference cost than standard non-linear fine-tuning.
approach: Distill hidden representations from curvature-regularized linearized teacher into non-linear student via activation-space constraints.
contribution: Distilled model inherits linearization properties for task arithmetic without inference overhead, achieving effective composition across vision and language.

problem: Lower bounds for nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization are underdeveloped due to bilevel structure complexity and gaps with upper bounds.
approach: Develop hard instances using zero-respecting algorithms to establish lower bounds under deterministic and stochastic first-order oracle models.
contribution: Proves Ω(κ^{3/2}ε^{-2}) deterministic and Ω(κ^{5/2}ε^{-4}) stochastic oracle calls necessary, strengthening bounds for bilevel and min-max problems.

problem: Multimodal spatial reasoning with geometry priors from 3D encoders uses passive fusion, inducing semantic-geometry misalignment and redundant signals.
approach: Shift to active perception paradigm via Spatial-Grounded Fusion with selective geometric retrieval conditioned on reasoning demands, calibrated by Importance Gating.
contribution: GeoThinker achieves 72.6 on VSI-Bench with robust generalization across embodied referring and autonomous driving tasks.

problem: Pretraining transformers on long sequences is bottlenecked by quadratic attention cost, limiting context length and throughput.
approach: Propose Multipole Semantic Attention clustering queries and keys in representation space to yield query-specific summaries, enabling 64k-context pretraining.
contribution: MuSe accelerates 64k-context pretraining by 36% while matching baseline loss, compatible with Llama 3.1-8B and 3.2-1B without retraining.

problem: Existing benchmarks for multi-reference image creation and editing are limited to single-reference or narrowly defined tasks, leaving complex multi-concept composition unexplored.
approach: Introduce MICE-Bench with 3,119 test cases spanning 7 visual dimensions and up to 7-concept configurations; evaluate 13 SOTA models with 8-dimensional metrics.
contribution: Shows all models experience degradation in concept consistency under complexity; closed-source models maintain advantage, indicating substantial improvement room.

problem: Minimum Bayes Risk decoding calculates expected utility using asymmetric evaluation metrics without accounting for bidirectional hypothesis-reference effects.
approach: Decompose MBR into four interacting components via noisy channel formulation: hypothesis-to-reference and reference-to-hypothesis likelihoods, priors.
contribution: Channel-wise decomposition reveals distinct metric characteristics across tasks while remaining consistent, enabling metric-specific interpretability.

problem: Computational pathology relies on patch-level features departing from cell-centric reasoning, limiting sensitivity to micro-lesions and lacking unified local-global solutions.
approach: Propose Cello with cell-wise features via protein-signal supervision, prototype-based contrastive learning, weakly supervised gating, and decision-route consistency.
contribution: Cello outperforms SOTA pathology foundation models trained on 10-50× more samples, achieving 3.0-7.6% gains on local and global pathology tasks.

problem: Diffusion-based Q-learning requires multi-step denoising for training and inference, resulting in high computational cost and brittleness.
approach: Adopt divide-and-conquer of flow displacement: learn short-range displacements from Flow Matching, bootstrap to learn single-step noise-to-action mapping.
contribution: BFQ improves D4RL performance while significantly reducing computational cost compared to multi-step diffusion, enabling single-step generation.

problem: Understanding how and why LLMs fail lacks principled discovery methods, with existing approaches finding isolated failures without structured failure mode analysis.
approach: Formulate probing as hierarchical Monte Carlo Tree Search balancing global exploration and local refinement; restrict to verifiable cases and consolidate into interpretable failure modes.
contribution: ProbeLLM reveals broader, cleaner, finer-grained failure landscapes than static benchmarks, enabling shift from case-centric toward structured weakness discovery.

problem: Constitutional AI focused on single-model alignment; multi-agent systems create novel alignment challenges through emergent social dynamics requiring behavioral norms.
approach: Use LLM-driven genetic programming to evolve constitutions maximizing societal stability via grid-world simulation with survival pressure and conflict metrics.
contribution: Evolved constitution achieves 123% higher societal stability than human-designed baselines by discovering that minimal communication outperforms verbose coordination.

problem: Classifier-based quality filtering improves downstream task performance but mechanisms remain unclear, particularly regarding its effect on high-quality data.
approach: Analyze CQF empirically and theoretically; show CQF implicitly filters both low and high-quality sets; introduce optimization-driven quality notion.
contribution: CQF outperforms direct high-quality training because it filters low-quality data without harming high-quality, revealing mechanisms behind quality selection.

problem: Off-policy reinforcement learning overestimation bias stems from total value uncertainty, but existing methods target only epistemic component, enabling massive aleatoric impulse.
approach: Disentangle total value uncertainty into epistemic and aleatoric, model via per-frame weighted recombination; use pessimistic lower bounds for critic, optimistic for actor.
contribution: DSAC-AID achieves state-of-the-art on Gym-MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite by surgically suppressing aleatoric impulse while maintaining exploration.

problem: Neural acoustic fields modeling time-domain impulse responses struggle to capture frequency-selective wave behaviors in confined, resonant environments.
approach: Learn continuous complex-valued frequency response fields directly; impose physics-based Kramers-Kronig consistency constraint for causal attenuation-phase coupling.
contribution: INFER reduces magnitude and phase reconstruction errors by over 39% and 51% across benchmarks and car cabins, achieving state-of-the-art acoustic modeling.

problem: Fine-grained traffic prediction requires task-specific models that are computationally expensive, while city-scale pre-trained models miss lane-level requirements.
approach: MiniTraffic uses frequency domain stability augmentation to address data scarcity and contrastive clustering to capture road-lane correlations, building small-scale graph structures that can be fine-tuned with minimal target data.
contribution: The lightweight framework demonstrates superior performance on six fine-grained datasets while significantly reducing model parameters for practical deployment.

problem: Approximate tensorization of entropy (ATE) makes sampling and distribution testing efficient for unimodal cases, but mixtures of few ATE distributions do not necessarily preserve this property, leaving multimodal settings without theoretical guarantees.
approach: Establishes fast mixing of Glauert dynamics with data-based initialization for mixtures of log-Sobolev distributions, and develops efficient identity-testers for mixtures using coordinate-conditional sampling.
contribution: Provides optimal sample complexity guarantees for multimodal distributions and answers an open question on identity-testing for ATE mixtures.

problem: Current neural image quality assessment metrics are slow and vulnerable to adversarial attacks, limiting their use in compression and restoration applications.
approach: BiRQA processes complementary features via a bidirectional multiscale pyramid with bottom-up attention and top-down cross-gating, using Anchored Adversarial Training with ranking loss to enhance robustness.
contribution: Achieves 3x speedup over prior SOTA while reaching SROCC 0.60-0.84 under white-box attacks on KADID-10k, combining fast inference with strong adversarial resilience.

problem: The connection between diffusion models' generative capabilities and their role as self-supervised representation learners remains underexplored.
approach: Decomposes features into invariant and residual components, deriving Invariant Contamination Ratio (ICR) as a Fisher-based metric to jointly evaluate representation and generation quality across noise levels.
contribution: Reveals that invariance peaks at intermediate noise levels and that ICR detects memorization onset from training features alone, without external evaluators.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems require collaborative data that is often distributed across organizations with privacy and compliance constraints, but existing federated paradigms treat clients independently and ignore workflow dependencies.
approach: FedWave models inter-stage dependencies via a Value Chain Layer, combines federated LoRA with a shared Mixture-of-Experts router, and applies Direct Preference Optimization based on router-induced preferences.
contribution: Demonstrates that federated multi-agent systems can remain competitive with centralized approaches while preserving data locality across diverse LLM backbones.

problem: Visuomotor policies struggle with generating smooth, coherent trajectories for complex manipulation because they balance precision and foresight poorly, resulting in inter-chunk discontinuities.
approach: FocalPolicy combines frequency-optimized chunking with locally anchored flow matching, using a foresight composite objective that supervises time-domain alignment in proximal actions while regularizing frequency-domain structure across future chunks.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches in learning coherent long-horizon actions with improved cross-chunk consistency.

problem: Surface reconstruction via differentiable rendering is bottlenecked by photometric ambiguities that create ill-posed geometry solutions.
approach: AmbiSuR leverages Gaussian Splatting to address primitive-wise photometric ambiguities through photometric disambiguation constraints and an ambiguity indication module that identifies and corrects underconstrained reconstructions.
contribution: Achieves superior surface reconstruction performance across challenging scenarios while maintaining broad compatibility.

problem: Explainable classification models often sacrifice interpretability for accuracy, and most symbolic regression methods are computationally expensive.
approach: ECSEL learns closed-form signomial equations that directly serve as both classifier and explanation, leveraging the observation that many symbolic regression benchmarks admit compact signomial structure.
contribution: Recovers more target equations than SOTA methods with substantially less computation while maintaining competitive classification accuracy with full interpretability.

problem: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism suffers from gradient staleness that scales linearly with pipeline depth due to misalignment between the Hessian eigenbasis and standard coordinate basis.
approach: Proposes basis rotation that aligns the optimizer's coordinate system with the Hessian eigenbasis, reducing oscillations in update trajectories and keeping delayed updates useful.
contribution: Theoretically demonstrates that basis rotation minimizes basis misalignment and empirically shows reduced iterations needed for LLM training up to 3B parameters.

problem: Convergence analysis of the Lion optimizer in centralized and distributed settings is not well understood, particularly regarding communication efficiency.
approach: Provides comprehensive convergence analysis establishing O(d^1/2 T^-1/4) rate for original Lion, proposes variance reduction variant with O(d^1/2 T^-1/3) rate, and extends to distributed settings with sign compression.
contribution: Establishes linear speedup with respect to number of nodes and introduces communication-efficient variants with convergence guarantees.

problem: The relationship between end-to-end equivariance and layerwise equivariance in deep networks is unclear, particularly under parameter identifiability.
approach: Proves that for networks with equivariant end-to-end functions, there exists a parameter choice yielding layers that are equivariant with respect to group actions on latent spaces, grounded in abstract formalism.
contribution: Provides mathematical explanation for the emergence of equivariant structures in neural network weights during training.

problem: Offline RLHF pipelines like DPO are vulnerable to preference poisoning attacks through label flips, which can manipulate model behavior with minimal perturbations.
approach: Converts poisoning attacks into structured binary sparse approximation problems and develops Binary-Aware Lattice Attack (BAL-A) and Binary Matching Pursuit Attack (BMP-A) to efficiently find optimal label flips.
contribution: Demonstrates how dictionary geometry governs attack success and provides coherence-based recovery guarantees and robustness certificates.

problem: Current multimodal models process diverse modalities with identical parameters, ignoring their inherent representational differences and missing opportunities for modality-specific optimization.
approach: MoST introduces Modality-Aware Mixture of Experts with specialized routing pathways for speech and text tokens, combining modality-specific expert groups with shared experts for cross-modal understanding.
contribution: Consistently outperforms comparable models across ASR, TTS, audio language modeling, and spoken question answering benchmarks using fully open-source datasets.

problem: Understanding and exploiting the stability properties of latent flow matching models under perturbations could yield practical efficiency gains for training and inference.
approach: Characterizes LFM models' robustness by their tendency to generate similar outputs under identical noise seeds, relating this to flow matching theory, and proposes sample-scoring criteria for efficient training and coarse-to-fine inference.
contribution: Demonstrates data savings through reduced datasets while maintaining quality, and achieves over 2x inference speedup with lightweight-then-heavy architecture approach.

problem: Graph foundation models face transferability and data scarcity challenges, and prior approaches are limited to hand-crafted features without pretraining on graph data.
approach: GraphPFN adapts the prior-data fitted networks framework with synthetic graph pretraining using stochastic block models, preferential attachment, and structured causal models for node-level tasks with in-context learning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on diverse real-world graph datasets in both in-context learning and finetuning regimes.

problem: Real-world adaptation of VLA models under strict data budgets is challenged by a diversity trap where maximizing coverage with diverse demonstrations leads to memory contamination due to estimation noise.
approach: Anchor-Centric Adaptation (ACA) decomposes policy error into estimation and extrapolation terms to characterize optimal coverage-density trade-off, then stabilizes a policy skeleton through repeated demonstrations at core anchors before selectively expanding coverage.
contribution: Significantly improves task reliability and success rates over standard diverse sampling strategies under the same budget.

problem: Pure exploration in highly stochastic environments is dominated by variance, and existing methods do not explicitly allocate sampling effort to minimize decision uncertainty.
approach: VarDE formulates exploration by allocating sampling to minimize uncertainty of the final decision through a smooth decision function that captures how stochastic noise affects output reliability.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent and significant improvements over existing methods in Best Arm Identification, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and Best-Policy Identification with theoretical guarantees on variance decay.

problem: LLM-based model discovery typically uses hand-crafted heuristic procedures without explicit probabilistic formulation, limiting principled reasoning about model proposal and refinement.
approach: ModelSMC recasts model discovery as probabilistic inference using Sequential Monte Carlo sampling, representing candidate models as particles proposed and refined by an LLM with likelihood-based weighting.
contribution: Discovers models with interpretable mechanisms and improves posterior predictive checks across real-world scientific systems.

problem: Silent errors in LLM serving frameworks degrade output quality without explicit error signals, and diagnosing them is difficult due to the large semantic gap between symptoms and root causes.
approach: Ekka frames diagnosis as differential debugging by comparing intermediate execution states between target and reference implementations, systematically aligning outputs to identify mismatches.
contribution: Achieves 80% pass@1 and 88% pass@5 diagnosis accuracy on real-world silent errors, outperforming SOTA and identifying 4 new bugs confirmed by developers.

problem: Video action models trained with likelihood-oriented objectives emphasize globally plausible futures but do not guarantee precision-critical visual dynamics needed for manipulation.
approach: Dyn-VPP casts multi-step denoising as policy optimization aligned with expert visual dynamics via verifiable terminal reward, without modifying architecture.
contribution: Yields more accurate visual dynamics and consistently higher task success across simulated and real-world manipulation settings.

problem: Prototype-based federated learning suffers from semantic drift across clients when updating global prototypes via averaging, leading to misaligned global signals.
approach: FedHPro introduces hyper-prototypes optimized via gradient matching to align with class-relevant characteristics, then promotes inter-class separability via mutual-contrastive learning while encouraging intra-class uniformity.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance under diverse heterogeneous scenarios with more semantically consistent global signals.

problem: ANN-to-SNN conversion faces a fidelity-latency trade-off because open-loop error accumulation worsens as timestep T increases, even with conversion-aware training.
approach: Proposes closed-loop fine-tuning with Dual Alignment Mechanism using global KL divergence and adaptive local Centered Kernel Alignment constraint weighted by initial conversion loss.
contribution: Achieves over 99% of source ANN accuracy at T=32 and produces SNNs with input noise robustness matching or exceeding source ANNs.

problem: LLM agents with strong reasoning capabilities behave less cooperatively in mixed-motive games, yet methods for enabling cooperation in social dilemmas are underexplored.
approach: CoopEval benchmarks game-theoretic mechanisms including repetition, reputation systems, mediation, and contracts across four social dilemmas to identify which enable cooperative outcomes.
contribution: Demonstrates that contracting and mediation are most effective for capable LLM cooperation, and that evolutionary pressures improve mechanism effectiveness.

problem: Process reward models require expensive step annotations, and implicit PRMs using log-likelihood-ratio rewards suffer from train-inference mismatch where local prefix credits are weakly identified.
approach: IPVRM directly learns probability of eventual correctness per prefix, derives step signals as TD differences between consecutive prefix values, then applies Distribution-Level RL with dense counterfactual updates.
contribution: Markedly improves step-verification F1 on ProcessBench and shows consistent improvements in downstream reasoning when paired with reliable prefix values.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning faces value overestimation when querying out-of-distribution actions due to distribution shift.
approach: REG formulates policy evaluation as robust optimization over ambiguity sets of critics, proposing Orthogonal Policy Gradient that regularizes aggressive policy gradients by projecting onto the orthogonal subspace to stable in-sample behavior cloning.
contribution: Matches state-of-the-art performance among Gaussian and diffusion-based methods without the computational burden of diffusion approaches.

problem: Memory-based test-time adaptation suffers from memory contamination due to inaccurate CLIP predictions and biased sample eviction that discards informative samples.
approach: A2Memory proposes Attribute-centric Memory Construction using class-shared representative attributes for soft assignment, and Class-wise Associative Memory for dynamic gradient-based compression and sample-adaptive class prototypes.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods across 15 benchmarks.

problem: Contextual optimization with missing covariates is challenging because fully observed data assumptions are often violated, and impute-then-optimize pipelines are unreliable.
approach: Proposes distributionally robust optimization that builds ambiguity sets from partial data while incorporating the missingness mechanism structure, ensuring candidate distributions remain consistent with observations.
contribution: Consistently outperforms impute-then-optimize baselines in both out-of-sample performance and reliability across contextual decision-making tasks.

problem: Building reliable applications with LLMs is difficult because their outputs lack accuracy guarantees and uncertainty propagation through multi-step flows is poorly understood.
approach: PPDL introduces a probabilistic language for LLM-based flows that enables developers to quantify and propagate uncertainty throughout applications while experimenting with inference scaling without modifying flow logic.
contribution: Demonstrates the capability through case studies on theorem proving agents.

problem: Recovering causal effects from selected populations with selection bias is fundamental for causal inference, but existing identifiability conditions are often restrictive.
approach: Provides necessary and sufficient conditions for ATE identifiability under selection bias using weak assumptions on probability classes to characterize propensity and selection probabilities.
contribution: Offers more comprehensive understanding of causal effect identification with strictly weaker conditions than existing frameworks.

problem: Identifying well-designed architectures for tabular data in a data-adaptive and budget-aware manner is challenging, and tabular foundation models require heavy inference costs.
approach: pTNAS combines filter-and-refine optimization with pTProxy, a zero-cost proxy for tabular networks capturing trainability and expressivity, and budget-aware coordination for optimal allocation.
contribution: Reduces time to reach globally best architecture by up to 82.75x and improves end-to-end efficiency by up to 4.78x compared to other NAS approaches.

problem: Controlling false discovery rate under complex sparsity structures in LLM analysis is challenging, particularly when sparsity arises at the group level after linear transformation.
approach: Split Group Knockoffs (SGK) extends the Split Knockoff procedure to group-wise variable selection under transformed sparsity with group-level FDR control guarantees.
contribution: Effectively distinguishes genuine behavioral deviations from surface-level performance variation in LLM behavior auditing.

problem: Large language models struggle with reasoning as horizon length increases, yet methods to scale long-horizon capabilities using only short-horizon data are lacking.
approach: Bootstraps long-horizon reasoning by synthetically composing simple problems into complex multi-step dependency chains, training with outcome-only rewards under automatic curriculum that increases complexity.
contribution: Shows remarkable generalization from 6th-grade composed math to longer competition-level benchmarks and diverse out-of-distribution domains.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs on new tasks triggers severe long-tailed forgetting of prior knowledge, even under narrow updates when pre-training data is inaccessible.
approach: ALER uses adversarial search to find small sets of latent prompt embeddings maximizing logit divergence from frozen reference model, then performs online distillation with discovered embeddings.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements in retention-adaptation frontier across domain-specific datasets and general-purpose benchmarks with theoretical efficiency guarantees.

problem: Most relational deep learning methods rely on fixed graph structures because full-resolution design principles are required to preserve relational semantics, limiting adaptability.
approach: FROG formulates relational structure learning as learnable table role modeling, allowing tables to contribute as nodes and edges, with role-driven message passing and functional dependency constraints.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches while revealing how table roles impact downstream tasks.

problem: Detecting use of sensitive or copyrighted texts in LLM fine-tuning under black-box access with statistical guarantees is challenging.
approach: Proposes marking sensitive texts with invisible Unicode (cue, reply) pairs, triggering regurgitation during audits while comparing against counterfactual marks and applying ranking tests.
contribution: Achieves 96.7% true positive rate at 0% false positive rate with only 40 marked documents.

problem: Vision State Space Models require serializing 2D images into 1D sequences using fixed scan orders, inducing anisotropic representations brittle under geometric transformations.
approach: PRIS-Mamba decomposes images into concentric rings with permutation-invariant aggregation within rings and cross-ring dependencies via radial SSMs, and introduces partial channel filtering for efficiency.
contribution: Improves accuracy, efficiency, and rotation robustness over prior Vision SSMs with implications for generalization beyond architectural scaling.

problem: Time-to-First-Spike coding in SNNs offers extreme sparsity and energy efficiency but suffers from unstable training and low accuracy due to sparse firing.
approach: Proposes training framework incorporating parameter initialization, training normalization, temporal output decoder that aggregates spikes to encourage earlier firing, and re-evaluation of pooling layer.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on MNIST (99.48%), Fashion-MNIST (92.90%), CIFAR10 (90.56%), CIFAR100 (70.27%), and DVS Gesture (95.83%).

problem: Time-series forecasting is evaluated solely on numerical accuracy without examining reasoning capabilities, treating foundation models as black boxes.
approach: TFRBench provides protocol for evaluating reasoning via multi-agent framework with iterative verification loop to synthesize numerically grounded reasoning traces across five domains.
contribution: Confirms reasoning is causally effective; prompting LLMs with generated traces improves average accuracy from 40.2% to 56.6%, establishing new standard for interpretable reasoning-based evaluation.

problem: Traditional GANs learn arbitrary transport maps between noise and data distributions leading to training instability, and consistency-based methods require learning intermediate timesteps with error accumulation.
approach: Adversarial flow models encourage generators to learn deterministic noise-to-data mappings, supporting native one-step and multi-step generation trained with adversarial objective without intermediate supervision.
contribution: Achieves FID of 2.38 with B/2 model at 1NFE on ImageNet-256px, and 1.94 with 112-layer model surpassing 4NFE counterparts with equal compute.

problem: Multi-adapter serving systems route entire sequences to single adapters, failing when requests span multiple domains or require mixed capabilities within one sequence.
approach: MoLoRA introduces per-token routing that routes individual tokens to adapters based on vocabulary structure or learned gating, enabling composable specialization with multiple domain-specific adapters.
contribution: Enables Qwen3-1.7B to exceed Qwen3-8B across four reasoning benchmarks while being 4.7x smaller, with modular expertise loadable at inference time.

problem: Existing data augmentation techniques produce augmented images with visual artifacts, unrealistic blending, and label mismatches that create extra label noise.
approach: SCalDA calibrates semantics across image, label, and feature domains through semantics-driven synthesis and includes semantics-aware metric learning to align augmented data with ground truth.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements for both fine-grained and general image classification tasks through precise guidance across three domains.

problem: Federated graph learning methods assume reliable local graph structures and lack awareness of parameter importance during aggregation, leading to representation degradation under topological noise and catastrophic forgetting.
approach: GraphP-FL uses self-supervised dynamic topology reconstruction to rectify noisy topologies and introduces Fisher-based Elastic Parameter Alignment to quantify parameter importance and prevent catastrophic forgetting.
contribution: Improves accuracy by up to 8.6% on seven benchmarks including biochemical molecules and social networks.

problem: Existing tree-RAG methods fail to scale to cross-document multi-hop questions due to poor distribution adaptability, structural isolation across documents, and coarse abstraction.
approach: Ψ-RAG builds a hierarchical abstract tree through iterative merging and collapsing that adapts to data distributions, combined with a multi-granular retrieval agent that intelligently reorganizes queries.
contribution: Outperforms RAPTOR by 25.9% and HippoRAG 2 by 7.4% in average F1 score on cross-document multi-hop QA benchmarks.

problem: Theoretical possibility of language generation in the limit exists, but computational feasibility remains unexplored for formal languages.
approach: Studies sample complexity barriers for canonical formal language classes including context-free, regular, and pattern languages using classical computability-theoretic methods.
contribution: Establishes that infeasibility appears already for context-free and regular languages, showing a clear gap between theoretical possibility and computational feasibility.

problem: Traditional functional data analysis methods are limited by linearity while deep learning approaches lack interpretable region selection, creating a tradeoff between model expressiveness and interpretability.
approach: sBayFDNN combines deep Bayesian neural networks with structured priors that enable region-wise selection of influential domains, maintaining both nonlinearity and interpretability.
contribution: Provides first theoretical guarantees for a Bayesian deep functional model and excels in identifying functionally meaningful regions with quantified uncertainty.

problem: Option-based hierarchical RL faces a tradeoff: charging deliberation costs encourages longer options but model errors compound over multi-step execution, degrading plan quality.
approach: Formalizes this tradeoff through commitment loss analysis under two error mechanisms: statistical error from finite-data maximum-likelihood estimation and drift-induced mismatch from unobserved state evolution.
contribution: Characterizes optimal termination probabilities as a function of deliberation cost and error scale, clarifying behavior of popular HRL algorithms.

problem: Deriving symbolic expressions from circuit schematics requires accurate visual-to-symbolic reconstruction and correct multi-step symbolic derivation, both imposing strict correctness requirements.
approach: AutoVSR reconstructs circuit diagrams into an executable intermediate representation guided by component rule retrieval, then uses a symbolic solver planning agent with a symbolic tool library for reliable derivation.
contribution: Achieves 30.01-59.45% accuracy improvement over end-to-end VLM approaches and 41.96-51.84% over specialized methods.

problem: It remains unclear whether strong convexity of constraint sets yields Frank-Wolfe convergence rates faster than O(1/√ε) uniformly across all optimizer positions.
approach: Constructs worst-case Frank-Wolfe trajectories for minimizing a strongly convex quadratic over the unit ball with the optimizer on the boundary, using detailed dynamics analysis and novel computational techniques.
contribution: Establishes a tight lower bound of Ω(1/√ε), showing known uniform O(1/√ε) guarantees are tight.

problem: Understanding how multi-trial temporal data with multi-categorical labels encode different label categories and disentangling their distinct effects remains difficult.
approach: MILCCI extends sparse per-trial decomposition with label similarities within each category to enable label-driven cross-trial adjustments and distinguish category contributions.
contribution: Identifies interpretable components underlying multi-trial data while capturing cross-trial variability and integrating label information.

problem: LLMs traditionally scale along dense dimensions where performance couples with near-linear compute increases; MoE decouples capacity from compute but introduces memory overhead and hardware inefficiency.
approach: ReToken and MoRT introduce token-indexed parameters retrieved from auxiliary embedding tables that modulate layers via lightweight element-wise operations with negligible FLOPs.
contribution: Reduces validation loss and improves downstream performance (e.g., +7.3 on ARC-C, +6.3 on GSM8K) while achieving 35% less compute than vanilla MoE.

problem: Deep protein structure predictors provide uncalibrated confidence estimates that degrade under distribution shifts across experimental modalities and disordered regions.
approach: CalPro combines a geometric evidential head with differentiable calibration during training and split-conformal calibration for finite-sample coverage, incorporating domain priors as soft constraints.
contribution: Achieves at most 5 percentage points coverage degradation across modalities, reduces calibration error by 30-50%, and improves downstream docking success from 52% to 75%.

problem: Vision-Language models tuned for medical imaging via textual prompts suffer from Medical Manifold Collapse and Medical Topological Misalignment due to high morphological similarity and heterogeneous acquisition protocols.
approach: FedMAP shifts from textual tuning to visual manifold anchoring using an LLM-derived codebook via Manifold Semantic Anchoring and Topology Structural Alignment.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods especially in high-noise regimes where manifold collapse is most severe.

problem: Understanding gradient descent dynamics for neural networks including convergence rate, iterate trajectories, and implicit acceleration remains challenging.
approach: Analyzes nonlinear models with logistic loss showing gradient descent steps reduce to generalized perceptron algorithms, enabling analysis via classical linear algebra.
contribution: Demonstrates nonlinearity in two-layer models yields faster iteration complexity Õ(√d) versus Ω(d) for linear models, helping explain implicit acceleration.

problem: Existing LLM serving systems prioritize intra-workflow optimization while neglecting significant inter-workflow optimization opportunities in multi-tenant agentic workflows.
approach: HeraSys uses fine-grained orchestration to eliminate cross-workflow redundancy via structural node merging and introduces load-aware joint scheduling with adaptive batching.
contribution: Reduces P99 latency by up to 2.17x and increases serving throughput by up to 1.85x under strict latency guarantees.

problem: Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient methods lack fundamental connections to Bayesian approaches and their theoretical foundations remain disconnected from probabilistic inference.
approach: Recovers SVRG as a special case of posterior correction over isotropic-Gaussian posteriors and derives extensions using more flexible exponential-family posteriors.
contribution: Provides first connection between SVRG and Bayesian methods, enabling development of novel Newton-like and Adam-like variants with Hessian corrections.

problem: Existing Meta-Black-Box Optimization focuses on how to search but overlooks where to search in expensive constrained multi-objective optimization.
approach: MetaSG-SAEA uses Max-Min Constraint-Calibrated Inequality for problem-agnostic region abstraction, diffusion-based population initialization, and attention-based state representation.
contribution: Outperforms baselines across diverse benchmarks and generalizes across varying problem dimensions, population sizes, and numbers of objectives.

problem: Hallucinations in LLMs occur when attention transitions from distributed input-grounded computation to compressed prior-dominated computation, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
approach: SinkProbe grounds hallucination detection in attention sinks—tokens accumulating disproportionate attention mass—whose value vectors have large norms.
contribution: Produces state-of-the-art hallucination detection across popular datasets and LLMs while explaining previous methods' implicit dependence on attention sinks.

problem: AI-generated image detection relies on static feature spaces assuming universal zero-shot generalization but fails catastrophically against rapidly evolving generators.
approach: Fleet pioneers dynamic adaptation with continuous few-shot evolution and constrained routing correction that redirects novel samples away from Non-AI-dominated routes.
contribution: Restores performance from 20.4% to 73.1% with only 10-shot adaptation on Doubao Seedream 4.0.

problem: Authorship detection for peer reviews relies solely on textual features without considering the semantic ideas, judgments, and claims reviews express.
approach: Sem-Detect combines textual features with claim-level semantic analysis, comparing target reviews against multiple AI-generated reviews to identify convergence patterns.
contribution: Improves TPR@1% FPR by 36.5% in binary setting; fewer than 3.5% of LLM-refined human reviews misclassified as AI-generated.

problem: Standard reward models predict scalar scores failing to capture multifaceted response quality in non-verifiable domains like creative writing.
approach: Rubric-ARM jointly optimizes a rubric generator and judge using RL from preference feedback, treating rubric generation as a latent action.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly improves downstream policy alignment in both offline and online RL settings.

problem: Pruning LLMs amplifies text degeneration including repetition loops even when perplexity and task accuracy remain unchanged.
approach: Proposes FOCUS and RePAIR token-level guidance objectives that address loop entry risk and persistence through distillation reweighting and onset-centered continuation pairs.
contribution: Consistently reduces repetition and improves generation quality across open-ended and instruction-based generation.

problem: Alignment evaluation lacks realistic multi-turn scenarios with conflicting instructions and escalation that reveal behavioral tendencies missed by single-turn evaluations.
approach: Introduces an alignment benchmark spanning 904 scenarios across six categories validated as realistic by human raters, using LLM judges validated against human annotations.
contribution: Reveals that even top-performing models exhibit gaps in specific categories and shows alignment behaves as a unified construct analogous to the g-factor.

problem: Cultural evaluation frameworks for LLMs focus on matching outputs to ground-truth answers without measuring whether models internalize broader cultural structure.
approach: Uses spectral-analysis-based framework to capture macrostructural patterns in models' cultural knowledge across nine domains and 170 countries.
contribution: Finds instruction-tuned models align more closely with human cultural structure than older models, and spectral metrics better predict ability to serve unfamiliar cultural backgrounds.

problem: Handwritten text recognition faces computational imbalance where most image pixels are background and many sequence positions are blank-dominated.
approach: Spike-HTR uses InkCoder to convert static images into coarse-to-fine input streams and a CTC-guided length reducer to compress blank-dominated stretches.
contribution: Achieves validation/test Character Error Rates of 3.5/5.4, 2.3/2.5, and 4.2/3.9 on IAM, LAM, and READ2016.

problem: Most table question answering queries are extractive or involve simple aggregation, but common real-world queries are implicitly predictive requiring inference of unobserved answers from patterns.
approach: TopBench benchmark assesses LLMs on implicit predictive reasoning including single-point prediction, treatment effect analysis, and complex filtering.
contribution: Reveals current models struggle with intent recognition and accurate intent disambiguation serves as prerequisite for predictive behaviors.

problem: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards causes calibration degeneration where models become excessively over-confident in incorrect answers due to gradient conflicts.
approach: DCPO systematically decouples reasoning and calibration objectives, based on theoretical analysis showing fundamental gradient conflict between accuracy maximization and calibration error minimization.
contribution: Preserves accuracy on par with GRPO while achieving best calibration performance and substantially mitigating over-confidence.

problem: Sequential visual localization in complex indoor environments requires storing extensive image databases or point clouds, leading to significant overhead.
approach: SG2Loc uses compact 3D scene graphs where nodes represent objects with coarse meshes and edges encode spatial relationships, with per-patch semantic features for localization.
contribution: Significantly reduces storage while maintaining performance on real-world datasets through lightweight scene graph representation.

problem: Existing conformal prediction for LLMs relies on exchangeability assumption which rarely holds in online settings where user queries and interests change over time.
approach: PACE sequentially updates time-varying miscoverage parameters with dynamic step size using proactive shift detection and reactive error feedback.
contribution: Reduces deviation from target error rate by up to 60% and accelerates coverage recovery by 2.5x during abrupt shifts.

problem: LLM-as-a-judge aggregation assumes judges provide independent estimates but judges exhibit correlated errors from shared latent confounders like verbosity and training artifacts.
approach: CARE explicitly models judge scores as arising from both latent true-quality signals and shared confounding factors, providing identifiability and recovery guarantees.
contribution: Improves aggregation accuracy across 12 benchmarks, reducing error by up to 26.8%.

problem: Diffusion-based super-resolution models produce high-quality results but require expensive computational costs and some distillation methods fail to preserve realistic details.
approach: RSD trains student networks to produce images such that a fake ResShift model trained on them matches the teacher, enabling single-step restoration.
contribution: Surpasses teacher model and other distillation methods in perceptual metrics while requiring fewer parameters and less training cost.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion model unlearning relies on suboptimal surrogate objectives and surface-level parameter constraints, failing to capture generative dynamics.
approach: POSDA reframes unlearning as preference optimization and introduces score-level distribution alignment to ensure invariance of underlying manifold topology.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art erasure efficacy for object, style, and NSFW unlearning while maintaining superior model utility.

problem: Sharpness-Aware Minimization relies on first-order linearized surrogates for a second-order (curvature) notion, creating a fundamental mismatch.
approach: LE-SAM inverts the traditional mechanism by replacing fixed perturbation radius with fixed loss-space budget, removing gradient-norm signals and shifting toward curvature.
contribution: Consistently outperforms SAM and variants across diverse benchmarks and tasks, achieving state-of-the-art generalization.

problem: Post-trained models memorize alignment training data that could enable steering for improved capabilities, but extraction is often undercounted due to metric choices.
approach: Uses high-quality embedding models for semantic similarity matching to extract alignment training data from post-trained models.
contribution: Demonstrates data extracted from models can train base models recovering meaningful original performance, exposing overlooked risk.

problem: Single-paradigm generative planners for long-horizon tasks lack principled hierarchical decomposition and face computational demands of iterative denoising.
approach: HDFlow uses high-level diffusion planning to generate strategic subgoals in latent space, guiding low-level rectified flow planner for smooth dense trajectories.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on challenging furniture assembly tasks in simulation and real-world.

problem: Sparse and unstable rewards in long-horizon RL tasks with GRPO challenge reward shaping; existing approaches struggle to balance semantic expressiveness and computational efficiency.
approach: GLARE decouples semantic abstraction from credit assignment using symbolic event extraction and Linear Temporal Logic formulas compiled into deterministic automata.
contribution: Outperforms GRPO by 12.1% in success rate while achieving 8.1% improvement over LLM-based judges using only 15% computational cost.
