contribution: CGPO achieves state-of-the-art performance on MuJoCo locomotion tasks and is the first diffusion policy method to succeed on real-world robotic manipulation.

problem: Conformal Prediction suffers from volatile quantile estimation in data-scarce regimes, leading to overly conservative and wide prediction intervals.
approach: RSA-CP aligns real calibration scores with a high-resolution reference distribution using optimal transport mapping to refine quantile increments.
contribution: RSA-CP maintains finite-sample coverage guarantees while consistently producing shorter and more precise prediction intervals.

problem: Long-context LLMs suffer from self-attention as a major efficiency bottleneck during decoding due to repeatedly processing ever-growing KV caches.
approach: BinaryPC constructs compact binary hash codes via binary principal component analysis for data-aware hashing, avoiding random projections or gradient-based training.
contribution: BinaryPC preserves accuracy relative to full attention while achieving 3.56× end-to-end decoding throughput improvement over FlashAttention on modern GPUs.

problem: Tool-using LLMs generalize poorly under shifts in tasks and toolsets because synthesized training lacks sufficient diversity in tool types and tool-use patterns.
approach: DIVE reverses synthesis order by executing diverse real-world tools first and reverse-deriving tasks entailed by traces, scaling diversity across tool-pool coverage and per-task toolset variety.
contribution: Training on 48k DIVE trajectories over 374 tools improves Qwen3-8B by +22 points on 9 OOD benchmarks, outperforming strongest 8B baseline by +68%.

problem: Federated Graph Learning suffers from optimization conflicts when subgraphs exhibit heterogeneous homophily levels, which existing multi-channel solutions address inefficiently.
approach: FedGCM divides clients into groups by homophily level and uses RPGrad, a gradient surgery mechanism based on residual projection, to filter inter-group conflicts.
contribution: FedGCM achieves superior performance on both homophilous and heterophilous graphs without augmenting client-side burden and includes formal convergence analysis.

problem: Activation sparsity for LLM inference acceleration causes severe accuracy degradation because sparsity disrupts input-dependent activation patterns learned during pretraining.
approach: SPON injects learnable, input-independent activation vectors as persistent representational anchors trained via distribution matching, which can be absorbed into bias after training.
contribution: SPON consistently restores performance and stabilizes latent representations across multiple LLM backbones with negligible inference overhead.

problem: Existing federated learning with synthetic data generation assumes balanced global distributions, but real distributions are imbalanced and unknown due to privacy constraints.
approach: FedPDG uses model performance discrepancy between local and global models to identify lacking regions and adapts diffusion via preference optimization for better distribution alignment.
contribution: FedPDG outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to 3.82% accuracy improvement.

problem: Optimal layer-wise learning-rate selection in deep networks lacks precise theoretical characterization of early training dynamics.
approach: The work derives exact closed-form expressions for gradients and test loss after one and two steps, characterizing how learning rates should scale and proving tight approximation error bounds.
contribution: Analysis reveals unequal layer-wise learning rates minimize test loss at initialization but equal rates become optimal afterward, validated empirically.

problem: Few-step diffusion models remain reliant on differentiable reward models, excluding important real-world non-differentiable rewards like human preferences and object counts.
approach: TDM-R1 decouples learning into surrogate reward learning and generator learning, obtaining per-step reward signals from deterministic trajectories for unified RL post-training.
contribution: TDM-R1 scales from 0.6B to 6B parameters, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain metrics across text rendering and preference alignment.

problem: GPU kernel optimization challenges LLMs because it requires understanding hardware architecture and parallel optimization strategies, not just standard coding.
approach: KernelFoundry uses MAP-Elites quality-diversity search with kernel-specific behavioral dimensions, co-evolves meta-prompts with kernels, and applies template-based parameter optimization.
contribution: KernelFoundry consistently outperforms baselines, achieving an average speedup of 2.3 on KernelBench for SYCL kernels.

problem: Watermarking LLM-generated code must respect strict syntactic constraints while embedding detectable patterns, which existing methods struggle to achieve.
approach: CodeTracer uses a policy-driven approach with reinforcement learning to bias token choices during generation, integrating execution feedback and watermark signals into a comprehensive reward system.
contribution: CodeTracer outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both watermark detectability and code functionality across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Contextual slate bandit problems under limited adaptivity require efficient regret bounds when constructing slates from multiple item sets with generalized linear rewards.
approach: B-SlateGLinCB partitions the horizon into O(log log T) batches; RS-SlateGLinCB adaptively updates only O(Nd log T) times. Both exploit diversity assumptions on item sequences.
contribution: B-SlateGLinCB achieves O(Nd^{3/2} √T) regret; RS-SlateGLinCB achieves O(Nd√T), both independent of non-linearity parameter κ.

problem: Existing post-training quantization for few-step diffusion models depends on full-precision calibration and still produces size-quality tradeoffs.
approach: Q-Sched adjusts diffusion sampling trajectories with quantization-aware preconditioning coefficients, using a reference-free Joint Alignment-Quality loss for fine-grained control.
contribution: Q-Sched delivers 4× model size reduction with 15.5% FID improvement over FP16 4-step LCM and 16.6% over FP16 8-step PCM, validated by 80,000+ user annotations.

problem: Knowledge injection into LLMs via synthetic data often relies on complex RL-based methods that suffer from diversity collapse and prompt-engineering overhead.
approach: SPA uses a small set of carefully designed prompts to generate large-scale synthetic data, achieving effectiveness without complex multi-stage pipelines or RL.
contribution: SPA outperforms several strong baselines and serves as a tough-to-beat baseline for knowledge injection, with careful prompt design proving surprisingly effective.

problem: Time-series imputation methods formulate the task as conditional reconstruction over limited context, restricting temporal information propagation and failing to model evolution explicitly.
approach: CTIP formulates imputation as conditional inference along temporal evolution; CBiT uses history compression and a partitioned modeling strategy for efficient feature-based imputation.
contribution: CBiT improves imputation accuracy by reducing Masked MAE by 27.3% and Masked RMSE by 18.6% across different missing rates.

problem: The precise emergence and characterization of induction heads in language model pretraining remains unclear, especially in natural language settings.
approach: The study investigates statistical properties of training data and their relationship to IH formation in both natural and synthetic settings.
contribution: A simple equation combining batch size and context size predicts IH emergence; surface bigram repetition and reliability strongly affect formation.

problem: Symbol grounding in language models—how words acquire meaning via real-world sensorimotor experiences—remains mechanistically unexplored despite evidence of emergence.
approach: The framework systematically traces symbol grounding through mechanistic and causal analysis, showing concentration in middle-layer computations via attention-head aggregation.
contribution: Grounding emerges through aggregate mechanisms in middle layers across Transformers and state-space models but not in LSTMs, with implications for controlling generation reliability.

problem: Rapid generative AI has made multimodal fake news increasingly realistic, but existing detection methods rely on manipulation-specific models with poor generalization.
approach: CORE constructs a Conflict Attribution Corpus with fine-grained conflict annotations and trains MLLMs on conflict-oriented representation enhancement for robust detection.
contribution: CORE surpasses state-of-the-art models by 9.7%, 14.1%, and 11.8% accuracy on DGM4, MMFakeBench, and MDSM benchmarks, generalizing to unseen manipulation types.

problem: Real-world RL for robotic contact-rich tasks requires substantial human-in-the-loop involvement and struggles with visual background disruptions and positional changes.
approach: FTC combines residual RL for base actions with affordance-guided rewards to focus on key interaction regions, optimizing human-in-the-loop implementation to prevent control conflicts.
contribution: FTC outperforms baseline methods on 6 contact-rich tasks, achieving high success rates and accelerating robotic learning under real-world RL settings.

problem: Federated Incremental Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting via replay, but sample replay poses privacy risks and incurs high overhead on resource-constrained edge devices.
approach: Li-FIL uses dense features synthesized by a server-side generator for feature-based replay, with clients extracting high-confidence features via mixup and a partitioned training strategy.
contribution: Li-FIL outperforms state-of-the-art methods by up to 10.14% in accuracy with superior resource efficiency on both old and new tasks.

problem: LLMs remain vulnerable to hallucinations, making systematic evaluation critical, but existing attacks either sacrifice semantic equivalence or fail to produce valid rephrasings.
approach: REALISTA constructs an input-dependent dictionary of valid editing directions via latent-space optimization, combining continuous attack flexibility with semantic realism.
contribution: REALISTA succeeds in attacking reasoning models in free-form settings where prior realistic attacks fail.

problem: ML Interatomic Potentials fail to reproduce the quantum potential energy surface smoothness, causing errors in downstream simulations that standard energy/force evaluations miss.
approach: The Bond Smoothness Characterization Test probes the PES via controlled bond deformations and uses BSCT as an in-the-loop design proxy with a Transformer backbone.
contribution: BSCT correlates strongly with MD stability while requiring a fraction of MD cost; optimizing via BSCT achieves low E/F error, stable MD, and robust property predictions.

problem: Token cramming with fixed budgets and 99% accuracy leaves unclear whether residual errors reflect optimization failures or fundamental compression limits.
approach: Progressive cramming grows target prefix tokens until reconstruction is no longer achievable within a fixed optimization budget, tracing causal degradation via attention knockouts.
contribution: Progressive trajectories reveal that perfect reconstruction is insufficient for meaningful compression; degradation traces to early-layer interactions.

problem: Masked Diffusion Models train on exponentially large masking patterns but must handle structured inference-time masks, creating a train-test mismatch that slows training.
approach: PUMA modifies the forward masking process to align training-time and inference-time patterns, focusing optimization on inference-aligned masks.
contribution: PUMA speeds up pretraining at 125M scale by ~2.3× and offers complementary advantages with autoregressive initialization.

problem: Large reasoning models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks despite safety training, requiring new defense approaches that operate beyond output-level interventions.
approach: CRAFT aligns reasoning models by integrating contrastive representation learning with RL to separate safe and unsafe reasoning trajectories in hidden state space.
contribution: CRAFT delivers 79.0% average improvement in reasoning safety and 87.7% improvement in final-response safety on Qwen3-4B-Thinking and R1-Distill-Llama-8B.

problem: Equilibrium Propagation is limited to conservative systems with reciprocal interactions, preventing its application to broader system classes.
approach: We extend EP to non-conservative systems by modifying the learning phase dynamics with a term proportional to the non-reciprocal part of interactions, and derive this through a variational formulation over an augmented state space.
contribution: We achieve exact gradient computation for EP in arbitrary non-conservative systems including feedforward networks, with improved performance and faster learning than prior proposals.

problem: Flow-based generative models provide strong priors for inverse problems but conditional generation requires computationally expensive trajectory optimization through the model.
approach: We formulate inverse problem solving as a sequence of model predictive control sub-problems, enabling training-free guidance that avoids backpropagation through the flow trajectory.
contribution: MPC-Flow achieves strong performance on image restoration tasks (inpainting, deblurring, super-resolution) and scales to large models like FLUX.2 (32B) on consumer hardware.

problem: Vision-Language Models face a perceptual bandwidth bottleneck: high resolution preserves details but sacrifices context, limiting complex visual reasoning.
approach: We formalize high-resolution reasoning as sequential Bayesian optimal experimental design, deriving a tractable coverage-resolution objective as a proxy for task-relevant information gain.
contribution: FOVEA, a training-free procedure, achieves consistent gains over direct and ReAct baselines on high-resolution benchmarks, with particularly strong improvements in remote-sensing tasks.

problem: Offline meta-RL methods using sequence-based or token-level routing fail to capture task-level structure and inter-task relationships for effective generalization.
approach: Task-Guided Router (TGR) explicitly models inter-task relationships through multi-view task representations combining semantic descriptors, behavioral summaries, and latent dynamics, enabling structure-guided expert routing.
contribution: TGR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art offline meta-RL methods in few-shot generalization across continuous-control benchmarks, especially under sparse data and heterogeneous dynamics.

problem: Fine-tuning APIs create attack surfaces where adversaries can bypass safety measures through targeted fine-tuning of LLM-based content classifiers.
approach: Trojan-Speak uses curriculum learning with GRPO-based hybrid reinforcement learning to teach models a communication protocol that evades LLM-based content classification.
contribution: We achieve 99+% classifier evasion for 14B+ models while incurring less than 5% capability degradation on reasoning benchmarks, demonstrating that LLM-based classifiers alone are insufficient.

problem: Standard RL assumes fixed environment dynamics, but agents could achieve higher rewards by actively modifying the RL model itself through model-changing actions.
approach: We introduce the multi-layer configurable time-varying Markov decision process (MCTVMDP), where lower-level policies operate on non-stationary dynamics configurable through upper-level model-changing actions.
contribution: We formalize a framework enabling agents to jointly optimize both configuration policies and primitive action policies to improve expected long-term reward.

problem: Grokking (sudden memorization-to-generalization transition) is understood mainly for group operations, limiting insights into algebraic structure's role in neural network generalization.
approach: We extend grokking analysis to finite-dimensional algebras (FDA), connecting learning to bilinear products and showing grokking emerges from discrete representation learning in finite fields.
contribution: We provide a unified framework showing how algebraic properties (commutativity, associativity, unitality) and structure tensor properties (sparsity, rank) influence grokking emergence and timing.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems face jailbreak and adversarial collaboration risks; existing defenses rely on brittle external guards or weak self-verification.
approach: AdvEvo-MARL jointly optimizes attackers (synthesizing evolving jailbreak prompts) and defenders (agents trained for both task performance and attack resistance) using co-evolutionary multi-agent RL.
contribution: We keep attack-success rate below 20% compared to 38.33% for baselines while preserving or improving task accuracy (up to +3.67%), demonstrating effective internalized safety.

problem: Current LLM fingerprinting focuses on model provenance but misses instance-level variations (prompt, sampling, quantization) that determine actual deployed behavior.
approach: FLIPS exploits biases in generated binary random sequences to identify LLM configurations, treating instance-level fingerprinting as a regulator-oriented identification task.
contribution: We achieve 96% closed-set and 90% open-set identification accuracy across 237 model instances versus 35% for adapted baselines, enabling regulation of actual deployed behaviors.

problem: Multi-reward alignment in text-to-image generation requires balancing conflicting objectives while avoiding reward hacking where scores increase but perceived quality deteriorates.
approach: PG-OT constructs a prompt-specific Pareto frontier and maps dominated samples toward it via distribution-aware optimal transport, with online/offline optimization strategies.
contribution: We achieve 11% gain in Joint Domination Rate and near 80% win rate in human evaluations, with principled metrics (JDR, JCR) quantifying multi-reward synergy and reward hacking.

problem: Time series modeling requires high-quality supervision but target measurements are scarce due to cost or accessibility, making zero-shot reconstruction to unobserved locations challenging.
approach: ZeroDiff constructs an informed prior from exogenous variables then calibrates reconstruction errors through diffusion, training on observed locations and generalizing to unobserved ones.
contribution: We achieve significant improvements over existing approaches on diverse real-world datasets for zero-shot time series reconstruction.

problem: Audio-visual speech separation relies on implicit multimodal fusion leading to semantic misalignment and contaminated speech representations.
approach: Neuro-SCNet makes selection and compensation explicit: auditory selection uses visually guided gain to isolate targets, while cross-modal compensation integrates temporally aligned articulatory cues.
contribution: We achieve state-of-the-art separation on LRS2, LRS3, and VoxCeleb2 with improved efficiency, validating explicit selection and reliability-aware compensation.

problem: Long-horizon LLM agents face prohibitive inference memory costs and reasoning degradation from unbounded context growth without parameter updates.
approach: ACON optimally compresses observations and history by iteratively refining compression guidelines based on agent failure analysis, then distills the compressor into smaller models.
contribution: We reduce peak token usage by 26-54% while improving task success over existing compression baselines, enabling smaller LMs to function effectively as long-horizon agents.

problem: Multi-agent LLM debates amplify single-model biases into collective norms, raising safety and fairness concerns for real-world deployment.
approach: We propose an analytical framework drawing on physics-inspired social dynamics models to explain collective bias emergence driven by noise and conformity.
contribution: We predict and empirically validate a phase transition to collective bias, showing agent heterogeneity suppresses emergence and insights generalize to realistic decision-making tasks.

problem: Standard graph algorithms for GraphRAG fail on real-world noisy, sparse, or incomplete Knowledge Graphs that lack sufficient explicit edges for multi-hop reasoning.
approach: INSES couples LLM-guided navigation (pruning noise) with embedding-based similarity expansion to recover hidden links, complemented by a lightweight router for query delegation.
contribution: INSES performs favorably compared to RAG and GraphRAG baselines, with notable robustness and adaptability across KGs constructed by varying methods.

problem: Sleeping experts problems with linear numbers of arriving experts prevent sublinear regret; awakening versions require fundamentally new analysis.
approach: For stochastic ACE, we employ pessimism-in-face-of-uncertainty to achieve O(T^2/3) regret; for adversarial ACE, we characterize a trade-off between competitive ratio and regret.
contribution: We provide optimal or near-optimal regret bounds with matching lower bounds for both stochastic and adversarial awakening expert problems.

problem: LLM agents using memory beyond context windows rely on offline query-agnostic construction that discards query-critical information and incurs inefficient costs.
approach: BudgetMem structures memory into modules with three budget tiers, using a lightweight RL-trained router for query-aware budget-tier routing.
contribution: BudgetMem surpasses baselines in high-budget settings and delivers better accuracy-cost frontiers under tight budgets, with analysis clarifying strengths of implementation/reasoning/capacity tiering strategies.

problem: Offline RL relies on finite static datasets restricting generalization beyond training distributions, while synthetic data augmentation often fails on unseen scenarios.
approach: RAD retrieves high-return reachable states from the offline dataset as target states and uses a generative model to generate sub-trajectories for planning.
contribution: RAD achieves competitive or superior performance compared to baselines across diverse benchmarks, improving offline RL policy generalization.

problem: Multimodal LLMs using explicit textual reasoning for visual tasks suffer from information loss, unstable perception-reasoning interaction, and high computational cost.
approach: LDPVR formulates reasoning as a Markov Chain of Recursive State Simplification where explicit textual states are refined under latent transition guidance via Interleaved Latent Grounding.
contribution: We improve reasoning accuracy while maintaining low inference latency across six multimodal reasoning benchmarks using curriculum learning with SFT, distillation, and GRPO.

problem: LLM-based symbolic regression methods remain sample-inefficient because they conflate candidate proposal with search guidance, relying solely on scalar feedback.
approach: Deliberate Evolution decouples symbolic generation from search control by guiding proposals with adaptive operators, analytical tools for diagnosis, and reflective memory.
contribution: DE consistently outperforms LLM-based SR baselines across diverse scientific domains using only 40% of the standard sample budget.

problem: UAV autopilot systems with separate navigation and flight-control hardware prevent holistic scheduling and optimization across the entire pipeline.
approach: UAV² integrates navigation and flight control onto single onboard hardware and formulates scheduling as a partially observable MDP solved with reinforcement learning.
contribution: The learned scheduling policy consistently outperforms fixed-rate scheduling in flight robustness and tracking performance.

problem: Latent manifolds of autoencoders lack computational tools for studying geodesics and geometric operators despite providing interpretable low-dimensional representations.
approach: We describe latent manifolds as implicit submanifolds and develop discrete Riemannian calculus tools by learning an approximate projection via denoising.
contribution: Our framework enables robust computation of geodesic paths and Riemannian exponential maps on latent manifolds across various autoencoders.

problem: Subgraph-based link prediction methods achieve superior performance but suffer from efficiency bottlenecks due to high per-query message-passing computational cost.
approach: MIMO-LP multiplexes multiple query node pairs within a shared latent space during single forward pass, superposing their message-passing while minimizing interference.
contribution: We achieve 14x-44x speedup over existing subgraph-based methods while maintaining comparable predictive performance.

problem: Scientific hypothesis search prioritizes optimization over exploration, leading to diversity collapse when scientists need high-quality alternative hypotheses to hedge downstream uncertainty.
approach: EvoDiverse formulates hypothesis search as a sampling problem using parallel tempering with multiple temperature levels enabling principled information exchange across temperatures.
contribution: We consistently improve both hypothesis quality and diversity under fixed validation budget across molecular discovery, equation discovery, and algorithm discovery.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs on benign multilingual data induces heterogeneous safety drift across languages and evaluation settings without corresponding capability changes.
approach: We conduct comprehensive empirical study of multilingual safety effects through fine-tuning Llama-3.2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 on benign translated data across nine languages.
contribution: We show safety outcomes are highly sensitive to fine-tuning language and evaluation language, with four-fold adversarial compliance increases in some settings, releasing SORRY-Bench-Multilingual.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models face incompatibility between intrinsic pre-training capabilities and post-training, causing visual search failures in long multi-step reasoning.
approach: SeProD uses self-regulation between pre- and post-training models where pre-training model acts as prophet and post-training model selectively accepts tokens via probability-based prophetic sampling.
contribution: SeProD improves multiple visual-search LVLMs across 12 benchmark splits without added computational overhead, enabling coherent multi-step visual reasoning.

problem: Heavy-tailed synaptic weight distributions are pervasive in biological neural networks but their computational role in generalization remains poorly understood.
approach: We develop optimal-transport-based optimization incorporating biological constraints (Dale's principle, heavy-tailed statistics) to train RNNs and analyze generalization via PAC-Bayes framework.
contribution: Heavy-tailed connectivity induces low-rank structure and favorable representational geometry, substantially improving generalization on cognitive tasks.

problem: Collaborative inference transmits intermediate representations enabling model inversion attacks that reconstruct original inputs, while existing defenses perturb shallow layers at utility cost.
approach: We analyze model partitioning to find the Golden Partition Zone (GPZ) where intrinsic resistance emerges via representational transitions marked by rising intra-class mean-squared radius.
contribution: Partitioning at GPZ yields over 4x higher reconstruction MSE compared to shallow splits, with decision-level representations providing 66% stronger resistance.

problem: Midtraining benefits are widespread in language model development but understanding what makes it effective remains unclear.
approach: We propose midtraining functions as distributional bridging and conduct controlled experiments studying domain distance, mixture weights, and timing.
contribution: Midtraining benefits scale with proximity advantage toward target distribution, with early introduction amenable to high mixture weights while late introduction requires lower ones.

problem: Speculative reasoning in multimodal models faces misalignment between speculative drafts and target-verified reasoning, limiting acceleration gains.
approach: DREAM-R trains draft models via Speculative Alignment Policy Optimization (SAPO) with Threshold-based Verification Mechanism (TBVM) enabling stable acceptance and fully parallel reasoning.
contribution: We achieve up to 2.49x speedup on reasoning-heavy benchmarks while preserving target-model accuracy without compromising reasoning quality.

problem: UI-to-code generation formulated as single-pass task mismatches real-world iterative UI development driven by visual feedback and refinement.
approach: We reformulate UI-to-code as interactive visual optimization using Relative Visual Policy Optimization (RVPO), a preference-based RL method optimizing relative visual rankings.
contribution: UI2Code^N achieves state-of-the-art on UI drafting, polishing, and editing benchmarks with continual improvement through iterative visual optimization.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLMs incur substantial memory overhead and mixed-precision quantization suffers from suboptimal expert-wise allocation overlooking router shifts.
approach: GEMQ formulates global expert-level mixed-precision quantization via linear programming capturing model-wide expert importance, with efficient router fine-tuning.
contribution: We significantly reduce memory and accelerate inference with minimal accuracy degradation through iterative refinement of importance estimation.

problem: Domain-specific LLM applications face out-of-domain interactions when treating the model as a black box without examining internal processing.
approach: We show layer transitions via sparse autoencoders (SAE) provide domain-specific signatures for detecting OOD texts through lightweight learning on internal dynamics.
contribution: SAE layer transitions exhibit great capability in distinguishing OOD texts across gemma-2 2B and 9B models with interpretable internal evolution analysis.

problem: Large reasoning models suffer from overthinking, producing unnecessarily long outputs and high latency despite strong performance, with early-exit probing adding overhead.
approach: SpecExit predicts future tokens and early-exit signals from lightweight draft model without probing overhead, leveraging hidden states for efficient reasoning.
contribution: We achieve up to 66% generation length reduction and 2.5x end-to-end speedup compared to speculative decoding without accuracy loss.

problem: LLM hallucinations (factually incorrect plausible responses) persist even when relevant knowledge is present, pointing to retrieval instability rather than knowledge gaps.
approach: APORIA studies repeated responses in sentence-embedding space using Fisher projection to show genuine responses cluster tighter than hallucinated ones.
contribution: We classify hallucinations with F1>90% from 30-50 annotations, releasing SOCRATES-300K dataset of 300k labeled responses for studying geometric hallucination signatures.

problem: Existing sketches for resettable streaming (where keys can be reset to zero) are vulnerable to adaptive adversarial attacks even with polynomial space.
approach: We design adaptively robust sketches via differential privacy and binary tree mechanism for continual observation to protect internal randomness.
contribution: We achieve polylogarithmic space complexity supporting (sub)linear statistics including L_p moments and Bernstein statistics with prefix-max error guarantees.

problem: Vision-language models interpret images at scale making decisions about recommendations and purchases, yet their visual preferences and susceptibilities remain poorly understood.
approach: We treat VLM decision function as latent visual utility inferred through revealed preference via systematically edited images using image generation models.
contribution: Optimized edits significantly shift VLM choice probabilities, revealing consistent visual themes driving selection and supporting proactive auditing.

problem: Action-controllable world models are limited by action label scarcity; latent action learning often fails to transfer across contexts due to entangled scene-specific cues.
approach: Olaf-World uses Seq-REPA (sequence-level control-effect alignment) to anchor latent actions to temporal feature differences, enabling cross-context action transfer.
contribution: We learn structured latent action spaces with stronger zero-shot transfer and data-efficient adaptation to new control interfaces over state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Transferring conceptual knowledge from language-only models to vision-only students typically requires paired multimodal data which is scarce.
approach: LaViD elicits conceptual signals by prompting LLM to generate multiple-choice questions probing semantic distinctions, mapping each class to soft label distributions.
contribution: Despite using no image data, LaViD outperforms vision-language model distillation across fine-grained benchmarks and improves worst-group accuracy on Waterbirds.

problem: Extending LLM capabilities to new skills via fine-tuning risks catastrophic forgetting; context-based approaches have limited expressiveness constrained by effective context.
approach: Skill neologisms are soft tokens optimized for specific skills that enable selective capability acquisition without weight updates and support zero-shot composition.
contribution: Independently trained skill neologisms compose zero-shot and maintain out-of-distribution skill compatibility on synthetic and natural language tasks.

problem: Compute-in-memory accelerators degrade neural network accuracy due to hardware-induced weight perturbations from noise and device drift during edge inference.
approach: Diversity-aware Weight Perturbation (DWP) uses an immune-system-inspired method that emulates selection by exploiting prediction disagreement under diverse noise to adaptively weight samples and build robustness.
contribution: DWP-trained models achieve over 15% accuracy improvements under severe weight perturbations and maintain 90% inference accuracy over simulated one-year CIM operation.

problem: Autonomous agents with fixed action spaces cannot generalize across diverse tasks and suffer from compounding errors in decoupled policy execution.
approach: DeepHA unifies heterogeneous action spaces via a hierarchical architecture, uses Chain-of-Action reasoning to structure high-level actions as guidance for low-level controls, and compresses context via KV caching for efficiency.
contribution: DeepHA establishes state-of-the-art on 800+ Minecraft tasks, demonstrating superior generalization in complex multi-step planning with 75% context length reduction.

problem: It is unclear when ordinal preference-based solution concepts in games can predict the long-run behavior of payoff-driven no-regret learning dynamics.
approach: The paper characterizes the relationship between preference graphs and dynamically stable sets, showing that preference stability is necessary but not sufficient, and introducing leaklessness to capture additional payoff-drift conditions.
contribution: The work proves dynamic stability equivalence for subgames and identifies conditions under which payoff-based leaklessness guarantees stability.

problem: Existing Nash regret bounds for linear bandits are suboptimal in ambient dimension, limiting fair multi-armed bandit algorithms.
approach: New analytical tools yield order-optimal Nash regret bounds; p-means regret framework unifies fairness and utility objectives as a meta-algorithm over existing bandit strategies.
contribution: Order-optimal Nash regret bound in linear bandits; framework instantiated with Phased Elimination and UCB showing sublinear p-means regret across all p values.

problem: Full-library surrogate inference is a computational bottleneck when screening candidates from billion-scale discrete molecular spaces under expensive evaluations.
approach: BOBA treats library partitions as arms in a multi-armed bandit, adaptively allocating inference and evaluations across partitions based on empirical promise while maintaining exploration.
contribution: Establishes tunable tradeoff between screening performance and inference cost, enabling practical optimization over current billion-scale molecular libraries.

problem: Negative-label-guided OOD detection in vision-language models lacks understanding of effectiveness in open-world scenarios where negative labels diverge from real OOD data.
approach: Energy-based framework quantifies label margins as energy functions; Rényi divergence refines potential distributions to avoid over-pessimism and reduce outlier sensitivity.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art OOD detection with theoretical analysis showing existing methods suffer from over-pessimism and proving Rényi divergence alleviates the problem.

problem: Physics-informed diffusion models enforcing PDE constraints only on outputs leave intermediate representations unconstrained, causing shortcut learning under shifted boundary conditions.
approach: REPA-P aligns intermediate features with physical states via first-principles residuals using lightweight projection heads decoded into physical quantities with PDE residual losses.
contribution: Reduces physics residuals by up to 66.4%, improves out-of-distribution robustness by up to 49.3%, and accelerates convergence by up to 2× with zero inference overhead.

problem: Diffusion-based dataset distillation lacks direct prototype matching due to indirect denoising objectives and generates target-agnostic samples that drift from task distributions.
approach: ProtoVAR uses coarse-to-fine Visual AutoRegressive modeling with injected multi-scale class prototypes to enforce representativeness while preserving diversity.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art distillation performance with comparable or lower computational cost than diffusion-based approaches.

problem: Existing structure prediction models fail to capture functionally relevant protein dynamics across conformational states in biological contexts.
approach: ProMiSE benchmark integrates multiple conformational change mechanisms (intrinsic, ligand-induced, protein-induced) and evaluates state-of-the-art models including AlphaFold3.
contribution: Reveals that current models exhibit limited multi-state sampling and insensitivity to biological context, with training-data exposure shifting predictions toward dominant states.

problem: Federated learning with noisy labels is exacerbated by heterogeneous label-noise types and ratios across clients, degrading model robustness.
approach: FedGR exploits the global model's slow memorization of noisy labels via three collaborative modules that rectify noisy labels and regularize local training in a self-contained manner.
contribution: Consistently outperforms eight baselines across three federated label-noise benchmarks, even under severe noise and data heterogeneity.

problem: Obtaining generalization guarantees for reinforcement learning is challenging due to Markov dependencies in sequential data violating independence assumptions.
approach: Novel PAC-Bayesian bound explicitly accounts for Markov mixing time; PB-SAC algorithm optimizes the bound during training to guide exploration.
contribution: Provides non-vacuous generalization certificates for off-policy algorithms like Soft Actor-Critic while maintaining competitive performance.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation suffers from substantial latency due to synchronous retrieval and existing asynchronous approaches rely on heuristic coordination.
approach: Predictive prefetching framework predicts when to trigger retrieval and what to retrieve using three components that exploit semantic precursors in generation dynamics.
contribution: Achieves up to 43.5% end-to-end latency reduction and 62.4% improvement in time-to-first-token while maintaining answer quality.

problem: 3D molecular diffusion generates inconsistently across sizes because larger molecules form coarse structures earlier due to larger spatial scales.
approach: Scaling the Prior (StP) rescales the prior distribution by molecular size to normalize learning across sizes and harmonize denoising trajectories.
contribution: Generates high-quality molecules with size-consistent generative patterns across diverse molecular sizes.

problem: Noise schedules for pixel diffusion are typically handcrafted and require manual tuning across different image resolutions.
approach: Principled per-image noise schedule design based on spectral properties derives theoretical bounds on efficacy of minimum and maximum noise levels.
contribution: Eliminates redundant diffusion steps and improves generative quality particularly in the low-step inference regime.

problem: Single-cell perturbation modeling is hindered because gene expression is dominated by perturbation-invariant information while perturbation-specific signals are sparse.
approach: PerturbedVAE explicitly separates perturbation-specific information from dominant invariant structure using a framework with identifiability analysis.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with significant gains in out-of-distribution combinatorial predictions and interpretable perturbation-response programs.

problem: Integrating GNNs and LLMs on text-attributed graphs requires achieving well-aligned representations without sufficient distributional constraints.
approach: ERAlign uses energy-based models to project GNN and LLM embeddings in shared latent space with layer-wise alignment quantified via distance metrics and optimized via EBM objectives.
contribution: Obtains state-of-the-art performance on TAG datasets with energy-discrepancy training enabling higher efficiency and reduced landscape distortion.

problem: Existing adaptation methods for diffusion models incur high computational overhead from training and rely on restrictive assumptions about reward differentiability.
approach: DOIT leverages Doob's h-transform to realize measure transport from pre-trained distribution to high-reward target via dynamic correction to sampling without modifying the model.
contribution: Provides convergence guarantees to target high-reward distribution and outperforms state-of-the-art on conditional synthesis and trajectory sampling.

problem: Native 4K video generation faces quadratic computational explosion from full-attention as spatiotemporal resolution increases.
approach: T3 retrofits pretrained full-attention models via multi-scale weight-sharing window attention and hierarchical blocking without altering core architecture.
contribution: Accelerates native 4K video generation by more than 10× with +4.29 VQA and +0.08 VTC performance improvements.

problem: LLM serving frameworks produce different outputs for identical inputs across different tensor parallel sizes due to floating-point non-associativity.
approach: Tree-Based Invariant Kernels (TBIK) enforce consistent reduction order across and within GPUs via custom matrix multiplication and reduction kernels.
contribution: Achieves bit-wise deterministic inference across different tensor parallel sizes and zero probability divergence between rollout and training in RL.

problem: Training-data attribution for vision generative models typically scores individual examples but practitioners need group-level answers.
approach: GUDA approximates Leave-One-Group-Out counterfactuals via machine unlearning applied to a full-data model, quantifying influence using likelihood-based scoring.
contribution: Identifies primary contributing groups more reliably than semantic similarity and gradient approaches with ~100× speedup over LOGO retraining.

problem: Image-to-video diffusion models frequently produce motion violating physical laws despite using many denoising steps.
approach: PhaseLock extracts motion priors from 2-step inference and enforces them via Latent Delta Guidance throughout denoising to prevent phase degradation.
contribution: Improves physical consistency by average 6.2 points with negligible overhead (1.06× time, 1.02× memory) while maintaining visual fidelity.

problem: Existing synthesis pipelines for reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards are bottlenecked by expert-written code and fixed templates.
approach: SSLogic uses an agentic meta-synthesis framework where LLM agents iteratively author and refine Generator-Validator pairs via Generate-Validate-Refine loops.
contribution: Starting from 400 seed families, two evolution rounds yield 953 families and 21,389 instances with gains of SynLogic +5.2, AIME25 +3.0, BBH +5.5.

problem: Policy optimization in contextual MDPs under general offline function approximation lacks regret bounds with optimal dependence on state and action spaces.
approach: OPO-CMDP introduces a policy optimization algorithm achieving near-optimal regret through careful interaction between offline function approximation and policy learning.
contribution: Achieves regret bound with optimal dependence on state and action spaces, improving over prior state-of-the-art.

problem: Watermarks embedded for AI-generated text detection trivially fail when users access multiple models through simple ensemble averaging.
approach: WASH solves practical ensemble challenges via vocabulary alignment and tokenization harmonization across heterogeneous models.
contribution: Averaging 3-5 models suppresses detection z-scores below 2 and reduces TPR@5%FPR below 50% while improving quality by 27.5%.

problem: Multimodal large language models cannot directly process structured non-visual data like human skeletons.
approach: SkeletonLLM translates skeleton sequences into MLLMs' native visual modality via differentiable renderer DrAction, with cooperative training combining causal reasoning distillation and discriminative finetuning.
contribution: Demonstrates universal skeleton understanding with strong generalization across recognition, captioning, reasoning, and cross-format transfer tasks.

problem: Clustered multitask learning with heterogeneous nuisance components violates aligned feature spaces and homogeneous task structure assumptions.
approach: Adaptive fused orthogonal estimator integrates Neyman-orthogonal losses with data-driven pairwise fusion penalties and adaptive aggregation.
contribution: Achieves exact recovery of latent clustering and pooled parametric convergence rates proportional to cluster size with asymptotic oracle equivalence.

problem: Watermarking schemes for language model attribution lack formal abstraction for reasoning about attribution decisions.
approach: Ideal attribution mechanisms formalize attribution via ledgers (append-only logs of interactions) with deterministic decisions based on explicit selection criteria.
contribution: Provides unified language for reasoning about watermarking guarantees and clarifies which properties are attainable for practical schemes.

problem: Deep neural network time-series forecasting models deployed as black-box APIs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that remain largely underexplored.
approach: TSFAdv embeds frequency-domain priors into Natural Evolution Strategies for sensitivity-guided gradient estimation under query constraints.
contribution: Achieves 38.78% median DTW improvement and 26.47% median SME improvement under 200-query budget across seven state-of-the-art architectures.

problem: Vision-language-action models assume task-relevant objects are always visible, leading to brittle reactive behaviors when targets fall outside the camera field of view.
approach: SOMA equips VLAs with persistent spatial memory constructed from multi-view observations, with components for memory construction, refinement, and retrieval.
contribution: Improves task success on out-of-vision manipulation tasks with faster target localization and near one-shot grasping under partial observability.

problem: Test-time guidance for generative models faces limitations with non-differentiable rewards, complex landscapes, and lacks theoretical guarantees.
approach: Source Parallel Tempering (SPT) operates in source space leveraging its simpler geometry via local exploration kernel and parallel tempering for barrier crossing.
contribution: Provides error bound linking training approximation to test-time performance and significantly improves over state-of-the-art on conditional synthesis.

problem: Existing optimizers like Muon are only half-aligned with maximal update parametrization, controlling updates but allowing weights to drift.
approach: Spectral Sphere Optimizer (SSO) enforces strict module-wise spectral constraints on both weights and updates via steepest descent on the spectral sphere.
contribution: Outperforms AdamW and Muon across diverse architectures with improved MoE router load balancing, suppressed outliers, and strictly bounded activations.

problem: Multi-agent offline learning struggles with catastrophic forgetting and plasticity loss when facing sequential tasks with exponential skill space.
approach: COMAD discovers skills via auto-encoder transformation of mixed behavior data and constructs skill-augmented policy learning with reusability estimation.
contribution: Continually expands skill library to mitigate interference, achieving superior forward and backward transfer across MARL benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating LLM conversational quality at human scale relies on synthetic metrics rather than human sources, falling short for multi-turn dialogue.
approach: UPHELD provides reference-full benchmark with hundreds of professionally-authored human dialogues and 36,000+ per-turn human annotations across 30,000+ turns.
contribution: Develops Mixture-of-Judges framework improving correlation with human judgment by ~30% over existing automatic metrics and LLM-as-a-judge approaches.

problem: Virtual screening on ultra-large combinatorial synthesis libraries routinely scores fewer than 0.1% of compounds, missing many high-scoring molecules.
approach: APEX uses neural surrogate exploiting CSL structure to enable full enumeration of approximate top-k sets on consumer GPU within a minute.
contribution: Enables exact retrieval of approximate top-k compounds and allows amortization across changing constraints and objectives.

problem: Domain adaptation under label shift challenges existing methods that rely on aligned feature spaces or homogeneous task structures.
approach: RDALS adapts via moment-matching linear system using LDA in deep latent space, providing rigorous finite-sample and generalization error bounds.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines in both data-scarce and extreme-shift regimes with superior robustness and accuracy.

problem: Classification error scales as a power law in number of classes, but the structure of optimal decomposition for chain-of-thought remains unclear.
approach: Theory shows classification error reduces via tree-structured decomposition of overall task into smaller classification problems, identifying critical degree threshold and optimal depth.
contribution: Identifies threshold below which thinking is detrimental and optimal depth minimizing error, proving error cannot be surpassed by increasing depth.

problem: Grokking (onset of generalization long after overfitting) lacks rigorous quantitative bounds relating generalization delay to training hyperparameters.
approach: End-to-end grokking results for over-parameterized ridge regression with gradient descent showing stages of overfitting, poor generalization, and recovery.
contribution: Provides first rigorous quantitative bounds on grokking time in terms of hyperparameters, proving grokking is consequence of specific conditions, not inherent failure mode.

problem: Iterated empirical risk minimization with prediction-dependent losses introduces intricate statistical dependencies across samples distinguishing from classical ERM.
approach: Sharp asymptotic characterization of test error for linear models trained with convex losses on Gaussian mixture data despite data reuse.
contribution: Removes oracle and sample-splitting assumptions in active learning, uncovering fundamental budget allocation tradeoff and double-descent driven purely by data selection.

problem: Causes of representational similarity across machine learning models remain underexplored despite numerous works documenting the similarity.
approach: Evaluates effects of dataset overlap and task overlap on model similarity through experiments across model sizes and modalities.
contribution: Finds dataset and task overlap positively associated with higher representational similarity, with greater similarity linked to increased adversarial transferability.

problem: Self-supervised learning for time-series has high computational costs and relies on assumptions that do not hold across diverse temporal dynamics.
approach: Di-COT avoids augmentation by contrasting informative substructures via stochastic partition of windows into overlapping sub-blocks with length-independent loss computation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on six large-scale datasets with substantially reduced training time and no reliance on augmentation.

problem: Generative priors in Image Super-Resolution (SR) often compromise faithful restoration, we attribute this limitation to a fundamental spectral misalignment between isotropic objectives and the intrinsic natural image manifold.
approach: To bridge this geometric gap, we propose ASASR, a theoretically grounded framework that recasts the generative flow into a Sobolev-induced Riemannian geometry by explicitly coloring the noise transition kernel to mirror natural spectral decay.
contribution: Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ASASR outperforms leading generative baselines, particularly in preserving spectral consistency and structural fidelity, offering a robust solution that effectively mitigates artifacts..

problem: This paper investigates the scaling properties of autoregressive next-pixel prediction, a simple, end-to-end yet under-explored framework for unified vision models.
approach:
Starting with images at resolutions of 32$\times$ 32, we
train a family of Transformers using IsoFLOP profiles across compute budgets up to 7e19 FLOPs and evaluate three distinct target metrics: next-pixel prediction objective, ImageNet classification accuracy, and generation-based completion where top half of the image serves as a spatial prompt.
contribution:
Starting with images at resolutions of 32$\times$ 32, we
train a family of Transformers using IsoFLOP profiles across compute budgets up to 7e19 FLOPs and evaluate three distinct target metrics: next-pixel prediction objective, ImageNet classification accuracy, and generation-based completion where top half of the image serves as a spatial prompt.

problem: Sample inefficiency remains a challenge in pixel-based visual reinforcement learning (RL), primarily due to ineffective state representation learning.
approach: While recent advances employ auxiliary tasks to improve representation learning, their representation goals (e.g., mask reconstruction, state prediction) are misaligned with the ultimate RL goal of maximizing return, constraining further improvements in representation quality.
contribution: Extensive experiments on both online (DMControl) and offline (V-D4RL) benchmarks demonstrate that RC significantly enhances the sample efficiency, particularly achieving 68% performance boost on average across nine challenging tasks from DMControl..

problem: Point forecasting for graph-structured multivariate time series is a fundamental problem, but rigorous uncertainty quantification for such predictions is still underexplored.
approach: Conformal prediction (CP) offers uncertainty estimation with a solid coverage guarantee under the exchangeability assumption, which requires the joint data distribution to be unchanged under permutation.
contribution: Experimental results on real-world benchmark datasets across multiple application domains show that SCALE not only achieves valid coverage but also consistently improves the coverage-efficiency trade-off over the state-of-the-art CP methods..

problem: Gesture interaction and touchless sensing is a natural and intuitive control method that allows users to control devices through natural hand or body movements, reducing reliance on physical input and enhancing convenience and functional efficiency.
approach: This paper proposes a novel IMU-based BiCrossNet model and two novel data augmentation models (delta-generator and embedding-generator) to address this challenge.
contribution: Compared with existing methods, the model proposed in this article boosts accuracy by 11.7% and 12.7% in UMAHand  (public datasets); and 8.85% and 5.25% in GRHand (self-developed datasets), with decreasing 27.8% pretrained feature-extractor model parameters.

problem: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) is important in building real-world learning systems.
approach: In CLIP-based CIL, the model performs classification by comparing similarity between visual and textual embeddings obtained from template prompts, e.g., ``a photo of a [CLASS]''.
contribution: Experiments show that AREA consistently outperforms SOTA methods.

problem:
Scaling the context length of large language models (LLMs) offers significant benefits but is computationally expensive.
This expense stems primarily from the self-attention mechanism, whose $O(N^2)$ complexity with respect to sequence length presents a major bottleneck for both memory and latency.
Fortunately, the attention matrix is often sparse, particularly for long sequences, suggesting an opportunity for optimization.
Block-sparse attention has emerged as a promising solution that partitions sequences into blocks and skips computation for a subset of these blocks.
However, the effectiveness of this method is highly dependent on the underlying attention patterns, which can lead to sub-optimal block-level sparsity.
For instance, important key tokens for queries within a single block may be scattered across numerous other blocks, leading to computational redundancy.
In this work, we propose Permuted Block-Sparse Attention (**PBS-Attn**), a plug-and-play method that leverages the permutation properties of attention to increase block-level sparsity and enhance the computational efficiency of LLM prefilling.
We conduct comprehensive experiments on challenging long-context datasets, demonstrating that PBS-Attn consistently outperforms existing block-sparse attention methods in model accuracy and closely matches the full attention baseline.
Powered by our custom permuted-FlashAttention kernels, PBS-Attn achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to $\mathbf{2.75\times}$ in long-context prefilling, confirming its practical viability.
Code available at \url{https://github.com/xinghao.
approach: Proposes a method to address the problem.
contribution:

problem: Conventional time-series discriminative forecasting relies on point-wise regression, which inherently induces over-smoothing and fails to capture stochastic volatility in complex systems.
approach: We introduce KineFlow, a generative time-series forecasting framework that augments flow matching with a phase-space Neural Acceleration Field, treating exogenous inputs as driving forces that produce gradual momentum shifts rather than abrupt state perturbations.
contribution: Extensive experiments on six real-world benchmarks demonstrate that KineFlow achieves an average 15% MSE improvement over discriminative baselines and an 8% gain in CRPS compared to state-of-the-art generative methods..

problem: Vertex-level clustering for directed graphs (digraphs) remains challenging as edge directionality breaks the key assumptions underlying popular spectral methods, which also incur the overhead of eigen-decomposition.
approach: This paper proposes *Parametrized Power Iteration Clustering* (ParPIC), a random-walk-based clustering method for weakly connected digraphs.
contribution: Empirical results on synthetic and real-world graphs demonstrate that ParPIC achieves competitive clustering accuracy with improved scalability relative to spectral and teleportation-based methods..

problem:
Text-conditioned image generation has made rapid progress, yet rendering images with long-form text remains challenging due to the limitations of existing datasets, which predominantly focus on short and simple text.
We introduce TextAtlas5M, a large-scale dataset designed to evaluate long-text rendering, where “long text” encompasses not only textual length but also layout complexity and semantic richness.
TextAtlas5M contains 5 million generated and collected images across diverse data types, enabling comprehensive evaluation of large-scale generative models.
We further curate 4,000 human-improved test cases (TextAtlasEval) spanning four domains, forming one of the most extensive benchmarks for text rendering.
Evaluations show that TextAtlas5M poses substantial challenges even for state-of-the-art proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4o), with significantly larger gaps observed for open-source models.
Training on TextAtlas5M consistently improves text rendering 
for both diffusion-based and autoregressive models, demonstrating 
its effectiveness for advancing text-rich image generation..
approach: Proposes a method to address the problem.
contribution:

We introduce TextAtlas5M, a large-scale dataset designed to evaluate long-text rendering, where “long text” encompasses not only textual length but also layout complexity and semantic richness.
TextAtlas5M contains 5 million generated and collected images across diverse data types, enabling comprehensive evaluation of large-scale generative models.
We further curate 4,000 human-improved test cases (TextAtlasEval) spanning four domains, forming one of the most extensive benchmarks for text rendering.
Evaluations show that TextAtlas5M poses substantial challenges even for state-of-the-art proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4o), with significantly larger gaps observed for open-source models.
Training on TextAtlas5M consistently improves text rendering 
for both diffusion-based and autoregressive models, demonstrating 
its effectiveness for advancing text-rich image generation..

problem: The minimal norm weight perturbations of DNNs required to achieve a specified change in output are derived and the factors determining its size are discussed.
approach: These single-layer exact formulae are contrasted with more generic multi-layer Lipschitz constant based robustness guarantees; both are observed to be of the same order which indicates similar efficacy in their guarantees.
contribution: These results are applied to precision-modification-activated backdoor attacks, establishing provable compression thresholds below which such attacks cannot succeed, and show empirically that low-rank compression can reliably activate latent backdoors while preserving full-precision accuracy.

problem: Expert-annotated time series datasets often suffer from low agreement, especially in medical applications where decisions rely on subjective criteria and inconsistent thresholds.
approach:
To address this, we propose to rely on a pairwise comparison-based approach, which provides a more robust alternative to individual annotation, since relative judgments are typically easier and yield higher consistency.
The problem is thus transformed into a ranking problem and we introduce an ideal point model adapted to time series data using elastic similarity measures such as Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) and Time Warp Edit Distance (TWED).
We prove Lipschitz continuity of these distances and demonstrate several convergence guarantees for this model.
contribution: Finally, we show through multiple experiments that our approach produces accurate and robust rankings under noisy annotation conditions..

problem: Research on the expressive power of transformers shows that transformers are equivariant to permutations and can approximate all permutation-equivariant continuous functions on a compact domain.
approach:
In this work, we investigate the representability of floating-point transformers that use floating-point parameters and floating-point operations.
Unlike existing results under exact arithmetic, we first show that floating-point transformers can represent non-permutation-equivariant functions even without positional encoding.
contribution: We also identify the minimal equivariance property in floating-point transformers, and show that all non-trivial additive positional encoding can harm the representability of floating-point transformers..

problem:
Generative models frequently suffer miscalibration, wherein statistics of the sampling distribution—such as the fraction of generations in a given class—deviate from desired values.
We frame calibration as a constrained optimization problem and seek the closest model in Kullback-Leibler divergence satisfying a calibration constraint.
approach:
To address the intractability of imposing these constraints exactly, we introduce two surrogate objectives for  fine-tuning: (1) the relax loss, which replaces the constraint with a miscalibration penalty, and (2) the reward loss, which converts calibration into a reward fine-tuning problem.
We demonstrate that these approaches substantially reduce calibration error across hundreds of simultaneous constraints and models with up to nine billion parameters, spanning applications in protein design, image generation, and language modeling.
Code is available at https://github.com/smithhenryd/cgm..
contribution:
To address the intractability of imposing these constraints exactly, we introduce two surrogate objectives for  fine-tuning: (1) the relax loss, which replaces the constraint with a miscalibration penalty, and (2) the reward loss, which converts calibration into a reward fine-tuning problem.
We demonstrate that these approaches substantially reduce calibration error across hundreds of simultaneous constraints and models with up to nine billion parameters, spanning applications in protein design, image generation, and language modeling.
Code is available at https://github.com/smithhenryd/cgm..

problem: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have substantially expanded the scope of Table Question Answering (TableQA).
approach:
However, existing benchmarks primarily treat TableQA as a passive, single-turn natural language understanding task, lacking the capacity to evaluate autonomous reasoning and tool-call trajectories in realistic, multi-turn scenarios.
To bridge this gap, we introduce TableAgent-Bench, a large-scale bilingual benchmark that reformulates TableQA as proactive, agentic interactions over structurally complex, multi-table environments.
contribution: Specifically, TAEF integrates a specialized agent toolset and 4 metric categories to systematically diagnose intermediate failure modes, assessing performance across table localization, tool-invocation rationality, and trajectory-level pass rate.

problem: Large language models are increasingly deployed in streaming scenarios, rendering conventional post-hoc safeguards ineffective as they fail to interdict unsafe content in real-time.
approach: While streaming safeguards based on token-level supervised training could address this, they necessitate expensive annotations and suffer from severe overfitting.
contribution: These results make NExT-Guard a universal and scalable paradigm for real-time safety, accelerating the practical deployment of streaming safeguards..

problem: Estimating density ratios between pairs of intractable data distributions is a core problem in probabilistic modeling, enabling principled comparisons of sample likelihoods under different data-generating processes across conditions.
approach: While exact-likelihood models such as normalizing flows offer a promising approach to density ratio estimation, naive evaluations are computationally expensive and prone to discretization errors because they require simulating each distribution's likelihood independently.
contribution: We demonstrate competitive performance on simulated benchmarks for closed-form ratio estimation, and show that our method supports versatile tasks in single-cell genomics data analysis, where likelihood-based comparisons of cellular states across experimental conditions enable treatment effect estimation and batch correction evaluation..

problem: The anchor-based multi-view clustering methods have received extensive attention due to their efficiency and scalability in large-scale data scenarios.
approach: Existing anchor-based methods still face challenges in learning compact and semantically discriminative anchors.
contribution: Experimental results demonstrate that DCMC outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmark tests, confirming its effectiveness and reliability..

problem: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are trained on massive multimodal data, making data unlearning increasingly important as data owners may request the removal of specific content.
approach:
However, most existing benchmarks are limited in scale and scope, failing to capture the complexities of MLLM lifelong unlearning.
  To fill this gap, we introduce the MLUBench, a large-scale and comprehensive benchmark featuring 127 entities across 9 classes under lifelong unlearning requests.
  We perform extensive experiments using MLUBench and reveal that existing unlearning methods suffer from severe, cumulative degradation.
contribution:
Experiments demonstrate that LUMoE significantly mitigates the degradation problem faced by baselines.
  The source code and the MLUBench dataset are open-sourced in this [URL](https://github.com/lihe-maxsize/Lifelong_Unlearning_main)..

problem: Accelerating scientific discovery requires the identification of which experiments would yield the best outcomes before committing resources to costly physical validation.
approach:
While existing benchmarks evaluate LLMs on scientific knowledge and reasoning, their ability to predict experimental outcomes---a task where AI could significantly exceed human capabilities---remains largely underexplored.
We introduce SciPredict, a benchmark comprising 405 tasks derived from recent empirical studies in 33 specialized sub-fields of physics, biology, and chemistry.
contribution: SciPredict establishes a rigorous framework demonstrating that superhuman performance in experimental s.

problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated sophisticated comprehension of sequential code, yet their capacity for reasoning about concurrent programs remains largely unquantified.
approach: We introduce DRPBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the concurrent code comprehension of LLMs by measuring their data race prediction performance.
contribution: Beyond benchmarking, we characterize two primary failure modes: (1) shared-variable distraction, where multiple variable appearances degrade comprehension accuracy, and (2) synchronization-logic myopia, the inability to interpret non-standard synchronization implementations.

problem: A probability distribution $\mathbb{P}$ is a measure on a $\sigma$-algebra, assigning mass to sets rather than points, which poses a challenge for the training of neural networks that often struggle to reconstruct the global topology of continuous manifolds from sparse samples.
approach: Specifically, we introduce a network, PriSpecNet, with a single-function evaluation (1-NFE) Pseudoinverse L\'evy Inversion (PiLI) solver that regards generation as a fast analytical problem, eliminating the need for iterative numerical integration while maintaining full compatibility with the stochastic interpolants.
contribution: For ImageNet $256 \times 256$, 1-NFE PiLI achieves a competitive FID of **1.66** using only **26** Gflops, representing a **170$\times$** reduction in total Gflops compared to the 4,436 Gflops required by the 25-NFE DPM-Solver++..

problem: A wide range of optimization problems can often be written in terms of generalized convex functions (GCFs).
approach: When this structure is present, it can convert certain nested bilevel objectives into single-level problems amenable to standard first-order optimization methods.
contribution: In both these cases, we show how our layer can be used to convert the existing bilevel or min-max formulations into single-level problems that can be solved efficiently with first-order methods..

problem: Diffusion language models (DLMs) are an attractive alternative to autoregressive models because they promise sublinear-time, parallel generation, yet practical gains remain elusive as high-quality samples still demand hundreds of refinement steps.
approach: In continuous domains, consistency training along the probability-flow ODE is a popular recipe to accelerate diffusion.
contribution: Together, these results position CDLM as a principled and scalable foundation for the ne.

problem: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference cost by removing low-importance architectural components.
approach: Due to the discreteness of the $\ell_0$ norm, prior work typically adopts stochastic hard-concrete relaxations to enable differentiable optimization; however, this stochasticity can introduce a train--test mismatch when sampled masks are discretized for deployment and restricting masks to a bounded, near-binary range.
contribution: We further demonstrate end-to-end inference speedups in realistic deployment settings with vLLM..

problem: Spatial-temporal time series forecasting is challenging due to complex lead-lag dependencies, which are often ignored or inadequately modeled by existing methods.
approach: Thus, we propose LagLLM, the first LLM-empowered framework that explicitly models lead–lag dependencies by unifying data-driven dynamics modeling and knowledge-driven semantic reasoning.
contribution: Experiments on eight real-world datasets show that LagLLM achieves the state-of-the-art performance with improved accuracy, robustness, and interpretability.

problem: Effective time series forecasting enables various real-world applications, benefiting from the proliferation of mobile devices.
approach: However, the volume of time series data may vary significantly across domains due to high data acquisition costs and data regulations.
contribution: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that TimeID outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, improving MSE and MAE by 10.7\% and 9.3\% on average.

problem: Tool-augmented reasoning has emerged as a promising direction for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
approach: However, existing studies mainly focus on enabling models to perform tool invocation, while neglecting the necessity of invoking tools.
contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate that AutoTool exhibits outstanding performance and high efficiency, yielding a 21.8\% accuracy gain on V* benchmark compared to the base model, and a 44.9\% improvement in efficiency over existing tool-augmented methods on POPE benchmark.

problem: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) deliver strong cross-domain generalization, but their scale makes deployment costly.
approach: Knowledge distillation is a natural compression route, yet prior TSFM distillation typically imitates teacher outputs, features, or pairwise relations, and therefore remains tightly coupled to teacher-specific training trajectories while underutilizing two empirical properties: (i) high-level representations across model scales tend to converge toward a shared, approximately low-rank geometry, and (ii) layer-wise utility follows a long-tail pattern.
contribution: Across forecasting and imputation, the distilled student matches or slightly improves upon the teacher, while exhibiting a.

problem: As language models improve and become increasingly deployed to solve a variety of tasks, trustworthiness becomes essential.
approach: Calibration is a good proxy for trust: well-calibrated confidence estimates help inform the risk versus reward trade-off when trusting a specific model output.
contribution: Taken together, our work shows that equipping LLMs with the ACUTE protocol can improve calibration, utility, and trustworthiness in numerous settings..

problem: In-context learning (ICL) derives its power from enabling Large Language Models to adapt to new tasks via prompt-based reasoning alone, entirely bypassing the need for parameter updates.
approach: To bridge this gap, we propose the first theoretical framework for in-context continual learning, modeling how a pretrained Transformer processes multiple sequential tasks within a single prompt through shared attention mechanisms.
contribution: This analysis exposes fundamental limits of attention-based continual inference and offers theoretical explanations for order sensitivity and performance degradation in long prompts..

problem: Tertiary structure-based RNA design aims to generate RNA sequences that can fold into desired 3D structures, but remains a challenging problem due to the scarcity of annotated data, structural noise, and the intrinsic complexity of RNA topology.
approach: To address these issues, we propose a unified framework, ATL-FGD, that integrates Adaptive Topology Learning (ATL) and FiLM-Guided Distillation (FGD) for robust RNA design.
contribution: Extensive experiments on tertiary structure-based RNA design benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves significant improvements in both sequence recovery and structural fidelity..

problem: The goal of this paper is to improve the performance and reliability of vision-language-action (VLA) models through iterative online interaction.
approach: We propose a simple iterative improvement algorithm that uses real-world roll-out data to improve the fidelity of the world model, which can then, in turn, be used to generate supplemental synthetic data for improving the VLA model.
contribution: We achieve a 39.2\% absolute success rate improvement over the base policy and 11.6\% improvement from training with the generated synthetic rollouts.

problem: While Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), or A/B tests, are the gold standard for optimizing online-platform policies, they are limited by discrete testing levels.
approach: We address this by developing Deep Learning for Policy Targeting (\textsf{DLPT}) to learn personalized continuous policies from discrete RCTs using high-dimensional features.
contribution: In a collaboration with a leading social media platform to optimize creator incentives, we show that \textsf{DLPT} substantially outperforms existing benchmarks..

problem: We study the robustness of stochastic mirror descent (SMD) under heavy-tailed noise, focusing on whether the method retains its convergence guarantees when run with infinite-variance stochastic gradient input.
approach: To address this question in a principled manner, we begin by introducing a continuous-time model of SMD as a stochastic differential equation (SDE) driven by a centered Lévy noise process with finite $p$-th order moments, $1 < p \leq 2$.
