problem: Existing LLM benchmarks for finance rely on simulated or generic data, creating a gap between reported performance and actual real-world efficacy where models still fail business requirements.
approach: BizFinBench.v2 is built on authentic user query-response data from Chinese and U.S. equity markets with 28,860 questions across offline and online tasks in Chinese and English.
contribution: Shows GPT-5 achieves only 61.5% accuracy against 84.8% business requirement, with DeepSeek-R1 showing superior investment efficacy.

problem: Spiking attention mechanisms are inherently sensitive to firing density, causing high-firing-rate neurons to dominate attention scores regardless of semantic relevance, especially problematic for sparse event-driven representations.
approach: DiceFormer proposes Spike Dice Attention using set similarity derived from Dice coefficient to replace density-sensitive measures, focusing on spike co-occurrence rather than firing rates.
contribution: Achieves SOTA mAP of 0.161 on AudioSet-20k with 54.3M parameters, outperforming prior SNNs and narrowing the gap with ANN-based models.

problem: Time series forecasting is hampered by non-stationarity, noise, missing values, and distribution shifts; industry solutions use costly customized frameworks that don't adapt well across diverse datasets.
approach: BECRA proposes an agent training paradigm that learns forecasting strategies through contrast-aware exploration and agent-level causal lesson extraction, distilling symbolic strategy lessons for zero-shot adaptation.
contribution: Enables zero-shot training adaptation on unseen datasets without human-annotated supervision through agent-extracted causal lessons.

problem: Human ratings are subject to inter-rater biases and judgment errors, and quantifying their uncertainty typically requires expensive repeated measurements.
approach: Proposes a Bayesian graphical model using auxiliary objective data to estimate instance-level and item-level uncertainty via learned shared latent representations and data-conditioned uncertainty priors.
contribution: Enables uncertainty quantification of subjective human ratings using scalable amortized variational inference with modality-appropriate neural encoders.

problem: It is fundamentally challenging to determine whether causal effects are identifiable in the presence of latent confounders without auxiliary variables, relying only on treatment-outcome joint distribution.
approach: For linear SCMs, provides complete characterization of causal effect identifiability contingent on exogenous noise distributions, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions on Gaussianity.
contribution: Establishes equivalence of independent monitoring and non-informative censoring for Case-1 data but not Case-K, and quantifies solution space cardinality for unidentifiable cases.

problem: State-space models with polynomial bases have global temporal support poorly matched to signals with localized or transient structure like physiological and audio data.
approach: WaveSSM constructs SSMs over wavelet frames leveraging localized temporal support through the HiPPO framework for continuous-time projection operators.
contribution: Outperforms polynomial-based SSMs like S4 on real-world datasets with transient dynamics on PTB-XL physiological signals and Speech Commands audio.

problem: Natural-language explanations prioritize human plausibility over accurately reflecting model behavior, and post-hoc approaches don't align with decision functions or generalize.
approach: OPeX directly optimizes behavioral faithfulness using GRPO reinforcement learning, optimizing recoverability (recovering predictions on seen examples) and simulatability (predicting behavior on unseen examples).
contribution: Achieves high simulatability (~0.85) and recoverability (~0.99) with an 8B backbone, outperforming GPT-4o and human explanations by 15% in user studies.

problem: Evaluating agentic web search capabilities of LLMs is challenging because existing benchmarks don't clearly separate internal knowledge from search capability or test multi-hop reasoning.
approach: LiveNewsBench automatically generates fresh question-answer pairs from recent news, featuring multi-hop searches requiring page visits and reasoning, with human-verified test samples.
contribution: Provides regularly updated benchmark for rigorous evaluation of agentic web search with public leaderboard, datasets, and code.

problem: State-space models lag behind Transformers on retrieval-heavy tasks because they cannot reproduce a small set of critical attention heads termed Gather-and-Aggregate that enable in-context retrieval.
approach: Retrieval-aware distillation converts a pretrained Transformer into a hybrid by preserving only retrieval-critical heads and distilling others into recurrent heads, identified via ablation on synthetic tasks.
contribution: Preserving just 2% of attention heads recovers 95% of teacher performance on retrieval tasks while achieving 5-6x better memory efficiency than comparable hybrids.

problem: Interval-censored data analysis requires assumptions about censoring mechanisms but the relationship between independent monitoring and non-informative censoring is not fully understood.
approach: Explores theoretical relationship between censoring assumptions and demonstrates their equivalence for Case-1 but not Case-K data; proposes first strictly proper scoring rule and calibration metric for interval-censored data.
contribution: Provides complete theoretical characterization and empirical validation showing neural networks trained with the proposed scoring rule compete with statistical baselines.

problem: The manifold of full-rank correlation matrices, a normalized alternative to SPD matrices, remains largely underexplored for neural network applications.
approach: Introduces Riemannian networks over correlation manifolds leveraging five correlation geometries, extending MLR, fully connected, and convolutional layers to these geometries with accurate backpropagation methods.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness of correlation manifold networks compared to existing SPD and Grassmannian approaches.

problem: Fast and accurate image inversion for FLUX diffusion transformers is challenging because discretization errors of linear solvers create trajectory errors during inversion.
approach: SlerpFlow uses a geometric view based on Manifold Hypothesis: applies Spherical Linear Interpolation to rectify flow velocity directions on the hypersphere, adhering to latent space curvature.
contribution: Achieves high-precision inversion while maintaining computational efficiency of first-order Euler solver without requiring additional training.

problem: Existing benchmarks for multimodal foundation models emphasize environment-centric spatial relations while overlooking observer-centric relationships requiring egocentric viewpoint and pose reasoning.
approach: SAW-Bench provides a benchmark with 786 egocentric videos from Ray-Ban Meta glasses, 2071 annotated question-answer pairs probing six awareness tasks including observer-environment understanding.
contribution: Reveals a 37.66% human-model performance gap and shows models fail to infer coherent camera geometry despite exploiting partial geometric cues.

problem: Vision-language-action models lack systematic understanding and evaluation of memory mechanisms despite their importance for long-horizon history-dependent manipulation tasks.
approach: RoboMME provides a large-scale standardized benchmark with 16 manipulation tasks under a taxonomy evaluating temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory, with 14 memory-augmented VLA variants.
contribution: Shows memory representation effectiveness is highly task-dependent with each design offering distinct advantages across different manipulation scenarios.

problem: Conditional kernel ridge regression statistical properties are not well understood in terms of behavior and generalization error compared to standard KRR.
approach: Studies statistical properties by reducing conditional KRR behavior to that of standard KRR with a residual kernel, with additional expected test risk term O(1/sqrt(N)).
contribution: Enables analysis of conditional KRR with principal eigenfunctions and random features, revealing connection between these two settings.

problem: GUI agents rely on model-centric step-wise interaction where LLMs re-interpret UI at each screen, causing fragility in long-horizon tasks.
approach: Executable Agentic Memory shifts planning from free-form generation to retrieval-and-execution via a structured Knowledge Graph using state-aware DFS and action-group mining with value-guided MCTS.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art by 19.6% on AndroidWorld while reducing token costs 6x relative to GPT-4o with 2.8s average latency.

problem: Multi-agent systems lack dynamic abstraction of sub-agents, remaining either context-isolated without specialization or static requiring heavy human engineering.
approach: AOrchestra models agents as tuples (Model, Task, Tools, Context) acting as compositional recipes, enabling dynamic on-demand sub-agent creation where orchestrator curates task-relevant context and selects tools.
contribution: Achieves 16.28% relative improvement over strongest baseline on challenging benchmarks while reducing human engineering effort.

problem: LLM-based kernel generation struggles to achieve both correctness and high performance because of lack of domain-specific optimization guidance for exploring the optimization space.
approach: EGG incorporates expert optimization principles with hierarchical stages: algorithmic structure design establishing computational foundations, then hardware-specific tuning via parallel mapping and memory optimization.
contribution: Achieves 2.13x average speedup over PyTorch, outperforming existing agent-based and RL-based kernel generation approaches.

problem: Video anomaly detection requires obtaining sufficient annotated anomaly data which is challenging due to rarity and wide variety of abnormal events, limiting scalability.
approach: TD-VAD proposes text-driven learning using LLM-generated video-like text descriptions with temporal characteristics and event evolution causal attention to model contextual dependencies without target-domain anomaly data.
contribution: Breaks visual dependence for VAD training and outperforms one-class and unsupervised methods on XD-Violence and UCF-Crime datasets.

problem: Example-based guidance for mathematical reasoning is unstable across problems and models because of a gap between whether a strategy appears in successful solutions and whether it remains effective when instantiated as guidance.
approach: Selective Strategy Retrieval explicitly models executability using empirical multi-route source-aware signals to retrieve and combine strategies from both human-written and model-generated sources.
contribution: Yields reliable and consistent improvements of up to +13 points on AIME25 and +5 points on Apex benchmarks through selective strategy retrieval.

problem: Data mixing for language models lacks well-understood design choices and assumes domain sets remain fixed, but real development involves adding and updating datasets.
approach: Olmix conducts comprehensive empirical study of design space choices and introduces mixture reuse to efficiently recompute mixing ratios after domain updates by reusing existing ratios.
contribution: Matches performance of full recomputation with 74% less compute after domain updates while improving downstream task performance by 11.6% over training without mixing.

problem: Memory agents traverse long sequences of memory operations before receiving sparse delayed rewards, hindering end-to-end optimization of memory management policies.
approach: Mem-T introduces hierarchical memory database for dynamic updates and multi-turn retrieval over streaming inputs, with MoT-GRPO framework transforming sparse rewards into dense supervision via memory operation tree backpropagation.
contribution: Surpasses frameworks like A-Mem and Mem0 by up to 14.94% while reducing inference tokens per query by 23.45%.

problem: Ensembling is important for tabular deep learning performance but ensemble-first systems are rare, and traditional approaches are computationally expensive.
approach: TabPack packs many base model-optimizer pairs with different hyperparameters into a single network and optimizer, training all base models in parallel with random hyperparameter sampling.
contribution: Produces powerful ensembles in a single run with substantial efficiency gains over traditional approaches, making tabular deep learning more accessible.

problem: Feature caching accelerates diffusion transformer inference but suffers from severe error accumulation at high acceleration ratios when relying on historical features.
approach: LearniBridge uses learnable calibration via lightweight LoRA updates to bridge multiple timesteps, with calibration characterized by shared low-rank subspace across diverse prompts.
contribution: Achieves up to 5.87x acceleration on FLUX, 5.75x on HunyuanVideo, and 4.10x on WAN 2.1 with minimal quality loss.

problem: Event sequences from complex systems are sparse and incomplete, and generated synthetic sequences must remain realistic, satisfy domain constraints, and allow controllable generation.
approach: FC-TPP maintains explicit latent symbolic state encoding predicates evolved through differentiable multi-hop forward-chaining, with temporal point process decoder generating events conditioned on evolving state.
contribution: Achieves higher generation quality under limited data with stronger constraint adherence and greater controllability on LogiCity, MIMIC-IV, EPIC-100, and IKEA ASM benchmarks.

problem: Multivariate time series forecasting struggles to reliably capture inter-variable dependencies because dense interactions amplify spurious correlations and cause representation over-smoothing.
approach: MS-FLOW uses sparse routing with a strict communication budget to replace dense cross-variable interactions, retaining only critical dependency paths while suppressing redundant connections.
contribution: MS-FLOW achieves state-of-the-art forecasting accuracy on 12 benchmarks with fewer, more reliable dependencies, shifting from dense to effective interaction.

problem: Demonstration selection for LLM few-shot learning is a complex combinatorial problem because demonstration effectiveness depends on contextual relationship to the query and presentation order.
approach: AutoSelect formulates demonstration selection as an auto-regressive sequential decision process, using a trainable policy model to sequentially select exemplars while embedding query and prior selections as matrix representations.
contribution: AutoSelect outperforms existing heuristic and learning-based methods by up to 11% across nine datasets by optimizing over the factorial space of demonstration permutations via KL-regularized Plackett-Luce ranking.

problem: Few-shot classification requires adapting pretrained models to novel classes with limited examples, but current methods heuristically combine pretrained knowledge and few-shot evidence without principled integration.
approach: BOIF interprets pretrained models as priors and few-shot evidence as likelihoods, using Bayesian-inspired optimal integration with decoupled prior and likelihood pathways and additive logit combination.
contribution: BOIF achieves state-of-the-art performance at 80.61% average accuracy on 11 benchmarks at 16-shot with strong out-of-distribution robustness via multi-level feature adaptation and simplified cache modules.

problem: Source selection for LLM families with shared vocabularies in scientific domains is difficult because representation-similarity metrics are non-identifiable under label-conditioned error geometry.
approach: FisherSketch estimates head Fisher alignment as a cosine between kernel mean embeddings in joint activation-error space through a single streaming pass, encoding transfer-relevant update structure in compact signatures.
contribution: FisherSketch makes K=128,256 head Fisher alignment practical with 16 KB task signatures and 192 KB per-task streaming state, providing diagnostic instruments for studying whether LLM task similarity is driven by activations, errors, or coupling.

problem: Rigorous theoretical understanding of how latent variables govern generalization performance in Variational Autoencoders remains elusive, particularly for continuous latent spaces.
approach: The paper establishes information-theoretic analysis for VAEs by adapting the leave-one-out conditional mutual information framework from supervised learning to unsupervised continuous latent spaces.
contribution: The first information-theoretic analysis shows that VAE generalization error is bounded solely by the information complexity of the encoder and latent variables, independent of the decoder.

problem: Speech-driven portrait animation and viewpoint control rely on strict reference conditioning and geometry-based inversion, leading to limited motion diversity and identity drift.
approach: STARCaster uses softer identity constraints and learns multi-view nature implicitly through 2D video diffusion, employing compositional progression from ID-aware motion modeling to audio-visual synchronization to novel view animation.
contribution: STARCaster generalizes effectively across tasks and identities, consistently surpassing prior approaches in different benchmarks via decoupled learning where view consistency and temporal coherence train independently.

problem: LLMs condition reasoning on statistical regularities from pretraining rather than explicit formal semantics, failing to follow supplied rules under distribution shift.
approach: PLSemanticsBench pairs featherweight C programs with operational and K semantics, probing whether LLMs can compose rules, select rules, sustain conditioning over long traces, and follow novel semantics.
contribution: Across 11 frontier LLMs, strong final-state accuracy (up to 90%) drops sharply by 40-60 percentage points under semantic mutations, with even the best achieving only 35% long-horizon conditioning accuracy.

problem: Imbalanced Unreliable Partial Label Learning (I-UPLL) suffers from severe class imbalance and unreliable candidate labels, making stable prior estimation difficult early in training.
approach: CLAPOR trains models under deliberately perturbed class priors sampled from a Dirichlet distribution that deviates from the current estimated prior, encouraging consistent performance under uncertainty.
contribution: CLAPOR demonstrates effectiveness across various I-UPLL settings by avoiding dependence on accurate prior estimation and naturally preserving attention to minority classes.

problem: Asynchronous reinforcement learning for LLM training suffers from policy lag because gradient variance scales exponentially with task difficulty under staleness, especially on hard tasks.
approach: GAS uses gradient-aware scheduling with a bandit-based curriculum for task difficulty, execution-aware staleness budgets, and curriculum-staleness coupling that tightens staleness budget as difficulty rises.
contribution: GAS improves code generation Pass@1 from 39.7% to 60.1% while training at 2.3× the throughput of synchronous GRPO by matching each task's staleness budget to its loss-landscape curvature.

problem: Dehazing struggles to effectively restore polarization information in images, leading to inaccurate polarimetric signatures and physical inconsistencies in scattering environments.
approach: DuRP proposes a dual-stage physics-embedded learning framework with generalized polarization physics models that relax ideal assumptions and use differentiable operators to estimate latent physical parameters.
contribution: DuRP achieves state-of-the-art joint restoration performance and significantly enhances polarization-based vision tasks by accurately recovering both polarimetric state and radiance.

problem: Chain-of-thoughts fail to accurately reflect LLMs' inner thinking processes, making it difficult to identify unsuitable and sensitive behaviors for monitoring.
approach: TELLME improves LLM transparency by working with hidden representations rather than external modules, helping monitors identify unsuitable behaviors.
contribution: TELLME achieves consistent improvement on detoxification tasks across multimodal test sets, distinct architectures, and varying parameter scales, with improvements analyzed from optimal transport theory and empirical perspectives.

problem: Partial model merging (PMM) mitigates privacy risks by keeping private parameters local, but the privacy properties remain underexplored and vulnerable to reconstruction.
approach: The paper proposes a novel model clone attack to assess risk of reconstructing the unshared private part under eight scenarios with varying prior knowledge of training data, parameters, or model structure.
contribution: Experiments reveal that merging NNs without adequate protection is highly vulnerable, with adversaries able to recover significant portions of private model performance even with limited exposure.

problem: Agentic reinforcement learning remains highly unstable, often leading to training collapse that limits scalability to larger environments and longer interaction horizons.
approach: ARLArena provides a stable training recipe and systematically decomposes policy gradient into four core design dimensions, proposing SAMPO to mitigate dominant sources of instability.
contribution: SAMPO achieves consistently stable training and strong performance across diverse agentic tasks with open-sourced code.

problem: Current LLM code agent evaluation focuses on single-turn code generation, failing to evaluate continuous optimization and multi-turn iterative development capabilities.
approach: CATArena introduces a framework where agents engage in multi-turn tournaments, refining code through self-reflection and peer-learning based on execution feedback, with dual metrics decoupling static proficiency from evolutionary potential.
contribution: Experiments show that an agent's evolutionary potential is not strictly correlated with initial proficiency, and current agents struggle to leverage both peer-learning and self-reflection effectively.

problem: Large-scale multi-agent communication faces a trade-off between scalability and task adaptivity, as growing pairwise interactions make traditional communication schemes ineffective.
approach: SOPS constrains communication to an exponential-graph backbone with small diameter while learning task-conditioned probabilistic subgraph distributions via pairwise scoring network over agent states.
contribution: SOPS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across cooperative benchmarks of diverse scales and exhibits robust zero-shot transfer capabilities.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLMs allow adversarial inputs to trigger severe routing concentration, creating computational bottlenecks and degrading service quality via denial-of-service.
approach: RepetitionCurse exploits MoE routing vulnerabilities using simple repetitive token patterns in a model-agnostic manner to construct attack prompts.
contribution: RepetitionCurse increases time-to-first-token by 20% to 148% on 8-GPU clusters, significantly degrading service quality through universal flaws in MoE router behavior.

problem: Capacitated fair-range k-clustering incorporating both capacity constraints and demographic fairness is computationally complex, with limited approximation guarantees.
approach: The paper strengthens inapproximability results and provides polynomial-time O(log k) and O(log^2 k)-approximation algorithms for k-median and k-means respectively in the constant-group regime.
contribution: The analysis shows inapproximability persists even when fair-range constraints are trivially satisfiable, while providing practical approximation algorithms with hardness-matched bounds.

problem: Unlearning for diffusion language models is unexplored, yet architectural differences create new challenges for effective and robust unlearning not addressed by autoregressive-focused methods.
approach: The paper proposes an adversarial reinforcement learning framework where a context generator adversarially produces informative contexts to elicit unlearned knowledge, while the DLM is optimized to suppress recall.
contribution: The approach achieves robust unlearning in DLMs by addressing credit assignment and stability issues in adversarial learning, with extended evaluation across diverse generation settings.

problem: Existing prototype-based anomaly detection methods model normal data via unimodal Gaussian priors, failing to capture inherent multi-modality and resulting in blurred decision boundaries.
approach: MPFM learns a continuous transformation from normal feature distributions to structured Gaussian mixture prototype space, modeling velocity field as a Gaussian mixture where each component corresponds to a distinct normal class.
contribution: MPFM achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks under both single- and multi-anomaly settings via mode-aware and semantically coherent distribution transport.

problem: Training-time defenses against neural backdoors need to isolate benign samples from poisoned data, but current methods either compromise natural accuracy or fail against certain attacks.
approach: ABCS formulates this as coreset selection using Cumulative Entropy as criterion to select benign samples with high informativeness, while unlearning chosen samples in each epoch.
contribution: ABCS mitigates backdooring attacks consistently with negligible impact on natural performance, with public implementation available.

problem: Large pretrained models may contain dense task-specific experts around pretrained weights, yet discovery of these solutions typically requires structured optimization methods.
approach: The paper samples N random parameter vectors, selects top K, and ensembles them via majority vote, treating pretrained weights as a distribution over parameter vectors.
contribution: This simple fully-parallel post-training method is competitive with standard methods like PPO, GRPO, and ES for contemporary large-scale models.

problem: Large vision-language models suffer from object hallucination because visual features and pretrained textual representations become intertwined in deeper layers.
approach: REVIS uses orthogonal projection to extract pure visual information vectors and employs calibrated sparse intervention only at the layer where suppression occurs.
contribution: REVIS reduces object hallucination rates by approximately 19% compared to baselines while preserving general reasoning capabilities through training-free sparse latent steering.

problem: Representation alignment in audio Flow Matching critically depends on choice of supervised layers, which is typically made heuristically based on depth rather than causal contribution.
approach: AG-REPA uses forward-only gate ablation (FoG-A) to quantify each layer's causal contribution to the velocity field, enabling sparse layer selection and adaptive weighting for alignment.
contribution: AG-REPA outperforms REPA baselines across unified speech and general-audio training by aligning to causally dominant layers rather than representationally rich but functionally passive ones.

problem: World model-based evaluation of robot policies is unreliable because visual predictions can self-correct failures into false positives or yield artifacts under out-of-distribution controls.
approach: dWorldEval uses action-centric discrete-diffusion that maps observations, instructions, and action chunks into a shared token space, with sparse keyframe memory and progress-as-text generation.
contribution: dWorldEval significantly outperforms video diffusion baselines in action controllability and stabilizes long-horizon multi-view rollouts for accurate policy ranking.

problem: Optimal Transport traditionally relies on fixed ground cost and produces single deterministic plans, overlooking inherent variability and noise in real-world data.
approach: The paper introduces Sinkhorn-parameterized Variational Inference, treating the Sinkhorn map as a differentiable reparameterization of entropic plans and using normalizing flows.
contribution: The method matches quality of intensive sampling techniques at a fraction of computational cost, scaling effectively to large-scale problems.

problem: Transformers face challenges in generalizing to out-of-distribution datasets, yet theoretical understanding of OOD detection learnability remains limited.
approach: The paper introduces OOD detection PAC Theory for transformers, establishing conditions for distribution and model configurations that enable OOD detection learnability.
contribution: By penalizing misclassification of outliers and strategically generating soft synthetic outliers, the derived algorithm achieves state-of-the-art OOD detection across various data formats.

problem: Agentic AI systems that exceed human capabilities pose a control problem: how can humans maintain meaningful oversight while lacking complex assumptions or practical methods?
approach: CCO aggregates auxiliary scoring functions into a penalty measuring deviation from conservative baseline, calibrating conservatism online via Conformal Decision Theory.
contribution: CCO achieves substantial reductions in ethical violations while preserving reward on MACHIAVELLI and constrains adversarially misaligned agents on SWE-bench, with empirical violation rates matching specified targets.

problem: Pretraining corpora contain extensive discourse about AI systems, yet the causal influence of this discourse on downstream alignment remains unknown.
approach: By pretraining 6.9B-parameter LLMs with varying amounts of (mis)alignment discourse, the paper shows discussion of AI contributes to alignment behavior through learned behavioral priors.
contribution: Upsampling aligned discourse reduces misalignment scores from 45% to 9%, establishing self-fulfilling alignment as a complement to post-training.

problem: LLM-based search agents can be misled by unreliable search results into producing unsafe outputs, introducing a new threat surface not addressed by current defenses.
approach: SafeSearch proposes an automated red-teaming framework spanning five risk categories (misinformation, prompt injection, etc.) to evaluate search agent scaffolds.
contribution: SafeSearch reveals substantial vulnerabilities with highest ASR reaching 90.5%, shows common defenses offer limited protection, and enables practical measurement of search agent safety.

problem: Referring video object segmentation assumes targets are visible in observed video, limiting real-world use when queries refer to objects outside the current view.
approach: RVAS introduces a new task combining reasoning about exploration policy with locating and segmenting objects, proposing LESA with state controller and hierarchical memory for efficient streaming.
contribution: LESA substantially reduces inference cost while maintaining competitive planning quality and consistently improves segmentation accuracy on the RVAS dataset.

problem: Designing high-performance neural networks for new tasks requires balancing optimization quality with search efficiency, but current methods fail to achieve this balance.
approach: M-DESIGN models performance gains from fine-grained architectural modifications as edit-effect evidence, building evidence graphs from prior tasks with adaptive retrieval and predictive planners.
contribution: Based on 67,760 graph neural networks across 22 datasets, M-DESIGN achieves search-space best performance in 26 of 33 cases under strict budget constraints.

problem: Domain generalization requires finding representations that remain predictive under distribution shifts, but alignment objectives that ignore discriminative structure become ill-conditioned under finite samples.
approach: RDI extends rate-distortion theory to Grassmann manifolds, modeling class-conditional representations as low-dimensional subspaces and optimizing cross-domain alignment with spectral-volumetric complexity.
contribution: RDI provides finite-sample stability guarantees under bounded shifts and is competitive with strong baselines on DomainBed with ablations confirming both alignment and complexity control are necessary.

problem: Continuous-Depth Neural Networks suffer from high computational costs due to solving numerous nonlinear ODEs during training and inference.
approach: CoDA uses Mori-Zwanzig/Koopman operator theory to replace continuous-depth layers with a compact GRU module, a single low-dimensional linear ODE, and a dense layer.
contribution: CoDA achieves 6.7× training speedup and 1.8× inference speedup on LFM-1.2B without loss of accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art acceleration techniques across six applications.

problem: Test-time scaling in AI discovery requires finding a single great solution to a specific problem rather than generalizing across problems, which existing methods don't optimize for.
approach: TTT-Discover performs reinforcement learning at test time so the LLM continues training with problem-specific experience, prioritizing promising solutions through specialized learning objective and search.
contribution: TTT-Discover sets new state of the art on mathematics, GPU kernel engineering, algorithm design, and biology problems, including Erdős problems and GPUMode kernel competition, using open models.

problem: Vision-language models assume fixed patch-based 2D vision features are necessary, but fine-tuned encoders develop increasingly abstract and less spatially coherent representations.
approach: RADIO1D compresses images into compact variable-length 1D token sequences using multi-teacher knowledge distillation and autoencoder design.
contribution: RADIO1D provides flexible accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs through adjustable token counts, delivering competitive VLM performance with lower computational overhead and better accuracy.

problem: Open deep research agents are trained on easily verifiable short-form QA via RL with verifiable rewards, which fails to extend to realistic long-form deep research tasks.
approach: RLER uses Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics where rubrics co-evolve with the policy during training, incorporating newly explored search information and contrasting responses.
contribution: DR Tulu-8B substantially outperforms existing open agents by 15.6% on average across science/healthcare benchmarks and matches proprietary agents while being 1000× cheaper per query.

problem: GRPO-style RL-based LLM fine-tuning relies on heuristic trust-region approximations that fail when importance ratios fall outside clipping range, leading to brittle optimization.
approach: QUATRO directly enforces trust-region constraints through principled optimization, yielding interpretable objectives with explicit control over policy updates and entropy-controlled optimization.
contribution: QUATRO shows stable training under increased policy staleness and aggressive learning rates on diverse mathematical reasoning benchmarks, maintaining well-controlled entropy.

problem: Unlearning in diffusion models aims to remove undesirable data while preserving utility, but these objectives conflict and require principled formulation.
approach: The paper formulates unlearning as constrained optimization minimizing deviation from pretrained models subject to explicit separation constraints from unlearning distributions, using KL divergences and likelihood constraints.
contribution: The approach achieves superior retention-unlearning tradeoffs for concept and data unlearning compared to weight-based baselines via explicit characterization of optimal solutions.

problem: Autoregressive models and energy-based models represent distinct paradigms for LLMs, but their relationship to optimal policy and lookahead capabilities remains unclear.
approach: The paper establishes an explicit bijection between ARMs and EBMs in function space via the chain rule of probability, corresponding to a special case of the soft Bellman equation.
contribution: The analysis derives equivalence between supervised learning of ARMs and EBMs and provides theoretical error bounds for EBM distillation into ARMs, offering insights into ARM planning ability.

problem: Temporal answer grounding in instructional videos is challenging due to need for semantic comprehension and significant length mismatch between untrimmed videos and target moments.
approach: CACR employs candidate selection via Vision-Language Pre-training, then applies temporal logic reasoning enhanced by rejection reward mechanism optimized via Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: CACR achieves state-of-the-art performance on six benchmarks via reasoning-based retrieval that efficiently generates candidate segments before applying causal reasoning.

problem: Token merging accelerates Transformers by reducing sequence length, but induces covariate shift and performance collapse under aggressive compression due to energy drift and biased attention distributions.
approach: Reframe token merging as statistical reconstruction and introduce asymptotic radial-angular decomposition to decouple magnitude and distributional distortions, yielding a single scaling factor correction √r.
contribution: Closed-form optimal corrections calibrate both energy balance and distributional fidelity, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness across compression levels on vision Transformers.

problem: Reference-guided video editing requires faithful application of text instructions while preserving motion and content, but existing methods suffer from modality gaps (decoupled encoders) or loss of spatial details (unified encoders).
approach: MiVE repurposes vision-language models as multiscale feature extractors, hierarchically extracting features from early layers (spatial details) and deeper layers (semantic understanding) and integrating them into a unified diffusion transformer.
contribution: MiVE achieves state-of-the-art performance in reference-guided video editing, ranking highest in human preference over both academic methods and commercial systems.

problem: Small language models lag behind larger counterparts in reasoning; existing fixes either invoke expensive LLMs at reasoning divergence or rely on limited distillation.
approach: Identify local sufficiency where LLM's preferred token resides in SLM's top-K predictions; propose Select to Think (S2T) to reframe LLM as selector among SLM proposals and distill selection logic into SLM via discrete ranking supervision.
contribution: S2T-Local improves 1.5B SLM's Math Avg. by 24.1% relative gain over greedy decoding, matching 8-path self-consistency with single-trajectory efficiency.

problem: Understanding educational social dynamics faces a fundamental dilemma: observational studies lack causal power while controlled experiments face ethical constraints.
approach: EduMirror provides a multi-agent simulator with value-driven agents grounded in psychological needs and a dual-track measurement protocol for observable behaviors and latent psychological states.
contribution: EduMirror generates educational social dynamics that are realistic, theory-consistent, and measurable, enabling in silico hypothesis testing and counterfactual intervention analysis.

problem: Black-box optimization of Lipschitz functions under noise lacks explicit optimality certificates and measurable progress guarantees.
approach: Certificate-Guided Pruning (CGP) maintains an active set of potentially optimal points via confidence-adjusted Lipschitz envelopes, with theoretical convergence under margin conditions.
contribution: CGP achieves sample complexity Õ(ε^-(2+α)) and demonstrates strong empirical performance across 12 benchmarks with principled stopping criteria.

problem: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference but judge-based verification relies on human annotations or verifiable ground truths, limiting generalizability across diverse NLP tasks.
approach: SelfJudge trains judge verifiers via self-supervision of the target model by assessing semantic preservation through token-substituted response analysis.
contribution: SelfJudge achieves superior inference-accuracy trade-offs over judge baselines and generalizes broadly across diverse NLP tasks without ground truth annotations.

problem: Building omni-modal assistants via end-to-end multimodal alignment incurs substantial data and compute costs while limiting extensibility.
approach: LLM Orchestration integrates off-the-shelf modality experts without gradient-based training via an LLM controller for expert selection, text-centric cross-modal memory for compression, and unified interaction layer for streaming support.
contribution: LLM Orchestration achieves strong performance on multimodal benchmarks with low overhead and modular upgradeability, providing practical alternative to costly joint training.

problem: Subjective LLM evaluation faces a reproducibility crisis where even the same evaluator contradicts itself on re-judging samples due to dimension drift in free-form protocols.
approach: Reformulate subjective evaluation as information-theoretic optimization using Expected Information Gain (EIG) framework to construct stable yet adaptive rubrics that eliminate dimension drift.
contribution: EIG-based approach substantially improves evaluation consistency and alignment with human judgments on six benchmarks including CharacterEval and MT-Bench, outperforming CoT and fixed-questionnaire baselines.

problem: Audio self-supervised learning models rely on finetuning for evaluation because simple probing fails to unlock their full potential and alters model rankings on AudioSet.
approach: Introduce Convex Gated Probing (CGP), a prototype-based method using gating to efficiently utilize frozen layers and expose latent task-relevant information.
contribution: Better Audio Transformer (BAT) refined via CGP establishes new state-of-the-art on audio benchmarks through improved preprocessing, architecture, and pretraining recipe.

problem: In multi-model self-consuming training regimes where models learn from each other's outputs, human curation of one model may dampen or invert alignment effects rather than consistently enhance them.
approach: Formalize multi-model self-consuming framework, characterize convergence dynamics, and analyze self-influence (local curation impact) versus cross-influence (propagation to other models).
contribution: Cross-model interactions can degrade long-term alignment despite local curation benefits, revealing fundamental limits of human curation in interconnected systems.

problem: Existing disease prediction models depend on event-level healthcare representations and lack explicit modeling of social determinants of health (SDoH), limiting personalized disease modeling.
approach: DiffDT integrates multi-organ sensor data with diffusion models and geometric diffusion for brain networks, conditioned on ICD-coded SDoH proxies for disease trajectory simulation.
contribution: DiffDT achieves significant improvements over autoregressive baselines on UK Biobank with multi-organ imaging and medical history data for in silico disease reasoning.

problem: LoRA convergence analysis is poorly understood due to lack of Lipschitz smoothness, with existing results only addressing asymptotic behavior or assuming strong boundedness.
approach: Provide non-asymptotic convergence analysis by reformulating LoRA in terms of outer product of stacked adapter matrices and applying modified descent lemma for reparametrized function.
contribution: LoRA gradient descent converges to stationary point at rate O(1/log T) without Lipschitz smoothness assumptions, reflecting actual practice.

problem: Vision-language models fail to generate personalized responses based on user-specific visual-textual context due to inability to associate visual inputs with accumulated experience.
approach: CoViP treats personalized image captioning as core task and improves through reinforcement-learning-based post-training and caption-augmented generation with diagnostic evaluations ruling out textual shortcuts.
contribution: CoViP improves personalized image captioning and yields holistic gains across downstream personalization tasks, with existing VLMs showing substantial limitations on visual context leveraging.

problem: Transformers for evidence-grounded binary adjudication are sensitive to evidence order, producing unreliable answers; token-level training minimizes expected description length but remains position-sensitive at fixed orderings.
approach: Formalize expectation-realization gap via Quantified Martingale Violation (QMV) bound and Expectation-level Decompression Law (EDFL), yielding information-theoretic gates (B2T, RoH, ISR) for answer/abstain decisions.
contribution: On 3,059 grounded items, ISR=1 gate achieves 0.0-0.7% hallucination with 20.6-27.9% abstention (95% CIs) without universal calibration claims.

problem: Long video understanding requires balancing cloud-based reasoning quality against prohibitive bandwidth costs and latency, with edge solutions sacrificing accuracy.
approach: SCOPE decomposes complex queries into a structured DAG observation plan via cloud LMM, guiding edge retrieval by logical necessity rather than statistical similarity.
contribution: SCOPE matches cloud-level accuracy with significantly lower transmission costs and outperforms baselines on Video-MME and LongVideoBench complex reasoning tasks.

problem: Chain-of-Thought reasoning in autoregressive LLMs remains brittle under distribution shift and long-horizon generation, with small deviations compounding into inference drift.
approach: Thinking in Flow (TiF) augments Transformers with persistent continuous-time thought state governed by dissipative ODE dynamics, with demand-supply gates determining when and how to intervene.
contribution: TiF improves robustness to distractions and semantic perturbations while maintaining or improving accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Single predictors deployed across multiple subpopulations require fairness approaches that account for different potential predictability levels across groups.
approach: Interpret group fairness as bargaining problem; propose relative improvement (ratio of actual to potential risk reduction), recovering Kalai-Smorodinsky solution with scale invariance and individual monotonicity.
contribution: Relative improvement provides axiomatic fairness justification and establishes finite-sample convergence guarantees under mild conditions.

problem: Autoregressive LLMs fail in complex reasoning because early-stage errors remain uncorrectable due to irreversibility in Transformer architecture.
approach: HEdit detects internal inconsistency at trigger points, backtracks to critical anchors, and uses lightweight trainable editor to refine Key-Value caches during generation.
contribution: HEdit improves mathematical reasoning by 2.2-10.8% with <0.5% added parameters, providing dynamic pluggable solution for low-resource environments.

problem: Training data reconstruction from KKT conditions shows empirical success but lacks clarity on when equations have unique solutions and how to reliably recover them.
approach: Provide sufficient conditions for KKT identifiability in two-layer networks with polynomial activations; introduce sample splitting for curvature-aware refinement escaping poor stationary points.
contribution: Sample splitting consistently improves reconstruction performance across multiple reconstruction methods on real datasets.

problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation suffers from prohibitive computational costs when incorporating large document volumes; existing compression heuristics compromise task performance.
approach: CORE-RAG uses performance-driven learning with task performance as feedback signal, with knowledge distillation initialization for robust policy learning.
contribution: At 3% compression ratio, CORE improves average EM score by 3.3 points compared to using full documents without performance degradation.

problem: Pre-Layer Normalization is standard but incurs statistical-computation overhead and suffers from curse of depth where hidden-state magnitudes grow with layer count, destabilizing training.
approach: Bounded Hyperbolic Tanh (BHyT) combines tanh nonlinearity with data-driven input bounding to keep activations in non-saturating range, computing exact statistics once per block with lightweight variance approximation.
contribution: BHyT achieves 1.6% faster training and 1.77% higher token throughput versus RMSNorm while maintaining strong pretraining and post-SFT performance.

problem: Estimating kernel means efficiently for query points requires bounds that improve in regimes with small error and intermediate diameter.
approach: Prove new bound Õ(d + ε∆²+1/ε³) for Gaussian kernel estimation via fast spherical embedding theorem that preserves local distances while limiting embedded diameter.
contribution: New bound improves over previous Õ(d+1/ε⁴) and Õ(d+∆²/ε²) in small-error and intermediate-diameter regimes.

problem: Hypergraph Neural Networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks but lack adversarial training mechanisms; existing attacks are white-box and customized for specific perturbation types.
approach: Propose MeLA, a generic meta-objective-based gray-box attack framework leveraging hypergraph Laplacian for structural and feature perturbations; develop adversarial training mechanism with convergence guarantees.
contribution: Adversarial training enhances HGNN defense and MeLA attacks are effective in poisoning and evasion settings across various models and datasets.

problem: Multi-modal brain network analysis treats phenotypes only as auxiliary features and assumes connectome should be learned uniformly across phenotypes, ignoring context-dependent interpretations.
approach: PhenoBrain injects phenotype information at mechanism level via phenotype-conditioned long-range routing kernel and phenotypic-guided attention regulation.
contribution: PhenoBrain achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-modal brain network analysis datasets with phenotype-conditioned architecture.

problem: Supervised graph outlier detection suffers from severe class imbalance; diffusion-based augmentation improves sample quality but incurs prohibitive multi-step computational costs.
approach: GOCM proposes single-step graph outlier synthesis via consistency model with Origin Consistency mechanism using Interval-based Origin Inference; MiVGAE handles heterogeneous graphs.
contribution: GOCM achieves superior detection performance with significantly improved generation efficiency compared to multi-step diffusion methods.

problem: Thinking with Images (TWI) for multimodal reasoning assumes interleaved chain-of-thought is faultless, but imperfect visual cue mining and reasoning cause error accumulation.
approach: RTWI estimates reliability of visual cues and textual reasoning in unified text-centric manner, employing robust filtering and voting modules to prevent noisy thinking.
contribution: RTWI demonstrates effectiveness against noisy thinking on seven benchmarks, preventing error accumulation from contaminating final answers.

problem: Inference-time steering relies on activation addition which alters hidden-state magnitudes, raising concerns about representation collapse and degraded open-ended generation.
approach: Spherical Steering rotates activations along geodesic toward target direction, preserving signal integrity; incorporates confidence gate dynamically modulating steering strength based on input uncertainty.
contribution: Spherical Steering outperforms addition-based baselines by +10% on TruthfulQA, COPA, and Storycloze while maintaining general generation quality.

problem: Multi-modal object re-identification uses MLLMs to generate text annotations as supervision but treats strong and weak correspondence image-text pairs equally, limiting discriminative learning.
approach: CCL framework explicitly models correspondence degree via Correspondence-Guided Semantic Refinement and Cognitive-Driven Dynamic Optimization modules for progressive learning.
contribution: CCL enhances feature-level alignment and optimization adaptivity, yielding robust and discriminative multi-modal representations.

problem: Autonomous GUI agents struggle with multi-step tasks due to constrained context windows and static policies failing to adapt to dynamic environments.
approach: SE-GA integrates hierarchical memory with iterative self-improvement; Test-Time Memory Extension (TTME) retrieves episodic/semantic/experiential memories; Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution (MASE) trains via collected data.
contribution: SE-GA achieves 89.0% on ScreenSpot and 75.8% on AndroidControl-High, with superior generalization on AndroidWorld benchmark.

problem: Message-passing neural networks suffer from information bottleneck and oversquashing when capturing long-range dependencies; spectral filtering enables global mixing but requires restrictive stability assumptions.
approach: S³GNN mitigates oversquashing by lightweightly reintroducing omitted components with lower complexity while maintaining effective stability constraints on feature transformations.
contribution: S³GNN achieves up to order-of-magnitude error reduction with up to 50% fewer parameters across diverse domains including long-range benchmarks and mesh-based dynamics.

problem: Fairness constraints in neural networks traditionally operate at prediction time but lack provable guarantees for streaming predictions with small batch sizes.
approach: Introduce fairness layer as differentiable optimization layer appended to output layer that guarantees output parity; develop online primal-dual inference algorithm for streaming predictions.
contribution: Fairness layer provides provable aggregate fairness guarantees and differentiability properties during backpropagation, validated through numerical experiments.

problem: Extreme model compression aims to realize spectral energy gain where low-rank binary approximations outperform tiny-rank floating-point, but latent geometry misalignment prevents realization.
approach: LittleBit-2 employs Internal Latent Rotation and Joint Iterative Quantization (Joint-ITQ) to align coherent latent distributions with binary hypercube as geometric preconditioner.
contribution: LittleBit-2 establishes new state-of-the-art in sub-1-bit regime (1~0.1 bpp) on Llama-2 and Llama-3, matching fidelity of leading 1-bit baselines.

problem: Federated recommender systems represent each user with single embedding, assuming fixed preferences; limited client data renders point estimates brittle.
approach: Model user preferences as distributions rather than points using diffusion-based generative framework, aggregating predictions across diverse embeddings to preserve uncertainty and diversity.
contribution: Distributional formulation yields more stable ranking behavior and improved robustness under ambiguous feedback on federated recommendation benchmarks.

problem: Prompt tuning of CLIP-like models is sensitive to label noise as mislabeled samples generate disproportionately large gradients that overwhelm pre-trained priors.
approach: Double-Softmax Prompt Tuning (DSPT) applies sequential probabilistic normalization inducing self-adaptive saturation zone that suppresses gradients from high-error noisy samples.
contribution: DSPT achieves state-of-the-art robustness across noisy benchmarks without hyperparameters, transforming gradient vanishing into principled noise-filtering shield.

problem: Network pruning improves efficiency but pruned models often fail in generative language tasks despite performing well in non-generative tasks; this discrepancy is poorly understood.
approach: Analyze pruning from representation-hierarchy perspective, decomposing computation into embedding/logit/probability spaces and tracking how pruning perturbations amplify through nonlinearities.
contribution: Shows stability of embedding and logit spaces enables pruning for retrieval/classification but probability-space amplification degrades generation; provides practical pruning guidance.

problem: Steering LLM reasoning trajectories toward truth is underexplored; naive representation editing through fixed steering vectors risks collateral damage to correct reasoning paths.
approach: DynaSteer employs pattern clustering to disentangle reasoning manifolds, uses Fisher-LDA to project purified truth, and dynamically monitors lookahead entropy for selective steering.
contribution: DynaSteer improves reasoning on MATH benchmarks and demonstrates generalization to out-of-domain coding tasks via dynamic representation editing.

problem: Model merging assumes improvements at fine-tuning stage propagate downstream, but long fine-tuning of experts for individual performance degrades merging due to memorization.
approach: Show late fine-tuning memorizes difficult examples creating negative parameter interference; propose task-dependent aggressive early stopping to improve model merging.
contribution: Early stopping strategies significantly improve model merging performance across vision and language modalities and multiple model scales.

problem: Long-context adaptation via fine-tuning remains brittle with high positional variance even when controlling for task format and difficulty.
approach: RoPE-Perturbed Self-Distillation forms alternative views by perturbing RoPE indices to move context to different positions and trains via self-distillation for consistent predictions.
contribution: Improves positional robustness with up to 12.04 pp gain on RULER-64K for Llama-3-8B and 2.71 pp on RULER-256K, plus improved length extrapolation.

problem: Static retrieval indices in RAG cause repeated multi-hop traversal for related queries, increasing latency and compute; implementations lack adaptive memory.
approach: GAM-RAG accumulates retrieval experience from recurring queries and updates hierarchical memory over time using Kalman-inspired gain rule for uncertainty-aware updates.
contribution: GAM-RAG improves average performance by 3.95% and by 8.19% with 5-turn memory while reducing inference cost by 61%.

problem: Coresets for clustering provide strong guarantees for all solutions but theoretical sizes are much larger than those sufficient in practice.
approach: Define approximation-preserving coresets providing weaker guarantees for good solutions only (those with low cost), balancing between strong and weak coreset guarantees.
contribution: Smaller approximation-preserving coreset sizes suffice empirically, with complementary lower bounds showing small distortion cannot reduce size further.

problem: Modern learned models like LLMs can achieve strong compression, but face critical challenges when deployed: model non-determinism causes different predictions on different machines despite identical parameters, leading to complete decoding failure during decompression.
approach: Generalize Probability Matching Interval Coding (PMATIC) to allow tighter theoretical results and more flexible parameter optimization, enabling robust compression and decompression despite bounded prediction mismatch.
contribution: Improved compression efficiency and robustness over PMATIC through generalized framework design.

problem: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are typically built with spherical tensors, but Cartesian tensor formulations are more naturally aligned with atomic coordinates and targets, yet remain underdeveloped.
approach: Develop a Cartesian framework for irreducible Cartesian tensors (ICTs) by introducing Cartesian-3j symbols and Cartesian Generalized Clebsch-Gordan Coefficients as analogues of spherical tensor coupling, enabling controlled comparison of tensor bases.
contribution: Cartesian counterparts of MACE, NequIP, and Allegro achieve comparable accuracy to spherical models; TACE-v1-OAM-M demonstrates competitive performance on Matbench Discovery.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs as agents overlooks critical coordination between long-term planning and multi-step execution, causing propagation of impractical plans and plan-deviated trajectories that hinder performance on long-horizon tasks.
approach: Propose CoPE, a framework that uses Self-Refining MCTS to generate plans and execution trajectories, quantifying planning-execution coordination and assigning higher optimization weights to well-coordinated samples.
contribution: CoPE substantially improves agent coordination and outperforms baselines on benchmarks with long-horizon multi-step tasks.

problem: Existing decentralized optimization algorithms are designed for single-level and two-level tasks but cannot efficiently handle decentralized stochastic K-level optimization (K>2) due to computation and communication overhead from multi-level structure.
approach: Propose a decentralized stochastic K-level variance-reduced gradient descent algorithm with novel theoretical analysis addressing recursive dependence issues caused by multi-level structure.
contribution: Novel algorithm effectively solves decentralized K-level optimization problems with improved efficiency.

problem: Deep Transformer training faces a fundamental trade-off: PreNorm ensures stability but risks performance degradation, while PostNorm offers strong performance but suffers from severe training instability.
approach: Introduce SpanNorm, combining PreNorm's clean residual path with PostNorm-style computation that normalizes the residual output, paired with principled scaling to maintain bounded signal variance.
contribution: SpanNorm maintains bounded signal variance throughout the network, prevents gradient issues from PostNorm, and consistently outperforms standard normalization in both dense and MoE scenarios.

problem: Spectral clustering via anchor-based approximations often yields degenerate or unbalanced partitions without explicit cluster-size control, and fails to enforce user-specified bounds on cluster sizes.
approach: Develop SC-FAGC, integrating entropy regularization and bilateral cardinality constraints within anchor-based spectral clustering, solved via an Iteratively Re-weighted scheme with Double-Bounded Optimal Transport (Sinkhorn-Knopp).
contribution: SC-FAGC achieves state-of-the-art performance on six clustering metrics while strictly enforcing prescribed anchor-level size constraints and inducing effective data-level control.

problem: Fair graph clustering requires proportional representation of protected groups within clusters, but existing spectral solutions rely on expensive eigendecompositions of the graph Laplacian, limiting scalability.
approach: Formulate fair spectral clustering as constrained optimization on a Riemannian manifold, employing Riemannian alternating direction method of multipliers with variable-splitting for efficient subproblem solution.
contribution: R-FairSC significantly improves computational efficiency over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining high clustering quality and fairness constraints.

problem: Understanding whether and how vision-language models acquire spatial relational understanding remains unclear; existing work does not explain the mechanistic basis for this capability.
approach: Use a controllable 1D testbed with paired image-text descriptions to probe how left-right relations emerge in CLIP-style Transformers, performing attention decomposition to identify mechanisms.
contribution: Contrastive training learns left-right relations driven primarily by label diversity; attention decomposition reveals that positional-token embedding interactions induce horizontal attention gradients that break symmetry.

problem: Foundation models yield overconfident, uncalibrated predictions; standard ensemble approaches for uncertainty quantification have prohibitive computational cost that scales linearly with ensemble size.
approach: Propose Singular Value Ensemble (SVE), which freezes singular vectors of weight matrices (assumed to be meaningful orthogonal knowledge directions) and trains only per-member singular values to modulate contribution.
contribution: SVE achieves comparable uncertainty estimation to explicit ensembles while increasing parameter count by <1%, making principled uncertainty estimation accessible for resource-constrained settings.

problem: State-space models like Mamba and gated linear attention offer linear complexity but lack expressivity and robust state-tracking for complex reasoning compared to Transformers.
approach: Reframe sequence modeling through Bayesian filtering using Kalman filters in information form, enabling associative scan for parallel training while maintaining explicit belief-state uncertainty.
contribution: Kalman Linear Attention (KLA) provides strictly more expressive non-linear updates than GLA while retaining computational advantages, matching or outperforming modern SSMs on language modeling benchmarks.

problem: Monitorability (whether chain-of-thought traces faithfully reflect internal computation) appears as a 'free gift' during early RLVR training, but when and why this occurs remains unclear and under-characterized.
approach: Systematically evaluate monitorability across model families and training domains; perform mechanistic analysis to identify causes via response distribution sharpening and attention to prompts.
contribution: Monitorability gains are strongly data-dependent and primarily driven by entropy reduction and increased prompt attention, not stronger causal reliance on reasoning; improvements are orthogonal to capability gains.

problem: LLM agents rely on on-the-fly reasoning that re-derives solutions in recurring scenarios, causing computational redundancy and instability from insufficient experience reuse.
approach: Propose Skill-Pro, which autonomously learns reusable procedural skills from interaction without parameter updates, using Non-Parametric PPO for high-quality skill verification and score-based maintenance.
contribution: Skill-Pro achieves superior skill reuse rates and significant gains with extreme memory compression, enabling transparent accumulation and refinement of procedural knowledge for long-term autonomy.

problem: Learning beneficial treatment allocations in precision medicine requires controlling treatment risk (unnecessary treated proportion), which is generally not identifiable from randomized or observational data.
approach: Develop a certifiable learning method that controls treatment risk using finite samples in the partially identified setting, with theoretical guarantees on risk bounds.
contribution: Method enables provably safe treatment allocation learning despite partial identifiability of treatment risk.

problem: Generalist graph anomaly detection aims for one-for-all universal detection across unseen graphs, but existing PCA-based feature alignment harmonizes dimensions while neglecting semantic alignment, causing negative transfer.
approach: Propose REFI-GAD using a Relational Fingerprint (REFI) that encodes anomaly-indicative cues from contextual and structural perspectives, combined with transformer encoder and SNR-guided refinement.
contribution: REFI-GAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art across 14 datasets through semantic-aware feature alignment and domain-specific adaptation.

problem: Finding expressive invertible scalar bijections for normalizing flows faces trade-offs: affine transformations lack expressivity, splines are piecewise-smooth with bounded domains, residual flows need numerical inversion.
approach: Introduce three families of analytic bijections globally smooth, defined on all R, and analytically invertible; develop radial flows that transform radial coordinates while preserving angular direction.
contribution: Analytic bijections match or exceed spline performance; radial flows achieve comparable quality to coupling flows with 1000× fewer parameters on radial-structure targets.

problem: Generalizing pretrained models to unseen numerical data without retraining is difficult due to large variations in feature dimensionality and semantics across datasets.
approach: Observe that graph structure induces a distinct representational axis (view space) beyond feature space; develop Graph View Transformation (GVT) with Recurrent architecture for fully inductive node classification.
contribution: Recurrent GVT pretrained on OGBN-Arxiv outperforms GraphAny by +8.93% and surpasses 12 individually tuned GNNs by >3.30% on 27 benchmarks.

problem: Listwise multimodal reranking for long documents is costly due to long visual-token inputs in VLMs and autoregressive decoding, resulting in high latency unsuitable for real-world systems.
approach: Propose ZipRerank, shortening input via query-image early interaction and eliminating multi-step generation by scoring all candidates in a single forward pass, trained via listwise pretraining and multimodal finetuning.
contribution: ZipRerank matches or surpasses state-of-the-art multimodal rerankers while reducing inference latency by up to an order of magnitude.

problem: Theoretical understanding of flow-matching transformers when data lie on low-dimensional manifolds remains limited, with unclear sample complexity bounds.
approach: Develop flow decomposition splitting motion along the manifold from motion off the manifold, establishing tighter sample-complexity bounds for velocity approximation and distribution estimation.
contribution: Flow-matching transformers escape the curse of dimensionality by utilizing intrinsic data structure through manifold-aware decomposition.

problem: Symbolic regression algorithms discover accurate and compact formulas that are often structurally irrational, numerically ill-conditioned, and physically inexplicable despite optimizing accuracy and complexity.
approach: Propose Effective Information Criterion (EIC) modeling formulas as information channels to measure noise amplification, distinguishing physically plausible from pathological structures without ground truth.
contribution: EIC-integrated workflows improve pre-training sample efficiency by 2-4× and boost generalization R² by 22.4%; aligns with human preferences in 70% of cases.

problem: Post-training weight-only quantization of LLMs struggles with low-bit performance due to inherent systematic weight outliers despite efforts like scaling and rotation.
approach: Propose OSAQ performing second-order low-rank derived additive weight suppression based on Hessian null space, leveraging low-rank consistency across inputs to suppress outliers without inter-layer transformations.
contribution: OSAQ effectively suppresses outliers and improves low-bit quantization performance through closed-form offline computation with no inference overhead.

problem: LLM-based multi-agent systems fail when agents misjudge their knowledge during planning despite correct execution, exhibiting epistemic miscalibration that is latent and dynamic.
approach: Propose EPC-AW assessing whether plans remain supported across varying information conditions via Information-consistency-based selection and Consistency-guided epistemic refinement.
contribution: EPC-AW improves system-level success by an average of 9.75%.

problem: Standard reinforcement learning ignores that deployed algorithms influence and shift the environments they act in, a performative setting where RL counterparts remain under-explored.
approach: Prove performative counterparts of performance difference lemma and policy gradient theorem; introduce Performative Policy Gradient (PePG) designed for performative RL.
contribution: PePG converges to performatively optimal policies that remain optimal under induced distribution shifts, extending prior work achieving only stability.

problem: Existing tool-integrated LLM alignment methods focus on maximizing task accuracy while overlooking auxiliary objectives like tool-use efficiency essential for practical deployment.
approach: Introduce ParetoPO, a two-stage multi-objective framework using hypervolume-guided dynamic scalarization for reward weighting and Pareto-ranking-based advantage computation.
contribution: ParetoPO discovers policies with superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs compared to static and heuristic baselines on mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA.

problem: MLLMs excel at high-level reasoning but fail at OCR tasks where fine-grained visual details are compromised; skip-path gradients in multi-layer fusion overwrite low-level signals.
approach: Propose Detached Skip-Links that reuse shallow features while stopping gradients through skip branches during training; introduce R-Probe measuring pixel-level visual token reconstructability.
contribution: Approach improves OCR-centric benchmarks and general multimodal tasks across multiple ViT backbones without adding learnable parameters.

problem: Applying autoregressive models to continuous control requires discretizing actions through quantization, a widely adopted practice poorly understood theoretically.
approach: Analyze how quantization error propagates along the horizon and interacts with statistical sample complexity; establish optimal sample complexity under stable dynamics and probabilistic smoothness.
contribution: Behavior cloning with quantized actions achieves optimal sample complexity with only polynomial horizon dependence on quantization error; characterizes when different schemes satisfy requirements.

problem: Existing ternary quantization methods require data-intensive quantization-aware training that is costly; practical post-training alternatives are lacking for diverse LLM architectures.
approach: Propose CAT-Q with learnable modulation and softened ternarization, using only 512 calibration samples to efficiently quantize LLMs into ternary models.
contribution: CAT-Q achieves superior performance than BitNet v1/v2 trained with 100B tokens using 100,000× fewer training tokens; scales to 235B parameters within 60 hours.

problem: Theoretical foundations of guidance mechanisms in continuous-time score-based diffusion models are underdeveloped, particularly for safety-critical planning applications.
approach: Adopt Doob's h-transform as a principled framework for characterizing ideal guided diffusion and analyze discrepancy from approximate guidance; formulate as stochastic optimal control.
contribution: Provides explicit error bounds and probabilistic safety guarantees for constraint satisfaction without additional model training.

problem: Advertising video understanding requires bridging pixel-level perception with high-level marketing logic, but multimodal agents struggle with this cognitive gap.
approach: Introduce AD-MIR with Structure-Aware Memory Construction converting video into structured database via semantic retrieval and keyword matching, plus Structured Reasoning Agent with evidence-based self-correction.
contribution: AD-MIR achieves state-of-the-art on AdsQA, surpassing DVD by 1.8 and 9.5 percentage points in strict and relaxed accuracy.

problem: Composing multiple pre-trained diffusion models risks domination or disagreement; existing coordination approaches cannot ensure fair and efficient division of labor.
approach: Propose Divide-and-Denoise using fair division game theory to allocate regions across models at each timestep, then aligning models to denoise within assigned regions.
contribution: Method outperforms baselines on conditional image generation, resolving common failures like missing objects and mismatched attributes.

problem: Multimodal systems with partial observability can exhibit same-support tail failures where worst-case metrics diverge despite matched-average performance.
approach: Propose H-CES controller stabilizing per-group pressure via deterministic increment-branch gating and group-wise decoupled weight decay without changing loss or inference.
contribution: H-CES improves same-support tail reliability while preserving clean performance across multimodal settings.

problem: Standard supervised fine-tuning with negative log-likelihood imposes disproportionately aggressive updates on low-probability target tokens, prioritizing difficult samples over overall generation quality.
approach: Propose SAFT, interpolating between aggressive NLL and probability-weighted optimization by adaptively balancing objectives based on token difficulty spectrum.
contribution: SAFT achieves state-of-the-art on mathematical reasoning benchmarks with superior generalization on out-of-distribution tasks and broad alignment adaptability.

problem: Geometric optimization problems like clustering must preserve both objective values and algorithmic consistency under data transformations, yet resilient summaries with stability guarantees are lacking.
approach: Introduce gamma-resilient coresets providing compact weighted summaries that guarantee (1+epsilon) approximation and enforce stable assignment outcomes.
contribution: Establishes theoretical framework for resilient clustering with lower bounds showing bi-criteria solutions are necessary for tight resilient approximations.

problem: Vision-language-action (VLA) models assume temporally aligned reasoning and control, but semantic inference is inherently delayed relative to real-time action generation.
approach: Introduce TIC-VLA with latency-aware framework conditioning action generation on delayed vision-language states and explicit latency metadata; include latency-consistent training pipeline.
contribution: TIC-VLA consistently outperforms prior VLA models while maintaining robust real-time control under multi-second reasoning latency in both simulation and real robots.

problem: Linear attention mechanisms mitigate quadratic complexity but suffer from critical loss of expressiveness due to normalization canceling query norm and non-negativity constraints causing information loss.
approach: Introduce NaLaFormer using norm-times-direction (ND) decomposition where query norm creates query-norm-aware kernel and direction vectors use cosine-based similarity for non-negativity.
contribution: NaLaFormer achieves up to 7.5% accuracy gain on ImageNet-1K and 4.7% mIoU on ADE20K over baselines; reduces peak memory by 92.3% on token-intensive tasks.

problem: Existing sleep analysis systems operate in closed label spaces for predefined stages/events and fail to describe, query, or generalize to novel sleep phenomena.
approach: Present SleepLM family using multilevel sleep caption generation for 100K+ hours dataset; employ unified pretraining combining contrastive alignment, caption generation, and signal reconstruction.
contribution: SleepLM outperforms state-of-the-art on zero-shot and few-shot learning, cross-modal retrieval, and exhibits language-guided event localization and targeted insight generation.

problem: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising, but greedy position unmasking can lock into suboptimal orders, especially on reasoning-heavy prompts.
approach: Present SOAR, a training-free algorithm adapting behavior to model uncertainty: widening search when confidence is low, collapsing search when high to decode in parallel.
