problem: Distinguishing whether language models genuinely reason or merely pattern-match remains open, and existing verification methods are either expensive or brittle.
approach: Treats each attention matrix as a weighted token graph and extracts four training-free spectral diagnostics (Fiedler value, HFER, spectral entropy, smoothness) to classify valid mathematical reasoning with 85-96% accuracy.
contribution: Reveals measurable spectral signatures in transformer attention that track logical coherence with effect sizes up to Cohen's d=3.30, and reranking with HFER improves proof search by 4.4-6.6%.

problem: Learning from long-tailed noisy data compounds two challenges, and existing methods ignore the non-uniform noise impact across classes, causing ineffective tail correction and over-regularization of head classes.
approach: CARE uses vision-language models to leverage three supervision sources (noisy labels, VLM text embeddings, visual features) with class-adaptive expert consensus that enforces stricter agreement for tail classes and permissive agreement for head classes.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.0% performance gains on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks by recalibrating class distributions more reliably.

problem: Unified hyperspectral image restoration across diverse degradations requires capturing multi-dimensional degradations, but current methods rely on impractical priors or black-box representations that overfit and fail on unseen scenarios.
approach: DAMP characterizes degradations through interpretable spatial-spectral metrics as Degradation Prompts, using Degradation-Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts with Spatial-Spectral Adaptive Modules that dynamically activate experts tailored to specific degradation profiles.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on natural and remote sensing datasets with exceptional zero-shot generalization to unseen restoration tasks.

problem: Test-time adaptation reduces error on new data but model parameters become dependent on past test inputs, raising privacy risks from memorizing sensitive testing data.
approach: Casts multiple TTA methods (Tent, EATA, SAR, DeYO, COME) into differential privacy forms using per-sample gradient clipping and Gaussian noise for all updates.
contribution: Provides adequate privacy at small accuracy cost on ImageNet-C, where low-privacy regimes even improve accuracy and stability of continual adaptation.

problem: Post-training LLM preference alignment requires access to sensitive user preference data, raising privacy concerns about dataset exposure.
approach: DPPrefSyn learns an underlying preference model from private data with formal differential privacy guarantees grounded in Bradley-Terry preference model, then synthesizes high-quality preference data using learned models and public prompts via DP-PCA.
contribution: Achieves competitive alignment performance under strong differential privacy guarantees, demonstrating synthetic preference data as a practical privacy-preserving alternative.

problem: Rank estimation under label noise requires handling structured ordinal label uncertainty rather than simple corruption, and existing methods fail to capture this.
approach: Reformulates rank estimation as a stochastic ordering problem where instances have multiple plausible ranks, using discriminative loss for instance-centroid interactions and stochastic order loss for probabilistic ordering relations.
contribution: Enables reliable rank estimation across diverse datasets under various types and levels of label noise.

problem: One-step and few-step flow-based generation requires enforcing long-range trajectory consistency, but directly supervising this over long time scales is difficult.
approach: Euler Mean Flows replace the trajectory consistency constraint with a principled linear surrogate derived from the semigroup formulation, enabling direct data supervision and supporting both u-prediction and x_1-prediction variants without explicit Jacobian computation.
contribution: Achieves improved optimization stability and sample quality with approximately 50% reductions in training time and memory compared to existing one-step methods.

problem: Time-series forecasting progress is obscured by complex architectures and fragile, misattributed gains, hindering meaningful comparison and understanding of what drives performance.
approach: CombinationTS decomposes forecasting models into orthogonal modules (Input Transformation, Embedding, Encoder, Decoder, Output Transformation) and evaluates under shared conditions with marginalized performance and stability metrics.
contribution: Reveals the Identity Paradox: well-designed data embedding often matches or outperforms complex backbones, enabling robust component attribution.

problem: Standard reward models in RLHF are susceptible to spurious features unrelated to human labels, leading to reward hacking where high predicted reward fails to translate to better behavior.
approach: Proposes factored representation learning that decomposes contextual embeddings into causal factors sufficient for reward prediction and non-causal factors capturing length/sycophancy, with adversarial training via gradient reversal on non-causal components.
contribution: Learns more robust reward models and consistently improves downstream RLHF performance while mitigating reward hacking on both mathematical and dialogue tasks.

problem: Machine unlearning typically requires modifying model parameters, but such updates are unstable, computationally costly, and limited by local approximations.
approach: Representation Unlearning learns a transformation in the model's representation space imposing an information bottleneck that maximizes mutual information with retained data while suppressing information about forgotten data, using variational surrogates.
contribution: Achieves more reliable forgetting, better utility retention, and greater computational efficiency than parameter-centric approaches in both zero-shot and full-data settings.

problem: LIME provides unfaithful and unstable explanations for tabular data when local feature effects exhibit nonlinear or heterogeneous behaviors, and relies on decoupled feature selection misaligned with the objective.
approach: PL-LIME models feature-wise local effects using instance-anchored piecewise linear functions under a fixed budget, with decoupled nonnegative shrinkage that directly scales estimated effects while preserving interpretability.
contribution: Achieves higher local fidelity and stability with more reliable explanations capturing finer-grained local effect structures than LIME.

problem: Vision foundation models fail to exploit 3D structure cues in 2D images, underperforming on tasks like multiview semantic consistency essential for robotics and autonomous driving.
approach: 3DPoV employs self-supervised learning with temporal nearest-neighbor consistency loss across video frames, reference-guided ordering for consistent patch alignment, and a mixture of video datasets tailored to these objectives.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on keypoint matching under viewpoint variation and improves diverse backbones including DINOv3 on depth and surface normal estimation.

problem: Anonymous multi-agent path finding faces exponential scaling challenges in standard optimization formulations, requiring efficient solution methods for real-world robotics problems.
approach: Casts MAPF as multi-marginal optimal transport with Markovian structure that collapses to a polynomial-sized LP, then introduces Schrödinger bridges for entropic regularization enabling iterative Sinkhorn-type solution for large-scale problems.
contribution: Demonstrates optimality and scalability via Schrödinger bridge formulation that achieves near-optimal integral solutions at significant computational reduction.

problem: Diffusion Policy excels at modeling multi-modal action distributions but its multi-step denoising makes real-time visuomotor control impractical, and existing caching methods fail to adapt to robot-environment dynamics.
approach: Sparse ActionGen introduces rollout-adaptive prune-then-reuse mechanism identifying prunable computations and reusing cached activations, with observation-conditioned diffusion pruner for environment-aware adaptation and zig-zag activation reuse across timesteps and blocks.
contribution: Achieves up to 4× generation speedup on multiple robotic benchmarks without sacrificing performance.

problem: ESG rating and responsible investing require modeling high-dimensional multi-modal time series spanning ESG risks, financial returns, and sentiment, but existing solutions cannot jointly reason over heterogeneous numerical signals.
approach: A domain-aware representation learning framework uses value-aware tokens with block-wise orthogonal embeddings and FACET tokens for trajectory-level structure, training with geometry-preserving loss to forecast values and organize entities.
contribution: Enables accurate ESG forecasting, trajectory-based entity grouping, and latent-space search for superior asset selection and portfolio applications.

problem: Existing multi-agent systems rely on manually crafted agent roles and natural language communication, leading to task-specificity, limited reusability, and error accumulation in long-context multi-stage interactions.
approach: Agent Primitives proposes three reusable latent building blocks (Review, Voting and Selection, Planning and Execution) communicating via KV cache, with automatic system construction via an Organizer agent selecting primitives guided by a knowledge pool of successful configurations.
contribution: Improves accuracy by 12.0-16.5% over single-agent baselines while reducing token usage and latency by 3×-4× compared to text-based MAS.

problem: Foundation model-driven agents struggle with long-horizon planning due to transient reasoning, and existing skill induction methods fail to capture conditional logic needed for robust dynamic environment execution.
approach: Neuro-Symbolic Skill Induction lifts interaction traces into modular logic-grounded programs by synthesizing explicit control flows and dynamic variable binding, empowering agents to discover when and why to act.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines enabling agents to efficiently generalize from few-shot examples and flexibly adapt to unseen goals.

problem: Reliable uncertainty quantification on frozen GNNs requires expensive multi-pass sampling or retraining with auxiliary models to obtain evidential semantics.
approach: X-EviProbe constructs class-wise Dirichlet evidence by probing frozen latent space and native outputs, incorporating graph structure via lightweight evidence-strength propagation without retraining or additional components.
contribution: Achieves up to 33.4% AUROC improvement for OOD detection and 8.7% for misclassification detection, ranking among top methods without parameter tuning.

problem: Evaluating AI reviewers is challenging because existing metrics favor overlap with human reviews despite humans often covering only partial issues and making mistakes.
approach: CoCoReviewBench builds category-specific subsets and uses reviewer-author-meta-review discussions as expert annotations while filtering unreliable reviews to strengthen both completeness and correctness in evaluation.
contribution: Curates 3,900 ICLR and NeurIPS papers showing AI reviewers remain limited in correctness and prone to hallucinations, with reasoning models as more effective reviewers.

problem: LLMs can optimize intermediate representations in compilers but lack rigorous evaluation on whether they understand IR and can rewrite it under compiler-grade semantic constraints with meaningful performance gains.
approach: CIRBench provides 800 curated IR instances across four compiler tracks (Analysis, Repair, Refactor, Transform) with verifier, equivalence checking, and end-to-end performance measurement in unified layered correctness-aware evaluation.
contribution: Shows current LLMs fail on many IR tasks and underperform compiler baseline on median, but observe maximum speedup of 4.96× over -O3.

problem: Monolithic robotic manipulation policies conflate heterogeneous regimes of coarse relocation and contact-critical interaction, limiting manipulation skill development.
approach: Move-Then-Operate decouples manipulation into two phases via dual-expert policy routed by learnable phase selector, with phase labels automatically generated via MLLM-based pipeline from contextual cues like end-effector velocity.
contribution: Achieves 68.9% average success rate on RoboTwin2 benchmark, outperforming monolithic baseline by 24% and matching models trained on 10× more data.

problem: Sparse MoE models require entire model in memory despite few experts activating per token, and existing expert pruning ignores complex inter-dependencies between experts.
approach: SCHUR-A* formulates post-training MoE pruning as reconstruction-driven subset selection, using A* search with Schur-complement-based admissible heuristic upper bound for globally optimal expert selection within each layer.
contribution: Significantly outperforms greedy and ranking-based baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B, maintaining comparable performance under aggressive pruning.

problem: Microcanonical Langevin Monte Carlo shows strong inference performance but requires full-dataset gradients, making it prohibitively expensive for large-scale Bayesian deep learning problems.
approach: Studies whether microcanonical dynamics can leverage mini-batch gradient noise via continuous-time theoretical analysis, identifying critical failure modes (anisotropic gradient noise bias and numerical instabilities) and proposing gradient noise preconditioning plus energy-variance-based adaptive tuner.
contribution: Develops robust scalable microcanonical Monte Carlo sampler achieving state-of-the-art on high-dimensional inference tasks like Bayesian neural networks.

problem: Token pruning accelerates VLMs but its safety implications are underexplored, and pruning strategies may introduce vulnerabilities through Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification.
approach: Identifies Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification mechanism where background token removal forces attention onto retained malicious anchors, proposes Safety-Aware Pruning that identifies malicious anchors, restores benign tokens, and reallocates attention.
contribution: Reduces Attack Success Rate by up to 62% without compromising efficiency or utility across three safety and four utility benchmarks.

problem: In-context tool calling incorporates detailed documentation into context causing substantial inference overhead and hallucination risks, while tuning methods fail to internalize specific tool details.
approach: ParaTool projects each tool into dedicated loadable parameters via three stages: parametric tool pre-training, soft tool selection with gating network, and parametric fine-tuning jointly updating tool parameters.
contribution: Significantly outperforms ICL-based baselines on Stable ToolBench and BFCL achieving superior performance while reducing computational complexity.

problem: Multi-task linear regression with contaminated tasks typically requires minimum eigenvalue bounds on task covariances, but these bounds fail in high-dimensional scenarios where prior guarantees become vacuous.
approach: Proposes matrix-weighted norm regularization estimator with relative balancedness condition quantifying each task's second moment relative to average inlier geometry, relaxing taskwise second-moment lower bounds.
contribution: In favorable regimes with moderate balancedness matches minimax optimal MSE rates under substantially weaker spectral assumptions with safety guarantee.

problem: Contrastive learning's conditions for recovering meaningful latent geometry remain incompletely understood, particularly how sampling diversity and encoder inductive bias interact.
approach: Develops measure-theoretic framework formalizing the diversity condition as support requirement on positive-pair sampling, showing full-support von Mises-Fisher implies latent recovery up to orthogonal transformation, introducing support-corrected InfoNCE variant.
contribution: Clarifies how sampling mechanisms and encoder inductive bias interact in contrastive learning through synthetic validation and CIFAR-10 experiments.

problem: Neural operators for dynamical systems exhibit spectral bias attenuating high-frequency components encoding small-scale structure, particularly damaging for weather forecasting where misrepresented high frequencies induce long-horizon instability.
approach: Multi-Scale Wavelet Transformers learn system dynamics in tokenized wavelet domain using wavelet-preserving downsampling retaining high-frequency features and wavelet-based attention capturing cross-scale dependencies.
contribution: Shows substantial error reductions and improved long-horizon spectral fidelity on chaotic systems, further reducing climatological bias on ERA5 climate reanalysis.

problem: Dominant video reasoning pipelines either plateau at model knowledge or require careful regularization with bounded context, limiting accuracy on complex multi-modal reasoning tasks.
approach: Uses frozen tool-integrated teacher to identify missing spatiotemporal dependencies and provide minimal evidence patches from original video, training student with chosen-rollout GRPO scheme and Robust Improvement Reward aligning optimization with outcome validity and dependency alignment.
contribution: Shows consistent accuracy gains and strong generalization across benchmarks via context repair approach minimizing training stack changes.

problem: MoE deployment is limited by high memory overhead storing all expert parameters as the number of experts increases, and existing merging methods suffer notable performance drop due to coarse-grained operations.
approach: PuzzleMoE performs sparse expert merging via element-wise weight redundancy identification with dual-mask approach capturing shared and expert-specific salient parameters, introducing bit-packed encoding reusing exponent bits for efficient inference.
contribution: Outperforms prior compression methods by up to 16.7% on MMLU at 50% compression ratio and achieves up to 1.80× end-to-end inference throughput gain.

problem: LLM fine-tuning remains bottlenecked by significant memory and computational demands despite parameter-efficient methods, with opportunities for selective backward computation.
approach: TokenDrop uses token-level importance-aware backpropagation skipping based on residual update magnitude during forward pass, introducing cumulative selection preserving gradient continuity and lazy scheduling deferring selection for globally informed scoring.
contribution: Achieves up to 42.9% memory reduction and up to 1.50× training speedup while preserving accuracy and outperforming existing backpropagation-skipping baselines.

problem: Video generation with Diffusion Transformers remains constrained by quadratic attention complexity, and existing sparse attention methods rely on oversimplified static patterns or expensive sampling, degrading quality.
approach: MOD-DiT uses Mixture-of-Distribution sampling-free dynamic attention framework with two-stage process: leveraging early denoising priors via distributed mixing for efficient linear approximation, then online block masking applying predicted masks with historical sparsity.
contribution: Achieves consistent acceleration and quality improvements across benchmarks and architectures for efficient high-quality video generation without sampling overhead.

problem: Existing debiasing methods suppress biased behavior but are brittle, weakly generalizable, data-inefficient, and prone to degrading general capability of LLMs.
approach: KnowBias identifies neurons encoding bias knowledge via attribution-based analysis on small bias-knowledge question sets, selectively enhancing them at inference time rather than suppressing.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art debiasing with minimal utility degradation, generalizing across bias types with data-efficient lightweight framework requiring no retraining.

problem: Early exit methods rely on output confidence as proxy for internal convergence, but don't directly examine when hidden state refinement truly completes.
approach: Examines geometry of hidden state trajectory discovering two-phase structure (large volatile early updates, small aligned later updates), tracking normalized update norm and cosine similarity with O(d) overhead, exiting when both indicate convergence.
contribution: Reduces FLOPs by 30-35% while retaining over 98% accuracy on LLaMA-2 models across QA and reasoning tasks.

problem: Graph prompting adapts frozen GNN encoders by modifying input structure, but existing approaches optimize continuous adjacency at training time with hard discretization at inference, causing train-test mismatch.
approach: DiP-G directly learns task-specific topology prompts in combinatorial space using perturbed Top-k solver on multi-hop local subgraphs, optimizing discrete structures via I-MLE gradient estimator with adaptive active-set screening.
contribution: Maintains scalability and accuracy while avoiding train-test mismatch through discrete prompting on few-shot datasets.

problem: Recovering latent order from noisy one-dimensional curve samples in high dimensions requires handling local geometric information while dealing with tangent direction sign ambiguity.
approach: STAGE estimates local tangent directions via neighborhood PCA, resolves sign ambiguity through graph-wide Z_2 synchronization, constructs signed local displacements by projecting onto oriented tangents, integrating into global scalar embedding via inhomogeneous least-squares.
contribution: Provides finite-sample Kendall's τ recovery bound explicit in curvature, noise, and sampling density, with accurate fast order recovery on synthetic curves and meaningful pseudotime on single-cell RNA-seq.

problem: Solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDE for diffusion models is computationally slow and sensitive to hyperparameter tuning, limiting practical high-dimensional sampling.
approach: Introduce a functional tensor train (FTT) solver that exploits low-rank structures for efficient PDE approximation, combined with a backward-in-time iterative scheme from backward stochastic differential equations.
contribution: A fast, robust diffusion sampling method that enables high-fidelity sampling from challenging target distributions with improved computational efficiency.

problem: Existing differentially private code generation assumes prompts are public while protecting only code, failing to protect sensitive information in both prompts and code.
approach: Propose PrivCode++ with a two-stage DP framework using Privacy-Free Latent Conditioning to enable fine-tuning without direct access to sensitive prompts or code snippets.
contribution: First work on DP code generation protecting both prompts and code, achieving substantially higher utility than baselines with stronger privacy guarantees.

problem: Data mixture selection for large language models is costly to search and existing scaling laws fail to extrapolate to large model sizes.
approach: Propose CAMEL, a capacity-aware mixture law modeling validation loss with nonlinear interactions between model size and data mixture, plus a loss-to-benchmark prediction law.
contribution: Reduce mixture optimization costs by 50% while improving downstream benchmark performance by up to 3% when applied to Mixture-of-Experts models up to 55B-A1.2B parameters.

problem: Applying machine learning to solve long-standing mathematical conjectures faces extreme reward sparsity, making standard RL ineffective.
approach: Recast counterexample construction as sparse-reward RL on graphs using constrained options-based HRL with equivariant graph neural network policies.
contribution: First application of hierarchical RL to commutative algebra, consistently outperforming classical RL and greedy search on Kalai's algebraic Hirsch conjecture.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models exhibit imbalanced routing that causes compute and memory failures on overloaded devices during post-training and inference.
approach: Introduce Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism (LLEP), an algorithm that dynamically reroutes excess tokens from overloaded to underutilized devices while respecting memory constraints.
contribution: Achieve up to 5x speedup and 4x peak memory reduction with ~1.9x faster inference for gpt-oss-120b compared to standard expert parallelism.

problem: Spectral representation alignment benefits diffusion training but the mechanism remains unclear, limiting principled improvements to diffusion models.
approach: Investigate connections between self-supervised spectral representation learning and diffusion through shared perturbation kernels, proposing spectral representation alignment regularization.
contribution: Consistent generation quality gains across images and 3D point clouds by integrating spectral regularization into diffusion training objectives.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs requires balancing data privacy and model IP protection, but existing methods protect only one or compromise utility.
approach: Propose PISA with three methods: Manifold Rectification Pre-training for robustness, Dual-Stream Semantic Compensation for feature recovery, and Utility-Aware Gradient Rectification.
contribution: Achieve 23% performance gain over privacy-prioritized baseline on GLUE while simultaneously protecting both data privacy and model intellectual property.

problem: Standard SSL for automatic modulation recognition struggles with ineffective augmentations, spectral instability, and semantic drift.
approach: Introduce Dynamic-Consistency Contrastive Learning (DyCo-CL) coupling Virtual Adversarial Augmentation with semantic consistency loss and Signal-Adaptive Swin Backbone.
contribution: Achieve 6.27% accuracy gain in 1-shot modulation recognition settings over prior methods.

problem: Group counterfactual explanations either don't generalize to new members, require strong assumptions, or poorly preserve group geometry.
approach: Learn an explicit optimal transport map sending any group instance to its counterfactual, minimizing total transport cost without re-optimization.
contribution: Enable generalization with fewer parameters, preserve group geometry, and provide mathematical characterization of group counterfactuals for linear classifiers.

problem: Efficient expansion of strategy sets in PSRO can lead to inefficient population growth that poorly approximates the full game.
approach: Guide population expansion by directly minimizing Population Exploitability (PE) through a two-phase exploration-selection framework with parameter-sharing conditional neural networks.
contribution: Achieve lower exploitability and better Nash equilibrium approximation with significantly fewer policy iterations than prior PSRO methods across multiple games.

problem: Composing multiple constraints in guided diffusion/flow model sampling causes off-manifold drift that degrades generation fidelity.
approach: Identify gradient misalignment as root cause and propose Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance (g^CAR), a learnable method that dynamically detects and resolves gradient conflicts.
contribution: Effectively rectify off-manifold drift in composite constrained generation across synthetic data, image editing, and planning tasks.

problem: Large models are costly to deploy across different computational budgets, requiring separate training for each budget.
approach: Leverage low-rank weight decomposition with nested, importance-based consolidation to extract submodels of increasing capabilities from a single pretrained model.
contribution: Enable train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm with graceful cost-performance trade-offs without retraining for each budget.

problem: The duality between structured state-space models and masked attention is limited to scalar-identity cases with unclear generalization potential.
approach: Formalize and extend the Structured State-Space Duality to general diagonal SSMs, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for equivalence to semiseparable masked attention.
contribution: Diagonal SSMs match scalar case complexity while supporting richer dynamics; clarify that standard softmax attention's rank explosion prevents duality extension.

problem: Current coding benchmarks lack exceptionally challenging problems, have insufficient test coverage, and depend on online APIs limiting accessibility.
approach: Introduce LiveOIBench featuring 403 expert-curated problems from 72 Informatics Olympiad contests with an average of 60 test cases each and offline evaluation.
contribution: Enable direct comparison of 34 LLMs to elite human contestants, finding GPT-5 achieves 81.76th percentile while GPT-OSS-120B reaches 60th percentile.

problem: Existing HGR maximal correlation methods have prohibitive computational cost for high-dimensional multimodal learning.
approach: Replace explicit whitening with centered l2-normalized cosine alignment in local-batch Gram space and remove invariant self-correlation via Trivial Spectrum Suppression.
contribution: Consistent gains across retrieval, classification, and emotion recognition with O(m^2K) structural cost and stable behavior at extreme feature dimensions.

problem: Detecting long-context attention heads in LLMs requires expensive inference on actual long texts without analyzing inherent parameter properties.
approach: Use kernel methods to analyze frequency kernels of attention heads and design Long-context Potential Score (LPS) to measure inherent long-context processing potential.
contribution: Fully static and offline LPS metrics predict long-context capability better than inference-based methods; amplifying low-frequency kernels improves long-context performance.

problem: Post-training flow matching models for alignment requires preference optimization but involves expensive preference collection and reward modeling.
approach: Propose Flow Matching Adversarial Imitation Learning (FAIL) minimizing policy-expert divergence through adversarial training with pathwise gradient variants.
contribution: Fine-tune FLUX with only 13K demonstrations achieving competitive prompt-following and aesthetic performance while generalizing to discrete generation.

problem: Model extraction attacks enable adversaries to replicate proprietary DNN functionality, but verifying ownership with rigorous guarantees is challenging.
approach: Employ mutual information to quantify model similarity, propose a practical verification threshold, and provide theoretical guarantees for certified ownership verification.
contribution: State-of-the-art certified ownership verification against model extraction attacks across multiple datasets and domains.

problem: Language models memorize and reproduce verbatim spans from training data, raising copyright and compliance risks.
approach: Propose Anchored Decoding, keeping generation bounded to a permissively trained safe LM while adaptively allocating information budget and enforcing per-step constraints.
contribution: Preserve near-original fluency while eliminating up to 75% of measurable copying gap between risky and safe models with modest inference overhead.

problem: Scaling RL for LLMs faces vanishing learning signals when problem difficulty distributions are static relative to model capabilities.
approach: Introduce RLVE with 400 procedurally generated verifiable environments that dynamically adapt problem difficulty during training.
contribution: Achieve 3.37% absolute average improvement across six reasoning benchmarks with environment scaling, substantially outperforming continued original RL training.

problem: Attribution methods produce unspecific explanations highlighting both important and irrelevant features.
approach: Show that using logits as attribution target is problematic; propose using distributions of attributions over multiple classes with existing methods.
contribution: Improve attribution specificity of 18 methods across 7 architectures up to 2x on common benchmarks via multi-class distribution analysis.

problem: Neural PDE solvers struggle to scale to industrial-grade meshes with over 10^8 cells due to prohibitive GPU memory requirements.
approach: Introduce Transolver-3 with faster slice/deslice operations using matrix multiplication properties, geometry slice tiling, amortized training, and physical state caching.
contribution: Handle meshes with over 160 million cells achieving impressive performance on aircraft and automotive design simulation tasks.

problem: Latent-space visual reasoning lacks sufficient semantic richness and visual supervision limits diverse region-level reasoning tasks.
approach: Propose SLVR with two-stage framework: enrich latents with attribute-level supervision, then align across multiple queries using Multi-query Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: Improve robustness and semantic consistency of latent visual reasoning over baselines; introduce SLV-Set with 400K region annotations and SV-QA benchmark.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models suffer from information collapse where language instructions become predictable from vision alone, causing models to ignore language.
approach: Propose LangForce enforcing instruction following via Bayesian decomposition with learnable Latent Action Queries to maximize Pointwise Mutual Information between actions and language.
contribution: Achieve 11.3% improvement on challenging OOD SimplerEnv benchmark, validating robust language grounding in robotic manipulation.

problem: Large vision-language models hallucinate by relying on language priors without visual grounding.
approach: Propose Dynamic Entropy-Guided Attention Perturbation (DEGAP) that perturbs visual attention layer-wise and dynamically selects layers based on model confidence.
contribution: Effectively mitigate various hallucination types across seven benchmarks while maintaining strong general VQA performance.

problem: The relationship between fixed-budget and fixed-confidence best-arm identification remains unclear despite matching sample complexities for K-armed bandits.
approach: Propose FC2FB meta-algorithm converting fixed-confidence algorithms to fixed-budget by leveraging existing FC methods constructively.
contribution: Show that fixed-budget is no harder than fixed-confidence up to logarithmic factors with improved sample complexity for several FB problems.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs for robotic planning requires costly chain-of-thought supervision and manual reward engineering for reinforcement learning.
approach: Propose Self-CriTeach where LLMs autonomously generate symbolic planning domains serving dual roles: generating problem-plan pairs for SFT and structured reward functions.
contribution: Achieve higher planning success, stronger cross-task generalization, reduced inference cost, and resistance to imperfect logical states.

problem: Multi-LLM serving on shared GPUs degrades inference performance, particularly time-to-first-token, due to lack of future workload awareness.
approach: Propose one-for-many GPU prewarming loading multiple model parameters based on workload forecasts, with model placement optimization and KV cache reservation.
contribution: Reduce tail time-to-first-token by up to 50.8x compared to autoscaling while supporting 2.5x higher throughput than GPU-sharing systems.

problem: Amortised sampling methods and particle-based methods each have limitations when sampling from unnormalised densities.
approach: Connect sequential Monte Carlo and neural sequential samplers via maximum-entropy RL, using learned samplers as SMC proposals with adaptive weight tempering.
contribution: Demonstrate improvements in approximating true distributions and training stability over both amortised and Monte Carlo methods alone.

problem: Estimating scaling laws requires substantial computational resources with limited guidance on strategic budget allocation.
approach: Explore Successive Halving combined with parametric and non-parametric surrogate models for systematic compute budget allocation.
contribution: Mean relative improvements of up to 5.47% on synthetic datasets while saving up to 98.7% computational cost compared to exhaustive approaches.

problem: Machine unlearning for multimodal LLMs risks hallucinations and rigid responses after unlearning, compromising model usability.
approach: Propose ASRU combining activation steering for initial refusal with reinforcement learning for fine-grained refusal boundaries using customized reward functions.
contribution: Improve unlearning effectiveness (+24.6%) and generation quality (5.8x) while preserving model utility on Qwen3-VL.

problem: Incremental object detection suffers from catastrophic forgetting and increased confusion between old and new classes due to separation-oriented paradigms.
approach: Propose Symbiosis-Inspired Knowledge Distillation leveraging object co-occurrence and occlusion dependencies via Spatial and Semantic Symbiosis Distillation.
contribution: Preserve old class knowledge and stabilize semantic topology during incremental learning over existing class-incremental methods.

problem: Existing load-balancing methods for Mixture-of-Experts are heuristic and operate on noisy mini-batch statistics, introducing bias.
approach: Propose phi-balancing, a principled framework minimizing a convex symmetric differentiable potential of expected routing distribution via mirror descent.
contribution: Consistently outperform prior baselines on pretraining and fine-tuning with more stable and effective expert utilization.

problem: Self-play LLM training exhibits non-sustained improvement where early gains degrade, caused by diversity collapse into recurring patterns.
approach: Propose R-Diverse with Memory-Augmented Penalty to discourage recycling across iterations and Skill-Aware Measurement to evaluate true reasoning diversity.
contribution: Sustain gains over more iterations and consistently outperform prior self-play methods across math and reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Understanding and interpreting LLM activations is difficult with most techniques requiring complex specialized methods.
approach: Train LLMs as Activation Oracles to accept LLM activations as inputs and answer natural language questions about them in generalist settings.
contribution: Recover fine-tuned information without training on fine-tuned activations; match or exceed white-box baselines on downstream interpretability tasks.

problem: Masked diffusion language models for non-autoregressive generation suffer performance loss when unmasking multiple positions in parallel due to ignored interactions.
approach: Propose Dilated Unmasking Scheduler partitioning positions into non-adjacent dilated groups and unmasking in parallel to minimize joint entropy gain.
contribution: Achieve up to 5.8x wall-clock speedup over token-by-token decoding with predictable quality-speed trade-offs.

problem: Block-wise decoding in diffusion language models uses rigid fixed partitioning that fragments semantic constituents, suboptimizing performance.
approach: Propose Swordsman, an entropy-driven adaptive block partitioning framework identifying constituent boundaries via entropy shifts to align with semantic structures.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance via training-free adaptive partitioning and dynamic threshold adjustment for improved efficiency and stability.

problem: Standard deep learning approaches for antibody engineering model marginal sequence distributions and miss affinity maturation as a source of evolutionary information.
approach: Introduce CoSiNE, a continuous-time Markov chain parameterized by neural networks that captures epistatic effects with quadratic error bounds in branch length.
contribution: Outperform language models in zero-shot variant effect prediction; introduce Guided Gillespie for classifier-guided antibody affinity optimization.

problem: Learning optimal reactive policies in non-Markovian environments with hard state aggregation is challenging under existing convergence assumptions.
approach: Introduce Committed Q-learning where behavior policy commits to single action upon entering feature, resampling only when observed feature changes.
contribution: Prove almost-sure convergence to optimal reactive policy under rewire-robustness assumption strictly weaker than q-star-realizability.

problem: Vision-language models produce self-reflective statements like rechecking images but may be learned patterns rather than genuine visual re-examination.
approach: Introduce VISUALSWAP framework replacing images mid-reasoning with visually similar but semantically different ones to test visual re-examination.
contribution: Reveal that VLMs overwhelmingly miss swaps (accuracy drops 60%); thinking models are 3x more vulnerable; multi-turn user instructions restore grounding.

problem: Inverse design requires finding design parameters that achieve target performance, but standard conditional flow matching is sensitive to arbitrary ordering and scaling of coordinates and labels.
approach: Introduces Diagonal Flow Matching (Diag-CFM) with zero-anchoring that pairs design coordinates with noise and labels with zero, making the learning invariant to coordinate permutations.
contribution: Achieves substantially lower round-trip error than CFM across dimensions up to 784, with order-of-magnitude gains on several benchmarks; provides two uncertainty metrics for selecting best candidates and detecting out-of-distribution targets.

problem: Flow matching on Riemannian manifolds still requires numerically integrating probability-flow ODEs during sampling, limiting efficiency.
approach: Extends MeanFlow to manifolds using parallel transport to define average-velocity fields and derives a Riemannian MeanFlow identity for intrinsic supervision in log-map tangent representation.
contribution: Achieves competitive one-step sampling on spheres, tori, SO(3), and SE(3) with improved quality-efficiency trade-offs and substantially reduced sampling cost.

problem: Generalized linear bandits with endogenous memory have loose regret bounds that don't reflect true performance under non-stationary reward dynamics.
approach: Provides sharpened analysis for linear case recovering sqrt(T) regret, extends to generalized linear models with block-wise algorithm using shrunken confidence bounds.
contribution: Achieves regret bound of Õ(sqrt(mT) + d*sqrt(T) + sqrt(κ)*d²*m^{1/4}*T^{1/4} + κ*d²), with leading term independent of link function curvature.

problem: Reward models in RLHF are vulnerable to reward hacking due to noisy annotations and systematic biases like response length or style.
approach: Proposes Bayesian Non-Negative Reward Model (BNRM) integrating non-negative factor analysis into Bradley-Terry preference models with disentangled instance-specific variables and sparse global factors.
contribution: Substantially mitigates reward over-optimization, improves robustness under distribution shifts, and yields more interpretable reward decompositions than baselines.

problem: Entropic optimal transport in continuous spaces has intractable log-partition terms that make existing approaches either computationally inefficient or require restrictive parameterizations or simulation-based training.
approach: Proposes Variational Entropic Optimal Transport (VarEOT) with exact variational reformulation of log-partition as tractable minimization over auxiliary positive normalizer.
contribution: Enables differentiable learning with stochastic gradients avoiding MCMC simulations; achieves competitive or improved translation quality on synthetic data and unpaired image-to-image translation.

problem: AI-generated text detection suffers from boilerplate token dominance and brittle point estimates that fail under adversarial manipulations.
approach: Proposes Uncertainty detector focusing on informative low-probability tokens via multiscale uncertainty estimation using log-probability averaging and Rényi entropy; extends with conditional independent sampling for Uncertainty++.
contribution: Demonstrates high effectiveness and generalization across seven datasets and sixteen LLMs with robustness to adversarial attacks; code available.

problem: Predictive memory in online video models exacerbates drift under occlusion or rapid motion as inaccurate predictions contaminate internal state leading to identity loss.
approach: Interprets video memory as dynamic latent process; introduces Reliability-Guided Predictive Memory (RPM) with latent world model based on state-space dynamics and reliability-aware fusion policy suppressing unreliable predictions.
contribution: Reduces drift after occlusion and outperforms baselines on visual object tracking; demonstrates transfer to video object segmentation across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Preference-based reward modeling with network-sampled annotators exhibits biased inclusion that correlates with graph centrality, leading to over-representation of structural communities.
approach: Proposes Graph-Preference Learning combining graph-personalized reward model sharing strength across neighbors and graph-balanced aggregation using stabilized importance weights.
contribution: Achieves up to 62% reduction in target-welfare recovery error and 17% reduction in cross-language performance gaps under biased inclusion.

problem: Static refusal direction analysis misses how refusal is constructed across layer-token positions, allowing jailbreaks to suppress terminal signals while upstream patterns persist.
approach: Uses causal tracing to identify Refusal Trajectory sparse upstream activation patterns; proposes SALO (Sparse Activation Localization Operator) lightweight white-box detector on hidden states.
contribution: Improves jailbreak detection across Qwen, Llama, and Mistral models on multiple attack families; identifies limitations of static representation engineering approaches.

problem: Dynamic network representation learning requires stable embeddings across nodes and time, but stability guarantees have remained out of reach for normalized Laplacian operators.
approach: Introduces Unfolded Laplacian Spectral Embedding (ULSE) extending unfolded adjacency spectral embedding to normalized Laplacian operators with explicit stability analysis.
contribution: Proves cross-sectional and longitudinal stability under dynamic stochastic block model; yields dynamic Cheeger-type inequality linking spectrum to conductance.

problem: EEG visual decoding ignores the brain's hierarchical visual processing, failing to model low-level to high-level feature organization.
approach: Proposes ViEEG decomposing stimuli into contour, foreground object, and contextual scene; uses three-stream EEG encoder with cross-attention routing and hierarchical contrastive learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms previous methods on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG datasets in both subject-dependent and subject-independent settings; enables zero-shot object recognition.

problem: Learning with distribution shift is typically viewed negatively, yet with well-chosen training distribution the shift can make hard computational problems tractable.
approach: Formalizes Positive Distribution Shift perspective where training on alternative distribution D' makes learning computationally easier; connects to membership query learning.
contribution: Shows certain hard function classes become learnable under PDS using standard gradient-based training; computational benefits often outweigh statistical ones.

problem: Text-based person retrieval relies on incomplete single-shot queries and chat-based methods lack direct user interaction with retrieved candidates for effective refinement.
approach: Proposes multimodal interactive person retrieval allowing iterative refinement via visual feedback; introduces MNEMO framework with atomic turn encoding and dialogue memory aggregation modules.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy and generalization; code and dataset publicly available at github.com/Flame-Chasers/MNEMO.

problem: Verifying research-level mathematics solutions is expensive requiring expert time, yet meaningful solutions should generalize to related problems.
approach: Proposes oracle-free Consequence-Based Utility evaluator that scores solutions by testing their value as in-context exemplars in solving related verifiable questions.
contribution: Outperforms reward models and LLM judges; for GPT-OSS-120B improves Acc@1 from 67.2% to 76.3% and AUC from 71.4% to 79.6%.

problem: Fine-grained vision-language alignment remains limited particularly in non-English settings with weak support for bilingual comprehension.
approach: Introduces FG-CLIP 2 bilingual model with region-text matching, long-caption modeling, and Textual Intra-modal Contrastive loss trained on English and Chinese data including new 12M Chinese region-text dataset.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on 29 datasets across 8 tasks for bilingual fine-grained alignment; releases model, code, and benchmark.

problem: Uniform frame sampling in long-video understanding fails to capture key evidence, and existing agentic thinking-with-videos methods are inefficient with rigid workflows.
approach: Proposes VideoTemp-o3 unified framework jointly modeling video grounding and QA with unified masking mechanism for SFT and dedicated rewards for RL to mitigate reward hacking.
contribution: Achieves remarkable performance on long-video understanding and grounding; develops high-quality long-video grounded QA benchmark.

problem: Strictly equivariant models suffer from runtime overhead while non-equivariant models ignore beneficial symmetries; approximately equivariant models need better efficiency.
approach: Proposes projection-based regularizer leveraging layer-wise orthogonal decomposition into equivariant and non-equivariant components with penalties in spatial and spectral domains.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior approximate equivariance methods in both performance and efficiency with substantial runtime gains over sample-based regularizers.

problem: DPO applies Bradley-Terry model only after deriving the objective, missing the autoregressive structure that shapes token-level preferences.
approach: Reformulates DPO with explicit autoregressive assumption prior to Bradley-Terry model, deriving Autoregressive DPO (ADPO) with shifted summation outside log-sigmoid.
contribution: Explicitly distinguishes token length and feedback length measures; first to analyze their implications for LLM preference optimization.

problem: Graph foundation models exhibit uneven and sometimes negative transfer across domains due to unknown structural mismatch between graphs.
approach: Uses graphon-based continuous limit to decompose cross-domain output shift into finite-sample approximation and relabeling-invariant domain discrepancy; analyzes positional encoding stability.
contribution: Establishes spectral PE stability guarantees and contrasts eigenvector versus subspace-based PE behaviors; translates theory into data curation guidance for GFM transfer.

problem: GNNs suffer from overfitting and over-squashing; edge deletion regularizes but introduces train-inference misalignment while rewiring improves connectivity without training regularization.
approach: Proposes Random Add-Drop Edge (RADE) stochastic augmentation jointly dropping and adding edges with mini-batch gradient-norm balancing for adaptive rates.
contribution: Provably aligns training and inference; mitigates both overfitting and over-squashing; hyperparameter-free in practice with strong node and graph classification results.

problem: Implicit bias of momentum-based optimizers on neural networks remains poorly understood compared to vanilla gradient descent.
approach: Shows momentum steepest descent algorithms (Muon, MomentumGD, Signum) are approximate steepest descent trajectories under decaying learning rates maximizing corresponding norm margins.
contribution: Proves Adam maximizes ℓ∞ margin and characterizes hybrid norms for Adam-variants; results extend to smooth homogeneous models with corroborating experiments.

problem: Dual-encoder vision-language models fail compositional constraints where similarity scores ignore logical operators like 'and' and 'no'.
approach: Proposes factored inference separating evidence extraction from constraint execution; introduces LCSE training-free method that executes constraints externally using frozen encoders.
contribution: Achieves 85.5% accuracy on FACTOR-Bench versus 73.2% for best fine-tuned baseline; improves NegBench COCO MCQ from 27.2% to 65.2% preserving retrieval performance.

problem: Large vision-language models have significant redundancy enabling layer skipping, but determining when to skip lacks principled criteria.
approach: Proposes unified framework characterizing redundancy conditions for layer pruning via experimentally verifiable notions of redundancy independent of downstream task performance.
contribution: Validates that early and late vision tokens are redundant; framework provides theoretically grounded understanding unifying modern layer-skipping techniques.

problem: Truncated linear regression with unknown survival set remains open beyond Gaussian features despite practical relevance.
approach: Develops novel subroutine for efficiently learning unions of bounded intervals using positive examples under smoothness; achieves poly(d/ε) runtime.
contribution: First algorithm for truncated regression with unknown set running in poly(d/ε) time requiring only sub-Gaussian features; advances positive-only PAC learning theory.

problem: Pretrained robot policies have broad behavioral coverage but lack the refinement needed for complex manipulation tasks.
approach: Proposes Distribution Contractive RL (DICE-RL) framework using selective behavior regularization and value-guided action selection to finetune diffusion/flow policies via stable off-policy RL.
contribution: Reliably improves performance with strong stability and sample efficiency; enables mastery of complex long-horizon manipulation in simulation and on real robots.

problem: Time series foundation models require task-specific fine-tuning for different analysis tasks despite having strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities.
approach: Presents Zeus unified TSFM with multi-scale Transformer using point-wise tokenization and U-shaped hierarchy; introduces Multi-Objective Temporal Masking supporting heterogeneous tasks.
contribution: Achieves competitive results across five analysis tasks without tuning; improves performance on out-of-domain benchmarks (+8.06%); code available.

problem: LLM-based time series reasoning fails to capture domain-specific patterns and simple objectives dominate learning in mixed-difficulty tasks.
approach: Introduces Pattern-Aware Alignment extracting trend and seasonality patterns; designs task-aware balanced reward harmonizing learning across difficulty levels.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on diverse Time Series Question Answering tasks; demonstrates superior cross-modal understanding and reasoning capability.

problem: Polypharmacology-guided drug design requires satisfying coupled constraints across multiple heterogeneous binding sites, but existing methods model pockets in isolation.
approach: Proposes pocket-structure-centric generative framework with novel protein representation masking ligand-irrelevant residues while modeling backbone geometry and inter-residue spatial proximity.
contribution: Generates valid candidates with significantly improved binding affinities on COVID-19, schizophrenia, and tumor targets compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Vertex-based message passing GNNs are limited in expressivity by the 1-Weisfeiler-Lehman test; edge-based alternatives need theoretical and practical improvements.
approach: Introduces EB-1WL edge-based color-refinement test and EB-GNN architecture passing messages along edges and triangles inspired by triangle-counting algorithm.
contribution: Shows EB-1WL is significantly more expressive than 1WL with complete logical characterization; EB-GNN admits near-linear time/memory and outperforms standard MPNNs.

problem: Neural compression methods operate at fixed points on rate-distortion-perception surface, requiring retraining to target different tradeoffs.
approach: Proposes training-free framework leveraging pretrained diffusion models with reverse channel coding module and score-scaled probability flow ODE decoder.
contribution: Theoretically proves optimal distortion-perception tradeoff under AWGN and optimal RDP function in Gaussian case; demonstrates flexibility navigating ternary RDP tradeoff.

problem: Long-context reasoning in LLMs lacks understanding of which data types are effective and why; few studies analyze structured table data.
approach: Mathematically analyzes tabular dependency structures using mutual information revealing periodic dependencies; proposes TableLong pipeline synthesizing high-quality table data for RL.
contribution: Table data enhances long-context reasoning across benchmarks (+8.24% average) and out-of-domain settings (+8.06%); provides practical guidance for post-training data.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models memorize training data leading to privacy and copyright concerns; existing methods hurt generation quality or require retraining.
approach: Introduces GUARD framework adjusting denoising to guide away from originals via novel cross-attention attenuation mechanism identifying prompt positions requiring attenuation.
contribution: Most robust memorization mitigation method achieving state-of-the-art results across architectures for verbatim and template memorization while improving image quality.

problem: Hamiltonian and underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo introduce asymptotic bias through numerical integration; unadjusted methods outperform but lack automated step size selection.
approach: Establishes relationship between energy change during integration and asymptotic bias; proposes automatic tuning scheme taking user-provided bias tolerance to select step size.
contribution: Rigorously bounds asymptotic bias for Gaussian targets and numerically validates beyond Gaussians; demonstrates practicality on Bayesian inference and statistical physics problems.

problem: Targeted instruction selection for LLM fine-tuning lacks clarity with fragmented methods, unclear baselines, and entangled components preventing actionable guidance.
approach: Systematically analyzes data representation and selection algorithms with controlled comparisons; unifies selection algorithms as approximate distance minimization with generalization bounds.
contribution: Gradient-based representations consistently choose similar subsets predictive of performance; gains diminish at larger budgets; provides foundation for principled data selection.

problem: Time Series Foundation Models contain redundant intermediate layers but understanding their redundancy and its causes remains unclear.
approach: Introduces mechanistic interpretability tools for TSFMs including ablation studies and logit attribution; develops kernel regressor framework explaining redundancy via stable rank of projection matrices.
contribution: Shows all studied models robust to layer ablation; identifies specific heads responsible for degenerate phenomena like motif parroting and seasonality bias.

problem: Extended context lengths in LLMs cause KV cache to grow linearly, exceeding device limits; existing compression methods incur unbounded peak memory and fail in multi-turn conversations.
approach: Introduces EpiCache training-free framework with block-wise prefill and episodic KV compression clustering conversation history into coherent episodes for episode-specific eviction.
contribution: Improves accuracy up to 30% with 4-6× compression; reduces latency and peak memory by 2.4× and 3.7×; spans three LongConvQA benchmarks.

problem: Predicting street-level socioeconomic indicators from street view imagery fails to exploit structured task-relevant signals and label-efficient learning opportunities.
approach: Proposes MetaStreet semi-supervised multimodal framework with semantic-spatial visual encoder, task-aware LLM encoder, and geography-aware graph contrastive learning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on two cities across three socioeconomic prediction tasks leveraging spatial autocorrelation.

problem: Controlling fidelity-diversity trade-offs in diffusion generation models lacks principled understanding of attention mechanisms' role.
approach: Characterizes pre-softmax attention as associative memory; decomposes into symmetric (energy landscape) and skew-symmetric (circulation) components; derives Hopfield stability measures.
contribution: Establishes meaningful correlations between Hopfield stability and fidelity-diversity trade-offs; proposes controllable knob modulating via circulation dynamics.

problem: Learning unified road representations across cities fails due to spectral misalignment of graph structures across heterogeneous urban layouts.
approach: Proposes CoSpec framework disentangling road networks into shareable low-frequency commonalities and city-specific high-frequency specificities via hierarchical dual-path architecture.
contribution: Bounds Wasserstein distance between city distributions; demonstrates superior generalization over state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Approximate furthest neighbor search in adaptive query model with adversarial queries lacks robust data structures achieving theoretical guarantees.
approach: Presents first adversarially robust data structure for c-approximate furthest neighbor with query time Õ(min(d*n^{1/c²}, n^{2/c²} + d)).
contribution: Matches n-dependency of oblivious setting for wide parameter ranges; proves oblivious algorithms fail under adaptive attacks via adversarial attack construction.

problem: Generative planning models are limited by their training data distribution, and scaling test-time compute is inefficient.
approach: A modified Open-Closed List (OCL) search algorithm synergizes a generative rollout model with a learned heuristic to efficiently optimize the inference process.
contribution: Outperforms neurosymbolic and classical baselines in computational efficiency and solution quality across combinatorial planning domains.

problem: Detecting machine-generated text is difficult when the source model is unknown and per-input contrastive generation is costly.
approach: SurpMark summarizes passages through token surprisal dynamics, discretizes them into interpretable states, and scores via generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence against fixed human and machine references.
contribution: Achieves robust cross-domain detection matching or surpassing baselines with strong performance across multiple datasets and source models.

problem: Gaze estimation suffers from poor generalization due to limited annotated data and domain shifts in unconstrained scenarios.
approach: DSCL leverages Jacobian regularization to disentangle features into task-specific subspaces and exploits ordinal ranking within subspaces for semi-supervised contrastive learning.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance using only 5%, 10%, and 20% of annotated data in both in-domain and cross-domain settings.

problem: Vision-Language Models can infer and link distributed multimodal information to construct individual profiles, creating significant privacy risks.
approach: MultiPriv introduces a Privacy Perception and Reasoning (PPR) framework with a bilingual dataset of synthetic profiles linking identifiers to sensitive attributes, enabling nine challenging evaluation tasks.
contribution: Over 50 open-source and commercial VLMs can perform individual-level privacy reasoning with up to 80% accuracy, demonstrating substantial privacy threats.

problem: Graph Neural Networks fail to generalize when node features are missing, particularly in realistic scenarios with dense features and non-random missingness patterns.
approach: The work provides theoretical analysis proving high sparsity limits information loss, introduces new benchmarks with dense features, and proposes a simple graph-adapted baseline that proves competitive with specialized architectures.
contribution: Shows that simple baselines can match specialized methods across diverse datasets and missingness regimes, challenging prior assumptions about GNN robustness.

problem: Current unlearning evaluation relies on task-level metrics that can be misleading, as models can appear to forget while easily restoring original behavior through fine-tuning.
approach: A representation-level analysis framework uses PCA, CKA, and Fisher information to measure representational drift and identify four distinct forgetting regimes based on reversibility and catastrophicity.
contribution: Exposes gaps in current evaluation methods and identifies that irreversible non-catastrophic forgetting is exceptionally challenging, offering insights for robust erasure algorithms.

problem: Existing SAE-based LLM steering requires contrastive datasets or large activation stores, making it expensive and impractical.
approach: CorrSteer correlates task outcomes with SAE activations during generation to identify steering features, then validates through intervention, requiring no task-specific tuning.
contribution: Achieves +3.3% on MMLU and +27.1% on HarmBench with lower side-effects than fine-tuning, scaling to 10^5 SAE features via streaming correlation.

problem: Post-training VLMs via sequential SFT then RLVR is inefficient and suffers from catastrophic forgetting, while single-stage approaches remain suboptimal.
approach: ViSurf integrates SFT and RLVR in a unified single-stage paradigm that injects ground-truth labels into RLVR rollouts with three novel reward control strategies.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standalone SFT, RLVR, and sequential pipelines across diverse benchmarks while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Training-free test-time adaptation for VLMs degrades under severe style and environment variations due to retrieval confounding and environment-biased priors.
approach: D^2O is a training-free debiasing operator outputting a content feature for semantic matching, a routing coordinate for bias tracking, and debiased logits for corrected priors.
contribution: Achieves clearest gains under style/environment shifts, with broader gains elsewhere, composing plug-and-play with retrieval-based and Gaussian adapters.

problem: VLMs are deterministic and lack mechanisms to quantify epistemic uncertainty reflecting model ignorance in representations.
approach: REPVLM computes probability density on the hyperspherical manifold of VLM embeddings using Riemannian Flow Matching, with negative log-density as an epistemic uncertainty proxy.
contribution: Achieves near-perfect correlation between uncertainty and prediction error, significantly outperforming baselines for classification, OOD detection, and automated data curation.

problem: Autoregressive models for high-precision vector graphics are constrained by discretization, causing precision loss and visual artifacts in logos, layouts, and circuit designs.
approach: A hybrid framework combines categorical prediction for discrete values with diffusion-based modeling for continuous values, incorporating EOS logit adjustment and length regularization.
contribution: Achieves higher-fidelity hybrid representations than discretization baselines, with ContLayNet benchmark of 334K semiconductor layouts demonstrating scalability to high-precision domains.

problem: Transparent objects violate Lambertian assumptions, degrading depth estimation and 3D reconstruction in downstream tasks.
approach: GHOST leverages visual foundation models to transform transparent regions into opaque, structurally consistent representations, using TransDINO, TransDecomp, DAF-Net, and GeoSemTransNet.
contribution: Significantly enhances accuracy of state-of-the-art depth and reconstruction models on transparent objects by restoring essential photometric cues.

problem: Analyzing large-scale text corpora for undesirable behaviors is costly with LLM-based techniques and lacks control with dense embeddings.
approach: SAE embeddings represent text where dimensions map to interpretable concepts, enabling cost-effective and controllable data analysis for semantic differences and bias detection.
contribution: SAE embeddings uncover semantic differences at 2-8x lower cost than LLMs and outperform dense embeddings on property-based retrieval through concept filtering.

problem: Pairwise preference methods for RL are inefficient in long-horizon problems and lack guarantees comparing Markov policies to history-dependent policies.
approach: A Markov decision contest formulation proves stationary Markov policies are optimal, that exact solution is in P, and proposes an iterative algorithm with sublinear convergence rate.
contribution: Shows superior learning efficiency compared to prior work in high-dimensional decision problems with long time horizons.

problem: LLM-based optimization modeling generates syntactically correct but semantically flawed code due to reliance on single-pass generation and solver error messages.
approach: SAC-Opt grounds modeling in problem semantics via a backward-guided correction framework that aligns original and reconstructed semantic anchors, selectively correcting mismatches.
contribution: Improves average modeling accuracy by 7.7% with gains up to 21.9% on ComplexLP, without requiring additional training or supervision.

problem: Simulating conditioned diffusion dynamics is challenging, especially for rare events where unconditioned dynamics rarely reach the terminal state.
approach: Learning diffusion bridges via a self-consistency property of optimal control, treating the problem iteratively in an online manner without differentiating through trajectories.
contribution: Exhibits strong empirical performance across settings, with theoretical connections to stochastic optimal control advances.

problem: Existing evaluations of unified multimodal models assess understanding and generation in isolation, overlooking synergy between comprehension and generation.
approach: Unison benchmark provides 2,169 high-quality unified task samples evaluating internal consistency, understanding-guided generation, and mutual enhancement, with both unified and decoupled tracks.
contribution: Uncovers critical limitations in current unified systems through holistic evaluation and provides Unison-Judge for human-aligned assessment.

problem: Sequential quantization-then-fine-tuning fails to leverage the interaction between quantization bit-width and LoRA rank for memory-constrained adaptation.
approach: AutoQRA jointly optimizes bit-width and LoRA rank via global multi-fidelity evolutionary search with importance priors followed by trust-region Bayesian optimization.
contribution: Achieves performance close to full-precision fine-tuning under given memory budgets through intelligent configuration search.

problem: Long-time simulation of Hamiltonian systems is limited by small timesteps required for stable numerical integration.
approach: Hamiltonian Flow Maps predict mean phase-space evolution over time span enabling stable large-timestep updates, trained on trajectory-free MLFF datasets via mean flow consistency.
contribution: Maintains comparable training/inference cost while supporting significantly larger timesteps than classical integrators on molecular dynamics simulations.

problem: Solving generalized Ising problems like MAX-CUT and Number Partitioning requires finding local minima efficiently.
approach: A polynomial relaxation provides one-to-one correspondence between local minima of the relaxation and one-flip local minima of the original problem, enabling gradient-based optimization.
contribution: Achieves strong performance on spin-glass models, MAX-CUT, and NPP benchmarks through ADAM optimization.

problem: Existing task-oriented dialogue methods fail to balance empathetic communication with budget-aware decision-making in LLM-based agents.
approach: InteractCS-RL reframes dialogue as multi-granularity RL with a User-centric Interaction Framework and Cost-aware Multi-turn Policy Optimization using PID-Lagrangian cost control.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines across user reward, global cost constraints, and tool-agent-user interaction benchmarks.

problem: 3D trajectory prediction requires capturing spatiotemporal dependencies while preserving SE(3) physical symmetries, which is challenging for flow matching.
approach: GSE-Flow extends flow matching to SE(3)-equivariant dynamics via Coherent Sequence Encoding and Geometry-Feature Tensorization with Context-Flow Fusion.
contribution: Guarantees theoretical SE(3)-equivariance and achieves SOTA accuracy on MD17, MD22, and CMU MoCap benchmarks for geometric trajectory prediction.

problem: Neural scaling laws are well-documented but their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood due to lack of scalable analysis tools.
approach: Spectral position measures which eigenvalues of the empirical neural tangent kernel drive loss reduction, revealing that learning shifts from dominant eigenmodes into the spectral tail.
contribution: Shows larger models achieve lower losses by reaching further into the spectral tail, with feature learning enabling this through gradient amplification.

problem: Adversarial attacks relying on dense feature manipulation have poor black-box transferability due to overfitting on surrogate models.
approach: LRS-Attack exploits low-rank and sparse decomposition of hierarchical feature subspaces with a hierarchical mixture of robust experts for transferable adversarial directions.
contribution: Consistently improves black-box transferability over state-of-the-art across CNN/ViT architectures and defense settings.

problem: Fine-tuning large models on edge devices is limited by memory-intensive backpropagation in federated and split learning.
approach: HO-SFL decouples optimization: servers use first-order updates while clients use zeroth-order optimization, enabling dimension-free model aggregation.
contribution: Achieves convergence speeds comparable to first-order methods while significantly reducing client memory and communication costs.

problem: Generalizable and Actionable Parts pose estimation requires cross-category perception but most works have insufficient symmetry handling or require rich symmetry annotation.
approach: SAFAG proposes a stepwise refinement two-stage framework with self-supervised learning for symmetry prediction as a probability distribution.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance and robustness for GAPart pose estimation without requiring symmetry annotations.

problem: RL for agentic multimodal models suffers from interaction collapse where models reduce tool usage and multi-turn reasoning.
approach: PyVision-RL combines oversampling-filtering-ranking rollout strategy with accumulative tool reward, using on-demand context construction for video reasoning.
contribution: Maintains sustained interaction and improved efficiency, demonstrating strong performance on image and video understanding with reduced visual token usage.

problem: Long-form generation in LLMs requires reliable uncertainty quantification, but existing methods ignore structural dependencies among facts and semantic variation across outputs.
approach: GAUSS models each paragraph as a semantic graph of atomic facts, quantifying uncertainty as expected alignment cost between graphs of anchor and alternative generations.
contribution: Offers more interpretable and theoretically grounded uncertainty measures than coarse, sentence-level scores by capturing semantic content and structural coherence.

problem: Recovering multiple physical parameters from high-dimensional optical measurements via Mueller matrix observations is challenging.
approach: MMPD-Bench reframes multi-polarimetric modalities decomposition as a modality fission problem, benchmarking state-space models, ViTs, diffusion models, and neural operators.
contribution: Reveals non-trivial trade-offs between accuracy and robustness in accelerated high-fidelity polarimetric decomposition with 21,412 Mueller matrix observations.

problem: Continual learning methods optimize for in-domain performance, learning spurious domain-specific cues that limit generalization to unseen domains.
approach: Sequential invariance alignment combines replay-based training with tailored learning to preserve invariant structures capturing causal mechanisms across domains.
contribution: Consistently outperforms CL baselines on generalization to unseen domains across vision, medicine, manufacturing, and ecology benchmarks.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models introduces new parameters and lacks theoretical justification for small subnetwork fine-tuning.
approach: SliceFine theory establishes spectral balance and high task energy in pretrained weights, proposing to update only selected slices without introducing new parameters.
contribution: Matches SOTA PEFT methods while significantly improving training speed, memory efficiency, and model compactness across language and vision tasks.

problem: LLM-based scientific agents suffer from inefficiencies due to adherence to fixed initial priors and static hypothesis spaces, limiting novel phenomenon discovery.
approach: PiEvo treats scientific discovery as Bayesian optimization over an expanding principle space with Information-Directed Hypothesis Selection and anomaly-driven augmentation.
contribution: Achieves 90.81-93.15% solution quality, 29.7-31.1% improvement over SOTA, and 83.3% convergence speedup with robust performance across domains and LLM backbones.

problem: LLMs frequently generate output contradicting explicit input evidence, limited by cognitive inertia from pretraining co-occurrence associations.
approach: LLMInertia probes input-related cognitive inertia and generates adaptive counter-inertial reminders injected into prompts to promote evidence-based reasoning.
contribution: Reduces hallucination rates by up to 35% and improves accuracy by up to 35.68% on co-occurrence and context-rich datasets.

problem: Identifying feature representations in language models via attention matrix singular vectors lacks sound theoretical justification.
approach: Demonstrates robustly aligned singular vectors with features and provides theoretical justification under a range of conditions, identifying sparse attention decomposition as a testable prediction.
contribution: Establishes alignment of singular vectors with features as a sound and theoretically justified basis for feature identification in language models.

problem: GFlowNets for LLM fine-tuning are prone to mode collapse manifesting as prefix collapse and length bias due to weak credit assignment and biased replay.
approach: RapTB anchors subtrajectory supervision at the root with absorbed suffix-based backups, while SubM uses submodular replay refresh promoting reward and diversity.
