contribution: Consistently improves optimization performance and molecular diversity on molecule generation with SMILES while preserving validity.

problem: Online conformal prediction requires manual learning-rate tuning and algorithm-specific analyses for achieving long-run coverage on adversarial data streams.
approach: UP-OCP reduces OCP to a two-asset portfolio selection problem via universal portfolio algorithms, controlled by linearized regret and $(1-\alpha)$-pinball loss.
contribution: Parameter-free method delivering consistently better size/coverage trade-offs than prior baselines with strong finite-time miscoverage bounds.

problem: Autoregressive language models lack interpretability, limiting trust and risking deception and hallucination despite strong performance.
approach: Prototype Transformer replaces quadratic self-attention with linear-cost prototype-based module that automatically captures nameable concepts during training.
contribution: Scales well, shows robustness to perturbations, and performs well on text generation and GLUE, with interpretable prototypes enabling targeted behavior editing.

problem: Detecting ReDoS vulnerabilities is challenging, requiring balance between efficiency and support for extended regex features like lookarounds and backreferences.
approach: RMGNN converts regexes to Heterogeneous Regex Graphs, encodes ReDoS-related motifs, and applies heterogeneous propagation with kernel-guided motif learning.
contribution: Outperforms six SOTA baselines in F1-score with 244x speedup over top F1-performing baseline across four real-world datasets of 317k+ regexes.

problem: Camouflaged Object Detection is challenging due to multi-object matching difficulties, low-quality samples, and visual distractors with similar textures.
approach: PMSPO uses curriculum learning with Sinkhorn multi-object matching IoU reward, Positive Learning Gain Filtering for sample curation, and semantic contrastive reward rules.
contribution: Achieves SOTA performance among RL methods on COD benchmarks across all evaluation metrics.

problem: Knowledge augmentation in LLMs operates on simplistic premises, overlooking knowledge-confidence gaps leading to overconfident errors or uncertain truths.
approach: A meta-cognitive framework leverages internal cognitive signals to partition knowledge into mastered, confused, and missing regions with cognitive consistency alignment.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in enhancing knowledge while fostering calibrated cognitive behaviors distinguishing knowns from unknowns.

problem: Reinforcement learning policies for reasoning collapse when positive sharpening and negative squeezing create irreversible contraction in the sampling probability of valid alternatives.
approach: Anchored Policy Optimization (APO) shifts from global shape-matching constraints to support coverage, using a safe manifold based on reference model confidence to permit aggressive sharpening while selectively invoking restorative forces during error correction.
contribution: APO breaks the accuracy-diversity trade-off by maintaining support coverage and improving both Pass@1 correctness and Pass@K diversity on mathematical benchmarks.

problem: Identifying root causes in complex microservice systems requires navigating intricate dependencies that exceed human expertise, and existing causal methods are sample-inefficient without full causal graphs.
approach: Bayesian Root Cause Discovery (BRCD) leverages partial causal structure via CPDAGs and uniform DAG sampling to perform Bayesian inference efficiently without enumerating all interventional Markov equivalence classes.
contribution: BRCD provides the first statistical consistency guarantees for nonparametric RCA with identifiability and finite-sample posterior bounds, achieving state-of-the-art top-l accuracy on microservice benchmarks.

problem: In decentralized social learning where each agent controls a short episode of decisions, exploration systematically fails and Bayesian regret grows linearly despite per-agent incentives to explore.
approach: Analyze a stylized multi-armed bandit protocol where self-interested agents collectively exhibit aggregate exploration failure even with diverse per-round utilities (min, max, sum).
contribution: The paper demonstrates that exploration failure is typical in episodic social learning, proving that externally driven exploration is necessary even when local exploration occurs organically.

problem: Predicting periodic charge densities in crystalline materials is computationally expensive due to explicit real-space grid probing and periodic image summation in traditional methods.
approach: ELECTRAFI constructs anisotropic Gaussians in real space and uses their closed-form Fourier transforms via the Poisson summation formula to analytically evaluate plane-wave coefficients with a single inverse FFT.
contribution: ELECTRAFI matches or exceeds state-of-the-art accuracy while being up to 633x faster than competing methods, reducing total DFT compute cost by approximately 20% when used to initialize calculations.

problem: Black-box agentic systems remain difficult to interpret and control because their internal workflows are opaque, limiting user understanding and editability.
approach: AgentXRay formulates Agentic Workflow Reconstruction (AWR) as a combinatorial optimization problem using Monte Carlo Tree Search with Red-Black Pruning to synthesize interpretable stand-in workflows that approximate black-box systems via input-output access.
contribution: AgentXRay produces editable white-box workflows matching target outputs without model parameters, achieving higher proxy similarity and reduced token consumption compared to unpruned search.

problem: Time series foundation models process temporal patterns through single-pass inference but regional climate prediction requires multi-scale temporal analysis and iterative refinement like expert climatologists employ.
approach: RGMR (Residual-Guided Multi-Resolution Refinement) performs structured coarse-to-fine refinement at inference-time via residual guidance without updating backbone parameters, working across multiple TSFM architectures.
contribution: RGMR reduces test-set MSE on SPEI drought forecasting by up to 18.9% across South Australian sites with consistent improvements on TimesFM, TimeGPT, and TabPFN architectures.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from the Likelihood Trap where standard alignment objectives (MLE, KL-regularization) drive generation toward generic high-probability templates, suppressing fine-grained visual details.
approach: Geo-RL reformulates caption generation from probabilistic likelihood to geometric coverage maximization via Determinantal Point Processes, enforcing orthogonality among descriptions to span the image's full semantic support.
contribution: Geo-RL escapes the likelihood trap, achieving significant improvements in semantic richness and detail coverage without compromising visual grounding.

problem: Designing RNA sequences that fold into specific secondary structures remains computationally challenging because the inverse design problem has high complexity and poor exploration of design policies.
approach: CocoRNA decomposes RNA inverse design into smaller sub-problems solved collaboratively by multiple agents using cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, with a centralized critic using global structural information.
contribution: CocoRNA substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in success rate and design speed on the Rfam dataset, with policies that generalize to unseen structures without additional training.

problem: Web agents require massive trajectories to generalize but real-world training is constrained by network latency, rate limits, and safety risks, necessitating efficient simulation.
approach: WebWorld series leverages a scalable data pipeline to train on 1M+ open-web interactions, supporting reasoning and multi-format data via a differentiable simulator enabling 30+ step long-horizon simulations.
contribution: WebWorld achieves simulation performance comparable to Gemini-3-Pro; Qwen3-14B trained on WebWorld-synthesized trajectories improves +9.2% on WebArena reaching GPT-4o performance levels.

problem: Learning-augmented paging algorithms have a robustness gap; prior work achieves 2H_k + O(1) competitive ratio but the optimal ratio is H_k, leaving room for improvement.
approach: Introduce the relative prediction budget as a unifying primitive to analyze robustness in learning-augmented paging, developing a framework that closes the gap between theoretical optimality and practical performance.
contribution: Achieve the best-possible robustness of H_k + O(1) competitive ratio for learning-augmented paging with strong practical performance demonstrated experimentally.

problem: Large Multimodal Models have static, limited knowledge that cannot keep pace with real-world developments, leading to the challenge of continuous knowledge acquisition while preventing catastrophic forgetting.
approach: KORE implements KnOwledge-oRientEd controls via a two-stage process: automatic conversion of knowledge items into structured forms for accurate learning, and storage of previous knowledge in covariance matrices while initializing adapters in the null space to minimize interference.
contribution: KORE achieves superior new knowledge injection and effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting across LLaVA-v1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL models.

problem: Adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs face a transferability problem because methods that maximize latent representation similarity overfit to specific targets with poor generalization.
approach: DART adopts a statistical lens using Energy Distance to characterize intrinsic image semantics for distribution-aware alignment, and trains a GNN to adaptively select surrogate models that maximize transferability.
contribution: DART demonstrates superior robustness and effectiveness in adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs compared to competing baselines.

problem: Reconstructing complete yet compact 3D Gaussian Splatting representations from sparse-view monocular video is challenged by correlated pseudo-views and repeated merging that accumulate structured, non-i.i.d. redundancy.
approach: CoverPruneGS implements coverage-preserving structured pruning via coarse-to-fine voxel-based diversity selection and ground-truth-guided lazy refinement with footprint-aware CUDA attribution for precise importance scoring.
contribution: CoverPruneGS reduces Gaussian counts by 56.8%, significantly accelerates inference, and enhances or maintains novel view synthesis quality across multiple datasets.

problem: Modeling Koopman dynamics for nonlinear systems is computationally burdensome due to sequential propagation that creates a linear-depth temporal composition bottleneck.
approach: Use Lie-algebraic structure to constrain neural generators within prescribed Lie subalgebras and construct finite-time flows via neural Magnus expansion, applying prefix-scan algorithms to reduce composition depth from linear to logarithmic.
contribution: The framework enables accurate long-horizon prediction while improving computational efficiency through scalable Koopman operator learning for nonlinear systems.

problem: scRNA-seq clustering using graph transformers has O(n^2) computational and space complexity, limiting applicability to large-scale single-cell RNA datasets.
approach: BGFormer introduces learnable anchor tokens as shared reference points and uses bipartite graph attention to learn similarity between cells and anchors, achieving linear computational complexity.
contribution: BGFormer achieves state-of-the-art clustering performance with linear complexity, demonstrating effectiveness and scalability on multiple large-scale scRNA-seq datasets.

problem: Multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability struggles to specify complex objectives and constraints without formal specification frameworks.
approach: HyPOLE integrates formal specifications via HyperLTL temporal logic with Centralized Training for Decentralized Execution (CTDE) to synthesize decentralized policies guided by expressive hyperproperties.
contribution: HyPOLE demonstrates clear advantages over baselines on SMAC, MessySMAC, and WildFire benchmarks for learning formally-specified multi-agent behaviors.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models require substantial task-specific demonstrations for adaptation, but action imitation ignores richer trajectory structure that could improve few-shot adaptation.
approach: DynVLA reformulates VLA learning from action imitation to motion dynamics modeling, using Motion Dynamics Mechanism (MDM) to distill latent embeddings via flow-matching inversion and projecting onto a Dynamics Bank of prior motion knowledge.
contribution: DynVLA outperforms SOTA by 15.8% in average success rate with around 20 demonstrations on 13 real-world manipulation tasks.

problem: Large-scale web-crawled datasets contain noise and bias but existing data-selection methods depend on hand-crafted heuristics, downstream datasets, or expensive influence computations.
approach: Mimic Score measures alignment between a sample's gradients and a target direction induced by a pre-trained reference model, with Grad-Mimic framework providing online re-weighting and offline filtering stages.
contribution: Mimic scores guide training to improve data efficiency and accelerate convergence with consistent gains across six image datasets; CLIP models trained with 4.7M fewer samples show improved performance.

problem: Web agents fine-tuned on specific trajectories and domains struggle to generalize out-of-domain, and offline training is compute-inefficient due to noisy, redundant trajectories and long accessibility-tree states.
approach: Weasel selects a fixed-budget trajectory subset by optimizing importance-diversity objectives over states, websites, and interaction patterns via greedy algorithms, with target-centered AXTree pruning and style-consistent rationale replacement.
contribution: Weasel improves out-of-domain performance with roughly 9.7-12.5x training speedups over standard fine-tuning across WebArena, WorkArena, and MiniWob benchmarks.

problem: Gastrointestinal motility assessment via bowel sounds is compromised by spectral overlap with non-stationary speech interference, and traditional Gaussian-based diffusion frameworks struggle with impulsive, heavy-tailed clinical noise.
approach: Propose Cauchy-driven Diffusion Bridge framework with closed-form score and density expressions derived to model heavy-tailed perturbations, implementing efficient sampling via Gaussian scale-mixture reparameterization.
contribution: Framework achieves state-of-the-art performance outperforming baselines by 13.4-49.8% across metrics, elevating abnormal bowel sound recognition accuracy to 88.01% on a large clinical dataset (25+ hours).

problem: Population dynamics inference typically focuses on gradient flows that minimize kinetic energy, but this selection criterion may not capture non-potential transport mechanisms present in real systems.
approach: Non-Gradient Inference Flows (NGIF) leverages gauge freedom to infer general vector fields using weak formulation of continuity equation, enabling parameterization with alternative selection criteria beyond minimal energy.
contribution: NGIF improves distributional accuracy over gradient-restricted baselines and better captures non-potential transport on low- and high-dimensional physics problems.

problem: In-Context Reinforcement Learning's efficacy in Ad-Hoc Teamwork with unknown partners remains unexplored, requiring rigorous evaluation with diverse teammate suites and train-test shifts.
approach: Introduce ICRL4AHT benchmark built on high-throughput JAX Overcooked-V2 with diverse teammate suite and reproducible pipeline for teammate generation, dataset construction, and evaluation.
contribution: Evaluation reveals that representative ICRL algorithms (AD, DPT) fail to exhibit robust test-time adaptation in multi-agent settings, underperforming random baselines across unseen teammates and layouts.

problem: Evidential Deep Learning can be overconfident and poorly calibrated while failing to represent multi-modal epistemic uncertainty despite single-pass inference capability.
approach: Gated Evidential Mixtures (GEM) learns an in-model energy signal to gate evidential outputs end-to-end; GEM-MIX adds mixture of evidential heads with learned routing; GEM-FI stabilizes via Fisher-informed regularization.
contribution: GEM improves calibration and ID/OOD separation with single-pass inference; GEM-FI improves CIFAR-10 accuracy from 91.11% to 93.75% and reduces Brier score substantially.

problem: Prototype-based few-shot point cloud semantic segmentation fails to adequately model feature distribution shift between support and query sets, resulting in insufficient prototype adaptation.
approach: DPR-Net constructs progressive adaptation via coarse-to-fine prototype evolution, decomposing features into common and distinctive subspaces to enable targeted adjustment while preserving class-shared semantics.
contribution: DPR-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on few-shot point cloud semantic segmentation with high efficiency and provides code availability.

problem: One-shot skeleton-based action recognition requires capturing hierarchical and compositional human motion structure while aligning with action semantics under extreme data scarcity.
approach: SkelHCC embeds skeleton sequences and action language into a shared hyperbolic space via Explicitly Hierarchical Hyperbolic CLIP (EH-HCLIP), leveraging hyperbolic geometry to encode anatomical hierarchy; LLM-guided Multi-granularity Voting Cache enables training-free adaptation.
contribution: SkelHCC outperforms state-of-the-art methods on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and PKU-MMD II datasets for one-shot action recognition.

problem: Recovering scene-consistent 4D crowd motion from monocular video in large-scale scenes is challenged by severe depth ambiguity and complex scene geometry with typical single-plane assumptions leading to unreliable metric scale.
approach: Crowd4D jointly optimizes crowd and scene via Human-Scene Interaction Proxy (HSIP) derived from Scene Interaction Point Clouds and Surface, with Crowd Structural Coherence Regularization (CSCR) to improve temporal stability under occlusions.
contribution: Crowd4D consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods for robust monocular 4D crowd reconstruction in complex, large-scale scenes.

problem: EEG foundation models inadequately model complex spatiotemporal topology and suffer from modality gap between low-level physiological signals and high-level textual semantics.
approach: KAST-BAR dynamically aligns physiological representations from multi-level brain topology with expert-level semantic space via Dual-Stream Hierarchical Attention (DSHA) encoder and Knowledge-Anchored Semantic Profiler (KASP), with Semantic Text-Aware Refiner (STAR).
contribution: KAST-BAR achieves state-of-the-art performance across six downstream tasks through large-scale pre-training on 21 diverse EEG datasets.

problem: Multimodal visual tracking requires training separate models for each modality or relying on pretrained models, limiting efficiency, scalability, and usability for unified multi-modal approaches.
approach: OneTrackerV2 introduces Meta Merger to embed multi-modal information into unified space; Dual Mixture-of-Experts (DMoE) models spatiotemporal relations (T-MoE) and multi-modal knowledge (M-MoE) with shared architecture and unified parameters.
contribution: OneTrackerV2 achieves state-of-the-art performance across five RGB and RGB+X tracking tasks with 12 benchmarks while maintaining high inference efficiency and strong performance under modality-missing scenarios.

problem: Standard expected-reward RL formulation is only a first-order approximation of maximum likelihood when feedback is terminal and binary, leading to suboptimal sample efficiency.
approach: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL) introduces a compute-indexed family of sample-based objectives that interpolate between expected-reward RL and maximum likelihood as sampling compute scales.
contribution: MaxRL Pareto-dominates existing methods, achieves up to 20x gains in test-time scaling efficiency over GRPO, and scales more favorably with additional training data and compute.

problem: Influence functions for data debugging and unlearning become impractical for high-query subset workloads like large-K cross-validation due to expensive inverse-curvature solves required per query.
approach: Clustered Influence Functions (CiF) amortizes subset influence computation by clustering training gradients once, solving damped Generalised Gauss-Newton only for cluster means, and answering queries via linear recombination using cluster membership counts.
contribution: CiF matches per-query influence rankings while significantly reducing total runtime in high-Q regimes, enabling influence-based workflows that are otherwise computationally prohibitive.

problem: Scaling inference-time computation through parallel reasoning in LLMs suffers from performance degradation compared to sequential counterparts and often requires specialized inference engines.
approach: ThreadWeaver enables adaptive parallel reasoning via a two-stage parallel trajectory generator for supervised fine-tuning, trie-based rollout for any off-the-shelf autoregressive engine, and parallelization-aware RL framework.
contribution: ThreadWeaver matches sequential reasoning accuracy (79.9% on AIME24, 71.9% average) while delivering up to 1.53x speedup in token latency on Qwen3-8B.

problem: Graph Transformers lack a unified theoretical understanding of desirable propagation operators despite diverse topology injection paradigms.
approach: BDFormer rethinks Graph Transformers from a graph signal denoising perspective with block-diagonal structure as a desirable prior, imposing spectral block regularization on compact anchor affinities and using hard assignments for sparse propagation.
contribution: BDFormer establishes superior performance and scalability by achieving block-diagonal propagation structure with linear-time complexity.

problem: Standard value function learning in reinforcement learning lacks geometric structure that could stabilize and accelerate learning by encoding symmetries and constraints.
approach: GCR-RL (Geometric Coherence Regularized RL) recasts value function learning through order theory as learning a desired poset, computing sequences of super-poset refinements via temporal difference signals while ensuring geometric coherence.
contribution: GCR-RL demonstrates significant improvements in sample efficiency and stable performance over strong baselines through Q-learning and actor-critic algorithms.

problem: Infrared object detection is vulnerable to physical adversarial attacks where shape geometry is the primary information carrier, but shape-based methods face a trade-off between representational capability and optimization power.
approach: Leverage learnable Fourier shapes in end-to-end differentiable framework where compact Fourier coefficients analytically map to pixel-space masks via winding number theorem for efficient gradient-based optimization.
contribution: Physical patches achieve over 88% attack success rate at distances greater than 25m, demonstrating striking robustness across diverse distances, angles, poses, and individuals.

problem: Vision-language models suffer efficiency collapse when vision tokens dominate compute and memory, and prior token-reduction strategies trade off salience and diversity with limited hyperparameter robustness.
approach: SPLIT estimates token importance via temporal shifts of hidden states to avoid attention-score biases, assigns adaptive region-level budgets for localized coverage, and selects tokens via diversity score prioritizing distinctive representations.
contribution: SPLIT preserves over 99% accuracy with 192 vision tokens and 92.8% with only 64 tokens on image understanding with LLaVA-1.5-7B.

problem: Rapid face recognition dataset evaluation without full-scale training requires metrics to assess inherent potential, but existing approaches lack validation-free alternatives.
approach: Intrinsic Quality (IQ) integrates Neighbor-Consistency Score quantifying local identity label agreement and Global Representation Subspace Complexity (Effective Rank) capturing embedding geometry and dataset diversity.
contribution: IQ enables rapid evaluation using lightweight proxy models or data subsets, facilitating dataset diagnosis and curation prior to resource-intensive training.

problem: Multi-objective discrete optimization in domains like molecular design faces challenges with vast combinatorial spaces where closed-source LLMs cannot update parameters and smaller models lack broad knowledge.
approach: MCCE unites a frozen closed-source LLM with trainable model via progressive refinement through reinforcement learning, maintaining trajectory memory and enabling mutual support through joint exploration and experience-driven learning.
contribution: MCCE achieves state-of-the-art Pareto front quality on multi-objective drug design benchmarks, outperforming baselines through hybrid LLM collaboration.

problem: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) incurs prohibitive computational costs due to extensive group-based sampling, and selective data utilization methods risk inducing estimation bias.
approach: Dynamic Pruning Policy Optimization (DPPO) enables dynamic pruning while preserving unbiased gradient estimation through importance sampling-based correction, with Dense Prompt Packing to maximize token density.
contribution: DPPO achieves 2.37x training speedup on Qwen3-4B MATH tasks and outperforms GRPO by 3.36% average accuracy across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Strong universal Bayes-consistency for general metric losses lacks necessary and sufficient characterization in the realizable setting, extending only partially beyond classification and regression.
approach: Extend realizable Bayes-consistency theory by introducing infinite non-decreasing (γ_k)-Littlestone trees where γ_k tends to infinity, providing sharp characterization via combinatorial obstruction.
contribution: Resolve the realizable case of open problem in metric loss learning by establishing conditions under which distribution-free learning rules achieve near-optimal risk.

problem: Quantum error correction decoder deployment is hindered by a fundamental accuracy-latency tradeoff on microsecond timescales, requiring evaluation of neural decoder practical deployability.
approach: Unify representative neural decoders into five architectural paradigms and develop end-to-end compression pipeline to evaluate deployability on FPGA hardware for surface-code decoding up to distance d=9.
contribution: Reveal that near-term performance is driven by data scale over architecture complexity, appropriate inductive bias is essential, and INT4 quantization enables microsecond-scale FPGA latency.

problem: Federated learning degrades under data heterogeneity and distribution shifts when using local feature statistics for test-time adaptation.
approach: FedPAT learns a global prototype affinity topology (the relational structure among class prototypes) by aggregating from source clients, then uses topology-aware diffusion and optimization for test-time adaptation on unseen target clients.
contribution: FedPAT consistently outperforms federated and classical test-time adaptation methods across various distribution shifts by leveraging stable prototype relationships.

problem: Federated learning deletion requests require client-level unlearning, but client influence is deeply entangled after aggregation, making unlearning slow and unstable.
approach: Influence-Disentangled Federated Training decomposes each round's updates into shared covarying directions and client-separable residual traces, using entanglement-aware shrinkage to suppress non-removable components.
contribution: IDFT achieves deletion with a single subtraction and short repair, attaining the lowest retrain gap and improving the fidelity-cost frontier on multiple benchmarks.

problem: LLM agents struggle with multi-step reasoning over FHIR-structured clinical graphs, often selecting wrong resources or violating traversal constraints.
approach: A CodeAct agent is post-trained with reinforcement learning using a custom harness, tools, and LLM Judge providing execution-grounded rewards over the queryable FHIR graph.
contribution: RL post-training improves answer correctness from 50% to 77% on FHIR-AgentBench using a smaller, cheaper Qwen3-8B model while enforcing data-integrity constraints.

problem: Existing relational learning methods use static entity representations and assume symmetric inference, inadequate for capturing context-dependent functions and asymmetric high-order relations.
approach: CONTEXTOR decomposes high-order relations into incomplete query tuples and response entities, contextualizing candidate responses via asymmetric conditional modulation and aligning via multi-fold contrastive learning.
contribution: CONTEXTOR consistently outperforms existing methods on benchmark datasets across diverse biomedical tasks.

problem: Neural networks are nonlinear, making classical linear algebra tools (SVD, projection, etc.) inapplicable to nonlinear mappings.
approach: The Linearizer framework identifies non-standard vector spaces where a neural network acts as a linear operator by sandwiching it between invertible networks, using transport of structure to derive custom addition and scaling.
contribution: Diffusion model sampling collapses from hundreds of steps into a single step; the framework also enables idempotency enforcement and modular style transfer.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for document understanding degrade under real-world degradations (noise, blur, low resolution) due to scarcity of large-scale training data and lack of transferable solutions across architectures.
approach: Uni-DocRobust proposes a universal plug-and-play framework with a frozen Universal Restoration Core trained via multi-teacher distillation in canonical feature space, integrated via lightweight Feature Adapters into target MLLMs.
contribution: With DocRobust-VQA (189K clean/corrupted pairs, 417K QA pairs), Uni-DocRobust significantly enhances robust MLLM performance across architectures via a cost-effective pre-train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm.

problem: Multi-headed self-attention has a large memory footprint, motivating specialized low-rank factorizations like GQA and MLA, but their theoretical foundations and parameter efficiency trade-offs are unclear.
approach: Tucker Attention generalizes GQA and MLA via a unified low-rank factorization strategy across embedding dimensions and attention heads, constructing a parameter-efficient scheme compatible with flash-attention and RoPE.
contribution: Tucker Attention requires an order of magnitude fewer parameters than GQA and MLA for comparable performance on LLMs and ViTs while encompassing them as special cases.

problem: SVD-based delta compression for fine-tuned LLM parameters lacks principled quantization, leading to poor generalizability and storage/distribution challenges.
approach: PrinMix models quantization as an optimization problem via 0/1 Integer Linear Programming, deriving quantization error theory and identifying singular-value-dominated scaling that necessitates mixed-precision quantization, with Reconstruction Target Correction for sequential quantization errors.
contribution: PrinMix outperforms SOTA Delta-CoMe by 22.3% on AIME2024 and 6.1% on GQA for 7B LLM compression.

problem: Enforcing measurement or physics consistency in inverse problems with diffusion models typically relies on heuristic guidance or task-specific training with limited feasibility guarantees.
approach: Terminal-conditioned inversion constructs a backward stochastic differential equation whose adapted solution defines a principled inverse map from terminal feasibility specifications to prior states, with a practical neural BSDE solver.
contribution: The framework achieves improved sparse-view CT reconstruction quality over training-free baselines while guaranteeing strict measurement feasibility under prescribed terminal specifications.

problem: Boltzmann Generators for molecular sampling face scalability limits, and coarse-grained surrogates lack reweighting procedures to ensure correct statistics.
approach: Coarse-Grained Boltzmann Generators use a flow-based model in reduced coordinate space and reweight via a learned potential of mean force, with the PMF learned from rapidly converged enhanced-sampling trajectories.
contribution: CG-BGs capture solvent-mediated interactions in highly reduced representations while substantially reducing computational cost relative to atomistic Boltzmann Generators.

problem: Sequential editing of structured knowledge in LLMs relies on complex regularization mechanisms whose necessity is unclear, and stability under accumulating edits remains unprincipled.
approach: Via optimization analysis, the work establishes formal equivalence between one-time and sequential editing, generalizing to a broader class of objectives and showing stability emerges from properly accounting for accumulated constraints rather than specialized regularization.
contribution: The framework simplifies sequential knowledge editing, eliminates unnecessary regularization strategies, and robustly handles conflicting edits while maintaining consistent behavior.

problem: Constrained saddle-point problems require projection onto feasible sets which is computationally expensive; existing projection-free methods lack unified analysis across nonconvex-concave settings.
approach: A unified dual dynamic smoothing framework enables efficient single-loop algorithms using linear minimization oracles with anytime convergence guarantees not requiring pre-specified iteration horizons.
contribution: The framework provides unified analysis for nonconvex-concave and nonconvex-strongly concave settings, significantly narrowing the performance gap between projection-free and projection-based methods.

problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer from object hallucinations driven by attention distraction, where spatial inconsistency in multi-head attention and temporal fading of visual tokens during decoding cause inaccurate descriptions.
approach: AFIP corrects attention distraction via cross-head attention enrichment and reinforces visual grounding through dynamic historical attention enhancement, without requiring additional training.
contribution: AFIP reduces hallucinations by addressing the underlying attention mechanism across multiple benchmarks and models.

problem: Combining multiple self-supervised learning objectives on graphs causes interference, training instability, and three failure modes: disagreement, drift, and drought.
approach: ControlG recasts multi-objective graph SSL as feedback-controlled temporal allocation, estimating per-objective difficulty and pairwise antagonism, planning budgets via Pareto-aware log-hypervolume, and scheduling with a PID controller.
contribution: ControlG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across 9 datasets while producing auditable schedules revealing which objectives drove learning.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for dense prediction tasks exhibits input-agnostic modeling and redundant cross-layer representations, limiting adaptation quality.
approach: ParaX employs a mixture-of-experts adapter with shared expert centers; during forward pass, each module dynamically generates tailored weight matrices via dynamic parameter routing that selectively aggregates parameter matrices.
contribution: ParaX achieves superior performance across diverse visual recognition tasks by enabling low-rank input-dependent adaptation and promoting cross-layer feature interaction.

problem: Conventional autoregressive MLLMs limit architectural alternatives; discrete diffusion models show promise for NLP but have not been applied to unified multimodal understanding and generation.
approach: Omni-Diffusion is the first any-to-any multimodal model built on mask-based discrete diffusion, directly capturing the joint distribution over discrete multimodal tokens for text, speech, and images.
contribution: Omni-Diffusion outperforms or matches existing multimodal systems on diverse benchmarks, demonstrating significant promise of diffusion models for next-generation multimodal foundation models.

problem: Continual learning is vulnerable to data poisoning attacks that trigger divergence or severe excess risk, yet a principled theoretical foundation for attack and defense is lacking.
approach: Framing adversary-defender interaction as an online zero-sum game, the work establishes performance limits, proposes task-to-task verification for infrequent attacks, and derives robust defense minimizing sensitivity to poisoned features.
contribution: The framework proves no defense succeeds against linear-proportion task poisoning, but identifies defensible regimes and provides verified convergence guarantees for robust defense.

problem: Large multimodal models achieve high scores on existing visual benchmarks, quickly eroding headroom and making it hard to benchmark progress on visual reasoning over time.
approach: ZeroBench is a lightweight visual reasoning benchmark curated via adversarial filtering to be initially impossible for frontier LMMs, tracking progress year-over-year with human baseline comparison.
contribution: Initial SotA was 0% pass@1, reaching 19% pass@5 after one year; ZeroBench demonstrates sustained benchmark difficulty and charts progress on 46 LMMs.

problem: CAD generation as sequence modeling lacks intermediate visual feedback, hindering association of individual tokens with their geometric effects.
approach: An Argument-induced 3D Point Loss maps argument tokens to corresponding 3D points for dense token-wise geometric supervision, and a Grammar-constrained Operator leverages structured CAD program syntax to regulate generation.
contribution: The approach improves generation accuracy and program validity across five CAD tasks with diverse input modalities (text, SVG, point clouds, CAD sequences).

problem: Large-scale web-harvested datasets suffer from noisy correspondence in cross-modal retrieval, degrading generalization; existing methods rely on discrete selection inducing fragility and discretization error.
approach: IN2R shifts from discrete substitution to synthesizing a reliable soft prototype via graph-based intra-modal reasoning over neighbors, leveraging intrinsic geometric stability of intra-modal data.
contribution: IN2R synthesizes continuous soft prototypes reflecting local semantic consensus on Flickr30K, MS-COCO, and CC152K, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Machine learning training under fully homomorphic encryption lacks theoretical convergence analysis and relies on costly per-sample gradient clipping for privacy.
approach: Theoretical convergence analysis of approximate gradient descent via polynomial approximations, integrated with differential privacy without per-sample clipping, plus data-independent hyperparameter selection and theoretically grounded polynomial approximation strategies.
contribution: The work advances feasibility of efficient, private, and secure machine learning on sensitive data with proven convergence guarantees.

problem: Exploration in visual reinforcement learning under sparse rewards struggles due to task-irrelevant variations; existing methods assume low-dimensional states or lack task-aware strategies.
approach: TEB couples task-relevant representations with exploration via a predictive bisimulation metric that measures global intrinsic novelty, with a predicted reward differential term preventing representation collapse.
contribution: TEB achieves superior exploration ability on MetaWorld and Maze2D, outperforming recent baselines through task-aware novelty measurement.

problem: Generative sequence modeling faces tension between Transformer expressivity and linear sequence model efficiency; iterative methods like Test-Time Training break hardware parallelism due to serial dependencies.
approach: PRISM reconstructs the gate × residual × direction iteration pattern of TTT in parallelizable form via Write-Forget Decoupling and a two-stage proxy architecture (short-convolution anchoring and learned predictor for refinement).
contribution: PRISM achieves comparable performance to explicit optimization while delivering 174x higher throughput via parallelizable feedforward operations.

problem: High-fidelity stock market simulation must balance structural and behavioral fidelity; existing approaches face persistent trade-offs in capturing complex market dynamics from heterogeneous participants.
approach: MarketSim simulates over 15,000 heterogeneous LLM agents in a hierarchical architecture decoupling strategy from execution, operating in nanosecond-resolution continuous double auction, grounded in 12k real news/policy/earnings documents.
contribution: MarketSim captures key complexity properties of real markets and outperforms baselines in tracking high-frequency price dynamics with 3.48% average MAPE.

problem: Deep networks exhibit simplicity bias aiding generalization, but a broadly applicable quantitative measure of simplicity remains elusive.
approach: Polynomial representations approximate network behavior along data-dependent interpolation paths using orthogonal polynomial bases, with effective degree serving as a distribution-aware simplicity metric.
contribution: Effective degree is predictive of generalization across tasks and architectures, outperforming sharpness; polynomial-based simplicity regularization improves generalization in classification, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

problem: Merging vision-language models with reasoning models at coarse-grained layer level trades off reasoning capability gain against visual capability loss.
approach: FRISM performs fine-grained reasoning injection via subspace-level model merging, decomposing LRM task vectors via SVD and adaptively tuning scaling coefficients per subspace through label-free self-distillation with dual-objective optimization.
contribution: FRISM effectively improves reasoning while largely preserving visual capabilities across diverse visual-language reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating long-form text-to-video generation under complex textual inputs with hierarchical metadata remains a significant challenge.
approach: LoCoT2V-Bench provides a benchmark for long video generation from multi-scene prompts with hierarchical metadata, plus LoCoT2V-Eval, a multi-dimensional framework covering perceptual quality, text-video alignment, temporal and dynamic quality, and HERD metric.
contribution: Experiments on 17 LVG models reveal strong perceptual quality but weak fine-grained text-video alignment and character consistency, identifying key challenges.

problem: Graph-based RAG over-relies on entity-centric node matching and lacks explicit causal modeling, leading to unfaithful or spurious answers; prior causality work is limited to local contexts.
approach: CausalRAG2 rethinks knowledge organization through causal gating across hierarchical modules, explicitly modeling causal relationships to suppress spurious correlations while enabling scalable cross-module reasoning over large-scale KGs.
contribution: CausalRAG2 consistently outperforms competitive graph-based RAG baselines on multiple datasets, establishing a principled foundation for structured, scalable, and causally grounded RAG.

problem: Existing 3D generation from single images is limited by restricted representation resolution, making them unsuitable for high-quality 3D scene generation.
approach: HIVE-3D introduces a hierarchical voxel enhancement framework: coarse initial scene, image segmentation and attention-based retrieval to align 2D/3D components, organizing relations into a component tree, then performing coarse-to-fine hierarchical voxel super-resolution.
contribution: HIVE-3D achieves state-of-the-art performance generating high-resolution, high-quality 3D scenes from single scene images.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models memorize training data; existing mitigation via weight pruning fails to prevent replication when text embeddings are perturbed, revealing fragility of local assumptions.
approach: The work demonstrates memorization is not inherently local: replication triggers are distributed throughout embedding space, pruned models still leak via perturbed prompts, and different pruning methods identify inconsistent weights.
contribution: Findings enable more robust mitigation through adversarial fine-tuning and inform development of more reliable defenses against DM memorization.

problem: Existing dimensionality reduction methods preserve specific invariants but lack a unified approach based on preserving point-distribution similarity across reduction.
approach: A new invariant—point-distributions similarity—is proposed with a linear, efficient method achieving dimensionality reduction while preserving this invariant.
contribution: Theoretical feasibility is proven; benchmark and single-cell expression data demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency.

problem: Time series foundation models rely on large-scale diverse pretraining, yet temporal pattern heterogeneity across domains hinders effective learning of transferable representations.
approach: Olivia harmonizes datasets via normalized power spectral density in the spectral domain; a Harmonizer module reshapes spectral structures and implicitly harmonizes PSDs, mediated by a low-dimensional HarmonicAttention design.
contribution: Olivia consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance on TSLib, GIFT-Eval, and GluonTS under zero-shot, few-shot, and full-shot forecasting scenarios.

problem: Vision-language models exhibit asymmetric confusion on downstream data and suffer from Base-New Trade-off: improving unseen class performance degrades known class accuracy.
approach: NeRP is a plug-and-play prompting correction strategy using neutral text prompts and reference images to measure class-wise prior preferences along pre-trained geometry, correcting prior-dominated mispredictions via local class-pair flips.
contribution: NeRP substantially improves accuracy on unseen classes without parameter modification across 15 few-shot and cross-domain benchmarks.

problem: Continual release of aggregates (MaxSum, MinSum, MaxSelect, MinSelect) under differential privacy inherently admits large additive error.
approach: Algorithms allowing relative error are proposed for non-adaptive streams, with proven separation between non-adaptive and adaptive stream regimes.
contribution: The work shows error can be substantially reduced via relative terms under non-adaptive streams while proving adaptive streams admit unavoidable large error for selection tasks.

problem: Modeling learning curves for cost-effective data collection is difficult; most parametric methods are inappropriate when no reliable form exists, and GP approaches struggle with monotonicity constraints.
approach: MOVE introduces a monotonic variational GP with virtual-derivative factors enabling tractable posterior inference, and develops an expected shortfall objective for target-driven data collection.
contribution: MOVE provides non-vanishing gradient signals enabling reliable optimization with consistent improvements on classification, segmentation, and detection benchmarks.

problem: Abductive reasoning remains underexplored in LLMs; existing deductive frameworks fail to generalize, suffering from evidence fabrication, context drift, failed backtracking, and early stopping.
approach: Graph of States grounds multi-agent collaboration in structured belief states with a causal graph encoding logical dependencies and a state machine governing valid reasoning transitions, aligning focus with symbolic constraints.
contribution: GoS significantly outperforms baselines on real-world abductive tasks by transforming aimless exploration into convergent directed search.

problem: Diffusion-based neural solvers for combinatorial optimization repeatedly re-evaluate dense interactions, making inference expensive in wall-clock time and memory-bound at scale.
approach: LoRe is a training-free inference-time wrapper enforcing per-step interaction-evaluation budgeting by dynamically routing computation to high-conflict/high-uncertainty interactions instead of fixed sparsification.
contribution: LoRe extends feasible MIS inference 3x beyond baseline's out-of-memory limit with ~8x speedup and ~12x memory reduction while preserving solution quality; achieves ~15x speedup on TSP with 44x memory reduction.

problem: Multi-turn LLM agent attacks split malicious intents across turns to hide future risks; existing detection methods rely on historical context and fail to identify deep attack strategies.
approach: Speculative Safety Honeypot uses a multi-agent simulation with small LLMs to speculate future agent behaviors, building a trajectory tree to expose risks, then verifies with real actions to calibrate and reduce false positives.
contribution: SSH provides existing detectors with rich decision redundancy, improving defense resilience and warning lead-time against complex temporal attacks.

problem: Batch normalization layers for neural networks on complex domains are understudied; less-studied domains like the Siegel disk lack practical implementations.
approach: BN layers for complex domains are proposed with close connections to Riemannian BN, deriving essential components for practical implementations on complex domains including Siegel disk.
contribution: Experiments on radar clutter classification, node classification, and action recognition demonstrate efficacy of complex domain batch normalization.

problem: DICE-based offline imitation learning with suboptimal supplementary data either relies on strict coverage assumptions or requires additional regularization, limiting performance.
approach: ReDICE reformulates the DICE objective to construct a mixture-distribution objective removing coverage assumptions; its dual reduces to stable Gumbel regression, with a novel policy extraction mechanism.
contribution: ReDICE consistently outperforms prior methods on standard and real-world offline IL benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art results.

problem: Learning effective ranking models from sparse and incomplete human feedback with rigid assumptions about the ranking model and censoring mechanism is challenging.
approach: Introduces PIRATE algorithm that unifies existing frameworks by considering ranking models satisfying complete consensus property and a new positional censoring feedback model that generalizes winner and top-h feedback.
contribution: Provides near-optimal instance-dependent sample complexity bounds for learning from incomplete rankings under this general framework.

problem: Generative models should give credit to works they depend on, but current approaches lack formal mechanisms to ensure this attribution.
approach: Studies counterfactual credit attribution (CCA) in autoregressive models that give credit to deployment-time datasets, uncovering fundamental barriers to two natural approaches: CCA does not compose autoregressively and retrofitting requires exponential query complexity.
contribution: Establishes theoretical barriers showing CCA autoregressive models face significant challenges unlike differential privacy approaches.

problem: Extending multimodal LLMs to dense prediction tasks like segmentation and depth estimation typically requires task-specific decoders that complicate the model architecture.
approach: Proposes DenseMLLM which uses vision token supervision strategy for multiple labels and tasks to enable standard MLLMs to perform dense predictions without additional task-specific decoders.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on dense prediction and vision-language benchmarks using a minimalist design with no architectural specialization.

problem: Diffusion language models require heuristic token unmasking strategies that need manual tuning and degrade with larger block sizes during inference.
approach: Formalizes masked diffusion sampling as an MDP and trains a single-layer transformer policy using reinforcement learning to map token confidences to unmasking decisions.
contribution: Trained policies match state-of-the-art heuristics in semi-autoregressive generation and outperform them in full-diffusion setting.

problem: Safety evaluation datasets lack geographic and cultural diversity, making it unclear whether cultural differences in safety ratings persist after controlling for demographics.
approach: Conducts multilevel modeling meta-analysis of safety datasets using Inglehart-Welzel cultural dimensions to jointly analyze geo-cultural and demographic correlates.
contribution: Demonstrates cultural zone membership explains variance in safety ratings beyond demographics (p<0.05 across 6 datasets) with ~10% of items being culturally sensitive.

problem: Video virtual try-on models fail to handle interactive scenarios where subjects actively engage with clothing through deformation and manipulation.
approach: Introduces iTryOn framework using video diffusion Transformer with multi-level interaction injection: 3D hand priors for spatial guidance and action-aware captions with rotational position embeddings for semantic guidance.
contribution: Enables video virtual try-on for interactive scenarios with active human-garment interactions like pulling or unzipping.

problem: LLM agents lose logical integrity over extended reasoning horizons because memory preprocessing compresses sequential dependencies into pre-defined structures that sever narrative coherence.
approach: Proposes E-mem framework shifting from memory preprocessing to episodic context reconstruction using heterogeneous hierarchical architecture where assistant agents maintain uncompressed contexts and master agent orchestrates planning.
contribution: Achieves 54% F1 on LoCoMo benchmark surpassing GAM by 7.75% while reducing token cost by 70%.

problem: Stochastic optimal control via dynamic programming suffers from error accumulation across time steps that remains theoretically underexplored.
approach: Formulates SOC in dynamic programming framework using RKHS-based value function estimation with Monte Carlo subsampling and derives error decomposition with backward time propagation analysis.
contribution: Provides theoretical error propagation analysis from maturity to initial stage with application to American option pricing.

problem: Multimodal fusion object detection suffers from substantial modality gap at the same backbone stage, making predefined stage-aligned fusion insufficient.
approach: Proposes MFH-NAS hybrid framework combining differentiable search for local fusion primitives with evolutionary search for global fusion topologies to discover optimal cross-stage connections.
contribution: Improves mAP@0.5 from 85.3% to 88.2% over strong fixed-stage fusion methods across LLVIP, RGBT-Tiny, and M3FD benchmarks.

problem: Reward design in RL remains challenging because hand-crafted rewards are hard to specify and learned rewards from preferences suffer from inefficiency and training instability.
approach: Proposes CoRe framework decomposing rewards into Formal Rewards (hand-designed based on task knowledge) and Residual Rewards (learned from video preferences) using vision-language models for feedback.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches on ten robotic manipulation tasks in simulation and five real-world tasks through preference-aligned reward construction.

problem: Diffusion models for image restoration have high computational overhead when operating in pixel space or require repeated encoder-decoder inference in latent space.
approach: Proposes projecting data into lower-dimensional subspaces using dynamic resolution DMs to accelerate inference while adapting existing pixel-space methods DPS and DAPS into SubDPS and SubDAPS variants.
contribution: SubDAPS++ outperforms recent DM-based approaches in majority of scenarios with improved inference speed and reconstruction quality.

problem: Disease screening models for medical images lack interpretability and effective mechanisms to reference historical cases for transparent reasoning.
approach: Introduces EviScreen framework leveraging region-level evidence from historical cases through dual knowledge banks with evidence-aware reasoning module and contrastive retrieval for abnormality localization.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on disease screening benchmarks with enhanced interpretability through regional evidence retrieval and abnormality mapping.

problem: Speculative Jacobi Decoding suffers from token ambiguity during token verification because vision tokens correspond to local unclear details that cannot be accurately expressed by single tokens.
approach: Proposes SJD-SV that leverages token correlations to recognize semantic-aware token subsequences and performs verification at subsequence level rather than token-by-token.
contribution: Plug-in method achieving significant performance improvement when integrated into existing SJD variants for accelerating autoregressive image generation.

problem: Success conditioning as a policy improvement technique lacks theoretical understanding of what optimization problem it solves and when it provably succeeds.
approach: Proves success conditioning exactly solves a trust-region optimization problem maximizing policy improvement subject to chi-squared divergence constraint, where action-influence measures how random action variation affects success.
contribution: Shows success conditioning is conservative improvement operator that cannot degrade performance, with identity between relative improvement, policy change magnitude, and action-influence at every state.

problem: On-policy reinforcement learning methods like GRPO suffer from mode collapse where solutions concentrate on a single high-reward trajectory and cease exploring alternatives.
approach: Proposes DMPO (Distribution-Matching Policy Optimization) preventing mode collapse through forward KL minimization by constructing group-level target distribution and aligning policy to it.
contribution: Achieves 43.9% Quality Ratio on text-based NP-Bench (vs GRPO's 40.1%) and 43.1% on vision-based NP-Bench (vs 38.4%) with 9% and 12% improvements demonstrating diversity-preserving benefits.

problem: Multi-task instruct-tuning of LLMs suffers from cross-task interference where conflicting gradients on shared parameters degrade performance despite parameter isolation attempts.
approach: Proposes BADIT that decomposes LLM parameters into orthogonal high-singular-value LoRA experts representing basic abilities and dynamically enforces orthogonality via spherical clustering of rank-1 components.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA methods on SuperNI benchmark across 6 LLMs by better mitigating cross-task interference through orthogonal ability decomposition.

problem: LLM unlearning via knowledge deletion suffers from biased deletion that only suppresses token sequences without complete removal, while refusal-based approaches keep underlying knowledge intact risking re-emergence.
approach: Proposes Distinguishable Deletion paradigm restricting response distribution in latent representation rather than specific tokens, combined with Energy-based Unlearning Alignment using energy index to quantify knowledge presence.
contribution: Significantly outperforms previous methods by enabling complete knowledge erasure while distinguishing unlearned from retained content through energy-boundary enforcement.

problem: In low-resource settings where data cannot be pooled and verification uses only fragmented local samples, data selection becomes biased and accelerates model collapse during recursive synthetic-data training.
approach: Theoretically proves siloed selection accelerates collapse and induces power-law diversity decay, then constructs Wasserstein proxy references from multiple silos without sharing raw data.
contribution: Demonstrates collaborative proxy references mitigate diversity degradation better than local-reference selection on skewed distributions.

problem: Standard SGD convergence guarantees degrade on heavy-tailed data where gradients lack finite second moments, even though empirical moments are finite once data is fixed.
approach: Separates data sampling from optimization randomness showing heavy-tailed data induce dataset-dependent noise scaling as N^(2/alpha-1) under tail index alpha, then proves SGD with gradient clipping avoids this growth.
contribution: Provides finite-sum convergence guarantees for SGD with clipping under heavy-tailed data and derives generalization bounds showing tail behavior at population minimizer links optimization and generalization.

problem: Large language models lack capability to handle time-series data natively despite strong performance on multimodal data, limiting their application to medical reasoning with longitudinal and wearable data.
approach: Proposes OpenTSLM family of time series language models integrating time-series as native modality into pretrained LLMs via soft prompting or cross-attention, with three new time-series reasoning datasets.
contribution: Achieves F1 scores of 69.88% in sleep staging and 67.64% in HAR, with cardiologist evaluations confirming strong reasoning on raw ECG data.

problem: Quantization error reconstruction methods allocate entire rank budget to error reconstruction, which is suboptimal when weights have intrinsic low-rank structure that quantization corrupts.
approach: Proposes Structured Residual Reconstruction (SRR) that preserves top-k singular subspace before quantization, quantizes only residual, and uses remaining rank for error reconstruction with theory-guided criterion.
contribution: Achieves consistent perplexity reductions across diverse models with 5.9 percentage-point average gain on GLUE under 2-bit QPEFT.

problem: Video creation systems treat script drafting and key-shot design as disjoint tasks using separate models, limiting narrative coherence and director-like creative control.
approach: Proposes UniMAGE unified director model using Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that unifies text and image generation with interleaved concept learning followed by disentangled expert learning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models generating logically coherent scripts and visually consistent keyframes.

problem: Soft label supervision from teacher models for dataset distillation causes local semantic drift when using limited crops per image, as visually ambiguous crops deviate from image-level ground-truth semantics.
approach: Proposes HALD that uses hard labels as content-invariant semantic anchors hybridized with soft labels to calibrate drift, providing intermediate corrective signals while preserving fine-grained soft label benefits.
contribution: Achieves 42.7% ImageNet-1K accuracy with only 285M soft-label storage (100x reduction) outperforming LPLD by 9.0%.

problem: Masked autoregressive models for text-to-image generation weaken spatial topology by flattening 2D latents into 1D sequences, limiting precise layout alignment for instance-level control.
approach: Proposes StructMAR integrating 2D Rotary Positional Embeddings with Layout-Guided Attention Bias to explicitly bias latent tokens toward layout instances, plus GRPO refinement to align MAR objective with detector-based metrics.
contribution: Achieves 57.2 AP on COCO-Position and 79.4 mIoU, 61.7 ISR on COCO-MIG with 4.05x inference speedup.

problem: Understanding how parameter symmetries relate to neural network phenomena like linear mode connectivity requires clarifying the exact interplay between parameters, data, and learned representations.
approach: Develops theoretical framework of effective function classes (functions a neuron can realize with their norm cost) and formalizes effective symmetry breaking via neuron identifiability across independent training runs.
contribution: Shows neural networks admit large families of approximately equivalent solutions even in structurally asymmetric models and characterizes when representation merging without alignment admits linear low-loss paths.

problem: One-step prediction of unknown marginally stable nonlinear dynamical systems is challenging without understanding how to learn effective mappings from observations.
approach: Describes algorithm based on spectral filtering using spectral representation of systems with online convex optimization for vanishing prediction error on nonexpansive systems.
contribution: Provides theory for spectral filtering on linear dynamical systems incorporating noise correction and asymmetric dynamics with rates governed by control-theoretic notion of learnability.

problem: 3D shape classification methods overlook geometric-topological regularities and symmetry principles intrinsic to CAD boundary representations.
approach: Introduces EquiCAD framework integrating equivariant representations with graph-based reasoning by leveraging group-theoretic decomposition of curve and surface descriptors with hierarchical message passing.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements on SolidLetters, Parts, Machining Feature benchmark, and newly constructed Features dataset over prior state-of-the-art.

problem: High-fidelity point cloud completion and generation rely on long sampling schedules creating substantial inference latency without distillation or rectification trade-offs.
approach: Presents 3D MeanFlow performing one-step average-velocity transport with instantaneous-average consistency objective and shape-level constraint, plus PointPlug for integrating completion into 3D object detectors.
contribution: Achieves one-step sampling with order-of-magnitude speedup while maintaining competitive fidelity, improving evaluated detectors on nuScenes and KITTI.

problem: Existing safety steering methods for defending against jailbreak prompts are supervised and tied to static training sets, failing on unseen out-of-distribution attacks.
approach: Proposes zero-shot defense using unsupervised latent direction discovery to simulate jailbroken activations without knowing jailbreak strategy, combined with bi-level adversarial training steering these states to refusal regions.
contribution: Achieves strong defense with attack success rates mostly below 5% across three LLMs and six classical jailbreak families.

problem: Verifying ensemble properties like robustness or fairness in decision tree ensembles is NP-hard with most research targeting specific verification tasks rather than unified approaches.
approach: Explores ensemble verification through OC-space (set of all possible output combinations) providing unifying view where variety of verification tasks become simple searches answered in linear or quadratic time.
contribution: Shows generic OC-space approach can be faster than task-specific approaches while being flexible for diverse verification objectives.

problem: Integrated Gradients for feature attribution yields unreliable explanations when integration path passes through regions with noisy gradients outside the data manifold.
approach: Proposes Manifold-Aligned Guided Integrated Gradients (MA-GIG) constructing attribution paths in latent space of VAE and decoding intermediate states to bias path toward learned generative manifold.
contribution: Produces faithful explanations by aggregating gradients on path features proximal to input, reducing off-manifold noise and outperforming prior path-based attribution methods.

problem: Time series imputation methods re-discover feature relationships at each layer lacking persistent anchors to maintain consistent representations across network depth.
approach: Proposes HELIX assigning learnable feature identity (persistent embedding) to each feature capturing intrinsic semantic properties throughout network with hybrid temporal-feature attention.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance surpassing 16 baselines on 5 public datasets across 21 experimental settings with learned identities aligning to latent physical and semantic structure.

problem: Object reassembly task in n-dimensional space is invariant to global rigid motions, but training on SE(n)^N is ill-posed because losses penalize different global transforms as distinct.
approach: Proposes SE(n)-invariant framework with Global Gauge Fixing strategy and quotient-invariant Flow Matching objective via orthogonal projection onto horizontal tangent bundle.
contribution: Improves accuracy on polygonal jigsaw puzzles and 3D fracture reassembly benchmarks through construction that factors out global pose at each timestep.

problem: LLM-based formal verification lacks concrete behavioral feedback and treats proof generation as static end-to-end prediction tied to limited training datasets.
approach: Presents ExVerus counterexample-guided framework enabling LLMs to reason about proofs using behavioral feedback via counterexamples and generalize them into inductive invariants.
contribution: Significantly improves proof accuracy, robustness, and token efficiency over state-of-the-art prompting-based Verus proof generator.

problem: Causal language models factorizing sequences using only preceding context leave future information unexploited during training despite its availability.
approach: Introduces Regret Pre-training framework grounded in LUPI paradigm with dual-view architecture generating causal Student and future-conditioned Teacher distributions, transferring future-aware signals via regret loss.
contribution: Achieves 33.9% average accuracy with GlobalRegret and 32.2% with LocalRegret on nine tasks (vs baseline 30.2%), with 18.1 percentage point improvement on BoolQ.

problem: Genome language models fail to capture biological signal when using sequence reconstruction tasks inspired by NLP despite their potential for understanding regulatory genomics.
approach: Introduces pretraining tasks predicting evolutionary rate composable with sequence reconstruction enabling controlled comparison of predicting sequence only, rate only, or both.
contribution: Models pretrained on both sequence and evolutionary rate outperform sequence-only training on biologically grounded benchmarks and variant effect prediction tasks.

problem: Comparing effectiveness of autonomous ML engineering agents is difficult because systems combine different techniques in varying configurations making unclear which components drive performance.
approach: Conducts over 4,000 controlled experiments systematically ablating architectural components with K-live benchmark of 25 active competitions providing contamination-free dynamic evaluation.
contribution: Finds iterative feedback contributes more than architectural complexity and multi-agent coordination can hurt as often as help, providing concrete guidance for practitioners.

problem: High-stakes agent verification for clinical diagnosis lacks domain knowledge and reliable calibration in existing verifiers.
approach: Establishes GLEAN framework compiling expert-curated protocols into trajectory-informed correctness signals via guideline-grounded evidence accumulation with Bayesian logistic regression calibration.
contribution: Surpasses best baseline by 12% in AUROC and 50% in Brier score reduction on agentic clinical diagnosis across three diseases.

problem: Mixture of Experts architectures have unexploited sparsity at tensor and neuron levels during post-training and inference that can improve efficiency.
approach: Proposes complete expert partition for post-training and threshold-based token-expert dropping for inference with dual-threshold approach and partial expert partition for enhanced trade-off.
contribution: Improves Mixtral-8x7B by 1% across nine benchmarks (4% on GSM8K) with 1.19x speedup and 0.5% accuracy gain when combining optimizations.

problem: KV cache eviction methods rely on instantaneous heuristic metrics assuming consistency across attention heads, overlooking heterogeneity in predictive fidelity and long-horizon utility.
approach: Proposes LU-KV formulating head-level budget allocation as global combinatorial optimization to maximize long-horizon marginal contribution using convex-hull relaxation and greedy solver.
contribution: Reduces KV cache by 80% with minimal performance degradation on LongBench and RULER benchmarks while decreasing latency and GPU memory.

problem: Learning hierarchical representations from asymmetric and noisy hierarchical knowledge is difficult because standard embedding methods interfere between semantic meaning and structural relationships.
approach: Polaris uses polar hyperspherical embeddings where angular geometry encodes hierarchy and radius encodes semanticity, employing exponential maps to learn unit-norm representations with structure-guided retrieval.
contribution: Achieves up to ~19 points improvement in top-K retrieval and ~60% reduction in mean rank over baselines across taxonomy expansion tasks.

problem: Existing flow matching and diffusion models for trajectory prediction ignore temporal correlations and spatial symmetries in N-body systems, complicating generation and limiting performance.
approach: GP-EquiFlow integrates vector-valued Gaussian processes to construct SE(3)-equivariant prior distributions that respect both spatial symmetries and temporal dynamics in flow matching.
contribution: Delivers more accurate predictions on N-body and molecular dynamics with fewer sampling steps than baseline flow matching approaches.

problem: Modern vision models rely on pointwise activations and softmax for nonlinearity, but this dependency may be unnecessary and introduces computational overhead.
approach: PolyNeXt replaces activation functions and softmax with Hadamard products to create polynomial alternatives within MetaFormer-style vision backbones (MLPs, convolutions, attention).
contribution: Matches or exceeds activation-based counterparts on ImageNet classification and ADE20K segmentation at multiple scales with reduced computational cost.

problem: Current VLM spatial intelligence benchmarks contain invalid QA pairs due to point-cloud reconstruction artifacts and misaligned annotations with video evidence, and assume full-scene access unavailable in practice.
approach: ReVSI re-annotates 413 scenes across 5 datasets to fix object labels and geometry, regenerates QA pairs with human verification, and provides frame-budget variants to match actual model inputs.
contribution: Enables more reliable and diagnostic assessment of spatial intelligence, revealing systematic VLM failure modes obscured by prior benchmarks.

problem: Variable clustering in multi-factor block models lacks efficient and principled approaches that connect to robust optimization.
approach: Connects variable clustering to regularized subspace clustering through distributionally robust nodewise regression with convex relaxation and ADMM algorithm.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on clustering tasks through a principled, data-driven approach for robust region selection.

problem: Offline LLM-based recommendation using GFlowNets suffers from non-identifiability in Sub-Trajectory Balance due to partial support on the dataset-induced DAG, causing probability mass to allocate to unsupported regions.
approach: CFlower introduces a conservative SubTB objective that explicitly penalizes unsupported forward flow mass and combines dataset-constrained policy learning with on-policy sampling on the dataset DAG.
contribution: Improves distributional matching and delivers stronger accuracy-exposure trade-off than GFlowNet and SFT baselines on Amazon recommendation datasets.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs carries substantial latency and compute costs, but the fundamental question of how many reasoning tokens are necessary as input size grows remains unanswered.
approach: Extends the bounded attention prefix oracle (BAPO) model to prove lower bounds on CoT tokens for binary majority, triplet matching, and graph reachability, showing Omega(n) scaling.
contribution: Identifies fundamental bottlenecks in inference-time compute through CoT, with empirical validation on frontier models showing linear reasoning token scaling.

problem: Monitoring treatment effects in online experiments with delayed outcomes and staggered entry requires robust methods that handle asynchronous potential outcome times and environmental nonstationarity.
approach: Adopts design-based perspective with carefully chosen arm-specific event-time filtrations to construct confidence sequences for treatment effects using arm-level IPW estimation.
contribution: Enables anytime-valid inference for delayed outcomes while outperforming traditional design-based variance bounds.

problem: Existing panoramic image editing methods fail to preserve global consistency because they ignore spherical geometry and use perspective-based approaches or cube-map decompositions.
approach: World-Shaper reformulates editing directly in equirectangular projection with distortion-aware attention modulation, layered shape loss, and curriculum training to internalize panoramic priors.
contribution: Achieves superior geometric consistency and editing fidelity on a new PEBench benchmark compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Probabilistic forecasting with exogenous variables faces topological disparity in sampling initialization and spurious covariate correlations during iterative generation, limiting robustness.
approach: KITE introduces a History-Conditional Manifold for informative sampling initialization and a Knowledge-Guided Conditioning module using statistical priors to regularize variable interactions.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting with exogenous variables.

problem: Distributionally robust assortment optimization under the contextual MNL model requires algorithms that handle worst-case distributional deviations across multiple divergence measures.
approach: Leverages strong duality from distributionally robust optimization integrated into assortment procedures to develop polynomial-time algorithms for TV, KL, and chi-square divergences.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis and establishes sample complexity bounds for all three robust MNL formulations.

problem: Video LLMs struggle with complex events requiring integrated spatial and temporal reasoning, and existing methods handle either dimension in isolation.
approach: VideoLoom uses a curated character-centric dataset with temporally grounded and spatially localized captions to train a unified Video LLM for joint spatial-temporal understanding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on spatial and temporal benchmarks with a novel metric for comprehensive evaluation.
