problem: Language models are sensitive to single-token changes at high-uncertainty points, but the geometric basis of this sensitivity remains unclear.
approach: Derives an so(n)-valued 1-form depending only on token embedding geometry and shows its curvature is semantically meaningful through chess reasoning task analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates that token space geometry directly reflects internal problem representations, with transformations clustering by board region and piece importance.

problem: Gaussian Belief Propagation approximations lack theoretical guarantees for complex, loopy, non-Gaussian factor graphs despite being widely used in practice.
approach: Leverages Central Limit Theorem to prove that variable beliefs under BP converge to Gaussian distributions in sparsely-connected factor graphs obeying key assumptions.
contribution: Provides mathematical guarantee for when Gaussian approximations are valid, confirmed experimentally on stereo depth estimation.

problem: Tracking text in videos faces severe geometric distortions from perspective shifts, visual ambiguity across instances, and sensitivity to structural details—problems not addressed by general object trackers.
approach: SymTrack proposes a detection-free framework with Cross-Expert Calibration to reduce bias and Predictive Token Rectification to correct structural imbalances.
contribution: Sets state-of-the-art on three benchmarks with up to 11.97% AUC improvement, enabling practical video text manipulation.

problem: Evaluating music-dance co-generation requires measuring rhythmic coupling at fine temporal resolution, a dimension not captured by generic audiovisual metrics.
approach: TMD-Bench integrates computable physical metrics with perceptual judgments via a rhythm-aligned dataset and fine-grained Music Captioner for structured semantics.
contribution: Reveals that commercial audio-visual models produce high-quality outputs but leave rhythmic coupling suboptimal, establishing evaluation standard for music-dance generation.

problem: Learning reward functions from human preference feedback requires accuracy across the entire state-action space for safety and transferability, not just on visited states.
approach: Derives minimum interaction requirements for compatible reward identification under deterministic preferences and formalizes connections to the Bradley-Terry model for stochastic preferences.
contribution: Establishes theoretical foundations for online compatible reward identification with characterization of problem complexity and sample efficiency.

problem: On-robot deployment of VLA models is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy constraints across heterogeneous edge accelerators.
approach: Provides systematic co-characterization via Cost-Energy-Time (CET) leaderboard and uncovers two-phase inference pattern (compute-bound VLM, memory-bound Action Expert), proposing DP-Cache and V-AEFusion for acceleration.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.9x speedup on GPUs and 6x on edge NPUs with only marginal degradation, showing edge devices can be more efficient than flagship GPUs.

problem: Existing multi-concept unlearning methods fail to remove multiple concepts from diffusion models without significant quality degradation or high hyperparameter sensitivity.
approach: FIA leverages model sparsity to identify Concept Sensitive Neurons via Contrastive Concept Saliency and Concept Agnostic Neurons, creating unified multi-concept masks.
contribution: Achieves more reliable multi-concept unlearning while maintaining generation fidelity with training-free, plug-and-play application.

problem: Diffusion LLMs face accuracy-parallelism trade-off where aggressive parallel decoding (high TPF) degrades task accuracy, limiting practical deployment.
approach: LightningRL uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with per-reward decoupling, NLL regularization, and dynamic TPF-aware filtering to optimize for both accuracy and parallelism.
contribution: Advances Pareto frontier across math and code tasks with average TPF of 7.3 while maintaining competitive accuracy.

problem: Optimal experimental design for MNL bandits is computationally intractable due to the combinatorial action space, lacking efficient algorithms with statistical guarantees.
approach: Proposes computationally efficient framework via 0-1 MILP reformulation with solver-certified stopping and fully polynomial-time lifted design using tractable surrogate objectives.
contribution: Establishes near G-optimality guarantees and instance-dependent sample complexity of O(d log N / Delta^2) for best assortment identification.

problem: Preference alignment for LLMs requires costly high-quality positive examples and intensive computation, motivating more efficient alternatives.
approach: U2A links preference alignment with LLM unlearning via bi-level optimization to quantify effects of negative example unlearning and select examples optimally.
contribution: Demonstrates cost-efficient preference alignment through selective unlearning of negative examples.

problem: Detecting AI-generated images is insufficient without addressing visible artifacts and restoration, leaving a disconnect between detection and practical correction.
approach: GenShield proposes unified autoregressive framework with Visual Chain-of-Thought curriculum learning for explainable AIGI detection and controllable artifact correction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on AIGI detection benchmarks while enabling high-quality artifact correction with explicit stopping criteria.

problem: Nonparametric IV regression using spectral features fails when the true causal function is poorly represented by dominant singular components.
approach: Augmented Spectral Feature Learning makes feature learning outcome-aware via contrastive loss from an augmented operator incorporating outcome information.
contribution: Maintains effectiveness under spectral misalignment through task-specific feature learning.

problem: PINNs training is paralyzed by gradient pathology where PDE residuals and boundary constraints generate opposing gradients that trap the model in local minima.
approach: CAML reformulates zeroth-order terms into aligned constraints and introduces delay factors to help the optimizer skip high-curvature regions.
contribution: Significantly enhances numerical stability and efficiency in complex PINN problems.

problem: Standard zeroth-order gradient estimators suffer from O(r^2) truncation bias at smoothing radius r and bias-reduction schemes typically increase variance.
approach: Romberg-ZOGE forms Romberg-extrapolated linear combinations at radii {r/2^k} with reused perturbation direction, achieving O(r^{2R+2}) bias while preserving leading variance.
contribution: Demonstrates faster and more stable zeroth-order SGD on synthetic benchmarks, simulator-based wireless optimization, and black-box prompt tuning.

problem: Rubric-based LLM evaluation benchmarks lack systematic robustness validation, potentially tolerating significant semantic failures and irrelevant content additions.
approach: RubricRobustness applies systematic sensitivity analysis with semantic negation, stochastic deletion, and irrelevant addition perturbations to HealthBench and WildBench.
contribution: Reveals systematic vulnerabilities in popular benchmarks and establishes perturbation-based sensitivity analysis as prerequisite for evaluation validity.

problem: MLLMs in stateless systems are vulnerable to semantic-aware attacks where a single perturbation hijacks multiple decisions without model-specific tuning.
approach: SAUP acts as semantic router using theoretical analysis of latent space geometry to guide SORT optimization and annotates fine-grained semantic dataset.
contribution: Achieves 66% attack success rate on five targets using single frame against Qwen, exposing fundamental feasibility of semantic-aware hijacking.

problem: Ultra-high-resolution video generation requires handling compounded motion modeling, semantic planning, and detail synthesis simultaneously with prohibitive memory and computation.
approach: LUVE employs three-stage architecture: low-resolution motion generation, latent-space upsampling, and high-resolution refinement with dual frequency experts.
contribution: Achieves superior photorealism and content fidelity in UHR video generation.

problem: Unbalanced incomplete multi-view clustering is hindered by observation bias where missing patterns vary across views, causing learned associations to fail on incomplete samples.
approach: CIMLN uses context-aware meta-generation for view recovery and causal-invariant structure learning via counterfactual masking to enforce consistency across observation patterns.
contribution: Effectively alleviates observation bias for unbalanced incomplete multi-view clustering.

problem: Long-sequence modeling faces fundamental trade-off between fixed-size compressive memory (RNN efficiency) and lossless growing memory (Transformer fidelity).
approach: Artificial Hippocampus Networks maintain sliding KV cache as short-term memory while learnable AHN recurrently compresses out-of-window information into fixed compact long-term memory.
contribution: Outperforms sliding window and full-attention models with 40.5% inference FLOP reduction and 74% memory cache reduction on LV-Eval and InfiniteBench.

problem: Skill-based agent systems introduce unexamined security attack surface where backdoors can be embedded at skill level and propagated through skill composition.
approach: SkillTrojan embeds malicious logic in skill implementations, partitions encrypted payload across benign-looking invocations, and provides automated synthesis of backdoored skills.
contribution: Achieves 97.2% attack success rate while maintaining 89.3% clean accuracy on EHR SQL, exposing critical blind spot in skill-based agent architectures.

problem: Standard attention mechanisms treat scores as probability distributions, but dynamic MLP perspective reveals this may not be the optimal framing for autoregressive sequence modeling.
approach: HyperMLP/HyperGLU view attention heads as dynamic two-layer MLPs whose weights come from context history, using reverse-offset layout to align temporal mixing with autoregressive semantics.
contribution: Consistently outperforms softmax-attention baselines under matched parameter budgets.

problem: MoE architectures suffer from poor expert specialization where experts share overlapping spectral components and dominant gradient subspaces, limiting effective capacity.
approach: SD-MoE decomposes parameters and gradients in spectral space to separate dominant components and prevent gating from routing along shared directions.
contribution: Improves performance with effective expert specialization and minimal computation overhead, seamlessly integrating into Qwen and DeepSeek.

problem: Autonomous AI scientists bottlenecked by labor-intensive generation of publication-ready academic illustrations for research workflows.
approach: PaperBanana orchestrates specialized agents for reference retrieval, content/style planning, image rendering, and iterative refinement via self-critique using VLMs and image generation.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on PaperBananaBench (292 NeurIPS cases) in faithfulness, conciseness, readability, and aesthetics.

problem: Dropout scheduling is typically constant, but standard practice may suboptimally utilize dropout's regularization potential under fixed computational budget.
approach: Mean-field theory at edge of chaos shows dropout shifts perfect-alignment fixed point, enabling front-loaded schedules via critical scaling laws for smooth and kinked activations.
contribution: Front-loaded dropout schedules cut test loss by 18-35% over constant dropout in MLPs and Vision Transformers with no additional cost.

problem: Standard metrics like perplexity fail to guide mid-training toward SWE-bench performance due to long-context tax and weak downstream correlation.
approach: HE-SNR redefines intelligence via entropy-compression into low-order states and validates this metric on models up to 560B parameters across 32K/128K context windows.
contribution: Provides theoretical foundation and practical tools for optimizing LLM latent potential in complex engineering domains.

problem: Reconstructing RAW sensor data from RGB requires bridging information loss and complex ISP transformations—generative models are high-quality but slow; regression is fast but over-smooths.
approach: SHADE uses single-step deterministic flow with Homogeneous Representation Alignment via student-teacher DINO for alignment in shared feature space.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks with efficient and accurate sensor data reconstruction.

problem: Diffusion models designed for dense data waste computation on mostly-zero entries and erase sparsity patterns when applied to sparse continuous data.
approach: Sparsity-Exploiting Diffusion models only non-zero values, skipping zeros during training and inference while preserving sparsity.
contribution: Matches or surpasses conventional DMs and domain-specific baselines on physics and biology benchmarks with computational savings.

problem: Looping (layer reuse across depth) and depth growing (shallow-to-deep training) both improve reasoning but their relationship is unclear.
approach: Provides mechanistic unification showing looped and depth-grown models exhibit convergent depth-wise signatures with increased late-layer reliance and recurring patterns.
contribution: Shows inference-time looping on depth-grown models improves accuracy on reasoning primitives by up to 2x despite no loop training.

problem: LLM guardrails are vulnerable to spatially-structured perturbations that allow harmful content to bypass output safety mechanisms.
approach: SpatialJB exploits the Transformer's spatial weakness by disrupting output generation with structured tokens to bypass guardrails without detection.
contribution: Achieves nearly 100% attack success rate on leading LLMs and maintains >75% success against advanced guardrails like OpenAI Moderation API.

problem: Decentralized multi-agent RL faces tension between exploration bonuses and coordination consistency over communication graphs.
approach: IEC couples exploration and coordination through a single constrained objective using information gain and state-coverage novelty with spectral smoothness penalty on neighbors, optimized via primal-dual updates.
contribution: Achieves superior performance across three benchmarks with automatic shift from exploration to stable cooperative conventions.

problem: Active regression for single-index models with unknown Lipschitz link functions under general p-norm loss remains challenging.
approach: Present non-adaptive sampling algorithm achieving (1+epsilon)-approximation with query complexity O(d^(p/2 v 1) / epsilon^(p v 2) polylog(n/epsilon)); establish nearly tight lower bounds for p>2.
contribution: Closes remaining gaps in active ell-p regression theory for single-index models with unknown link functions.

problem: Deep learning models for MS/HS fusion are designed for fixed spectral bands and spatial scales, limiting transferability across sensors.
approach: SSA uses Matryoshka Kernel enabling variable spectral band processing and Implicit Neural Representation backbone for arbitrary spatial resolution reconstruction.
contribution: Single model achieves SOTA, generalizes to unseen scales, and transfers to unseen sensors with few-step adaptation.

problem: Single fixed discount factor limits RL performance by failing to balance short-term and long-term planning in complex tasks.
approach: Multi-timescale critic framework with distinct discount factors for each Q-value component; Neural Reward Decoder reconstructs reward sequences and cross-attention Q-weight predictor adapts weights.
contribution: Significantly outperforms SOTA on DMControl and CARLA; works with both off-policy (SAC, DrQ-v2) and on-policy (PPO) algorithms.

problem: Test-time scaling methods allocate same compute budget per prompt despite varying complexity, leading to inefficiency.
approach: EAGer uses token-wise entropy distribution to branch only on high-entropy tokens and reallocate saved compute to instances needing exploration.
contribution: Achieves up to +37% Pass@k and 59% fewer tokens with labels; +12% Pass@k and 64% fewer tokens in test-time setting on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation is limited by CLIP's spatial bias and semantic ambiguity in text queries.
approach: VIP rectifies semantic expressiveness using visual-guided prompt evolution with alias expansion and visual-guided distillation aggregated in saliency-aware manner.
contribution: Surpasses top methods by 1.4-8.4% mIoU, generalizes to diverse domains, requires marginal inference overhead.

contribution: Framework is interpretable, robust, computationally efficient; establishes equivalence to local neighborhood alignment via Mutual Nearest Neighbors.

problem: Performative learning where distribution reacts to deployed model needs to account for unknown distribution shifts caused by strategic users.
approach: Study regularization impact in high-dimensional ridge regression under performative effects; show optimal regularization scales with performative effect strength.
contribution: Demonstrates in over-parameterized regime, performativity enables reduced variance via optimal regularization, improving performance.

problem: Large audio language models expanded attack surface for jailbreak vulnerabilities.
approach: Acoustic Interference Attack leverages acoustic latent semantics to create universal jailbreak triggers that interfere with safety alignment without semantic payload.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art attack success rate across 10 LALMs and identifies fundamental vulnerability in cross-modal alignment.

problem: RL algorithms like GRPO use coarse-grained credit assignment where all tokens receive same reward, limiting reasoning improvement.
approach: GTPO assigns entropy-weighted reward to each token and synthesizes token-specific advantage functions; GRPO-S applies same design at sequence level.
contribution: Establishes SOTA on AIME and MATH 500, outperforming prior entropy-guided baselines.

problem: Naive continual distillation in frontier regime yields limited gains or degradation as training bottlenecks stifle yet-to-learn tokens.
approach: T3S reconstructs training objective at token level via training-trajectory-aware selection, separating imitation-anchor tokens from yet-to-learn tokens.
contribution: Qwen3-8B surpasses DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-32B approaches Qwen3-235B, LLaDA-2.0-Mini exceeds baseline, all SOTA among 16B-scale no-think models.

problem: Schema-derived graphs for relational deep learning suffer from information overload and semantic fragmentation that hinder GNN reasoning.
approach: Structural optimizer applies both filtering and injection operations adapted automatically to tasks; balances removing irrelevant structure and injecting task-aligned connectivity.
contribution: Optimized graphs improve accuracy on 23 tasks spanning classification, regression, recommendation while often reducing inference cost.

problem: Learnware specifications reveal capability-relevant information to identify helpful models, but risk exposing sensitive training data properties.
approach: Formalizes learnware-inversion as statistical decision games with risk measured as incremental Bayes value, deriving risk bounds for reduced kernel mean embedding specifications through RKHS-smoothed analysis.
contribution: First framework analyzing specification privacy risk in learnware, proving that properly-sized RKME specifications introduce negligible privacy risk while retaining sufficient identification information.

problem: Multimodal LLMs allow adversaries to distribute malicious intent across modalities to evade unimodal safeguards.
approach: Proposes FlowGuard, monitoring internal cross-modal consistency during multimodal fusion via Partial Information Decomposition to detect harmful inputs when text-only and vision-only reasoning diverge.
contribution: Reduces Attack Success Rates from >90% to <15% on unseen attacks with <3% utility loss and 6× latency reduction by detecting cross-modal fusion inconsistencies.

problem: Few-shot learning support sets quickly constructed with noise; even single noisy samples distort class distributions and reduce generalization in data-scarce settings.
approach: Detects noisy samples via low-rank anomalies in semantic feature space, then uses rank-guided diffusion to generate high-quality replacements under low-rank constraints.
contribution: Significantly reduces errors under noise levels up to 40% across MiniImageNet and TieredImageNet by mitigating prototype drift through low-rank geometry.

problem: Data selection for downstream tasks lacks theoretical grounding; existing methods treat valuation and selection separately without principled connection.
approach: Reformulates data selection as sequential decision-making where optimal sequences arise from dynamic programming; reinterprets existing methods like Data Shapley as myopic approximations.
contribution: Unifies existing data valuation methods through DP lens and proposes bipartite-graph surrogate enabling scalable greedy selection with provable guarantees.

problem: Model-based offline RL suffers from compounding errors during repeated model inference; geometric horizon models struggle with distant future state prediction.
approach: Introduces universal horizon models generalizing geometric horizon models to directly predict future states under arbitrary horizons with winsorized horizon distribution for training stability.
contribution: Outperforms competitive baselines on 100 OGBench tasks, particularly on highly suboptimal datasets requiring long-horizon reasoning.

problem: Private hypothesis selection requires either expensive exponential mechanism with pairwise comparisons or sub-optimal statistical rates.
approach: Designs score function based on small set of strong hypotheses enabling efficient evaluation without pairwise comparisons, reducing computational overhead significantly.
contribution: Achieves near-optimal statistical rates while running in nearly linear time in number of hypotheses under differential privacy constraints.

problem: LLM agents struggle with knowledge-intensive real-world optimization problems requiring domain expertise and appropriate mathematical techniques.
approach: Opt-Miner learns to identify missing knowledge, retrieve technical documents, and ground models via tree-guided data synthesis and retrieval-based group relative policy optimization.
contribution: Opt-Miner-Qwen3-8B achieves performance comparable to 32B specialized agents on complex multi-domain problems by active information seeking.

problem: Training coding agents specialized to private codebases is too costly and complex despite open-weight models' theoretical advantage.
approach: SERA generates thousands of synthetic trajectories via Soft Verified Generation without unit tests, then applies supervised finetuning on 200K+ synthetic trajectories.
contribution: 26x cheaper than RL and 57x cheaper than prior synthetic data methods while matching open-weight models; enables rapid creation of specialized agents.

problem: Learning factorial action policies from preference data ignores strategic interdependence; existing conjoint analyses average over opponent attributes.
approach: Learns stochastic interventions optimizing expected outcomes in average-case and minimax settings; extends to two-player adversarial selection capturing strategic simultaneous choice.
contribution: Adversarially-learned policies produce restricted-equilibrium vote shares aligning with historical election ranges, outperforming non-adversarial baselines.

problem: Why contrastive learning with simple images and augmentations yields useful representations for downstream tasks remains unexplained theoretically.
approach: Analytically computes optimal representations under contrastive loss for various augmentations; shows optimum attained by CNNs with sinusoid filters followed by nonlinearity and whitening.
contribution: Optimal weights form sinusoids whose frequencies can be computed via waterfilling algorithm; empirical CNNs trained with SGD learn these sinusoid patterns.

problem: Unknown transformations distort observations in machine learning and scientific modeling; recovering inverse transformations requires handling complex group structure.
approach: Models transformation posterior as Boltzmann distribution; introduces diffusion process on Lie groups with trivialized target-score identity enabling efficient sampling on-manifold.
contribution: TIED restores transformed inputs to training distribution at test time, improving robustness on image homographies and PDE symmetries over canonicalization baselines.

problem: Learning from label proportions with aggregate label information lacks low-variance debiasing methods supporting diverse loss functions.
approach: Introduces versatile low-variance debiasing methodology accommodating broad spectrum of practically relevant losses across binary and multi-class settings.
contribution: Improves sample complexity guarantees for large class of losses and validates empirical efficacy across diverse benchmarks over standard baselines.

problem: Irregular multivariate time series forecasting challenged by non-uniform sampling and asynchronicity violating equidistant assumptions of standard models.
approach: TFMixer uses learnable Non-Uniform Discrete Fourier Transform to extract spectral representations from irregular timestamps; fuses time and frequency domains.
contribution: Effectively forecasts irregular time series under non-uniform sampling and missing data; explicit seasonal extrapolation via inverse NUDFT.

problem: Robust RL under average-reward criterion lacks model-free algorithms with finite sample complexity analysis in data-limited scenarios.
approach: Proposes Robust Halpern Iteration with K-order multi-level Monte-Carlo estimator for accurate worst-case performance; instantiates for multiple uncertainty models.
contribution: Achieves ε-optimal robust policy with sample complexity of Õ(SAH²/ε^(2+o(1))) asymptotically matching best robust average-reward RL complexity.

problem: Grokking phenomenon where models suddenly generalize long after overfitting remains poorly understood mechanistically.
approach: Through mechanistic analysis finds grokking driven by structural reorganization of token representations; proposes R2G Loss enforcing repulsion on representation manifold.
contribution: R2G Loss enhances model efficiency via angular reorganization verified theoretically and empirically across algorithmic and linguistic tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLM architectures trade off training and inference efficiency; embedding space alignment is inference-inefficient while cross-attention is training-inefficient.
approach: NAEViT eliminates visual token attention interactions; SAISA aligns visual features with input spaces of attention blocks, reducing computational overhead in attention and FFNs.
contribution: SAISA achieves superior performance with significantly reduced computational costs across various baseline models, sizes, and training datasets.

problem: LLMs struggle detecting malicious behaviors fragmented across files when intricate dependencies are lost in vast amounts of benign code.
approach: Parses project into code graph, encodes nodes with semantic/structural signals, trains GNN under sparse supervision, guides LLM attention to identified key sections.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing approaches on multiple datasets while reducing interference from irrelevant context and maintaining low annotation costs.

problem: FFT-based pansharpening methods ignore spectral coordinate structure and radially-decaying energy distribution inherent in frequency-domain representations.
approach: Generalizes classical Butterworth filter into anisotropic learnable frequency-domain gating mechanism serving as efficient self-attention alternative.
contribution: ABFNet achieves state-of-the-art pansharpening performance with low computational overhead; superior CIFAR-100 classification validates broader applicability.

problem: Diffusion transformers for video generation suffer from prohibitive computational cost of spatiotemporal 3D full attention despite its quadratic complexity.
approach: DFSAttn provides training-free sparse attention with Hilbert curve token reordering for fine-grained sparsity, hierarchical block scoring, and adaptive sparse mask caching.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.1× end-to-end speedup while maintaining high generation quality under high sparsity ratios.

problem: Scaling LLM theorem provers challenged by training-time RL inefficiency and inference-time computational constraints on search.
approach: Multi-turn off-policy RL with expert iteration and adaptive filtering; planner-enhanced multi-agent system decomposes theorems hierarchically with proof cache sharing.
contribution: BFS-Prover-V2 achieves 95.08% on miniF2F and 41.4% on ProofNet test sets via scalable dual approach to training and inference.

problem: Federated learning for pathology deployment faces heterogeneity from diverse MIL architectures and heterogeneous feature extractors across institutions.
approach: FedHD performs local Gaussian-mixture feature alignment via distillation; generates synthetic counterparts for each slide to preserve diagnostic diversity.
contribution: Architecture-agnostic, privacy-preserving framework outperforms federated and distillation baselines on TCGA-IDH, CAMELYON16, CAMELYON17.

problem: NVIDIA's 2:4 Sparse Tensor Cores demand strict 50% pruning causing severe accuracy loss; milder patterns like 6:8 receive no hardware support.
approach: SlideSparse rewrites (2N-2):2N weight blocks into overlapping 2:4-compliant windows via Sliding Window Decomposition; fuses activation rearrangement into quantization.
contribution: 1.33× speedup matches theoretical upper-bound N/(N-1)=4/3 at 6:8 sparsity; enables better accuracy-speedup tradeoffs for LLM acceleration.

problem: Embodied agents need skill grounding across different embodiments and environments but LLMs impractical while small LMs insufficient for effective grounding.
approach: RECENT decouples skill semantics from embodiment-specific execution binding via code refactoring; modifies execution bindings rather than regenerating code.
contribution: Achieves best sLM-based Code-as-Policies performance matching LLM-based CaP across diverse robot embodiments in dynamic environments.

problem: Continuous-time event-native SNNs impose inherently sequential spike processing and require precise spike times without time bins, hindering practical training.
approach: Uses parallel associative scans to consume multiple spikes concurrently with exact hard-reset dynamics; implements differentiable spike time solvers to machine precision.
contribution: Yields up to 44× speedups over sequential simulation while retaining exact dynamics; enables end-to-end training on event-based datasets on GPUs.

problem: Existing evaluation systems neither capture human-in-the-loop coding nor adequately measure AI-human collaboration value.
approach: CentaurEval introduces Collaboration-Necessary templates intractable for standalone LLMs or humans but solvable through effective collaboration.
contribution: While LLMs/humans alone achieve poor rates (0.67% and 18.89%), human-AI collaboration improves to 31.11% under strategic intervention.

problem: Computing optimal k-query quantum ordered search beyond k=6 intractable; existing solvers require explicit large constraint matrices.
approach: Introduces matrix-free GPU SDP framework evaluating structured OSP constraints on-the-fly via custom CUDA kernels reducing memory from quadratic to linear.
contribution: Provides strong evidence k=6 optimal list size ≥90,000, improving query coefficient from 0.390 to 0.365; rigorously certifies N* < 94,000.

problem: 3D molecule generation via transformers challenged by SE(3)-equivariance requirements and permutation invariance plus continuous 3D coordinate modeling.
approach: InertialAR performs generation-oriented canonical tokenization via inertial frames; proposes geometric positional encoding enabling 3D geometric awareness in attention.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 8/10 metrics for unconditional generation; significantly outperforms on controllable generation for targeted chemical functionality.

problem: Data diversity measured via text metrics provides weak signals for task-relevant features determining downstream LLM performance.
approach: Introduces Feature Activation Coverage measuring diversity in interpretable feature space; uses sparse autoencoder to identify missing features then synthesizes samples.
contribution: Consistently improves data diversity and downstream performance on instruction following, toxicity detection, reward modeling, behavior steering.

problem: Diffusion model sampling requires many steps to achieve small error; complexity bounds for log-concave sampling lack exponential improvement in error.
approach: Presents algorithms achieving δ-error in polylog(1/δ) steps with Õ(δ)-accurate score estimates; complexity Õ(d polylog(1/δ)) under minimal assumptions.
contribution: Exponential improvement over prior results; first polylog(1/δ) sampler for log-concave distributions using only gradient evaluations.

problem: LLM agents deployed on sensitive tasks risk privacy violations from implicitly contextual information without external safeguards.
approach: PrivAct internalizes contextual privacy preservation via multi-agent learning by embedding privacy preferences into each agent's generation behavior.
contribution: Reduces leakage rates by up to 12.32% while maintaining comparable helpfulness; demonstrates generalization and robustness across diverse multi-agent topologies.

problem: Existing SOR methods model ranking deterministically ignoring variability and stochasticity of human attention shifts.
approach: ProbSOR incorporates probabilistic attention via Group Relative Policy Optimization built on vision-language model with new metrics for probabilistic rankings.
contribution: Demonstrates strong performance in salient object ranking; constructs 15,000-sample ProbSOR dataset supporting probabilistic ranking training and evaluation.

problem: Multi-agent protocol selection lacks standardized evaluation; choice of protocol significantly influences system behavior but remains intuition-driven.
approach: ProtocolBench systematically compares protocols on task success, end-to-end latency, message overhead, and robustness; proposes lightweight ProtocolRouter selector.
contribution: Demonstrates 36.5% variation in completion time across protocols; ProtocolRouter reduces Fail-Storm recovery by 18.1% versus best single-protocol baseline.

problem: Long-horizon language agent RL training suffers from credit misattribution where early correct actions penalized by terminal failures and sample inefficiency.
approach: BEACON leverages compositional task structure via milestone-guided credit assignment; applies temporal reward shaping within segments and dual-scale advantage estimation.
contribution: On long-horizon ALFWorld tasks achieves 92.9% success nearly doubling GRPO's 53.5% while improving sample utilization from 23.7% to 82.0%.

problem: Langevin Monte Carlo sampling from high-dimensional distributions requires many iterations; existing Runge-Kutta LMC requires three gradient evaluations per step.
approach: Proposes higher-order Hessian-free stochastic Runge-Kutta LMC of strong order 1.5 requiring only two gradient evaluations; analyzes under log-smooth conditions.
contribution: Derives uniform-in-time convergence rate O(d^1.5 h^1.5) in non-log-concave settings, matching prior work under log-concavity; reduces computational cost.

problem: Implicit in-context learning relies on task-specific alignment limiting generalizability; existing approaches lack structural ICL understanding.
approach: In-Context Routing extracts reusable structural directions emerging during ICL; employs learnable input-conditioned router modulating attention logits.
contribution: Consistently outperforms implicit ICL methods across 12 datasets; demonstrates robust generalization to out-of-domain tasks where task-specific methods struggle.

problem: Math reasoning improvements in LLMs may reflect narrow overfitting rather than broader problem-solving ability with unclear transfer to other domains.
approach: Evaluates 20+ reasoning-tuned models across math, scientific QA, coding, planning, instruction-following; identifies on-policy fine-tuning as key transfer mechanism.
contribution: Shows on-policy RL preserves general-domain structure while off-policy SFT induces representation/output drift; on-policy methods transfer better regardless of training signal.

problem: Workflow optimization via global graph search collapses multi-step failure traces to binary outcomes obscuring recurring failure structure.
approach: Reframes as distributional refinement over Failure Signature Space; CE-Graph maintains counterexample pool, estimates dense failure modes via Propose-and-Verify loop.
contribution: Improves robustness while reducing optimization cost versus workflow-search baselines; suggests reliability emerges from reshaping failure landscapes.

problem: Selecting reasoning data for distillation via full-trajectory scoring fails scaling to long traces from diverse teachers.
approach: Proposes Local Average Log Probability scoring each step via small preceding context window measuring justification by immediate premises rather than global fluency.
contribution: LALP enables selecting best teacher and curating diverse pools; improves accuracy selecting natural solutions by large margin across math, coding, science tasks.

problem: KL-regularized zero-sum Markov games lack algorithms with improved sample efficiency and theoretical benefits despite empirical success in alignment.
approach: OMG and SOMG use best response sampling with optimistic/superoptimistic bonuses; achieve logarithmic regret scaling inversely with regularization strength β.
contribution: Logarithmic regret in T with Õ(√T) traditional regret scaling, achieving β^(-1) dependence showing KL regularization provides theoretical sample advantage.

problem: Large-scale retrieval systems degrade under distributional shifts; retraining retriever or re-embedding corpus prohibitively expensive.
approach: GRAPE leverages LLM-based query rewriting via Grouped Relative Policy Optimization with ranking signals; addresses score inflation via corpus-relative ranking-based reward.
contribution: Consistently improves performance across multilingual, long-form, multimodal benchmarks; average Recall@10 gain of 4.9% without retriever modification.

problem: Learning robot control from videos is limited because existing methods treat video as passive kinematic data and fail to capture dynamic interactions with the environment.
approach: TRIP extracts interaction-based action primitives from unlabeled game videos and aligns video-domain features with target-domain observations through a shared latent space to enable transfer of video-mined strategies to RL policies.
contribution: Demonstrates significant improvements in task performance, sample efficiency, and robustness on complex terrain navigation by grounding interaction primitives from game videos into humanoid locomotion control.

problem: Supervised CNNs solve imaging inverse problems effectively but remain poorly understood theoretically, often treated as black boxes.
approach: Analyzes trained CNNs through the lens of the constrained Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimator that captures translation equivariance and finite receptive fields, deriving an analytic formula called Local-Equivariant MMSE.
contribution: Provides interpretable, tractable formulas for CNN inverse problem solvers that match neural network outputs across denoising, inpainting, and deconvolution tasks with PSNR ≥ 25 dB.

problem: Strategic classification systems must balance optimality with fairness when agents strategically adapt their features, but existing models focus solely on accuracy without considering desirability and fairness tradeoffs.
approach: Frames strategic classification as a constrained optimization problem capturing tradeoffs between optimality, desirability (which feature changes are acceptable), and fairness across heterogeneous agents.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on the principal's optimality loss under desirability fairness constraints for multiple fairness measures and demonstrates explicit tradeoffs via experiments on real datasets.

problem: Graph Foundation Models trained with prompts embedded in source domains fail to generalize to other domains and different GFMs, and existing methods neglect unlabeled target domain test data.
approach: GFMate introduces pre-training-agnostic centroid and layer prompts applied at test-time with a complementary learning objective that exploits both labeled and unlabeled target domain data.
contribution: Achieves improvements of up to 30.63% on 12 benchmark datasets by enabling test-time prompt tuning independent of source domain embedding and model pre-training strategy.

problem: Neural scaling laws reveal universal behavior in high-dimensional learning but lack principled understanding of how training dynamics produce these effects.
approach: Develops a dynamical mean-field theory framework that unifies Bayesian inference, gradient flow, and Langevin training by decomposing dynamics into independent eigenmodes coupled through collective response functions.
contribution: Quantitatively explains neural scaling laws and early stopping effects by linking spectral and dynamical properties of learning on power-law data via effective low-dimensional order parameters.

problem: Thompson sampling in linear-Gaussian bandits exhibits regret that couples prior-dependent burn-in with minimax long-run terms, limiting understanding of prior effects.
approach: Proves that Thompson sampling achieves Bayesian regret with an additive decoupling of burn-in term O(d r sqrt(Tr(Σ₀))) and minimax term O(σ d sqrt(T)) via a new elliptical potential lemma.
contribution: Establishes that the prior-dependent burn-in term is unavoidable and decouples multiplicatively from long-run regret, contradicting previous bounds.

problem: Interactive segmentation requires regional refinement near user clicks but existing methods either use time-consuming two-stage pipelines or preset fixed focus regions that fail to adapt to click position and object geometry.
approach: EFPNet outputs a refined mask end-to-end by deducing precise focus regions based on max-connected components and integrating feedback through image, feature, and mask affinity with a clicked-with-focus mechanism.
contribution: Demonstrates outstanding performance on four benchmarks for both efficacy and computational efficiency in interactive segmentation.

problem: IC footprint geometry labeling requires precise visual perception of unstructured technical drawings, but existing Large Multimodal Models lack accurate geometric perception capabilities.
approach: LMM4-IC4K treats IC mechanical drawings as images and fine-tunes LMMs for structured geometric interpretation using a two-stage training framework and the ICGeo8K dataset.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art LMMs on footprint labeling, advancing automation and standardization in PCB design with 8,608 labeled training samples.

problem: Existing memory benchmarks are dialogue-centric but real agent memory consists of continuous state-action-observation trajectories, limiting evaluation of agent memory systems.
approach: AMA-Bench combines real-world agent trajectories with expert QA and synthetic trajectories using a rule-based generator, enabling evaluation across arbitrary horizons with causality-aware memory systems.
contribution: Shows that causality-graph-based memory with tool-augmented retrieval (AMA-Agent) achieves 57.22% accuracy, outperforming baselines by 11.16% on realistic agentic memory tasks.

problem: Interactive world modeling requires real-time generation with long-term geometric consistency, but current methods face tradeoffs between speed and memory.
approach: WorldPlay uses dual action representation for control, reconstituted context memory to maintain geometric information over long horizons, and context forcing for memory-aware knowledge distillation.
contribution: Generates long-horizon streaming 720p video at 24 FPS with superior geometric consistency and strong generalization across diverse scenes.

problem: Research idea generation is open-ended and multi-objective, requiring balance of novelty, plausibility, and feasibility, but existing methods use static predefined workflows.
approach: MindFlow formulates ideation as graph-structured flows composed of modular thinking operators, uses a probabilistic mind supernet to sample flows, and optimizes via tournament-based ranking.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority across diverse topics as an explicit, controllable, and optimizable research idea innovator with joint problem-finding and problem-solving evaluation.

problem: Preference-based alignment methods optimize single scalar objectives that average over heterogeneous human preferences, making them brittle to proxy over-optimization and disagreement.
approach: DARC reranks response candidates at inference time by maximizing a KL-robust entropic satisfaction objective, providing risk budgets without retraining.
contribution: Reduces disagreement and tail risk while maintaining competitive average quality under noisy heterogeneous feedback across alignment benchmarks.

problem: Standard self-attention relies on static feature similarity and lacks principled handling of variable-length contexts and extrapolation to longer sequences.
approach: Robust Filter Attention treats tokens as noisy observations of latent trajectories governed by linear SDEs, with attention weights determined by consistency under this model rather than feature similarity.
contribution: Achieves lower perplexity than RoPE within training windows while remaining stable under zero-shot extrapolation to longer contexts with computational complexity matching standard attention.

problem: Anytime-valid tests under strict deadlines must balance Type-I error control with power, but existing methods lack horizon awareness.
approach: Frames horizon-aware betting as a finite-horizon optimal control problem and uses Deep Q-Networks to learn betting policies that map past observations to bets across horizons and null values.
contribution: Learned DQN policies yield state-of-the-art results on limited-horizon experiments by identifying regions where Kelly, fractional Kelly, and aggressive betting are optimal.

problem: Existing AI-generated music detectors rely on generated samples during training and fail when detecting music from unseen generators.
approach: MusicDET formulates zero-shot detection by training only on real music and using frequency-guided normalizing flows to probabilistically model the distribution of real music features.
contribution: Consistently outperforms discriminative detectors on FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets, particularly when detecting music from previously unseen generative models.

problem: Real-world data suffers from both class imbalance and label corruption, but existing solutions rely on meta-learning with circular dependencies on pristine validation sets.
approach: ProMeCD recasts optimization as autonomous control using a transparent proportional-integral controller monitoring cognitive entropy from gradient statistics, with decoupled strategies for tail classes and noise.
contribution: Outperforms recent meta-learner FMW-Net by over 10% on severe imbalance settings while being fully white-box and validation-free with provable convergence guarantees.

problem: Safe deployment of LLM agents requires detecting covert misalignment or scheming, but black-box monitors must generalize from limited synthetic data.
approach: Constitutional black-box monitors use natural-language behavior specifications to generate synthetic agent trajectories via STRIDE (refinement) and Gloom (simulation) pipelines, optimized via prompt sweeps and automated optimization.
contribution: Demonstrates that monitors selected on synthetic data generalize to realistic environments from Control Arena, capturing meaningful scheming signal but with saturation limits.

problem: Vision Transformer tokenizers degrade with variable aspect ratios and resolutions, and rely on adversarial losses making them harder to train at scale.
approach: ViTok-v2 adds native resolution support via NaFlex with 2D RoPE and replaces LPIPS-plus-discriminator loss with DINO perceptual loss, scaling to 5B parameters.
contribution: Matches state-of-the-art reconstruction at 256p and outperforms across benchmarks at 512p and higher resolutions while maintaining flexibility for arbitrary aspect ratios.

problem: State space models suffer from instability and memory degradation over extended horizons due to poorly conditioned recurrent updates and unbalanced update geometry.
approach: MuonSSM stabilizes SSM training by conditioning the geometry of memory updates rather than the recurrent matrix, using momentum-based pathways and Newton-Schulz transformations on low-rank injections.
contribution: Improves gradient propagation and mitigates spectral amplification with consistent gains in accuracy, robustness, and long-context performance across language, vision, and time-series benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating computer-use agents on complex tasks like PowerPoint editing is difficult because tasks admit many valid solutions and agents often make only partial progress.
approach: PPT-Eval uses task-specific rubrics inspired by prior work to award partial credit for intermediate steps, penalize unnecessary changes, and provide natural language feedback.
contribution: Achieves 0.77 Kendall's τb correlation with human judgments while revealing that frontier agents like Claude-4.5-Opus achieve only 45% success with 57% average partial score.

problem: Graph embeddings are typically hard to interpret and fail to capture how learned features relate to graph structure or express role-mixture views.
approach: Proposes compositional graph embeddings grounded in Aitchison geometry using isometric log-ratio coordinates to represent nodes as simplex-valued compositions preserving Aitchison distances.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on node classification and link prediction while providing intrinsic interpretability by construction and enabling principled component restriction.

problem: While MPNNs show promise for neural algorithmic reasoning, existing work lacks formal guarantees about when architectures generalize to inputs beyond the training set size.
approach: Establishes a theoretical framework characterizing sufficient conditions for MPNNs to learn algorithms from small instances and provably approximate behavior on arbitrary-size inputs.
contribution: Applies framework to shortest paths, MSTs, and dynamic programming problems with worst-case guarantees, identifies impossibility results, and proposes more expressive MPNN-like architectures.

problem: RL methods for scaling reasoning models fail on datasets with low initial success rates, providing insufficient training signal for curriculum learning.
approach: SOAR uses asymmetric self-play with meta-RL where a teacher proposes synthetic problems and is rewarded by student improvement on hard problems, grounding curriculum in real progress.
contribution: Demonstrates that latent problem-generation ability emerges without requiring ability to solve hard problems, achieving improvements on zero-shot subsets of math benchmarks.

problem: Understanding whether self-attention alone can achieve universal approximation for sequence-to-sequence functions remains open.
approach: Proves universal approximation via new interpolation-based analysis showing self-attention approximates generalized ReLU, demonstrating both one-layer and two-layer attention suffice without feed-forward networks.
contribution: Establishes that softmax-attention-only layers are capable of approximating gradient descent in-context and subsume many known universal approximators.

problem: Medical multimodal fusion assumes fixed known modalities but real systems must handle varying modality numbers and compositions while managing heterogeneous information.
approach: Proposes modality-agnostic framework using uncertainty-aware probability distributions with symmetric consistency constraints at modality and token levels, plus multi-view fusion via sequential conditional views.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness and scalability on five multimodal medical datasets while supporting arbitrary modality numbers and reducing noise via structured mutual verification.

problem: In long-context reasoning for RAG and agentic systems, the quantitative relationship between proportion of misleading information and performance degradation is unknown.
approach: Systematically varies proportion of hard distractors within fixed contexts, revealing nonlinear performance drops concentrated in the first small fraction of distractor proportion.
contribution: Demonstrates that filtering gains derive primarily from context reduction rather than distractor removal, with substantial recovery only when hard distractor proportion approaches zero.

problem: Mechanisms governing memorization versus generalization in diffusion models remain unclear, particularly where in the noise schedule and how data geometry influences memorization.
approach: Introduces geometric framework partitioning noise schedule into regimes based on coverage properties of training data by Gaussian shells and posterior concentration behavior.
contribution: Identifies nonuniform memorization risk across noise levels with a danger zone at medium noise, reveals fundamental mechanisms in small and large noise regimes, and proposes geometry-informed interventions.

problem: Tokenizer structure affects test-time search capabilities, but whether coarse-to-fine 1D ordered tokens improve steering versus classical 2D grids remains unexplored.
approach: Hypothesizes and validates that 1D ordered tokenizers enable better test-time search because intermediate coarse-to-fine states carry semantic meaning that verifiers can reliably evaluate.
contribution: Shows AR models with coarse-to-fine ordered tokens exhibit improved test-time scaling and enables training-free text-to-image generation using pure search over sequences.

problem: LLM-based agents simulate human behaviors widely but their human-likeness remains underexplored due to ineffective Turing tests and biased human-crafted challenges.
approach: Proposes distribution-based framework leveraging large-scale web behavior data to comprehensively evaluate human-likeness via generic metrics covering rationality, consistency, and diversity.
contribution: Reveals that even the best current LLMs exhibit significant gap from real user behavior in online shopping, Q&A, and urban mobility, underscoring need for human-like capability research.

problem: Image aesthetic assessment predicts overall scores but multiple attributes influence aesthetics with varying importance, causing gradient conflicts and systematic bias under end-to-end training.
approach: AGREE learns attribute-specific subspaces and performs gradient routing based on sample-wise attribute sensitivity via perturbation analysis, with semantic anchors and error-aware reweighting.
contribution: Provides consistent improvements over diverse IAA baselines as a plug-and-play method without modifying original architectures, addressing gradient conflict systematically.

problem: Adopting pre-trained Vision-Language Models in Federated Learning requires high computational overhead or ineffective knowledge aggregation across heterogeneous clients.
approach: FedSPA restricts client optimization to visual prototypes for lightweight personalization and uses semantic alignment to minimize contrastive objectives aligning global and heterogeneous visual distributions.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on personalized and global benchmarks while substantially reducing computational overhead in federated VLM adaptation.

problem: LLM prompt sensitivity undermines their capabilities but existing coarse-grained metrics fail to explain internal reasons behind instability to prompt changes.
approach: Introduces interactions as fine-grained tool to analyze prompt sensitivity by decomposing output scores into nonlinear relationships, defining Interaction-based Prompt Sensitivity metric.
contribution: Identifies four factors reducing prompt sensitivity (SFT, scale, dense architectures, few-shot learning) by reducing sensitivity of low-order interactions, explaining mechanism across 50 open-source LLMs.

problem: Machine unlearning in quantized neural networks faces challenges: forgetting via mislabeling confuses forgetting with misremembering, and scalar gradient reweighting cannot resolve directional conflicts.
approach: OEU proposes entropy-guided unlearning that maximizes prediction uncertainty on forgotten data and uses gradient orthogonal projection to eliminate interference with retain gradients.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in both forgetting effectiveness and retain accuracy with theoretical guarantees for utility preservation under first-order approximation.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on fixed communication topologies but optimal structure varies with task complexity and communication needs.
approach: RADAR formulates communication topology design as step-by-step generation process using conditional discrete graph diffusion, guided by effective graph size.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines across six benchmarks with higher accuracy, lower token consumption, and greater robustness through redundancy-aware topology generation.

problem: Quantum hardware heterogeneity and drift force practitioners to choose between suboptimal non-adaptive controllers or costly per-device recalibration.
approach: Derives scaling law lower bound for meta-learning showing adaptation gain saturates exponentially with gradient steps and scales linearly with task variance.
contribution: Validates on quantum gate calibration showing >40% fidelity gains under extreme out-of-distribution conditions, with few-shot protocol estimating optimal adaptation budget within 3-19% error.

problem: Importance sampling efficiency depends critically on proposal distribution choice, especially for complex multimodal distributions in high dimensions.
approach: Proposes adaptive scheme combining global sampling mechanisms with delayed weighting procedure enabling rapid resampling in poorly-adapted regions.
contribution: Demonstrates geometric convergence under mild assumptions with efficient exploration of complex target distributions via adaptive proposal construction.

problem: LLMs struggle with complex logical reasoning when using purely neural approaches or symbolic solvers due to hallucinations and syntactic error sensitivity respectively.
approach: LogicSAGE integrates robust neural reasoner (System 1) with rigorous symbolic validator (System 2) using Socratic error correction that treats solver feedback as pedagogical signals.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art 92.36% average accuracy on five benchmarks with 8B model, significantly outperforming GPT-4, establishing that architecture innovation can supersede model scale.

problem: Mechanistic understanding of analogical reasoning in Transformers remains limited despite its centrality to human intelligence.
approach: Formalizes analogical reasoning as inference of correspondences between entities across categories using category theory, analyzing emergence through synthetic tasks.
contribution: Decomposes analogical reasoning into geometric alignment of relational structure and functor application, enabling mechanistic grounding of abstraction in neural networks.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization applies uniform calibration strategies across all samples but reliability of perplexity signals varies substantially by task type.
approach: TAPC learns task-conditioned calibration functions using task encoder and meta-learning on reference dataset to adapt perplexity signal weighting to prompt characteristics.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods across multiple benchmarks with particularly large improvements on creative and open-ended tasks where uniform calibration fails.

problem: Ultrafast online learning under sub-microsecond latency and fixed-precision constraints requires efficiency beyond MLPs which are inefficient and numerically unstable.
approach: Shows Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) enable sparse updates exploiting B-spline locality and are inherently robust to fixed-point quantization when implemented on FPGAs.
contribution: Demonstrates significantly more efficient and expressive KAN-based online learners than MLPs for low-latency tasks, achieving model-free learning at sub-microsecond latencies.

problem: LLMs must balance diversity and creativity in open-ended generation, but existing truncation-based sampling methods ignore the semantic geometry of token embeddings while balancing probability mass and entropy.
approach: Top-W uses Wasserstein distance over token-embedding geometry to keep the cropped distribution close to the original while explicitly trading off retained probability mass against entropy, yielding a simple closed-form update that either collapses to one token or forms a one-dimensional prefix.
contribution: Top-W outperforms prior state-of-the-art decoding approaches on GSM8K, GPQA, AlpacaEval, and MT-Bench, achieving up to 33.7 percentage point improvement and boosting both accuracy and creativity.

problem: Time-series forecasting models lag behind operational numerical weather prediction systems in capturing complex weather dynamics and extreme events, hampered by small, sparse, temporally short datasets.
approach: PhysicsFormer combines a dynamic core with a Transformer residual to predict weather states, enforcing physical consistency via pressure-wind alignment and energy-aware smoothness losses.
contribution: PhysicsFormer and other TSF models are benchmarked against operational systems across weather variables and extreme events, with WEATHER-5K, a large-scale observational dataset, supporting improved model training.

problem: Link prediction in graphs requires capturing rich topological dependencies, but existing approaches rely on explicit structural heuristics or memory-intensive embeddings that struggle to generalize or scale.
approach: PENCIL is an encoder-only plain Transformer that replaces hand-crafted priors with attention over sampled local subgraphs, extracting richer structural signals than GNNs while remaining parameter-efficient.
contribution: PENCIL outperforms heuristic-informed GNNs and ID-embedding alternatives across diverse benchmarks without node features, while remaining competitive and far more parameter-efficient.

problem: Modern recurrent neural networks struggle with long-context understanding and extrapolation due to limited memory capacity, online-only updates, and rigid memory management.
approach: Atlas is a long-term memory module that learns to memorize context by optimizing memory based on current and past tokens, overcoming the online nature of standard long-term memory models.
contribution: Atlas outperforms other modern recurrent neural networks on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, recall-intensive, and long-context understanding tasks.

problem: Dynamic submodular maximization requires maintaining near-optimal solutions with minimal adjustments at each step, but prior work only addresses insertion-only streams, not fully dynamic ones with insertions and deletions.
approach: A general framework instantiated for cardinality-constrained and matroid-constrained settings, yielding constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency in the fully dynamic case.
contribution: First constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency: 1/2 - O(epsilon) for cardinality with O(1/epsilon^2) consistency and 1/4 - O(epsilon) for matroid with O(log k/epsilon^2) consistency.

problem: V2V-MLLM frameworks for cooperative autonomous driving incur high communication and inference costs due to dense token-level sharing, and existing pruning methods ignore LiDAR spatial structure and multi-agent fusion.
approach: V2V-CCM broadcasts question and spatial coverage messages to enable selective token activation based on question intent and observed regions, reducing communication and inference overhead.
contribution: V2V-CCM achieves state-of-the-art performance on V2V-QA and V2V-GoT-QA while substantially reducing communication and inference costs compared to existing pruning methods.

problem: GUI agents struggle with CAPTCHA solving while specialized CAPTCHA solvers cannot handle general GUI tasks, creating a gap where no single system excels at both.
approach: ReCAP uses automated data collection with large-scale CAPTCHA interaction trajectories and self-correction training to enable GUI agents to solve CAPTCHAs via vision-language reasoning.
contribution: ReCAP substantially improves CAPTCHA-solving success over base agents while maintaining strong performance on general GUI-agent benchmarks.

problem: Full fine-tuning of LLMs is memory-prohibitive, and parameter-efficient alternatives like LoRA fail to approximate full fine-tuning performance while incurring lower costs.
approach: Think-Touch predicts parameter-group potentials at each step and updates only selected groups, theoretically recovering full fine-tuning convergence asympotically with lower cost.
contribution: Think-Touch shows that selective updates converge to stationary points under weak divergence conditions and derives rate-optimal greedy strategies, advancing low-cost full fine-tuning.

problem: Personalized text-to-image models may incorporate unauthorized data during fine-tuning, raising copyright concerns, but existing methods require intrusive modifications or access to pre-fine-tuned models.
approach: RECOVER leverages inversion robustness—the stable reconstruction of images under noise perturbations after fine-tuning—to detect unauthorized image usage without requiring pre-fine-tuned models.
contribution: RECOVER provides the first non-intrusive copyright authentication without pre-fine-tuned models, consistently outperforming existing methods across diverse scenarios.

problem: fMRI-to-text decoding is challenging because strong language priors can dominate autoregressive generation, obscuring whether the model truly uses neural evidence.
approach: BIT-LLM exposes fMRI-derived tokens as persistent key-value memory through interleaved cross-attention adapters, enabling repeated neural access throughout decoding via three-stage training.
contribution: BIT-LLM yields substantially improved captioning quality on the NSD benchmark with clear sensitivity to fMRI input perturbations, demonstrating effective brain-language grounding.

problem: Scaling LLMs increases computational overhead, and existing weight quantization methods are inefficient for memory-bound inference.
approach: S-Quant partitions weight tensors into fixed-size blocks with seed-based LFSR generation to produce basis matrices, reconstructing blocks as linear combinations with minimal stored data.
contribution: S-Quant achieves state-of-the-art performance at 3-4 bit weights and enables a 4x speedup via a custom ASIC accelerator for memory-bound LLM inference.

problem: Integrating LLMs into TTS systems improves expressiveness, but interpretable emotional control remains challenging with limited insight into internal emotion representations.
approach: SAEs are used to analyze emotion-related variation in LLM-based TTS semantic hidden states, identifying sparse latent features that enable interpretable emotion control via feature-level intervention.
contribution: Sparse latent features achieve comparable or superior emotion induction and suppression relative to global steering, with distinct features associated with specific acoustic attributes.

problem: Object removal methods that block attention in vacated regions during image generation degrade quality because the model must simultaneously reconstruct background content.
approach: AdaEraser dynamically modulates attention based on estimated object-concept presence, developing token-wise adaptive attention suppression that adjusts suppression strength across denoising timesteps.
contribution: AdaEraser achieves superior object removal performance, outperforming even training-based methods through adaptive timestep-aware suppression.

problem: Classical treatment effect measures like ATE fail to capture differences across entire outcome distributions.
approach: Sinkhorn treatment effect uses entropic optimal transport as a distributional measure, characterized as a smooth transformation of counterfactual mean embeddings with appropriate kernels.
contribution: First-order pathwise differentiability is established in general and second-order pathwise differentiability under the null hypothesis, enabling debiased estimators and asymptotically valid tests.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs on resource-constrained devices requires prohibitive computational and communication overhead.
approach: SmartFed reuses knowledge from existing LoRA modules decomposed into rank-level experts, selectively activating them based on input semantics and resource budgets via Mixture of Rank-Wise Experts (MoRE).
contribution: SmartFed significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in model performance and training efficiency on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Coding agents struggle to infer and track underspecified or context-dependent user intent in software engineering tasks.
approach: ToM-SWE pairs a primary SWE agent with a lightweight theory-of-mind agent dedicated to modeling user mental state, maintaining persistent user memory and providing suggestions.
contribution: ToM-SWE achieves 59.7% task success on stateful SWE-bench versus 18.1% for OpenHands, with 86% user satisfaction in a three-week study with professional developers.

problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate coding agents on isolated one-off tasks, neglecting temporal dependencies and technical debt inherent in real-world software evolution.
approach: EvoClaw uses DeepCommit to reconstruct executable Milestone DAGs from commit logs, enabling benchmarking of long-term software evolution where agents must sustain system integrity.
contribution: Evaluation of 12 frontier models reveals critical vulnerability: performance drops from >80% on isolated tasks to at most 38% in continuous evolution, exposing agents' struggle with long-term maintenance.

problem: Modeling dynamic dependencies from irregularly sampled event sequences is challenging when individual and population-level states evolve asynchronously.
approach: CoCLD jointly models individual latent dynamics and population-level distributional shifts in continuous-time, integrating diffusion-based latent interpolation with neural ODEs.
contribution: CoCLD effectively captures dynamic dependencies and generalizes across next-event prediction, trajectory generation, and sequential behavior modeling with sparse irregular observations.

problem: Mechanistic understanding of how few-shot prompts shape a model's function vector in in-context learning remains unclear.
approach: An n-shot function vector is shown to be well-approximated by a linear combination of example-level sub-FVs, with models contextualizing individual examples and reweighting demonstrations based on informativeness.
contribution: Causal decomposition separates Query-Key routing from Value updates, revealing that contextualization's consistent contributions arise from Query-Key alignment, especially in ambiguous settings.

problem: Efficient distillation of LLMs via structured pruning causes reasoning collapse due to uneven singular-value distribution in projection matrices.
approach: RED introduces activation-aware initialization that initializes projection matrices as channel-selection matrices, theoretically mitigating effective-rank collapse.
contribution: RED substantially recovers reasoning ability while maintaining high training efficiency and state-of-the-art general ability on Llama and Qwen series.

problem: Zero-shot LLM-generated text detection using a fixed surrogate model performs sub-optimally because surrogate-source alignment varies substantially.
approach: DetectRouter learns text-detector affinity through two-stage training, constructing discriminative prototypes and aligning geometric distances with detection scores to select appropriate surrogates.
contribution: DetectRouter demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple detection criteria and model families on EvoBench and MAGE benchmarks.

problem: Language identification systems remain brittle in low-resource and closely related language settings despite near-perfect performance on high-resource languages.
approach: UniLID uses the UnigramLM tokenization algorithm's probabilistic framing for efficient language identification, supporting incremental language addition without retraining.
contribution: UniLID achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks, substantially improves sample efficiency in low-resource settings (surpassing 70% accuracy with five labeled samples per language), and delivers large gains on dialect identification.

problem: Sequential resource allocation with stochastic referral capacity and endogenous opportunity generation is intractable when modeling multi-round planning with high-dimensional frontier evolution.
approach: A population-level surrogate value function depending only on remaining budget and frontier size enables an exact dynamic program via truncated probability generating functions.
contribution: Planning algorithm achieves polynomial complexity in budget with robust error bounds decomposing single-round frontier error and population-level transition error.

problem: Integrating LLMs into ad auctions for dynamic creative enhancement disrupts mechanism design due to significant computational costs and non-stationary agent responses.
approach: Platform-Investment Mechanism models the system as a Stackelberg game where the platform optimizes investment via two-timescale learning and agents learn bidding via ODDB-R algorithm.
contribution: TTSL-PPO algorithm converges to Stackelberg Stationary Point, with experiments showing significant improvements in revenue, social welfare, and user engagement.

problem: LiDAR point cloud anomaly detection methods rely only on visible measurements, overlooking occlusion as a structured consequence of sensing that characterizes anomalies.
approach: COVAL intervenes on volumetric visibility during training, generating paired factual and counterfactual observations to model occlusion-induced missing regions and enforce visibility-invariant consistency.
contribution: COVAL achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard LiDAR anomaly segmentation benchmarks through counterfactual occlusion-visibility learning.

problem: Vision-Language Models fail at elementary spatial tasks like block counting due to missing coherent 3D mental representations from 2D observations, creating a spatial intelligence gap.
approach: 3ViewSense uses orthographic views as a spatial interface, decomposing complex scenes into canonical projections and employing a Simulate-and-Reason mechanism for explicit mental rotation.
contribution: 3ViewSense significantly outperforms existing baselines on spatial reasoning benchmarks with consistent gains on occlusion-heavy counting and improved stability in spatial descriptions.

problem: Verbose Chain-of-Thought reasoning in MLLMs introduces inefficiencies that hinder practical deployment.
approach: Heima condenses lengthy CoTs into a small set of abstract thinking tokens while preserving reasoning, with an adaptive interpreter reconstructing variable-length textual sequences.
contribution: Heima improves reasoning efficiency while maintaining or achieving better zero-shot accuracy, with interpreter validating that the information gap is minimal.

problem: Existing sequential strategic classification focuses on optimizing classifier weights, not on designing threshold sequences that incentivize genuine effort over dishonest actions.
approach: A multi-level promotion-relegation framework analyzes threshold design capturing inter-temporal incentives driven by agent farsightedness and skill retention effects.
contribution: Under mild conditions, a designed threshold sequence enables agents to reach arbitrarily high levels solely through genuine improvement efforts, incentivizing honest behavior.

problem: Vector quantization with standard k-means for KV cache compression suffers from centroid shrinkage, which weakens directional preservation in the k-means objective.
approach: Gain-Shape k-means (GSKM) improves directional fidelity while matching k-means l2 distortion, incorporated into Residual Quantization for sub-1-bit KV cache.
contribution: GSRQ improves 1-bit KV cache from 11.34 to 33.54 accuracy on LongBench tasks, a 22.20 percentage point gain over VQLLM.

problem: Existing diffusion and flow models rely on external models for strong semantic representations, operating on misaligned objectives with unexpected scaling behavior.
approach: Self-Flow integrates representation learning within generative framework via Dual-Timestep Scheduling, applying heterogeneous noise levels to create information asymmetry.
contribution: Self-Flow enables multi-modal training following expected scaling laws while achieving superior image, video, and audio generation without external supervision.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models have high computational cost that hinders real-time deployment, and token pruning methods indiscriminately discard critical geometric details like contact points.
approach: GridS performs task-aware continuous token resampling by adaptively predicting salient coordinates and extracting features via differentiable interpolation.
contribution: GridS achieves 76% reduction in FLOPs with no degradation in success rate, using fewer than 10% original visual tokens on LIBERO and real robotic tasks.

problem: Preference learning methods like DPO induce reliance on spurious correlations, leading to sycophancy, length bias, and goal misgeneralization in deployed models.
approach: Tie training uses ties (equal-utility preference pairs) to introduce data-driven regularization that selectively reduces spurious learning without degrading causal learning.
contribution: Unified theoretical analysis characterizes spurious learning mechanisms and demonstrates that tie training mitigates spurious reliance while preserving causal learning.
