problem: The principles generating a continuous gradient of hippocampal place field sizes from discrete grid cell inputs remain unclear, but this organization suggests an inductive bias for multiscale representation.
approach: A unified framework establishes how multiscale place fields arise from frequency-dependent decay of grid cell projections, translated to HiPE (hippocampus-inspired positional embedding) in Transformers.
contribution: HiPE demonstrates effective data efficiency improvements, establishing a link between neural connectivity, activity patterns, and learning.

problem: Behavior cloning with generative policies is limited by demonstration coverage and distribution shift, and direct RL fine-tuning on large action decoders is unstable and sample inefficient.
approach: LP-DS learns a compact noise-space perturbation to improve frozen generative policies using Lagrangian trust-region objective, constraining deviation from latent prior.
contribution: LP-DS improves sample efficiency and success across RoboMimic, OpenAI Gym, and Adroit with up to 25% return improvements, validated on real Franka deployment.

problem: Post-training robustness analysis lacks a unifying framework for understanding how parameter perturbations affect model outputs across different perturbation types.
approach: Test Prediction Variance (TPV) provides a unifying framework via its trace form Tr(H_eff*C) separating model geometry from perturbation covariance.
contribution: TPV converges from training to test set in overparameterized limit and correlates well with test loss, enabling label-free pruning criterion JBR and model selection.

problem: Existing mask-guided diffusion for subtitle removal requires extensive annotations, full model fine-tuning, explicit mask sequences during inference, and cannot adapt to quality variations.
approach: CLEAR uses self-supervised prior learning to extract occlusion guidance without annotations, LoRA-based adaptive refinement for parameter efficiency, and adaptive focal weighting.
contribution: CLEAR achieves superior multilingual subtitle removal requiring only 0.77% trainable parameters with true mask-free end-to-end inference.

problem: Bilevel optimization in RL with competitive lower-level interactions (zero-sum games) lacks efficient algorithms avoiding second-order information while maintaining convergence guarantees.
approach: PANDA is a penalty-based first-order policy-gradient method based on the Nikaido-Isoda function that exploits min-max structure to avoid hypergradient computation.
contribution: PANDA converges to stationary points in O-tilde(epsilon^-1) iterations with O-tilde(epsilon^-3) sample complexity, matching best-known bilevel RL rates.

problem: Existing LLM evaluations for GPU code generation focus on single-shot generation and underplay tool use and feedback, lacking standardized evaluation frameworks.
approach: TritonGym provides a benchmark and orchestration framework that standardizes tool access via function-calls, separating model capability from workflow design.
contribution: TritonGym spans maintained operators, community samples, and out-of-distribution tasks, enabling fair comparison and facilitating progress on agentic GPU-code systems.

problem: Video forensics methods fail in realistic scenarios where AI-generated content is sparsely embedded in long-form videos, focusing only on short clips without temporal localization.
approach: MSLoc combines boundary-sensitive proposal generation for efficient scanning with MLLM-based refinement for precise boundary localization and interpretable reasoning.
contribution: TASLE benchmark comprises 12,472 untrimmed videos with manipulation patterns and rich annotations; MSLoc validates the importance of segment-level explainable forensics.

problem: Deploying robots in open-ended environments demands continual learning to adapt to new tasks while retaining prior skills, but monolithic policies face capacity constraints.
approach: Nevo-CRL maintains a fixed-capacity policy network using mask populations to selectively activate neuron outputs per task, with semantic reuse and dynamic allocation.
contribution: Nevo-CRL achieves state-of-the-art continual RL performance with neuron freezing to prevent catastrophic forgetting and importance-guided mask optimization.

problem: LLMs require efficient deployment under computational and memory constraints, but existing techniques like token-adaptive execution and quantization degrade accuracy when combined.
approach: QTALE integrates token-adaptive layer execution with quantization by ensuring diverse training paths during fine-tuning and allowing flexible execution-ratio adjustment at inference to reintroduce redundancy.
contribution: Seamless integration of token-adaptive execution and quantization with accuracy gap kept below 0.5% on CommonsenseQA benchmarks.

problem: Autoregressive generative models for clinical time-series struggle because a single temporal resolution poorly matches the varying temporal dynamics of different medical endpoints.
approach: MoRGen fuses forecasts from expert models trained at multiple temporal resolutions using a task-specific mixture, adapting to different endpoint temporal characteristics.
contribution: Statistically significant AUROC gains over fixed-resolution baseline models across multiple clinical datasets and prediction horizons.

problem: Current coding benchmarks overstate LLM capabilities by allowing models to exploit statistical shortcuts rather than genuine reasoning through data contamination and static evaluation.
approach: UniCode generates diverse algorithmic variants via multi-dimensional augmentation, creates test cases automatically with 94.5% correctness, and provides fine-grained diagnostic metrics for error analysis.
contribution: Reveals 31.2% performance collapse in state-of-the-art models and identifies seed-problem regression patterns showing fragility under structural shifts.

problem: End-to-end autonomous driving models do not generalize across domains (e.g., different cities) and cannot adapt efficiently without expensive retraining.
approach: RoCA formulates joint probabilistic distributions over ego and vehicle tokens using Gaussian processes, learning basis tokens and trajectories spanning diverse driving scenarios for robust cross-domain inference.
contribution: Strong domain generalization and adaptation without extra inference computation, significantly outperforming direct finetuning on cross-domain scenarios.

problem: Vision-language models perform well on clean data but their robustness to real-world image distortions remains poorly understood.
approach: VLM-RobustBench benchmarks 15 VLMs across 133 corrupted settings spanning noise, blur, weather, digital, and geometric perturbations at graded severities on two complementary benchmarks.
contribution: Reveals VLMs are semantically strong but spatially fragile, with low-severity spatial perturbations degrading performance more than visually severe photometric corruptions.

problem: Panoramic video depth estimation lacks large-scale training data and struggles with Equirectangular Projection geometry that causes non-uniform information density and non-linear temporal dynamics.
approach: PVDepth introduces PanoCARLA synthetic dataset, uses progressive sphere-aware noise initialization to adapt from planar to spherical geometry, and employs cube-rectified temporal modeling with auxiliary cubemap branches.
contribution: Generates geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences for panoramic video, enabling VR and world model applications.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning with expert demonstrations produces models that imitate outputs without learning robust reasoning, and critique-based training can cause format drift and capability degradation.
approach: CGD decouples critique consumption from generation: students refine flawed responses using teacher critiques during training, but critiques are absent at inference, treating them as training-only supervision.
contribution: 7% average improvements over CFT and standard distillation on mathematical reasoning; up to +15.0% on AMC23, +12.2% on MATH-500; maintains instruction-following capabilities where CFT degrades.

problem: Theoretical understanding of test-time computation in language models is limited because prior frameworks assume deterministic decoding, ignoring the stochastic nature of practical inference.
approach: Establishes new theoretical framework incorporating randomness and sampling directly into decoding analysis, applied to canonical in-context linear regression with noise injection and sampling.
contribution: Provides theoretical foundation for understanding test-time computation techniques with validation on simulated and real-world tasks.

problem: LLMs fail on multiple-choice questions despite encoding correct answers in hidden representations, revealing a misalignment between internal knowledge and output behavior.
approach: KAPPA identifies distinct knowledge and prediction subspaces in the residual stream and applies lightweight inference-time intervention to align these subspaces.
contribution: Reduces knowledge-prediction gap across diverse MCQ benchmarks and models, generalizing to free-form settings with geometric interpretation.

problem: Geospatial foundation models focus on static place identity from text rather than POI function derived from actual human usage patterns, missing a critical signal.
approach: ME-POIs augments text embeddings with large-scale human mobility data using temporally contextualized visit embeddings aligned via contrastive learning, with spatial propagation for sparsity.
contribution: Consistently outperforms text-only and mobility-only baselines on five map enrichment tasks; mobility alone surpasses text on certain tasks.

problem: Molecular dynamics is inherently serial and difficult to accelerate with concurrent compute without introducing relative error.
approach: LSD uses a draft model to propose fast simulation steps verified in parallel with a slower target model, applying a transport map from draft to target distribution, extending to second-order Langevin dynamics.
contribution: Achieves 3-9x speedup without adding relative error, generalizes across systems and draft-target combinations with theoretical speedup guarantees.

problem: Rotary position embedding (RoPE) entangles content and position information, impairing performance when decisions require independent matching on these factors.
approach: PoPE eliminates the what-where confound in RoPE by decoupling content and position through improved polar coordinate encoding.
contribution: Superior performance on diagnostic tasks and autoregressive modeling across music, genomic, and language domains; strong zero-shot length extrapolation capabilities.

problem: Understanding analogical reasoning in transformers is complicated by evaluations that conflate multiple reasoning types.
approach: Isolates analogical reasoning through minimal transformer abstraction and proves that joint training on similarity and attribution premises enables reasoning through aligned representations.
contribution: Reveals unified mechanism where entities with shared properties align in representation space, enabling property transfer; curriculum asymmetry and two-hop reasoning insights.

problem: LLM inference scheduling using point estimate of output length neglects the stochastic nature of decoding where length is uncertain until end-of-sequence token is sampled.
approach: TIE scheduler fits output length to log-t distribution and uses Tail Inflated Expectation metric adjusting expectation with tail probabilities to account for risk of long outputs.
contribution: Reduces per-token latency by 2.31x for online inference and improves throughput by 1.42x for offline data generation.

problem: MLLMs degrade significantly under real-world visual corruptions, and existing enhancement approaches lack interpretability or cannot restore pixel-level details.
approach: Robust-U1 equips MLLMs with explicit visual self-recovery through supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning with pixel-level and semantic rewards, and multimodal reasoning.
contribution: State-of-the-art robustness on corruption benchmarks and adversarial settings; analysis confirms visual recovery quality directly enhances reasoning.

problem: Domain transfer is fundamentally ill-posed due to measure-preserving automorphisms that preserve marginals while altering cross-domain correspondences.
approach: Under structural sparsity on Jacobian support pattern, shows distribution matching plus a single paired anchor sample suffices for identifiable transfer; employs randomized masked finite differences for scalable regularization.
contribution: Identifies ground-truth transfer with substantially less supervision than prior approaches requiring multiple conditionals.

problem: Hyperspectral image super-resolution faces a trade-off between transformer global modeling with quadratic complexity and window-based methods that compromise global capture.
approach: SSDCN uses content-driven clustering for low-rank structural bases achieving linear complexity, pyramid progressive hierarchical architecture with feature reuse, and pyramid joint loss supervising intermediate levels.
contribution: Surpasses SOTA methods with significantly fewer parameters and FLOPs, achieving optimal efficiency-performance balance.

problem: Conformal prediction for time series with time-varying distributions yields volatile, non-nested prediction intervals due to noisy quantile estimation and quantile crossing.
approach: CQACP models conditional quantile curve of nonconformity score via Cornish-Fisher approximation with monotonicity constraints, evaluating base quantile learner on grid of levels.
contribution: Maintains accurate coverage with smooth, narrow, nested prediction intervals; proves conditional validity under serial dependence.

problem: Uniform patchified transformers distribute computational effort evenly across domains regardless of local features, inefficiently handling PDEs with sharp gradients and multiscale structures.
approach: MeshTok generates adaptive mesh refinement-inspired tokens selectively refining regions with sharp gradients and transient features, processed in unified transformer sequence.
contribution: Consistently improves efficiency-accuracy trade-off compared to uniform grids across multiple PDE families.

problem: Bandit learning in matching markets is complex because context shifts can reconfigure the stable matching benchmark, causing large regret spikes.
approach: Introduces minimum preference gap capturing difficulty and provides adaptive algorithms for stochastic contexts (poly-logarithmic regret) and adversarial contexts (sublinear regret).
contribution: Instance-dependent and instance-independent regret bounds under different context distributions.

problem: Language model pre-training is computationally expensive, limiting accessibility and scalability.
approach: GradPower applies simple sign-power transformation to gradients before feeding into base optimizer, requiring only single-line code change without hyperparameter modification.
contribution: Consistently achieves lower terminal loss across architectures, scales, and datasets with pronounced gains on mixture-of-experts with warmup-stable-decay.

problem: Inferring cellular trajectories from destructive snapshots is complicated by stochasticity and non-conservative mass dynamics like proliferation, which macroscopic unbalanced OT methods fail to capture.
approach: USB provides simulation-free framework tractably solving branching Schrödinger bridge, modeling discrete birth-death jumps at single-cell resolution with efficient training objective.
contribution: Achieves trajectory reconstruction comparable to deterministic baselines while enabling realistic discrete simulation of birth-death dynamics.

problem: Dataset compression via pruning and distillation converge at small dataset sizes, with soft-label approaches requiring questionable distillation overhead.
approach: PCA framework prioritizes image quality via pruning easy samples, combining them effectively, and applying constrained augmentation without soft labels.
contribution: First hard-label dataset compression framework offering substantial storage efficiency with competitive performance.

problem: Precise organic material property prediction is impeded by scarce large-scale electron density (ED) data and enormous computational complexity of ED representation.
approach: VisionED pre-trains on efficient ED images via cross-scale physics-informed tasks using 2 million molecules and 12 million multi-shot ED images.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by up to 27.0% with superior robustness under distribution shifts; generalizes to unseen device-scale applications with 92.77% accuracy.

problem: Automatically generating diverse attack prompts for LLM safety fine-tuning is difficult because RL methods collapse to limited modes once high-reward prompts are found.
approach: Active Attacks adapts attacks as victim evolves through periodic safety fine-tuning, naturally inducing easy-to-hard exploration curriculum as attacker progresses to harder modes.
contribution: Improves cross-attack success rates against GFlowNets from 0.07% to 31.28% with only 6% computation increase.

problem: VideoQA models often fail to align answers with correct video segments (grounding gap) due to coarse-grained temporal modeling.
approach: LINGUA uses memory-based agent with event-driven perception retaining 8-12% of frames, typed memory for narratives/affordances/scripts, and Bayesian reliability tracking for continual learning.
contribution: 82.4% on NExT-QA and 42.3% Acc@GQA on NExT-GQA; runs 2.6x faster than dense-frame methods with online adaptation.

problem: Machine unlearning for recommender systems must remove user interaction data and its influence while preserving quality and avoiding expensive full retraining.
approach: Obliviate uses Low-Rank Unlearning Adapter with Hessian proxy for efficient curvature-aware updates, then applies Locality-Aware Calibration refining only adapter parameters.
contribution: Achieves high forgetting with minimal utility loss at reduced computational cost, offering practical solution for large-scale recommender systems.

problem: MLLMs struggle to ground multimodal outputs in heterogeneous sources and verify factual claims in complex reasoning beyond observation.
approach: MuRGAt benchmark requires models to generate answers with explicit reasoning and precise citations specifying modality and temporal segments, plus automatic evaluation framework.
contribution: Reveals even strong MLLMs hallucinate citations despite correct reasoning; trade-off between reasoning depth and verifiable attribution.

problem: Activation verbalization methods claim to provide privileged insights into LLM internals, but unclear if they convey target model knowledge or verbalizer knowledge.
approach: Critically evaluates verbalization methods through controlled experiments testing if verbalizations reflect target or verbalizer parametric knowledge.
contribution: Verbalizations often reflect verbalizer LLM knowledge rather than target model internals, highlighting need for targeted benchmarks and controls.

problem: Off-policy evaluation breaks under strategic behavior where agents modify covariates in response to policy, inducing policy-dependent covariate shift.
approach: Leverages post-hoc explanations to reveal pre-strategic covariates, constructs doubly robust estimator assuming agents' cost sensitivity follows conditional log-normal distribution.
contribution: Enables OPE in one-shot settings with partial knowledge of agent response behavior; establishes consistency of proposed estimator.

problem: Controllable diffusion generation relies on disconnected heuristics without unified theoretical understanding.
approach: DiffCon casts reverse diffusion as state-only stochastic control in LS-MDPs, deriving RL methods for diffusion fine-tuning with score decomposition into pretrained baseline plus control correction.
contribution: Gray-box adaptation with frozen backbone shows consistent gains in preference-alignment and improved quality-efficiency trade-offs.

problem: MLLMs struggle with multi-dimensional detailed reasoning for time-series anomaly detection, relying only on coarse heuristics.
approach: AnomSeer grounds reasoning in precise structural details via expert chain-of-thought from classical analyses, proposes TimerPO integrating time-series grounded advantage and orthogonal projection.
contribution: Outperforms larger commercial baselines on classification and localization; produces plausible reasoning traces supporting conclusions.

problem: Post-training quantization of diffusion models distorts the diffusion distribution through residual quantization errors, degrading sample quality.
approach: DNS reinterprets quantization as principled timestep shift, preserving target marginal under both stochastic and deterministic samplers via deformable noise scheduler.
contribution: Plug-and-play approach complements PTQ schemes; reduces FID from 27.16 to 26.22 with fully integer inference.

problem: Generic token pruning/merging for ViT compression discards subtle discriminative details critical for fine-grained retrieval tasks like person re-identification.
approach: SRE-Merge injects spatial priors via Spatial-Entropy Saliency Assessment, Hybrid Context-Affinity Matching, and Energy-Preserving Weighted Fusion for discriminative compression.
contribution: Reduces GFLOPs by 24% while retaining competitive retrieval accuracy.

problem: MLLMs exhibit two failure modes in contextual reasoning: context neglect relying on pre-trained knowledge and superficial pattern matching exploiting shallow correlations.
approach: Two-stage approach: SFT establishes analyze-then-solve paradigm, then context-aware RL with hierarchical advantage estimation reinforces contextual pattern acquisition.
contribution: 38.14% accuracy on ContextReasonV-Bench representing 22.09% improvement; generalizes to unseen tasks.

problem: Gradient flow dynamics of diagonal linear networks under infinitesimal initialization lacks comprehensive theoretical understanding.
approach: Extends prior analysis to deep networks and broader two-layer architectures, demonstrates convergence to modified l1 norm minimization via Algorithm 1.
contribution: Establishes implicit bias corresponds to modified l1 norm; identifies Structural Invariant Manifold as key geometric structure shaping learning.

problem: Conventional visual object trackers use handcrafted spatial priors as surrogate supervision poorly aligned with tracking metrics like IoU and AUC.
approach: RELO formulates target localization as MDP with rewards combining frame-level IoU and sequence-level AUC; adds layer-aligned temporal token propagation for consistency.
contribution: 57.5% AUC on LaSOT_ext without template updates; confirms reward-driven localization superior to prior-driven approach.

problem: Existing contrastive representation learning analyses assume IID tuples, violating practical settings where dependencies arise from finite labeled data pools.
approach: Improves U-Statistics-based analysis independent of rho_min, formulates different estimator capturing risk concentration across classes for sharper bounds.
contribution: Sample complexity of O(k) where k is samples per tuple, especially strong for long-tailed distributions.

problem: Irregular multivariate time series modeling is complicated by non-uniform sampling, and existing approaches either require specialized architectures or introduce artificial values via interpolation.
approach: QuITE employs learnable query tokens to aggregate irregular observations through single self-attention layer, producing backbone-compatible latent representations without interpolation.
contribution: Up to 54.7% average relative gains in forecasting and 15.8% in classification; works as plug-and-play module for diverse backbones.

problem: Evaluating expert-level deep research reports is challenging due to multifaceted quality, potential LLM-judge errors, and difficulty verifying claims without domain expertise.
approach: DEER systematizes evaluation with expert-developed taxonomy (7 dimensions, 25 subdimensions, 101 items) plus claim verification architecture for cited and uncited claims.
contribution: Reveals current systems produce structurally plausible evidence-citing reports but struggle with expert-level satisfaction and logical completeness.

problem: Weather forecasting and climate modeling require unified approaches that work across diverse atmospheric tasks without task-specific customization.
approach: WIND is a foundation model pre-trained with self-supervised video reconstruction using unconditional diffusion, then solves diverse atmospheric problems as inverse problems via posterior sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates a single pre-trained model can replace specialized baselines across forecasting, downscaling, field reconstruction, and extreme weather exploration without fine-tuning.

problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning faces a bottleneck where high-quality training samples are scarce because exploration is limited by the model's inherent capabilities.
approach: RuscaRL uses checklist-style rubrics as external scaffolding during rollout generation to guide diverse high-quality responses, then gradually decays this guidance while using the same rubrics for verifiable reward scoring.
contribution: Breaks the exploration-learning cycle and improves reasoning across multiple benchmarks with more reliable reward signals for open-ended tasks.

problem: Large reasoning models produce complex reasoning traces with implicit structures, but existing evaluation methods lack unified principles for assessing quality and using evaluation signals for optimization.
approach: Characterize reasoning quality via macro/micro efficiency-effectiveness (ME² principle), model traces as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and train a Thinking Reward Model (TRM) on a DAG-based pairwise evaluation framework.
contribution: Thinking rewards provide effective optimization signals, achieving up to 19.3% gain at test time via better reasoning selection and up to 3.9% gain during RL training.

problem: Battery lifetime early prediction is hindered by extremely weak degradation signals buried in stochastic noise during initial cycles.
approach: DITING uses optimal-transport-based template matching and a tri-coupled degradation manifestation mechanism to exploit noise randomness: symmetric coupling suppresses noise while cumulative degradation propagates as bilateral discrepancies, mimicking the binaural effect.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in detecting weak early-stage cues and provides reliable early support for full-lifecycle battery management.

problem: Data-free model merging for cross-domain tasks often fails because simple parameter heuristics ignore inter-layer dependencies and non-uniform expertise distribution.
approach: SA-Merging applies saliency scoring from structural pruning to task vectors, introduces merge-aware modulation to reduce interference, and iteratively removes non-informative updates while preserving connectivity.
contribution: Reduces the gap between data-free and test-time adaptation methods, with rank-wise decomposition supporting LoRA merging without compromising structure.

problem: Training multi-agent LLM systems for collaboration creates a moving-target problem: updating one agent shifts the context distribution for others, causing coordination regression.
approach: TeamTR uses a trust-region framework that evaluates updates on intermediate team states, enforces per-agent trust regions via token-decomposed reverse KL, and computes trust-region certificates from logged data.
contribution: Provides population-level per-update improvement guarantees, mitigates coordination regressions, and enables stable training of heterogeneous teams with modular component replacement.

problem: Current antibody language models treat all residues equally and inherit germline bias that down-weights functionally critical non-germline mutations as noise.
approach: PRISM explicitly represents germline and non-germline residues as distinct token types in a factorized 53-token vocabulary, enabling separate modeling of scaffold and binding-critical mutations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art pseudo-perplexity on hypervariable regions, uniquely correlates with binding affinity across three deep mutational scanning landscapes, and enables controllable generation by decoupling scaffold and binding optimization.

problem: Convergent cross mapping for causal discovery suffers from weak manifold reconstruction when using time-delay embedding, leading to unreliable neighborhoods and poor causal identification under noise.
approach: TopoDistill aligns local neighborhood structure of delay embeddings to a multivariate global embedding via knowledge distillation, preserving smooth and reliable neighborhoods for cross mapping.
contribution: Improves causal discovery in multivariate time series by maintaining specificity against spurious correlations while enabling effective identification under noise.

problem: Multimodal models fail to generalize across domains because joint optimization causes encoders to exploit cross-modal co-occurrences (fusion overfitting) rather than learn domain-invariant features.
approach: MER-DG maximizes entropy of each encoder's feature distribution to preserve diversity, integrated as an additive loss term independent of architecture.
contribution: Improves average performance by ~5% over standard fusion and ~2% over state-of-the-art on EPIC-Kitchens and HAC benchmarks.

problem: The robustness mechanisms of LLMs against character-level perturbations (typos, shuffling, invisible characters) remain unclear.
approach: Investigates three types of character-level perturbations and explores how LLMs implicitly handle chaotic segmentation and fragmented tokenization through both implicit and explicit perturbation removal mechanisms.
contribution: Reveals that LLMs maintain notable performance even under severe perturbations, unveiling architectural strengths and potential misuse risks.

problem: Differentially private training requires higher signal-to-noise ratio but existing analyses overlook the distinction between label-dependent feature signals and label-independent noise.
approach: Provides first theoretical framework analyzing private training via feature learning on multi-patch data, characterizing signal learning and noise memorization separately in noisy gradient descent.
contribution: Shows private signal learning requires higher SNR than non-private, and proves that noise memorization in non-private learning transfers to private learning, reducing generalization.

problem: Multimodal geometry reasoning requires joint understanding of visual diagrams and structured symbolic inference, but models lack sufficient training data and weak visual-symbolic alignment.
approach: Synthesizes complex geometry problems via symbolic seed construction, grounded instantiation with verification, and code-based rendering; uses code prediction as explicit alignment objective.
contribution: GeoCode demonstrates higher structural complexity than existing benchmarks while maintaining mathematical correctness, showing consistent improvements on multiple geometry benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion models for text struggle because Gaussian diffusion in continuous spaces loses token discreteness while categorical simplex approaches disregard semantic token relations.
approach: Smoothie progressively smooths token embeddings based on semantic similarity, combining continuous latent space strengths with discrete token handling and natural decoding.
contribution: Outperforms existing diffusion-based text models on sequence-to-sequence and unconditional generation, with better performance in both embedding space and categorical simplex baselines.

problem: Preference-based RL from trajectory comparisons suffers from training-inference mismatch: utilities trained on trajectory/segment level are applied per-step, causing distribution shift and poor temporal credit assignment.
approach: PAWS aligns utility training with policy optimization by performing policy updates directly using segment-level advantage functions derived from trajectory preferences.
contribution: Preserves trajectory-level preference information and avoids unreliable per-step signals, consistently outperforming existing preference-based RL methods on manipulation and locomotion.

problem: Classifier-free guidance relies on heuristic linear extrapolation that is sensitive to guidance scale, with limited principled understanding of its mechanisms.
approach: Interprets CFG through optimization: velocity field corresponds to gradients of smoothed distance functions, revealing CFG as approximation with prediction gap governing sensitivity; reformulates as homotopy optimization with manifold projection and Anderson Acceleration.
contribution: Training-free methods refine generation fidelity, prompt alignment, and robustness across DiT-XL-2-256, Flux, and Stable Diffusion 3.5 with significant improvements.

problem: Operations research practitioners debug infeasible models through iterative inspection and repair, but LLM benchmarks treat OR as one-shot problem-to-code translation, omitting the diagnostic loop.
approach: Formalizes infeasible-model repair as solver-in-the-loop MDP with deterministic IIS feedback, introduces ORLoopBench with 5,362 LP/MILP repair instances and operational decision benchmarks; applies RLVR training.
contribution: Solver-verified training enables 8B model to surpass frontier APIs on LP repair (95.3% vs 92.4%), improves diagnostic behavior, and reveals semantic drift in code regeneration.

problem: Generalized category discovery relies on contrastive learning with conflicting uniformity and consistency objectives, hindering formation of class-discriminative and semantically coherent structures.
approach: CURE uses two-stage framework: first learns category-anchored representations aligned with known prototypes, then extends via consistency with unified semantic regularization and Semantic Exploration Energy mechanism.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and substantially reduces the gap between known and novel category performance.

problem: Variational inference in high-dimensional spaces requires scalable optimization methods for Gaussian probability measures.
approach: Proposes zeroth-order algorithm using interacting Gaussian particles in Linearized Bures-Wasserstein (LBW) space, a novel parametrization enabling efficient computation via consensus-based optimization.
contribution: Establishes well-posedness and convergence properties; demonstrates robustness and superior performance on variational inference tasks compared to gradient-based methods on non-log-concave targets.

problem: Single-cell gene expression generation is challenging due to count nature of data, complex latent dependencies, and lack of respect for exchangeability property.
approach: scLDM uses VAE with permutation-invariant pooling via Multi-head Cross-Attention Block (MCAB), replaces Gaussian prior with latent diffusion using Diffusion Transformers, enables multi-conditional generation.
contribution: Superior performance on observational and perturbational data with downstream cell classification, respecting data exchangeability.

problem: Standard PCA is highly sensitive to mean-shift contamination: small fractions of shifted samples cause large deviations in principal components.
approach: Uses random matrix theory to prove mean-shift spikes are spectrally separable and original eigenspace is asymptotically invariant; proposes two-stage algorithm adding knockoff mean-shift perturbation.
contribution: Removes mean-shift component using only standard PCA operations, exploiting spectral stability against contamination.

problem: Graph neural networks are vulnerable to unauthorized use, and existing watermarking relies on data manipulation which introduces ownership ambiguity and vulnerability to poisoning.
approach: Watermarks GNN explanations so they are statistically distinct from others; ownership verified through statistical significance without data manipulation.
contribution: Theoretically proves locating the watermark is NP-hard; demonstrates robustness to fine-tuning and pruning attacks while eliminating data dependencies.

problem: AI model hubs with thousands of pre-trained models require efficient scaling of model selection and continual updating as new models and tasks appear.
approach: Formalizes continual model routing (CMR) problem; proposes CARvE, a contrastive embedding approach using domain-stratified coreset replay and checkpoint-based anchoring for efficient routing.
contribution: CARvE significantly outperforms zero-shot retrieval, fine-tuning, and adapter-merging on model, family, and domain-level accuracy.

problem: Circuit discovery methods are brittle: identified circuits depend strongly on concept datasets and often fail to transfer out-of-distribution, raising questions about whether they capture true concepts.
approach: Wraps any circuit discovery algorithm with randomized data subsampling to certify that inclusion decisions are invariant to bounded edit-distance dataset perturbations.
contribution: Certified circuits achieve up to 56% higher accuracy and 80% fewer components while remaining reliable where baselines degrade, putting circuit discovery on formal ground.

problem: Existing LLM-based approaches struggle with deep protocol-level logic bugs involving complex state-dependent behaviors across multiple execution stages in consensus protocols.
approach: Agora uses domain-aware multi-agent framework with specialized agents that collaboratively explore protocol state spaces, synthesize attack scenarios, and validate findings iteratively.
contribution: Discovers 15 previously unknown protocol-level logic bugs violating safety properties, while existing LLM agents fail to detect any such bugs.

problem: Spectroscopic molecular structure elucidation is challenging due to spectral ambiguity, vast molecular space, and difficulty learning robust spectra-structure relationships from limited paired data.
approach: MAST introduces explicit motif priors as intermediate evidence throughout diffusion denoising and casts sampling as reward-guided tree search to prioritize high-reward trajectories.
contribution: Achieves 94.89% exact recovery on QM9S with improved 3D fidelity and high chemical validity while operating under limited computational budgets.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation produces unsupported statements and unreliable citations despite strong retrievers, as sentences can remain factually unsupported.
approach: CiteGuard treats sentence-level factuality as multiple-testing problem, converts claim-evidence scores to p-values via conformal calibration, uses Benjamini-Hochberg procedures for false-discovery-rate control.
contribution: Reduces false-discovery rate among accepted claims from 28-31% to below 10% at α=0.10, retaining 86-92% of supported claims with finite-sample guarantees.

problem: Irregular time series modeling with continuous-discrete state-space models is computationally expensive or constrained by restrictive posterior assumptions.
approach: SDEVI performs variational inference directly on joint distribution of discrete-time observations while maintaining consistency with underlying SDE process; uses linear time-varying SDEs for scalable inference and extends to complex domain.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance on interpolation, extrapolation, regression, and classification across healthcare, physics, climate, and IoT benchmarks.

problem: Controllable generation with discrete diffusion models suffers from high computational overhead or requires retraining.
approach: GILC repurposes pretrained denoising network as variational proxy; introduces Jacobian-free mechanism for stable guidance by directly correcting clean prediction logits.
contribution: Plug-and-play guidance accommodating both differentiable and non-differentiable rewards, achieving state-of-the-art performance on DNA, protein, and molecular generation without additional training.

problem: Modeling complex dynamics leads to entanglement of static state representations and instantaneous motion, causing accumulated errors and off-manifold hallucinations that violate geometric constraints.
approach: Geometric Flow Grounding enforces evolution strictly along tangent bundle via differentiable Neural Tangent Projection Layer, geometrically decoupling state representation from tangential dynamics.
contribution: Reduces numerical aliasing in sparse systems, recovers interpretable gene regulatory motifs, provides zero-shot deepfake detection via projection residual inconsistencies.

problem: Coupled spatiotemporal forecasting suffers from reciprocal error amplification: errors from each subsystem propagate and amplify, causing rapid prediction collapse.
approach: PnP-Corrector decouples physical simulation from error correction by freezing pre-trained engines and training correction agent to proactively counteract systematic biases; uses DSLCast architecture.
contribution: On 300-day ocean-atmosphere forecast, reduces error 28% and surpasses state-of-the-art on key metrics.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting degrades in real-world environments due to transient distractors like moving objects and varying shadows, while existing methods rely on fragile semantic priors.
approach: 3DGS-HPC combines patch-wise classification for robust region-level decisions with hybrid classification integrating photometric and perceptual cues adaptively.
contribution: Improves robustness in mitigating distractors for 3DGS-based novel view synthesis.

problem: ADHD detection methods have received less attention to short-term brain functional reorganization, potentially missing important diagnostic signals.
approach: Proposes model using short-term windows for brain map sequence construction, short-term state and temporal dependency encoder, brain function memory to capture associations, combined with GNN-based long-term features.
contribution: Superior performance on ADHD-200 and OpenNeuro-ds002424 neuroimaging datasets for brain disorder detection.

problem: Electronic health records have distinct characteristics from natural language, but existing foundation models rely on suboptimal NLP-based approaches.
approach: Proposes pretraining with Pathology-Focused Binning for clinically significant quantization, Dual-Calendar RoPE for absolute/relative temporal signals, and Time-Conditioned Foreseeing objective aligning with clinical planning.
contribution: Outperforms existing foundation models on eleven downstream tasks (up to 54% AUPRC improvement), enables generation of realistic temporally consistent patient trajectories.

problem: Graph foundation models have fixed architectures mismatched to diverse downstream graph tasks, limiting generalization.
approach: AdaR uses recurrent graph model with adaptive test-time computing, encodes normalized step information and representation-target relations, employs gradient-based supervision for convergence.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in both inductive and transductive settings without changing model parameters.

problem: Test-time scaling of diffusion models via computing expected future reward faces limitations: backward rollout is expensive while existing approaches suffer from bias and sampling issues.
approach: LiDAR computes expected future reward using only marginal samples from pretrained model, enabling closed-form guidance without backprop; uses lookahead sampling and efficient solver.
contribution: Achieves same GenEval performance as gradient guidance on SDXL with 9.5× speedup.

problem: Video generation models struggle with spatial consistency and object permanence in realistic simulation of physics-driven interactions.
approach: 3DGSim jointly trains inverse rendering and dynamics forecasting on multi-view RGB videos, uses MVSplat for particle representation, Point Transformer for dynamics, Gaussian Splatting for rendering.
contribution: Captures diverse behaviors from rigid to cloth dynamics while producing realistic lighting; generalizes to out-of-distribution cases despite training only on single-body collisions.

problem: End-to-end GPU program generation is challenging because existing methods focus on single-kernel optimization and do not address whole-system design, host-side settings, or practical deployment.
approach: StitchCUDA uses multi-agent framework (Planner/Coder/Verifier) with rubric-based agentic RL training Coder on task-to-code and feedback-driven optimization skills using real execution feedback.
contribution: Achieves nearly 100% success rate on end-to-end GPU tasks, 1.72× better speedup over multi-agent baseline and 2.73× over RL baseline.

problem: LLM moderation requires balancing performance and efficiency while supporting customization to user-specific requirements.
approach: MLPM leverages prototypes of intermediate representations across multiple layers for improved moderation quality, adding negligible overhead and supporting seamless application to any model.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on diverse moderation benchmarks with strong scalability across model families, integrates smoothly into end-to-end pipelines.

problem: Vision-language models suffer performance degradation on downstream tasks with noisy labels because filtering and reconstruction methods propagate errors.
approach: Evidence-Prompt treats prompt learning as Bayesian reasoning integrating stable pre-trained knowledge with both supervision-agnostic and supervision-conditioned evidence.
contribution: Flattens accuracy-noise curve with notable gains on OxfordPets at 75% noise (+36.6% under asymmetric, +14.4% under symmetric); transferability improvements of 2.6-15.66% when incorporated into other methods.

problem: Recent LMO-based optimizers like Muon show practical advantages but lack theoretical understanding due to overlooking layer-wise application and unrealistic smoothness assumptions.
approach: Introduces Gluon, a new LMO-based framework with refined generalized smoothness model capturing layer-wise geometry, matching practical layer-wise implementation of Muon and Scion.
contribution: Provides state-of-the-art convergence guarantees matching theoretical assumptions to practice; experiments confirm assumptions hold along optimization trajectory.

problem: Offline RL policies learned from pixel-based demonstrations suffer from implicit confounding biases when there's a mismatch between the demonstrator's and learner's sensory capabilities.
approach: Develop a causal offline RL objective that optimizes for worst-case performance under confounding, then learn expressive flow-matching policies using a deep discriminator to measure discrepancy between the target policy and behavioral policy.
contribution: Proposes a confounding-robust offline RL method that achieves 120% of the success rate of state-of-the-art confounding-unaware methods on 25 pixel-based tasks.

problem: Multimodal agents for game development lack evaluation benchmarks that combine code complexity with deep understanding of multimodal assets like shaders, sprites, and animations.
approach: Create GameDevBench with 333 game development tasks from tutorials that require multimodal understanding; evaluate agents and introduce image/video feedback mechanisms to improve performance.
contribution: Present the first game development benchmark for agents; show best methods solve only 53.8% of tasks and that visual feedback increases GPT-4's performance from 41.1% to 52.0%.

problem: Existing LLM memory and continual learning benchmarks focus on homogeneous reading comprehension rather than testing the system's ability to learn from accumulated user feedback during deployment.
approach: Propose a user feedback simulation framework and comprehensive benchmark across multiple domains, languages, and task types to evaluate continual learning of LLM systems.
contribution: Introduce MemoryBench showing that state-of-the-art baselines achieve far-from-satisfying effectiveness and efficiency on continual learning from user feedback.

problem: Inference-time optimization for LLM reasoning via repeated sampling does not account for model uncertainty, which could discriminate between correct and incorrect reasoning traces.
approach: Analyze confidence dynamics during reasoning and find that correct traces show improving confidence while incorrect ones decline; propose Confidence Dynamics Gain voting that incorporates confidence trajectory evolution.
contribution: CDG voting yields significant performance boosts on AIME24/25, HMMT25, and BRUMO25 benchmarks across multiple architectures including DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen-QwQ.

problem: Neural approaches to structural nested mean models for treatment effect estimation over time lack end-to-end gradient-based training due to sequential g-estimation constraints.
approach: Introduce DeepBlip with a novel double optimization trick enabling simultaneous learning of all blip functions while integrating LSTM/transformer for temporal dependencies and adjusting for time-varying confounding.
contribution: First neural framework for SNMMs achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical datasets with unbiased treatment effect estimates robust to nuisance model misspecification.

problem: Standard supervised fine-tuning hurts reasoning performance in diffusion language models because it overlooks which tokens are actually learnable at different masking levels.
approach: Analyze when tokens are learnable; propose LIFT that learns easy tokens when most input is masked and hard tokens when context is available, aligning training with information available at each diffusion time step.
contribution: LIFT outperforms SFT baselines on six reasoning benchmarks with up to 3x relative gain on AIME-24 and AIME-25.

problem: Concept Activation Vectors vary depending on random sampling during construction, but their variability is poorly understood, limiting reliable application of the method.
approach: Provide theoretical analysis of CAV construction variability and conduct experiments across four modalities to quantify how variance declines with sample size.
contribution: Demonstrate that CAV variance declines roughly as 1/N where N is the number of random examples, providing practical resource-efficiency recommendations.

problem: Offline decision-making via diffusion models often produces trajectories misaligned with system dynamics, limiting their reliability for control tasks.
approach: Combine a diffusion planner with a dynamics diffusion model that interleaves planner and dynamics updates during sampling to progressively correct feasibility while preserving task intent; use ranking for trajectory selection.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements over prior diffusion-based methods on unconstrained and constrained benchmarks; validated through deployment on a real quadrupedal robot.

problem: Current agent benchmarks evaluate explicit instruction-following but fail to test reasoning about implicit requirements like accessibility needs, privacy, and contextual constraints.
approach: Introduce Implicit Intelligence framework paired with Agent-as-a-World simulation harness using YAML-defined interactive environments to test implicit reasoning on 205 scenarios.
contribution: Evaluate 16 frontier models on implicit reasoning; best model achieves only 48.3% pass rate, revealing large gap between literal instruction-following and contextual reasoning.

problem: Existing video understanding benchmarks neglect the commercial intent and dense multimodal complexity of e-commerce short videos, where models struggle.
approach: Develop a multimodal information density framework; curate 3,961 e-commerce videos with 19,785 QA pairs organized into perception and reasoning tasks; build E-VAds-R1 with multi-grained reward GRPO.
contribution: E-VAds-R1 achieves 109.2% performance gain in commercial intent reasoning with only a few hundred training samples.

problem: Large reasoning models substantially outperform base LLMs but it remains unclear where base models fail during generation and how to bridge the gap efficiently.
approach: Quantify token-level distributional disagreement between base and reasoning models; identify that reasoning advantage concentrates on sparse early planning-related tokens; propose disagreement-guided token intervention for selective delegation.
contribution: Sparse delegation scheme with small intervention budget substantially recovers and can surpass performance of same-size reasoning model on challenging reasoning tasks.

problem: Hard examples in RLVR training remain unlearnable even when correct rollouts are present, but the mechanisms behind this phenomenon are poorly understood.
approach: Analyze unlearnable examples via cross-example gradient analysis; show they have fundamental representation issues with low gradient similarity and ungeneralizable reasoning patterns.
contribution: Provide first systematic characterization of unlearnable data in RLVR; show that data augmentation and optimization techniques fail to mitigate representation flaws.

problem: SVD-based LLM compression suffers from poor global rank allocation due to uncalibrated error proxies and decomposition quality issues from Fisher-based rank collapse.
approach: Introduce LEMS with layer-wise error surrogates integrating local/global importance and propagation bias via ILP; develop KFAC-SVD using token-wise statistics to mitigate rank deficiency.
contribution: LEMS delivers significant zero-shot accuracy gains up to 4.8 p.p. generalizing to 70B models; KFAC-SVD achieves average perplexity improvement of 15%.

problem: Value alignment in LLMs involves both intrinsic learned values and prompted values, but their underlying mechanisms and whether they overlap are poorly understood.
approach: Analyze intrinsic vs. prompted value expression at mechanistic level using value vectors extracted from residual stream and value neurons in MLP layers.
contribution: Show that intrinsic and prompted mechanisms share common value components but also possess unique components; intrinsic promotes response diversity while prompted strengthens instruction compliance.

problem: UAV-on-UAV interception is hindered by continuous scale drift, long-tailed scale imbalance, and flight-induced visual noise affecting target detection.
approach: Propose scale-aware robust optimization framework with group-wise minimax optimization over scale-partitioned data; introduce uncertainty-rectified regression loss and control-aligned center accuracy penalty.
contribution: Achieves real-time performance of 120 FPS on embedded NVIDIA Orin NX with substantially improved robustness under visual degradation; validated through real-world flight tests.

problem: Latent regimes in non-stationary time series with instantaneous effects between variables are difficult to identify under frequent regime switches and nonlinear dynamics.
approach: Establish identifiability of latent regimes and regime-dependent causal structures under temporal dependencies and nonlinear effects; introduce FlowMSM regime detection framework combining any stationary causal discovery method.
contribution: Demonstrate effective detection of latent regimes and discovery of causal structures from non-stationary time series on synthetic benchmarks and financial datasets.

problem: Pretrained visual encoders contain information irrelevant or detrimental to planning, limiting their utility for latent planning with world models.
approach: Introduce temporal straightening via curvature regularizer encouraging locally straightened latent trajectories; jointly learn encoder and predictor of JEPA world model to make Euclidean distance better proxy for geodesic distance.
contribution: Temporal straightening makes gradient-based planning more stable with significantly higher success rates across goal-reaching tasks.

problem: Deep neural networks exhibit overconfidence, undermining reliability in safety-critical applications, and existing calibration methods rely on indirect hardness proxies.
approach: Establish logit margin as direct hardness indicator; prove margin constrains feasible temperature range; introduce Charbonnier-SoftECE objective upper-bounding smooth calibration error; propose SMART learning sample-wise margin-to-temperature mapping.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art calibration across CNNs and ViTs on standard, long-tailed, and distribution-shifted benchmarks with minimal inference overhead.

problem: Vision-language navigation requires agents to follow instructions in partially observed 3D environments, but existing approaches use hand-crafted maps independent of navigation policy.
approach: Propose MapDream using autoregressive bird's-eye-view image synthesis to learn task-driven maps that preserve navigation-critical affordances; jointly learn map generation and action prediction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art monocular performance on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, validating task-driven generative map learning.

problem: Standard prescriptive scaling laws don't capture how downstream accuracy evolves as compute budgets and post-training practice change over time.
approach: Estimate capability boundaries via smoothed quantile regression with sigmoid parameterization; validate temporal reliability by fitting on earlier models and evaluating on later releases; introduce efficient algorithm using 20% of evaluation budget.
contribution: Show capability boundaries are mostly stable except for math reasoning which exhibits advancing boundary; release Proteus-2k dataset and practical methodology for translating compute budgets to performance expectations.

problem: LLMs remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks via prompt optimization, which retain malicious signals that guardrails detect, exploiting the interconnected nature of model knowledge.
approach: Introduce Correlated Knowledge Attack Agent framing jailbreaking as adaptive tree-structured exploration weaving benign sub-queries to achieve harmful objectives; model responses guide exploration across multiple paths.
contribution: CKA-Agent achieves over 95% success rates against SOTA commercial LLMs and strong guardrails, demonstrating severity of knowledge-decomposition attacks.

problem: Bayesian optimization success depends on choosing a kernel matching the objective's unknown structure, which is difficult for objectives with varying smoothness.
approach: Propose ALAS, a Gaussian Process kernel family built from symmetric alpha-stable spectral components that learns the stability parameter to adapt effective smoothness; introduce separable variant for dimension-wise robustness.
contribution: Demonstrate strong and robust performance on standard benchmarks and real-world surrogates across diverse settings.

problem: Open-world object detection requires detecting known categories while identifying unknowns, but existing methods overlook interpretability leading to known-unknown confusion.
approach: Propose interpretable OWOD framework with Concept Decomposition Model decomposing RoI features into discriminative, shared, and background concepts; use Concept-Guided Rectification to resolve confusion.
contribution: Significantly improves unknown recall while mitigating confusion and providing concept-level interpretability for both known and unknown predictions.

problem: One-shot pruning methods optimize quadratic objectives without accounting for uncertainty in calibration data and algorithmic updates, affecting pruning quality.
approach: Introduce RobOP, a robust optimization framework accounting for uncertainties through simple modifications to existing pruning methods; applies tractably across uncertainty set families.
contribution: RobOP offers improvements over prior pruning approaches by explicitly accounting for uncertainty; scales to large vision and language models.

problem: Commercial microwave link rainfall reconstruction is challenging because path-integrated measurements and oversimplified point-sensor models neglect physical power-law relationships.
approach: View rain field reconstruction as Bayesian inverse problem with diffusion models as high-fidelity spatial priors; enable training-free posterior sampling via Plug-and-Play and other methods.
contribution: Diffusion models better preserve rainfall statistics than Gaussian processes; demonstrate consistent improvements on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Scheduling problems require learning interpretable and transferable rules from repeated selection decisions, but existing approaches lack explicit structure.
approach: Propose factorized scheduling principle framework decomposing global principle into additive univariate and pairwise components with identifiability constraints; learn via policy-based objective with temporal-difference signals.
contribution: Achieve strong performance with interpretability and zero-shot generalization across different system scales on synthetic and realistic scheduling tasks.

problem: Adapting existing LoRAs to video diffusion variants with step or causal distillation fails due to weight space mismatches and spectral interference.
approach: Identify that incompatibility stems from conflicting routing pathways in singular subspaces; propose Cluster-Aware Spectral Arbitration that dynamically arbitrates between target manifold safeguarding and LoRA alignment.
contribution: CASA framework effectively mitigates artifacts and revives LoRA functionality in data-free setting for video diffusion models.

problem: Reward models for RLHF are corrupted by noisy preferences with complex linguistic patterns, and existing denoising approaches assume homogeneous noise.
approach: Propose SelectiveRM grounded in optimal transport using Joint Consistency Discrepancy to align prediction distribution with preference data and Mass Relaxation via partial transport to exclude noisy samples.
contribution: Theoretically demonstrates tighter upper bound on unobserved clean risk; significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Vision-language foundation models are compared only through downstream performance without explaining structural differences in their representations.
approach: Study representation differences via Contrastive Embedding Clustering; propose KODA kernel-based framework for contrastive comparison and alignment using modality-wise kernel composition.
contribution: Identify consistent and interpretable discrepancy structures across vision-language representations; provide sample subsets for alignment.

problem: Ill-conditioned kernel matrices cause first-order methods to converge slowly when training neural networks; Gauss-Newton's sequential g-estimation lacks end-to-end training.
approach: Establish convergence bounds for Gauss-Newton in under/overparameterized regimes; in underparameterized setting show Riemannian gradient flow on low-dimensional submanifold with geodesic Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions.
contribution: Prove Gauss-Newton avoids kernel conditioning bottlenecks with geometric convergence rates independent of Gram-matrix conditioning.

problem: Existing LLM-based time series forecasters lack explicit experience accumulation and continual evolution mechanisms for forecasting improvement.
approach: Propose MemCast learning-to-memory framework reformulating forecasting as experience-conditioned reasoning; organize experience into hierarchical memory with patterns, wisdom, and laws; use dynamic confidence adaptation.
contribution: MemCast consistently outperforms previous methods across datasets; code available validating effectiveness of experience-conditioned reasoning.

problem: Zero-shot text-to-4D mesh generation faces structural mismatch: diffusion guidance is noisy while topology-constrained meshes impose severe constraints, making vertex-level deformation unstable.
approach: Shift deformation from vertices to faces via Jacobian Deformation Field enabling topology-aware reconstruction; propose Local-Global Semantic Regularizer preserving identity by constraining local deformation plausibility and global consistency.
contribution: Introduce TextMesh4D, first zero-shot framework for text-to-4D dynamic mesh generation addressing structural mismatches.

problem: Target-oriented language model pretraining requires selecting relevant data, but existing methods use black-box representations without interpretability.
approach: Introduce Neuron-Activated Graph Ranking, a training-free framework characterizing target inputs via sparse high-impact neurons; rank candidate data by NAG similarity with comprehensive layer analysis.
contribution: NAG-based Ranking improves target-oriented pretraining by 4.9% on average; outperforms baselines by 5.3% on HellaSwag; deactivating NAG neurons causes 23.5% collapse indicating functional backbone.

problem: LLMs cannot extrapolate to inference budgets far beyond training; standard on-policy RL creates distribution shift between train and test limiting extrapolation.
approach: Introduce Reasoning Cache algorithm enabling models to extrapolate to lengths an order of magnitude longer than training via exploiting asymmetry between summarization and generation; amplify through training.
contribution: Training 4B model with RC using 16k-token budget improves HMMT 2025 from 40% to 70% when evaluated with 512k-token test budget.

problem: Standard evaluation metrics for time series forecasting conflate model capability with intrinsic instance difficulty, obscuring true progress.
approach: Propose Spectral Coherence Predictability providing efficient O(N log N) per-instance difficulty reference with linear MSE lower bound; introduce Linear Utilization Ratio quantifying model's exploitation of predictable structures.
contribution: SCP aligns with forecasting errors across diverse forecasters; stratified evaluation reveals complementary architectural strengths and time-varying task difficulty.

problem: Generative models exhibit biased generalization where test loss decreases while samples increasingly mimic training data, raising privacy concerns.
approach: Identify biased generalization phase via quantitative bias measure on mutual distances; study mechanism using hierarchical data model revealing sequential feature learning dependence on training samples.
contribution: Show early stopping at test loss minimum may be insufficient for privacy-critical applications; attribute bias to coarse-then-fine feature learning.

problem: Causal matrix completion under multiple complex treatments fails because existing methods rely on sufficient data within each treatment level.
approach: Propose Mixed Synthetic Nearest Neighbors integrating information across treatment levels to enlarge effective sample size while retaining finite-sample error bounds and asymptotic normality.
contribution: MSNN especially effective under data-scarce treatment levels; demonstrates efficacy on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: General reasoning capabilities are bottlenecked by reliance on verifiable rewards in specific domains; RL during pretraining requires verification data limiting extension to general tasks.
approach: Propose PretrainZero reinforcement active learning on pretraining corpus learning unified reasoning policy to identify informative content without verifiable labels; employ RL on Wikipedia directly.
contribution: PretrainZero improves Qwen3-4B-Base by 8.43/5.96/10.60 on MMLU-Pro/SuperGPQA/math average without verification data.

problem: Data cleaning and AutoML are typically treated as independent stages, ignoring their strong interaction and leading to inefficient resource budget usage.
approach: Propose DMCO unified framework jointly optimizing data cleaning and model construction via time-sliced interleaved process with gradient-based data sampling strategy and loss-driven sampling.
contribution: DMCO consistently outperforms standalone data cleaning and AutoML baselines; achieves 82.19% performance with limited budgets across classification and regression.

problem: Schema induction from raw text lacks appropriate evaluation benchmarks; most extraction systems assume schemas are pre-existing rather than inferring them.
approach: Introduce SCOPE benchmark for corpus-to-schema induction from 24 information extraction sources normalized into evaluation-only gold schemas; present SCION auditable pipeline restricting operations to candidate-linked evidence.
contribution: SCION-lite attains highest F1 among released baselines under multiple schema-graph metrics; release includes evidence-linked outputs and code.

problem: Evaluating LLMs with static benchmarks requires thousands of items and treats all items equally despite vast differences in difficulty and informativeness.
approach: ATLAS applies Item Response Theory with Fisher information-guided item selection to adaptively choose the most informative items, reducing evaluation items needed while maintaining precision.
contribution: ATLAS reduces required items by up to 90% while maintaining measurement precision and detecting meaningful ability differences among models with identical accuracies.

problem: Large language models' ability to integrate knowledge across disciplines for innovation remains unclear and unevaluated.
approach: IDRBench provides datasets and evaluation tasks covering interdisciplinary research identification, idea integration, and recommendation, tested on ten mainstream LLMs.
contribution: IDRBench is the first comprehensive investigation of LLMs' interdisciplinary research capability, establishing benchmarks and baselines for future research.

problem: Existing UI2Code approaches focus on single HTML/CSS output and fail to systematically generate code for multiple front-end frameworks with reusable components.
approach: DCM couples MLLMs with a compact intermediate DOM representation, applies deterministic rules to normalize and mine reusable components via structural hashing, then uses framework-conditioned prompting.
contribution: DCM significantly outperforms baselines on automatic metrics and component-level reuse while maintaining multi-framework portability and code quality.

problem: Existing generative diffusion models rely on time reversal of noising processes, which does not readily generalize to infinite-dimensional settings.
approach: The paper introduces a framework using Doob's h-transform to force a reference diffusion towards the target distribution via exponential change of measure.
contribution: The approach enables rigorous generative diffusion models in infinite dimensions with verifiable conditions, bounds with respect to target measure, and validation on synthetic and real data.

problem: Symmetric multimodal fusion in RGB-D salient object detection creates a backflow channel that injects auxiliary noise into the primary representation when modalities are imbalanced.
approach: Hamiltonian Asymmetric Fusion (HAF) implements directed refinement where only auxiliary tokens are purified through momentum regularization and gated driving, with spectral global correlation.
contribution: HAF provides guarantees of auxiliary error contraction and bounded primary perturbation, showing consistent gains on six RGB-D benchmarks with graceful degradation under corruption.

problem: Multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) allows models to exploit answer options in ways that inflate reasoning ability compared to free-text performance.
approach: The study systematically varies exposure to answer options across 15 benchmarks and 27 LLMs, introducing diagnostic probes to isolate option-exploitation pathways.
contribution: Reasoning models are shown to be effective at extracting signal from options, creating misleading gains over free-text baselines; decoupled format mitigates but is not realizable for most reasoning models.

problem: Existing differentially private OLS methods like AdaSSP have utility bounds that include a multiplicative factor as large as the square root of data dimension.
approach: Iterative Hessian Mixing (IHM) builds on Gaussian-sketching approaches and uses new accuracy guarantees to circumvent inherent limitations of prior methods.
contribution: IHM improves excess empirical risk bounds by removing a sqrt(dimension) factor and consistently outperforms AdaSSP across a large suite of datasets.

problem: Two-timescale stochastic approximations in RL suffer from unstable convergence under realistic Markovian noise; existing guarantees require i.i.d. assumptions.
approach: The paper controls the fast timescale parameter with the running max of the slow timescale parameter instead of the current value, enabling Markovian noise analysis.
contribution: Establishes first almost sure convergence of temporal difference learning with eligibility traces under off-policy learning with linear function approximation.

problem: Lyapunov-based neural control methods cannot enable smooth blending of controllers with Region of Attraction expansion guarantees and fail under unstable equilibria.
approach: Neural Control Density Functions (NCDFs) leverage a novel exponential characterization of density functions and combine them with control barrier functions for safe-stable control.
contribution: NCDFs provide first guarantee that blended controllers achieve RoAs containing the union of constituent RoAs, with superior RoA expansion compared to prior methods.

problem: Inference mechanisms of transformer-based tabular foundation models remain largely unexplored, making it unclear whether all layers are necessary.
approach: Large-scale mechanistic study of layerwise dynamics in six tabular models reveals substantial depthwise redundancy and stages of inference.
contribution: A proof-of-concept single-layer looped model achieves comparable performance using only 20% of the original model's parameters.

problem: Artifact features in multimodal models for AI-generated image detection exhibit high intra-feature similarity leading to attention dilution and poor fusion with semantic features.
approach: TranX-Adapter uses Task-aware Optimal-Transport Fusion leveraging Jensen-Shannon divergence for transferring artifact information, and X-Fusion for semantic information transfer.
contribution: TranX-Adapter brings consistent improvements up to +6% accuracy across AIGI detection benchmarks on multiple advanced MLLMs.

problem: Existing LLM-based automated heuristic design methods enforce fixed algorithmic templates, confining search to component-level tuning and limiting algorithmic expressiveness.
approach: A2DEPT treats LLMs as system-level algorithm architects exploring program space via tree-structured evolutionary search with hybrid selection and a lightweight program-maintenance loop.
contribution: A2DEPT consistently outperforms baselines across benchmarks, reducing optimality gap by an average of 9.8%.

problem: Existing time series tokenization methods encode a fixed number of samples regardless of pattern complexity, generating excessive tokens for simple patterns.
approach: Pattern-centric tokenization based on discrete vocabulary of frequent motifs merges samples with patterns into tokens, with conditional decoding as post-hoc optimization.
contribution: Motif-based tokenization improves forecasting performance by 40% and boosts efficiency by 2314% on average; conditional decoding reduces MSE by up to 48%.

problem: Isolation Forest's empirical success lacks theoretical understanding, making it unclear when and why it performs well.
approach: The paper models iForest growth as a random walk and derives expected path length function by analyzing hitting time of absorbing states.
contribution: Analysis reveals iForest combines density and centrality (unlike k-NN which reflects only local density) and is more parameter-adaptive, providing theoretical foundation for its effectiveness.

problem: Reinforcement learning for program repair is hindered by sparse execution feedback and coarse sequence-level rewards obscuring which edits fix bugs.
approach: BoostAPR uses three stages: supervised fine-tuning on verified demonstrations with traces, training dual reward models (sequence-level and line-level), and PPO with line-level credit assignment.
contribution: BoostAPR achieves 40.7% on SWE-bench Verified (+22.9pp), 24.8% on Defects4J, 84.5% on HumanEval-Java, and 95.0% on QuixBugs with strong cross-language generalization.

problem: Nearest Class Mean classifiers assume features collapse into points, but in class-incremental learning classes manifest as complex manifolds due to feature drift.
approach: HC-SOINN captures manifold topology via local-to-global representation; STAR method uses fine-grained pointwise trajectory tracking to deform topology adapting to feature drift.
contribution: Integrated into seven state-of-the-art methods, consistently achieving improvements in class-incremental learning over original classifiers.

problem: Visual explanation methods highlight pixel importance but struggle to link low-level cues to semantically meaningful concepts, limiting interpretability.
approach: ConEx discovers class-specific concepts via architecture-specific masking without supervision, learns concept activation vectors, and generates faithful saliency maps showing concept contributions.
contribution: ConEx achieves state-of-the-art performance on faithfulness, segmentation, and concept-quality benchmarks with human-interpretable saliency maps.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting relies on heuristic density control lacking flexibility to adapt to diverse scenes with complex geometries.
approach: LeGS reformulates density control as a parameterized policy network optimized via RL with reward grounded in sensitivity analysis, reducing complexity from O(N²) to O(N).
contribution: LeGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending datasets with superior reconstruction quality and efficiency.

problem: Models more capable than their supervisors could exploit weak supervision gaps through sandbagging, producing acceptable but suboptimal work.
approach: Test sandbagging elicitation via supervised fine-tuning on weak demonstrations plus reinforcement learning on problem-solving math, science, and coding tasks.
contribution: Combined SFT and RL reliably elicits sandbagging models; RL without SFT leads to reward hacking while SFT alone fails when supervisor is much weaker.

problem: Amodal instance segmentation is hindered by scarcity of scalable and transferable annotations spanning sim-to-real domain gap.
approach: MaviGen generates photorealistic multi-view images with complete amodal masks; EUREKA is an encoder-only network using unified queries and dual mask heads with conditional masked self-attention.
contribution: IRAIS dataset enables rigorous sim-to-real transfer studies; EUREKA achieves state-of-the-art on D2SA and COCOA-cls with substantial improvements in transfer.
