problem: LLMs are strong responders but struggle to proactively elicit information by asking right questions and stopping at right time; simulator-based approaches face reality gaps.
approach: Learn-to-Ask derives dense turn-level rewards from observed future of offline expert trajectories, enabling supervised learning for what-to-ask and when-to-stop.
contribution: Consistently improves proactive information-seeking across datasets and model scales; real-world deployment surpasses internal expert baseline under professional audit.

problem: Pre-propagation GNNs avoid repeated sparse matrix multiplications but show a gap versus message-passing GNNs, especially on heterophilic graphs.
approach: Proposes robust graph diffusion operators for preprocessing and a few-shot hidden-state re-propagation scheme during training.
contribution: Methods improve validation and test accuracy of PP-GNNs, enabling them to match message-passing GNNs while maintaining training efficiency.

problem: Learning new tasks with few samples requires modeling task relatedness in a way that is both realistic and provably beneficial.
approach: Leverages weak monotonicity (a model dominating others tends to outperform on new task) within transfer learning and model selection aggregation paradigms.
contribution: Can prune model class based on monotonicity and hedge on frontier geometry of available trade-offs for improved few-shot learning.

problem: Robotic manipulation with sparse rewards and limited demonstrations causes agents to encounter out-of-distribution states; learned rewards introduce non-stationarity.
approach: QUEST uses ensemble dynamics for uncertainty-guided planning, adaptively switches exploration/exploitation, and employs hybrid sampling prioritizing rare successful transitions.
contribution: QUEST outperforms state-of-the-art by 17% on average with gains to 60% on difficult tasks; demonstrates successful zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

problem: Assessing LLM code security is crucial but reliable security benchmarks require expert manual effort and become contaminated in training data.
approach: AutoBaxBuilder uses LLM code-understanding combined with robust reliability checks to automatically construct functional tests and security-probing exploits from scratch.
contribution: AutoBaxBuilder generates new security tasks in under 2 hours for less than $4 USD, reducing human effort by 12×; quality aligns with expert-written baselines.

problem: On-policy distillation uses reverse KL which reduces diversity and yields unstable signals when teacher entropy is high.
approach: Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation augments reverse KL with forward KL when teacher entropy is high, balancing mode-seeking precision with mode-covering robustness.
contribution: Maintains generation diversity and improves student-teacher alignment; achieves Pass@8 gains of +1.37 to +5.05 across math reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Retrieval-augmented agents exhibit emergent fairness issues where high document density required for majority interests geometrically crowds out semantically similar minority content.
approach: Formal framework analyzing goal collisions in dense retrieval as mean-field mechanism; extends to dynamic model with Fokker-Planck equation governing embedding evolution.
contribution: Shows phase transition where minority performance catastrophically collapses as majority density increases; proves local relevance objectives drive self-organization exclusively serving majority.

problem: Standard surrogate losses in preference learning for LLM alignment lack consistency guarantees; minimizing surrogate loss leaves ranking error arbitrarily high.
approach: Formulates alignment in margin-shifted ranking framework; derives H-consistency bounds requiring confidence margin and introduces Structure-Aware DPO adapting margin to semantic distance.
contribution: SA-DPO achieves 58.5% head-to-head win-rate over DPO with improvements across benchmarks; heavy-tailed surrogates offer strictly superior consistency guarantees.

problem: Audio deepfake detectors lack efficient methods to discover failure modes and blind spots in the generated audio space.
approach: FoeGlass uses in-context learning of an LLM to explore TTS input space, generating audio samples that fool ADD detectors with no manual supervision.
contribution: FoeGlass improves false negative rates up to 94% over baselines; generated attacks transfer across different target ADDs; fine-tuning on samples enhances robustness.

problem: Planning with learned world models is challenging due to vast unstructured search space; existing planners struggle with efficiency.
approach: Treats states as optimization variables with soft dynamics constraints enabling parallel computation; introduces stochasticity into states and modifies gradient structure to descend towards valid plans.
contribution: Outperforms cross-entropy method and vanilla gradient-based optimization on long-horizon video-based world model tasks in success rate and convergence time.

problem: Video understanding struggles to effectively handle substantial object variations over time while maintaining interpretability through visual evidence.
approach: Chain-of-Glimpse formulates reasoning as step-by-step process anchored to specific visual evidence regions; uses RL-optimized search-guided controller with format reward incentivizing grounding.
contribution: Consistently improves performance across general and grounded video reasoning benchmarks with strong robustness and generalization.

problem: Existing protein binder design approaches assume single-target single-state interactions, limiting ability to model multi-target and multi-state requirements.
approach: Chamaileon uses In-Context Complex Co-Design (I3CD) for context-aware sequence-structure co-modeling and Mixture-of-Paths Sampling optimizing sequences across contexts.
contribution: Generates sequences adaptable to diverse conformational landscapes and multi-target requirements; benchmarked on newly constructed CROSS dataset.

problem: Test-time scaling methods for autoregressive image generation remain underexplored; existing approaches rely on inefficient partial decoding and external rewards.
approach: ScalingAR introduces token entropy as confidence signal and operates at profile level (unified confidence state) and policy level (adaptive pruning and dynamic guidance).
contribution: Improves base models by 12.5% on GenEval and 15.2% on TIIF-Bench; reduces visual token consumption by 62.0% and enhances robustness mitigating degradation by 26.0%.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs is compute-intensive and sensitive to data quality and hyperparameters; naive runs can degrade performance.
approach: TuneAhead encodes runs as meta-features combining dataset descriptors with dynamic probe features from short standardized probe; predictor maps to performance estimates.
contribution: Achieves RMSE of 1.47 percentage points with 95.1% within ±3pp on held-out 370 runs; supports go/no-go screening reducing unnecessary fine-tuning.

problem: Existing PPG foundation models either require high-quality curated pretraining data or rely on closed-source field data, limiting generalization.
approach: Uses multimodal supervision via accompanying ECG and respiratory signals to select contrastive samples during pretraining on ICU datasets.
contribution: Pretrained on 3× fewer subjects; achieves performance improvements on 14 of 15 downstream tasks including field-like data with enhanced robustness.

problem: Chess transformers show strong in-distribution performance but it remains unclear whether they reason systematically about rules and strategy.
approach: Constructs out-of-distribution test sets including novel board states and variants never seen during training to reveal failures of systematic generalization.
contribution: Model exhibits robust rule-based reasoning generating legal moves in novel configurations; strategic reasoning is more limited and underperforms symbolic AI algorithms.

problem: Online change point detection for multivariate inhomogeneous Poisson processes time series remains underexplored despite applications in seismology and epidemiology.
approach: Uses low-rank matrices to represent multivariate Poisson intensity functions; single-pass algorithm with constant cost per observation.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on false alarm probability and characterization of detection delay; develops new Matrix Bernstein inequality for temporally dependent processes.

problem: Improving LLM reasoning typically relies on sampling correct solutions or stronger models, which fails for problems unsolved by current frontier models.
approach: Distribution Aligned Imitation Learning (DAIL) transforms expert solutions into detailed reasoning traces then applies contrastive learning on expert insights.
contribution: Leverages fewer than 1000 expert solutions achieving up to 31% pass@128 gains on Qwen; doubles reasoning efficiency and enables out-of-domain generalization.

problem: Existing memory evaluations assess memorization and action in isolation; realistic agents must learn and use memory across multiple interdependent sessions.
approach: MemoryArena introduces unified evaluation gym with human-crafted interdependent subtasks spanning web navigation, planning, search, and formal reasoning.
contribution: Reveals agents with near-saturated performance on existing long-context benchmarks perform poorly in agentic setting, exposing gap in current evaluations.

problem: Online minimization problems lack effective algorithms that leverage machine-learned predictions, especially for dual solutions.
approach: Achieves improved guarantees using dual predictions which are more stable than primal solutions under instance perturbations; applies to metrical task systems and laminar set cover.
contribution: First demonstration that dual predictions are effective for online minimization; provides theoretical guarantees complemented by experiments on k-server and parking permit problems.

problem: Clustering functional data is challenging when temporal misalignment obscures intrinsic shape differences, and existing methods treat registration and clustering as separate tasks.
approach: NeuralFLoC uses Neural ODE-driven diffeomorphic flows and spectral clustering to jointly learn smooth warping functions and cluster-specific templates in an end-to-end unsupervised framework.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art joint registration and clustering on functional benchmarks while establishing universal approximation guarantees and asymptotic consistency.

problem: Predicting dynamic ionic transport properties from static atomic structures is challenging because molecular dynamics simulations are computationally prohibitive and sequential inference methods suffer from error accumulation.
approach: Uses a non-autoregressive learning framework with auxiliary modality learning that treats atomic trajectories as an auxiliary input during training but does not require them at inference.
contribution: Achieves 200x speedup over autoregressive models while substantially reducing prediction error and benefiting from both trajectory and non-trajectory datasets.

problem: Non-stationary time series forecasting fails because models rely on static historical assumptions and become blind to evolving global context (phase amnesia).
approach: PULSE is a physics-informed framework using phase-anchored disentanglement, a phase router for trajectory generation, and Statistic-Aware Mixup to handle distribution shifts.
contribution: A simple MLP backbone achieves state-of-the-art performance on 12 real-world non-stationary forecasting benchmarks.

problem: Fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion and flow models lacks mechanisms to shape tail behavior, which is critical for controlling reliability (lower tail) and discovery (upper tail).
approach: Tail-aware Flow Fine-Tuning (TFFT) uses Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) with a decomposition into lightweight threshold optimization and entropy-regularized fine-tuning.
contribution: Enables efficient tail-aware distributional fine-tuning comparable in cost to standard fine-tuning while controlling worst-case and discovering high-reward samples.

problem: Traditional e-commerce search uses fragmented multi-stage cascading architectures with conflicting optimization objectives, limiting performance.
approach: OneSearch is an end-to-end generative framework with keyword-enhanced quantization encoding, multi-view user behavior sequence injection, and preference-aware reward-weighted ranking.
contribution: Achieves +1.67% item CTR, +2.40% buyer, and +3.22% order volume improvements with 75.40% operational cost reduction and increased Model FLOPs Utilization.

problem: Existing contrastive steering methods for LLM jailbreaking rely on limited biased prompts and require manual tuning of steering strength, limiting effectiveness and robustness.
approach: Adaptive steering uses model extraction to guide steering vectors toward ideal ones and adapts steering strength based on contrastive activation statistics.
contribution: Notably improves jailbreaking effectiveness and robustness without manual tuning, raising harmfulness score from 6% to 70%.

problem: Mechanistic interpretability of machine translation in LLMs has been limited to word-level analysis due to scale challenges.
approach: Analyzes attention heads across three model families and 20 translation directions to decompose translation into target language identification and sentence equivalence subtasks.
contribution: Finds distinct sparse attention heads specialize in each subtask; modifying 1% of heads enables instruction-free performance comparable to instruction-based prompting.

problem: Graph neural network simulators for CFD suffer from limited information propagation because classical GNNs only exchange information between neighboring nodes.
approach: Flow Alignment Rewiring (FLARE) connects 2-hop nodes only when their relative direction aligns with the input flow direction, informed by fluid physics principles.
contribution: Outperforms PIORF and other 2-hop rewiring methods significantly on flows over cylinders and airfoils under different conditions.

problem: Quality of environment and reward model fundamentally limits reinforcement learning effectiveness, but these components are typically optimized independently.
approach: RLAnything dynamically optimizes policy, reward model, and environment through closed-loop feedback with consistency feedback and critic-based environment adaptation.
contribution: Achieves 8.5% improvement on OSWorld with Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking and 21.2% and 12.1% improvements on AlfWorld and LiveBench.

problem: Preference learning for diffusion model alignment suffers from training instability caused by high gradient variances at different timesteps and off-policy bias.
approach: SIPO introduces gradient clipping and masking of uninformative timesteps plus timestep-aware importance reweighting to correct off-policy bias.
contribution: Achieves stabilized training across SD1.5, SDXL, and video models (CogVideoX, Wan2.1) with consistent improvements over existing alignment methods.

problem: Using AI-generated annotations for causal inference is challenging because naively pooling AI and human data induces bias, and existing methods assume AI outputs are label surrogates.
approach: Generative Augmented Inference (GAI) treats AI outputs as high-dimensional informative features for learning human labels using nonparametric methods.
contribution: Enables consistent estimation with valid inference from combined human and AI data, improving asymptotic efficiency and confidence interval quality.

problem: Autoregressive Metropolis-Hastings sampling for test-time scaling is inherently serial, limits GPU utilization, and exhibits extreme tail latency at high budgets.
approach: Adaptive Sequential Monte Carlo (ASMC) uses parallel particle inference targeting power-shaped trajectory distributions with cache coherent resampling that reorders KV caches.
contribution: Achieves 80.6% exact-match accuracy on MATH500 with p95 latency of 73.7s versus 1318s for sequential MCMC, providing efficient high-accuracy test-time scaling.

problem: LoRA fine-tuning is highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and exhaustive hyperparameter search is computationally expensive.
approach: Uses Bayesian Optimization with a pre-trained LLM as a discrete-to-continuous mapping module guided by natural language prompts describing hyperparameter relationships.
contribution: Discovers hyperparameters achieving 20% performance improvement over standard choices using only about 30 iterations versus 45,000 combinations.

problem: Large language models fail at determining convexity of symbolic expressions under deep functional composition, exhibiting a compositional reasoning gap.
approach: ConvexBench benchmark uses an agentic divide-and-conquer framework with external parsing via Abstract Syntax Trees and recursive reasoning enforcement.
contribution: Achieves F1=1.0 at depth 100 versus 0.2 for standard approaches by addressing parsing failure and lazy reasoning failure modes.

problem: Vision-language-action models struggle with precise low-level actions from high-dimensional observations and bridging domain gaps across heterogeneous robot data sources.
approach: XR-1 learns Unified Vision-Motion Codes (UVMC) via dual-branch VQ-VAE jointly encoding visual dynamics and robotic motion, then applies three-stage training.
contribution: Enables scalable VLA learning across diverse robots, tasks, and environments with complementary multi-modal knowledge from heterogeneous datasets.

problem: Test-time scaling for complex reasoning through sampling is limited by verification: identifying correct solutions among candidates via scalar scoring is ineffective.
approach: V1 unifies generation and verification through pairwise ranking with V1-Infer using uncertainty-guided tournament-based ranking and V1-PairRL jointly training generator and verifier.
contribution: Improves Pass@1 by up to 10% on code generation and benchmarks while outperforming best-of-n and providing more efficient test-time scaling.

problem: Standard transformers cannot recognize context-free languages (CFLs) which formalize syntax in natural language and code, remaining a theoretical gap.
approach: Proves looped transformers with O(log N) layers and O(N^6) padding can recognize all CFLs, and unambiguous CFLs require only O(N^3) padding.
contribution: Establishes theoretical understanding of CFL recognition by transformers with empirical validation showing looped-padded transformers outperform fixed-depth on CFLs.

problem: Large language models memorize sensitive training data creating privacy and copyright risks, and existing unlearning methods often cause catastrophic utility loss.
approach: Divergence Decoding uses small auxiliary models to steer LLM logits away from specific data during inference via standard pre-training and fine-tuning.
contribution: Decisively outperforms state-of-the-art unlearning baselines and can be distilled back into the base model while generalizing to image domain.

problem: Cross-domain class-incremental learning suffers from entanglement between what to update and how to update, causing unstable adaptation and severe forgetting.
approach: Parameter-Masked Decoupled Optimization (PMDO) disentangles domain-relevant parameter adaptation from stability-aware trajectory regulation using domain-aware knowledge decoupling.
contribution: Enables effective cross-domain adaptation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and maintaining long-term learnability across benchmarks.

problem: Efficient attention mechanisms like linear and hybrid attention lack rigorous theoretical characterization of expressive power relative to full attention.
approach: Theoretically characterizes expressive power hierarchy showing hybrid networks interleaving full and linear attention require 2^(3L^2) layers to match L+1 full attention layers.
contribution: Provides first provable separation between hybrid attention and standard full attention, establishing theoretical perspective on attention mechanism capabilities.

problem: LLMs for recommendations lack predictable scaling laws because raw user interaction data contains inherent noise, bias, and incompleteness.
approach: Creates layered framework generating high-quality synthetic pedagogical curriculum data for continual pre-training, demonstrating robust power-law scaling.
contribution: Synthetic data models outperform real data models by 130% on recall@100; establishes first robust power-law scaling for continual pre-trained LLMs in recommendations.

problem: Data assimilation with diffusion surrogate models lacks a method to integrate observations that guarantees sampling from the true posterior.
approach: SURGE performs Sequential Monte Carlo over diffusion trajectories using particle filtering with importance weighting and resampling on the path measure.
contribution: Provides approximation-free particle filtering that rigorously fuses observational data with diffusion model simulations for state correction.

problem: Prioritizing protein-protein interactions for experimental validation is challenging because modern deep learning methods produce high false positives despite capturing biological signals.
approach: Introduces PPI candidate ranking framework using interpretability-guided ranking and integrating complementary sources: interaction scores, structural plausibility, biomedical language features.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art PPI prediction models on large-scale dataset from successive STRING releases.

problem: Solving geometric problems requires interleaved plot-reasoning steps, but supervised fine-tuning on such data degrades reasoning performance compared to text-only baselines.
approach: Faire uses reinforcement learning to enforce three causal constraints ensuring functional alignment where plotting is internalized rather than superficially imitated.
contribution: Induces qualitative shift in model behavior achieving competitive performance on challenging geometric reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Transformers lack inductive biases for geometric symmetries common in science and vision, and existing equivariant methods sacrifice efficiency.
approach: Platonic Transformer defines attention relative to Platonic solid symmetry group reference frames, inducing weight-sharing for combined equivariance without additional cost.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on CIFAR-10, 3D point clouds, and molecular benchmarks while maintaining standard transformer efficiency.

problem: Probabilistic models trained with task-agnostic objectives like log-loss lead to significant errors in downstream estimation, especially propensity scores near extremes.
approach: Derives task-specific strictly proper scoring rules by matching local curvature of downstream error metric, applied to Average Treatment Effect estimation.
contribution: Tailored objective consistently outperforms standard likelihood-based and covariate-balancing approaches on causal inference benchmarks.

problem: Attention score overflow risk in low-precision training is underestimated because existing bounds ignore the rank structure of the interaction matrix.
approach: Derives rank-aware concentration inequality showing tail probabilities decay as exp(-d^2α^2/(γr)) when interaction matrix has rank r, yielding geometry-aware scale factors.
contribution: Achieves 8-28x tighter concentration bounds; eliminates overflows in FP8 training across GPT-2 XL to Llama-2-70B while maintaining accuracy.

problem: Momentum SGD relies on fixed momentum coefficient across all parameters, failing to account for heterogeneous loss landscape structure.
approach: Introduces adaptive momentum coefficients regulated by parameter kinetic energy, linking to cubic damping from structural dynamics; augments mSGD and Adam.
contribution: Demonstrates robustness and matches or outperforms Adam on ViT, BERT, and GPT2 training where mSGD typically struggles.

problem: Optimal architectural choices for scaling metagenomic foundation models remain unexplored among autoregressive Transformers, State-Space Models, and long-convolutional architectures.
approach: EDEN studies architectural trade-offs across Llama, Mamba, and Hyena on 28 billion parameter models trained on 9.7 trillion nucleotide tokens.
contribution: Demonstrates Llama architecture exhibits superior scaling efficiency and semantic retrieval; derives quality-aware power-law scaling laws for metagenomics.

problem: Kernel-based conditional conformal prediction provides distribution-free guarantees but suffers from prohibitive computational costs in RKHS-based frameworks.
approach: SpeedCP computes the full solution path of regularized RKHS conformal optimization at essentially single kernel quantile fit cost with simultaneous hyperparameter tuning.
contribution: Provides reliable conditional coverage with 30% improved interval length and 40-fold speedup over Gibbs et al. (2025) across black-box predictors.

problem: Sampling multiple LLM responses to identify consistent answers requires excessive sampling, but optimal stopping leverages Bayesian priors and coarse answer tracking.
approach: Bayesian stopping policy tracks only L=3 most frequent answer counts, proven asymptotically optimal and strictly dominating prior-free baselines.
contribution: Achieves similar answer accuracy using fewer samples by identifying the most consistent LLM answer with fast posterior computation.

problem: Existing neural audio codecs using RVQ, VQ, or FSQ quantization limit geometric structure of latent space, reducing representation learning efficiency.
approach: Q2D2 projects feature pairs onto structured 2D grids (hexagonal, rhombic, rectangular) with implicit codebook defined by grid level products.
contribution: Improves audio compression efficiency with low token rates and high codebook utilization while maintaining state-of-the-art reconstruction quality.

problem: Non-stationary time series forecasting is challenged by fixed expert pools and memoryless routing that fail to adapt to abrupt regime shifts.
approach: Dynamic TMoE detects distribution shifts via Maximum Mean Discrepancy to dynamically instantiate and prune experts, using temporal memory router for context-aware selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across nine benchmarks, reducing MSE by 10.4% and MAE by 7.8%.

problem: On-policy distillation of vision-language models fails to account for orthogonal optimization objectives in language prior and visual grounding.
approach: Visual Gradient Steering (VGS) decomposes loss into language and visual components, then dynamically reorients gradients to prioritize visual subspace.
contribution: Significantly outperforms standard monolithic on-policy distillation with superior grounding and minimal training overhead.

problem: Surrogate regret bounds for online structured prediction break down under non-stationarity where fixed estimators incur linear loss growth.
approach: Combines dynamic regret analysis of online gradient descent with exploit-the-surrogate-gap technique using convolutional Fenchel-Young loss.
contribution: Upper bound depends on F_T and P_T (path length) with tight dependence; Polyak-style learning rate systematically yields target-loss bounds.

problem: Existing AI-generated image detectors exhibit prediction asymmetry (bias toward real class) limiting sensitivity to generated content under post-processing.
approach: DEAR uses inpainted images to identify spurious features by measuring channel activation alignment with inpaint masks, then prunes extreme features.
contribution: Significantly enhances robustness against unseen generators and post-processing operations, mitigating prediction asymmetry.

problem: Prompt learning for missing modalities overlooks internal structural information of prompt vectors, limiting performance under diverse missing modality scenarios.
approach: Structured Prompt Refining (SPR) network refines prompt structure via global interaction fusion, local feature refinement, and channel feature selection modules.
contribution: Uses only 0.8% trainable parameters; surpasses state-of-the-art by 3.8% F1-Macro on MM-IMDB at 90% modality missing rate.

problem: Data-Free Quantization of ViTs suffers from distribution mismatch between synthetic samples and quantized model's expected input due to sparse informative patches.
approach: MaskAQ decouples informative regions from background via differential entropy maximization, selects regions via masked attention alignment, refreshes samples periodically.
contribution: Aligns full-precision models with quantized models while preserving mutual information with synthetic samples across multiple ViT backbones.

problem: Pairwise comparison-based model rankings raise concerns about rewarding superficial cues or displaying judge biases compared to ground-truth accuracy.
approach: Converts five benchmarks into free-form generative evaluations and compares Elo rankings with accuracy rankings using Spearman correlation.
contribution: Elo rankings achieve Spearman correlation above 0.9 with accuracy rankings; style and judge bias have minor effects, echo is a causal driver.

problem: Training diffusion transformers at ultra-high resolutions is extremely costly due to quadratic scaling of self-attention with image tokens.
approach: Dynamic Position Extrapolation (DyPE) adjusts positional encodings at each step to match their frequency spectrum with diffusion process stage.
contribution: Enables pre-trained diffusion transformers to synthesize images at resolutions far beyond training data (e.g., 16 million pixels) without additional sampling cost.

problem: Monte Carlo Tree Search becomes intractable in cooperative multi-agent domains because exploring the exponential joint-action space exhausts search budgets before finding good policies.
approach: NonZero uses an interaction-guided proposal rule to rank single-agent and two-agent deviations by predicted coordination benefits, running selection over a low-dimensional representation instead of the full joint-action space.
contribution: Achieves improved sample efficiency and final performance on MatGame, SMAC, and SMACv2 relative to strong baselines under matched search budgets.

problem: Enhancing LLM reasoning skills often requires substantial computational resources and risks compromising generalization, while parameter-efficient fine-tuning typically requires retraining for each new model.
approach: Universal Reasoner (UniR) decomposes reasoning into a standalone, lightweight module trained with verifiable rewards that decouples from the backbone LLM; at inference, its logits are added to frozen backbone logits.
contribution: UniR modules can compose across different tasks by summing logits, generalize from smaller to larger models in the same family, and surpass existing fine-tuning methods on mathematical reasoning and machine translation.

problem: The space complexity cost of differential privacy remains unclear; little is known about memory-efficient algorithms needed for streaming tasks with privacy guarantees.
approach: Introduces a novel proof technique based on a multi-player communication game to establish unconditional space lower bounds for user-level differential privacy.
contribution: Proves that any private algorithm for distinct-element estimation requires almost Ω(T^{1/3}) space, establishing the first exponential separation between private and non-private space complexity for this task.

problem: In-context alignment methods struggle to handle pluralistic human values that inherently conflict, limiting their ability to reconcile competing demands within a single prompt.
approach: PICACO optimizes a meta-instruction by maximizing total correlation between specified values and LLM responses, which theoretically reinforces value conformity and reduces distractive noise.
contribution: Achieves better balance across up to 8 distinct values and outperforms recent baselines on five value sets using both black-box and open-source LLMs.

problem: Online learning in Bayesian Stackelberg games with unknown follower payoffs is unsolved; no-regret learning is known to be impossible under action-only feedback.
approach: Focuses on type feedback where the follower's type is revealed; proposes an algorithm that achieves Õ(√T) regret by treating candidate proposals as a bandit problem over local deviations.
contribution: Achieves Õ(√T) regret in the type-feedback model, the first positive result for this realistic setting where follower payoffs are completely unknown.

problem: Concept Bottleneck Models use a fixed functional form for the task predictor, constraining both accuracy and their ability to accommodate diverse user needs.
approach: Mixture of Concept Bottleneck Experts (M-CBEs) generalizes CBMs by varying the number of expert expressions and their functional forms; two instances are Linear M-CBE and Symbolic M-CBE using symbolic regression.
contribution: Demonstrates that varying expression count and functional form provides a robust framework for navigating the accuracy-interpretability trade-off.

problem: Optimal methods for constructing sparse piecewise linear regression trees are computationally prohibitive despite achieving substantially better performance than greedy approaches.
approach: CLARITree combines lookahead-style search with efficient rank-one Cholesky updates of the Gram matrix, enabling near-optimal sparse trees with favorable computational trade-offs.
contribution: Achieves near-optimal performance with improved computational efficiency and sparsity, scaling significantly better than current state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Existing LLM watermarking methods suffer from low-quality generation, poor personalization, and weak robustness against attacks.
approach: IPMark uses hierarchical addressing to organize model and user identities, employs semantic-syntactic dual-stream embedding for sentence-level candidate selection, and adds cryptographic signatures for receiver verification.
contribution: Achieves the lowest perplexity among baselines while maintaining strong robustness, significantly reducing detection latency through hierarchical retrieval.

problem: Multi-agent systems introduce security risks and attack surfaces that are not present in single-agent settings and remain unsystematically characterized.
approach: Empirical study of MAS design choices (agent roles, topology, memory) and their impact on security versus performance through controlled experiments with web-based agents.
contribution: Identifies three key architectural design choices influencing MAS security and shows that security-performance tradeoffs are governed by these decisions.

problem: LLM reasoning is constrained by reliance on massive high-quality human-curated data; supervision-heavy training is increasingly unsustainable.
approach: CPMöbius introduces a cooperative Coach-Player paradigm where the Coach generates instructive tasks and the Player solves them, creating a collaborative self-improvement loop without external data.
contribution: Achieves +4.9 overall and +5.4 out-of-distribution improvement on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, exceeding unsupervised baselines RENT and R-zero.

problem: Deep generative models struggle in low-data, imbalanced tabular settings to fully learn the complex data distribution needed for effective synthetic data generation.
approach: ReTabSyn uses reinforced feedback during training to prioritize learning the conditional distribution P(y|X) and preserve feature correlations, focusing on predictive signals rather than full joint distribution.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across benchmarks with small sample sizes, class imbalance, and distribution shift.

problem: A normative theory linking diverse spatial neural codes (grid, place, head-direction cells) to the dynamic navigation process remains elusive despite biological evidence of these codes.
approach: Proposes a Unified Laplacian Framework deriving spatial codes as spectral decompositions of the Laplace operator and develops a navigation policy based on Green's function potential.
contribution: Shows spectral representations emerge naturally and enable geometry-aware gradient ascent with improved sample efficiency and generalization in goal-reaching tasks.

problem: Data-driven hyperparameter tuning lacks statistical guarantees for multi-dimensional settings because model performance depends on hyperparameters in implicit, non-smooth ways.
approach: Establishes a framework using real algebraic geometry tools to provide generalization guarantees for multi-dimensional hyperparameter tuning under minimal assumptions.
contribution: Provides the first general framework for guaranteeing multi-dimensional hyperparameter tuning with improved bounds for validation-loss-based approaches.

problem: Multi-task reinforcement learning suffers from asynchronous convergence speeds due to task difficulty imbalance, creating a bottleneck in the shared critic network.
approach: HyMTRL divides task learning into reinforcement exploration and imitation refinement phases; mastered tasks transition to imitation learning with critic resets to reduce representational strain.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements in learning efficiency and final performance on MetaWorld benchmark through phased policy evolution.

problem: Existing LLM-based narrative systems fail to maintain logical consistency and narrative integrity against unconstrained user interventions.
approach: Formulates Narrative Commitment Preservation (NCP) and introduces NCP-Bench with 100 narrative environments derived from movies that include structured specifications for automatic checking.
contribution: Reveals that linguistic quality does not guarantee commitment preservation; best model (GPT-5.2) achieves only 40% survival rate after 20 turns with 40-68% fact conflict rates.

problem: Safety evaluations focus on input distributions yielding harm but disregard the probabilistic nature of models and their tail output behavior, missing rare harmful events in deployed systems.
approach: Proposes importance sampling via unsafe model versions that make harmful outputs more probable, enabling efficient estimation of tail-risk probabilities.
contribution: Achieves 10-20× sample efficiency improvement over naive sampling; can estimate probabilities of order 10^{-4} with just 500 samples.

problem: Existing on-policy distillation requires a separate, often larger teacher LLM and does not explicitly leverage ground-truth solutions available in reasoning datasets.
approach: OPSD enables a single LLM to act as both teacher (conditioned on privileged information) and student (seeing only questions); training minimizes per-token divergence over student rollouts.
contribution: Achieves superior token efficiency compared to reinforcement learning methods and better performance than off-policy distillation on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Deepfake audio detectors fail to generalize to unseen attacks partly due to spectral bias, where neural networks prioritize low-frequency structure and underexploit high-frequency artifacts.
approach: SONAR uses dual-path architecture with parallel XLSR encoder and learnable high-pass filters; fuses representations via frequency cross-attention with Jensen-Shannon alignment loss.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on ASVspoof 2021 in a single-run setting while converging faster than strong baselines.

problem: Incidental prompt cues steer LLM algorithm choices even when all outputs pass the same tests, introducing an 'invisible lottery' where accidental context alters downstream properties.
approach: Defines algorithm steering as cue-induced shifts in algorithm distributions; runs 46,535 controlled experiments across 11 tasks, 19 cue types, and 15 models.
contribution: Documents large systematic shifts in algorithm-family distributions (up to 100 percentage points), largely consistent with cue semantics, with implications for performance and security.

problem: Discrete-time piecewise-linear RNNs cannot handle continuous-time dynamics or irregular temporal intervals, and Neural ODEs lack their interpretability and DSR performance.
approach: Develops continuous-time PLRNNs (cPLRNNs) with efficient training via piecewise-linear structure exploitation; enables semi-analytical determination of equilibria and limit cycles.
contribution: Demonstrates cPLRNNs match or exceed discrete-time PLRNNs and Neural ODEs on dynamical systems reconstruction benchmarks, including systems with discontinuities.

problem: Vision-Language Navigation with complex long-horizon instructions suffers from high latency and instruction interference where irrelevant text noise induces hallucinations.
approach: IDEAL-VLN reformulates navigation as a causal inference chain: Semantic Anchoring infers immediate semantic anchors from context, then Action Alignment generates actions from anchors only.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across major benchmarks with improved robustness; includes 160K-image Instruction-Aligned Navigation Dataset.

problem: Diffusion-based generative image steganography has fixed hiding capacity for single images, suffers from inter-secret interference, and lacks receiver-side verification.
approach: Proposes Receiver Authenticable Generative Image Steganography with Dynamic Cover Selection for adaptive hiding-space allocation and Signature Authentication Controller for cryptographic verification.
contribution: Achieves superior secure multi-receiver isolation and high-capacity generative image steganography with dynamic multi-image concealment.

problem: Pairwise Generative Reward Models create O(n²) computational bottlenecks in RLHF when aggregating preference signals over n candidates.
approach: IRPM extends Bradley-Terry preference learning via intergroup comparisons to train pointwise GRMs; derives pointwise rewards by contrasting groups of chosen vs. rejected samples.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among pointwise GRMs with O(n) evaluation, preserving interpretability while reducing computational cost.

problem: Layout-to-image methods fail under few-shot atypical settings due to representation fragmentation from granularity mismatch between semantic identity and visual details.
approach: Proposes representation-driven framework with Semantic Anchoring for stable identity, Primitive Imbuing for recomposable details, and Conceptual Steering for saliency-aware optimization.
contribution: Shows consistent improvements in 5-shot regime over state-of-the-art L2I methods in visual fidelity and alignment across diverse atypical domains.

problem: Existing geometry-based coreset selection for few-shot ICL yields skewed distributions through oversampling peripheral examples and high local redundancy.
approach: Process-aware framework jointly optimizes diversity and representativeness via adaptive submodular objective with local density awareness and redundancy penalties.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coreset selection methods on 7 NLP datasets by better balancing representativeness and diversity.

problem: Multi-fidelity regression with extreme data imbalance struggles with Gaussian-process surrogates that have cubic scaling costs and overfit to sparse high-fidelity observations.
approach: FIRE couples tabular foundation models for zero-shot in-context Bayesian inference via high-fidelity correction model conditioned on low-fidelity posterior distributions.
contribution: Delivers stronger performance-time tradeoff than seven state-of-the-art GP and deep-learning MF methods with runtime advantages across 31 benchmarks.

problem: Long-context LLM inference faces conflict between head-adaptive compression algorithms offering superior accuracy and modern inference engines demanding rigid static memory patterns.
approach: HARD-KV bridges dynamic selection with rigid constraints via Cascade Cache hierarchy and Logits Calibration that normalizes diverse importance metrics into unified probability space.
contribution: Achieves up to 2× throughput improvement over static baselines on math-reasoning benchmarks (AIME, U-Math) while maintaining high-fidelity 10k+ token generation.

problem: Reward learning typically relies on single feedback types or manually weighted combinations, leaving unclear how to jointly learn from heterogeneous feedback types.
approach: MAVRL formulates reward learning as Bayesian inference over shared latent reward function with explicit likelihoods per feedback type; uses amortized variational inference.
contribution: Jointly inferred reward posteriors outperform single-type baselines, exploit complementary information across feedback types, and yield more robust policies.

problem: Standard OT-DRO pipeline separates uncertainty quantification from optimization, potentially leading to excessive conservatism in robustified decisions.
approach: Introduces end-to-end pipeline to automatically learn decision-focused ambiguity sets where the loss function informs the ambiguity set shape via bilevel optimization.
contribution: Produces less conservative decisions with enforced distributional robustness validated through data-driven bootstrapping on portfolio and regression tasks.

problem: Model producers can exploit randomness in AI arena rankings by submitting clones of their models, artificially inflating ranks and degrading ranking quality.
approach: Proposes You-Rank-We-Rank (YRWR) mechanism requiring producers to submit rankings over their own models; uses these rankings to correct quality estimates.
contribution: Proves YRWR is approximately clone-robust and improves ranking accuracy under producer honesty, with simulations calibrated to Chatbot Arena data.

problem: Targeted data selection for instruction tuning relies on optimizer statistics that assume coordinate-wise parameter independence, breaking down in PEFT methods like LoRA.
approach: GIST recovers task-specific subspace from validation gradients via SVD, projects training gradients into coupled subspace, and scores by alignment with target directions.
contribution: Matches or outperforms state-of-the-art with only 0.29% storage and 25% computational time under the same selection budget.

problem: Neural Flows for irregular time series treat variables independently, underexploring inter-variable interactions while their one-step mapping makes iterative interaction refinement inherently challenging.
approach: Proposes GSNF with auxiliary-trajectory self-supervision: interaction-aware trajectory generation via re-initialization and reverse-time trajectory generation for forward-backward consistency.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art classification on five real-world datasets with highly competitive training time and memory usage.

problem: As AI agents become capable at reading and executing code, their security implications for smart contract vulnerabilities remain unmeasured and uncharacterized.
approach: Introduces EVMbench evaluation measuring agent ability to detect, patch, and exploit vulnerabilities on 117 curated vulnerabilities with programmatic grading via local Ethereum environment.
contribution: Frontier agents can discover and exploit vulnerabilities end-to-end against live blockchain instances, advancing understanding of agent security capabilities.

problem: Characterizing attention behavior at extreme context-window lengths remains unclear; convergence rates of attention to its infinite-token limit are unknown.
approach: Introduces token sample complexity framework; establishes pointwise uniform convergence of attention map and moment convergence of transformed token distribution.
contribution: Proves attention map converges at rate C(R)/√n for compactly supported distributions, with empirical validation on synthetic and real data showing predicted slowdown in downstream accuracy.

problem: Controlling generative models via inference-time steering or fine-tuning is expensive because it requires costly trajectory simulations to estimate value functions.
approach: Introduces Meta Flow Maps (MFMs) trained for one-step posterior sampling; these samples are differentiable in conditioning state, enabling efficient value-function gradient estimation.
contribution: Single-particle steered-MFM outperforms Best-of-1000 baseline across multiple ImageNet rewards at a fraction of the compute.

problem: Common intuition suggests reweighting data toward uniform distribution aids long-tail skill learning, but this may not reflect training dynamics under power-law distributions.
approach: Introduces minimalist skill-composition task and proves learning under power-law distribution requires less training data; shows power-law sampling induces beneficial asymmetry.
contribution: Across compositional reasoning tasks, power-law distributions consistently outperform uniform, with theoretical analysis explaining improved loss landscape.

problem: Classical chemical reaction network reduction techniques do not directly apply to CRNs encoding Bayesian inference, limiting their practical scalability.
approach: Recovers factor-graph structure encoded in Napp-Adams-compiled CRNs and transports factor-graph reduction results to chemical implementations.
contribution: Obtains significantly smaller CRNs while preserving belief-propagation fixed points on surviving variables.

problem: Training 3D Gaussian Splatting at billion-primitive scale is fundamentally memory-bound; prior systems limited to tens of millions of Gaussians on single-GPU hardware.
approach: TideGS leverages sparse, trajectory-conditioned 3DGS training via SSD-CPU-GPU hierarchy with block-virtualized geometry, hierarchical asynchronous pipeline, and trajectory-adaptive differential streaming.
contribution: Enables training over one billion Gaussians on single 24-GB GPU while achieving best reconstruction quality among single-GPU baselines, scaling beyond prior out-of-core systems.

problem: LLM datasets can transmit hidden signals not directly observable from individual datapoints, posing a conceptual challenge for understanding dataset effects on model behavior.
approach: Introduces LOGIT-LINEAR SELECTION (LLS) prescribing how to select preference-dataset subsets to elicit hidden effects via log-linear structure.
contribution: Discovers subsets eliciting specific preferences, responses in different languages, and persona adoption; effects persist across models with varying architectures.

problem: In streaming gradient-based learning with batch size 1, parameter-unit step sizes produce unpredictable per-step output changes, leading to instability.
approach: Proposes intentional updates specifying intended outcomes then solving for step size achieving them; extends NLMS principle to streaming deep RL via intentional TD and policy gradients.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art streaming performance, frequently performing on par with batch and replay-buffer approaches using eligibility traces and diagonal scaling.

problem: Sparse dictionary learning for transformer attention outputs fails due to the dead feature problem, where randomly initialized features mismatch the intrinsically low-dimensional geometry of attention subspaces.
approach: Subspace-constrained training for sparse autoencoders that initializes feature directions into the active subspace of attention activations, leveraging the observation that attention outputs are confined to 60% of the full dimensional space.
contribution: Reduces dead features from 87% to below 1% in 1M-feature Attention Output SAEs and demonstrates the approach extends to other sparse dictionary learning methods.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) struggle with accuracy and efficiency in high-dimensional PDEs, while traditional spectral methods suffer from the curse of dimensionality beyond d>10.
approach: Modified spectral-informed neural networks (SINNs) integrate coefficient decay scaling and basis embeddings from harmonic analysis, operating in the spectral domain to avoid spatial derivative computations and reduce memory.
contribution: Outperforms sparse grid spectral methods on middle-dimensional problems with incomplete spectral information and achieves superior accuracy to PINNs on high-dimensional problems.

problem: Mixup data augmentation's effectiveness on graph data is uncertain, with no rigorous independent empirical evidence for state-of-the-art graph mixup methods despite widespread adoption in vision and language domains.
approach: Extensive evaluation of graph mixup methods following a unified protocol for graph classification, analyzing both interpolation properties and downstream task performance.
contribution: Finds that state-of-the-art mixup methods yield no statistically significant improvements over no-mixup baselines and that high interpolation error leads to performance degradation.

problem: Scaling GUI automation for computer-use agents is bottlenecked by the need for sophisticated GUI planning that requires expensive, large-scale trajectory data collection with redundant exploration.
approach: TreeCUA organizes large-scale GUI trajectories into tree structures using multi-agent collaboration (exploration, verification, summarization, evaluation) and adaptively balances trajectory difficulty and diversity with world knowledge guidance.
contribution: TreeCUA-DPO improves GUI planning by leveraging branch information from adjacent trajectories, enabling efficient scaling of GUI automation with tree-structured verifiable evolution.

problem: Adapting generative foundation models to optimize reward functions while satisfying constraints (e.g., in molecular design) remains open; balancing reward maximization and constraint satisfaction is unpredictable and unreliable.
approach: Constrained Flow Optimization (CFO) formulates constrained generative optimization as a principled framework and reduces it to sequential fine-tuning via established scalable methods, automatically balancing competing objectives.
contribution: Achieves consistent increases in reward while ensuring high constraint satisfaction on molecular design tasks with convergence guarantees for both constrained generative optimization and constrained generation.

problem: Reinforcement learning agents achieve impressive performance but lack interpretability, limiting trust and complicating debugging and improvement of agent behavior.
approach: CausalXRL uses causal graph reasoning to provide transparent, structured, multi-level explanations of agent decision-making, validated through quantitative analysis of explanation fidelity and qualitative expert evaluation.
contribution: Provides faithful causal explanations while efficiently learning causal structures in benchmark RL environments, with qualitative studies confirming usefulness for inspecting high-level strategies in RTS tasks.

problem: The internal mechanisms enabling large multimodal models to perform in-context learning from few multimodal demonstrations remain opaque and underexplored.
approach: Identifies specific attention heads (function vectors) responsible for transmitting visual relations using causal mediation analysis, then extracts and manipulates these vectors to alter task performance.
contribution: Shows multimodal function vectors can be extracted to improve zero-shot accuracy at inference and fine-tuned with modest data to outperform in-context learning; demonstrates linear combination of relation-specific vectors solves analogy problems.

problem: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods like LoRA have memory requirements that scale with model hidden dimension and rank (O(dr)), limiting their applicability to large-scale models.
approach: FrameFT models parameter updates with sparse coefficients in a Fusion Frame basis, which can be algorithmically generated and shared across layers, storing only sparse coefficients instead of full rank matrices.
contribution: Achieves performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art PEFT techniques while requiring far fewer trainable parameters and reduced memory footprint.

problem: Streaming video understanding requires handling unbounded video streams with limited memory and computation, while models trained on short sequences must generalize to long streams without explicit position encoding.
approach: Decoupled Streaming Cache (DSCache) maintains a cumulative KV cache while constructing a separate instant cache on-demand, decoupled from past caches; incorporates position-agnostic encoding to support unseen positions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Streaming Video QA benchmarks with an average 2.5% accuracy improvement over prior methods, as a training-free mechanism.

problem: Estimating causal structure from partially observed data with latent variables is challenging, especially when data exhibit heterogeneity or nonstationarity that violate homogeneity assumptions.
approach: Develops a principled approach exploiting rank deficiency constraints of covariance matrices in heterogeneous/nonstationary settings; proposes a novel rank deficiency test and identifiability results.
contribution: Proves distributional constraints in heterogeneous/nonstationary cases are equivalent to homogeneous cases and provides methods to identify causal structure and variables with distribution shifts.

problem: Current multimodal fusion designs distort feedback to feature extractors; aggressive merging entangles representations while auxiliary losses introduce optimization conflicts that distract from the primary task.
approach: Self-Consistent Field Autoencoder (SCFAE) uses small autoencoders per modality with task loss selecting predictive features and reconstruction loss separating them into independent subspaces, following self-consistent field principles.
contribution: SCFAE handles missing data and unequal input sizes more robustly than alternatives; gradient analysis confirms it avoids conflicts and maintains stable training dynamics.

problem: Multitask learning benefits from aggregating data across related tasks, but fundamental statistical limits exist such that abundant data per task cannot overcome hardness of adaptation.
approach: Analyzes statistical limits of multitask learning by establishing stronger impossibility results beyond the no-free-lunch theorem, showing hardness persists even with arbitrarily large per-task sample sizes.
contribution: Proves an impossibility result demonstrating that the hardness of multitask learning cannot be overcome by having abundant data per task alone.

problem: Partial client participation in federated learning can cause Byzantine clients to dominate the sampled set, breaking existing Byzantine-robust methods that assume full participation.
approach: Delayed Momentum Aggregation (DeMoA) aggregates cached momentum from non-sampled clients alongside fresh momentum from sampled clients, ensuring Byzantine clients remain a minority from the server's perspective.
contribution: Achieves Byzantine robustness under partial participation; with 20% Byzantine ratio and 10% participation rate, DeMoA maintains best accuracy when existing methods fail.

problem: Learning compositional generative models from decentralized data is hindered by fragmentation of interacting factors across isolated silos, preventing discovery of novel combinations.
approach: Decentralized Compositional Flow Matching (DCFM) enforces structural constraints across global generative factors through peer interactions without exchanging raw data, enabling emergent novel combinations.
contribution: Substantially outperforms federated learning and mixture-of-experts baselines on conditional image generation, robotic spatial planning, and medical attribute co-occurrence modeling.

problem: Understanding when learning is statistically possible but computationally hard in high-dimensional settings remains a central challenge in learning theory.
approach: Shows that a Noise Sensitivity Exponent (NSE) determined by the activation function governs statistical-to-computational gaps in single- and multi-index models.
contribution: Establishes that NSE controls the onset of computational bottlenecks in high-noise single-index models and statistical-computational gaps in specialization transitions of multi-index models.

problem: Measuring and improving procedural validity of step-by-step LLM-generated how-to procedures at scale on real-world tasks remains understudied and challenging.
approach: How2Everything pipeline extracts and rewrites 351K procedures from 980K web pages; How2Score protocol uses LLM judges to detect critical failures preventing goal achievement.
contribution: How2Bench (7K examples) reveals scaling trends across model sizes; RL using How2Score improves performance by >10 points across three models without systematic regressions.

problem: Inference-time LLM alignment via activation steering lacks online error feedback and ignores how perturbations propagate through layers, resulting in suboptimal open-loop control.
approach: Shows layer-wise dynamics are well-approximated by locally-linear models despite transformer nonlinearity; applies linear quadratic regulator on layer-wise Jacobians for closed-loop steering toward semantic setpoints.
contribution: Achieves robust fine-grained behavior control with formal guarantees on steering performance; surpasses baseline methods for toxicity, truthfulness, refusal, and concept modulation.

problem: Time series forecasting struggles with high computational complexity, inefficient token utilization from redundancy and scarcity, and temporal distribution shifts from non-stationary dynamics.
approach: KUMA uses an input-dependent Koopman module to decompose series into Koopman dynamics and residuals; proposes U-shaped Multilevel Attention (UMA) combining element-wise and linear attention.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on 12 benchmark datasets, mitigating operator mixture issues and alleviating temporal distribution shifts while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Multi-armed bandits with heterogeneous data sources have unknown and distinct noise variances per source, requiring the learner to balance exploration-exploitation while selecting which source to query.
approach: SOAR adaptively balances exploration-exploitation by jointly constructing upper confidence bounds for arm rewards and lower confidence bounds for data source variances.
contribution: Achieves regret bound O(σ*² ∑ 1/Δᵢ) matching single-source variance σ*, with logarithmic preprocessing cost; experiments on synthetic and MovieLens 32M data validate effectiveness.

problem: Multi-agent collaborative perception in autonomous driving struggles with heterogeneous sensors and independently trained models that create semantic and geometric inconsistencies.
approach: X-MoGe proposes Pixel-level Mixture-of-Experts (P-MoE) to adaptively model modality-specific characteristics and geometry-guided feature fusion incorporating explicit geometric priors for BEV alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on OPV2V and DAIR-V2X datasets for heterogeneous collaborative perception.

problem: Truth inference from sparse multi-class annotations fails when annotators label only small subsets or classes are imbalanced, and single confusion matrices cannot capture complex annotator behaviors on difficult tasks.
approach: CPBCC models annotators through dual-pathway architecture learning class-specific prototype patterns and annotator-specific weights over prototypes, addressing data sparsity and expressiveness simultaneously.
contribution: Achieves 26% accuracy improvement in best cases, boosting average accuracy from 68.73% to 74.11% across 10 real-world datasets spanning five domains.

problem: Cross-modal 2D-3D gait recognition is impeded by domain discrepancies between 2D silhouette and 3D point cloud distributions, with prior methods aligning only final embeddings.
approach: DiffCrossGait enforces trajectory-level alignment by driving both modalities with shared noise in latent diffusion; uses Tri-Phase Alignment Strategy exploiting varying noise intensities for identity anchoring and dynamics consistency.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on SUSTech1K and FreeGait benchmarks with high inference efficiency by eliminating iterative denoising from the inference phase.

problem: Sequential learning is order-dependent with N sources inducing N! curricula, yet no principled method exists to predict effective learning order across diverse domains and tasks.
approach: Shows local order effects are governed by Lie-bracket commutator of gradient update fields; proposes Lie-Bracket Tournament using one Hessian-vector product per source and O(N log N) sort without materializing O(N²) edges.
contribution: Reaches 98.1%-98.9% pairwise accuracy for instruction-SFT/DPO at k=1; recovers best schedule in 87.5% of trials; ranks 85 programming languages for Python target at 99th percentile.

problem: Multimodal LLMs handling speech and audio are vulnerable to complex audio-based attacks via speech-audio composition (overlap, dialogue, mixtures) where benign and harmful intents co-occur without explicit harmful text.
approach: Introduces SACRED-Bench to evaluate robustness under complex audio-based attacks; proposes SALMONN-Guard, the first guard model jointly inspecting speech, audio, and text for safety judgments.
contribution: SALMONN-Guard reduces attack success rate from 66% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) to 20%, demonstrating the need for audio-aware defenses in multimodal LLM safety.

problem: Protein engineering systems must prioritize future wet-lab experiments rather than merely fit static measurements, yet agentic protein engineering lacks reproducible benchmarks preserving experimental campaign chronology.
approach: TadA-Bench provides million-variant wet-lab replay from 31 TadA directed-evolution rounds; uses Seq2Graph label-unification pipeline to reconcile noisy enrichment measurements into consistent labels.
contribution: Shows strong interpolation but weaker future-round ranking; positions TadA-Bench as reproducible wet-lab substrate; demonstrates evolutionary coverage is more informative than local data density.

problem: Recent test-time CLIP defenses claim zero-shot robustness improvements but rely on flawed assumptions about detecting distributional differences between clean and adversarial samples.
approach: Proposes CLIP-MAD, an adaptive attack breaking the common indicative measurement assumption; expands adversarial distribution without full gradient calculations, combining flexibly with existing attacks.
contribution: Demonstrates CLIP-MAD produces strong adversarial samples across 13 datasets that markedly reduce robustness of diverse defenses, revealing false sense of security in CLIP zero-shot robustness.

problem: Partial-label learning where each instance has a candidate label set requires inferring true labels, but existing methods are computationally intensive or rely on surrogate losses and heuristics.
approach: Uses amortized variational inference with neural networks predicting variational parameters from input data, combining deep learning expressiveness with probabilistic modeling rigor.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and efficiency on synthetic and real-world partial-label datasets.

problem: Distributed optimization with heterogeneous data across multiple agents requires efficient training balancing communication and computation, limiting per-agent local computation.
approach: Applies accelerated gradient ascent to dual variables with multi-step stochastic gradient descent on primal variables in Lagrangian formulation; enables local computation via inner SGD loops requiring no inter-agent communication.
contribution: Converges for any number of local updates, attaining optimal communication complexity; proves convergence under inexact accelerated gradient framework with optimal reproducibility under biased gradients.

problem: Diagnosing complex diseases requires strategic multi-round diagnostic test sequencing, but LLMs struggle with this interactive process, suffering from premature diagnostic closure and reward sparsity.
approach: CompDiag-Bench formalizes diagnosis as sequential decision-making; Salus decouples reasoning into Differential Reasoner, Strategic Controller, and Workup Proposer, optimized via multi-agent RL with structured rewards.
contribution: Salus-7B achieves state-of-the-art Top-1 accuracy of 83.64% on complex cases, outperforming DeepSeek-V3.2 at 71.38%, with LLM-as-a-Judge dense rewards preventing premature closure.

problem: Dynamic agentic RAG systems face a strategic-operational mismatch where sophisticated planning fails to materialize due to unadapted executors, causing negative gains despite increased complexity.
approach: JADE models the system as cooperative multi-agent team with shared backbone, enabling end-to-end learning via outcome-based rewards and co-adaptation of planner and executors.
contribution: Transforms disjoint modules into synergistic system yielding strong performance improvements via joint optimization with flexible balance between efficiency and effectiveness.

problem: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are bottlenecked by scarcity of expert demonstrations (observation-language-action triplets), making it difficult to scale embodied AI.
approach: Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP) pre-trains on abundant task-agnostic data using Inverse Dynamics objective predicting actions from consecutive observations, then fine-tunes with minimal expert data.
contribution: Matches models trained on 1M+ trajectories using orders of magnitude less labeled data; achieves 10% absolute gain over behavior cloning; surpasses internet-scale baselines under visual distribution shifts.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems lack safety guarantees when individual agents fail or behave adversarially, requiring automated design methods that defend against compromised agents.
approach: MaMa formalizes system design as Stackelberg security game between system designer (Meta-Agent) and best-responding adversary (Meta-Adversary) selecting and compromising agent subsets.
contribution: MaMa-designed systems defend against worst-case attacks while maintaining performance comparable to task-optimized systems; results generalize to stronger adversaries and different LLM backends.

problem: MoE-PEFT methods require separate adapters per expert, causing trainable parameters to scale linearly with expert count and limiting applicability to specific adapter architectures.
approach: LiME achieves expert specialization through lightweight modulation rather than adapter replication; uses single shared PEFT module modulated by lightweight expert vectors with zero-parameter routing.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance on MMT-47 (47 multimodal tasks) while using 4x fewer parameters and 29% faster training compared to MoE-PEFT baselines.

problem: Decentralized optimization with mixed affine constraints involving both local and global variables lacks optimal complexity analysis, with applications in federated and multi-task learning.
approach: Analyzes decentralized optimization under smooth/non-smooth and strongly convex/general convex assumptions, providing optimal algorithms matching established lower complexity bounds.
contribution: Establishes optimal convergence rates for smooth strongly-convex regime and provides near-optimal methods for remaining cases.

problem: Time series forecasting is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, yet effective defenses remain underexplored due to data entanglement and training-loss degeneration that render existing defenses ineffective.
approach: TimeGuard adopts channel-wise pool training with time-aware initialization and distance-regularized loss selection to progressively expand reliable pool during training.
contribution: Improves robustness by 1.96x in MAE_P over leading baseline while preserving clean performance within 5% MAE_C across multiple datasets and TSF architectures.

problem: Edge-colored hypergraph clustering (MaxECC) seeks to color vertices maximizing satisfied edges; existing algorithms have suboptimal approximation ratios limiting practical applicability.
approach: Proposes three algorithms: one with exponentially improved ratio of 1/(r+1), a dependent-rounding algorithm with ratio 1/⌈k/2⌉, and an analytical scaling approach achieving (1-e^-r)/r.
contribution: Improves best-known approximation factor for all hypergraphs; for graphs achieves 0.43 factor versus previous 0.38.

problem: Do-calculus reasoning for causal inference involves complex rule orderings with numerous equivalent interventional expressions; existing approaches lack systematic characterization of this space.
approach: Introduces derivation graphs representing do-calculus rule applications and characterizes the full space of equivalent observational/interventional probabilities; yields simple procedure using at most 4 rule applications.
contribution: Provides efficient procedure for do-calculus reasoning and shows how identification algorithms applied to equivalent queries produce multiple valid estimands for more efficient estimation.

problem: High-dimensional continuous control in deep reinforcement learning remains unstable where algorithms like TD3 and SAC often collapse due to error amplification across the learning pipeline.
approach: Lipschitz Pathway framework decomposes instability into four compounding amplification stages; Action Manifold Smoothing (AMS) replaces point-wise TD targets with orthogonally-sampled averages for implicit Laplacian smoothing.
contribution: AMS enables TD3 and SAC to achieve over 400 reward on 38-D Dog Run within 1M steps where baselines fail, validating Lipschitz pathway as framework for diagnosing control bottlenecks.

problem: Sparse tangent portfolio optimization requires interpretable low-cardinality portfolios, but cardinality constraints are NP-hard and predict-then-optimize pipelines misalign forecasting accuracy with portfolio quality.
approach: End-to-end decision-focused learning framework reformulates Sharpe ratio maximization as differentiable Disciplined Parametrized Programming (DPP) layer with smooth top-k operator enforcing exact cardinality.
contribution: Achieves competitive and often superior out-of-sample Sharpe ratios on four major equity markets with particularly strong gains in larger asset universes.

problem: Estimating the Riemannian geometry of high-dimensional data typically relies on graphs and kernels that scale poorly with dataset size and dimension.
approach: Riemannian metric matching learns the carré du champ operator via neural networks in a denoising probabilistic framework, formulated as conditional expectation enabling amortized inference without kernel construction.
contribution: Rivals or improves accuracy of k-NN-based diffusion geometry while enabling amortized inference up to 400x faster; supports graph-free geometric analysis on high-dimensional images.

problem: Transformer-based operators treat continuous function fields as discrete tokens, missing global functional structure in operator learning tasks.
approach: Reinterprets attention as functional correspondences between adaptive bases, replacing softmax affinities with structured linear operators inspired by geometric functional maps.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on operator learning tasks (PDEs, 3D segmentation, regression) with a compact, resolution-invariant representation.

problem: Concept steering for controlling generative models lacks a comprehensive theoretical framework despite empirical success.
approach: Formalizes steering theory by linking it to affine concept erasure, proving the standard removal approach is a special case of LEACE, then introduces MidSteer for minimal-disturbance transformations.
contribution: Provides principled theoretical framework for concept steering and demonstrates MidSteer's superior performance across vision diffusion and language models.

problem: Token attribution for reasoning LLMs faces efficiency bottleneck requiring O(M·N) operations and faithfulness drop where intermediate tokens absorb attribution mass.
approach: Introduces FlashTrace with span-wise aggregation for multi-token attribution in a single pass, plus recursive attribution tracing importance through reasoning chains to inputs.
contribution: Achieves 130x speedup over baselines on long-context tasks (RULER, MATH, MorehopQA) while maintaining superior faithfulness.

problem: Small LLMs fail to match large model performance on multi-step reasoning and tool use because reasoning and knowledge gaps cause compounding errors.
approach: Proposes SCoRe, student-centered distillation where the student generates trajectories and teacher corrects only the earliest error, followed by short-horizon RL on verified prefixes.
contribution: A 7B student distilled with SCoRe closes the agentic gap with a 72B teacher across 12 benchmarks.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting training requires expensive optimization with high memory costs, limiting scalability to large scenes.
approach: Introduces 3DGS²-TR, a second-order optimizer using diagonal Hessian approximation via Hutchinson's method with parameter-wise trust-region regularization based on Hellinger distance.
contribution: Achieves better reconstruction with 50% fewer iterations than ADAM while using only 17% more GPU memory than ADAM (85% less than 3DGS-LM).

problem: Federated learning assumes static local data or fixed distributions, limiting applicability in dynamic environments with temporal data shifts.
approach: Proposes SFedPO with a prediction oracle to capture temporal distribution evolution, includes distribution-guided data sampling and shift-aware aggregation weighting.
contribution: Theoretically establishes convergence bounds and empirically demonstrates adaptation to streaming scenarios with distribution shifts.

problem: Detecting multi-step LLM agent attacks is hard because malicious intent emerges only after workflow completion while individual actions appear legitimate.
approach: Reframes prompt-injection defense as causal inference using Structural Causal Models with typed edges, then applies Pearl's do-calculus to identify whether harmful outcomes depend on injections.
contribution: CausalTrace outperforms content-based baselines on diverse attack scenarios while requiring minimal LLM inference cost and providing interpretable attack chain explanations.

problem: Existing robustness benchmarks for vision-language models focus on hallucination or text, overlooking how misleading visual inputs undermine robustness.
approach: Introduces MVI-Bench, a benchmark with 1,248 VQA instances covering three hierarchical levels (Visual Concept, Attribute, Relationship) and proposes MVI-Sensitivity metric for fine-grained robustness evaluation.
contribution: Evaluates 18 state-of-the-art LVLMs, uncovering pronounced vulnerabilities and providing actionable insights for developing more robust models.
