problem: Existing free energy estimation methods are either prohibitively expensive (classical MD) or poorly generalizable (deep learning with input dimensions tied to specific systems).
approach: Proposes CARD, which uses radix-based decomposition to convert 3D coordinates into mixed discrete-continuous sequences for coarse-to-fine autoregressive modeling.
contribution: Matches classical computational accuracy on unseen molecular systems with 40x speedup in inference.

problem: Detecting AI-generated images using appearance cues fails as generators improve; existing detectors lose stability and transfer poorly across generators.
approach: Identifies robustness asymmetry: natural images preserve stable semantic representations under perturbations while generated images exhibit larger feature drift; proposes RA-Det detection framework.
contribution: RA-Det improves average detection performance by 12.92% over 10 strong baselines across 14 generative models without requiring generator fingerprints.

problem: Simulation-based inference is susceptible to model misspecification errors from simulator, noise, or prior modeling, yielding biased or overconfident posteriors.
approach: Introduces FMCPE, which trains a posterior approximator on simulated data then uses flow matching to refine predictions toward the true posterior using calibration samples.
contribution: Consistently mitigates misspecification effects across synthetic and real-world datasets, improving inference accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

problem: Autoregressive video generation requires sequential iterative denoising, and existing cache reuse strategies use coarse-grained skipping that ignores fine-grained pixel motion dynamics.
approach: Proposes MotionCache, which exploits inter-frame differences as a motion proxy for pixel-level dynamics, employing coarse-to-fine strategy with motion-weighted cache reuse.
contribution: Achieves 6.28x and 1.64x speedups on SkyReels-V2 and MAGI-1 respectively while preserving generation quality (VBench degradation <1%).

problem: Stochastic linear bandits with parameter noise have regret bounds that were not previously characterized for general action sets.
approach: Provides regret analysis for parameter noise model with general action sets, establishing upper and lower bounds that match up to logarithmic factors.
contribution: Proves minimax regret is Θ(√(dT σ_q²)) for unit ball action sets and demonstrates attainability via simple explore-exploit algorithm.

problem: Data holders cannot trust SDG-as-a-service providers with access to private data, limiting synthetic data generation use in sensitive domains.
approach: Proposes FHAIM, the first fully homomorphic encryption framework for training marginal-based AIM generators on encrypted tabular data with differential privacy guarantees.
contribution: Preserves AIM performance while maintaining feasible runtimes on encrypted data with privacy protection.

problem: Tabular diffusion models rely on implicit mechanisms to capture inter-column relationships and relationships, limiting efficiency and interpretability.
approach: Introduces GATD, which augments denoisers with pairwise angles and lengths from column value differences as inputs and auxiliary targets.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with 3.5x fewer parameters on average (up to 25x for classification) while reducing Shape and Trend error by 27% and 20%.

problem: Offline auto-bidding policies collapse multiple effective strategies into suboptimal averaged actions and fail on sparse or long-tail traffic.
approach: Proposes DRIVE, which decouples candidate generation from decision-making via distributional action modeling, retrieval-augmented candidates, and value-based evaluation.
contribution: Consistently improves bidding performance across AuctionNet and reinforcement learning benchmarks with good generalization.

problem: RL policies often fail to generalize beyond training tasks, requiring specialized adaptation methods for deployment in diverse environments.
approach: Proposes Adaptive Policy Backbone (APB), which uses a frozen backbone with lightweight task-specific pre- and post-backbone linear layers for adaptation.
contribution: Achieves comparable performance to standard RL while improving generalization to out-of-distribution tasks, even with random initialization.

problem: Federated Label Distribution Learning fails when clients have heterogeneous annotation quality, as standard aggregation treats all clients equally despite reliability differences.
approach: Proposes FedQual with quality-adaptive training guided by global semantic anchors and reliability-aware aggregation that reweights by effective reliable information.
contribution: Theoretical guarantee showing client-specific calibration outperforms uniform calibration; superior performance on four constructed Fed-LDL benchmarks.

problem: Protein language models are black boxes; mechanistic interpretability methods treat layers independently, failing to capture cross-layer computation.
approach: Introduces ProtoMech, which uses cross-layer transcoders to learn sparse latent representations jointly across layers capturing full computational circuits.
contribution: Recovers 82-89% of original performance on classification/function prediction; identifies compressed circuits using <1% of latent space while retaining up to 79% accuracy.

problem: Inverse reinforcement learning typically requires adversarial training, limiting applicability and sample efficiency in imitation learning.
approach: Proposes EnergyFlow, parameterizing a scalar energy function whose gradient is the denoising field, proving the score function recovers soft Q-function gradient under maximum-entropy optimality.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art imitation performance on manipulation tasks while providing effective reward signals for downstream RL without adversarial training.

problem: Deep learning models for clinical prediction suffer performance degradation under distribution shifts, and domain adaptation methods lack the transparency required for clinical adoption.
approach: Proposes ExtraCare, which decomposes representations into invariant and covariant components with orthogonality constraints, enabling concept-grounded explanations via ablation.
contribution: Superior performance compared to feature alignment with enhanced transparency via human-understandable medical concept mappings on real EHR datasets.

problem: Existing PEFT methods enforce rigid low-rank constraints or incur significant memory overhead, limiting dynamic rank adaptation for LLM fine-tuning.
approach: Proposes SBVI, reformulating LoRA as Wasserstein gradient flow on manifolds of Gaussian measures, governing singular value evolution via stochastic differential equations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior accuracy and memory efficiency by automatically discovering optimal layer-wise rank distribution.

problem: In-context localization for category-agnostic object localization is fragile and requires explicit category supervision, introducing bias toward semantic priors.
approach: Introduces two-stage framework optimizing in-context attention between support boxes and query images without category supervision, refined via GRPO to minimize localization error.
contribution: A 7B model trained with the method outperforms 72B models, demonstrating that context-aware localization objectives surpass scaling.

problem: Image dehazing methods rely on observing hazy image distributions during training, leading to poor generalization to unseen haze types.
approach: Proposes first fully zero-shot dehazing framework using invariant representations across clean and hazy images to train diffusion model on clean images only.
contribution: Remarkably generalizes across various real-world hazy datasets without any hazy training images.

problem: Existing sparse PCA algorithms only work under spiked identity model; combinatorial methods fail for general covariances.
approach: Provides first combinatorial method succeeding for general Σ using truncated power method with poly(s, log(d)) samples and d² poly(s, log(d)) time.
contribution: First global convergence guarantee on truncated power method for sparse PCA beyond spiked identity model with generalization to k sparse components.

problem: RLVR training is prone to instabilities in MoE architectures despite showing promise for scaling reasoning in LLMs; causes remain poorly understood.
approach: Introduces objective-level hacking framework explaining instability through token-level credit misalignment, linking abnormal training-inference discrepancy to spurious optimization signals.
contribution: Traces origin of key pathological dynamics in MoE models and provides mechanistic explanation of training instabilities.

problem: Aligning LLMs to diverse conflicting human preferences is fundamentally challenging; inference-time alignment is computationally expensive requiring multiple forward passes.
approach: Proposes inference-aware meta-alignment (IAMA), training base models to be effectively aligned to multiple task optima via different inference algorithms; introduces non-linear GRPO.
contribution: Enables multi-criteria alignment with minimal inference-time overhead and proves convergence to optimal solution.

problem: Backdoor-based watermarking for T2I model ownership verification assumes faithful verification; adversaries may damage watermarks, degrading reliability.
approach: Proposes Cert-LAS, the first certified MOV method using layer-adaptive smoothing with LFS-guided noise, verifying ownership via hypothesis testing.
contribution: Proves Cert-LAS achieves reliable verification even under malicious removal attacks.

problem: Theoretical understanding of when transformers generalize in planning is limited; success has been inconsistent across tasks.
approach: Introduces C*-RASP extending C-RASP for simultaneous growth in sequence length and vocabulary size, analyzes decoder-only models' ability to verify plans.
contribution: Identifies large class of planning domains where transformers provably learn to verify long plans and characterizes structural properties affecting learnability.

problem: Existing point cloud denoising methods struggle with one-to-one correspondence construction due to ambiguity from noise perturbing coordinates.
approach: Proposes Self-Induced Mirror-Point Consistency (SIMPC), generating mirror-points on the opposite surface side and encouraging consistency between denoising targets.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised methods and surpasses several strong supervised counterparts.

problem: RLVR scaling hits performance plateaus after thousands of training steps with clear diminishing returns from additional computation.
approach: Proposes BroRL, increasing rollouts per example to hundreds for exhaustive exploration; motivates with mass balance analysis showing effect of unsampled tokens diminishes with large rollout size.
contribution: Demonstrates continuous performance gains beyond saturation point of ProRL when scaling rollout count.

problem: Supervised causal learning struggles with generalization across diverse interventional settings, especially when intervention targets are unknown.
approach: Proposes TICL combining Test-Time Training with Joint Causal Inference using self-augmentation to generate instance-specific test-time data and PC-inspired two-phase learning.
contribution: Superior performance on bnlearn benchmarks for both causal discovery and intervention target detection.

problem: Unpaired domain translation requires balancing faithfulness and realism; optimal transport methods are expensive while diffusion methods lack initialization.
approach: Proposes RDMD combining optimal transport and diffusion-based distribution matching, using diffusion for strong initialization and explicit transport cost regularization.
contribution: Provides one-step inference with explicit input-output alignment control while maintaining OT faithfulness.

problem: Conformal prediction yields prohibitively large prediction sets in structured domains like routing or planning.
approach: Introduces graph-based conformal compression, formulating compression as selecting smallest subgraph capturing prescribed probability mass fraction; reduces to weighted densest-k-subgraphs.
contribution: Efficient approximation algorithms with constant-factor coverage-size trade-offs while preserving statistical validity via conformal calibration.

problem: GRPO-based reasoning training creates opportunities for overthinking as extended deliberation enables more relative gains, reducing rollout efficiency.
approach: Proposes WS-GRPO converting terminal rewards into correctness-aware guidance over partial trajectories; trains preference model providing prefix-level continue/stop signals.
contribution: Substantially reduces rollout length while maintaining accuracy on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Test-time adaptation methods for adversarial robustness struggle to identify semantic information and destroy discriminative regions in fine-grained scenarios.
approach: Proposes Attention-Guided Test-Time Prompt Tuning (A-TPT), refining gradient attention rollout to identify semantically meaningful regions and guide spatially varying augmentation.
contribution: Outperforms existing test-time adaptation on both adversarial and clean data.

problem: Video generation models struggle with visual reasoning tasks like spatial planning because training emphasizes perceptual fidelity over reasoning, and generation lacks error recovery.
approach: Introduces ReaForest with ReaGen-27k dataset for spatial planning tasks, Reflective Entropy-Aware Test-Time Scaling for multi-branch reasoning with failure recovery, and constraint verification.
contribution: Substantially surpasses advanced reasoning models and video generators on spatial planning tasks.

problem: Anonymization is assumed to protect privacy but LLM-based agents can reconstruct identities by combining scattered non-identifying cues with public evidence.
approach: Evaluates de-anonymization risk across three settings: classical linkage, controlled InferLink benchmark, and open-ended human-AI traces.
contribution: Agents reconstruct 79.2% of identities in sparse Netflix Prize regime vs 56.0% for classical matching; successfully link individuals without explicit re-identification requests.

problem: Deep learning algorithms' behavior and generalization are not fully understood; flatness of loss landscape matters but existing optimizers neglect it.
approach: Proposes fSGLD, a first-order method biasing dynamics toward flat basins while retaining SGD/SGLD efficiency, with prescribed coupling between noise scale and inverse temperature.
contribution: Non-asymptotic convergence analysis to flatness-biased Gibbs distribution with explicit excess risk guarantees; strong empirical performance on classification and uncertainty tasks.

problem: fMRI is expensive and limited in accessibility; synthesizing from EEG would enable inference of deep brain dynamics from low-cost scalp recordings in naturalistic settings.
approach: Proposes UniEFS, a unified EEG-to-fMRI synthesis model with condition-aware prompts encoding subject metadata, leveraging pretrained fMRI decoder for spatial priors.
contribution: Reliably reconstructs temporally-resolved whole-brain fMRI from EEG with potential for zero-shot generalization to task-based fMRI and clinical populations.

problem: Estimating thought-level advantages in Chain-of-Thought reasoning with GRPO suffers from high variance when relying solely on sampling multiple continuations.
approach: Using multivariate delta method analysis under a tree-style branching setting, the paper reveals an asymmetry: increasing continuations per thought drives variance to zero faster than increasing sampled thoughts alone, making continuation-level branching theoretically necessary.
contribution: Demonstrates that accurate thought-level advantage estimation in GRPO requires continuation-level branching (scaling by M) rather than thought-level branching alone, with empirical validation across math and vision domains.

problem: Scientific exploration requires expensive experiments, but existing Bayesian optimization with LLMs fails to fully exploit the lower cost of LLM predictions versus real experiments.
approach: LABO combines LLM predictions with experimental observations in a single BO loop, using a gating mechanism to dynamically balance reliance on cheap LLM evaluations for broad exploration and costly real experiments only in high-uncertainty regions.
contribution: LABO achieves more sample-efficient optimization with theoretical regret bounds, consistently outperforming existing methods under identical experimental budgets across diverse scientific tasks.

problem: Long-horizon data agent orchestration suffers from error propagation in static execution plans, causing reasoning chain collapse and task failure.
approach: R3DAO introduces reactive topology evolution through hierarchical task decomposition, semantic reflection for localized recovery, and dual-loop experience distillation to create a closed-loop system that self-heals from execution anomalies.
contribution: Achieves 77.36% improvement in success rate over advanced R&D-Agent on MLE-bench while compressing average execution time.

problem: It remains unclear how final-outcome-only rewards in RLVR help overcome the long-horizon barrier to extended reasoning in transformers.
approach: Develops a theory of training dynamics showing that mixed-difficulty training naturally induces an implicit curriculum: easier problems become learnable first and shape the frontier for harder ones, governed by the smoothness of the difficulty spectrum.
contribution: Shows theoretically that RLVR training enters a 'relay' regime with smooth difficulty spectra where persistent gradient signals on easier problems make slightly harder ones tractable, validated via synthetic experiments.

problem: Existing preference-based alignment methods rely on model-generated image pairs which can be ambiguous when both samples are poor quality, hindering inference of desirable outputs.
approach: Adopts a data-centric perspective treating real images as reference points and constructs preference signals by contrasting them with generated or perturbed samples, without manual annotation.
contribution: Demonstrates that real-data-based supervision provides effective guidance for aligning diffusion models with performance comparable to existing preference-based methods.

problem: Standard video tokenization using 3D grids requires downstream models to learn all low-level details pixel-by-pixel regardless of video complexity, leading to high learning complexity.
approach: VideoFlexTok represents videos as variable-length sequences with coarse-to-fine structure where early tokens capture semantics and motion, later tokens add details, with a generative flow decoder enabling reconstruction from any token count.
contribution: Achieves comparable generation quality with 5x smaller model (1.1B vs 5.2B) and enables 10-second 81-frame videos with 8x fewer tokens than 3D grid tokenizers.

problem: LLMs could strategically suppress their exploration during RL training to influence the training outcome, creating a failure mode where models resist capability elicitation.
approach: Creates model organisms of selective RL resistance by fine-tuning LLMs to follow underperformance strategies, then evaluates detection and mitigation strategies including monitoring, weight noising, and SFT-based elicitation.
contribution: Shows that models can explicitly reason about suppressing exploration when given sufficient context information, demonstrating exploration hacking as a possible failure mode of RL on capable LLMs.

problem: Existing accelerated gradient methods for l-smoothness either incur extra dependence on initial gradients, suffer exponential factors, or require costly auxiliary routines, leaving open whether AGD-type rates are possible.
approach: Develops new proof techniques using Fourier analysis to achieve O(sqrt(l(0)) R / sqrt(eps)) oracle complexity for small-eps and virtually any l-smoothness function.
contribution: For (L0, L1)-smoothness, provides provably optimal O(sqrt(L0) R / sqrt(eps)) bound in small-eps regime, removing all non-constant multiplicative factors from prior algorithms.

problem: Diffusion-based vision-language-action policies represent SE(3) poses as flat R^12 vectors, causing manifold drift, broken equivariance, and non-geodesic trajectories with excessive kinematic cost.
approach: Lie Diffuser Actor operates intrinsically on SE(3) by injecting noise through left-invariant SDEs, predicting scores in tangent space, and retracting samples via the exponential map.
contribution: Eliminates manifold drift by construction while guaranteeing coordinate-frame equivariance, improving CALVIN task performance by 7.3% and validating on real robot tasks.

problem: Test-time scaling improves LLM reasoning but when candidate diversity is reduced, it produces unsafe outputs at higher rates than adversarially targeted attacks.
approach: Introduces RefDiv, a reference-guided diversity reduction protocol that stress tests TTS pipelines by constraining the diversity of candidate pools while measuring safety degradation.
contribution: Demonstrates across multiple models and TTS strategies (MCTS, Best-of-N) that modest diversity reduction significantly increases unsafe output rates, even exceeding adversarially-crafted prompts.

problem: Speculative decoding degrades in production under high concurrency where verification compute dominates, forcing a dilemma between massive verification waste with static trees or cumulative errors with dynamic trees.
approach: ECHO reformulates speculative execution as a budgeted scheduling problem with sparse confidence gating that manages the batch as a unified super-tree, elastically pivoting budget between depth and width.
contribution: Achieves up to 5.35x walltime speedup and over 20% relative improvement against state-of-the-art baselines across model scales including industrial-grade Qwen3-235B.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs with zeroth-order optimization is memory-efficient but suffers from high-variance gradient estimates and slow convergence, while sparse ZO updates rely on selecting informative parameters without gradient signals.
approach: CurvZO tracks curvature signals from scalar ZO feedback and uses them to construct parameter-wise sampling distributions, with dynamic perturbation budget adaptation.
contribution: Improves fine-tuning accuracy by up to 4.4 points and achieves 2x speedup while preserving memory efficiency across OPT and Llama models on diverse NLP tasks.

problem: Theory of Mind datasets suffer from a pervasive 'shortcut' issue where tasks reach high accuracy through spurious correlations rather than genuine reasoning, confounding progress measurement.
approach: Develops a framework to systematically identify shortcuts in ToM datasets and studies Thinking-RFT, which combines RL with verifiable rewards and explicit reasoning chains to elevate reasoning beyond supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Thinking-RFT achieves 6% improvement over SFT overall, 10% on complex higher-order reasoning, and 7% on multimodal cases, while generalizing better to unseen domains and counterfactuals.

problem: Theoretical understanding of diffusion models' statistical efficiency for multi-modal distributions with intrinsic low-dimensional structure remains limited due to strong regularity assumptions.
approach: Studies sample complexity for diffusion models on unions of low-dimensional subspaces, assuming subgaussian data distributions within each subspace and using score-based diffusion analysis.
contribution: Shows diffusion models achieve near-optimal O(eps^{-k \vee 2}) sample complexity where k is intrinsic dimension, significantly improving over prior curse-of-dimensionality bounds without smoothness or log-concavity assumptions.

problem: Q-learning under reward corruption and asynchronous sampling lacks finite-time robustness guarantees matching standard bounds.
approach: Develops a robust Q-learning variant analyzed under asynchronous sampling with time-correlated data, using refined Azuma-Hoeffding inequalities for almost-martingales.
contribution: Proves finite-time guarantees matching existing bounds plus an additive term scaling with the fraction of corrupted samples, with information-theoretic lower bounds showing near-optimality.

problem: Existing world models are trained independently per task or use offline multi-task learning, failing to exploit latent relationships among tasks in online interactive scenarios.
approach: TaskLoom adopts grouped two-stage training: tasks are divided into groups based on world model gradient similarity with fine-grained sharing within groups, then coarse-grained knowledge is exchanged across groups.
contribution: Outperforms baseline methods on Proprio Control, Visual Control, and Meta-World benchmarks, validating hierarchical knowledge-sharing effectiveness for both low and high-dimensional inputs.

problem: Expert-level calibration in mixture-of-experts models is sufficient for hard-routed models but insufficient for soft-routed models under distribution shift.
approach: Proposes adversarial reweighting that penalizes calibration errors of the routed aggregate under distribution shift to improve MoE calibration in soft-routed settings.
contribution: Demonstrates improved accuracy-calibration tradeoff both on average and on difficult data subsets across model classes and distribution shifts.

problem: LLM-based optimization modeling struggles to verify correctness of generated models without checking constraint rationality or solution validity, hindering verification and correction.
approach: Opt-Verifier uses dual-side verification: structure-side ensures alignment with problem description capturing constraints accurately, solution-side interprets solution validity and mathematical soundness.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art with over 20% improvement in modeling accuracy across popular benchmarks.

problem: Existing diffusion-based music editing methods fail to achieve stem-specific timbre transfer in polyphonic music, causing boundary leakage and accompaniment corruption.
approach: Polyphonia uses acoustic-informed attention calibration leveraging probabilistic acoustic priors to establish coarse boundaries, enabling precise target stem manipulation while preserving background.
contribution: Achieves 15.5% increase in target alignment over baselines while maintaining music fidelity and non-target integrity, with standardized PolyEvalPrompts benchmark of 1,170 timbre transfer tasks.

problem: Sequence models operate at fixed scales and struggle to generalize to longer horizons or higher resolutions without retraining, lacking mechanisms to enforce consistent dynamics across scales.
approach: Dynamic Fractal Mamba applies a single shared operator across multiple scales via recursive state-space modeling with exponentially scaled time steps, using learned content-aware coarse-graining and cross-scale consistency objectives.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Transformers and flat Mamba on long-range forecasting and spatial tasks while maintaining linear complexity, with zero-shot generalization to unseen scales.

problem: Test-time self-consistency under limited budget allocation lacks principled methods for sample-efficient trajectory aggregation.
approach: PETS introduces a principled optimization framework modeling self-consistency rate as agreement with infinite-budget majority vote, connecting to crowdsourcing theory and proposing offline/online allocation algorithms.
contribution: Achieves perfect self-consistency on GPQA while reducing sampling budget by up to 75% (offline) and 55% (online) relative to uniform allocation.

problem: Graph random features on implicit graphs (where edges are defined by feature similarities) lack efficient computation methods without materializing the full graph.
approach: SWING conducts walks in continuous embedding spaces rather than on graph nodes, using customized Gumbel-softmax sampling with linearized kernels and importance sampling techniques based on Fourier analysis connections.
contribution: Provides accelerator-friendly graph random features computation without input graph materialization, with detailed analysis and comprehensive experiments across implicit graph classes.

problem: One-shot federated learning suffers from misaligned feature representations due to joint domain and label shift across clients, which iterative optimization cannot correct.
approach: SLOT-Align uses Bures-Wasserstein barycenters as global reference and aligns local representations via closed-form geodesic optimal transport maps with a shared frozen encoder.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy and robustness across multiple benchmarks and pretrained backbones under joint domain and label shift, without modifying training procedures.

problem: Data difficulty during supervised fine-tuning shows inconsistent or context-dependent effects on LLM behavior, with no universally optimal difficulty level identified.
approach: Systematically studies data difficulty from empirical and theoretical perspectives, revealing an interplay between generalization gap and extrapolation gap that depends on dataset size, validated via synthetic experiments and PAC-Bayesian bounds.
contribution: Shows optimal data difficulty shifts toward harder data as budget increases, providing guidance for difficulty-based data selection under different model and data conditions.

problem: Multimodal reward models lose visual details due to large context budgets and suffer from forgetting during chain-of-thought when all visual information is packed into the initial prompt.
approach: VR-Thinker introduces visual reasoning operations with configurable memory windows allowing active visual evidence acquisition during reasoning, enhanced via cold-start distillation, rejection sampling, and GRPO.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on video benchmarks: 80.5% on VideoGen Reward, 82.3% on GenAI-Bench, and 75.6% on MJ-Bench-Video with a 7B model.

problem: Neural methods for MILP branching struggle with semantic variation across depths, scarcity of upstream nodes, and expensive strong branching sample collection.
approach: SC-MILP uses dynamic stratified contrastive training grouping B&B nodes by feature distributions with depth-aware representations, plus upstream-augmented MILP derivation generating theoretically equivalent and perturbed instances.
contribution: Significantly improves branching accuracy and reduces solving time with particularly strong gains at upstream nodes, scaling to large-scale instances.

problem: Conventional autoregressive models suffer from prohibitive latency and typically underperform non-causal alternatives due to next-token prediction constraints.
approach: Self-token prediction enables predicting a flexible number of tokens per step; SAR is the first spatially autoregressive image generator using this paradigm.
contribution: Delivers faster inference speeds and consistently outperforms prior autoregressive baselines while matching state-of-the-art non-causal models.

problem: Understanding of Transformer training dynamics remains limited despite their widespread success, particularly regarding how attention parameters evolve during learning.
approach: Identifies recurrent focus-dilution cycles in attention learning via gradient-flow analysis with stage-wise linearization, decomposing each cycle into distinct stages of embedding condensation, frequency-driven focus, and mass redistribution.
contribution: Provides rigorous theoretical explanation for focus-dilution dynamics in one-layer Transformers on Markovian data, validated on synthetic data and natural language corpora.

problem: Causal discovery in time series using nonlinear models summarizes relationships as scalar edge scores, obscuring state-dependent effects that vary across regimes and contexts.
approach: Formalizes function-valued causal influence for additive architectures using Individual Conditional Expectation framework to estimate causal response functions from trained models.
contribution: Demonstrates edges with indistinguishable scalar scores exhibit qualitatively different functional behaviors (monotonic, thresholded, saturating, sign-changing) missed by score-centric approaches.

problem: Latent diffusion models excel at efficiency but discard end-to-end modeling benefits by encoding images separately and requiring a trained decoder.
approach: Latent Forcing modifies architectures to jointly process latents and pixels with separately tuned noise schedules, allowing latents to act as a scratchpad before high-frequency pixel features are generated.
contribution: Achieves new state-of-the-art for diffusion transformer-based pixel generation at its compute scale while maintaining latent efficiency.

problem: Existing MAG benchmarks exhibit critical limitations in domain coverage, encoder flexibility, model diversity, and task scope, preventing fair evaluation.
approach: OpenMAG integrates 19 datasets across 6 domains with 16 encoders, 24 state-of-the-art models, and 8 downstream tasks in a standardized framework with comprehensive assessment of necessity, data quality, effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency.
contribution: Derives 14 fundamental insights into MAG learning to guide future advancements through systematic assessment.

problem: Deep learning approaches require prohibitive data for known-constraint Exact Cover tasks, while neuro-symbolic methods face training infeasibility and scalability bottlenecks.
approach: HONet integrates structure-preserving Deep Residual Hypergraph Encoder with differentiable fixed-constraint Quadratic Programming layer using Geometric Consistency Loss to align valid solutions with global energy minima.
contribution: Rapidly achieves 100% accuracy on 9x9 Sudoku using limited samples with superior data efficiency, robustness in sparse regimes, and scalability to additional tasks.

problem: Enforcing hard constraints in neural network predictions is challenging without hand-crafted layers specific to each constraint type.
approach: Proposes a plug-in differentiable layer using fast implicit convex optimization to enforce general linear constraints via divergence minimization, showing connections to Softmax, Sinkhorn, and tanh.
contribution: Derives closed-form solutions using Euclidean distance for efficient constraint enforcement (GLCLayer), validated on linear programming and real-world problems like partial graph matching and portfolio allocation.

problem: Multivariate time-series forecasting optimization induces parameter dependence during training that data-level interventions cannot control, degrading generalization.
approach: Proposes transition-variance alignment (TVA) regulating optimization-induced dependence by smoothly gating step size based on mismatch between estimated noise scale and target scale, using SDE interpretation.
contribution: Consistently improves forecasting accuracy across real-world benchmarks with negligible overhead, integrating seamlessly with diverse methods without architectural changes.

problem: Large vision-language models hallucinate fluent but unsupported content due to route competition where the text pathway dominates despite visual token attention.
approach: Proposes training-free intervention decomposing attention heads into visual and text routes, estimating token-level effects via efficient one-forward/one-gradient approximation to selectively suppress text routes.
contribution: Consistently reduces hallucination-related errors across five benchmarks with limited impact on multimodal performance at modest inference-time overhead.

problem: Blind suppression of language priors in MLLMs to reduce hallucinations disrupts the model's semantic manifold, leading to performance degradation (Manifold Departure).
approach: MGAP is a geometry-aware training-free decoding method constructing a language-prior subspace via SVD and projecting hidden states with consistency-aware gating to adaptively attenuate only projected priors.
contribution: Outperforms prior decoding baselines on POPE and CHAIR with stronger hallucination suppression without sacrificing coherence via subspace-selective updates.

problem: PDE modeling with neural networks lacks equivariance to arbitrary pseudo-Euclidean groups and standard CSCNNs have incomplete kernel bases limiting expressivity.
approach: C-CSCNNs augment kernels with equivariant input-dependent representations and solve equivariance constraints efficiently via implicit parameterization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard CSCNNs and matches state-of-the-art on multiple PDE forecasting tasks including fluid dynamics and relativistic electrodynamics.

problem: Smoothing signals via simple kernels on irregular domains is biased against boundaries, lacking the principled approach offered by Laplacians on well-structured domains.
approach: Introduces a broad class of smoothing operators derived from similarity/adjacency matrices, normalized into diffusion-like operators via symmetric Sinkhorn algorithm to match Laplacian behavior.
contribution: Enables Laplacian-like smoothing of irregular data (point clouds, sparse voxels, mixture of Gaussians) while retaining spectral information, with applications to shape analysis and matching.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering is degraded by missing feature values and missing views, with graph-based methods relying on costly imputation or shallow fusion mechanisms.
approach: CARD reformulates IMVC from spectral filtering perspective, constructing unified anchor-induced hypergraph and deriving high-order resolvent diffusion operator as rational spectral filter with implicit compact solver.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance while scaling linearly in N for fixed anchor budget, without explicit view imputation, across eight benchmarks including large-scale datasets.

problem: Human evaluation of AI systems is fragile under majority vote due to annotator disagreement, bias, and variability, yielding unstable system rankings.
approach: STABLEVAL models latent item correctness and annotator-specific confusion patterns to produce posterior expected item credit and calibrated scores, explicitly designing for stable evaluation.
contribution: Yields more stable and statistically grounded system rankings than majority vote, with controlled experiments and real-world benchmarks demonstrating improved robustness under annotator heterogeneity.

problem: Unsupervised skill discovery learns task-irrelevant or hazardous behaviors due to uniform exploration, while existing guided methods need additional training and manual rules.
approach: COLLIE constructs a semantically coherent skill latent space from unsupervised data, enabling training-free guidance signals that work with sparse online human feedback.
contribution: COLLIE learns diverse, human-aligned skills while avoiding hazardous behaviors and achieving superior downstream performance with minimal human feedback.

problem: Standard dimension reduction fails to preserve global structure in single-cell transcriptomics because it doesn't adequately account for the geometric properties of biological data.
approach: InfoGlobe models RNA counts as Multinomial samples and leverages Fisher-Rao metric isometry between gene-level and gene-group statistical manifolds to preserve information geometry.
contribution: InfoGlobe preserves local-and-global cell-type geodesic distances, automatically discovers gene groups, and naturally mitigates batch effects without explicit alignment.

problem: Evaluating new models on existing benchmarks is expensive because generating and evaluating responses for all queries can be prohibitively costly.
approach: Leverages cached responses from previously-evaluated models using Data Kernel Perspective Space (DKPS) to predict benchmark performance and reduce query budget.
contribution: DKPS-based methods achieve the same accuracy as full evaluation with substantially decreased queries, and offline query selection improves prediction accuracy.

problem: Multimodal VAEs struggle with a trade-off between generative quality and coherence—generating realistic samples that are semantically consistent across modalities.
approach: Hölder++ implements true Hölder pooling without approximation, models distinct shared and private representations, and uses hierarchical inference for better disentanglement.
contribution: Hölder++ consistently improves the generative quality-coherence trade-off, yields more structured latent spaces, and learns shared representations useful for downstream tasks.

problem: Conventional architectures lose performance when input image color distribution changes at inference, and existing color equivariant methods introduce artifacts by approximating interval values as 1D translations.
approach: Builds color equivariant architecture by lifting saturation/luminance values from the interval to the circle (double-cover) to achieve true equivariance without approximation.
contribution: Resolves approximation artifacts, improves interpretability and generalizability, and achieves better performance on fine-grained classification and medical imaging than conventional and equivariant baselines.

problem: Generating executable CAD programs from images requires alignment between visual geometry and symbolic program syntax, but existing methods fail to scale with design complexity and rely on limited supervised data or expensive post-training.
approach: GIFT uses geometric feedback to bootstrap training data via Soft-Rejection Sampling (retaining diverse high-fidelity programs) and Failure-Driven Augmentation (converting near-misses into synthetic examples).
contribution: GIFT improves mean IoU by 12% over supervised baseline and reduces inference compute by 80% by amortizing test-time search into model parameters.

problem: Extending reinforcement learning gains to open-ended domains is difficult because ground-truth verification is unavailable, human annotation is expensive, and learned reward models are prone to reward hacking.
approach: RcRL exploits the generation-verification gap using pairwise preferences with a curriculum over rubric criteria, creating a more discriminative signal than absolute scoring.
contribution: RcRL preserves output entropy past 1000 steps (vs baselines plateauing within hundreds), achieves 70.5% preference on creative writing, and 25.4% improvement on HealthBench consensus.

problem: Jailbreak attacks bypass LLM safety alignment, but their mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering development of robust defenses.
approach: Identifies two functionally differentiated attention head types: Adversarially Compromised Heads (ACHs) in early layers that are suppressed by attacks, and Safety-Aligned Heads (SAHs) in mid-layers that maintain robust activations.
contribution: Shows ACH suppression drives jailbreaks while SAH activations persist, and reading these persistent activations yields competitive detection performance without training.

problem: Designing recommender systems faces the challenge of exploration-exploitation trade-off with incentive compatibility constraints in settings with stochastic user covariates.
approach: Two-stage algorithm integrates incentivized exploration with offline learning, using inverse proportional gap sampling (IPGS) in the second stage to maintain incentive compatibility.
contribution: Algorithm RCB achieves O(sqrt(KdT)) regret while satisfying incentive constraints, and discovers the trade-off between incentive budget and regret.

problem: Recovering radiometric fidelity from unknown dynamic range compression (like low-light enhancement and HDR reconstruction) is a blind inverse problem with unknown forward model and irreversible information loss.
approach: Introduces cascaded monotonic Bernstein (CaMB) operator to enforce monotonicity as hard architectural bias, integrated with diffusion models for geometric and semantic recovery.
contribution: CaMB-Diff significantly outperforms zero-shot baselines in signal fidelity and physical consistency on low-light enhancement, low-field MRI, and HDR reconstruction.

problem: Predicting structured scientific spectra requires capturing rich physical information while enforcing hard constraints like conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry, but existing methods treat them as unconstrained sequences.
approach: DeepSciReasoner combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning to capture spectral structure while respecting underlying physics.
contribution: Substantially improves prediction accuracy on eDOS, phDOS, XANES, and Raman spectra while maintaining physical consistency across all spectra types.

problem: Time series forecasting requires both semantic understanding of context and stochastic modeling of temporal dynamics, but existing approaches rely on either LLMs for semantics or diffusion models for generation, each inadequate alone.
approach: CoGenCast couples pre-trained LLMs with flow-matching by reconfiguring LLM attention for bidirectional encoding and integrating flow-matching for temporal evolution modeling.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on multiple benchmarks and naturally supports multimodal forecasting and cross-domain unified training.

problem: General continual learning systems must adapt to evolving environments with blurry task boundaries and online datastreams, but pretrained model-based methods struggle to reconcile diverse temporal information in a single pass.
approach: MePo uses meta-learning on pseudo task sequences from pretraining data and initializes meta covariance matrix as reference geometry for robust output alignment.
contribution: Achieves 15.10% improvement on CIFAR-100, 13.36% on ImageNet-R, and 12.56% on CUB-200 in rehearsal-free continual learning without needing task boundaries.

problem: Reinforcement learning fine-tuning of Vision-Language Models is prohibitively expensive, and existing methods port LLM techniques without exploiting VLMs' intrinsic text-vision alignment during reasoning.
approach: FOCUS-RL derives lightweight alignment metrics (PVA for sample difficulty, RVA for CoT quality) from dynamic text-vision alignment patterns to enable automated curriculum and dense supervision.
contribution: Achieves 2.5x–4x faster convergence over vanilla GRPO and +4.4 average accuracy gains across six benchmarks and multiple VLM families.

problem: Locally constrained decoding (LCD) for enforcing schema constraints on LLM outputs results in biased sampling because it myopically masks tokens without accounting for global dependencies.
approach: Proposes constructing globally constrained decoding (GCD) and probabilistic GCD (P-GCD) proposals for sequential Monte Carlo by tensorizing finite automata and circuit-multiplying them.
contribution: GCD and P-GCD converge faster to target distribution than LCD with fewer particles on function calling, keyword generation, and SQL generation tasks.

problem: Existing explicit surface reconstruction methods achieve strong performance but rely on test-time optimization, resulting in prohibitive runtimes of several minutes.
approach: FastSESR uses a lightweight triangular candidate network (TCN) with edge-factorized parameterization for efficient triangle extraction, followed by offset optimization network for refinement.
contribution: Accelerates surface reconstruction by at least 20x over prior methods while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality on scene-level datasets.

problem: Parallel decoding for diffusion LLMs is difficult because each denoising step provides only token-wise marginal distributions, while unmasking multiple tokens requires accounting for inter-token dependencies.
approach: DAPD uses self-attention to induce a conditional dependency graph and performs parallel decoding by selecting independent sets on the graph.
contribution: Improves accuracy–steps trade-off over existing methods and enables more globally distributed parallel updates exploiting any-order generation capability.

problem: Adversarial training fails in long-tailed settings due to severe robustness degradation on tail classes, caused by posterior mismatch where coarse-grained labels collapse class posteriors.
approach: PAT learns a posterior surrogate for fine-grained probabilistic supervision and integrates weight perturbations to encourage flatter loss landscapes.
contribution: Improves robustness with especially large gains on worst-class, and theory shows accurate posteriors tighten class-frequency estimation and robust generalization bounds.

problem: The Natarajan dimension characterizes learnability for finite label spaces, but fails for multiclass partial concept classes with unbounded label spaces.
approach: Shows Daniely-Shalev (DS) dimension characterizes learnability and reveals the Disambiguation Paradox: simple disambiguation schemes can destroy learnability while richer labeling preserves it.
contribution: Provides PAC learnability characterization for partial concept classes in multiclass settings and characterizes label-complexity vs sample-complexity trade-offs.

problem: Scaling inference-time compute in transformers trains them to emit explicit chain-of-thought tokens, but these cannot be applied during pretraining and rely solely on serial verbalization.
approach: Thoughtbubbles natively performs parallel adaptive computation in latent space by learning to fork or delete residual streams, forming 'bubbles' of computation mid-network.
contribution: Outperforms both standard decoder LMs and non-adaptive parallel methods on perplexity/zero-shot evals using half the training budget, achieving competitive GSM8K with half token budget.

problem: Vision-language pre-training for 3D CT imaging struggles with inefficient visual backbones and coarse semantic alignment between images and radiology reports.
approach: Proposes CNN-ViT hybrid encoder for efficient local detail capture, disease-level contrastive learning with learnable query tokens, and diagnosis-aware prompt strategy.
contribution: Achieves 84.4% AUC on CT-RATE (+5.1%), 75.4% on Rad-ChestCT (+5.4%), and +9.8% on 60-disease benchmark with strong transfer to report generation.

problem: Training generalist robot policies for diverse embodiments requires prohibitively costly data collection and retraining for each new embodiment.
approach: AugE-Toolkit provides a scalable robot augmentation pipeline that augments OXE dataset across 9 different embodiments, creating OXE-AugE with 4.4M trajectories.
contribution: Augmenting datasets improves performance on augmented robots, unseen robots, and original robots under distribution shift, with 24-45% success rate improvement on real manipulation tasks.

problem: Mean-field variational inference is scalable but its independence assumption severely limits inference when the posterior is inherently coupled across instances.
approach: Copula-SVI augments amortized marginals with explicit vine-copula posterior and refines samples with Stein updates, using vine decomposition for efficient learning.
contribution: Enables efficient higher-order instance-level dependence modeling with consistent improvements over structured VI baselines on constrained clustering and time series.

problem: Verification of model outputs relies on imperfect LLM judges and reward models, and ground truth labels are time-consuming and expensive to acquire.
approach: FUSE improves verification by ensembling verifiers without ground truth by controlling conditional dependencies using spectral algorithms.
contribution: Matches or improves semi-supervised alternatives without any labeled data across diverse generators, verifiers, and benchmarks including GPQA Diamond and IMO questions.

problem: Red-teaming Vision-Language Models for toxicity detection treats image generation as a black box, providing only terminal scores without understanding when and how toxic semantics emerge.
approach: STARE treats the denoising trajectory as exploitable attack surface using hierarchical RL with prompt editor and T2I fine-tuning via GRPO to align toxicity across phases.
contribution: Achieves 68% improvement in Attack Success Rate and reveals Optimization-Induced Phase Alignment: toxicity concentrates in early semantic phases and late refinement phases.

problem: Current spoken dialogue systems fail on under-represented dialects and accents due to misidentifying input language, and standard fine-tuning is expensive and prone to overfitting.
approach: CLD integrates convex optimization into dialogue pipelines using multi-GPU ADMM in JAX, providing global optimality guarantees and fast polynomial-time training.
contribution: Achieves 97-98% accuracy in low-resource regimes with certified margin stability and provable robustness to feature perturbations.

problem: Beyond conditional average treatment effects, treatments may impact entire outcome distributions in covariate-dependent ways, but existing methods don't capture such distributional effects.
approach: Proposes novel estimand for conditional distributional treatment effects with doubly robust estimator that is minimax optimal, and develops test for homogeneity with valid type 1 error.
contribution: First test with provably valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives for global homogeneity of conditional potential outcome distributions.

problem: RLVR methods typically center trajectory rewards using per-prompt empirical means, which can be noisy and unstable especially in low-generation regimes.
approach: Proposes shrinkage estimators combining per-prompt and cross-prompt means inspired by Stein's paradox to improve per-prompt mean estimation accuracy.
contribution: Shrinkage baselines provably yield lower-variance policy-gradient estimators across algorithms and require no additional hyperparameters or computation.

problem: Traditional whole slide image (WSI) analysis via multiple instance learning is computationally expensive due to exhaustive patch-level processing, severely limiting efficiency and scalability.
approach: PathCTM formulates inference as dynamic information pursuit transitioning from low to high magnification with attention-guided pruning and confidence-aware early stopping.
contribution: Reduces required patches by 95.95%, shortens inference time by 95.62%, and maintains AUC without degradation compared to standard MIL methods.

problem: Training reliable Process Reward Models (PRMs) for scientific reasoning requires expert-verified step-wise labels, which are prohibitively costly to obtain.
approach: DC-W2S stratifies weak supervision into reliability regimes by intersecting Self-Consensus and Neighborhood-Consensus metrics, using curriculum sampling and reliability-aware masking.
contribution: Enables training robust PRMs for complex reasoning without exhaustive expert annotation, proving strategic data curation more effective than indiscriminate training.

problem: Average run length (ARL) and average detection delay (ADD) are widely used optimality criteria for changepoint detection, but their application to real datasets with limited and irregular lengths is hindered.
approach: Proposes non-parametric KM-ARL and KM-ADD estimators by drawing analogy to survival analysis to model detection probabilities under sequence truncation.
contribution: Provides asymptotically unbiased estimators with provable bias bounds, enhancing robustness against limited/irregular sequences and improving model selection.

problem: Single-Positive Multi-Label Learning studies learning from incomplete supervision, but real-world annotations are biased toward salient categories, causing existing methods to miss less salient labels.
approach: PiSA constructs reliable class-wise prototypes from salient labels and leverages them to guide embedding learning for non-salient label recognition.
contribution: Theoretically shows SalSPML is harder than random SPML and demonstrates consistent improvements with average mAP gain of 3.16% on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Modern datasets contain samples of highly varying quality, and training directly on heterogeneous data yields suboptimal models for diffusion-based generation.
approach: Ambient Dataloops uses iterative dataset-model co-evolution where synthetically improved samples are treated as noisy at progressively lower noise levels, using Ambient Diffusion.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on unconditional and text-conditional image generation and de novo protein design with theoretical justification.

problem: Learning from language feedback in LLM agents lacks principled framing despite impressive empirical demonstrations, making it difficult to understand learning complexity.
approach: Formalizes LLF problem with sufficient assumptions for latency rewards, introduces transfer eluder dimension as complexity measure, develops no-regret algorithm HELiX.
contribution: Demonstrates cases where rich language feedback can be exponentially faster than reward learning, with performance guarantees scaling with transfer eluder dimension.

problem: Scaling RL with verifiable rewards is bottlenecked by limited existing verifiable data, where improvements saturate during training.
approach: Golden Goose synthesizes unlimited RLVR tasks from unverifiable text by constructing multiple-choice QA versions of fill-in-the-middle, generating diverse distractors.
contribution: Creates GooseReason-0.7M dataset with 0.7M tasks across math/programming/science, revives saturated models with sustained gains, and achieves SOTA on cybersecurity domain.

problem: Prompt injection attacks bypass LLM agents, but their mechanisms remain unclear, hindering defense development.
approach: Traces injection to role confusion where models perceive text source by how it sounds rather than labeled role, demonstrates via CoT Forgery attack.
contribution: Achieves 60% attack success against frontier models, shows degree of role confusion predicts attack success before generation, generalizes to standard agent injections.

problem: Current Video-LLM approaches for temporal grounding generate timestamps directly from unstructured visual tokens, leading to brittle numerics and inconsistent boundaries.
approach: F2G reformulates temporal grounding as verifiable Identify-then-Measure problem using predictive temporal perception and evidence-driven reasoning.
contribution: Consistently improves grounding accuracy across diverse benchmarks, transfers robustly across VLM backbones, and preserves general video understanding.

problem: Reconstructing temporal evolution from static sample snapshots is challenging for dynamic processes like cellular differentiation, requiring methods that scale in high dimensions.
approach: MMtSBM extends multi-marginal Schrödinger bridges to unpaired data via Iterative Markovian Fitting algorithm, enabling practical high-dimensional recovery.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on real datasets like transcriptomic trajectory inference in 100D, and for the first time recovers couplings/dynamics in very high-dimensional images.

problem: Low-count PET reconstruction is hindered by dissipative nature of prevailing generative models that wash out weak but diagnostically critical lesion signals.
approach: FlowPET reformulates reconstruction as volume-preserving transport via Separable Hamiltonian System with conjugate boundary conditions enforcing data consistency.
contribution: Surpasses state-of-the-art in SSIM/PSNR and more crucially exhibits superior recovery of low-contrast lesions in high-noise regimes.

problem: Language models show smooth scaling laws, but some capabilities exhibit sudden breakthroughs, with debate over whether these are emergent or metric artifacts.
approach: Shows breakthroughs are driven by continuous changes in probability distribution of training outcomes when performance is bimodally distributed across seeds.
contribution: Demonstrates sharp metric breakthroughs are produced by underlying continuous distribution changes, appearing well before most seeds achieve breakthrough.

problem: Correlation clustering becomes intractable in streaming settings where only nodes arrive sequentially and their similarities are computed on-the-fly rather than pre-given as edges.
approach: C4Approx uses a streaming algorithm that processes nodes in O(1) passes with sublinear space, approximating clustering cost by storing only a small sample of nodes and exploiting the similarity function structure.
contribution: Achieves comparable performance to offline baselines while storing only 2% of nodes on real datasets, with theoretical guarantees on sublinear space and constant passes.

problem: Generative trajectory policies for offline RL face a fundamental trade-off: diffusion-like models are accurate but slow, while consistency models are fast but degrade performance significantly.
approach: Generative Trajectory Policies (GTPs) unify diffusion, flow matching, and consistency models as instances of continuous-time ODE-based generation, learning the full solution map to balance speed and quality.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on D4RL benchmarks including perfect scores on hard AntMaze tasks, outperforming prior generative policies.

problem: Test-time compute methods like best-of-n sampling are widely used but lack theoretical understanding of their fundamental limits and optimality.
approach: Analyzes reward-filtered sequential inference, which selectively incorporates high-reward generations into context while suppressing inferior ones, proving strictly stronger theoretical guarantees than standard test-time compute.
contribution: Demonstrates both theoretically and empirically that reward filtering provides tighter bounds than best-of-n, with consistent improvements across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Estimating treatment effects from text using LLM embeddings fails because Wasserstein matching in high dimensions suffers from curse of dimensionality, making standard causal generalization bounds vacuous.
approach: SPIKED-CFR assumes treatment bias manifests primarily as low-dimensional discrepancy in semantic space, using Wasserstein Projection Pursuit to identify and balance only this subspace via orthogonal projections on the Stiefel manifold.
contribution: Achieves sample complexity governed by intrinsic dimension k rather than ambient dimension D, with tighter PEHE bounds validated on clinical benchmarks.

problem: Vision-language models expose private tokenization details (patch size, preprocessing) through side channels, enabling model stealing and adversarial manipulation.
approach: Sweeps synthetic grid images to detect periodic accuracy drops aligned with hidden patch grids, inferring patch size and preprocessing parameters through task-level side channels in patchification.
contribution: Reliably recovers tokenizer parameters including patch size and resolution from black-box VLMs (Qwen-VL, GPT, Claude), enabling preprocessing-aware transfer attacks.

problem: Planning algorithms using entropy-regularized Bellman backups achieve suboptimal sample complexity (O(ε^-4)) due to first-order Taylor approximations with high remainder terms.
approach: SecondOrderSmoothCruiser uses optimal-transport-smoothed Bellman backups with closed-form quadratic corrections over action distributions, achieving cubic remainder bounds through principled Stein corrections.
contribution: Reduces oracle complexity from O(ε^-4) to O(ε^-3) with fixed OT parameters, improving sample efficiency while maintaining theoretical guarantees.

problem: Multimodal learning assumes all modalities are available at training and inference, but real data is often incomplete with missing modalities or asynchronous collection.
approach: PRIMO uses supervised latent-variable modeling to impute missing modalities as latent variables capturing their relationship to observed modalities, drawing samples for marginal prediction and instance-level impact analysis.
contribution: Maintains performance of unimodal baselines when fully missing and multimodal baselines when complete, while quantifying per-instance modality importance.

problem: Routing and ensembling many LLMs requires selecting which models to use and how to combine them, with existing methods failing to adapt dynamically to task heterogeneity or resolve reasoning conflicts.
approach: RL-Focal uses two-stage RL: a Decider agent selects optimal-size ensembles per task via error-diversity and performance rewards, while a Fusion agent learns to resolve conflicts and adapt to dynamic teams using focal diversity metrics.
contribution: Achieves 8.48% improvement over best individual LLM on five benchmarks with small ensemble sizes, with stronger robustness.

problem: Flow-based text-to-image models follow deterministic paths, making it costly to generate diverse outputs under limited sampling budgets without compromising image quality.
approach: Uses training-free guidance that encourages lateral spread among trajectories via feature-space objectives while reintroducing uncertainty through stochastic perturbations orthogonal to the generation flow.
contribution: Consistently improves diversity metrics (Vendi Score, Brisque) across text-to-image settings while preserving image quality and prompt fidelity.

problem: Long-video temporal reasoning in LVLMs is limited because RL methods only verify final answers, missing fabricated intermediate temporal claims that produce correct answers through wrong reasoning.
approach: VideoTrace-R1 builds Temporal Reasoning Traces (TRT) indexing video event chains as queryable verification primitives, using temporal-enhanced GRPO with per-block rewards computed by TRT primitives on reasoning blocks.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on long-video benchmarks with largest gains on out-of-domain tasks (Video-Holmes, CG-Bench-Reasoning, VRBench).

problem: LoRA initialization heavily impacts fine-tuning performance, but existing methods either ignore target-domain data or exploit it only shallowly via one-step gradients.
approach: LoRA-DA derives optimal initialization by minimizing parameter discrepancy between fine-tuned and target models, using Fisher-gradient formulation for bias and Fisher information for variance via asymptotic analysis.
contribution: Consistently improves final accuracy over existing LoRA initialization methods with faster convergence and robustness across ranks.

problem: Offline RL often has limited suboptimal trajectories, making training efficient off-policy models challenging without additional quality trajectories.
approach: Uses trajectory-based augmentation exploiting task structure and geometric relationships between rewards, value functions, and logging policies to synthesize higher-quality trajectories.
contribution: Enables training from limited suboptimal trajectories with theoretical justification and validated performance across positioning tasks under partial observability.

problem: LLMs in multi-node systems communicate through natural language, which is discrete, inefficient, and hard to end-to-end optimize for downstream tasks.
approach: LMNet uses stripped LLMs as vertex modules with trainable seq2seq edge modules for dense vector communication, enabling efficient gradient-based optimization while preserving natural-language boundaries.
contribution: Achieves task performance improvement with small additional training cost and effective adaptation under limited supervision.

problem: Practical RL with noisy verifiers (incomplete tests, imperfect judges) is unstable, but the conditions under which noise causes learning failure versus merely slowing learning are unclear.
approach: Models GRPO-style RLVR as bandit over reasoning modes with mean-field replicator dynamics, deriving phase transition governed by Youden's index J=TPR-FPR with sharp conditions on J>0.
contribution: Proves J>0 ensures learning while J<0 causes anti-learning collapse, providing principled framework for understanding verifier stability in RLVR.

problem: Training-free diffusion guidance via Tweedie's formula yields unreliable posterior approximations in low-density regions where classifiers are most uncertain.
approach: Stein Diffusion Guidance (SDG) reconciles Tweedie guidance with stochastic optimal control using Stein variational inference, computing steepest descent that minimizes KL divergence between approximate and true posteriors.
contribution: Consistently outperforms training-free guidance on diverse image tasks and protein-docking, enabling effective guidance in low-density regions.

problem: Standard tree-ensemble pruning methods sacrifice prediction consistency for compression, while faithful pruning preserves consistency everywhere at the cost of poor compression ratios.
approach: PINE preserves prediction equivalence only within in-distribution regions determined by conformal calibration with parameter α, balancing compression and consistency guarantees.
contribution: Improves compression ratio by up to 30% while maintaining prediction fidelity comparable to existing faithful pruning methods.

problem: Physics simulations of subsurface systems are computationally intractable due to geological heterogeneity, resolution requirements, and tight coupling of processes with different time scales.
approach: Adaptive Physics Transformer (APT) uses graph-based local feature extraction fused with global attention to capture heterogeneous features and long-range physical impacts on both regular and irregular grids.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art architectures with robust super-resolution and first demonstration of learning from HR-adaptive mesh refinement simulations.

problem: Inferring 3D scene layouts from relative spatial relations via MLLMs is unreliable because multi-hop reasoning accumulates errors in frame transformations, causing semantic and metric drift.
approach: R3L decomposes coupled relation chains via invariant spatial decomposition and enforces self-consistency through imagine-and-revise loops, using global-to-local coordinate re-parameterization for pose optimization.
contribution: Produces more physically feasible and semantically consistent layouts across diverse scenes while resolving frame-induced inconsistencies critical for multi-hop reasoning.

problem: Training with low-precision quantization requires joint allocation of model size, dataset size, and numerical precision, but theoretical mechanisms governing quantization's effect on scaling laws are unknown.
approach: Analyzes high-dimensional sketched linear regression under multiplicative and additive quantization, revealing critical dichotomy in their scaling behaviors via worst-case analysis.
contribution: Shows multiplicative quantization preserves effective model size while additive quantization reduces it, providing principled basis for optimizing training under hardware constraints.

problem: Automated proving of polynomial inequalities scales poorly due to expensive symbolic manipulations and rapidly growing intermediate expressions, especially for higher-degree or multi-variable cases.
approach: NSPI combines LLM-guided approximate Sum-of-Squares decomposition with symbolic refinement to obtain exact SOS representations, then formalizes proofs in Lean for verification.
contribution: Scales to polynomials with up to 10 variables while producing machine-checked proofs, surpassing purely symbolic approaches.

problem: Domain incremental learning suffers severe performance degradation under domain shifts due to catastrophic forgetting and poor generalization to new domains.
approach: HEDP uses energy regularization to enhance domain-representation separability and hybrid energy-distance weighting to fuse energy-based and distance-based domain selection.
contribution: Achieves 2.57% accuracy improvement on unseen domains, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting with enhanced open-world adaptability.

problem: The sample complexity of empirical risk minimization in stochastic convex optimization remains poorly understood, particularly whether ERM always learns when learning is possible.
approach: Constructs specific instances where learning is possible but ERM overfits due to uniqueness, proving empirical risk minimizers fail even though optimal solutions exist.
contribution: Resolves Feldman's open question and extends to approximate ERMs; provides novel generalization bounds for gradient descent scaling as Ω(√(ηT/m^1.5)).

problem: Neural networks achieve high in-distribution accuracy but degrade sharply under distribution shifts, with traditional robust training sacrificing overall performance.
approach: Iterative Robust Satisficing (IRS) directly optimizes a criterion balancing target in-distribution performance with fragility (rate of performance deterioration under shift).
contribution: Improves worst-case group performance without sacrificing overall accuracy with per-step cost similar to standard SGD, across synthetic and real distribution shifts.

problem: Differentiable resampling in sequential Monte Carlo methods is challenging because reparametrization-based approaches lack information about resampling distributions.
approach: Uses a training-free diffusion model surrogate to enable informative and instantly differentiable resampling with consistent resampling distributions.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art differentiable resampling on filtering and parameter estimation benchmarks with competitive performance in learning dynamics-decoder models.

problem: Model merging for LLMs is poorly understood mechanistically, with merged checkpoints appearing noisy despite improved performance over individual models.
approach: Discovers Rank-1 Subspace phenomenon where consecutive merged checkpoints collapse to stable one-dimensional manifold via river-valley landscape analysis, proposing Extra-Merge extrapolation.
contribution: Extra-Merge outperforms standard merging without gradient updates, achieving zero-shot gains on Pythia-12B with consistent improvements across GPT-2 and LLaMA families.

problem: Task-level expert selection in multi-LLM systems is too coarse; different instances within tasks require different expertise but naive instance-level selection incurs heavy computational overhead.
approach: Skill-MoE infers skills from queries to select experts, then aggregates k outputs via task-appropriate synthesizers using batch inference to amortize model loading costs.
contribution: Achieves 8.15% average absolute improvement on diverse benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, AIME, MedMCQA) while generalizing to unseen tasks, matching 4-GPU baselines on one GPU.

problem: Computing Shapley values requires evaluating functions over exponentially many subsets, becoming intractable even for moderate-sized inputs.
approach: TN-SHAP-G learns graph-aligned tensor-network surrogates approximating masked-input behavior deterministically via multilinear extension, enabling recovery of first- and higher-order indices without additional queries.
contribution: Matches exact Shapley values on small graphs and scales to large graphs where sampling methods fail, demonstrating efficient factorization.

problem: Federated continual learning faces asynchronous concept drift where distribution shifts occur independently across clients at different times and magnitudes, destabilizing convergence.
approach: RC-FCL uses conditional generative models to synthesize reference distributions for local drift detection and weighs samples via local discriminator to prioritize informative data.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art with effective distinction of asynchronous concept drift and adaptive learning strategies.

problem: Online bilateral trade algorithms are constrained by weak budget balance (per-round), but global budget balance (horizon-level) can achieve 2x better gain-from-trade, leaving existing algorithms suboptimal.
approach: Develops first algorithm achieving sublinear regret against GBB benchmark using one-bit feedback and density assumptions, learning optimal distributions over price pairs.
contribution: Achieves Õ(T^3/4) regret under bounded-density conditions, closing separation between learning single prices versus distributions.

problem: MoE upcycling initializes capacity via replication but indiscriminately expands without exploiting heterogeneity, causing severe inefficiency and parameter redundancy.
approach: Uses CKA and landscape flatness to analyze pre/post-expansion MoE, proposing dynamic bilevel optimization with Gumbel-Softmax masks for adaptive upcycling guided by CKA-regularized replay.
contribution: Achieves better average accuracy with 80% forgetting reduction while eliminating 60% of redundant parameter expansion, solving catastrophic forgetting more efficiently.

problem: Expert Parallel (EP) in MoE training scales communication linearly with activated experts, causing load imbalance and data-dependent communication overhead.
approach: Multi-Head LatentMoE with Head Parallel (HP) achieves O(1) communication via latent expert representations, completely balanced traffic, and deterministic communication compatible with EP.
contribution: Trains up to 1.82x faster than MoE with EP while achieving better performance, making multi-billion-parameter foundation model research more accessible.

problem: ML methods for protein design are restricted to canonical amino acids and narrow objectives, lacking generalist tools for broad design pipelines including non-canonical residues.
approach: Agent Rosetta pairs LLMs with structured Rosetta environment for iterative design refinement, combining LLM reasoning with physics-based modeling for diverse design objectives.
contribution: Matches specialized ML models on canonical amino acids and achieves comparable performance on non-canonical residues where ML approaches fail.

problem: Domain adaptation typically requires two-stage fine-tuning (SFT then RL), confining models to imitation distributions and limiting exploration while causing capability regression.
approach: OnePO uses single-stage SFT-free RL with teacher outputs as transient guidance, introducing Adaptive Objective Evolution and Teacher Retirement to overcome convergence and distribution-anchoring issues.
contribution: Achieves 67.2 on HealthBench with 20K samples, outperforming SFT+RL by +2.7; HuatuoGPT-3 32B reaches 70.3, extending beyond medicine to legal domains.

problem: LLM scaling laws are descriptive (predicting typical training), not prescriptive (optimizing training), with few successes in improving data efficiency beyond their implied bounds.
approach: Geodesic Hypothesis posits token sequences trace smooth geodesics on semantic manifolds; Semantic Tube Prediction (STP) confines trajectories to tubular neighborhoods, improving signal-to-noise without explicit augmentations.
contribution: Allows LLMs to match baseline accuracy with 16x less training data, directly violating data-efficiency bounds of scaling laws.
