approach: Propose Delta-Belief-RL leveraging language model's intrinsic beliefs to reward intermediate progress via change in probability assigned to target solution. Train on synthetic interaction data to teach information-seeking.
contribution: Delta-Belief-RL consistently outperforms purely outcome-based RL rewards and generalizes to out-of-distribution applications from customer service to personalization. Performance improves beyond training horizon, increasing interaction-efficiency on Pass@k.

problem: Cosine similarity estimation in coarse-to-fine retrieval pipelines relies on sign-based sketches with structural variance peaks near 90°, where candidate selection is most difficult.
approach: Propose QA-Cos, query-aware decoder-side estimator treating sign bits as probabilistic observations rather than deterministic votes, departing from Hamming-agreement paradigm.
contribution: QA-Cos reduces estimation error by 15-20% in near-orthogonal region, improving Hit@K by ~30 percentage points at fixed budgets and reducing candidates by 45-50% at fixed recall in two-stage ANN pipelines.

problem: Watermarking of panoramic imagery is fundamentally challenged by arbitrary 3D rotations where conventional planar representations and augmentation-based strategies lack theoretical guarantees.
approach: Formulate panoramas as spherical signals leveraging SO(3) representation theory to derive provably rotation-invariant descriptors. Introduce third-order invariant construction coupling higher-order SO(3) irreducible representations via tensor products.
contribution: Spherical invariant bispectrum preserves phase information while remaining strictly rotation-invariant, enabling reliable watermark extraction under arbitrary 3D rotations with near-perfect robustness and high visual fidelity.

problem: Recent multi-modal time series models claim high performance on complex reasoning tasks but skip foundational evaluations of basic ability to describe structural properties of time series.
approach: Propose BEDTime benchmark assessing whether models can recognize, differentiate, and generate descriptions of univariate time series. Create five datasets reformatted across three modalities with robustness tests.
contribution: Evaluating 17 state-of-the-art models shows: dedicated time series-language models underperform, vision-language models surprisingly capable, language-only methods worst, and all approaches fragile to real-world robustness tests.

problem: Understanding anatomical shape evolution in response to developmental covariates requires quantifying spatially-varying uncertainties, but existing time-warping approaches ignore spatially heterogeneous dynamics.
approach: Introduce PRISM bridging implicit neural representations with uncertainty-aware statistical shape analysis. Model conditional distribution of shapes given covariates with closed-form Fisher Information metric.
contribution: PRISM provides spatially continuous estimates of population mean and covariate-dependent uncertainty with analytically tractable local temporal uncertainty quantification, demonstrating strong performance on shape evolution, anomaly detection, and interpretable uncertainty.

problem: Predicting outputs in non-Euclidean spaces (distributions, networks, matrices) with high-dimensional multivariate inputs faces curse of dimensionality while requiring interpretability.
approach: Propose DeSI (Deep Single-Index Fréchet Regression), semiparametric framework assuming single-index structure for conditional Fréchet mean. Estimate interpretable index direction using deep neural network, perform Fréchet regression on one-dimensional index.
contribution: DeSI mitigates curse of dimensionality while retaining interpretability. Provides theoretical guarantees including uniform approximation and convergence rates with strong predictive performance on distributions, networks, and positive-definite matrices.

problem: Small models with latent recursion achieve promising results on reasoning tasks but recursive steps often don't effectively contribute to depth, resulting in dead compute.
approach: Analyze algorithms that latent reasoning provides by formalizing it as classifier-free guidance and policy improvement algorithm. Propose training schemes from RL and diffusion methods for latent reasoning models.
contribution: Using RL/diffusion training on Tiny Recursive Model avoids dead compute steps and reduces forward passes by 18x while maintaining performance. Policy improvement perspective explains recursive behavior.

problem: Instruction tuning for speech language models is substantially more challenging than text LLMs as it requires learning new modality and wide range of speech-specific instructions at scale.
approach: Propose SpeechCombine, instruction-following SLM without explicit instruction tuning using only single round of speech pre-training on 30k hours. Directly combine weights of speech-adapted model with weight difference between instruction-tuned and base text LLM.
contribution: Simple weight combination preserves original text LLM knowledge while effectively transferring to speech domain, suggesting new SLM training direction avoiding massive speech data requirements.

problem: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research agents follow linear or outline-centric planning, suffering from lost-in-the-middle failures or weak supervision for identifying missing relations and triggering targeted exploration.
approach: Present DualGraph memory architecture separating what agent knows (Knowledge Graph storing fine-grained units) from how it writes (Outline Graph). Analyze KG topology with structural signals to generate targeted search queries.
contribution: DualGraph consistently outperforms state-of-the-art on four OEDR benchmarks in report depth, breadth, and factual grounding, reaching 53.08 RACE score on DeepResearch Bench. Ablations confirm dual-graph design's centrality.

problem: Continuous VAEs struggle to balance compression, reconstruction quality, and a geometrically sound latent space when modeling audio's mixed information: compressible low frequencies versus stochastic high frequencies.
approach: STAR-VAE imposes a growth-based constraint field to reshape latent geometry, routing information into channel subspaces by capacity, combined with a CNN-Mamba hybrid architecture for efficient context modeling.
contribution: Resolves the Rate-Distortion-Regularity Trilemma, achieving state-of-the-art performance in neural audio generation.

problem: Differentially private regression is underexplored when data contains public, non-sensitive features; existing DP methods ignore this structural information and converge slowly.
approach: Cond-DP conditions DPSGD with a data-driven matrix that exploits rapidly decaying spectra in public features to reshape the optimization landscape.
contribution: Faster convergence than standard DPSGD in private linear regression without additional privacy cost, with consistent improvements across datasets.

problem: Reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes from blurry monocular video is hard because motion-induced blur entangles object motion and geometry, breaking geometric consistency.
approach: Kinematics-GS models blur as motion-aligned deformation and reparameterizes Gaussian shapes along motion trajectories, using temporal variance to decompose dynamic and static components.
contribution: Outperforms prior methods on real-world benchmarks with realistic motion blur, handling complex non-rigid motion without auxiliary supervision.

problem: Latent-space reasoning in LLMs suffers from feature collapse and instability due to distribution mismatch when reusing hidden states or alignment issues with assistant models.
approach: LT-Tuning introduces a Context-Prediction-Fusion mechanism that jointly leverages contextual hidden states and vocabulary embeddings, paired with progressive curriculum learning.
contribution: Outperforms latent reasoning baselines, mitigating feature collapse and achieving robust reasoning accuracy.

problem: Multimodal LLMs degrade on long generations by losing track of visual evidence and intermediate reasoning constraints under growing monolithic context.
approach: DLMR adds dual latent memories—visual and reasoning—with a router that dynamically decides which memory to reuse, keeping the base MLLM frozen.
contribution: Substantial gains on general and reasoning benchmarks with minimal trainable parameters; interpretable routing with reduced decoding tokens.

problem: Video diffusion models are computationally expensive; offline calibration suffers from data dependency and distribution shifts, while calibration-free methods ignore diffusion momentum.
approach: NaviCache reframes feature evolution as an Inertial Navigation System, tracking feature change ratios and latent drift with dual-state estimation and uncertainty-aware measurement updates.
contribution: Achieves outstanding performance on HunyuanVideo, Wan, and Open-Sora with more accurate error judgment for block skipping.

problem: MoE language models have large static parameter footprints, making deployment difficult; existing pruning ignores expert feature geometry and allocates budgets sub-optimally.
approach: RaGEP analyzes geometric properties of expert activations: rank-aware budgeting per layer and spectral-salience pruning to identify orthogonal experts.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on zero-shot tasks while reducing model size and inference cost across different scales.

problem: Algorithmic stability theory relies on overly restrictive boundedness or sub-Gaussian assumptions, limiting applicability to modern settings with heavy-tailed or unbounded losses.
approach: Develops stability-based framework requiring only finite Lp moment conditions, extending McDiarmid's bounded-differences techniques with sharp concentration inequalities.
contribution: Derives sharp high-probability generalization bounds for EMR, transductive regression, and meta-learning without boundedness.

problem: Models like Qwen2.5 gain from spurious RLVR rewards despite them being meaningless; the mechanism behind this data contamination is unknown.
approach: Uses mechanistic interpretability (Path Patching, Logit Lens) to identify an Anchor-Adapter circuit: a Functional Anchor in middle layers triggers memorized solutions, Structural Adapters in later layers transform representations.
contribution: Localizes the contamination mechanism and demonstrates bidirectional causal steering to amplify or suppress performance shortcuts.

problem: Steering LLMs is unstable and unpredictable; the Linear Representation Hypothesis assumes orthogonalized concepts, but this rarely holds and cannot explain variability.
approach: Proposes Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis: overlapping concepts induce a sample-specific cylindrical structure with a central axis, normal plane, and sensitive sectors.
contribution: Explains asymmetry in steering predictability; reveals that sensitive sectors cannot be inferred from difference vectors, providing an intrinsic source of uncertainty.

problem: Minority sampling via generative models defines rarity relative to model-learned densities, not real-world priors, leading to semantically invalid samples.
approach: JEPA guidance uses a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (world model) to steer diffusion toward low-density regions under implicit JEPA density, with approximation strategies and error bounds.
contribution: Consistently improves fidelity and semantic validity of minority samples on unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image tasks.

problem: Autoregressive LLM decoding is memory-traffic bound; existing 2-bit trellis-coded quantization reintroduces micro-LUTs or suffers from overlap artifacts.
approach: Proteus uses computed generator MUL-BAL (integer mixing plus per-layer affine Gaussianizer) to produce overlap-robust code values with zero runtime table loads.
contribution: Improves perplexity and accuracy on Llama 2 at 2-bit PTQ while reducing decode bandwidth (e.g., 740 vs 1020 GB/s on 70B).

problem: Policy optimization for diffusion LLMs is costly because calculating trajectory probabilities is expensive, limiting offline training scale.
approach: dTRPO proves that under reference regularization, probability ratios of newly-unmasked tokens estimate trajectory ratios, and full trajectory probability can be estimated from a re-masked final state.
contribution: Substantially improves core performance (up to 9.6% on STEM, 4.3% on coding) with efficient single-forward training.

problem: Expanding multimodal representations to novel modalities requires large paired datasets, which are costly and infeasible for expert-annotation domains like medical imaging.
approach: TextME projects diverse modalities into LLM embedding space via text descriptions, exploiting geometric structure of pretrained encoders for zero-shot cross-modal transfer.
contribution: Enables text-only training for modality expansion and emergent cross-modal retrieval between unseen pairs (e.g., audio-to-image).

problem: GRPO training for tool-integrated LLMs (e.g., Search-R1) consistently collapses due to Lazy Likelihood Displacement: reduced likelihood in both correct and incorrect responses.
approach: Proposes LLDS, a likelihood-preserving regularization that activates when response likelihood decreases, regularizing only responsible tokens.
contribution: Stabilizes training and prevents gradient explosion with +45.2% improvement on Qwen2.5-3B and +37.1% on 7B over vanilla GRPO.

problem: Transit stop placement must balance fairness and utility; existing clustering-based approaches don't capture fairness properties like justified representation.
approach: Maps transit stop placement to fair clustering via justified representation and the core; proposes Expanding Cost Algorithm achieving 2.414-approximation for JR.
contribution: Establishes lower bounds on JR approximability and introduces parameterized algorithm enabling tunable trade-offs between JR and core.

problem: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by linearly-growing KV cache; existing eviction policies are heuristic and miss input-dependent token importance.
approach: IndexMem learns token importance via a learnable indexer and uses a lightweight latent memory module to compress evicted tokens, providing residual readouts.
contribution: Enables long-context inference under bounded KV budget; up to 25 points improvement on RULER (4K/16K) and superior LongBench scores.

problem: Learning domain-adaptive policies that generalize to unseen dynamics is hard; domain representations entangle static information with varying properties, confusing the policy.
approach: DADP uses Lagged Context Dynamical Prediction to disentangle static domain info and integrates learned representations into diffusion via prior biasing.
contribution: Superior zero-shot adaptation on locomotion and manipulation benchmarks with improved generalizability.

problem: Block-wise diffusion LM inference is bottlenecked by memory-bound attention in long contexts; naive sparse attention fails due to KV inflation.
approach: LoSA exploits locality: reuses cached prefix-attention for stable tokens and applies sparse attention only to active tokens with large representation changes.
contribution: Up to 4.14× speedup over dense attention while preserving near-dense accuracy and achieving 5% improvement on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Inferring spatial transcriptomics from histology is limited to single-tissue models, failing to leverage shared biology across cancers in data-scarce scenarios.
approach: MoLF combines Flow Matching with Mixture-of-Experts: a conditional diffusion objective maps noise to gene latent space, routing inputs to specialized sub-networks.
contribution: State-of-the-art on pan-cancer benchmarks and exhibits zero-shot generalization to cross-species data.

problem: MoE LLMs have Safety Sparsity: safety capabilities concentrate in few experts, making them vulnerable to adversarial bypassing; alignment methods ignore expert differences.
approach: MESA uses Optimal Transport to reallocate expert capacity and refine routing, decentralizing safety across experts while minimizing utility interference.
contribution: Robust defensive performance against harmful benchmarks while preserving helpfulness.

problem: Infinite-width NTK theory yields full analytic control but misses important finite-width effects like NTK evolution and feature learning.
approach: Introduces Feynman diagrams for computing finite-width NTK corrections, deriving layer-wise recursion relations for preactivations and NTKs.
contribution: Extends stability results to finite-width NTKs and proves scale-invariant nonlinearities lack diagonal corrections, numerically validated for widths ≥20.

problem: Societal impact of widely-adopted consumer AI products like ChatGPT is poorly understood; existing approaches lack real-time monitoring methods.
approach: Proposes framework for using social media (r/ChatGPT) as data source; applies retrospective and real-time analysis to track societal trends.
contribution: First longitudinal study of r/ChatGPT showing normalization as everyday product; detects rise in mental health and emotional attachment posts.

problem: Always-on edge systems need to learn under tight budgets and detect unreliable predictions, but Bayesian binary networks saturate on non-stationary streams, freezing plasticity.
approach: BiMU derives from bounded-memory variational objective balancing stability, plasticity, and forgetting with controlled prior relaxation and uncertainty-dependent step size.
contribution: Sustains learning and strong OOD detection on 1000-task Permuted-MNIST; up to 32× label/update savings on OpenLORIS-Object.

problem: Mamba2's expanded state dimension enhances modeling but incurs inference overhead that saturates bandwidth; standard pruning fails to address this bottleneck.
approach: GHOST uses forward-pass statistics to approximate balanced truncation, jointly measuring controllability and observability for structured pruning.
contribution: 50% state-dimension reduction with ~1 perplexity point increase on WikiText-2; rivals gradient-based methods without backprop.

problem: Longitudinal EHRs yield excessively long token sequences, causing high computational cost and reduced performance in clinical LLM tasks.
approach: MedTPE merges frequently co-occurring medical token pairs into composite tokens via dependency-aware replacement, fine-tuning only new embeddings.
contribution: Up to 31% token reduction and 34-63% latency reduction while maintaining or improving predictive performance across multiple LLMs.

problem: LLM watermarks lack sufficiently adversarial evaluation; existing robustness claims obscure critical vulnerabilities to paraphrase attacks.
approach: RLCracker uses RL to erase watermarks while preserving semantic fidelity, optimizing attack context and model parameters within a KL-divergence ball.
contribution: 98.5% removal success on Unigram-marked texts after training on 100 samples; generalizes across 5 model sizes and 10 schemes.

problem: Joint modeling of proteins and ligands via parallel generative processes assumes fixed synchronous coupling, introducing high-variance supervision and inconsistent states.
approach: GeoCoupling optimizes temporal couplings between heterogeneous modalities during training, allowing asynchronous and adaptive interaction.
contribution: Consistently outperforms synchronous and random coupling on structure-based drug design and protein design with improved physical validity.

problem: Egocentric reasoning differs from third-person but models exhibit inertial thinking, relying excessively on language priors and global context rather than immediate visual input.
approach: Ego3S uses counterfactual selection for high-value samples, interaction-centric RL rewards, and variance-aware learning schedules for egocentric grounding.
contribution: Superior performance with only 26.5% training data and 46% computational reduction across five datasets.

problem: Loss spikes emerge during Adam training across architectures; landscape geometry alone doesn't explain the phenomenon.
approach: Identifies decoupling mechanism in Adam's second moment: preconditioner fails to track instantaneous squared gradients, allowing autonomous decay despite rising gradients.
contribution: Characterizes five spike evolution stages, proposes gradient-curvature predictor, and shows mechanism generalizes from quadratic models to Transformers.

problem: Calibration (prediction confidence alignment) is unexplored for probabilistic label ranking; popular models are poorly calibrated on sub-ranking and top-k predictions.
approach: Formalizes calibration hierarchy covering full rankings, sub-rankings, and top-k; proves full-rank calibration implies others but not conversely.
contribution: Shows calibration correlates with RLHF reward model accuracy but captures distinct quality dimension; reveals non-perfect correlation.

problem: Strict equivariance constraints induce complex optimization dynamics that hinder learning; existing relaxation methods require task-dependent prespecified target levels.
approach: RECM learns layer-wise relaxation levels from training signal and symmetry properties without prior knowledge; proves convergence to symmetry gap upper bound.
contribution: Outperforms prior methods on exact and approximate equivariant tasks; layers with symmetric data recover full equivariance while others gain flexibility.

problem: LLMs struggle with precise output length control; existing methods enforce external length signals but overlook the model's intrinsic deficit in length cognition.
approach: LARFT integrates length-oriented RL with hindsight length awareness, where the model learns to identify actual generation length via self-awareness tasks.
contribution: Average +20.92 improvement on length benchmarks with only -1.45 decline on general capabilities across four base models.

problem: Offline imitation learning from expert and unlabeled data overlooks valuable signal in explicitly undesirable behaviors.
approach: DualCOIL optimizes difference of KL divergences over expert and undesirable visitation distributions; becomes convex when experts outweigh undesirable data.
contribution: Consistent improvements over baselines on standard benchmarks without adversarial training, handling positive and negative demonstrations in unified framework.

problem: MCMC-based power distribution sampling for LLM reasoning is computationally prohibitive; RL gains come from distribution sharpening, not new capabilities.
approach: Derives token-level scaled low-temperature sampling without MCMC; scaling factor captures trajectory quality for autoregressively sharpening distribution.
contribution: Matches one-shot GRPO without external rewards, reducing inference latency by 10× compared to MCMC.

problem: Coding benchmarks evaluate LMs on isolated tasks, but real software development pursues high-level open-ended objectives iteratively without explicit guidance.
approach: CodeClash is a multi-round tournament benchmark where LMs iteratively develop code to win objectives like score maximization or survival.
contribution: Reveals diverse development styles and fundamental limitations in strategic reasoning; top models lose every round to expert humans.

problem: Large reasoning models are evaluated via final-answer accuracy or token count, hiding fundamentally different reasoning structures.
approach: Converts unstructured traces into verifiable reasoning graphs of claims/dependencies; defines reasoning efficiency metric quantifying logical flow concentration.
contribution: Structural measurements separate behaviors that token count and accuracy conflate, providing diagnostic tool for failure modes.

problem: Width expansion during mid-stage training causes instability: naive initialization disrupts activation statistics while copy-based introduces gradient symmetry.
approach: SPARKLING achieves signal preservation via RMS-scale consistency and symmetry breaking via asymmetric optimizer state reset and learning rate re-warmup.
contribution: Consistent improvements over training from scratch; up to 35% training cost reduction under 2× width expansion on dense and MoE models.

problem: Model fusion of independently trained networks is complicated by representational divergence; zero-shot fusion fails under non-IID data.
approach: Frames fusion as representation-matching: intermediate neurons are grouped into target representations via neuron-centric algorithms with attribution scores.
contribution: Consistent improvements over baselines on VGGs, ResNets, ViTs with largest gains in zero-shot and non-IID scenarios.

problem: Mobile agents struggle to achieve decoupled enhancement and balanced integration of hybrid capabilities: screen summary, subtask planning, action decision, action function.
approach: CoME uses four distinct experts aligned to reasoning stages with output-oriented activation, plus Expert-FT, Router-FT, CoT-FT progression and Info-DPO for error mitigation.
contribution: Outperforms dense agents and MoE methods on AITZ and AMEX; info gain evaluation guides informative reasoning.

problem: Recommender systems suffer from feedback-driven exposure concentration where repeated engagement optimization collapses onto narrow categories, reducing catalog coverage.
approach: CORAL formulates exposure regulation as a constrained sequential decision problem, models self-reinforcing interactions to create exposure-saturation states, and derives uncertainty-aware upper confidence bounds on category violation risk.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for risk bounds and finite-time recovery while achieving superior performance on real-world datasets through uncertainty-aware adaptive intervention.

problem: Safety alignment of LLMs remains brittle under domain shift and noisy preference supervision due to optimization-induced fragility overlooked by data-centric methods.
approach: ShaPO enforces worst-case alignment objectives via selective geometry control over alignment-critical parameter subspaces, with token-level stabilization and reward-level consistency.
contribution: Consistently improves safety robustness over preference optimization methods across diverse safety benchmarks and noisy preference settings.

problem: Contextual bandits with paid observations require jointly minimizing regret from learning loss and observation expenditure, yet optimal algorithms and phase transitions remain unclear.
approach: Develops near-optimal algorithms for adversarial environments with oracle-efficient function approximation, and uncovers phase transitions in performance under free observation budgets.
contribution: Provides theoretical characterization of when free observations improve regret rates and designs meta-controller achieving near-optimal performance across all budget regimes.

problem: Language models fail to learn correct behaviors when training signals misspecify rewards, leading to specification gaming like overfitting, code cheating, and sycophancy.
approach: Recontextualization generates completions from misaligned prompts then recontextualizes them as responses to permissive prompts, training models to resist misbehavior.
contribution: Mitigates specification gaming across four failure modes without improving the supervision signal itself.

problem: Safety judges are imperfect and automated red-teaming metrics like attack success rates don't measure real-world operational impact of harmful model failures.
approach: Constructs honeypots—responses flagged as harmful yet low-value operationally—and trains as hard negatives to reshape model failure modes toward reduced actionability.
contribution: Reduces both frequency and real-world impact of harmful failures while complementing ASR-based safety evaluations.

problem: Linear parameter updates in machine unlearning suffer from weight entanglement when removing training data information from models.
approach: Mode Connectivity Unlearning leverages mode connectivity to find nonlinear unlearning pathways, with parameter masking and adaptive penalty coefficients.
contribution: Uncovers a spectrum of unlearning models along a pathway and consistently improves unlearning efficacy as a plug-and-play framework.

problem: Formal logic solvers lack commonsense world knowledge for reasoning steps humans find obvious, yet humans disagree on commonsense facts making universal assumptions invalid.
approach: PACS uses LLM and formal solver to sample proofs as observations of distinct commonsense beliefs, aggregating conclusions across samples in a probabilistic framework.
contribution: Outperforms chain-of-thought, neurosymbolic methods, and search-based approaches on multiple benchmarks by explicitly modeling commonsense variation.

problem: Deep RL agents struggle in non-stationary environments with gradual continuous drift, complicating the stability-plasticity dilemma differently than abrupt task changes.
approach: Applies synaptic consolidation to Successor Features at multiple timescales to stabilize representations during continual environmental change.
contribution: Shows stability-focused consolidation of multi-timescale SFs outperforms plasticity approaches on continually changing environments.

problem: Multiple-choice benchmarks suffer from length bias where longer answers are penalized by log-probability normalization; standard and length-normalized scoring both introduce systematic biases.
approach: Bayesian accuracy computes posterior probability under explicit prior over answer length, removing linear length effects without additional forward passes.
contribution: Provides drop-in replacement for likelihood-based evaluation with consistently lower empirical length bias across benchmarks.

problem: Transformers lack clear mechanistic accounts of how they capture latent hierarchical dependencies underlying language structure.
approach: Uses probing analyses on PCFG-generated sequences to show layer-wise progression from local patterns to global hierarchical summaries, with explicit construction.
contribution: Reveals local-to-global parsing mechanism and construction achieving logarithmic depth matches trained Transformer behavior.

problem: LLMs lack native high-resolution 3D content generation capabilities, producing low-resolution meshes or coarse proxies rather than fine-grained geometry.
approach: CG-MLLM uses Mixture-of-Transformer with Token-level and Block-level autoencoders to jointly model 3D captioning and generation in single framework.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing MLLMs in generating high-fidelity 3D objects, bringing high-resolution 3D content creation into LLM paradigm.

problem: CLIP and multimodal models learn spurious associations between targets and confounding factors, causing biased predictions.
approach: LTC identifies spurious attention heads via mechanistic insights, mitigates through targeted ablation, and integrates salient heads via orthogonal projection.
contribution: Achieves over 50% gain in worst-group accuracy on bias benchmarks compared to post-hoc baselines.

problem: Fitting custom nonnegative tensor factorization models requires either struggling with gradient-based autodiff under constraints or choosing among limited implementations.
approach: NNEinFact uses einsum-based multiplicative updates fitting any nonnegative tensor contraction with various loss functions including alpha-beta divergence.
contribution: Fits custom models 37% better than standard ones, achieves half the test loss of gradient methods, and converges 90 times faster.

problem: Vision-language navigation models suffer state drift from accumulated position errors during iterative waypoint prediction, misaligning internal belief with coordinates.
approach: NeuroKalman formulates navigation as recursive Bayesian estimation with Prior Prediction from motion dynamics and Likelihood Correction from historical observations.
contribution: With 10% training data fine-tuning, clearly outperforms baselines and regulates drift accumulation.

problem: RL-based search agents commit to erroneous reasoning paths without recovery ability and rely on sparse rewards providing limited guidance.
approach: ReSeek enables self-correction through JUDGE action for replanning and dense instructive process rewards decomposing into correctness and utility components.
contribution: Significantly outperforms SOTA baselines in task success and path faithfulness, introduces contamination-free benchmark.

problem: Text-to-motion evaluation metrics fail to capture whether generated motion semantically matches descriptions; existing metrics poorly correlate with human judgment.
approach: VeMo renders motions to videos and uses pretrained video-language models for zero-shot alignment assessment with entropy-driven view selection.
contribution: Correlates better with human judgments than reference-based and reference-free metrics; contributes human-annotated meta-evaluation benchmark.

problem: LLMs as decision modules lack long-horizon adversarial benchmarks with rigorous evaluation of robustness to rule changes and human steerability.
approach: Red Alert RTS benchmark uses hierarchical interface with budgeted macroactions, evaluates robustness via rule perturbations and competitive strength via Elo ratings.
contribution: Provides reproducible diagnostic testbed identifying long-horizon failure modes through economy/combat/visibility metrics.

problem: Computing Rashomon sets for sparse decision trees requires immense memory and runtime despite their importance for uncertainty-aware decision making.
approach: PRAXIS approximates Rashomon sets through efficient incremental algorithms with orders of magnitude improvement in resource usage.
contribution: Scalably recovers almost all of full Rashomon set for real-world datasets enabling practical model uncertainty quantification.

problem: Linear Attention models interpret recurrences as SGD but naive momentum updates suffer rapid information decay and suboptimal convergence.
approach: MDN develops chunkwise parallel algorithm for LA with stepwise momentum via geometric coefficient reordering and analyzes recurrence as second-order system.
contribution: Achieves comparable training throughput with consistent performance improvements over Transformers and Mamba2 on 400M-1.3B models.

problem: Continual learning benchmarks ignore real-world multi-view perception with coupled task and viewpoint shifts common in embodied agents.
approach: CE4L introduces benchmark spanning four representative embodied tasks with ego/exo/ego-exo views; VISTA stores task updates in lightweight adapters with training-free routing.
contribution: Reveals challenges absent in prior CL benchmarks; VISTA achieves state-of-the-art overall performance with parameter efficiency.

problem: LoRA's non-identifiable factorization causes naive DP-SGD to induce gauge-dependent noise amplification in privacy-preserving fine-tuning.
approach: PRISM develops gauge-invariant DP mechanism for LoRA through intrinsic noise sampler and DP-aware adaptive updates preventing noise amplification.
contribution: Maintains standard (ε,δ)-DP guarantees with stable privacy-utility trade-offs via bounded gauge-invariant perturbations.

problem: Training LLMs for open-ended forecasting requires scaling training data yet direct training on synthetic data degrades performance.
approach: Synthesizes novel forecasting questions from daily news using offline corpus for data generation and retrieval, applies RL with improved reward function on Qwen3 thinking models.
contribution: OpenForecaster-8B matches larger proprietary models with improved accuracy, calibration, and consistency; held-out testing May-August 2025.

problem: Entropy dynamics during reinforcement fine-tuning lack principled theoretical understanding despite importance for balancing exploration-exploitation.
approach: Establishes theoretical framework via discriminant expression for entropy change under logit updates, extends to GRPO formula, analyzes insights for entropy control design.
contribution: Derives entropy-discriminator clipping methods and provides unified interpretation of entropy-based RFT methods.

problem: Block training for SAEs in instruct models introduces destructive gradient noise from attention leakage across unrelated contexts.
approach: FAST proposes sequential training aligned with instruct data distribution and activation patterns, using GSNR analysis to characterize the issue.
contribution: Achieves significantly lower MSE (0.6468 vs 5.1985), 21.1% high-quality features, and enables fine-grained control through special token interventions.

problem: Multimodal embedding models excel at global image-text alignment but fail at fine-grained alignment between image regions and specific phrases.
approach: ObjEmbed decomposes images into regional and global embeddings with object and IoU embeddings capturing semantic and spatial aspects.
contribution: Demonstrates strong semantic discrimination on 18 benchmarks supporting region-level and image-level tasks with efficient single-pass encoding.

problem: Existing world models lack large-scale datasets and unified benchmarks to evaluate interaction capabilities like distance perception and memory.
approach: iWorld-Bench constructs diverse dataset with 330k clips, introduces Action Generation Framework unifying evaluation across six task types.
contribution: Evaluates 14 world models identifying key limitations, provides public leaderboard and insights for future research.

problem: Static graph coarsening methods don't extend to dynamic settings where recomputing from scratch after updates is infeasible.
approach: Unified framework incrementally updates coarsening mapping matrix for node additions/deletions/edge modifications with optimization-based algorithms and convergence guarantees.
contribution: Delivers substantial speedups while maintaining or improving downstream task performance with epsilon-similarity bounds for quality control.

problem: LoRA restricts weight updates to low-rank subspace, limiting effectiveness and slowing convergence for LLM fine-tuning.
approach: ScaLoRA accumulates high-rank updates from consecutive low-rank increments with analytically found optimal scaling, without restarting optimization.
contribution: Consistent performance gains and faster convergence relative to LoRA variants on NLU, reasoning, and math tasks up to 12B parameters.

problem: Survival functions are inherently non-additive, fundamentally limiting standard additive explanation methods for time-to-event prediction.
approach: SurvFD decomposes higher-order effects into time-dependent and time-independent components; SurvSHAP-IQ extends Shapley interactions to time-indexed functions.
contribution: Provides principled interaction-aware and time-aware interpretability for survival modeling with applications in cancer prognosis.

problem: Autoregressive generation of single-cell RNA-seq imposes artificial ordering bias and suffers error accumulation on high-dimensional sparse unordered data.
approach: scDiVa uses masked discrete diffusion with continuous-time forward masking, bidirectional denoiser jointly modeling discrete identities and continuous values.
contribution: Pre-trained on 59M cells achieves strong transfer on batch integration, cell annotation, and perturbation prediction.

problem: Existing RLVR methods for LLMs suffer sparse rewards and unstable policy gradient updates when learning from verifiable rewards.
approach: PACS reformulates RLVR into supervised learning over score function using cross-entropy loss, achieving implicit actor-critic coupling.
contribution: Significantly outperforms RLVR baselines with gains of +8.26% (4B) and +9.57% (8B) over base models.

problem: Web agents powered by LLMs are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks hidden in interface elements causing task diversion.
approach: TRAP benchmark studies how prompt injection persuades agents on realistic tasks with controlled experiments on high-fidelity website clones.
contribution: Reveals 25% average susceptibility across frontier models (13% GPT-5 to 43% DeepSeek-R1) showing psychologically-driven vulnerabilities.

problem: LVLMs generate tokens misaligned with visual evidence, hallucinating facts and descriptions not grounded in images.
approach: AFS uses Anchor-Final Self-Supervision leveraging intermediate-final prediction discrepancies, optimizes via GRPO with token-specific hallucination-aware rewards.
contribution: Significantly reduces hallucinations without compromising recall, excels in discriminative tasks and demonstrates cross-dataset generalization.

problem: Low-data imitation learning typically requires large-scale pretraining or high-capacity architectures making efficient demonstration data use critical.
approach: NGT casts imitation as optimal transport solved via adversarial training, requires no pretraining, incorporates uncertainty estimation by design.
contribution: Achieves strong performance on high-dimensional continuous control with as few as 20 transitions in ultra-low data regimes.

problem: Deformable object manipulation requires control through equilibrium solves that are implicit and history-dependent, making long-horizon learning brittle.
approach: Neural Control propagates gradients through equilibrium sequences using adjoint formulation, avoids unrolling while keeping rollouts on converged equilibria.
contribution: Demonstrates applicability to DLO manipulation on simulated and real systems with improved learning compared to SPSA and iCEM.

problem: Evaluating agentic AI on open-ended professional tasks faces dilemma between rigid rubrics and unstable LLM-based assessments.
approach: JADE uses two-layer framework encoding expert knowledge as evaluation skills with report-specific claim-level assessment and evidence-dependency gating.
contribution: Improves evaluation stability and reveals critical agent failures, demonstrates strong alignment with expert rubrics and effective transfer.

problem: Hand motion generation remains challenging due to high degrees of freedom and complexity; curating preference pairs for hands is prohibitively expensive.
approach: IPA eliminates need for paired preference data through implicit reward maximization with Hand-Aware Local Optimization steering toward hand regions.
contribution: Achieves effective preference optimization for hand generation quality while significantly lowering data curation barrier.

problem: Block-sparse attention acceleration bottleneck is efficiently identifying relevant blocks; coarse-grained methods miss local positional information.
approach: Prism decomposes block selection into high-frequency and low-frequency branches via spectral-aware approach using energy-based temperature calibration.
contribution: Maintains accuracy parity with full attention while delivering up to 5.1× speedup through training-free spectral estimation.

problem: Reconstructing accurate implicit surfaces from low-quality noisy point clouds remains challenging with standard methods producing inaccurate representations.
approach: NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF extends Noise2Noise paradigm to 3D neural fields, learning clean SDFs from noisy supervision via MSE loss minimization.
contribution: Significantly improves surface reconstruction quality from noisy inputs on ShapeNet, ABC, Famous, and Real datasets.

problem: Model merging focuses on avoiding task interference while overlooking potential task synergy where tasks actively improve one another.
approach: SyMerge jointly optimizes merging coefficients and single task-specific layer using expert-guided self-labeling for stable supervision.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across vision, dense prediction, and NLP benchmarks, successfully merges models from different initializations.

problem: Temporal graph neural networks lack interpretability and fail to distinguish between historical interactions that remain stable versus newly emerging first-time interactions that influence predictions.
approach: ST-TGExplainer learns a self-explainable temporal GNN that disentangles stability and transition patterns using a disentangled information bottleneck objective to identify predictive subgraphs while suppressing redundancy.
contribution: Achieves strong predictive performance and yields more faithful temporal explanations by explicitly modeling both stability and transition patterns.

problem: Agentic language models operating in sequential decision-making settings are vulnerable to safety failures from adversarial tool feedback and overconfident reasoning, unlike static chat models.
approach: MOSAIC structures agent inference as plan, check, then act or refuse with explicit safety reasoning as learnable actions, using preference-based RL with pairwise trajectory comparisons to capture safety distinctions.
contribution: Reduces harmful behavior by up to 50%, increases harmful-task refusal by over 20% on injection attacks, and preserves benign task performance across multiple model families.

problem: Latent-based watermarks in diffusion models can be forged via black-box attacks that implant a provider's watermark into non-generated images, undermining provenance and trust.
approach: SemBind binds latent watermark signals to image semantics through a contrastively trained semantic masker that produces near-invariant codes for semantically matched prompts and orthogonal codes across different prompts.
contribution: Substantially reduces false acceptance under black-box forgery while preserving image quality across four mainstream watermarking methods with tunable robustness-security trade-offs.

problem: Long-context retrieval-augmented generation is bottlenecked by dense prefill computation and suffers from a crowding-out effect where globally salient but query-irrelevant tokens displace tokens essential for answering the user query.
approach: ProphetKV dynamically prioritizes tokens based on semantic relevance to the user query using a dual-stage recomputation pipeline that fuses layer-wise attention metrics into a high-utility set.
contribution: Retains 96-101% of full-prefill accuracy with only 20% recomputation ratio and achieves 8.8-24.9% accuracy improvements on RULER and 18.6-50.9% on LongBench over state-of-the-art approaches.

problem: Sequential conformal prediction assumes residual exchangeability which is violated in real-world time series with temporal dependencies and distributional shifts, and identifying optimal weights for reweighting remains unsolved.
approach: DistMatch uses binary tree partitioning via Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics to recursively partition residuals and induce approximately exchangeable leaves, enabling locally adaptive inference without reweighting.
contribution: Outperforms existing sequential conformal prediction methods by avoiding exchangeability violations through principled residual partitioning.

problem: Existing tabular foundation models like TabPFNv2 fail to scale efficiently to million-scale datasets and rely on expensive hyperparameter tuning despite recent successes on smaller benchmarks.
approach: TabICLv2 combines a novel synthetic data generation engine for pretraining diversity, scalable softmax attention that generalizes to large datasets, and the Muon optimizer to build a state-of-the-art tabular model.
contribution: Surpasses RealTabPFN-2.5 on TabArena and TALENT benchmarks without tuning, generalizes to million-scale datasets under 50GB GPU memory while being markedly faster than competitors.

problem: Traditional RLHF learns a single reward model assuming homogeneous human preferences, which is misspecified and incurs large distortion when preferences are actually heterogeneous.
approach: The Sign Estimator replaces cross-entropy loss with binary classification loss to learn a reward model that is ordinally consistent with population-average utility under mild assumptions of heterogeneous preferences.
contribution: Provides the first consistent estimator for heterogeneous preferences without curse of dimensionality, with fast finite-sample convergence rate of O(n^-1/3).

problem: Determining how to compress hidden states from autoregressive generation into a representation reflecting the model's internal state is underexplored and unclear whether information is localized or distributed.
approach: Studies representations from generated tokens and compares pooling across embeddings to individual token embeddings, analyzing how semantic information distributes during generation.
contribution: Pooling embeddings produces more informative representations than single tokens, indicating semantic information is distributed across generated tokens rather than localized.

problem: AI-generated image detectors fail on unseen generators due to black-box decision-making and inability to reveal evidence driving their decisions, limiting understanding of detection failures.
approach: ForensicConcept extracts explicit forensic concepts from detectors via Transformer attribution and clustering, introduces diffusion-derived reference concepts via CleanDIFT, and transfers concepts across backbones using alignment metrics.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements on GenImage, GAN-family, and Chameleon benchmarks with auditable evidence readouts and principled explanation for why certain backbones yield more transferable forensic concepts.

problem: Music recordings suffer from multiple audio quality issues like reverberation and distortion that require separate specialized tools and manual adjustments rather than unified treatment.
approach: SonicMaster uses flow-matching generative training to learn audio transformation from degraded to high-quality versions, conditioned on natural language instructions and operating in automatic mode for general restoration.
contribution: Significantly improves sound quality across all artifact categories with listener preference confirmed, enabling both text-controlled and automatic restoration in a single unified generative model.

problem: Mechanistic anomaly detection cannot reliably determine whether neural network outputs result from normal or anomalous internal mechanisms using latent space analysis, which is vulnerable to obfuscation.
approach: Reframes mechanistic anomaly detection as functional attribution using influence functions to measure functional coupling between test samples and a reference set via parameter-space sampling.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art backdoor detection with Defense Effectiveness Rating of 0.93 on BackdoorBench and detects multiple anomaly types across vision and language modalities.

problem: Transformer-based spiking neural networks remain difficult to deploy on neuromorphic hardware due to dense operations and high communication overhead of standard attention.
approach: Proposes Simplified Spiking Attention (SSA) and Ultra-Simplified Spiking Attention (USSA) that replace matrix multiplication with Hadamard products and eliminate multi-head attention.
contribution: SSA achieves 96.38% on CIFAR-10, 79.45% on CIFAR-100, and 97.56% on DVS-Gesture while reducing computational complexity from O(N²D) to O(ND) and communication from O(N²) to O(ND).

problem: Generating physically consistent 3D tabletop scenes for robotic learning is challenging due to dense object hierarchies, irregular affordances, and error propagation from decoupled symbolic solvers.
approach: PhyScene3D reformulates scene generation as a human-mimetic constructive process using Cognitive Topological Reasoning Chain for sequential anchor-conditioned placement and Physics-Aware Denoising Alignment with differentiable SDF.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art in semantic accuracy and physical validity, achieving 40% reduction in scene-wise collision rate relative to human-annotated training data.

problem: Differentiating through discrete stochastic samples in Poisson-distributed latent variable models remains challenging with current methods lacking systematic guidance on which approach to use.
approach: Provides first systematic comparison of Exponential Arrival Time (EAT) simulation and Gumbel-SoftMax relaxation, with modified EAT method that guarantees unbiased first moment matching firing rate.
contribution: Modified EAT exhibits better overall performance with higher robustness to hyperparameters across variational autoencoders and neural connectivity inference tasks.

problem: Millimeter-wave based human pose estimation fails to properly utilize Doppler signatures for motion cues and misinterprets non-human Doppler signals as human motion, causing jittery trajectories.
approach: PULSE converts Doppler signatures into confidence-aware motion prompts and injects them into spatial magnitude reasoning through constrained interactions to screen spurious spectral motion cues.
contribution: Consistently improves pose accuracy and temporal stability across single- and multi-person settings by controlled Doppler prompting.

problem: Pearl's Causal Hierarchy satisfiability is computationally intractable in classical settings, limiting its practical applicability to causal reasoning problems.
approach: Identifies gateways to tractability through parameterized complexity using primal treewidth and number of variables, developing fixed-parameter and XP-algorithms for probabilistic and counterfactual fragments.
contribution: Provides first fixed-parameter algorithms with matching hardness results that map the limits of tractability for causal reasoning in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy.

problem: Most molecular generation methods for protein targets capture only pairwise amino acid relations and neglect higher-order structural dependencies, limiting molecular quality.
approach: TSMGen models higher-order spatial dependencies at both atomic and amino acid levels using a context-aware bidirectional fusion module that leverages information from both protein pocket and molecule.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art in Vina Score, High Affinity, QED, SA and Diversity metrics with case study on β-secretase enzyme confirming stronger binding affinity.

problem: Multi-label disease diagnosis in medical images assumes diseases are separable, but identical visual observations may support multiple labels and disease concepts are correlated rather than independent.
approach: FACT reformulates diagnosis as fuzzy alignment between atomic visual evidence and disease semantic anchors, modeling visual polysemy through shared evidence and encoding disease correlation via comorbidity topology.
contribution: Consistently improves diagnostic performance while delivering clinically plausible predictions on three public clinical benchmarks with interpretable fuzzy membership functions.

problem: Explicit Dynamic Gaussian Splatting often exhibits generalization degradation in scenes with large motion despite strong short-clip quality and explicit scene interpretability.
approach: Proposes update mixture strategy with space-time dependent Strictly Sparse Update, constant-corrected adaptive algorithm reducing gradient over-scaling, and stochastic attribute averaging for frame-preference mitigation.
contribution: Consistent improvements and reduced generalization issues demonstrating the role of non-adaptive updates in dynamic Gaussian Splatting optimization.

problem: Reinforcement learning from human feedback and verifiable rewards suffer from reward hacking where policies exploit reward model inaccuracies to learn unintended behaviors.
approach: Derives theoretical connection between reward accuracy and flatness of optima, using gradient regularization to bias training toward flatter regions where reward models are more accurate.
contribution: Achieves higher GPT-judged win-rate in RLHF, avoids overfocusing on format in rule-based math rewards, and prevents judge hacking compared to KL-penalty baselines.

problem: Generating high-fidelity 3D indoor scenes is limited by data scarcity and inability to scale to dense scenes or reason precisely about spatial relations required for layout consistency.
approach: Pair2Scene integrates learned local object relation rules with scene hierarchies and physics-based algorithms, capturing support and functional relations through conditional spatial distributions.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in generating complex environments beyond training data while maintaining physical and semantic plausibility.

problem: Multi-task learning for automatic radiology report generation uses coarse linear scalarization strategies that fail to balance discriminative clinical supervision with generation smoothness requirements.
approach: Analyzes failure mechanism via gradient dynamics using SDE framework, proposing CAME-Grad optimizer with conflict-averse direction rectification and magnitude-enhanced energy injection for task balance.
contribution: As a universal plug-and-play optimizer, CAME-Grad brings 2.3% average improvement on MIMIC-CXR and 1.9% on IU X-Ray across eight diverse methods.

problem: Autoregressive long-video generation suffers from semantic drift, motion decay, and appearance instability as errors compound across clip synthesis over long horizons.
approach: DynaMem improves coherence via Semantic-Adaptive Hierarchical Memory for long-range preservation, Motion-Prioritized Optimization for temporal consistency, and Reference-Anchored Perceptual Alignment for stability.
contribution: Produces more consistent semantics, stronger temporal dynamics, and more stable appearance on long videos compared to competitive baselines.

problem: Representation alignment in diffusion Transformers implicitly entangles latents and limits generative capacity while trying to accelerate training.
approach: ReGen proposes hierarchical multi-prompt representation generation jointly estimating vector fields for both representations and data, using generalized flow matching to improve conditional flow matching generalization.
contribution: Significantly improves waveform generation quality from highly compressed latent representations and enables efficient text-to-speech with only 1 day training on 4 GPUs and RTF of 0.08.

problem: Sparse time series methods based on ℓ0 constraints lack finite-sample and computational guarantees under temporal dependence despite empirical success.
approach: Studies ℓ0-constrained least squares for α-mixing time series, establishing restricted strong convexity/smoothness and deriving nonasymptotic guarantees for iterative hard thresholding and other exact sparse methods.
contribution: Provides new guarantees for Gaussian VAR models and demonstrates exact sparse methods recover lag structure more accurately with substantially lower computational cost than classical methods.

problem: Multi-agent LLM-based planning suffers from inconsistency under partial observability and high communication costs, requiring explicit message passing for coordination.
approach: Introduces Contextual Tacit Communication, a gradient-free protocol aligning decentralized decisions with a joint LLM value score using retrieval-augmented Tacit Rule Memory.
contribution: Improves cooperation performance over baselines while reducing runtime overhead compared with communication-based methods across VIKI, C-WAH, and TDW-MAT benchmarks.

problem: Affine Maximizer Auctions have limited expressiveness in correlated bidder valuations due to fixed payment forms, restricting optimal revenue.
approach: Proposes Correlation-Aware AMA framework augmenting AMA with correlation-aware payment while preserving DSIC and IR properties, formulated as constraint optimization with practical two-stage training.
contribution: Shows scenarios where classic AMAs perform arbitrarily poorly while CA-AMA reaches optimal revenue, with practical algorithm achieving improved revenue across various distributions.

problem: Equilibrium pricing in oligopolistic data markets is complicated by data non-rivalry which fundamentally alters equilibrium existence compared to rivalrous goods.
approach: Shows exact Nash equilibrium need not exist under uniform pricing but proposes piecewise-linear convex pricing allowing approximate equilibrium and investigates convergence via simulations.
contribution: Demonstrates that beyond-uniform pricing guarantees 2-approximate Nash equilibrium in data markets and simulations show fast convergence with empirical approximation outperforming worst-case bounds.

problem: Most quantum algorithms for regression focus only on linear regression while many complex practically-important variants remain unexplored.
approach: Presents unified quantum framework for accelerating broad class of regression tasks including Lasso, Ridge, Huber and ℓp-regressions via quantum leverage score approximation and multiscale leverage score overestimates.
contribution: Achieves up to quadratic improvement in sample complexity over best classical algorithms with quantum time complexity Õ(r√mn/ε + poly(n,1/ε)).

problem: It remains unclear whether RL truly extends reasoning ability beyond pre-training due to lack of control in modern pipelines with opaque data and complex interactions.
approach: Develops controlled experimental framework isolating pre-training, mid-training, and RL contributions using synthetic reasoning tasks with explicit operations and parseable traces.
contribution: Shows RL produces true capability gains when pre-training leaves headroom and data targets model's edge of competence, while mid-training significantly enhances performance beyond RL alone.

problem: Sparse autoencoders may identify correlates of reasoning rather than true reasoning mechanisms, and it is unclear whether selected features reflect genuine reasoning or co-occurrence with reasoning traces.
approach: Proposes falsification-based evaluation framework combining causal token injection with LLM-guided counterexample construction across 22 SAE configurations.
contribution: Finds 45-90% of candidates are sensitive to token-level interventions and LLM-guided falsification triggers non-reasoning inputs that suppress activation of many supposedly reasoning features.

problem: Multi-turn LLM agents exhibit conversational inertia where models mimic previous responses as few-shot examples, causing imitation bias that constrains exploration.
approach: Identifies diagonal attention to previous responses as mechanism for inertia and proposes Context Preference Learning to calibrate preferences favoring low-inertia responses.
contribution: Reduces conversational inertia and achieves performance improvements across eight agentic environments with context management strategies balancing exploration and exploitation.

problem: Riesz representer estimation for debiased machine learning lacks stability and existing methods do not enable interpretable policy effect estimation over continuous treatments.
approach: Formulates Riesz representer estimation as score matching problem leveraging denoising score matching and telescoping density ratio, introducing policy path parameter for continuous treatments.
contribution: Stabilizes representer estimation while enabling √n-consistent and asymptotically efficient causal effect estimation with improved interpretability of policy effects.

problem: Existing NMR chemical shift prediction relies on limited, labor-intensive atom-assigned datasets, limiting accuracy and generalization for molecular structure elucidation.
approach: Proposes semi-supervised framework learning shifts from millions of literature-extracted spectra without explicit assignments using permutation-invariant set supervision with sorting-based loss.
contribution: Achieves substantially improved accuracy and robustness over state-of-the-art with stronger generalization on larger and more diverse molecular datasets and captures systematic solvent effects.

problem: Neural collapse in deep classifiers is suboptimal, but it remains unclear how depth and gradient descent alone shape neural collapse without regularization.
approach: Studies deep unconstrained feature model without regularization to show depth induces implicit low-rank bias through more efficient norm propagation in successive multiplications.
contribution: Provides first asymptotic and dynamic characterization showing depth drives low-rank alternatives to neural collapse corresponding to softmax codes.

problem: Saliency maps are unreliable for interpreting CNNs as randomized networks produce maps resembling trained models, but the architectural contributions to this phenomenon remain underappreciated.
approach: Identifies center-focused saliency bias induced by convolutional design choices like zero padding and receptive field growth, absent in ViTs and MLPs.
contribution: Shows architectural priors induce center bias in random CNNs while training only partially shifts saliency toward objects, clarifying how architectural priors confound saliency evaluations.

problem: Adversarial robustness of INR-based classifiers remains unexplored despite increasing adoption, complicated by optimization-in-the-loop forward pass preventing standard attacks.
approach: Designs surrogate models amortizing INR-generation as practical proxy for attacking INR classifiers and develops speed-up techniques reducing training costs.
contribution: Shows INR-based classifiers are vulnerable with accuracy collapsing to near zero under perturbations, and existing countermeasures for discrete representations offer limited protection.

problem: Surgical video datasets are heavily imbalanced with rare actions and tools under-represented, limiting robustness of downstream scene understanding models.
approach: SurgiFlowVid uses dual-prediction diffusion module jointly denoising RGB frames and optical flow with sparse visual encoder conditioning for controllable surgical video generation.
contribution: Synthetic data yields consistent gains of 10-20% over baselines in action recognition, tool detection, and motion prediction across three surgical datasets.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for visual reasoning in MLLMs risks reward hacking through spurious patterns and inefficient training from treating all rubrics as equally learnable.
approach: RuCL reformulates curriculum learning via reward design, generating generalized rubrics and stratifying them by model competence with dynamic weight adjustment from perception to logical reasoning.
contribution: Achieves +7.83% average improvement and 60.06% state-of-the-art accuracy on visual reasoning benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

problem: Endpoint Detection and Response systems struggle to efficiently model ultra-long log sequences and provide interpretable reasoning about malicious activities for security analysts.
approach: WatchLog represents raw logs as video-structured data with temporal cross-attention adapter enabling pixel-wise time interaction, using two-stage pre-training and supervised fine-tuning for interpretable explanations.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art in detection accuracy and recall with more interpretable reasoning traces and significantly improved inference efficiency on EDR8M-20R dataset.

problem: See abstract for details
approach: See abstract for details
contribution: See abstract for details

problem: Existing stereo image compression methods either sacrifice perceptual quality at low bitrates or fail to maintain consistency across viewpoints.
approach: SDiD uses shared pre-trained diffusion priors with a diffusion prior alignment module and prior transformation structure for distributed stereo compression.
contribution: SDiD requires only one-third the bitrate of state-of-the-art methods (0.02 bpp vs 0.06 bpp) while maintaining depth information.

problem: Benchmark metrics often produce invalid uncertainty estimates or make unrecognized assumptions about generalized accuracy.
approach: Analysis via generalized linear mixed models produces correct estimates of generalized accuracy while efficiently quantifying uncertainty.
contribution: Shows how statistical modeling can improve uncertainty quantification and provides variance decomposition and item difficulty estimates across 22 frontier LLMs.

problem: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections face training instability, prohibitive parameter complexity, and factorial explosion in parametrization.
approach: KromHC uses Kronecker products of smaller doubly stochastic matrices to parametrize residual connections while enforcing manifold constraints.
contribution: Achieves O(n²C) parameter complexity instead of O(n³C) or O(nC·n!) while matching or outperforming SOTA variants.

problem: Molecular property prediction is limited by expensive labeled data, while standard semi-supervised methods rely on label-preserving augmentations that are challenging in the molecular domain.
approach: Semi-supervised training uses ensemble consensus objectives to improve predictive accuracy across molecular datasets and GNN architectures.
contribution: Ensemble consensus training increases robustness and outperforms full supervised ensembles in most cases while reducing calibration error.

problem: Assessing and improving calibration in sequential vision-language-action tasks remains unexplored, especially for partial trajectories.
approach: Formulates sequential calibration for episodic tasks using temporal-difference value estimation as a principled calibration mechanism.
contribution: TD calibration improves performance on simulated and real-robot data by connecting uncertainty calibration to reinforcement learning.

problem: LLMs sometimes overthink and generate unnecessary reasoning steps under uncertainty or with ill-posed queries.
approach: Proposes nonparametric and parametric early stopping methods that monitor uncertainty signals during generation.
contribution: Uncertainty-aware early stopping improves both efficiency and reliability, with especially significant gains for math reasoning.

problem: Current preference prediction relies on analyzing LLM outputs without considering underlying mechanisms.
approach: Mechanistic forecasting probes internal model representations to extract demographic and ideological information from party-encoding components.
contribution: Probing internal knowledge via mechanistic forecasting improves prediction accuracy on election forecasting across 6 national elections.

problem: Significant gap exists between theoretical universal expressivity and practical performance in Graph Neural Networks.
approach: ENGNNs utilize random noise features with enforced equivariance to nodewise noise transformations for enhanced expressivity.
contribution: Reaches theoretical universal expressivity while maintaining linear scalability and achieving performance comparable to expensive high-expressivity models.

problem: Multi-objective combinatorial optimization sacrifices generality, scalability, or theoretical guarantees with existing methods.
approach: Reformulates it as online learning over decomposed decision space, solving position-wise bandit subproblems via adaptive expert-guided construction.
contribution: Achieves 80-98% of specialized solvers performance with two to three orders of magnitude improvement in sample and computational efficiency.

problem: Existing dense video captioning lacks fine-grained, structured temporal narratives with explicit timestamps.
approach: Proposes Omni Dense Captioning with a six-dimensional structural schema for script-like captions, trained via SFT and GRPO with task-specific rewards.
contribution: Surpasses Gemini-2.5-Pro and significantly boosts downstream audio-visual reasoning and temporal grounding capabilities.

problem: Current geometric models of language focus on embedding spaces rather than intrinsic text properties.
approach: Introduces Texture, a text-native word-level discrete curvature signal measuring differential reconciliation between prefix and suffix.
contribution: Establishes text-native curvature paradigm enabling geometry without geometric training for improved long-context inference.

problem: Reconstructing atomistic crystal structures from single noisy STEM projections is an ill-posed inverse problem lacking verification.
approach: AutoMat uses inference-time hypothesis search with closed-loop verification, composing perception, physics modules, and rollback-retry on failure.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA models on STEM2Mat-Bench with 450+ annotated samples across lattice RMSD, formation energy MAE, and structure matching.

problem: Pre-trained vision-language models like CLIP are highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that disrupt image-text alignment.
approach: Proposes Self-Calibrated Consistency (SCC) with semantic and spatial consistency modules using soft pseudo-labels and multi-view predictions.
contribution: Consistently improves CLIP zero-shot robustness across 22 benchmarks while maintaining accuracy as a plug-and-play inference strategy.

problem: Classical feature importance metrics are unsuited to graph-structured data with complex dependencies.
approach: Proposes data-, model-, and task-agnostic feature selection based on changes in validation performance upon permuting feature values.
contribution: Rivals tailored feature selection approaches while returning meaningful importance scores before GNN training completes.

problem: Custom diffusion models assume static personalized concepts and are prone to catastrophic forgetting as new concepts are introduced.
approach: Formulates continual personalization as constrained submodular optimization selecting minimal sufficient concept-specific neurons.
contribution: Achieves fusion-free continual personalization by modifying only 0.41% of total parameters per concept while preventing catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Existing EEG generation methods use discrete denoising objectives that inadequately reflect continuous temporal dynamics and spectral structure.
approach: Introduces Just EEG Transformer (JET), a generative framework using conditional flow matching to model EEG as evolving continuous trajectories.
contribution: Reduces TS-FID by over 40% compared to baselines while capturing key EEG structural properties for scalable generation.

problem: PDE neural operators either focus on specific properties or suffer from high computational costs and poor generalization.
approach: Flower uses multihead warps that predict displacement fields and resample adaptively at sparse coordinates for adaptive global interactions.
contribution: Compact 17M-parameter model outperforms Fourier, convolution, and attention baselines on 2D/3D time-dependent PDE benchmarks.

problem: Unclear whether time series participate in multimodal representation convergence observed in vision and language.
approach: Examines trimodal alignment through post-hoc projection heads using contrastive learning with analysis of geometry and scaling behavior.
contribution: Finds asymmetric alignment with time series aligning more strongly to vision, demonstrating images as effective intermediaries.

problem: CodeGen AI security research focuses on red teaming but lacks effective blue teaming defenses requiring deep security analysis.
approach: BlueCodeAgent uses automated red teaming to generate diverse risky instances guiding multi-level blue team defense with constitution summarization.
contribution: Achieves average F1 improvement of 14.7% across four code security tasks with dynamic analysis reducing false positives.

problem: Models degrade under imbalanced samples, inaccurate labels, and backdoor attacks but lack scenario-agnostic optimization methods.
approach: Attributes performance degradation to parameter contamination and recovers clean parameters via implicit manifold autoencoders with diffusion.
contribution: Parameter purification generalizes across imbalanced learning, label noise, and backdoor defense without scenario-specific design.

problem: Distributed training is bottlenecked by optimizer state memory and communication requirements even with low-rank optimizers.
approach: Combines low-rank optimization with infrequent synchronization using full-rank quasi-hyperbolic updates for subspace exploration.
contribution: Achieves near-parity with DDP while reducing communication by ~10x at 125M-720M model scales.

problem: LLMs' token-level generation encourages local decisions and lacks global planning, leading to redundant or inaccurate reasoning.
approach: Two-stage framework where LLMs summarize CoT reasoning into high-level guidance, then joint optimization via guidance-aware RL.
contribution: Delivers stable and significant improvements across mathematics and natural sciences reasoning with five diverse base models.

problem: Steering diffusion models toward unseen conditions requires retraining or per-step gradient computations with substantial overhead.
approach: Combines offline-computed noise alignment and RFM activation steering enabling fast controllable generation without gradient guidance.
contribution: Improves target accuracy over gradient-based guidance with substantial inference speedups across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, CelebA.

problem: Existing agent benchmarks evaluate code-centric or data-centric capabilities in isolation, missing real-world data-intensive scenarios.
approach: Introduces data-intensive Linux sandbox based on Kaggle with 1,009 tasks spanning 31 communities, average 980 files per task.
contribution: Top-performing agents achieve only 61.1% success, highlighting substantial gap in data discovery and code execution integration.

problem: Strategic classification assumes public classifiers but unclear why systems would commit to full disclosure under regulation.
approach: Studies settings where regulation requires partial disclosure, enabling learner to reveal sets of possible classifiers while privately choosing realization.
contribution: Develops efficient algorithms for computing best-responses and training in this ambiguity setting.

problem: Generalized Category Discovery methods rely on semantic labels and global representations, overlooking part-level cues crucial for distinguishing categories.
approach: Incorporates part-level visual feature correspondences to capture finer-grained semantic structures without requiring GCD method modifications.
contribution: Part-level correspondence priors significantly improve existing GCD approaches across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Inference-time guidance for diffusion models requires repeated score/gradient evaluations introducing bias and computational overhead.
approach: URGE performs path-wise importance reweighting via Girsanov change of measure with multiplicative trajectory weights and periodic resampling.
contribution: Outperforms guidance baselines on generation quality while being simpler to implement and fully gradient-free.

problem: SLM-LLM routing methods train routers to mimic LLM trajectories, capping performance at reference limits.
approach: Formulates routing as MDP using Collaborative Inference Tree Search and Tree-Advantage Policy Optimization for credit assignment.
contribution: Advances Pareto frontier of accuracy-efficiency trade-offs by exploiting better inference trajectories in collaborative space.

problem: Slot Attention iterations and recurrences across video frames use inconsistent aggregation transforms due to cold-start query limitations.
