approach: Preheats cold-start queries with input-feature information and differentiates aggregation transforms using full and single iterations.
contribution: Improves object discovery, recognition, and visual reasoning through smoothed slot attention across iterations and recurrences.

problem: LLM inference pipelines are stitched together as services obscuring cross-stage interference and limiting pipeline-level optimization.
approach: Treats inference pipelines as first-class compilation targets with declarative dataflows and distributed execution plans with backpressure.
contribution: Achieves 16 requests/s at 700+ tokens/request with 1ms overhead and 57% P99 latency reduction under multi-pipeline contention.

problem: Dataset bias leads deep learning models to exploit spurious correlations instead of task-relevant signals.
approach: Introduces Standard Anti-Causal Model framework with conditional independence criterion, enabling conditional distance correlation regularization.
contribution: DISCO outperforms or matches bias mitigation approaches with fewer hyperparameters across six datasets and multi-bias scenarios.

problem: Neural operators have opaque latent states and attention-based models can be costly at high resolutions.
approach: Gaussian Particle Operator represents fields with learned Gaussian basis atoms carrying geometric parameters, operating in modal space via PG Gaussian Attention.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy against neural operators and Transformers while providing representation-level interpretability.

problem: OCL models are evaluated solely through object discovery and simple reasoning, not regarding compositional generalization and OOD robustness.
approach: Uses instruction-tuned VLMs as scalable evaluators across diverse VQA datasets and introduces unified task jointly assessing localization and usefulness.
contribution: Demonstrates that OCL representation usefulness varies significantly across datasets, establishing more comprehensive evaluation paradigm.

problem: Organizations face rising payments when AI evaluation is noisy, and elaborate evaluation methods' benefits are overshadowed by costs.
approach: Adaptive contracts allow selective detailed evaluation after coarse signals to conserve resources with efficient algorithms for optimal contracts.
contribution: Demonstrates benefits of adaptivity over non-adaptive baselines using question-answering and code-generation datasets.

problem: Visual mechanistic interpretability paradigms exhibit statistical biases and fail to balance interpretability and faithfulness.
approach: Establishes distributional view modeling feature influence on natural image distribution via KL-minimal optimization and energy-guided diffusion.
contribution: Resolves biases under distributional view and demonstrates practical effectiveness on DINOv3 vision models.

problem: Fundamental representational units of LLMs remain undefined, limiting understanding of their mechanisms.
approach: Introduces Atom Theory using atomic inner product metric to define units with criteria for faithfulness and stability identifiable via TSAEs.
contribution: Identifies atoms with near-perfect faithfulness (99.9%) and stability (99.8%) across Gemma2 and Llama3.1 models.

problem: Margin-based preference optimization methods suppress chosen responses while suppressing rejected ones.
approach: Unified incentive-score decomposition reveals local update directions, and disentanglement band identifies when to suppress losers without affecting winners.
contribution: Reward calibration method adaptively rebalances updates to satisfy disentanglement band with better downstream performance.

problem: Model robustness against natural image corruptions requires better understanding of internal computational pathways.
approach: Identifies progressive decay of robust features across layers and proposes S&D refinement using dynamic pathway selection and symmetry-preserving transformations.
contribution: Improves robustness across eight benchmarks with architecture-agnostic, parameter-free approach and zero test-time overhead.

problem: Modern LLMs deployed under compute constraints need flexible capacity control without requiring model-specific architectural modifications.
approach: Plug-and-play framework inducing sparse and low-rank structures during training via augmented Lagrangian and adaptive controller.
contribution: Single training run yields continuous spectrum of model capacities enabling elastic deployment without retraining.

problem: Multimodal language models fail to ensure visual evidence supports their answers, allowing models to generate correct answers without grounding them in correct visual regions.
approach: Integrates positive, counterfactual, and random-masking training paradigms with a language-guided pipeline to automatically localize question-relevant regions and generate counterfactual variants, trained with GRPO-based reinforcement learning using three complementary rewards.
contribution: DeFacto substantially improves both answer accuracy and evidence-answer consistency over strong baselines on diverse benchmarks, with new DeFacto-1.5K benchmark for evaluating evidence-grounded consistency.

problem: Large language models' effectiveness in real-world blue team threat-hunting scenarios remains insufficiently explored, as cyber threats grow in scale and sophistication.
approach: CYBERTEAM constructs a standardized workflow in two stages by modeling realistic threat-hunting workflows with task dependencies and addressing each task through operational modules tailored to specific analytical requirements.
contribution: CYBERTEAM integrates 30 tasks and 9 operational modules to guide LLMs through standardized threat analysis, revealing improvements from standardized design while exposing limitations of open-ended reasoning in real-world threat hunting.

problem: Federated adversarial learning enhances robustness but existing work focuses on convergence with limited understanding of generalization capabilities under adversarial perturbations.
approach: Analyzes federated adversarial learning through algorithmic stability, deriving perturbation-dependent generalization bounds via stochastic gradient descent and proposing Moreau envelope optimization for perturbation-independent bounds.
contribution: Establishes unified theoretical framework showing stronger adversarial attacks degrade generalization, with Moreau envelope approach demonstrating efficacy in simultaneously enhancing both robustness and generalization.

problem: Zero-shot 3D scene understanding via 2D vision-language models struggles with retaining task-relevant 3D details under limited input budget and suffers from redundancy among patches across views.
approach: KeyVT uses hierarchical view-to-token transportation with optimal transport framework to select task-relevant views based on semantic content and geometric position, then identifies representative tokens to minimize redundancy.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements over existing tuning-free methods and performance comparable to training-based approaches on three widely used benchmarks for 3D question answering.

problem: Tree-search decoding for language models suffers under fixed per-query token budgets where existing policies are budget-agnostic and risk late-stage over-branching or premature termination.
approach: Budget-Guided MCTS aligns tree-search policy with remaining token budget by starting with broad exploration, then prioritizing refinement and answer completion as budget decreases while reducing late-stage branching.
contribution: Consistently outperforms budget-agnostic tree-search baselines across inference budgets on mathematical reasoning and physics reasoning benchmarks with open-weight LLMs.

problem: Neural networks typically use uniform learning rates across layers despite empirical evidence that layer-specific learning rates accelerate training, but principled understanding of when and why remains limited.
approach: Investigates non-uniform learning rates via Stackelberg optimization, showing smaller learning rates for body layers and larger for final layers can be interpreted as two-time-scale alternating gradient descent on a Stackelberg reformulation.
contribution: Establishes finite-time convergence guarantees and identifies two mechanisms by which non-uniform learning rates outperform uniform ones: Stackelberg objective optimization structure and sharper local curvature.

problem: Determining whether language models have been trained on specific target texts is crucial for privacy and data contamination detection, but existing local token-based methods neglect probability dynamics during generation.
approach: Shifts detection paradigm from local tokens to global sequence perspective using Adaptive Entropic Convolutional Analysis to conceptualize probability sequences as dynamic signals with calibration and convolutional filtering.
contribution: AECA surpasses previous methods by up to 1.5% in average AUC on WikiMIA benchmark with advantages particularly pronounced in long-text scenarios.

problem: Prover-verifier games offer verifiability in classification but have not been applied to complex high-dimensional inputs like images, while concept encodings effectively translate data to interpretable concepts but work with low-capacity predictors.
approach: Neural Concept Verifier combines prover-verifier games for formal verifiability with concept encodings to handle high-dimensional inputs interpretably, using minimally supervised concept discovery to extract structured encodings.
contribution: Outperforms classic concept-based models and pixel-based PVG baselines on high-dimensional logically complex datasets while helping mitigate shortcut behavior.

problem: Standard actor-critic methods like PPO rely on scalar value functions that only estimate expectation of cumulative returns, discarding higher-order statistics and leading to inaccurate value estimation for complex reasoning tasks.
approach: DisPPO integrates non-parametric quantile regression into PPO to model full return distribution, with Wasserstein-metric contraction guarantee for convergence and on-policy framework avoiding off-policy replay instability.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard PPO and recent baselines on Llama and Qwen models across mathematical reasoning and Text-to-SQL generation in both Pass@1 and Pass@k metrics.

problem: Extracting causally meaningful features from time-series data is challenging when operating conditions change, as existing methods capture either temporal causal relationships or cross-environment invariance but not both simultaneously.
approach: Causal Feature Learning formulates feature extraction as generalized Rayleigh-quotient problem, maximizing correlation with target variables while penalizing sensitivity to environment-dependent mean shifts.
contribution: Achieves 93.69% average fault detection rate on Tennessee Eastman Process, outperforming 15 baseline methods and validating benefit of jointly capturing temporal relevance and environment mean invariance.

problem: Reparameterization policy gradient achieves high sample efficiency but suffers from under-utilization of computationally expensive dynamics Jacobians and inherent training instability under sample reuse.
approach: Reparameterization Proximal Policy Optimization enables sample reuse by showing RPG naturally optimizes PPO-style surrogate objective via backpropagation through time, with clipped policy gradient mechanism and KL divergence regularization.
contribution: Maintains superior sample efficiency and consistently outperforms or achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks while addressing stability concerns.

problem: Large language models can be controlled via prompts and activation steering but existing accounts treat these disparate methodologies separately despite their common goal of controlling behavior.
approach: Develops unifying Bayesian perspective where steering alters concept priors and in-context learning leads to evidence accumulation, producing closed-form model predictive of LLM behavior across interventions.
contribution: Explains empirical phenomena like sigmoidal learning curves and predicts novel ones including additivity in log-belief space and distinct behavioral shift phases from intervention control changes.

problem: Federated learning faces model heterogeneity where architectural differences yield incompatible representations, making knowledge-sharing challenging as proxy models incur high costs and prototype-based carriers cause semantic confusion.
approach: Rule-based federated learning shares interpretable class-discriminative rules via a rule network that unifies clients' decision features, with selective activation of rules relevant to local classes.
contribution: Achieves better accuracy-communication trade-off across heterogeneous settings compared to proxy-model and prototype-based approaches while maintaining personalization.

problem: Handling large-scale incomplete multi-view data poses challenges as anchor-based strategies rely on shallow bipartite graphs failing to capture complex high-order correlations, and treat observed and missing instances indiscriminately.
approach: Hypergraph-Augmented Incomplete Multi-View Clustering constructs consensus anchor-guided hypergraph modeling group-wise interactions with dual-adaptive reweighting mechanism calibrating importance at view and sample levels.
contribution: Achieves superior clustering accuracy and maintains high efficiency even in scenarios with severe data incompleteness, validated across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Large language models are prone to hallucination and untruthful responses particularly when tasks demand information outside their parametric knowledge, as approaches optimizing accuracy often amplify hallucinations.
approach: TruthRL implements GRPO with ternary reward distinguishing correct answers, hallucinations, and abstentions to incentivize models reducing hallucinations through both correct responses and abstention when uncertain.
contribution: Significantly reduces hallucinations (43.5% to 19.4% on benchmarks) and improves truthfulness (5.3% to 37.2%) across four knowledge-intensive benchmarks with gains across various backbone models.

problem: Multi-task learning with shared linear representations remains underdeveloped for likelihood-based efficiently solvable algorithms due to non-convex structure intrinsic to matrix factorization.
approach: Proposes first-order algorithm jointly learning shared representation and task-specific parameters with guaranteed efficiency, achieving convergence in Õ(1) iterations via likelihood-based optimization.
contribution: Attains near-optimal estimation error of Õ(dk/(TN)), improving over existing likelihood-based methods by a factor of k where d, k, T, N denote input dimension, representation dimension, task count, and samples per task.

problem: Test-time scaling methods like majority voting depend critically on error distribution across samples as concentrated errors degrade aggregation and suppress exploration in iterative refinement.
approach: D-FUSEr introduces theoretically grounded diverse failure reward incentivizing calibrated disagreement in model errors, with anti-votes predicting common mistakes to explicitly reweight probability mass.
contribution: Substantially improves majority vote and iterative refinement performance across three model families and four benchmarks without degrading single-sample accuracy.

problem: Large language models struggle with structural understanding when processing graph topologies in serialized format despite demonstrating remarkable semantic understanding.
approach: SLASH analyzes internal LLM attention mechanisms finding spontaneous graph topology reconstruction via sawtooth patterns in attention maps, then proposes attention redistribution to amplify structural understanding.
contribution: Delivers significant and consistent performance gains across diverse LLMs on graph tasks and molecular prediction with training-free solution requiring only attention redistribution.

problem: Training large-scale generative models is resource-intensive and relies on heuristic dataset weighting while it remains unclear if experts can be combined modularly to match monolithic performance robustly.
approach: Formulates modular generative modeling as minimax game to find robust gate minimizing divergence to worst-case data mixture, proven to exist via Kakutani's fixed-point theorem with modularity as strong regularizer.
contribution: Proves modular approach theoretically outperforms models retrained on aggregate data with gap characterized by Jensen-Shannon divergence, with scalable Stochastic Primal-Dual algorithm and Structural Distillation.

problem: Multi-agent systems using large language models introduce trustworthiness concerns as adversarial agents can inject misleading information that propagates contagiously, corrupting benign agents.
approach: Models multi-agent communication as signed directed acyclic graph computing each agent's contribution to final decision via backward propagation for accurate identification and isolation of malicious agents.
contribution: Notably outperforms existing multi-agent system defense mechanisms in complex and dynamic environments, providing effective guardrail for trustworthy multi-agent system deployment.

problem: Machine learning attacks on Learning with Errors with binary or small secrets succeed only on simple settings and fail to recover denser secrets or larger Hamming weights.
approach: Shows larger training sets and repeated examples allow recovery of denser secrets with observed power-law relationship, introducing stepwise regression technique to recover cool bits of the secret.
contribution: Allows recovery of denser binary secrets up to Hamming weight 70 for dimension 256 and 75 for dimension 512 (versus 33 and 63 in previous works), with substantial improvements on denser ternary secrets.

problem: Equivariant neural networks for general linear symmetries remain limited as most are built for compact groups, restricting reuse on matrix-valued data like covariances or shape tensors.
approach: Introduces Reductive Lie Neurons that achieve exact GL(n)-equivariance natively supporting matrix-valued and Lie-algebraic features using non-degenerate adjoint-invariant bilinear form.
contribution: Matches or outperforms strong equivariant and self-supervised baselines while using substantially fewer parameters and compute, with consistent improvements across diverse symmetry groups.

problem: Multimodal language models face security threats from visual prompt injection attacks with existing defenses lacking principled understanding of mechanisms and struggling to balance efficiency and fidelity.
approach: Localizes critical image tokens via gradient analysis then neutralizes through masking, introducing Hidden-State Gradient Norm score for adversarial behavior attribution with theoretical consistency guarantees.
contribution: Reduces attack success rates to near zero while preserving model utility with negligible computational overhead, requiring only single forward-backward pass to identify and mask tokens.

problem: Machine learning weather forecasting models suffer from spectral degradation from training to predict ensemble mean deterministically and compressive encoding creating information bottlenecks.
approach: MOSAIC combines learned functional perturbations for ensemble forecasting with block-sparse attention sharing keys and values across spatially adjacent queries to capture long-range dependencies at linear cost.
contribution: At 1.5° resolution matches or outperforms models trained on 0.25° data on IFS HRES with individual ensemble members exhibiting near-perfect spectral alignment across all resolved frequencies.

problem: Self-interpretation methods prompting language models to describe internal states remain unreliable due to hyperparameter sensitivity in LLMs.
approach: Trains lightweight adapters on interpretability artifacts while keeping LM frozen, using scalar affine adapter with only d_model+1 parameters to generate feature labels from sparse autoencoders.
contribution: Generates sparse autoencoder feature labels outperforming training labels (70% versus 50% at 70B), identifies topics with 94% recall@1, decodes bridge entities in reasoning without chain-of-thought.

problem: Learning optimal individualized dosing policies to maximize utility faces high experimental costs imposing strict budget constraints, with continuous dosing and policy optimization underexplored in active learning.
approach: Active learning framework exploiting dose-response curve structure showing policy optimization regret bounded by expected posterior gradient variance, with batch acquisition strategy minimizing target gradient variance.
contribution: GVALID achieves superior performance under strict budget constraints on optimal policy learning for individualized dosing.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation systems remain brittle under realistic retrieval noise as retrievers and rerankers optimize for relevance alone, selecting trivial or unsuitable evidence for generators.
approach: BAR-RAG reframes reranker as boundary-aware evidence selector targeting generator's Goldilocks Zone through reinforcement learning using generator feedback and two-stage fine-tuning pipeline.
contribution: Consistently improves end-to-end performance under noisy retrieval achieving average gain of 10.3% over strong RAG and reranking baselines while substantially improving robustness.

problem: Online learning for Cox proportional hazards model is challenging because partial likelihood is non-decomposable with each risk set requiring summation over all samples.
approach: COLSA replaces partial likelihood with full likelihood using sieve approximation of baseline hazard, maintaining sufficient statistics for higher-order basis with data-driven basis projection.
contribution: Achieves asymptotic normality and statistical efficiency matching pooled-data partial likelihood estimator without accessing full data and only requiring constant memory.

problem: Continual learning on long task sequences struggles to effectively learn discriminative and comprehensive feature representations while maintaining stability and plasticity across 100+ tasks.
approach: CaRE uses bi-level routing mixture-of-experts with router selection stage dynamically activating task-specific routers and expert routing phase for dynamic expert aggregation across network layers.
contribution: First continual learner scaling to 100-300+ non-overlapping tasks significantly outperforming all baselines, with new OmniBenchmark-1K dataset for very long task sequences.

problem: Users accessing large language models via black-box APIs must transmit sensitive prompts, outputs, and fine-tuning data to external providers, creating critical privacy risks at API boundary.
approach: AlienLM provides API-only privacy layer translating text into Alien Language via vocabulary-scale bijection enabling lossless recovery, with Alien Adaptation Training adapting models to operate on alienized inputs.
contribution: Retains over 81% of plaintext-oracle performance on average substantially outperforming baselines, recovering fewer than 0.22% of alienized tokens under adversaries with model weights access.

problem: Generating long-horizon molecular dynamics is difficult due to error accumulation in time-domain autoregressive models causing drift and fixed step-size constraints on temporal resolution.
approach: BioDynaSpec reformulates protein dynamics as spatio-spectral generation via Independent Windowed Fourier Decomposition combined with low-to-high frequency autoregression and diffusion denoising.
contribution: Improves 250-frame trajectory generation with R_250=1.509 Å reducing error by 60.4% versus MDGEN and 57.2% versus ProAR, achieving best PCA and distribution matching metrics.

problem: Computational protein design requires substantial domain expertise with traditional physics-based methods or relies on restricted functional ontologies that fail to bridge semantic gap between text and protein sequences.
approach: PDAgent uses LLM-driven autonomous agent framework with ReAct reasoning loop implementing five phases (think, plan, act, observe, reflect) integrating template retrieval and conservation-aware mutation.
contribution: Achieves 91.86% average constraint satisfaction rate with high structural quality (mean pLDDT 87.69) substantially outperforming direct LLM generation and specialized deep learning methods.

problem: Semi-supervised learning faces challenges in realistic scenarios where labeled data is scarce and unlabeled data follows unknown arbitrary distributions with pseudo-labeling methods prone to erroneous labels.
approach: SAGE leverages inter-sample relations for structural inference using simplex anchored graph-state equipartition capturing high-order dependencies, with simplex equiangular tight frame guiding representation separation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on five standard benchmarks with average accuracy gain of 8.52% by bypassing distribution estimation via structural consensus.

problem: High-fidelity solubility prediction must couple molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior across diverse chemical environments but existing methods sacrifice interpretability for predictive power.
approach: DISSOLVR challenges this trend by developing transparent framework using physically-grounded descriptors with LLM-assisted post-hoc explanation pipeline bridging symbolic artifacts and chemically grounded narratives.
contribution: Approaches aleatoric limit of experimental uncertainty achieving out-of-distribution generalization through structural invariance without requiring non-transparent architectures.

problem: Graph convolutional networks treat adjacent nodes as equally important and may limit representational power by failing to capture highly correlated information between nonadjacent nodes.
approach: Global Interacted Graph Convolutional Network leverages Dominant Set solution vectors to adaptively characterize global importance distribution over all nodes modulating message passing across layers.
contribution: Effectively captures highly correlated information between nonadjacent nodes emphasizing critical graph-level information while enhancing discriminative power with optimized memory complexity.

problem: Heterogeneous federated learning approaches often rely on sharing model parameters or representations exposing sensitive information and incurring overhead.
approach: SoHip enables collaboration via memory sharing rather than model sharing, abstracting agents' short-term memory into individual long-term memory through hippocampus-inspired mechanism.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods achieving up to 8.78% accuracy improvements while preserving on-device raw data and local models with only lightweight memory exchange.

problem: Machine learning interatomic potentials follow scaling laws but lack scalable distributed training systems due to double-backward execution pattern creating mismatch with existing systems.
approach: JanusPipe integrates SymFold for memory-efficient pipeline parallelism with WaveK reducing pipeline bubbles by balancing four-phase compute time in 3D-parallel training.
contribution: Improves throughput by 1.51× and 1.45× on average over 1F1B and Hanayo respectively on 32 GPUs for machine learning interatomic potential training.

problem: Understanding what generative models retain from training data remains challenging beyond verbatim reproduction with subtle traces exploitable for membership inference.
approach: Analyzes Rectified Flows interpolation path finding gap between train and test data reconstruction following bell-shaped curve over interpolation parameter that accumulates during training.
contribution: Shows bell-shaped membership signal structure is universal with peak location derivable in closed form under Gaussian assumptions, enabling membership inference attack exploiting λ-resolved structure.

problem: Visual document retrieval models are historically repurposed from generative VLMs but this design choice constrains performance in multi-vector embedding settings.
approach: ModernVBERT systematically develops VDR models from ground up through controlled experiments isolating key training factors including attention masking and contrastive objectives.
contribution: Trains 250M-parameter vision-language encoder outperforming recent models up to 10 times its size on document retrieval tasks while enabling efficient CPU inference.

problem: Goal-conditioned policies' downstream performance is highly sensitive to discrete text prompts but bypassing text limitations through latent control remains underexplored.
approach: Preference Goal Tuning formulates post-training as latent control where goal embedding serves as continuous control variable to modulate frozen policy behavior optimized with trajectory-level preference objective.
contribution: Achieves average relative improvements of 72.0% and 81.6% on Minecraft tasks with minimal data, surpassing full fine-tuning by 13.4% in out-of-distribution settings.

problem: Existing unified medical models treat understanding and generation as separate objectives, missing the opportunity for understanding to directly improve generative synthesis performance.
approach: SynerMedGen introduces generation-aligned understanding tasks and a two-stage training strategy that transfers understanding representations to improve medical image synthesis, with bidirectional synergy between the two objectives.
contribution: Achieves strong zero-shot performance on 22 medical image synthesis tasks and outperforms specialized and recent unified models with generation training, while releasing SynerMed dataset with 1M synthesis samples and 2M understanding instances.

problem: Training prediction models in predict-then-optimize requires minimizing decision regret through linear/combinatorial optimization, but the piecewise-constant decision mapping has zero gradients almost everywhere, making direct gradient-based optimization intractable.
approach: Proposes a solver-free training pipeline based on measure transformation that yields a surrogate loss avoiding expensive solver calls during gradient evaluation.
contribution: Achieves decision quality competitive with state-of-the-art methods while reducing training time by orders of magnitude through elimination of per-gradient solver calls.

problem: Existing activation decomposition methods assume concepts map to individual global directions, overlooking concepts with nonlinear or multi-dimensional structure in language model activations.
approach: Uses Mixture of Factor Analyzers as an unsupervised alternative to model activation space as a collection of Gaussian regions with local covariance structure, decomposing activations into region centroids and local variations.
contribution: Outperforms unsupervised baselines and is competitive with supervised localization methods while achieving stronger steering performance than sparse autoencoders for concept discovery.

problem: Computing gradients of LogSumExp with large or infinite numbers of exponential terms is computationally challenging, limiting applications in entropy-regularized optimal transport and distributionally robust optimization.
approach: Proposes a convexity- and smoothness-preserving approximation to LogSumExp via a novel Safe KL divergence that can be efficiently optimized with stochastic gradient methods.
contribution: Demonstrates advantages over existing baselines in DRO and continuous optimal transport problems through theoretical analysis and experiments.

problem: Optimization-based adversarial attacks on LLMs produce incoherent high-perplexity suffixes easily detected by defenses or, when constrained for coherence, achieve low success rates against robust models.
approach: Introduces Greedy Coordinate Diffusion leveraging discrete diffusion language models to guide the search for adversarial suffixes that maintain semantic coherence and low perplexity without gradient access.
contribution: Achieves highest attack success rate while remaining competitive on response-quality scores and being detected at lower rates than other methods by perplexity-based and guard-model filters.

problem: LLM-conditioned segmentation suffers from semantic misalignment where high-quality mask candidates fail to match the linguistic condition because language semantics are used statically rather than actively guiding the iterative mask generation.
approach: FlowSeg introduces dynamic semantic guidance via bidirectional flow between intermediate decoding states and LLM-derived condition embeddings, with condition embeddings progressively updated by visual evidence and boundary-aware refinement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on referring expression and reasoning segmentation tasks with improved language-mask alignment through dynamic semantic guidance.

problem: Existing backdoor attacks on Vision-Language Models rely on data poisoning with visual triggers and modified labels, creating image-text mismatches that are easy to detect.
approach: Proposes Clean-Label Backdoor Attack via diffusion models that generates natural poisoned examples through score matching, guiding generation with textual information and using GradCAM-guided masks to restrict modifications to semantically important regions.
contribution: Achieves over 80% attack success rate while preserving normal functionality and maintaining stealthiness against both perplexity-based and guard-model defenses.

problem: Under distribution shift and time-varying optimization, momentum variants of SGD are often used as heuristics for gradient smoothing, but their theoretical properties under nonstationary conditions are unclear.
approach: Provides comprehensive theoretical analysis decomposing tracking error into transient, noise-induced, and drift-induced components, revealing that momentum incurs explicit drift-amplification penalties that diverge as momentum parameter approaches 1.
contribution: Proves via minimax lower bounds that momentum's tracking penalty is not an artifact but an information-theoretic barrier, precisely delineating regimes where vanilla SGD provably outperforms accelerated variants.

problem: Data augmentation strategies in contrastive learning are typically treated as heuristics; the relationship between augmentation choices and learning objectives is not well understood theoretically.
approach: Converts contrastive loss to an auxiliary Gaussian distribution using information theory to define task entropy, proving that predefined augmentations can be regarded as point estimation of beneficial Pi-Noise, then proposes a learnable noise generator instead.
contribution: Successfully learns effective augmentations through the noise generator framework, providing theoretical grounding for data augmentation in contrastive learning.

problem: Evaluating long-context language models conflates architectural capacity to capture dependencies with semantic knowledge and vocabulary statistics, preventing clean diagnosis of whether failures stem from architectural limitations or domain knowledge insufficiency.
approach: Introduces L-CUBE, a synthetic benchmark with hierarchical Gaussian sequences and controllable bipartite mutual information scaling, providing exact ground-truth conditionals and enabling unconfounded evaluation via conditional KL divergence.
contribution: Validates L2M capacity theory predictions and uncovers new phenomena across transformers, state space models, and efficient alternatives; enables practitioners to test long-context capability at target sequence lengths before expensive real-data training.

problem: Precise training-free image editing with text-to-image diffusion models requires balancing three conflicting objectives (alignment, consistency, quality), and existing sparse autoencoder steering approaches rely on heuristic feature selection and manual tuning.
approach: Proposes SRLS casting steering-vector discovery as a convex sparse recovery problem using Lasso for feature selection and support-restricted ridge refitting, with fixed-budget Bayesian optimization replacing manual strength tuning.
contribution: Improves the alignment-consistency-quality trade-off over competing methods through automatic feature selection and optimized steering strength.

problem: Biomedical regression tasks require predicting continuous targets from heterogeneous evidence, but LLMs inherently use discrete tokenization and cross-entropy objectives lacking awareness of numerical proximity.
approach: Introduces SPR-RAFT with a learnable soft prompt and lightweight regression head combined via hybrid objective merging distribution-based text generation with representation-based robust regression, aligning both modalities.
contribution: With only 0.04% trainable parameters, consistently outperforms prompting strategies and fine-tuning across biomedical benchmarks including clinical trial duration, biological age estimation, and molecular property prediction.

problem: Time series decomposition methods lack unified evaluation frameworks; their quality is assessed informally with no standard benchmark comparing component recovery under controlled mechanisms.
approach: Introduces a synthetic evaluation suite with explicit trend and cycle taxonomies, a unified interface for representative decomposition families, and complementary metrics capturing shape, phase, and spectral fidelity errors.
contribution: Reveals that STL-family methods perform near-ceiling under stationary periodicity, while subspace/time-frequency methods better preserve seasonal consistency under non-stationary conditions; downstream symbolic regression improves structure discovery.

problem: Spiking Neural Networks trained with surrogate gradients suffer from timestep scaling paradox where increasing timesteps counterintuitively degrades performance, linking to temporal gradient vanishing and weakened cross-timestep dependencies.
approach: Proposes Timestep-Scalable neuron model with long-term memory reconsolidation to enhance cross-timestep information flow and temporal forgetting mechanism to suppress excessive temporal buildup.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on time-series and event-based tasks while maintaining strong performance on image classification and object detection, with improved performance when scaling timesteps.

problem: Narrow-task fine-tuning of large models degrades broad capabilities through trajectory lock-in where task loss and generalization collapse onto a shared degradation curve, defeating most stabilizer approaches.
approach: Introduces objective-agnostic geometric probes tracking the effective update subspace and an online harm signal reflecting curvature-dominated channeling; identifies that escaping lock-in requires spectral bifurcation toward softer curvature modes.
contribution: Provides practical procedures to achieve spectral bifurcation that improves broad generalization while maintaining matched training performance across model scales and modalities.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models exhibit remarkable capabilities but struggle significantly with spatial reasoning tasks due to representation-output misalignment where internal spatial encoding differs from final text output.
approach: Proposes GRASP, a training-free framework using Manifold Differential Search to identify geometric counterfactuals, then applying dual-level rectification with Implicit Trajectory Correction for intermediate layers and Explicit Distribution Alignment for output.
contribution: Achieves accuracy gains up to 26.1% on image spatial reasoning and 9.7% on video reasoning without parameter updates, consistently outperforming baselines across diverse architectures.

problem: Batch inference for agentic workloads severely degrades throughput when long-lived agents accumulate state over time, causing middle-phase thrashing before GPU memory capacity is exhausted.
approach: CONCUR implements lightweight agent-level admission control inspired by congestion control in distributed systems, dynamically adjusting the number of active agents using runtime cache signals to bound aggregate cache pressure.
contribution: Prevents middle-phase thrashing and improves batch inference throughput by up to 4.09x on Qwen3-32B and 1.90x on DeepSeek-V3 while remaining compatible with existing LLM serving systems.

problem: Existing forgery detection methods limit themselves to uni-modal or bi-modal settings, unable to handle interleaved text, images, and videos prevalent in real-world misinformation.
approach: Proposes OmniVL-Guard with a Self-Evolving CoT Generation pipeline to synthesize high-quality reasoning, then uses Adaptive Reward Scaling Policy Optimization (ARSPO) to dynamically modulate reward scales and task weights for balanced joint optimization.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods with robust zero-shot generalization across out-of-domain scenarios for unified omni vision-language forgery detection and grounding.

problem: Most deep video codecs emphasize low-level motion modeling and remain semantics-agnostic, degrading perceptual quality in complex scenes and failing to incorporate semantic understanding.
approach: Proposes MoVie, a multimodal framework with Text-guided Video Transformer-CNN mixed blocks using dual-stage text fusion, history-conditioned coding, and spatial-channel factorized entropy model for adaptive bit allocation.
contribution: Achieves -50.23% BD-rate for FID and -14.64% for LPIPS relative to HM while requiring only 55.76% of DCVC-FM's per-pixel computation, with human preference confirmed.

problem: Existing benchmarks for LLM compositional reasoning focus on single-turn restricted scenarios, failing to capture capability boundaries exposed by real-world interactive scientific workflows.
approach: Introduces XDomainBench formalizing composition order and mixture structure with 8,598 interactive sessions across 20 domains and 4 task categories, featuring 8 realistic trajectory patterns.
contribution: Reveals systematic reasoning collapse as composition order increases, caused by direct difficulty increases and interaction-amplified failures where trajectory patterns trigger error accumulation.

problem: Reward-maximizing RL methods enhance LLM reasoning but often reduce generation diversity; GFlowNet approaches match target distributions while learning partition functions, but treat the partition function solely as a normalizer.
approach: Reinterprets the partition function as per-prompt expected-reward (accuracy) signal, proposing PACED-RL which prioritizes informative prompts during training and uses accuracy-estimate error-prioritized replay.
contribution: Demonstrates strong performance improvements over GRPO and prior GFlowNet approaches with improved sample efficiency by reusing information from existing GFlowNet training.

problem: Prompt-based few-shot adaptation of LLMs initializes trainable prompts with irrelevant tokens, underutilizing the model's In-Context Learning ability during lightweight adaptation.
approach: Introduces Context Tuning which initializes trainable prompts with task-specific demonstration examples, leveraging the model's inherent ICL ability to extract relevant information.
contribution: Outperforms traditional prompt-based methods and achieves competitive accuracy with Test-Time Training at significantly higher training efficiency on CrossFit, UnifiedQA, MMLU, BIG-Bench Hard, and ARC.

problem: AI agents execute procedural workflows as sequential action traces, obscuring latent concurrency and inducing repeated step-by-step reasoning that leads to inefficient execution.
approach: Introduces BPOP, a Bayesian framework inferring latent dependency partial orders from linearized traces via MCMC with a tractable frontier-softmax likelihood avoiding #P-hard marginalization.
contribution: Recovers dependency structure more accurately than baselines and enables a compiled executor that prunes irrelevant context, yielding substantial reductions in token usage and execution time.

problem: Vision-Language Models for autonomous driving lack explicit modeling of world dynamics, limiting informed and physically grounded decision-making in interaction-intensive scenarios.
approach: Proposes DynVLA introducing Dynamics CoT paradigm with a Dynamics Tokenizer compressing future evolution into compact tokens, decoupling ego-centric and environment-centric dynamics, then trained via SFT and RFT.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Textual CoT and Visual CoT methods on NAVSIM, Bench2Drive, and large-scale driving datasets, validating Dynamics CoT effectiveness.

problem: Fixed clipping bounds in PPO strictly constrain upward updates of low-probability actions, suppressing high-advantage tail strategies and inducing rapid entropy collapse in LLM RL.
approach: Introduces Band-constrained Policy Optimization (BandPO) replacing fixed clipping with Band, a theoretical operator projecting trust regions into dynamic probability-aware clipping intervals.
contribution: Consistently outperforms canonical clipping and Clip-Higher while robustly mitigating entropy collapse across diverse models and datasets.

problem: Differentially private optimization with per-sample gradient clipping and noise injection limits convergence within a constant-radius neighborhood of stationary points, inducing solution bias.
approach: Proposes DP-C4 framework incorporating a coupled clipping scheme with shifted threshold strategy ensuring clipping bias and noise variance asymptotically vanish, plus tailored privacy budget allocation.
contribution: Injects significantly less noise than DP-SGD under the same privacy level and converges to the optimum in strongly-convex case or diminishing neighborhood in non-convex case.

problem: Subquadratic recurrent operators ignore the curvature of the least-squares loss during optimization, operating as first-order approximations that miss important structure for improved efficiency.
approach: Introduces preconditioning to delta-rule recurrences derived from online least-squares theory, realizing diagonal approximations for DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, and Kimi Delta Attention with efficient chunkwise parallel algorithms.
contribution: Preconditioned variants yield consistent performance improvements across synthetic recall benchmarks and language modeling at 340M and 1B scale.

problem: RL training for software engineering agents is constrained by scarcity of large-scale task collections with reproducible execution environments and reliable test suites across diverse programming languages.
approach: Introduces SWE-rebench V2, a language-agnostic automated pipeline synthesizing repository-specific installation and test procedures via an interactive setup agent, filtering via LLM judge ensemble.
contribution: Constructs dataset of 32,079 tasks spanning 20 languages and 3,617 repositories with pre-built images, plus 120,000+ tasks with generated problem statements based on pull requests.

problem: Conventional transformers for traffic forecasting lack interpretability through their black-box self-attention, and mixed-graph approaches are limited by local receptive fields or quadratic complexity.
approach: Builds a lightweight interpretable transformer-like network by unrolling a mixed-graph optimization algorithm (ADMM) with undirected graph for spatial correlations and directed graph for sequential relationships, inserting graph learning modules.
contribution: Achieves competitive traffic forecast performance as state-of-the-art schemes while drastically reducing parameter counts through the unrolled algorithm design.

problem: Rectified Flow models for precipitation nowcasting suffer from accumulated velocity estimation errors during ODE integration, inducing progressive off-manifold drift and morphological distortions at extended lead times.
approach: Proposes PDRF re-parameterizing the generative ODE in data space where the network predicts clean future sequences, analytically inducing a coupled vector field with implicit restoring effects, plus semi-Lagrangian teacher for transport.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements in event-based skill and better preservation of intense-echo morphology over long horizons compared to existing approaches.

problem: Existing causal discovery approaches face significant time and space efficiency bottlenecks when scaling to large graphs, limiting applicability in scientific AI and large-scale data analysis.
approach: Presents CauScale, a neural architecture with a reduction unit compressing data embeddings and tied attention weights avoiding axis-specific attention maps, using a two-stream design for data and graph features.
contribution: Scales inference to 1000-node graphs, achieves 99.6% mAP on in-distribution and 84.4% on out-of-distribution data, with 4x-13,000x speedups over prior methods.

problem: Flow Matching models rely on iterative ODE solving creating latency bottlenecks; existing solutions face a trade-off between training-free solvers with poor performance at low NFE and costly training-based methods.
approach: Proposes Bi-Anchor Interpolation Solver (BA-solver) with lightweight SideNet learning bidirectional temporal perception and utilizing two anchor velocities for efficient high-order integration.
contribution: Achieves generation quality of 100+ NFE Euler solver in just 10 NFEs on ImageNet-256 with high fidelity in 5 NFEs, incurring negligible training costs.

problem: Translation-equivariant Neural Processes with generic components obscure induced function class and lack interpretability; convolutional designs require dense uniform grids while attention methods scale quadratically.
approach: Characterizes translation-equivariant operators via Volterra series and proposes Set Fourier Convolutions operating directly on irregular points with approximately global receptive fields scaling linearly.
contribution: Demonstrates efficacy of SFConvCNPs and SFVConvCNPs against state-of-the-art baselines on synthetic and real-world datasets with improved interpretability and efficiency.

problem: Existing protein structure tokenizers create tokens by pooling local neighborhood information, limiting performance on generative and representation tasks through error accumulation and fixed resolution.
approach: Presents a method for global tokenization where successive tokens contribute increasing levels of detail to a global representation, enabling task-specific adaptation of tokenized sequence information content.
contribution: Matches or outperforms existing models on reconstruction and generative tasks, enables zero-shot protein shrinking and affinity maturation, and outperforms other tokenizers on CATH classification.

problem: Existing spatial understanding benchmarks rely on limited manually annotated datasets, severely constraining scalability and causing domain gaps from narrow data curation.
approach: Proposes Holi-Spatial, an automated large-scale spatially-aware multimodal dataset from raw video without human intervention using data curation pipeline, supporting multi-level spatial supervision from 3D Gaussian Splatting to semantic annotations.
contribution: Constructs Holi-Spatial-4M with 12K optimized 3DGS scenes, 1.3M 2D masks, 320K 3D bounding boxes, 320K instance captions, and 1.2M spatial QA pairs, demonstrating exceptional data quality.

problem: Logit-based LLM watermarking effectiveness depends on fundamental detection-distortion trade-off, but existing analyses provide limited guidance for principled hyperparameter selection.
approach: Develops a power-calibrated statistical framework establishing quantitative relationships between hyperparameters, detection power, and distortion, transforming design into a guided optimization problem.
contribution: Derives practical parameter selection procedures achieving optimal trade-offs under constraints, validated across multiple language models with Pareto-optimal point identification.

problem: Existing generative recommendation approaches largely rely on alignment-centric fusion, underexploring synergistic information across modalities that encode emergent item properties.
approach: Proposes SynGR framework explicitly encouraging exploitation of cross-modal dependencies during generation by constraining overreliance on dominant modalities.
contribution: Achieves superior performance across three benchmark datasets by capturing emergent item semantics beyond shared or modality-specific signals.

problem: 3D VAE training for high-fidelity generation requires rendering supervision that only covers visible geometry, leaving many latent voxels weakly constrained while incurring unnecessary compute.
approach: Introduces Focusing, a view-consistent sparse-voxel training scheme performing depth-driven voxel carving in latent space before decoding, with adaptive zooming adjusting camera intrinsics to maintain target voxel counts.
contribution: Improves Chamfer Distance and F-score over baselines while reducing memory and computation through view-dependent sparsity and concentrated learning on surface regions.

problem: High-dimensional convex ERM under non-Gaussian data lacks asymptotic characterization of key statistics, limiting prediction of mean and covariance of ERM estimators.
approach: Extends the Convex Gaussian Min-Max Theorem to non-Gaussian settings under concentration assumptions, deriving asymptotic min-max characterization and showing regularizer equivalences.
contribution: Clarifies scope and limits of Gaussian universality for ERMs, proving Convolution with centered Gaussian variable and proving any C2 regularizer is asymptotically equivalent to specific quadratic forms.

problem: Federated domain-incremental learning under partial participation lacks guarantee of backward knowledge transfer and convergence rates that hold uniformly across task sequences.
approach: Introduces SPECIAL, adding a server-side anchor proximal step to FedAvg that blends updates with the previous global model, maintaining replay-free transfer without task-specific heads.
contribution: Bounds backward knowledge transfer with drift-controlled terms and achieves task-uniform convergence at O(sqrt(E/(NT))) while explicitly separating optimization variance from inter-task drift.

problem: Smooth nonconvex nonconcave minimax optimization lacks theoretical guarantees for convergence rates even under favorable structural conditions like the two-sided Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality.
approach: Uses Lyapunov functions both for algorithm design and convergence certification; replaces an intractable idealized Lyapunov function with a computable gradient-based surrogate to derive TALDA, a single-loop algorithm that enforces Lyapunov descent by construction.
contribution: TALDA achieves linear convergence under the two-sided PL condition with explicit dependence on cross-smoothness, recovering existing rates while improving performance on weakly coupled min-max problems.

problem: LoRA-based continual learning methods suffer from incomplete knowledge transfer because they overlook task-shared directions and fail to identify truly task-specific directions when tasks are correlated.
approach: Proposes LoDA with task-driven decomposition that builds general and task-specific LoRA subspaces using energy-based objectives; learns robust up-projections via Gradient-Aligned Optimization and derives closed-form recalibration for knowledge sharing.
contribution: LoDA outperforms existing continual learning methods by decoupling knowledge sharing and isolation while maintaining robust performance.

problem: Spatial proteomics analysis remains fragmented with manual orchestration of heterogeneous tools, limiting research scalability and reproducibility for understanding tumor microenvironments.
approach: SP-Mind is an autonomous AI agent combining expert-curated biological skills with specialized computational tools to convert natural-language queries into end-to-end analytical workflows without task-specific fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on SP-Bench (102 tasks across 18 categories) compared to existing open-source biomedical agent baselines.

problem: Compressing long chains of thought into compact tokens while preserving reasoning structure requires balancing global structure capture with fine-grained reasoning details.
approach: ImgCoT renders chain-of-thought as images and learns latent visual tokens instead of textual reconstruction, substituting linguistic bias for spatial inductive bias; loose variant augments visual tokens with selected key textual steps based on log-likelihood.
contribution: Enables compact encoding of reasoning with fewer tokens while retaining both global structure and details across multiple LLM architectures.

problem: Real-time diffusion-based compression requires lightweight models that generation-oriented pre-training fails to optimize for, and standard approaches are too slow for practical deployment.
approach: CoD-Lite uses compression-oriented pre-training paired with lightweight convolutions instead of transformers; distillation and adversarial learning enable one-step diffusion for real-time encoding/decoding at 1080p.
contribution: Achieves real-time 60 FPS encoding and 42 FPS decoding with 85% bitrate reduction compared to MS-ILLM.

problem: Spurious correlations causing models to learn wrong features remain difficult to address because group-balanced approaches require expensive bias annotations or pretrained models limited to interpretable biases.
approach: Reframes spurious correlations as class-conditional distribution mismatches and uses sample reweighting to maximize conditional entropy of labels given spurious factors, automatically highlighting minority groups.
contribution: Delivers competitive robustness to bias-supervised methods while eliminating need for bias annotations or predictions.

problem: Motion imitation evaluation metrics conflate policy limitations with intrinsic learning difficulty of target motions, preventing principled error diagnosis in physics-based humanoid control.
approach: Proposes Torque Variation Score (TVS), a physics-grounded metric measuring how torque magnitude must vary to correct pose perturbations, revealing which motions have flat reward landscapes and vanishing gradients.
contribution: TVS enables accurate error attribution: high error on low-TV motions indicates policy deficiency, while high error on high-TV motions reflects fundamental learning constraints; supports mocap quality control.

problem: Multimodal alignment fails under deployment shift because standard objectives entangle cross-modal dependence with marginal-sensitive geometry, lacking interpretable diagnostics.
approach: SSCA uses clipped soft-rank Gaussianization to suppress marginal effects, dependence-weighted sliced Wasserstein coupling for global alignment, and diagonal-stabilized block-spectral learning with auditable diagnostics for monitoring drift.
contribution: Improves robustness under perturbations and monotone distortions with reduced degradation compared to standard approaches; provides label-free, actionable diagnostic signals.

problem: Pruning at initialization methods lack rigorous theoretical characterization of global sparsity patterns that emerge at scale, limiting understanding of when and why they work.
approach: Connects discrete pruning heuristics to graph limit theory via graphons; proves masks converge to deterministic bipartite graphons, establishing topological taxonomy distinguishing homogeneous unstructured methods from heterogeneous data-driven methods.
contribution: Derives universal approximation theorem for sparse networks and connects limiting graphons to NTK-style generalization bounds with path-density interpretation.

problem: Generative models struggle with equality-constrained distributions because their support cannot match ambient space while satisfying manifold constraints, causing sampling instability.
approach: Perturbs data distribution in constraint-aware manner to increase support dimension while preserving manifold geometry; applies to both diffusion models and normalizing flows.
contribution: Enables stable sampling and data distribution recovery for equality-constrained generative models across representative scientific tasks.

problem: Source-free domain adaptation for regression lacks effective methods because continuous labels pose unique challenges for representation adaptation and pseudo-label refinement.
approach: Leverages discretized density-informed supervisory signals with instance-dependent weighting and auxiliary distribution learning to refine pseudo-labels and promote compact feature representations.
contribution: Demonstrates robust SFDA for regression under distribution shift with theoretical guarantees on perturbation resilience.

problem: Representing microbial dynamics in soil organic matter models requires connecting genomic data to biokinetic parameters, but the complex relationship between genomes and microbial processes remains unknown.
approach: Hybrid framework uses neural network to predict biokinetic parameters from metagenome-inferred functional traits while integrating ecological theory constraints ensuring realistic behavior even for unobserved state variables.
contribution: Improves generalization on synthetic and real genomic data; effectively learns dynamics of unmeasurable model components even with small datasets.

problem: Pretraining and post-training of reasoning models follow contradictory data-quality principles—large diverse pretraining versus smaller high-quality post-training—with unclear theoretical justification.
approach: Theoretically analyzes transformers on in-context weight prediction for linear regression; reveals balanced pretraining induces latent capabilities, SFT benefits from challenging examples, and RL favors large-scale non-difficult data.
contribution: Identifies key findings about dataset quality requirements at different training stages, validated on large nonlinear architectures.

problem: Simulating deformable objects under rich robot interactions requires jointly modeling environmental effects and robot-controlled dynamics without predefined physics.
approach: SoMA couples deformable dynamics, environmental forces, and robot joint actions in unified latent neural space using learned 3D Gaussian Splats for end-to-end real-to-sim simulation.
contribution: Improves resimulation accuracy and generalization on real robot manipulation by 20%, enabling stable long-horizon tasks like cloth folding.

problem: Adversarial distillation with robust teachers often fails because teacher confidence on unlearnable samples causes students to memorize spurious noise, leading to robust overfitting.
approach: Analyzes feature learning dynamics of two-layer networks to show teacher-student misalignment on Robustly Unlearnable Set drives robust overfitting; proposes using teacher uncertainty as robustness indicator.
contribution: Demonstrates robust overfitting is driven by teacher-student interaction on unlearnable samples; provides principled guideline via teacher predictive entropy.

problem: Zeroth-order optimization appears to work well for fine-tuning massive LLMs despite classical theory predicting dimension-dependent slowdown, leaving a theoretical gap.
approach: Derives one-step learning dynamics of ZO-SGD showing empirical Neural Tangent Kernel emerges with elements corresponding to inner products on random low-dimensional subspaces; invokes Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma.
contribution: Shows approximation error depends on model output size rather than parameter dimension, explaining ZO scalability to LLMs.

problem: Accelerated Noisy Power Method for PCA with inexact products requires overly restrictive perturbation bounds in prior work, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Provides improved analysis showing accelerated convergence under much milder perturbation conditions; proves analysis is worst-case optimal and derives accelerated decentralized PCA algorithm.
contribution: First decentralized PCA algorithm with provably accelerated convergence and similar communication costs to non-accelerated methods.

problem: Computing globally optimal policies in multi-agent systems with graph-structured local dynamics is intractable due to exponential state-action space scaling.
approach: Studies conditions for approximating optimal policies with local policies depending on m-hop neighborhood states; controls influence propagation using Dobrushin-type stability matrix.
contribution: Shows globally optimal policies can be approximated by local policies with sub-optimality gap decaying exponentially in neighborhood radius.

problem: Understanding dynamic point cloud sequences in multimodal LLMs is unexplored due to lack of large-scale datasets and difficulty modeling spatio-temporal motion.
approach: Constructs 4DPC²hat-200K dataset via topology-consistent 4D point construction and two-level captioning; proposes Mamba-enhanced temporal reasoning MLLM with failure-aware bootstrapping to iteratively strengthen reasoning.
contribution: First MLLM for dynamic point clouds with 44K sequences and 200K QA pairs; significantly improves action understanding and temporal reasoning.

problem: Risk prioritization in high-stakes decisions requires interpretability, but falling rule lists have restricted expressivity due to single-path structure.
approach: Introduces falling trees extending rule lists with tree-structured branching while preserving monotonic risk constraint; proposes GraviTree algorithm for learning Rashomon sets under depth and branching constraints.
contribution: Falling trees match or outperform FRL baselines with greater sparsity for high-risk cases; interpolates between rule lists and decision trees.

problem: Fairness research documents metric trade-offs but lacks quantitative frameworks to measure intrinsic compatibility without requiring causal graphs.
approach: Introduces game-theoretic framework decomposing metrics into interaction vectors; enables compatibility measurement via cosine similarity and mechanistic attribution to attribute coalitions.
contribution: Reveals fairness and utility are often structurally orthogonal rather than conflicting; debiasing improves fairness by compressing compatibility space.

problem: Unified multimodal models suffer from mutual impairment between understanding and generation branches due to incompatible inductive biases in supervision signals.
approach: DIVA framework transforms representation divergence into synergy by factorizing visual representation into shared and unique components based on complementary information flows; uses mutual information estimation.
contribution: Achieves improvements in visual understanding (+7.82%) and generation (+8.46%).

problem: Existing fake media research treats media authenticity and content veracity separately, overlooking how real-world deception jointly exploits both dimensions.
approach: FakeWorld 1.0 unifies authenticity and veracity assessment in omni-modal benchmark spanning text/audio/image/video with web-based presentation scenarios; introduces OmniChecker agent for joint detection.
contribution: Exposes fundamental capability limits in MLLMs for detecting high-fidelity mixed-source deception with explainable per-instance rationales.

problem: Transformer circuits lack stability assessment across different training runs, making it unclear whether reported circuits emerge universally or are instance-specific.
approach: Systematically studies attention-head stability across independently initialized refits in increasingly complex models; quantifies per-layer representational similarity and functional importance.
contribution: Establishes cross-instance robustness as prerequisite for scalable oversight; weight decay substantially improves stability; middle layers show strongest divergence.

problem: Training instability in deep learning stems from rare extreme gradient spikes causing oversized updates and optimizer corruption, requiring principled safeguards beyond gradient clipping.
approach: GradientStabilizer preserves gradient direction while replacing magnitude with statistically stabilized estimate from running gradient-norm statistics; proven uniformly bounded on spikes.
contribution: Improves training stability across LLM pre-training, quantization, ImageNet, RL, and forecasting; widens stable learning-rate regions with reduced divergence.

problem: Finetuning pretrained generative control policies requires expensive online experience collection; existing exploration relies on weak baselines.
approach: DF-ExpEnse leverages multimodal policy to create expressive candidate set; ensemble of critics identifies actions balancing quality with exploration interest; enables cross-agent communication in fleet settings.
contribution: Consistently improves finetuning sample-efficiency across manipulation and locomotion tasks compared to default and alternative baselines.

problem: Survey-based opinion elicitation relies on fixed questionnaires and static respondent sets, failing to adapt to partial responses across rounds.
approach: Proposes adaptive information elicitation framework jointly selecting queries and respondents based on information gain maximization; combines graph neural networks for imputation with information-theoretic criterion.
contribution: Achieves 12% relative improvement on CES at 10% respondent budget for population-level response prediction.

problem: Image-to-3D generation under occlusion lacks mechanisms to complete unseen regions while strictly preserving observed parts, requiring distinct control granularities.
approach: RelaxFlow decouples control granularity via Multi-Prior Consensus Module and Relaxation Mechanism; theoretically proves relaxation is equivalent to low-pass filtering on generative vector field.
contribution: Successfully steers unseen-region generation to match text intent while preserving visual fidelity; introduces ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D benchmarks.

problem: Standard conformal prediction breaks under domain shift in LLMs, leading to under-coverage and unreliable prediction sets despite finite-sample guarantees.
approach: DS-CP reweights calibration samples based on proximity to test prompt within conformal prediction framework, preserving validity while enhancing adaptivity.
contribution: Delivers more reliable coverage under substantial distribution shifts while maintaining efficiency; validated on MMLU benchmark.

problem: Machine learning Hamiltonian models predict orbital/density structures but lack evaluation as energy-force predictors, leaving unclear how well they perform for molecular dynamics.
approach: Proposes QHFlow2 with SO(2)-equivariant backbone and two-stage edge update; directly evaluates energy and forces from predicted Hamiltonians.
contribution: Achieves 40% lower Hamiltonian error with NequIP-level force accuracy and 20× lower energy MAE; demonstrates consistent scaling behavior.

problem: Language models generalize poorly beyond pretraining context lengths due to quadratic attention scaling, limiting long-horizon reasoning despite continued pretraining.
approach: L2A enables conditional token-wise long-range memory access by deciding when to invoke global attention; skips attention for ~80% of tokens via learned gating.
contribution: Extends Qwen context from 32K to 128K tokens with 3% performance loss; achieves 2× throughput and time-to-first-token improvements; enables 50% KV cache reduction.

problem: Graph structural entanglement from spurious correlations contaminates node embeddings, particularly affecting boundary nodes where structural noise blurs decision boundaries.
approach: BES selectively suppresses spurious structural noise at decision boundaries using adaptive contrastive learning GNN plug-in with minimal parameter perturbation.
contribution: Improves GCN performance by 3.3% average in node classification and achieves superior link prediction accuracy.

problem: Scientific data annotation bottleneck remains the last-mile verification and correction, which standard approaches ignore by discarding supervision in expert navigation strategies.
approach: Framework studies behavioral cloning on 9 synthetic annotation tasks simulating realistic human strategies; reveals hierarchical skill emergence and multi-task learning benefits.
contribution: Shows larger models are more data-efficient; multi-task pretraining enables efficient fine-tuning; models learn mistake representation generalizing across tasks.

problem: LoRA's low-rank assumption limits performance by failing to capture duplicated directions and update diversity in fine-tuning.
approach: Proposes LoKRA using Kruskal rank instead of matrix rank to characterize update diversity; LoKRA+ provides tighter theoretical lower bound.
contribution: Consistently outperforms LoRA across LLMs with state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks.

problem: LiDAR-based 3D detectors are vulnerable to adversarial attacks with incomplete disappearance difficult to achieve in physical settings.
approach: OBJVanish uses prompt-driven text-to-3D generation framework iteratively refining object/verb/pose to create LiDAR-invisible pedestrians under physical constraints.
contribution: Consistently evades six SOTA LiDAR detectors in simulation and real-world settings, exposing critical vulnerabilities in autonomous driving safety.

problem: Protein language models lack generalization across domain shifts encountered in real protein engineering campaigns, limiting practical utility.
approach: FLIP2 introduces seven new protein fitness datasets with splits measuring generalization relevant to engineering practice; evaluates suite of models.
contribution: Reveals simpler models often outperform fine-tuned protein language models, challenging utility of existing transfer learning techniques.

problem: Graph neural networks for dynamics modeling suffer from oversmoothing while unitary convolutions overconstraining smoothness despite physical systems requiring natural smoothing.
approach: Proposes relaxed unitary convolutions balancing smoothness preservation with natural smoothing required by PDEs; generalizes from graphs to meshes.
contribution: Outperforms transformers and equivariant networks on PDEs over complex meshes and weather forecasting.

problem: Egocentric video understanding requires maintaining spatial memory of object locations relative to user movement and answering long-horizon queries, which existing models struggle with.
approach: DirectMe incrementally constructs structured spatial memory from streaming egocentric observations, coupling perception with memory updates and spatial reasoning.
contribution: Significantly improves spatial reasoning of leading MLLMs on UCS-Bench with 170+ hours and 8.1K+ timestamped questions.

problem: Open-ended image-to-text generation in continual learning faces catastrophic forgetting when visual data distribution shifts over time.
approach: ECA employs Mixture of Query module for task-specific adaptation, Fisher Dynamic Expansion for structure growth, and embedding dictionary with replay to retain past knowledge.
contribution: Significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting; outperforms baselines on four new IL benchmarks reflecting real-world scenarios.

problem: Auto-bidding algorithms in digital advertising ignore the true marginal value of winning: the outcome difference between winning and losing accounting for organic alternatives.
approach: Models ad value as treatment effect and develops online learning algorithms for second-price auctions that exploit information revealed by payment rule.
contribution: Attains rate-optimal regret under several feedback models with improvement over first-price auction settings.

problem: Multi-agent decision-making over long horizons is complicated by model mismatches and uncertainties, making it difficult to establish equilibrium solutions and effective algorithms.
approach: The paper derives optimal policies via a robust Bellman equation, establishes stationary Nash Equilibrium existence using a set-valued map, and designs two algorithms (Robust Nash-Iteration and robust TD Descent) with convergence guarantees.
contribution: Provides comprehensive theoretical and algorithmic foundations for distributionally robust Markov games with average-reward criterion, including convergence proofs and approximation results from discounted to average-reward settings.

problem: Long-form video understanding is challenging due to complex temporal dependencies and multi-event narratives, with existing methods suffering from high computational cost and suboptimal performance.
approach: Video-MTR reformulates video understanding as dynamic decision-making via reinforcement learning, where an agent iteratively selects key segments based on context, using a gated bi-level reward system combining trajectory-level and turn-level rewards.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on VideoMME, MLVU, LongVideoBench, LVBench, and EgoSchema using only ~8K training samples (vs. 257K-4.4M), with 20× reduction in reasoning overhead.

problem: Current time series foundation models lack evaluation on complex real-world data like astronomical light curves with irregular sampling and heteroskedasticity.
approach: StarEmbed introduces a benchmark of ~40,000 real astronomical observations across seven classes, evaluating TSFMs on clustering, classification, and OOD detection tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates that Chronos achieves state-of-the-art clustering and OOD detection on light curves despite non-astronomical pre-training, establishing a pathway toward universal light curve embeddings.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models struggle to generate complete images within irregular-shaped canvas constraints while preserving semantic integrity.
approach: AnyCanvas converts binary masks into a differentiable potential field via a Mask-to-Potential Field paradigm, guiding content generation without training.
contribution: Achieves 4.23% higher spatial adherence to constraints while maintaining 99.45% semantic fidelity (CLIP score), with robust generalization across model backbones.

problem: Offline goal-conditioned navigation suffers from compounding value-estimation errors over long horizons and dense keypoint requirements, while lacking mechanisms to adapt to topological changes.
approach: Adaptive Quasimetric Mapping learns a time-to-reach quasimetric from data, builds a sparse dominating-set cover of the dataset support, and enables zero-shot replanning by pruning edges based on observed traversal time.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance while requiring up to 100× fewer keypoints than prior approaches.

problem: Chemical LLMs relying on explicit Chain-of-Thought force nonverbal chemical logic into discrete language, creating a modality mismatch that bottlenecks reasoning.
