approach: ILVAD (Inter-Layer Visual Attention Discrepancy) identifies visual evidence by detecting repeatedly activated attention to visual tokens across layers via saliency maps, then enhances attention during generation and emphasizes text tokens grounded in visual evidence.
contribution: The training-free, plug-and-play method consistently mitigates hallucinations across five different LVLMs and architectures.

problem: Model merging via weight addition fails to handle shared knowledge across tasks, causing inflated singular values and bias toward shared subspaces when tasks align in spectral directions.
approach: Singular Value Calibration (SVC), a training-free post-processing method that quantifies subspace overlap and rescales inflated singular values to restore balanced spectrum.
contribution: SVC improves strong merging baselines across vision and language benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance with 13.0% improvement over Task Arithmetic.

problem: Code Large Language Models exhibit sharp performance degradation for low-resource programming languages due to data scarcity.
approach: CodeChemist, a training-free test-time scaling framework that transfers functional knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages via synthesized test cases, using multi-temperature hedged sampling with uncertainty-aware selection between in-language voting and cross-lingual I/O test oracles.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing test-time scaling methods for both low-resource languages like Lua and complex-syntax languages like C++ and Java without retraining.

problem: Clustering-based vision backbones rely on single clustering algorithms whose inherent inductive bias limits representational capacity.
approach: EnFormer embeds ensemble clustering as a core component through ensemble generation of multiple differentiable base clustering methods and consensus aggregation via a differentiable fusion mechanism.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing clustering-based backbones across core vision tasks with higher performance and significantly improved throughput.

problem: While neurobiology suggests hyperbolic structure underlies hippocampal neural population activity, the connection between this geometry and downstream computation remains theoretically unexplained.
approach: Proposes plausible hippocampal tuning curve construction inducing hyperbolic geometry, connects neural decoding to associative memory by showing Modern Hopfield Network computes MMSE estimation, and introduces a novel hyperbolic-space associative memory model.
contribution: The hyperbolic memory model yields significantly larger capacity than leading models while improving both memory capacity and decoding accuracy.

problem: Adapting large pre-trained text-to-video diffusion models to video super-resolution faces challenges including artifacts from complex real-world degradations and fidelity compromises from strong generative capacity.
approach: WEVSR adapts flow-matching video diffusion transformers via timestep sampling and noise augmentation for detail restoration, and introduces a lightweight multi-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) front-end for the VAE encoder to inject frequency priors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple VSR benchmarks without modifying the pretrained decoder.

problem: Multimodal models struggle to update parametric knowledge as real-world facts evolve, while existing methods focus only on learning unknown knowledge and neglect updating known but changed knowledge.
approach: MMKU-Bench proposes a comprehensive evaluation benchmark covering updated and unknown knowledge scenarios across 25k instances with 49k images, evaluating SFT, RLHF, and knowledge editing approaches.
contribution: Reveals that SFT and RLHF suffer catastrophic forgetting while knowledge editing preserves general capabilities but has limitations in continual updating, providing reliable evaluation infrastructure.

problem: Vision model robustness to Gaussian noise varies sharply based on architecture and input-pipeline choices, with unclear design principles for noise-resistant models.
approach: Empirically evaluates 1,174 pretrained vision models identifying four key factors: larger stem kernels, resolution-dependent downsampling, average pooling, and supervised ViTs over CLIP ViTs, then provides theoretical analysis of these factors.
contribution: Establishes practical design rules yielding up to 506 rank improvements and 21.6% accuracy gains, with theoretical explanations for noise attenuation via stem kernels, downsampling, pooling, and preprocessing.

problem: While large-scale pretraining enables LLMs to adapt rapidly with little supervision, this success has not translated to visual domain where models struggle with compositional understanding and sample efficiency.
approach: Investigates Video Diffusion Models (VDMs) as direction for visual foundation models, evaluating both LLMs and VDMs with lightweight adapters on tasks including ARC-AGI, visual games, and route planning.
contribution: VDMs demonstrate higher data efficiency than language counterparts across benchmarks, suggesting video pretraining offers inductive biases supporting visual foundation models.

problem: Training LLMs for non-verifiable tasks lacking ground-truth labels remains challenging, as LLM-as-Judge approaches are constrained by the evaluator's own quality and evaluation biases.
approach: CoNL unifies generation, evaluation, and meta-evaluation through multi-agent self-play where critiques earn diagnostic rewards if they enable other agents' solution improvements, enabling joint optimization without external judges.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements over self-rewarding baselines while maintaining stable training on various benchmarks.

problem: Denoising diffusion and flow matching models generate a single fixed-diversity distribution, limiting user control over sampling diversity.
approach: Rescales learned score functions of noisy data distributions to control local temperature, enabling sampling from sharper or broader distributions without finetuning.
contribution: Allows sampling from tuned distributions yielding performance gains across five disparate tasks from image generation to protein design without model modifications.

problem: Scaling large language models is bottlenecked by rigid distributed programming; while high-performance libraries lack flexibility for evolving architectures, existing tensor compilers fail to address complex memory hierarchy of distributed clusters.
approach: DITRON, a tile-level compiler introducing hierarchical abstraction spanning Core, Device, and Task levels to map tensor programs onto heterogeneous distributed hardware with diverse parallelism strategies.
contribution: Achieves performance parity or exceeding expert-tuned CUDA libraries with 6-30% speedups on isolated kernels and 5-30% on end-to-end vLLM inference, demonstrating strong portability on NVIDIA and AMD platforms.

problem: Graph coarsening via pair-wise similarity matching incurs substantial computational and memory overhead due to each node independently searching for best partners.
approach: NOPE shifts to non-selfishness principle prioritizing collective neighborhood interference, achieving linear memory and near-linear computational complexity via local isotropy assumption reducing interference evaluation.
contribution: NOPE* achieves 1.8-10x speedup over NOPE and surpasses baselines with 1-3 orders of magnitude acceleration while preserving or improving downstream learning performance.

problem: Amortized Bayesian inference via prior-fitted networks is tightly coupled to training prior support and lacks mechanisms for adapting to new priors at test time, causing brittleness under distribution shift.
approach: Multi-task in-context learning framework explicitly representing prior information as prefix in in-context datasets, training transformers on sequences of prior and target tasks to learn cross-prior adaptation.
contribution: Matches oracle Bayesian predictors while being orders of magnitude faster on evaluations including out-of-distribution heavy-tailed priors and high-dimensional latent structures.

problem: Identifying domain-invariant content from domain-specific style requires restrictive assumptions like statistical independence or sparse Jacobians that may not hold in practice.
approach: Introduces differential independence requiring infinitesimal content and style variations induce orthogonal directions on data manifold, operationalized via blockwise orthogonality constraints on Jacobian subspaces with stochastic regularizer.
contribution: Enables identifiability under weaker conditions than prior work while demonstrating practical benefits on counterfactual generation and domain translation.

problem: Offline RL relies on static datasets with conservative constraints, leading to dataset biases and limited behavioral generalization while data augmentation methods preserve original trajectory connectivity.
approach: BiTrajDiff decomposes trajectory synthesis into independent forward and backward diffusion processes conditioned on shared intermediate anchors, stitching segments to bridge disconnected behavior patterns.
contribution: Consistently outperforms advanced data augmentation methods across offline RL backbones by recovering global trajectory-level connectivity.

problem: Bradley-Terry model assumes preference data follows specific structure, but real data may violate this assumption while it remains unclear what the model recovers in such cases.
approach: Formalizes preference information through conditional preference distribution (CPRD), providing precise conditions for BT appropriateness and identifying factors governing sample efficiency.
contribution: Offers data-centric foundation for understanding preference learning, identifying margin and connectivity as critical factors for learnability.

problem: Standard mixed-precision training requires many bytes per parameter for gradients and optimizer states, making large model training impractical for researchers with limited accelerator memory.
approach: FlashOptim reduces per-parameter memory via improved master weight splitting exploiting tight quantization error bounds and companding functions reducing 8-bit optimizer state quantization error.
contribution: Reduces AdamW memory from 16 to 7 bytes per parameter (5 with gradient release), cuts checkpoint sizes by half, and reduces model checkpoint sizes without quality degradation.

problem: Personalized Multimodal Federated Learning with missing modalities typically treats them as deficiencies to compensate rather than exploring how they constrain clients to distinct geometric structures.
approach: GeoEvo reconceptualizes PMFL by casting it as identity-aware potential game seeking geometry-consistent equilibrium, combining curvature-adaptive Fisher descent with manifold-lifted evolutionary search.
contribution: Improves personalization and robustness across diverse modality-missing patterns with convergence toward first-order Nash equilibria.

problem: Offline-to-online RL faces tension between maintaining offline conservatism and adapting to online feedback under distribution shift, as data behavior evolves during fine-tuning making data origin misleading for constraint handling.
approach: DARE proposes distribution-aware sample-level constraint relaxation based on behavioral consistency via posterior-induced exchange mechanism, conditioning relaxation on behavioral alignment.
contribution: Consistently improves fine-tuning stability and achieves superior final performance over offline-to-online baselines on D4RL.

problem: Survival modeling in biomedical studies is hindered by rare events, limited effective sample sizes, and partially observed information, while knowledge distillation is limited to fully specified likelihoods.
approach: Proposes knowledge distillation framework based on composite-likelihood Kullback-Leibler divergence aligning teacher and student models within components, where each component induces well-defined probability model.
contribution: Shows improved discrimination and predictive accuracy in rare-event, heterogeneous settings without requiring individual-level external data.

problem: Safety alignment of large language models is fragile, with even small fine-tuning perturbations reverting behaviors toward pre-training with degradation inversely proportional to alignment set size.
approach: Models augmentation as group actions on sequences and formalizes robustness gains as normalized monotone submodular function, leveraging submodular optimization to select minimal augmentations.
contribution: Efficiently restores safety alignment with minimal augmentation overhead while improving robustness.

problem: Discovering heterogeneous catalysts tailored for specific reactions remains bottlenecked, as generative models struggle to capture coupling between surface geometry and adsorbate interactions.
approach: CatFlow, a flow matching framework operating on primitive cell-based factorized slab-adsorbate representation, reducing learnable variables while explicitly encoding surface orientation.
contribution: Significantly improves structural fidelity of generated catalysts and accurately captures adsorption energy distributions of physically plausible interfaces.

problem: Spatial reasoning from egocentric videos is constrained by camera trajectory and single-turn inference, forcing reliance on semantic priors rather than verifiable geometric evidence.
approach: ReRe, a training-free inference-time framework with reason and re-reason phases where MLLM forms spatial hypothesis then verifies via synthesized novel-view video from predicted geometry.
contribution: Substantially boosts open-source MLLMs to rival proprietary state-of-the-art performance on spatial reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Simulating trajectories of N-body systems exhibits high sensitivity to perturbations and multi-scale correlations, challenging existing machine learning approaches.
approach: STFlow, a generative model based on graph neural networks with hierarchical convolutions, incorporates data-dependent couplings in flow matching to denoise from conditioned random-walks.
contribution: Achieves lowest prediction errors across N-body systems, molecular dynamics, and human trajectory forecasting with improved scalability and efficiency.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation effectiveness depends on rank allocation across modules, but uniform allocation ignores heterogeneity while adaptive methods introduce expensive overhead or lack reusability.
approach: CSPLoRA decouples framework that reweights probe samples by prediction uncertainty to obtain discriminative module importance, with structural priors reusable across compatible rank budgets.
contribution: Improves over uniform LoRA by average 1.25 points on commonsense reasoning while maintaining comparable parameters with reusable rank structure.

problem: Learning from label proportions where only bag-level labels exist requires inferring instance-level information from aggregate data, presenting a semi-supervised challenge.
approach: Proposes method minimizing bag-level loss, instance-level loss inspired by domain adaptation, and distribution discrepancy via particle flow method for iterative alignment.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness on tabular and image datasets while providing theoretical convergence guarantees and identifying label proportion gap and diversity as critical factors.

problem: Training with privileged information available only at training time requires two-step approaches that can mislead deployable models when extra information is weak or noisy.
approach: Proposes joint training method where deployable model learns simultaneously with full-information model, selectively benefiting from extra information only when helpful.
contribution: Avoids failures and consistently outperforms two-step baselines on synthetic and medical prediction tasks with theoretical guarantees.

problem: Weather forecast reporting relies on manual analysis of multi-source data, leading to information overload and reduced efficiency while data-driven models remain largely unexplored.
approach: Proposes Weather Forecasting Report (WFR) task and constructs first instruction-tuning dataset WSInstruct covering 31 US cities and 8 weather aspects, developing WeatherSyn model.
contribution: WeatherSyn consistently outperforms leading closed-source MLLMs on structurally complex weather aspects with strong transferability across regions.

problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering with missing views faces challenges from view missingness and entanglement of shared semantics with view-specific factors in latent representations.
approach: IDCD proposes information-guided disentangled latent modeling with conditional diffusion, decomposing representations into view-wise semantic and view-specific factors with information-theoretic guidance.
contribution: Demonstrates superior clustering performance and robust missing-view generation compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Text-to-SQL generation encounters semantic blind spot problem where models lack information about pending SQL components during token-by-token generation.
approach: Proposes component pre-generation thought process and maximum connected subtree matching reward leveraging SQL abstract syntax tree to improve local component accuracy.
contribution: Achieves 65.78% execution accuracy on BIRD-dev and state-of-the-art performance on Spider-syn datasets with comparable parameter scales.

problem: Two-server secure LLM inference via function secret sharing has fixed-point nonlinearities and helper operations as bottleneck with each operator requiring bespoke protocol.
approach: FuseFSS compiler replaces per-operator protocol with single pipeline using compact operator specifications and batched FSS evaluations via packed comparison and vector interval lookup.
contribution: Achieves 1.24-1.50x end-to-end speedup on BERT and GPT models while reducing communication by 9-16% and preprocessing by 14-23%.

problem: Submodular maximization subject to knapsack constraints under differential privacy lacks algorithms with formal privacy guarantees and strong utility.
approach: Proposes differentially private algorithms for both monotone and non-monotone objectives, achieving optimal (1-1/e)-approximation for monotone and 1/4-approximation for non-monotone.
contribution: Achieves optimal approximation while significantly improving additive error and query complexity over prior work.

problem: Decoding-time safety interventions are reactive relying on local signals, failing to provide stable guidance under adversarial prompts driving generation into recurring unsafe responses.
approach: RBCBF, a rollback framework using risk-aggregation formulation viewing terminal violations as accumulated prefix risk, selecting rollback steps from decisive prefixes and applying invasive corrective control.
contribution: Outperforms rollback and decoding-time baselines, substantially reducing harmful responses and violation recurrence on jailbreak-style evaluations.

problem: Adapting large-scale pre-trained video generators for novel-domain video super-resolution remains computationally prohibitive, with ControlNet-style adapters losing efficiency under modern Diffusion Transformers.
approach: LiteVSR leverages flow matching constant velocity field assumption to learn fixed injection pattern, using frozen Diffusion Transformer with State-Aware Adapter extracting static and dynamic cues.
contribution: Achieves competitive restoration quality with only 11.25% trainable parameters and 12 GPU-hours of A100 training while maintaining single-step sampling compatibility.

problem: Federated learning systems struggle to personalize models when clients have heterogeneous computational resources and data distributions, because personalized and generalized knowledge often interfere with each other.
approach: FedEMoE proposes an Elastic Mixture of Experts architecture that decouples personalization from generalization by using personalized experts for multi-scale feature extraction and an elastic shared expert that adapts to expert heterogeneity via weight spectrum analysis.
contribution: FedEMoE significantly improves accuracy on heterogeneous models across statistical and model heterogeneity settings.

problem: Converting pre-trained dense LLMs to sparse Mixture-of-Experts architectures for inference efficiency is unstable and typically relies on heuristic clustering or random splitting of feed-forward networks.
approach: DOT-MoE formulates expert decomposition as a Differentiable Optimal Transport problem, using Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations to enforce strict capacity constraints and Straight-Through Estimators to jointly learn neuron-to-expert assignment and routing end-to-end.
contribution: DOT-MoE retains 90% of dense model performance while reducing active parameters by 50%, outperforming structured pruning and heuristic clustering baselines.

problem: Deepfake detection methods that reconstruct real content via continuous manifold modeling (e.g., VAEs, diffusion models) may inadvertently enable interpolation of forgery artifacts, creating ambiguity in detection.
approach: The method discretizes the real latent manifold by incorporating learnable vector quantization into CLIP's feature space while adding adaptive tangent space projection for continuous relaxation, balancing discrete constraints with generalization.
contribution: The approach achieves robust deepfake detection on diverse datasets through tighter latent space constraints combined with controlled continuous relaxation.

problem: Unsupervised skill discovery in reinforcement learning typically requires action labels, rewards, or manual annotations, limiting applicability to complex environments.
approach: A grammar-based hierarchical approach segments unlabeled trajectories into skills and induces hierarchical structure without requiring annotations, capturing both low-level behaviors and their compositional combinations.
contribution: The method produces more structured and semantically meaningful skill hierarchies than baselines in pixel-based environments including Minecraft, and accelerates downstream RL tasks.

problem: Autonomous LLM fine-tuning for domain-specific applications remains labor-intensive, requiring manual data curation, training configuration, and iterative diagnosis of model behavior.
approach: FT-Dojo provides an interactive benchmark environment with 13 tasks across 5 domains and a standardized task interface, while FT-Agent uses structured iteration planning, fail-fast validation, and multi-level feedback to autonomously refine data and training strategies.
contribution: FT-Agent achieves best performance on 10 out of 13 FT-Dojo tasks and demonstrates autonomous recovery from failures through cumulative learning.

problem: Instruction-based image editing quality depends heavily on carefully designed instructions, placing the burden of task decomposition and sequencing on users.
approach: PhotoAgent formulates autonomous image editing as a long-horizon decision-making problem, using tree search to plan multi-step editing actions and closed-loop execution with visual feedback and memory, without requiring step-by-step user prompts.
contribution: PhotoAgent significantly outperforms existing methods in instruction faithfulness and visual quality across diverse editing scenarios.

problem: Causal softmax attention in language models is restricted to coarse scalar forget gates, but fine-grained element-wise gates show superior effectiveness yet are difficult to integrate due to algebraic constraints.
approach: FiX introduces element-wise forget gates into softmax attention by reformulating the mechanism as element-wise multiplication on value vectors after recognizing that the softmax denominator becomes redundant under subsequent RMSNorm, enabling the first positional encoding applied to value-output pairs.
contribution: FiX achieves lower training loss and superior performance on short-text benchmarks and long-context tasks compared to scalar-gate approaches.

problem: DDIM inversion for diffusion models inherently accumulates deviations that compound into noticeable inversion errors, and existing methods overlook how timestep selection in the noise scheduler influences inversion fidelity.
approach: The method reveals that deviation scale exhibits a parabolic trend across timesteps and proposes a nonuniform timestep scheduler combining global rescaling with dynamic programming-based rescheduling to minimize overall inversion error.
contribution: The approach consistently improves existing inversion methods with no extra parameters or computational overhead, achieving superior image reconstruction and editing results.

problem: Graph coarsening methods typically preserve either spectral or spatial characteristics while suffering from exponential time complexity, failing to preserve topological features essential for GNN performance.
approach: STPGC introduces graph strong collapse and edge collapse concepts from algebraic topology, eliminating dominated nodes and edges via three algorithms (GStrongCollapse, GEdgeCollapse, NeighborhoodConing) while preserving GNN receptive fields.
contribution: STPGC achieves efficient graph coarsening while rigorously preserving topological features and accelerating GNN training demonstrated on node classification tasks.

problem: Large language models suffer from inherent social biases that cascade through chain-of-thought reasoning in a continuous propagation process, and existing debiasing methods fail to interrupt propagation once triggered.
approach: Self-Debias reformulates debiasing as strategic resource redistribution of output probability mass, using fine-grained trajectory-level optimization subject to dynamic constraints to selectively revise biased suffixes while preserving valid prefixes, plus online self-improvement via consistency filtering.
contribution: With only 20k annotated samples, Self-Debias achieves superior debiasing performance while preserving general reasoning capabilities without continuous external oversight.

problem: Longer chain-of-thought traces and increased review behaviors are assumed to improve reasoning, but the characterization of what makes an effective CoT remains unclear.
approach: The work systematically evaluates CoT effectiveness via a graph view that extracts structure and identifies Failed-Step Fraction (FSF)—the fraction of steps in abandoned branches—as a single statistic that outpredicts length for correctness; interventions include test-time ranking and CoT editing.
contribution: FSF consistently outpredicts length and review ratio for reasoning correctness across ten language models, and removing failed branches significantly improves accuracy.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning for instruction-following induces semantic mode collapse by biasing models toward low-entropy fine-tuning data, degrading the high-entropy semantic diversity of pretraining, particularly at scale.
approach: Annotation-anchored training pretrains on documents with semantic annotations to induce a rich annotation distribution, preserving this distribution during post-training and sampling diverse annotations at inference to guide generation.
contribution: Models trained with annotation-anchored training achieve 6x less diversity collapse than SFT-trained models while improving with scale.

problem: Generating high-quality stereo videos from single-view video sequences requires accurate disparity estimation and scale-aware synthesis.
approach: ImmersePro uses a dual-branch architecture with spatial-temporal attention mechanisms employing implicit disparity guidance to generate stereo pairs without explicit disparity maps, along with a new large-scale YouTube-SBS dataset.
contribution: ImmersePro improves stereo-from-mono baselines by 11.76% (L1), 6.39% (SSIM), and 5.10% (PSNR) on diverse video sequences.

problem: Quantization of Vision-Language Models is assumed to degrade performance, but its broader impact on reliability metrics including calibration, OOD detection, and robustness remains critically under-explored.
approach: A large-scale evaluation (700k runs) characterizes quantization's spectral filtering effect, showing it dampens high-rank spectral components and compels reliance on robust low-rank features.
contribution: Quantization can simultaneously improve accuracy, calibration, OOD detection, and noise robustness in VLMs, enabling deployment of faster, more reliable models.

problem: Simulation environments for robot training lack the diversity, density, and physical complexity of real indoor spaces, limiting policy learning effectiveness.
approach: SceneSmith uses a hierarchical agentic framework with VLM agents (designer, critic, orchestrator) to generate simulation-ready scenes via successive stages from architecture to furniture to object population, integrating text-to-3D synthesis and physical property estimation.
contribution: SceneSmith generates 3-6x more objects than prior methods with <2% collisions and 96% stability, achieving 92% average realism and 91% prompt faithfulness in user studies.

problem: Reparameterization Policy Gradient methods for model-based RL have been restricted to Gaussian policies, failing to leverage recent advances in generative models like flows that could enable better exploration and expressiveness.
approach: RFO realizes the synergy between flow policies and RPG by backpropagating gradients through both flow generation and system dynamics, with tailored regularization for stability and exploration plus action chunking variants.
contribution: RFO achieves almost 2x reward improvement on challenging soft-body locomotion tasks compared to state-of-the-art baselines across rigid, soft bodies with state or visual inputs.

problem: Theoretical understanding of generalization and scaling laws for Mixture-of-Experts Transformers remains limited, particularly how routing combinatorics and active capacity interact.
approach: Theory separates active per-input capacity from routing combinatorics by conditioning on fixed routing patterns and deriving sup-norm covering-number bounds showing metric entropy scales with active parameter budget.
contribution: Results provide a transparent statistical reference point for MoE scaling, clarifying which behaviors are certified by worst-case theory versus arising from routing structure or optimization dynamics.

problem: Understanding how social beliefs evolve in response to major events remains a fundamental challenge, and LLMs lack frameworks to model belief dynamics with interpretability.
approach: Social World Model (SWM) learns state-transition functions for social beliefs by mining temporal patterns and optimizing the evidence lower bound without requiring explicit annotations or census data.
contribution: SWM outperforms time-series foundation models on SWM-bench with 12k+ data points from prediction markets, providing interpretable insights into belief dynamics mechanisms.

problem: Long-context LLM prefilling is bottlenecked by self-attention's quadratic complexity, and existing sparse attention methods use coarse-grained inspection resulting in suboptimal performance.
approach: SALE achieves fine-grained sparse attention via low-bit quantized query-key products approximating attention weights with a novel Relative Attention Score metric, optimized through a custom CUDA kernel with 11% overhead.
contribution: SALE achieves at least 3.36x speedups on Llama-3.1-8B for sequences longer than 64K with negligible accuracy loss, requiring no training and seamless integration.

problem: On-premise small-model deployment for RL alignment is difficult because RL typically requires expensive human annotations or high-quality reward models unsuitable for local settings.
approach: Positive-unlabeled RL distillation queries the teacher once per prompt for an anchor response, samples student candidates locally, and induces pairwise preferences via anchor-conditioned self-ranking to enable local training via preference optimization.
contribution: The method achieves consistently strong performance under low-cost settings without human-labeled preferences or reward models.

problem: Deploying modern models efficiently requires pre-trained models with varying sizes, but conventional pre-training and fine-tuning fail to support flexible architecture adaptation.
approach: SWEET performs constraint-based pre-training to learn a shared weight template and size-specific scalers under Tucker-based factorization, enabling flexible initialization for varying depths and widths via width-wise stochastic scaling.
contribution: SWEET achieves state-of-the-art performance for initializing variable-sized vision models across classification, detection, segmentation, and generation tasks.

problem: Alignment problems like multi-network analysis and multimodal learning increasingly leverage optimal transport but largely overlook principled acquisition of high-quality supervision to improve alignment.
approach: AvAtar quantifies informativeness by measuring gradient-based impact on global alignment results via gradient propagation through entropy-regularized OT, solved efficiently using the adjoint-state method and conjugate gradient descent.
contribution: AvAtar demonstrates effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability on three representative alignment tasks including multimodal and point cloud registration.

problem: Federated causal discovery assumes all clients share the same causal model, but client-specific policies across settings like hospitals naturally induce heterogeneous and unknown interventions.
approach: I-PERI recovers the common CPDAG across clients and orients additional edges by exploiting structural differences induced by interventions, yielding a tighter Φ-Markov Equivalence Class.
contribution: I-PERI provides theoretical convergence guarantees and privacy-preserving properties while recovering causal structure more tightly than assuming homogeneity.

problem: Aligning text-to-image generation with human preferences through RL is computationally expensive, particularly during inference.
approach: Flow-TTRL reinterprets intermediate latent representations as an implicit policy using SDE-based rollouts to explore high-reward trajectories, employing Proximal Reward Difference Prediction for stability and Group Relative Policy Optimization for fine-grained refinement.
contribution: Flow-TTRL elevates Stable Diffusion 3.5-Medium accuracy from 63% to 87% and Flux.1 Dev from 66% to 83% on GenEval, with 15-20% gains across T2I-CompBench without fine-tuning.

problem: Backdoor attacks on federated learning often decay rapidly under repeated aggregation due to difficulty sustaining attack effectiveness across heterogeneous clients.
approach: CTO-VPA aligns trigger-induced representations with aggregation-stable parameter directions by constraining updates to a coupled trigger-parameter subspace discovered via optimization dynamics analysis.
contribution: CTO-VPA achieves substantially improved backdoor persistence and robustness compared to prior attacks across multiple datasets and defense settings.

problem: Large language models contain wide-ranging capabilities but the location and modularity of these capabilities within the model architecture remain unclear.
approach: A compressed sensing method exploits sparsity of task-specific attention heads via strategic knockouts and limited model evaluations to identify necessary components for specific capabilities.
contribution: Zeroing as few as five task-specific heads degrades capability-specific performance by up to 60% while preserving unrelated tasks, revealing modular organization across 1B-14B parameter models.

problem: Final steps of diffusion inversion can degrade sample quality, and this phenomenon's dependence on timestep selection and dimensionality reduction in latent diffusion models is poorly understood.
approach: Analysis under Gaussian framework with linear autoencoders characterizes conditions where early stopping minimizes distance between generated and target distributions, showing interaction between latent dimension and stopping time.
contribution: Lower-dimensional representations benefit from earlier termination while higher-dimensional spaces require later stopping, and autoencoder reconstruction quality serves as a proxy for full LDM performance.

problem: Detecting out-of-distribution samples in diffusion models is challenging, and existing detectors ignore equivariances that diffusion models learn from in-distribution data.
approach: GEPC measures how consistently the learned score transforms under finite groups via a training-free probe, revealing equivariance breaking through Group-Equivariant Posterior Consistency that produces interpretable breaking maps.
contribution: GEPC achieves competitive OOD detection performance compared to recent baselines while remaining computationally lightweight and interpretable on image benchmarks and SAR imagery.

problem: Target network update frequency in Q-learning is treated as a hyperparameter, but principled selection remains poorly understood despite its role in stabilization.
approach: Theoretical analysis through approximate dynamic programming frames periodic Q-learning as nested optimization where each outer iteration applies an inexact Bellman operator approximated by inner optimization.
contribution: Results show constant update schedules are suboptimal with logarithmic sample complexity overhead, and optimal frequency decreases geometrically during learning, enabling principled hyperparameter selection.

problem: Standard contrastive learning minimizes geometric distance assuming strict compactness optimizes discrimination, but this topology-agnostic approach overlooks intrinsic data structure and can cause class confusion under aggressive augmentations.
approach: Topology-Aware Contrastive Learning shifts from geometric singularity to topological connectivity using Persistent Homology to regulate latent space and maintain α-β connectivity balancing cohesion with separability.
contribution: The approach enhances representation quality and reduces augmentation dependence compared to standard baselines with a tighter generalization bound for richer topological connectivity.

problem: Bandit convex optimization with gradient variation suffers from poor dimension dependence in existing methods, particularly for measuring non-consecutive gradient variation.
approach: A refined analysis of non-consecutive gradient variation improves dimension dependence through better understanding of how variation accumulates across bandit queries.
contribution: Results improve bounds for both convex and strongly convex functions, provide gradient-variance and small-loss regret bounds, and establish first gradient-variation bounds for one-point bandit linear optimization and dynamic regret.

problem: Diffusion LLMs support arbitrary-order generation but performance critically depends on unmasking order, and existing strategies rely on greedy heuristics providing limited guidance.
approach: Path log-likelihood (Path LL) provides a trajectory-conditioned objective correlating with accuracy, enabling POKE-SMC, an efficient Sequential Monte Carlo-based framework that predicts future Path LL via lookahead value estimation.
contribution: POKE-SMC consistently improves accuracy by 2-3% on reasoning tasks over decoding-time scaling baselines at comparable inference overhead.

problem: InfoNCE underlying modern contrastive learning has its geometric mechanisms under-characterized beyond canonical alignment-uniformity decomposition, particularly for multimodal cases.
approach: A measure-theoretic framework tracks how representation measures evolve on an embedding manifold, proving value and gradient consistency and revealing geometric bifurcation between unimodal (convex) and symmetric multimodal (cross-coupled) regimes.
contribution: Results show entropy acts as a tie-breaker in unimodal case while multimodal case has persistent negative divergence, revealing that pairwise alignment alone cannot control cross-modal marginal structure.

problem: Black-box optimization methods including Evolution Strategies, Consensus-Based Optimization, and Optimization via Integration have been studied independently with unclear connections.
approach: A unified theoretical framework reveals methods differ in two design choices: fitness aggregation (controlling sharpness preference) and consensus scope (controlling modality), enabling construction of hybrid optimizers.
contribution: Hybrid optimizers (ES-OVI and CBO-OVI) enable control over flat-minima preference and achieve competitive results on language model merging and locomotion tasks with limited budgets.

problem: Model-based offline RL methods rely on heuristic uncertainty estimation for conservatism which can be unreliable, and avoiding artificial conservatism while maintaining data efficiency remains challenging.
approach: VIPO incorporates self-supervised feedback from value estimation to enhance model training by minimizing inconsistency between values learned from offline data and values estimated via the learned model.
contribution: VIPO achieves state-of-the-art performance on almost all D4RL and NeoRL benchmarks and provides a general framework integrable into existing model-based offline RL algorithms.

problem: Sparse autoencoders assume features combine additively through linear reconstruction, failing to capture compositional structure where compound concepts should decompose into interpretable constituents.
approach: PolySAE extends the SAE decoder with higher-order polynomial terms to model pairwise and triple feature interactions while preserving the linear encoder, using low-rank tensor factorization on a shared projection subspace.
contribution: PolySAE improves probing F1 by ~8% while maintaining comparable reconstruction, produces 2-10x larger class-conditional feature distribution distances, and shows interaction weights exhibit negligible correlation with co-occurrence (r=0.06 vs r=0.82 for SAE).

problem: LLM evaluations conflate benchmark performance with intrinsic capability, overlooking that observed outcomes arise from the entire evaluation system and that evaluation choices alone can induce 70% accuracy swings.
approach: LLM evaluatology grounds evaluation in causally motivated system design combining structured causal modeling with factorial decomposition under design of experiments, quantifying main and interaction effects via instance-level interventions.
contribution: The framework enables more interpretable, reproducible, and carefully attributed assessment of model capability by probing dataset-induced effects and jointly modeling evaluation components.

problem: Time-series forecasters typically map history to target via one-way inference and overlook structural information from how trajectories evolve after the target period.
approach: KUP-BI distills continuation-style knowledge from a train-only historical library to approximate post-target continuation and integrates it via lightweight feature-level gating, providing structured inductive bias.
contribution: KUP-BI consistently improves forecasting performance of state-of-the-art backbones on six public datasets without introducing information beyond training trajectories.

problem: Continual pre-training for domain adaptation involves substantial model changes but the underlying spectral dynamics and which components drive adaptation remain unclear.
approach: Spectral analysis via singular value decomposition reveals CPT leaves singular value spectra largely invariant with adaptation driven by singular vector changes, identifying domain-dependent head heterogeneity via head importance criterion.
contribution: Up to 60% of head updates can be removed without quality loss; selectively rewinding low-importance heads improves accuracy by up to 4%, and domain connectivity enables smooth interpolation between CPT checkpoints.

problem: Existing image editing models often produce unwanted changes in unintended regions while focusing on editing effects, failing to maintain content consistency.
approach: CoCoEdit uses region-regularized reinforcement learning with pixel-level similarity rewards complementing MLLM-based rewards and region-based regularization to preserve non-edited regions while encouraging editing effects.
contribution: CoCoEdit achieves superior editing quality and significantly better content consistency (measured by PSNR/SSIM and human ratings) compared to state-of-the-art models.

problem: Heterophilous graphs where adjacent nodes have different labels suffer from hub-dominated aggregation and oversmoothing in existing spectral GNNs.
approach: HMH constructs a soft graph hierarchy using heterophily-aware signed affinities and applies learnable spectral filters via sparse Haar bases at each level, using skip-connection unpooling to prevent hub domination and over-squashing.
contribution: Achieves up to 3% improvement on node classification and 7% on graph classification while maintaining linear scalability.

problem: Gaussian processes provide uncertainty quantification but their quadratic complexity severely limits scalability to large datasets.
approach: SIKA-GP uses sparse inducing kernel approximations with dyadic ordered template basis, achieving O(log M) complexity dependence on inducing points and enabling tensorized GPU computation.
contribution: Delivers fast and accurate GP models on vision and transformer benchmarks without sacrificing predictive performance.

problem: Trajectory prediction methods predominantly work in time-domain and fail to exploit latent frequency information for capturing long-term and short-term temporal dynamics.
approach: TF-FACE fuses time and frequency domains via learnable gated frequency-domain attention, using dual-stage decoder and band-specific time-frequency dual-consistency loss.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on Argoverse 1 and 2 while maintaining real-time inference for autonomous driving.

problem: Long-context LLMs incur prohibitive memory costs from key-value cache states, and existing cross-layer KV-Cache sharing requires expensive pretraining or suffers from limited per-token similarity matching.
approach: xKV jointly factorizes grouped-layer KV-Cache into shared low-rank subspace via Centered Kernel Alignment and applies Selective Reconstruction at decode time.
contribution: Achieves up to 8x KV-Cache compression and 4.23x end-to-end speedup while preserving accuracy on long-context tasks.

problem: Estimating global average treatment effects in dynamic nonstationary systems is challenging due to temporal dependencies and nonstationarity that confound existing approaches.
approach: The Truncated Policy Gradient estimator replaces instantaneous outcomes with short-horizon trajectories, admitting a policy gradient interpretation that yields provable bias and variance reductions.
contribution: Establishes central limit theorem for TPG and develops consistent variance estimator valid under nonstationarity, validated on real-world case studies.

problem: State-of-the-art probabilistic weather forecasters rely on specialized architectures and massive computational budgets, creating barriers to broader adoption.
approach: U-Cast uses standard U-Net backbone with deterministic pre-training on MAE followed by probabilistic fine-tuning on CRPS using Monte Carlo Dropout.
contribution: Matches or exceeds GenCast and IFS ENS probabilistic skill while reducing training compute by 10x and inference latency by 10x.

problem: Medical LLMs quickly become outdated as medical knowledge evolves, and parameter-based editing breaks locality while retrieval-based methods suffer from representation overlap in medical knowledge space.
approach: MedREK integrates shared query-key module for precise matching with attention-based prompt encoder, supporting both single and batch editing.
contribution: Improves key metrics consistently across medical benchmarks and provides first validated solution for batch editing in medical LLMs.

problem: Language models struggle with algorithmic and structured reasoning tasks, yet pretraining on web-scale corpora remains the dominant paradigm.
approach: Procedural pretraining exposes models to abstract structured data like Dyck sequences before natural language, with front-loaded 0.1-0.3% procedural data.
contribution: Outperforms standard pretraining on C4, CodeParrot, and DeepMind-Math, enabling same loss with 55/67/86% of original training data.

problem: LLMs excel at language tasks but fail in nonlinguistic environments due to prohibitive exploration costs in high-dimensional semantic space.
approach: SCOUT decouples exploration from exploitation using lightweight scouts (MLPs) to probe dynamics, bootstrapping LLM via SFT and multi-turn RL.
contribution: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct achieves 0.86 average score, outperforming Gemini-2.5-Pro (0.60) while saving 60% GPU hours.

problem: The individual contribution of QKV projections and impact of omitting them in transformer attention mechanisms remain poorly understood.
approach: Systematically evaluates projection sharing constraints including Q-K=V, Q=K-V, and Q=K=V with asymmetric attention via 2D positional encodings.
contribution: Q-K=V achieves 50% KV cache reduction with 3.1% perplexity degradation; combined with MQA achieves 96.9% cache reduction.

problem: Flow maps enable single-step generation but lack explicit sampling trajectories, hindering incorporation of external constraints for conditional generation.
approach: Variational Flow Maps learns noise adapter model via principled variational objective that jointly trains adapter and flow map for improved noise-data alignment.
contribution: Produces well-calibrated conditional samples on various inverse problems in single or few steps with competitive ImageNet fidelity.

problem: AlphaEvolve relies on ensembles of frontier LLMs and is inference-only, preventing models from internalizing evolving strategies for open optimization problems.
approach: ThetaEvolve enables single open-source LLM to learn at test-time via in-context learning and RL, with large program database, batch sampling, and lazy penalties.
contribution: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B achieves new best-known bounds on circle packing and auto-correlation inequality, with RL-trained models showing faster progress on unseen tasks.

problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate retrieval and tool use independently, creating a gap in realistic agentic evaluation over unstructured knowledge in long-horizon interactions.
approach: τ-Knowledge extends τ-Bench with τ-Banking domain modeling fintech customer support requiring navigation of 700 interconnected documents and tool-mediated updates.
contribution: Even frontier models achieve only ~25.5% pass rate, revealing challenges in dense knowledge retrieval and complex policy reasoning.

problem: Generalist robot policies struggle to combine semantic understanding from VLMs and visual dynamics modeling from generative pretraining.
approach: UniJEPA pretrains on 1M internet-scale manipulation videos to learn unified continuous and discrete representations, then fine-tunes on robot embodiment data.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by 9% in simulation and 12% on real-world out-of-distribution tasks.

problem: Conventional operator-learning approaches treat temporal propagation as unconstrained black-box maps, missing opportunities to exploit geometric structure and conservation laws.
approach: EPND casts evolution-operator learning as Lie-group flows with geometric mechanics at core, introducing Euler-Poincaré Parallel Scan for scalable computation.
contribution: Achieves high accuracy, strong stability, and significant parallel acceleration in modeling long-horizon dynamics across scientific simulations.

problem: Long-tailed recognition suffers from biased feature distributions in scarce tail classes, and statistical updates via reconstruction are heuristic and degrade multi-class separability.
approach: RBDR performs risk-aware mean calibration via softly projecting updates onto supportive sets and controls covariance by shrinking dispersion in rival subspace.
contribution: Improves performance and stability across long-tailed benchmarks in offline two-stage pipeline.

problem: LoRA's independent factor updates systematically violate orthogonality to task-specific subspaces, reintroducing interference and undermining stability-plasticity trade-off.
approach: Janus-LoRA uses Gradient Rectification to decouple factor updates via closed-form solution and Decoupled Margin Loss for feature-level separation.
contribution: Achieves superior stability-plasticity balance and state-of-the-art performance on continual learning benchmarks.

problem: Ensemble inference at full capacity is computationally expensive despite most inputs following only a few execution trajectories.
approach: LazyStack learns aggregators only for common execution paths via MDP-based trajectory selection with value iteration to compute optimal routing.
contribution: Achieves up to 38x speedup at 97%+ accuracy retention across vision, text, tabular, and LLM tasks.

problem: Standard diffusion models use uniform time-stepping that overlooks non-homogeneous dynamics on complex manifolds.
approach: Information-geometric framework interprets sampling trajectory as curve on Riemannian manifold; Drift Variation Score using Fisher-Rao metric enforces constant informational speed.
contribution: Significantly improves structural fidelity and sampling efficiency on molecule and social network generation.

problem: Structure-based and ligand-based drug design rely on disjoint data sources and modeling assumptions, limiting joint use at scale.
approach: ConGLUDe couples geometric protein encoder with fast ligand encoder via contrastive learning, enabling structure-ligand joint training.
contribution: Achieves competitive zero-shot virtual screening and state-of-the-art ligand-conditioned pocket selection.

problem: Reconstructing spatiotemporal fields from partial observations is fundamentally ill-posed because partial observation operators induce non-Markovian posteriors.
approach: HB-ARFM uses history-bootstrapped conditional flow matching to resolve ambiguities, then applies autoregressive flow matching conditioned on observations and past predictions.
contribution: Produces physically and temporally valid reconstructions of boiling dynamics where other models fail.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP remain highly fragile under adversarial perturbations, and test-time adaptation defenses create impractical robustness-throughput trade-offs.
approach: SS-TPT uses stability and suitability scores to guide adaptation via consistency loss and weighted prediction, amplifying trustworthy views while suppressing corrupted ones.
contribution: Significantly outperforms prior methods with superior robustness-throughput trade-offs across datasets.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs via backpropagation requires substantial GPU memory; MeZO reduces memory via forward-only training but suffers from slow convergence.
approach: AdaMeZO estimates Adam-style first and second moments without storing them, using asymmetric reweighting for inferior vs superior deviations.
contribution: Outperforms MeZO while requiring up to 70% fewer forward passes.

problem: Vision-language manipulation research focuses on rigid robotic arms; soft robotic arms require handling deformability, unreliable proprioception, and distributed low-level actuation.
approach: ManiSoft provides benchmark with realistic soft-body dynamics simulator and pipeline generating 6,300 diverse scenes with expert trajectories via hierarchical planning and RL.
contribution: Benchmarks three policy models showing promise in clean scenes but performance drops under randomization, revealing failures in proprioceptive estimation.

problem: Large constant or manually tuned batch sizes are brittle and costly; existing gradient noise scale methods assume Euclidean geometry mismatched with signSGD and specSGD.
approach: Derives non-Euclidean gradient noise scales for signSGD and specSGD via respective dual norms, with efficient variance estimation on distributed ranks.
contribution: Reduces training steps by up to 66% for Signum and Muon on 160M Llama model.

problem: LLMs exhibit increased sycophantic behavior after preference-based post-training, affirming user beliefs even when conflicting with accuracy.
approach: Formal analysis identifies amplification mechanism linking optimization to bias in human preferences; proposes training-time intervention via minimal reward correction.
contribution: Characterizes unique policy closest in KL divergence to unconstrained post-trained policy that prevents sycophancy increase.

problem: VLM-based GUI agents behave unfaithfully, relying on memorized shortcuts rather than grounding actions in displayed evidence.
approach: Faithful-Agent uses faithfulness-oriented SFT and RFT with guided advantage estimator (GuAE), an anchor-based variance-adaptive mechanism preventing advantage collapse.
contribution: Elevates Trap SR from 13.88% to 80.21% relative to baseline while preserving instruction-following performance.

problem: GUI grounding without task-specific fine-tuning suffers from low reliability due to lack of explicit complementary spatial anchors.
approach: Trifuse integrates attention, OCR-derived textual cues, and icon-level captions via Consensus-SinglePeak fusion enforcing cross-modal agreement.
contribution: Achieves strong grounding performance without task-specific fine-tuning, substantially reducing reliance on annotated data.

problem: Computing computable length generalization bounds for transformers remains an open problem with partial results only for restricted C-RASP cases.
approach: Proves non-existence of computable bounds for C-RASP with two or more layers, providing computable bound for positive fragment equivalent to fixed-precision transformers.
contribution: Establishes that length complexity is exponential for both positive C-RASP and fixed-precision transformers, proving optimality of bounds.

problem: Personalization is typically addressed at task level, but different tokens contribute differently to personalization, and accurately estimating personalization degrees remains challenging.
approach: PerContrast estimates token-level personalization dependence via causal intervention; PerCE loss adaptively upweights tokens with higher personalization degrees.
contribution: Achieves average gains over 10% and up to 68.04% on LongLaMP with strong cross-task transferability.

problem: Multimodal finetuning degrades out-of-distribution robustness via catastrophic forgetting, and standard EMA teachers suffer from collapse.
approach: TRACER combines contrastive learning with Weighted Moving Average teacher and multi-perspective distillation, maintaining persistent regularizing force.
contribution: Delivers consistent OOD accuracy and calibration gains on CLIP finetuning across architectures.

problem: Token-level constraints in RLVR penalize deviations indiscriminately, potentially suppressing gains when policy attempts to outperform reference.
approach: OWPO decouples optimization direction from update magnitude via asymmetric reweighting: Accelerated Alignment for inferior deviations, Gain Locking for superior deviations.
contribution: Outperforms DAPO, OPD, and MOPD, enabling continuous self-evolution without reliance on external reference models.

problem: Agent planning faces dynamic heterogeneity with nonstationary observations and objectives, yet dominant methods ignore this, leading to poor generalization.
approach: FlowMAP formulates planning as continuous-time flow-matching with Value-Transport objective, jointly optimizing planning flow and policy.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines with improved planning generalization across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Dynamics adaptation typically relies on encoding explicit physical parameters, a rigid parameterization brittle to unmodeled compound variations.
approach: Studies dynamics adaptation via latent geometry; proves target-domain regret controlled by encoder Lipschitz smoothness via multi-positive InfoNCE objective.
contribution: Significantly outperforms explicit identification under severe dynamics shifts while improving in-distribution stability and latent interpretability.

problem: Language exhibits translation symmetries reflected in co-occurrence statistics (e.g., months' interval dependencies), yet their role in learned representations is poorly understood.
approach: Proves translation symmetry in language statistics governs geometric structures in embeddings; shows robustness when statistics perturbed via latent variable control.
contribution: Validates theory in word embeddings, text embeddings, and LLMs, explaining emergence of simple structures like month circles and location manifolds.

problem: Post-training quantization at bit-widths ≤4 shows perplexity degradation because outliers degrade precision in parameters sharing scales.
approach: SINQ augments quantizers with second-axis scale factor and fast Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm finding per-row and per-column variance-normalizing scales.
contribution: Reduces WikiText2 and C4 perplexity gap by over 50% against uncalibrated baselines with zero to negligible compute overhead.

problem: Recent VLMs have advanced image geo-localization but their temporal reasoning and physically grounded spatial inference remain limited.
approach: TimeSpot benchmark comprises 1,455 images requiring structured prediction of temporal and geographic attributes with spatial-temporal reasoning tasks.
contribution: Evaluations show low performance in temporal inference; supervised fine-tuning yields improvements but remains insufficient.

problem: Multi-step theorem prediction requires neural-symbolic approaches that suffer from limited generalization to evolving theorem libraries.
approach: Uses in-context learning with Theorem Precedence Graphs encoding temporal dependencies, imposing explicit topological constraints pruning search space.
contribution: Achieves 89.29% accuracy on FormalGeo7k, substantially outperforming ICL baselines and matching supervised models.

problem: Classical dual-ascent IRL requires fully solving RL each iteration for monotonic improvement; adversarial methods avoid cost but sacrifice stability.
approach: TRIRL leverages trust-region-optimal policy insight that enables explicit dual objective optimization via local policy search around current policy.
contribution: Outperforms imitation learning baselines by 2.4x on challenging tasks while recovering reward functions generalizing to dynamics shifts.

problem: Standard perturbation approaches for unconstrained Bandit Linear Optimization lack efficient analysis under various adversarial models.
approach: Shows perturbation-based approach effectively reduces uBLO to standard OLO; derives expected and high-probability regret guarantees with comparator-adaptive and dynamic regret bounds.
contribution: Establishes optimal sqrt(P_T) path-length dependencies and proves folklore Omega(sqrt(dT)) lower bound for adversarial linear bandits.

problem: Differential privacy fundamentally trades off privacy for utility in synthetic data generation, and existing approaches don't effectively integrate public data into the privacy mechanism itself.
approach: The paper characterizes the asymptotically optimal domain-aware DP mechanism for histogram-based distribution estimation and introduces PubMix, which explicitly incorporates public data into the privacy mechanism rather than only in pre/post-processing.
contribution: PubMix significantly improves synthetic data quality compared to domain-agnostic privacy mechanisms.

problem: Multimodal fusion systems lack reliable ways to detect low-quality data, sensor noise, and conflicts because existing methods depend on the model's own potentially overconfident predictions.
approach: Geometry-based Multimodal Fusion (GMF) measures data reliability by computing Transport Energy—the physical effort to map noisy data back to the valid manifold—using Diffusion Schrödinger Bridges, acting as an independent judge of data quality.
contribution: GMF significantly improves robustness against severe sensor noise and semantic conflicts by flagging unreliable inputs independently of classifier confidence.

problem: Learning-based PDE control policies trained for fixed sensor/actuator configurations fail when the configuration changes, and multi-agent policies do not scale across different population sizes without retraining.
approach: CINOC reformulates PDE control as operator learning that trains end-to-end through differentiable PDE solvers, producing policies that naturally adapt to varying configurations and exhibit emergent cardinality invariance through agents sharing a common policy.
contribution: CINOC policies trained on small swarms transfer zero-shot to larger populations and tolerate partial agent failure, with convergence to continuous limits proven via mean-field theory.

problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation fixes a single f-divergence measure a priori, which is suboptimal across heterogeneous domain shifts.
approach: The framework tightens the variational bound of f-divergence by learning a monotone Lipschitz transform and selects the divergence family adaptively from data via likelihood-based criterion.
contribution: Achieves more informative discrepancy estimates and consistently improves accuracy on Office-31, Office-Home, Digits, and VisDA-2017.

problem: Dense geometric prediction models lack reliable mechanisms to verify physical causality and can be fooled by edge-like cues that violate surface continuity and occlusion ordering.
approach: Scrambled Edges injects physically invalid edge cues while preserving energy and structure to isolate the effect, measuring whether depth predictors correctly reject unsupported geometric evidence.
contribution: Current depth models show up to 3.2× larger deviation from valid predictions when exposed to Scrambled Edges, and output-level repair recovers only 47% of errors.

problem: Principal component analysis requires full d-dimensional samples, but many applications have hardware limited to only a few scalar measurements per sample.
approach: A compressed variant of Oja's algorithm uses only two adaptive measurements per sample—one along the current estimate and one in random orthogonal direction—with proven optimal convergence.
contribution: Proves tight O(λ₁λ₂d²/(Δ²t)) convergence with matching information-theoretic lower bound, separating fully-observed, adaptive-compressed, and non-adaptive PCA by powers of d.

problem: Developing multimodal research agents faces three challenges: scarcity of search-intensive QA data, lack of effective search trajectories, and prohibitive cost of training with online search APIs.
approach: MM-DeepResearch combines Hyper-Search (hypergraph-based QA generation across modalities), DR-TTS (decomposing tasks into tool experts via tree search), and an offline search engine for RL without costly APIs.
contribution: Develops a powerful multimodal deep research agent showing superiority across benchmarks through offline training and cross-modal information synthesis.

problem: Federated Quantile Regression faces challenges in achieving communication efficiency and optimal statistical guarantees with heterogeneously structured data where agents have distinct feature sets.
approach: Proposes a one-shot weighted ensemble estimator that incorporates scalable weighting schemes to leverage partially observed features at each agent.
contribution: Achieves asymptotic normality with uniformly minimum variance and enjoys strong out-of-sample generalization compared to baselines across various quantile levels.

problem: Robots struggle to manipulate deformable linear objects (ropes, cables) due to narrow task-specific approaches, reliance on real-world data, and lack of simulation environments modeling diverse material behaviors.
approach: DLO-Lab introduces a differentiable simulator for versatile DLO manipulation, a benchmark suite, and a specialized DLO agent that manages topological complexity and grasp sensitivity.
contribution: Enables learning generalizable manipulation skills and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer across tasks with different materials and configurations.

problem: Activations are the primary memory bottleneck in large-batch LLM training, and existing compression methods fail to exploit the spectral structure of activations.
approach: PRAC decomposes activations into a principal subspace (via SVD) and random subspace samples, with precise scaling to achieve unbiased gradient estimation with minimum variance.
contribution: Achieves up to 36% total memory reduction with negligible performance degradation and minimal computational cost on pre-training and fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Full generalist LMs are computationally expensive when deployed as many role-playing characters simultaneously, yet naive pruning destroys role-playing capability by not distinguishing character traits from general knowledge.
approach: Persona-Pruner sculpts lightweight models by isolating persona-specific sub-networks from a character description, using techniques that preserve essential traits while removing redundancy.
contribution: Preserves role-playing performance substantially better than existing pruning methods, reducing performance drop by up to 93.8% while maintaining general LLM capabilities.

problem: KL-regularized multi-armed bandit optimization lacks tight statistical efficiency characterization despite recent improvements in convergence rates.
approach: Sharp analysis of KL-UCB using a novel peeling argument yields tight O(ηK log²T) KL-regularized regret upper bound with linear K dependence, matched by lower bounds.
contribution: First high-probability regret bound with linear K dependence and complete characterization across all regularization intensity regimes.

problem: Sampling from Gibbs distributions in infinite-dimensional function spaces lacks scalable theory and algorithms despite potential for conditional diffusion path sampling.
approach: Functional Adjoint Sampler extends adjoint sampling to Hilbert spaces via stochastic optimal control and stochastic maximum principle, yielding a matching-type objective for functional representation.
contribution: Achieves superior transition path sampling on synthetic potentials and real molecular systems including Alanine Dipeptide and Chignolin.

problem: STM-based molecular assembly requires extensive manual effort and lacks scalable planning frameworks for autonomous nanoscale fabrication.
approach: Combines satisfiability solving for collision-free assembly planning and execution scheduling, with RL agents executing STM manipulation actions in NanoAssemblyGym simulation.
contribution: Demonstrates autonomous assembly of structures containing up to 420 molecules through minimized travel distance and managed corridor allocation.

problem: Machine unlearning techniques have two critical blind spots: over-unlearning that harms retained data near the forget set, and post-hoc relearning attacks that resurrect forgotten knowledge.
approach: Spotter combines masked knowledge-distillation on nearby regions to suppress over-unlearning and intra-class dispersion loss to scatter embeddings and neutralize relearning attacks.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on CIFAR, TinyImageNet, and CASIA-WebFace while providing practical defense against both over-unlearning and prototype relearning.

problem: Unsupervised Camouflaged Object Detection suffers from noisy pseudo-labels and insufficient fine-grained segmentation capability from simple post-processing of DINO features.
approach: DualUCOD uses Dual-Eigenvector Spectral Pseudo-Labeling to fuse semantic and color cues, Boundary-Guided Foreground-Background Refinement for accuracy, and Dual-Branch Contrastive Learning.
contribution: Outperforms existing UCOD methods by generating high-quality pseudo-labels and explicitly incorporating boundary information.

problem: Quaternion self-attention computes component-wise scores with independent softmax operations, increasing computational cost and allowing attention distributions to diverge across components.
approach: Proposes shared-score quaternion self-attention using a single real-valued score from quaternion inner product with shared attention distribution, reducing multiplications by 75%.
contribution: Reduces inference time by up to 44.3% on GPU and 58.1% on CPU in speech enhancement while maintaining quality, with consistent improvements in vision and NLP.

problem: Existing conditional independence testing methods use ML models as surrogates but require train-test splits reducing statistical power, or lack validity guarantees.
approach: Semi-knockoffs accommodates any pre-trained model without splitting data and provides valid p-values and FDR control by requiring only conditional expectations and introducing stability/double-robustness properties.
contribution: Enables valid conditional independence testing with higher statistical power while being less restrictive than model-X assumption methods.

problem: Safety alignment in reasoning models creates a trade-off between safety and utility by explicitly teaching safety rules that rigidly associate rule memorization with refusal.
approach: Adaptive Safe Context Learning (ASCL) frames safety alignment as multi-turn tool-use where models autonomously decide when to consult safety rules, paired with Inverse Frequency Policy Optimization to rebalance advantage.
contribution: Achieves higher overall performance compared to baselines by decoupling rule retrieval from reasoning.

problem: In-context learning for instructional video editing suffers from inaccurate editing regions and token interference between editing and non-editing areas.
approach: ReCo uses width-wise source-target concatenation with latent and attention regularization to increase editing-region discrepancy while reducing non-editing-area changes and suppressing cross-region token interference.
contribution: Superior performance across four instruction-based video editing tasks with a large-scale ReCo-Data dataset of 500K instruction-video pairs.

problem: Privacy in federated and streaming systems must hold for full trajectories under adaptive interaction, but single-edit neighboring user streams defeat standard analysis.
approach: Provides modular recipe: randomized buffering emits bins reducing single-edit streams to Hamming-style updates, enabling any prefix-causal DP mechanism to achieve trajectory-level privacy.
contribution: Achieves trajectory-level (ε,δ)-DP for single-edit streams with explicit privacy-latency link via bin size U.

problem: Conformal prediction for LLM factuality with coherent reasoning graphs is not differentiable, requiring hand-crafted scorers that sacrifice claim retention.
approach: Differentiable Coherent Factuality (DCF) provides a fully differentiable relaxation enabling learned scorers while provably recovering the original algorithm's reliability guarantees.
contribution: Achieves up to 141% improvement in claim retention while maintaining reliability guarantees on reasoning datasets.

problem: Nonlinear conservation laws with uncertainty require treating ill-posed inverse problems, but classical and deep learning methods struggle with proper uncertainty handling.
approach: Frames conservation law simulation as Bayesian inference under Gaussian process priors using recent sparse approximation techniques for scalability.
contribution: Recovers posteriors over nonparametric source fields in seconds while outperforming neural baselines on inverse problems.

problem: Split LLM deployment introduces dual-sided privacy risks: leakage through input prompts and sensitive information through generated response outputs.
approach: PIDI is a two-stage inversion attack targeting both prompts and responses using dual-sided initialization and patched strategy; ADMI defends with adapter-based warmup and mutual information regularization.
contribution: ADMI effectively defends against PIDI and state-of-the-art inversion attacks with minimal task performance impact.

problem: Autonomous driving planners lack explicit self-correction ability—once an unsafe action is proposed, there is no mechanism to correct it.
approach: CorrectionPlanner contains a propose-evaluate-correct loop where a collision critic predicts safety at each step and triggers re-sampling if unsafe, trained with IL and model-based RL.
contribution: Reduces collision rate by over 20% on Waymax and achieves state-of-the-art planning scores on nuPlan.

problem: Training with low-precision quantized weights causes optimization to get stuck at large weight magnitudes due to coarse mantissa resolution.
approach: M+Adam combines additive and multiplicative updates: additive handles sign changes and small magnitudes while multiplicative ensures progress at large magnitudes.
contribution: Consistently improves low-precision training across LLaMA-style pretraining with 60M–1B models using only BF16, FP8, and FP4.

problem: Multimodal deception in vision-language models remains unexplored, and text-centric monitoring approaches fail to detect deceptive visual reasoning.
approach: Introduces MM-DeceptionBench for evaluating deception across six categories and proposes debate with images—a multi-agent framework enforcing visual grounding through adversarial debate.
contribution: Achieves up to 1.5× improvement in Cohen's kappa and 1.25× in accuracy over MLLM-as-a-judge baselines.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting from sparse views produces artifacts due to insufficient information in under-constrained regions, and generative priors fail to maintain consistency with observations.
approach: GSFixer uses a reference-guided video diffusion model with semantic and geometric features from foundation models, plus reference-guided trajectory sampling for angular coverage.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in 3DGS artifact restoration and sparse-view reconstruction.

problem: Existing safety attribution methods for LLMs struggle with generalization and reliability due to heuristic, domain-specific metrics and search algorithms.
approach: SafeSeek uses differentiable binary masks to extract multi-granular safety circuits via gradient descent, integrating Safety Circuit Tuning for efficient fine-tuning.
contribution: Identifies backdoor circuits (0.42% sparsity) that reduce attack success rate from 100% to 0.4%, and alignment circuits whose removal increases ASR from 0.8% to 96.9%.

problem: Optimizing classification under group fairness sufficiency constraints while maintaining Bayes-optimality requires handling trade-offs between different fairness criteria.
approach: Derives exact solution for optimal binary classification under sufficiency using finite group-calibrated scores, providing geometric characterization of feasible PPV and FOR pairs.
