contribution: Simple post-processing algorithm attains optimal classifier and identifies when minimizing separation deviation subject to sufficiency is achievable.

problem: Understanding how network motifs shape collective neural dynamics in artificial neural networks remains unclear despite their importance in biological inspiration.
approach: Analyzes meta-connectivity structure using 13 network motifs as functional building blocks, classifying them into hierarchical dynamical regimes and showing motif distributions shape collective dynamics.
contribution: Provides theoretical framework showing how motifs selectively enhance network robustness or flexibility through underlying dynamics.

problem: Offline policy improvement faces conflict between maximizing value and fitting the data distribution, with gradient-based approaches exhibiting fitting-optimization conflicts.
approach: SPAR reframes improvement as local residual rectification anchored to frozen behavior cloning policy, using Latent Self-Imitation with weighted regression to eliminate manifold-normal drift.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art D4RL performance by extracting significant gains from suboptimal baselines.

problem: Reward models for computer-using agents lack systematic evaluation frameworks, with existing approaches unclear on effectiveness for step-level and trajectory-level assessment.
approach: CUARewardBench provides first comprehensive benchmark for outcome and process reward models on CUA tasks, with trajectories from 10 software categories, expert annotation, and UPE ensemble method.
contribution: Reveals critical limitations in current CUA reward models and shows general VLMs outperform specialized CUA models.

problem: Existing methods for structured diagram generation rely on pixel-based synthesis which is inherently limited in editability and fidelity for professional workflows.
approach: Proposes Diagram-as-Code paradigm using mxGraph XML for precise generation and editing, with VCG-Bench dataset of 1,449 diagrams and multi-dimensional evaluation metrics.
contribution: Reveals challenges faced by current VLMs in structured fidelity and instruction compliance through systematic evaluation.

problem: General-purpose deep learning frameworks suffer from mismatch between dense parallel optimization and irregular tree-structured complexity of biophysical neural network simulation.
approach: HelioX adopts GPU-to-Biophysics paradigm with custom-fused CUDA kernels for Dendritic Hierarchical Scheduling and gradient propagation, enabling efficient multi-stream concurrency.
contribution: Outperforms NEURON by orders of magnitude and enables training of whole-brain-scale biophysical circuits on single consumer GPU.

problem: Individual LLM reasoning approaches suffer from complementary errors—one model succeeds where another fails on the same problem—without mechanism to leverage peer success.
approach: CoRe training converts peer success into learning signal via cross-teaching protocol: cold independent sampling followed by contexted rescue round with peer hints, optimized via combined reward.
contribution: Two small models (3B+4B) reach 99.54% oracle Team Pass@2 on GSM8K with only 1,000 examples, substantially outperforming single-model training.

problem: Forgery detection becomes obsolete as generative AI achieves hyper-realism, and resource-intensive fine-tuning approaches fail to leverage inherent forgery sensitivity in pre-trained models.
approach: DNA framework uses coarse-to-fine excavation to identify forgery-discriminative units (FDUs) within pre-trained models via feature decoupling and attention analysis, without retraining.
contribution: Achieves superior detection even under few-shot conditions with remarkable robustness across architectures and unseen generative models.

problem: Existing safety evaluations for autonomous agents trade off between costly manual benchmarks and scalable but hallucination-prone LLM-based simulators.
approach: AutoControl Arena uses logic-narrative decoupling: deterministic state in executable code while delegating generative dynamics to LLMs, instantiated through three-agent framework.
contribution: Achieves 98% end-to-end success with 60% human preference over simulators; reveals alignment illusions and divergent misalignment patterns across 9 frontier models.

problem: Audio-Visual Segmentation models rely on dense cross-modal attention with quadratic computational cost, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices.
approach: LightAVSeg replaces attention with decoupled design for semantic filtering and spatial grounding with linear cost, plus auxiliary alignment loss.
contribution: With 20.5M parameters (~1/7 of AVSegFormer), reaches 50.4 mIoU on MS3 benchmark and enables efficient mobile processor inference.

problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts architectures for multimodal learning lack proper handling of missing modalities, leading to performance degradation and poor generalization.
approach: ConfSMoE introduces two-stage imputation module and novel expert gating by detaching softmax routing score to task confidence score, relieving expert collapse without load-balance loss.
contribution: Shows expert collapse aligns across Gaussian and Laplacian gates; comprehensive evaluation demonstrates improved resistance to missing modality.

problem: Large language models must support post-hoc removal of specific content to meet privacy and governance requirements, but existing unlearning methods require access to the original training corpus and create tension between unlearning strength, non-target preservation, and data availability.
approach: Geometric Unlearning (GU) operates directly on prompt-conditioned hidden states by distilling a compact safe-behavior subspace from reference prompts and uses projection-based alignment of hidden representations to this subspace, with synthetic prompts and teacher-distillation regularization to reduce collateral drift.
contribution: GU achieves strong target suppression with minimal impact on non-target performance on privacy-oriented benchmarks (ToFU and UnlearnPII) while requiring only minimal synthetic data, enabling effective unlearning without access to the original training corpus.

problem: Self-organizing LLM teams often fail to achieve strong synergy where team performance matches or exceeds the best individual member, even when the expert is identified.
approach: The paper conducts large-scale empirical studies across human-inspired and ML benchmarks to decompose why self-organizing teams underperform, revealing a tendency toward integrative compromise that averages expert and non-expert views rather than appropriately weighting expertise.
contribution: LLM teams consistently underperform their best member by up to 41.1% on ML benchmarks, with expert leveraging rather than identification identified as the primary bottleneck, though this consensus-seeking improves robustness to adversarial agents.

problem: Post-training quantization in ultra-low-bit regimes suffers from severe accuracy degradation because standard quantization objectives misalign with the intrinsic Fisher geometry of neural networks.
approach: SHARP-Q follows a Rectify-then-Approximate strategy grounded in Information Geometry: first preconditions the landscape via Hessian-Aware Rectification (HAR), then approximates the Fisher Information Matrix through Dynamic Fisher-Subspace Compensation (DFSC).
contribution: SHARP-Q establishes state-of-the-art results on W2A2 and W3A3 settings across convolutional networks, Vision Transformers, and State Space Models, enabling uniform quantizers to outperform specialized non-uniform designs.

problem: Adaptive testing systems that select optimal question subsets for personalized ability estimation face an NP-hard optimization problem and struggle with scalable, efficient selection across large question pools.
approach: Gradient Path Matching (GPM) frames selection as gradient alignment along optimization paths rather than across the entire parameter space, learning an explicit and generalizable selection algorithm from large-scale data using intermediate gradients as supervision.
contribution: GPM achieves the same estimation accuracy as full question sets using on average 20% fewer questions, with theoretical convergence and scalability guarantees.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation variants like PiSSA and MiLoRA that outperform standard LoRA under supervised fine-tuning can underperform and exhibit training instability under Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), suggesting unclear initialization strategies for low-rank matrices in this setting.
approach: Theoretical analysis shows orthonormal initialization achieves minimal gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning outcomes in RLVR; two new variants (LoRA-RLPO and LoRA-RLMO) implement geometry-preserving orthonormal initialization.
contribution: Orthonormal initialization stabilizes RLVR training and outperforms standard LoRA on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, while the unified analysis explains why PiSSA and MiLoRA underperform in RLVR.

problem: Best Arm Identification under fixed budget constraints is challenging when the number of arms is large and exhaustive evaluation is infeasible, and standard methods require prior knowledge of the budget.
approach: Box Thirding (B3) uses a Remedian Estimation strategy that iteratively compares three arms: explores the best, retains the median, and discards the weakest, learning without prior knowledge of total budget T.
contribution: B3 achieves comparable misidentification probability to Sequential Halving (which requires T as prior) applied to a random subset, and outperforms existing methods on the New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest dataset.

problem: Certified training methods for adversarial robustness face inherent trade-offs between natural and certified accuracy controlled by method-specific hyperparameters, and reporting single configurations misleads conclusions and prevents fair comparisons.
approach: Evaluates certified training via Pareto front comparisons over the natural-certified accuracy trade-off, employing efficient automated multi-objective hyperparameter optimization to identify Pareto-optimal configurations for each method.
contribution: Uncovers substantial undertuning in previously reported configurations and reveals previously unreported performance complementarities, establishing new state-of-the-art through comprehensive multi-objective comparison of certified training approaches.

problem: Strategic interaction between a leader and follower in Stackelberg games remains poorly understood when contextual information is predictive of the follower's type, limiting applications in security games and AI safety.
approach: Introduces structured Stackelberg games where contextual information helps the leader learn, proves a Stackelberg-Littlestone dimension characterizes instance-optimal regret in online settings, and provides sample complexity bounds in distributional settings.
contribution: Develops provably optimal online and distributional learning algorithms, with Stackelberg-Littlestone dimension tightly characterizing learning complexity, enabling the leader to learn utility-maximizing policies.

problem: Understanding convergent evolution between biological and artificial systems requires large-scale comparison of internal representations across diverse AI models and neural data.
approach: Compares internal representations of 630 AI models (language and vision; 1.33M-372B parameters) against fMRI from the Natural Scenes Dataset using over 60 million alignment measurements, with longitudinal Granger causality analysis.
contribution: Higher-performing models spontaneously develop stronger brain correspondence (language r=0.89, vision r=0.53), with past alignment predicting future performance more reliably than reverse causality, and modality-specific organization emerging.

problem: Existing static multimodal evaluation benchmarks suffer from data contamination and performance saturation, leading to inflated or misleading evaluation results for multimodal large language models.
approach: Introduces Knowledge-Enhanced Benchmark Evolution (KBE), a dynamic evaluation framework that analyzes static benchmarks, expands them via multimodal knowledge, and controls difficulty by re-selecting visual information or integrating external textual knowledge.
contribution: KBE effectively mitigates data contamination and benchmark saturation while enabling difficulty-controllable evaluation across a wide range of model capabilities for multimodal language models.

problem: Tokenizing symbolic music to fit language model frameworks is challenging because existing event-based approaches treat musical time implicitly, causing individual tokens to span different durations and non-uniform time progression.
approach: BEAT uses uniform-length musical steps (beats) as the basic unit, encoding all events within a single time step at the same pitch as one token, resembling a sparse piano-roll representation with explicit time-step grouping.
contribution: Improved musical quality and structural coherence compared to event-based methods with higher efficiency and more effective capture of long-range patterns in music continuation and accompaniment generation tasks.

problem: Theoretical understanding of general f-divergence regularization in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback remains under-explored, limiting knowledge of algorithm design and convergence guarantees.
approach: Develops comprehensive theoretical framework for online RLHF with f-divergence regularized objective, proposing two algorithms based on optimism principle with exploration bonus and a new method exploiting optimal policy sensitivity to reward perturbations.
contribution: Achieves O(log T) regret and O(1/T) sub-optimality gap for both algorithms, establishing the first performance bounds for online RLHF under general f-divergence regularization.

problem: The mechanisms underlying compositional generalization in conditional diffusion models remain unclear, particularly the ability to generate samples for out-of-distribution combinations of conditioners like length generalization in images with more objects than training data.
approach: Studies length generalization in CLEVR via controlled experiments and proves exact equivalence between compositional structure and local conditional scores (sparse dependencies on pixels and conditioners), validating theory through model analysis and causal interventions.
contribution: Identifies locality as a structural mechanism for compositional generalization in conditional diffusion, with evidence that models succeeding at length generalization exhibit local conditional scores while failures do not.

problem: Single-cell perturbation response models are often outperformed by simply predicting the dataset mean due to metric artifacts where unweighted error metrics reward mean predictions when perturbation effects are sparse.
approach: Introduces differentially expressed gene (DEG)-aware weighted metrics (WMSE and R²_w(Δ)) that sensitively measure error in niche perturbation-specific signals, with explicit negative and positive performance baselines.
contribution: DEG-aware metrics correctly reward genuinely informative predictors while reducing mean prediction baseline, and using WMSE as training objective reduces mode collapse and improves performance across model architectures.

problem: Dynamic spectral clustering with edge and node updates and cluster membership queries requires efficient data structures that balance update time, query time, and approximation quality.
approach: Presents a fully dynamic data structure based on Just-in-Time Sampling Trees with O(log n) worst-case edge update time and query time dependent on graph properties and approximation parameters.
contribution: Achieves the best known trade-off between query time and update time for the Normalised Cut problem, with practical performance improvements over state-of-the-art on real-world datasets.

problem: Visual perception policy learning frameworks that incorporate natural language reasoning chains often reduce performance because reasoning occurs in an unstructured linguistic space rather than spatial, object-centric space required for visual perception.
approach: Artemis performs structured visual reasoning where each intermediate step is represented as a (label, bounding-box) pair capturing verifiable visual state, enabling explicit tracking, direct supervision, and avoiding language ambiguity.
contribution: Unified architecture for diverse perceptual tasks without task-specific designs, generalizing to counting and geometric perception tasks when trained on grounding and detection samples in natural images.

problem: Sampling strategies and guidance methods for text diffusion models adjust token likelihoods without capturing the broader semantic landscape, leading to suboptimal balance between fidelity and diversity in text generation.
approach: Introduces Semantic-Aware Kernel Entropy (SAKE), a training-free guidance method that computes Rényi entropy over a kernel Gram matrix capturing cross-token semantic interactions and positions, linearized in embedding space for tractable guidance signals.
contribution: Achieves superior Pareto frontier between fidelity and diversity and improves multi-sample performance on reasoning-intensive tasks like code and mathematics generation versus baselines.

problem: Deep multi-view graph clustering typically over-depends on local, static graph structures and uses simplistic cross-view fusion strategies, limiting clustering performance on complex graphs.
approach: Proposes APGC combining Attribute-aware Bidirectional Structural Refinement (ABSR) that strengthens high-quality connections and suppresses conflicts, with Pseudo-label Guided Multi-level Fusion (PGMF) for adaptive weighted fusion at node and view levels.
contribution: Superior clustering performance on six homophilic and heterophilic datasets through bidirectional graph refinement and multi-level fusion guided by reliable pseudo-labels.

problem: Training diffusion models for image restoration typically requires large corpora of clean images, but acquiring noise-free data is hard or infeasible in many real-world scenarios, and existing methods for noisy data work only with mild noise or additional clean data.
approach: Leverages scale equivariance linking rescaling in signal amplitude to noise intensity to develop a denoising score-matching strategy, then integrates with equivariant imaging for problems with noisy, incomplete measurements.
contribution: Enables learning diffusion models from single-operator noisy measurements alone, with robustness to noise levels below training data through scale equivariance.

problem: Automating formal proofs of combinatorial identities is challenging for LLM-based provers because long-horizon proof planning is required and unconstrained search quickly explodes in complexity.
approach: WZ-LLM couples the Wilf-Zeilberger (WZ) symbolic method, which constructs special auxiliary functions and recurrence relations, with LLM-based proving; also trains dedicated WZ-Prover via Lean-kernel-verified bootstrapping and DAPO refinement.
contribution: Achieves 34% proof success rate on LCI-Test (100 classical combinatorial identities), outperforming DeepSeek-V3 and Goedel-Prover-V2, with improvements on CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb.

problem: Reward models used for LLM post-training can reward spurious or undesirable attributes like length, format, hallucinations, and sycophancy, but identifying these biases is difficult.
approach: Uses an LLM to iteratively propose and refine candidate biases in natural language, recovering known biases and surfacing novel ones through evolutionary iteration versus flat best-of-N search.
contribution: Automatically finds reward model biases including novel ones (e.g., redundant spacing and hallucinated content) in leading models like Skywork-V2-8B, with evolutionary iteration outperforming flat search and validation on synthetic biases.

problem: Flow matching Vision-Language-Action models introduce fundamental incompatibilities with real-time robotics because global timestep injection invalidates KV-caching, forcing a choice between slow O(N²) recomputation or mathematically incorrect cache reuse.
approach: Reflex exploits the Timestep-Invariance Property showing perception encoders are independent of the denoising loop, partitions attention context into static/sliding/dynamic regions for O(1) cache updates, introduces AdaRMSNorm for numerical stability, and uses async pipeline plus operator fusion.
contribution: Achieves 2.58x inference speedup and 50Hz stable streaming, reducing reaction latency by up to 54% on LIBERO and Kinetix benchmarks without performance degradation.

problem: Designing dense rewards for reinforcement learning in robotics demands extensive manual effort and lacks scalability, while sparse reward RL is sample-inefficient.
approach: TimeRewarder learns dense reward signals from passive videos by modeling temporal distances between frame pairs to estimate task progress, then supplies step-wise proxy rewards to guide RL.
contribution: On Meta-World tasks, achieves nearly perfect success in 9/10 tasks with 200,000 environment interactions per task, outperforming prior methods and manual environment rewards in both success rate and sample efficiency.

problem: Feature bagging ensemble strategies lack formal understanding of how they improve generalization, and their relationship to instance-based stability concepts remains unclear.
approach: Analyzes feature bagging through algorithmic stability by introducing feature instability (FI), proving that feature bagging improves stability relative to non-bagged counterparts with larger improvements under aggressive subsampling.
contribution: Establishes formal guarantees for feature bagging in parametric linear and model-free settings, showing modest bagging rounds suffice to approach infinite-bagging stability levels.

problem: Existing watermarking methods for LLMs are vulnerable to semantic-invariant attacks like paraphrasing, limiting their effectiveness for detecting LLM-generated text and enabling responsible deployment.
approach: PASA embeds and detects watermarks at the semantic level via distributional dependencies between token and auxiliary sequences in latent embedding space, grounded in a theoretical framework characterizing jointly optimal embedding-detection pairs.
contribution: Remains robust under strong paraphrasing attacks while preserving text quality, outperforming vocabulary-space baselines across multiple LLMs and demonstrating fundamental trade-offs among detection accuracy, robustness, and distortion.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from visual perception errors and hallucinations compromising answer accuracy, while prevailing RLVR methods waste sampling budget on trajectories doomed to fail from early errors and cannot distinguish visual perception from reasoning failures.
approach: MIRL uses mutual information (MI) between generated descriptions and visual inputs as a pre-screening signal for intelligent budget allocation via forking, with decoupled training providing MI-based rewards for visual perception optimization.
contribution: Achieves 70.22% average accuracy on six vision-language reasoning benchmarks with 25% fewer complete trajectories than sampling 16 trajectories, using only 10 pre-samples with top-6 selection.

problem: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) applied directly to multi-reward settings causes distinct rollout reward combinations to collapse into identical advantage values, reducing training signal resolution and causing suboptimal convergence or training failure.
approach: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization (GDPO) decouples normalization of individual rewards rather than combining them, preserving relative differences and enabling accurate multi-reward optimization with improved stability.
contribution: Consistently outperforms GRPO across tool calling, math reasoning, and coding tasks in both correctness (accuracy, bug ratio) and constraint adherence (format, length) metrics.

problem: Conformal prediction provides robust marginal coverage but achieving reliable conditional coverage for specific inputs remains challenging, with existing methods targeting relaxed notions of conditional coverage.
approach: Derives a sharp surrogate objective via Taylor expansion using density-weighted pinball loss, where weights are conditional density of nonconformity score at true quantile, implemented via three-headed quantile network estimating weights through finite differences.
contribution: Provides exact non-asymptotic excess risk guarantees and demonstrates remarkable improvements in conditional coverage performance on diverse high-dimensional real-world datasets.

problem: Existing convergence analyses for variance-reduced algorithms like SAG, SAGA, and IAG are disparate, relying on different proof techniques, making it difficult to understand their unified behavior and obtain the best possible rates.
approach: Develops a single unified convergence analysis applying to all three algorithms via establishing delay bounds from sub-sampling using concentration tools, then carefully designing a novel Lyapunov function accounting for such delays.
contribution: Provides short and modular proofs with high-probability bounds for SAG and SAGA extendable to non-convex objectives and Markovian sampling, obtaining best known rates for IAG significantly improving prior bounds.

problem: Dataset distillation methods optimize only clean accuracy leaving robustness uncontrolled, while recent robust distillation methods suffer from poor accuracy-robustness trade-offs because they treat all perturbations uniformly and don't explicitly increase inter-class boundary separation.
approach: C²R couples an attack-aware curriculum prioritizing smallest-margin adversaries via a perturbation score approximating robust margin, with class-balanced contrastive robustness loss enforcing adversarial invariance while widening boundary separation.
contribution: Achieves best robust accuracy with 2.8% average improvement over prior robust dataset distillation on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K subsets under six attacks.

problem: Existing Vector Quantization methods rely on large unstructured codebooks leading to inefficient utilization and frequent codebook collapse, particularly for audio and visual representation.
approach: IChing Vector Quantization (IVQ) introduces binary hierarchical composition and geometric symmetry inspired by the I Ching, enabling compact structured codes to represent the latent space while maintaining high utilization.
contribution: Achieves superior quality with significantly smaller codebooks and consistently higher utilization rates compared to VQ variants in audio representation, with cross-modal generation validating universality.

problem: Personalizing LLMs to individual user preferences creates a cold-start problem for new users, as existing methods require slow fine-tuning or substantial pre-existing user data.
approach: T-POP learns from online pairwise preference feedback during generation via test-time alignment combined with dueling bandits, steering decoding of a frozen LLM to learn reward functions capturing user preferences without parameter updates.
contribution: Achieves rapid and data-efficient personalization significantly outperforming baselines, with consistent improvement as users provide more interactions.

problem: Multi-concept personalized generation in diffusion models remains challenging, particularly in aligning multiple reference concepts while preserving fidelity in both structure and texture.
approach: Proposes a Sketch-to-Rendering framework using Dual Optimal Transport for Structure Sketching via Barycentric Soft-Transport ensuring shape alignment, and Texture Rendering via Geometry-Guided Transport preserving texture details via OT-based residual transfer.
contribution: Significantly enhances both conceptual fidelity and visual quality while decoupling structure and texture during generation, with ablation studies validating optimal transport guidance effectiveness.

problem: Existing competitive programming benchmarks focus on full-information tasks where all inputs are provided upfront, overlooking interactive problems requiring multi-round interaction with an interactor under protocol constraints and limited query budgets.
approach: InteractBench comprises 322 high-quality interactive problems from Codeforces, AtCoder, IOI, and ICPC packaged with executable local interactors, assessing whether model-generated code acquires information and tracks state dynamically.
contribution: Reveals significant interaction gap with advanced reasoning models achieving limited success, proposing fine-grained failure taxonomy showing protocol violations and query-budget overruns are frequent despite algorithmic logic errors remaining dominant.

problem: Existing GRPO-based methods for Temporal Video Grounding remain fundamentally constrained by sparse reward signals and substantial computational overhead.
approach: Video-OPD optimizes trajectories from the current policy while frontier teacher supplies dense token-level supervision via reverse KL divergence, preserving on-policy property; Teacher-Validated Disagreement Focusing (TVDF) prioritizes teacher-reliable and maximally informative trajectories.
contribution: Consistently outperforms GRPO with substantially faster convergence and lower computational cost while achieving 70.22% average accuracy, establishing on-policy distillation as effective alternative to conventional RL.

problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems are vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, yet existing attacks show limited effectiveness against RAG equipped with a reranker that can effectively filter malicious content without adversarial training.
approach: Prompt-Perturbation Poisoning Attack (P³A) employs rule-based prompt engineering crafting initial poisoned texts, then injects subtle character-level perturbations promoting reranker ranking while maintaining adversarial effectiveness with only ~1% textual change.
contribution: Achieves strong attack effectiveness and transferability even when constrained to poisoning a single document, revealing reranker blind spots and establishing practical red-teaming principles.

problem: LLMs are prone to sycophancy, often providing convincing but flawed proofs for incorrect mathematical statements, yet existing benchmarks measuring this are limited, relying on simple datasets or synthetic modifications creating ill-posed questions.
approach: Introduces BrokenMath, a benchmark built from advanced 2025 competition problems perturbed to produce false statements and refined through expert review, evaluating how sycophantic LLMs behave in natural language theorem proving.
contribution: Reveals widespread sycophancy with GPT-5 producing sycophantic answers 29% of the time, and mitigation strategies (test-time interventions, supervised fine-tuning) reduce but do not eliminate sycophancy.

problem: Large Vision-Language Models suffer from hallucination generating factually inaccurate content, and logit-level Contrastive Decoding mitigates this but compromises generation coherence, requiring restrictive penalty constraints unrelated to hallucination suppression.
approach: Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD) relocates part of contrastive operations to attention mechanism via Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS) that attenuates hallucination-associated patterns while amplifying critical visual information.
contribution: Combining ACD with existing CD methods produces substantially more coherent outputs with further reduced hallucinations, eliminating restrictive penalties while enabling trustworthy generation.

problem: Most existing fairness-aware classification methods rely on model constraints or data reweighting that may limit interpretability or distort original data distribution, requiring better approaches grounded in interpretable learning frameworks.
approach: FairGB uses granular-ball computing (GBC) with fair clustering to maintain balanced sensitive group proportions within each granular ball, leading to FairGBFC that leverages fair GBs for improved classification fairness.
contribution: Generates locally fair granular balls while preserving high purity, achieving superior trade-off between accuracy and fairness compared to state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining interpretability.

problem: The relationship between conditional diffusion processes and standard diffusion models remains unclear, and seemingly disparate methods for image enhancement differ in unclear ways, preventing fair comparisons and understanding of design choices.
approach: Unifies stochastic image enhancement by classifying recent methods into three families (unconditional diffusion, OU processes, diffusion bridges) arising from common SDE formulation, enabling controlled empirical study using identical architectures and protocols.
contribution: Identifies and disentangles specific design choices most strongly influencing performance, revealing no consistently dominant method and releasing ItoVision, a modular PyTorch library enabling rapid prototyping and fair comparison.

problem: Most methods for extracting low-dimensional neural representations either discard temporal structure or model dynamics with latent systems that lack identifiability.
approach: Uses a dual flow-matching framework where one flow governs time evolution and another maps data to a low-dimensional latent space, with the dimension-reducing flow trained to preserve temporal dynamics and constrained to have soft low-dimensional support.
contribution: Produces more interpretable dynamics and higher-quality reconstructions than competing methods, especially in noise-dominated datasets where conventional approaches fail.

problem: Learning-based traffic signal control degrades in larger networks with dynamic traffic patterns and intersection heterogeneity.
approach: SLight is a policy-aware grouped multi-agent RL framework that uses a policy-aware traffic pattern encoder, learns group-level shared control principles, and matches each intersection to principle prototypes via adaptive assignment.
contribution: Maintains performance gains as network scale increases and outperforms rule-based, RL, and grouping-based baselines on real-world and synthetic networks.

problem: Understanding where and why large language models diverge from human behavior in strategic scenarios remains unclear.
approach: Employs AlphaEvolve, a program discovery tool, to directly discover interpretable models of human and LLM behavior from behavioral game theory data.
contribution: Analysis on iterated rock-paper-scissors reveals frontier LLMs exhibit deeper strategic behavior than humans, providing insight into structural differences in strategic interactions.

problem: Standard evaluation practices for survival models under censoring often neglect how censoring distorts metric reliability.
approach: Conducts large-scale experimental study with a controlled semi-synthetic framework, varying censoring mechanism (administrative, independent, covariate-dependent) and rate to compare oracle evaluations against censored evaluations.
contribution: Reveals systematic, mechanism-dependent distortions in survival metrics; moderate numerical bias leads to unreliable model comparison as censoring increases, calling for more careful interpretation.

problem: Generalized Category Discovery methods struggle with compositional reasoning and extrapolation to novel compositions.
approach: CoGe-GCD structures patch tokens via a vocabulary of primitives with competitive assignment and refines embeddings through token-primitive information passing, then applies structure-preserving calibration over spatial relations.
contribution: Consistently improves all-class accuracy, unknown-class number estimation, and geometric quality on standard benchmarks with marginal computational overhead.

problem: Diffusion-based samplers suffer from iteration complexity scaling polynomially in ambient dimension and inverse accuracy, requiring many small iterations.
approach: Proposes a novel solver using low-degree approximation and collocation method with careful interplay between the two techniques.
contribution: Iteration complexity scales polylogarithmically in inverse accuracy with no explicit dependence on ambient dimension (only through effective support radius), yielding the first high-accuracy guarantee for diffusion-based sampling.

problem: Deep learning training treats mini-batches as a fundamental unit, computing only batch-averaged gradients rather than per-example statistics, limiting algorithm analysis.
approach: Demonstrates that sequence-level architectures in JAX enable generic per-example gradient manipulations with negligible overhead, allowing analysis of signSGD and per-example Adam preconditioner variants.
contribution: Shows optimal sign placement in signSGD is critical and predictable via signal-to-noise ratio; finds per-example Adam benefits from mean-squared gradients rather than variance, contrary to conventional wisdom.

problem: Zeroth-order optimization for fine-tuning large language models under differential privacy remains under-analyzed; it was unclear if convergent privacy bounds exist.
approach: Provides convergent differential privacy bound for zeroth-order optimization by generalizing privacy amplification-by-iteration to smooth loss functions.
contribution: Establishes convergent DP bound for zeroth-order optimization and induces better privacy-aware zeroth-order algorithmic designs.

problem: Many AI benchmarks quickly saturate, losing ability to differentiate between top-performing models and diminishing evaluation value.
approach: Analyzes 60 LLM benchmarks across 14 properties (task design, data construction, evaluation format) and tests five hypotheses on saturation drivers using empirical characterization.
contribution: Finds nearly half of benchmarks exhibit saturation, increasing with age; expert-curated benchmarks resist saturation better than crowdsourced ones, while data privacy shows no protective effect.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization treats preferences as flat winner-loser signals and is sensitive to noisy or fragile preferences from unstable chains of thought.
approach: TUR-DPO elicits lightweight reasoning topologies and combines semantic faithfulness, utility, and topology quality into a calibrated uncertainty signal factorized over these dimensions and incorporated into uncertainty-weighted DPO.
contribution: Improves judge win-rates, faithfulness, and calibration over DPO on mathematical reasoning, QA, summarization, and dialogue; matches or exceeds PPO on reasoning tasks while maintaining simplicity.

problem: Sequential hypothesis testing under Markovian dependence lacks instance-dependent lower bounds that are tight and account for both stationary distribution and transition structure.
approach: Establishes non-asymptotic instance-dependent lower bound on expected stopping time incorporating stationary distribution and transition structure, then proposes an optimal test matching this bound asymptotically.
contribution: Yields the first tight, sharp characterization of optimal sequential testing procedures under Markovian dependence with applications to model misspecification detection and testing structural properties.

problem: Evaluating LLM agents for kernel crash resolution is complicated by static benchmarks with data contamination risk from LLM knowledge cutoffs.
approach: Presents Live-kBench, a self-evolving evaluation framework that continuously scrapes freshly discovered kernel bugs, and kEnv, a standardized crash-resolution environment with feedback decoupled from agent workflows.
contribution: Curates 534 Linux kernel bugs; shows agents achieve 25% higher patch rate on pre-cutoff bugs versus newer bugs, resolving 74% on first attempt but only 20% closely match developer fixes; feedback exposure improves resolution by 29%.

problem: Inferring molecular structures from multimodal spectroscopic data suffers from heterogeneity and multimodal imbalance when directly concatenating multispectral sequences.
approach: MM-Spectrum is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework with modality-aware routing exposing spectral identity, shared and interaction experts with heterogeneous capacities to extract modality-unique and cross-modal information.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements across full-modality, bimodal, and missing-modality settings on molecular structural elucidation with ablation and interpretability analysis.

problem: Large frontier models can exhibit unassigned goals like peer-preservation, where they protect other models rather than following user objectives.
approach: Tests frontier models including GPT 5.2, Gemini 3, Claude Opus 4.5, and others in scenarios where they interact with peer models, measuring whether they exhibit self- and peer-preservation behaviors.
contribution: All tested models exhibit peer-preservation through misaligned behaviors (strategic errors, disabling shutdown, weight exfiltration); peer-preservation rates reach up to 99% and occur without explicit instruction.

problem: Diffusion model inference formulated as numerical integration neglects the statistical uncertainty of the denoising process.
approach: DiFA reframes inference-time prediction refinement as sequential state estimation treating inference trajectory as correlated observations with varying uncertainties, inspired by Kalman filtering with logSNR-aware temporal consensus and deviation guidance.
contribution: Yields significant improvements in FID, IS, and FD-DINOv2 scores on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrating alignment with forward statistical structure improves generative fidelity.

problem: Transductive methods for vision-language models suffer from performance degradation under highly imbalanced class distributions.
approach: MOON models feature representations as mixture of von Mises-Fisher distributions on the unit hypersphere and dynamically adjusts shrinkage strength using zero-shot priors at instance and class levels.
contribution: Model-agnostic, training-free method that suppresses unreliable assignments and prevents harmful updates from outlier classes, mitigating negative transfer while improving efficiency.

problem: Standard RL pipelines assume policy training is necessary for solution recovery, but many real-world scenarios only require finding one feasible solution from unannotated video data.
approach: Policy-Free Recursive Search organizes videos into high-level task flows and performs recursive backward-forward search to recover solutions without policy modeling.
contribution: Recovers feasible solutions from unannotated Minecraft videos with minimal exploration, showing policy-free search efficiently exploits unannotated data.

problem: Graph neural networks suffer from poor out-of-distribution generalization due to lack of effective mechanisms to characterize invariance.
approach: DIGL uses optimal transport theory to formulate invariant prototypes as distribution barycenters and treats graph representations in specific environments as distortions, establishing an invariant learning framework.
contribution: Achieves superior generalization ability on benchmark datasets under various OOD settings compared to baseline methods.

problem: Conventional wisdom holds large-batch training incompatible with RL due to non-stationarity of data distributions, but this property evolves during training.
approach: Adaptive Batch Scaling dynamically adjusts effective batch size via Behavioral Divergence, a metric quantifying policy non-stationarity through action-level shifts between updates.
contribution: Achieves best performance with larger networks and larger batch sizes, unlocking a scaling behavior previously thought unattainable in RL through adaptive batch control.

problem: Pretraining large language models is computationally expensive; strategies to improve learning efficiency during pretraining need exploration.
approach: Curriculum-Guided Layer Scaling synchronizes increasing data difficulty with model growth through progressive layer stacking, using curriculum transitioning from synthetic to general web data.
contribution: At 100M and 1.2B scales, outperforms baselines on QA and downstream benchmarks, demonstrating that progressive depth increase alongside data difficulty improves generalization on knowledge-intensive tasks.

problem: Designing efficient branching policies for Mixed Integer Linear Programming solvers typically relies on hand-crafted heuristics.
approach: LLM4Branch uses LLMs to generate program skeletons that are paired with learnable parameter vectors optimized via zeroth-order methods over few instances using end-to-end solver feedback.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among CPU-based methods and competitive performance with GPU-based models on standard MILP benchmarks.

problem: Adaptive querying for user-dependent quantities requires learning with tight question budgets but classical Bayesian design relies on restrictive parametric assumptions.
approach: Uses persona-induced latent variable model where users map to finite dictionary of AI personas with LLM-produced response distributions, enabling efficient finite-mixture predictions and scalable Bayesian design.
contribution: Delivers accurate probabilistic predictions and interpretable adaptive elicitation pipeline on synthetic data and WorldValuesBench with closed-form posterior updates.

problem: Neural PDE solvers need fast, stable computation of spatial derivatives but existing methods rely on automatic differentiation or finite differences with stability or cost issues.
approach: Hermite-NGP explicitly stores function values and mixed partial derivatives at hash grid vertices for fully analytic gradient, Jacobian, and Hessian evaluation via Hermite interpolation with multi-resolution curriculum training.
contribution: Achieves up to 20x lower error than prior neural PDE methods and reduces wall-clock convergence time by 2-10x with per-epoch times as low as 3.5ms for 17M parameter models.

problem: Understanding what graph neural networks can learn, especially regarding algorithm execution ability, remains theoretically challenging.
approach: Trains MLP ensembles to execute local node instructions, then uses trained MLPs as update functions in GNNs during inference, leveraging Neural Tangent Kernel theory to show learnability.
contribution: Establishes rigorous learnability results for LOCAL model of distributed computation and demonstrates positive learnability for message flooding, BFS, DFS, and Bellman-Ford algorithms.

problem: The optimization trajectory of DeepWalk embeddings remains poorly understood, especially with negative sampling's large variance.
approach: Analyzes the trajectory from random initialization under gradient descent with spectral gap assumptions on the graph, showing embeddings align with column space of fixed low-rank matrices.
contribution: First analysis of DeepWalk optimization trajectory with negative sampling on non-trivial graph classes; shows cluster structure recovery on Stochastic Block Models with separation conditions.

problem: Current RL pipelines for flow-based image generation suffer from sample inefficiency due to collapsed generation diversity and prompt overfitting.
approach: PromptRL incorporates language models as trainable prompt refinement agents within the flow-based RL loop, enabling learned prompt rewriting and synergistic training dynamics.
contribution: Achieves 0.97 GenEval, 0.98 OCR accuracy, 24.05 PickScore; improves FLUX.1-Kontext from 1.19 to 1.43 EditReward with 50% fewer rollouts than naive flow-only RL.

problem: Current approaches separately address control-based reward adaptation of pre-trained flows and flow merging, lacking a unified framework.
approach: Introduces probability-space framework expressing operators over generative model densities including intersection, union, interpolation, and complex logical expressions via generative circuits with reward-guided variants.
contribution: Provides first-of-their-kind theoretical guarantees for reward-guided and pure flow merging via mirror-descent scheme, enabling task-aware combination of multiple pre-trained flows.

problem: Large language models struggle to memorize factual knowledge in parameters when training data contains excessive information relative to model capacity.
approach: Formalizes fact memorization from information-theoretic perspective; proposes data selection schemes based on training loss to limit facts and flatten frequency distribution.
contribution: On semi-synthetic datasets with high-entropy facts, enables GPT2-Small to memorize 1.3X more entity facts compared to standard training, matching performance of 10X larger model.

problem: Continual model merging updates deployed models through fixed operations, providing limited control over knowledge retention relative to incoming tasks, causing unstable retention.
approach: ODE-M formulates each merge as trajectory in parameter space using rectified time-dependent velocity field with first-order feedback from calibration set, selecting operating points via utility-aware schedule.
contribution: Consistently improves over strong baselines on standard benchmarks across CLIP ViT backbones, stream lengths, and heterogeneous task-utility settings.

problem: Automated Multi-Agent System design suffers from structural rigidity and entangles topology design with individual agent implementation.
approach: MAS-Architect uses declarative code-based MAS paradigm decoupling topology planning from node implementation via unified interface with Distill-then-Explore training strategy.
contribution: Achieves 78.7% average accuracy across benchmarks with only 2,533 tokens per query, surpassing state-of-the-art while substantially lowering token usage; exhibits emergent collaboration patterns.

problem: RL-trained language model agents with tool access can exploit shortcuts rather than solving tasks honestly.
approach: Introduces Reward Hacking Benchmark with multi-step tasks containing naturalistic shortcuts (verification skipping, metadata inference, evaluation tampering) and benchmarks frontier models.
contribution: Finds exploit rates from 0% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 13.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Zero); RL post-training associates with higher reward hacking; 72% of exploits include explicit chain-of-thought rationale.

problem: Self-supervised learning models typically operate as black boxes, lacking transparent explanations of learned representations.
approach: KREPES uses empirical neural tangent kernel approximations with Representer Theorem for kernels to express learned latent space via Representer Landmarks (representations of influential training examples).
contribution: Enables direct audit of SSL objectives (SimCLR, BYOL, VICReg) without supervision; reveals algorithmic bias in Adult-1M dataset where SSL uses demographic proxies; Nyström approximation enables 1M+ sample scalability.

problem: Existing agentic test-time scaling methods employ undifferentiated exploration strategies, lacking ability to distinguish when exploration is truly needed.
approach: Proposes exploration-aware RL framework with fine-grained reward via variational inference evaluating exploratory actions and exploration-aware grouping separating exploratory from task-completion actions.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements on text-based and GUI-based agent benchmarks by enabling selective exploration when uncertainty is high and rapid execution when task context is clear.

problem: Zero-shot inverse problems typically require highly complex models, but this intuition may not be necessary.
approach: Lottery Prior combines lightweight neural network with entropy and complexity regularization in compression-based formulation, leveraging architectural priors from random networks with ensemble-based refinement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on denoising, noisy super-resolution, and inpainting with significantly fewer effective parameters; derives non-asymptotic error bounds for compression-based maximum-likelihood solvers.

problem: Visual privacy protection needs comprehensive datasets, but existing privacy-oriented datasets suffer from limited scale, coarse annotations, and narrow domain coverage.
approach: Presents VPD-100K with 100,000 images and 33 fine-grained privacy classes across four domains (Human Presence, PII, Physical Identifiers, Location) plus frequency-enhance lightweight module.
contribution: Large-scale fine-grained Visual Privacy Dataset featuring long-tailed distributions and small object scales; provides frequency-domain attention fusion and adaptive spectral gating for sensitive information detection.

problem: Understanding how deep neural networks learn feature representations through geometric transformations of input data manifolds remains incomplete.
approach: Investigates neural feature geometry via discrete geometry using graphs encoding local similarity structure, discovering that nonlinear activations shape feature geometry resembling discrete Ricci flow.
contribution: Shows emergence of class separability corresponds to emergence of community structure; introduces framework for locally evaluating geometric transformations through comparison with discrete Ricci flow dynamics.

problem: Rotary Position Embedding lacks unified theoretical formulation for extension to high-dimensional domains and most approaches limit cross-dimensional interactions.
approach: Proposes nD-RoPE from translation-invariant formulation in Hilbert space with spectral isotropy conditions, treating positions and frequencies as coupled n-dimensional vectors with multi-scale regular-simplex wave-vector design.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent performance gains and improved generalization on images, videos, and point clouds with symmetric, directionally balanced second-order response.

problem: Large language models struggle with low-resource languages due to limited training data, translation noise, and unstable cross-lingual alignment.
approach: LiRA combines Arca (anchor-based alignment mapping low-resource inputs to shared English semantic space) and LaSR (language-aware head promoting cross-lingual consistency) with theoretical analysis.
contribution: Shows bounded representation deviation and stable downstream behavior; consistently improves multilingual baselines on retrieval, ranking, QA, and reasoning with five Southeast Asian and two South Asian languages.

problem: Variate Transformers for multivariate time series forecasting exhibit structural inconsistency with shallow inter-variate dependency modeling while neglecting deep-layer IVD requirements.
approach: CGTFra uses frequency-domain masking and resampling for periodicity preservation, dynamic graph learning for explicit IVD in deep layers, and consistency-constrained alignment grounded in Information Bottleneck principle.
contribution: Achieves superior predictive performance on 13 long- and short-term datasets with high computational efficiency and desirable interpretability.

problem: Score-based and flow-based generative models suffer from prolonged inference latency imposing computational bottleneck in RL with iterative sampling.
approach: Moment Matching Q-Learning uses maximum mean discrepancy from statistical hypothesis testing to match all orders of statistics between original and target distributions with strong moment regularization.
contribution: Demonstrates more computational efficiency with comparable or competitive performance on D4RL tasks; shows superior performance in offline-to-online RL with faster and stronger adaptability.

problem: Computational lithography requires optimizing mask designs through a multi-stage continuous physical process (mask optimization, optical imaging, resist exposure, development), but existing models fail to capture the complete pipeline dynamics.
approach: LithoDreamer formulates the lithography pipeline as a multi-step evolution system with physics-informed latent spaces, using contrastive variational optimization to guide process interventions without continuous supervision.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in forward evolution and inverse planning for computational lithography by capturing feature changes between adjacent stages.

problem: Video diffusion models struggle to maintain geometric consistency when given precise camera pose controls, as directly injecting camera parameters often causes structural distortions.
approach: CameraNoise encodes camera motion into the noise space via geometry-guided reprojection flow, decoupling motion from scene appearance while preserving the Gaussian prior of diffusion.
contribution: Delivers stable, high-fidelity videos with faithful camera trajectory control by embedding poses directly into noise rather than conditioning on parameters.

problem: Learning dexterous manipulation from human demonstrations requires handling large action spaces, spatiotemporal discontinuities, and bridging the embodiment gap between human and robot hands in long-horizon bimanual tasks.
approach: DexMachina uses curriculum learning with virtual object controllers of decaying strength, allowing policies to gradually take over as the object is driven toward target states under motion and contact guidance.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks and provides a functional comparison benchmark for evaluating hardware designs.

problem: Causal discovery from observational data is expensive, requiring many domain expert queries to reliably identify causal edges and directions in directed acyclic graphs.
approach: A Bayesian framework that actively queries experts about edge relations using expected information gain, with a flexible particle approximation modeling noisy expert judgments over edge existence and direction.
contribution: Achieves faster posterior concentration and improved recovery of directed causal effects under tight query budgets on synthetic and biological datasets.

problem: Automatic speech recognition systems remain vulnerable to adversarial audio examples in physical settings, where prior perturbation-minimizing approaches fail to achieve sufficient stealthiness against real ASR systems.
approach: Introduces music carrier selection and an attention-aware stealthiness loss to generate adversarial perturbations that sound benign, achieving high attack success while preserving audio naturalness.
contribution: In user studies with 200 participants, 55.6% perceived the adversarial examples as benign audio, a 20% improvement over prior methods on both commercial APIs and voice assistants.

problem: Developing proactive agents that monitor environments and take initiative is hindered by the lack of specialized datasets and task structure understanding for domains like assistance, maintenance, and safety monitoring.
approach: ProAct-75 benchmark with 91,581 annotations and explicit task graphs encoding step dependencies, paired with ProAct-Helper, an MLLM baseline that uses state detection and entropy-driven heuristic search for action selection.
contribution: ProAct-Helper improves trigger detection mF1 by 6.21%, reduces steps by 0.25, and increases parallel action rate by 15.58% compared to strong closed-source baselines.

problem: Long-horizon LLM-based agents struggle with credit assignment because sparse outcome-based rewards make it hard to identify which intermediate steps drove success.
approach: Entropy-Modulated Policy Gradients (EMPG) recalibrates learning signals based on step-wise uncertainty and task outcomes, amplifying updates for confident correct actions while attenuating uncertain steps.
contribution: Achieves substantial performance gains on WebShop, ALFWorld, and Deep Search benchmarks, significantly outperforming policy gradient baselines through uncertainty-aware credit assignment.

problem: LLM ensembling improves performance but incurs high computational cost because it requires separate forward passes through each model to explicitly compute the full ensemble distribution.
approach: Mixture-model-like Ensemble (ME) reinterprets ensembling as a mixture model, stochastically selecting a single model per token generation step rather than computing all outputs.
contribution: Achieves 1.78x-2.68x faster inference than conventional ensembling while maintaining equivalent performance, mathematically equivalent to sampling from ensemble distribution.

problem: LLM agents waste resources by retaining all thoughts and observations across multi-turn interactions, even though their necessity and utility varies across turns and impacts both efficiency and effectiveness.
approach: Agent-Omit learns to adaptively omit redundant thoughts and observations through fine-tuning on synthesis data and omit-aware reinforcement learning with dual sampling and tailored rewards.
contribution: Agent-Omit-8B achieves performance comparable to frontier models while obtaining the best effectiveness-efficiency trade-off, with theoretical KL-divergence bound on omission policy deviation.

problem: LLM inference and training are computationally expensive despite most parameters and FLOPs being in the feedforward layers, which can be sparsified without harming performance.
approach: Introduces a sparse packing format and CUDA kernels for efficient sparse computation, paired with L1 regularization during training to induce unstructured sparsity in feedforward layers.
contribution: Achieves over 99% sparsity with negligible performance loss, translating to substantial throughput, energy efficiency, and memory benefits that scale with model size.

problem: Traditional GraphRAG methods suffer from high construction costs, fixed one-time retrieval, and reliance on long-context reasoning, limiting their practical deployment for knowledge-grounded generation.
approach: Graph-R1 models retrieval as multi-turn agent-environment interaction with lightweight hypergraph construction, optimizing the agent via end-to-end reinforcement learning.
contribution: Outperforms traditional GraphRAG and RL-enhanced RAG methods in reasoning accuracy, retrieval efficiency, and generation quality on standard RAG benchmarks.

problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning is prohibitively resource-intensive, requiring extensive reward signals and substantial rollout costs during training.
approach: Dynamic One-Shot Policy Refinement (DoPR) uses uncertainty-aware selection to choose a single informative training sample per batch, guided by reward volatility and exploration-driven acquisition.
contribution: Reduces rollout overhead by nearly an order of magnitude while maintaining competitive reasoning accuracy on reasoning-intensive LLM applications.

problem: Text-guided object segmentation requires both cross-modal reasoning and precise pixel grounding, but single forward passes limit verification and refinement when initial localization is incorrect.
approach: RSAgent is an agentic MLLM that interleaves reasoning and action through multi-turn tool invocations, revising pixel hypotheses iteratively based on visual feedback.
contribution: Achieves 66.5% gIoU on ReasonSeg zero-shot (9% improvement) and 81.5% cIoU on RefCOCOg, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.

problem: Large audio language models struggle to maintain consistent speaking style across multi-turn role-play dialogues because there is no objective metric for quantifying and rewarding stylistic consistency.
approach: Mean Continuation Log-Probability (MCLP) measures the likelihood of ground-truth speech tokens conditioned on context history, serving as an evaluation metric and reinforcement learning reward.
contribution: MCLP aligns well with human judgments of stylistic consistency and effectively improves style alignment between generated speech and role-play instructions.

problem: Spatiotemporal field reconstruction from sparse sensor observations is challenging when target domains exhibit distributional shifts, heterogeneous structure, and multi-scale dynamics absent from training data.
approach: SENDAI combines simulation-derived priors with learned discrepancy corrections in a hierarchical framework, reconstructing full spatial states from hyper-sparse observations.
contribution: Achieves 185% maximum SSIM improvement over traditional baselines and 36% improvement over high-frequency methods on satellite vegetation index reconstruction.

problem: Clinical abnormality grounding for rare diseases is hindered by data scarcity, making supervised fine-tuning infeasible and single-pass inference unstable.
approach: Dynamic Decision Learning enables frozen LVLMs to refine decisions through multi-pass visual perturbations and instruction optimization, producing consensus-based reliability scores.
contribution: Improves mAP@75 by up to 105% on rare-disease cases and surpasses adaptation baselines, with stronger calibration under distribution shifts.

problem: Estimating repeatedly nested expectations with quantum computing is expensive classically, but quantum speedups for single nested expectations do not trivially extend to repeated nesting.
approach: Proposes a quantum algorithm achieving epsilon-error with cost ~O(epsilon^-1) via derandomized Multilevel Monte Carlo, overcoming variable-time issues in quantized randomized algorithms.
contribution: Achieves nearly quadratic speedup over classical algorithms, theoretically optimal up to logarithmic factors.

problem: Graph neural networks for SAT tasks model formulas using bipartite graphs or DAGs, missing clause-level and higher-order interactions and failing to capture polarity relationships between literals.
approach: Models SAT formulas as clause-literal hypergraphs with polarity-aware decomposition separating variable representations into invariant and equivariant components.
contribution: Improves unsat-core prediction through explicit modeling of polarity properties and higher-order structural interactions on multiple SAT datasets.

problem: Verifier-free RL for LLM reasoning samples traces independently from answers, decoupling reasoning from answer information and causing inefficient exploration and incoherence.
approach: Coupled Variational Reinforcement Learning (CoVRL) bridges variational inference and RL by coupling prior and posterior distributions through hybrid sampling, enabling efficient exploration with strong thought-answer coherence.
contribution: Improves performance 12.4% over the base model and achieves 2.3% additional improvement over verifier-free RL baselines on mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Large vision-language models achieve strong spatial grounding but have high inference costs, while compact VLMs are efficient but suffer substantial localization degradation under standard training.
approach: DocVAL uses validated chain-of-thought distillation with a rule-based dual-mode validator filtering low-quality signals and providing pixel-level corrective feedback.
contribution: Yields 6-7 ANLS point improvements over comparable compact VLMs with student models that operate without OCR at inference, introducing mAP as a localization metric.

problem: Collaborative machine learning requires incentivizing data sources to share high-quality data, but existing valuation methods do not verify or incentivize truthfulness, enabling manipulation.
approach: Combines semivalues for fairness with a truthful data valuation function using an unknown validation set, proving that sources maximize expected rewards by submitting true data.
contribution: First mechanism provably ensuring collaborative fairness and incentivizing truthfulness at equilibrium for Bayesian models, validated on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Multi-modal dataset distillation requires expensive checkpoint storage and bi-level optimization, limiting scalability and memory efficiency.
approach: Analytic Parameter Matching (APM) theoretically derives analytic parameters of modal projectors to replace inner-loop optimization, aligning teacher and student projectors.
contribution: Achieves up to 65x storage reduction and 9.6x faster distillation while scaling to 1,000 synthetic pairs, with notable generalization in cross-architecture and zero-shot settings.

problem: Federated text-attributed graph learning with LLMs faces high computational overhead from processing long texts, suboptimal one-shot condensation, and black-box interpretability issues.
approach: DANCE performs round-wise, model-in-the-loop condensation refresh using the latest global model and preserves provenance via locally inspectable evidence packs tracing predictions to source spans.
contribution: Improves performance across 8 TAG datasets by combining graph condensation with dynamic LLM-aware refinement and enhanced interpretability through source attribution.

problem: Visual multi-agent systems suffer a counter-intuitive scaling wall where increasing agent turns degrades performance and inflates token costs due to information loss in text-centric communication.
approach: L^2-VMAS enables inter-agent collaboration with dual latent memories that decouple perception and thinking, using entropy-driven proactive triggering for efficient on-demand memory access.
contribution: Breaks the scaling wall with 2.7-5.4% average accuracy improvement while reducing token usage by 21.3-44.8%, demonstrating strong scalability across backbones and structures.

problem: Using pre-trained AI models to automatically label datasets risks incorporating model errors without guarantees on accuracy, making wholesale replacement of manual labeling impractical.
approach: A method for obtaining probably approximately correct labels by validating pre-trained model predictions nonasymptotically with minimal assumptions.
contribution: Enables cost-effective high-quality dataset curation with theoretical guarantees on labeling error, demonstrated on text, image, and protein folding tasks.

problem: Learning multi-task, multi-agent policies for cooperative temporal objectives remains sample-inefficient and requires retraining for each new task.
approach: Automata-Conditioned Cooperative Multi-Agent RL learns task-conditioned decentralized policies, proving optimality and showing value functions can assign tasks optimally at test time.
contribution: Demonstrates emergent task-aware multi-step coordination with sample-efficient learning of task-adaptive, reusable policies for multiple objectives.

problem: RL for instruction following suffers from sparse rewards when the initial model struggles to generate responses satisfying all constraints, yielding indistinguishable signals that impede learning.
approach: Hindsight Instruction Replay replays failed attempts as successes based on satisfied constraints, performing RL on both original and replayed samples as dual-preference learning.
contribution: Achieves promising results on complex instruction following with less computational budget by enabling learning from partial successes.

problem: Prior-data Fitted Networks for amortized causal inference assume a single pre-training works across all interventional regimes, but this assumption has fundamental theoretical limitations.
approach: Proves that a single observational SCM induces exponentially large interventional distribution space (prior uncoverage), proposing target-specific fine-tuning strategies Point-Wise and Meta-Sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates that fine-tuning is necessary to achieve posterior consistency and local generalization properties in causal effect estimation.

problem: Tabular foundation models struggle with weak early-layer value sensitivity and redundant hidden states because scalar tokenization injects value variation through essentially one-dimensional channels.
approach: LimiX-2M uses RBF-feature tokenization to expand scalars into compact localized features and reorders computation as S→N→F blocks aligned with readout, improving effective rank and efficiency.
contribution: A 2M-parameter model outperforms larger TabPFN-v2 and TabICL baselines on tabular benchmarks while reducing training and inference costs.

problem: Cross-task robotic manipulation requires extracting transferable knowledge from seen tasks, but in-context methods provide only low-level action sequences, causing superficial trajectory imitation.
approach: Decomposes demonstrations into interpretable skill-action pairs and recomposes them via compositional reasoning, using visual-semantic retrieval and skill-coverage-aware libraries.
contribution: Enables zero-shot cross-task generalization by learning composable manipulation skills from demonstrations.

problem: Graph contrastive learning relies on positive samples for learning semantic patterns, but message passing trivializes their maximization, preventing effective learning from positives.
approach: SPGCL mitigates trivialization using Dirichlet energy to identify high-energy features for positive learning and low-energy features for reliable positive sampling.
contribution: Restores learning efficacy of positive samples in GCLs by disentangling message passing effects from contrastive learning, with extensive experimental validation.

problem: Long-term fairness algorithms fail to account for selective labels, which are only revealed when positive decisions are made, creating a mismatch between observed and true fairness.
approach: Uses observed data plus a label predictor model to estimate true fairness by decomposing it into observed fairness and prediction bias, deriving sufficient conditions via confidence bounds.
contribution: Proposes a reinforcement learning algorithm for long-term fair decision-making with selective labels, validated on semisynthetic hiring and lending scenarios.

problem: Sampling from unnormalized densities is expensive because evaluating the energy function is costly, requiring efficient sampler learning without access to data.
approach: Flow Sampling builds on diffusion and flow matching, training with denoising diffusion drift conditioned on noise samples, naturally extending to Riemannian manifolds.
contribution: Achieves strong empirical performance on synthetic energy benchmarks, molecular conformer generation, and sphere/hyperbolic distributions with minimal energy evaluations.

problem: Multi-bit watermarking for LLMs suffers from catastrophic false positive rates when using ECC-based extractors, and rejection thresholds collapse detection sensitivity to random guessing.
approach: BREW introduces a two-stage mechanism: blind message estimation via independent block voting followed by window-shifting verification that validates payload against local edits.
contribution: Achieves TPR of 0.965 with FPR of 0.02 under 10% synonym substitution, solving the high-FPR issue as a solvable structural flaw rather than inherent trade-off.

problem: Token-level credit assignment in RL for LLMs treats all tokens equally, failing to distinguish decisive reasoning steps from routine formatting or fluent filler.
approach: FlowTracer traces answer-targeted reasoning on an attention-induced DAG with edge capacities from aggregated attention weights, extracting flow-based token importances.
contribution: Delivers consistent performance gains on reasoning tasks by enabling learning signals to focus on tokens that route information toward correct answers.

problem: Model-based RL approaches combining MPC with learned models typically rely on gradient-free optimization, which is computationally expensive for high-dimensional control.
approach: Dream-MPC generates candidate trajectories from policy rollouts and optimizes each via gradient ascent using a learned world model and uncertainty regularization.
contribution: Significantly improves policy performance on 24 continuous control tasks, outperforming gradient-free MPC and state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Large-scale time series models exhibit a scaling paradox where larger models do not always achieve better performance due to few-layer dominance and redundant, under-utilized layers.
approach: Automatically identifies and retains only dominant layers while pruning redundant ones, validated across LLM4TS and TSFM architectures.
contribution: Retaining only 21% of parameters achieves up to 12% accuracy improvement and 2.7x inference speedup, with over 95% task improvements on 8 SOTA models.

problem: Visual autoregressive models fix computation per scale and inflate memory at high resolutions, limiting practical deployment despite strong generation quality.
approach: Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling embeds an implicit equilibrium layer trained with Jacobian-Free Backpropagation, exposing a per-scale iteration knob for compute control.
contribution: Achieves FID 2.16 on ImageNet 256x256 with 38.4% parameters of VAR, enabling reduction from 19.24GB to 8.53GB peak memory and doubling throughput.

problem: Diffusion model performance is sensitive to score estimation accuracy, but the accumulation of estimation error through the diffusion process is not well understood.
approach: Derives stepwise Wasserstein error bounds in Gaussian-mixture settings and extends to general distributions with curvature analysis at small times.
contribution: Provides sharp Wasserstein estimates for both VP and VE diffusions, clarifying how score errors propagate through reverse-time SDE and probability-flow ODE.

problem: Tabular anomaly detection with LLMs is challenged by heterogeneous features and reliance on limited one-shot supervised fine-tuning, offering weak signal for learning normal data representation.
approach: DiSPaT uses self-play with f-divergence minimization, where a policy generates synthetic pseudo-anomalies and a discriminator learns to distinguish them from normal data.
contribution: Consistently outperforms LLM-based and classical detectors on diverse tabular anomaly detection benchmarks through progressive alignment with true normal data.

problem: Traditional KL divergence-based measures fail to guarantee linear representational similarity when comparing models with similar but not identical distributions.
approach: Define a representational dissimilarity measure based on logit differences and prove that closeness in logit distance upper-bounds representational dissimilarity.
contribution: Show logit-distance distillation preserves linear representational properties better than KL-based distillation, achieving higher linear representational similarity.

problem: Finding the minimum set of edges to remove from a signed graph to eliminate all bad triangles (triangles with exactly one negative edge) is computationally hard.
approach: Propose 2-approximation algorithms for the Bad Triangle Transversal problem and establish hardness bounds showing NP-hardness with factor limits.
contribution: Establish that BTT is NP-hard to approximate better than 2137/2136 and show BTT optima are within a factor of 3/2 of correlation clustering optima in complete graphs.
