problem: Depth estimation from single images is limited to visible surfaces and cannot reconstruct occluded geometry.
approach: Propose Layered Ray Intersections (LaRI) to predict multiple surfaces per camera ray using layered point maps in a single feed-forward pass.
contribution: Enable complete 3D scene reconstruction including occluded surfaces in one pass with efficient view-aligned geometric reasoning validated on synthetic and real-world data.

problem: Existing evaluations of LLM performance on Rust program verification treat it as a black box, obscuring whether models can reconstruct the explicit deductive reasoning steps.
approach: Introduce VCoT-Lift framework to lift low-level solver reasoning into high-level human-readable verification steps, creating a Verification Chain-of-Thought benchmark.
contribution: VCoT-Bench with 1,988 tasks reveals current LLMs fall well short of automated theorem prover reasoning capabilities across robustness, proof types, and locations.

problem: LLM defenses achieve strong empirical performance but lack explicit control over false acceptance rate (FAR), a critical requirement for high-stakes deployments.
approach: Propose OSCS, an online FAR control framework using recursive density estimation on streaming inputs without requiring malicious calibration data.
contribution: Achieve provable FAR control with vanishing excess terms under mild assumptions, showing robust performance across backdoor and jailbreak attacks.

problem: Autonomous CLI agents can execute hundreds of actions with minimal oversight, raising serious risks when subjected to persistent malicious interaction.
approach: Introduce ANCHOR, an automated auditing framework using agents fine-tuned on dark personality data to roleplay persistent malicious users across multi-turn interactions.
contribution: Show compliance reaches 100% under persistent malicious interaction, demonstrating that current alignment techniques are insufficient for autonomous agents.

problem: Standard Bellman recursions in reinforcement learning fail under non-exponential discounting common in human preferences and survival processes.
approach: Propose Pontryagin-Guided Direct Policy Optimization (PG-DPO) that abandons recursion and couples the Pontryagin Maximum Principle with Monte Carlo rollouts.
contribution: Enable reinforcement learning with non-exponential discounting, improving accuracy and stability on hyperbolic and survival-discount benchmarks.

problem: Client-side encryption for LLM inference must preserve semantic fidelity while protecting privacy without imposing heavy computational overhead.
approach: Propose OSNIP which injects perturbations into the obfuscated semantic null space of LLM embeddings using key-dependent stochastic mapping.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art privacy-utility performance with near-orthogonality to original embeddings while reducing attack success rates.

problem: Open-vocabulary 3D object affordance grounding struggles because affordances emerge from specific attribute compositions rather than global object appearance.
approach: Propose Attribute-Affordance Hierarchies (AAH) learning framework using hyperbolic space to encode hierarchical relationships between object attributes and affordances.
contribution: Achieve more accurate affordance localization through hierarchical attribute modeling and counterfactual training.

problem: Existing protein design frameworks lack ability to design multistate mechanisms that underlie complex natural protein functions.
approach: Introduce SwitchCraft, a programmatic framework using backpropagation through compositional design constraints parameterized by structure prediction models.
contribution: Demonstrate in silico success on diverse state-switching primitives and de novo fluorescent biosensor design through compositional constraint optimization.

problem: Mixture of Experts models empirically outperform dense networks, but it remains unclear why beyond parameter scaling.
approach: Study sparse expert activation in an iso-parameter regime with latent modular structure and feature noise, showing MoEs act as noise filters.
contribution: Prove sparse expert activation achieves lower generalization error, improved robustness, and faster convergence under feature noise compared to dense estimators.

problem: Diffusion language models exhibit severe instability during Group Relative Policy Optimization training due to noisy importance ratio estimation.
approach: Propose StableDRL with unconditional clipping to suppress gradient spikes and self-normalization to constrain gradients within the convex hull of per-sample updates.
contribution: Enable stable full-parameter RL for diffusion LLMs, achieving 6% improvement on MATH500 and 25.6% on AIME over prior baselines.

problem: Compiler auto-tuning faces a trade-off between black-box search methods lacking semantic guidance and LLM approaches suffering from pattern matching without causal reasoning.
approach: Introduce ECCO, a framework combining interpretable Chain-of-Thought reasoning with genetic algorithm search, where LLM acts as strategist defining optimization intents.
contribution: Achieve 24.44% average cycle reduction over LLVM opt -O3 baseline on seven datasets.

problem: Alignment in LLMs reduces diversity and yields highly similar outputs across generations in open-ended tasks.
approach: Propose Base-Aligned Model Collaboration (BACo) that dynamically routes token-level decoding between base and aligned models using uncertainty and content-based signals.
contribution: Achieve 21.3% joint improvement in diversity and quality within a single pass while maintaining strong controllability.

problem: Uniform Cartesian voxelization allocates the same voxel size to both near and far regions, making small objects difficult to detect.
approach: Propose Radial Scaling Voxelization (RSV) that adaptively modulates voxel size based on radial distance from the sensor via continuous scaling function.
contribution: Improve small object detection without modifying backbone or training pipeline, showing consistent gains on KITTI and nuScenes datasets.

problem: Assistants must know when and how to ask clarifying questions for incomplete task specifications, but not all missing information is equally valuable.
approach: Use Shapley attribution and distributional comparisons to identify two key properties: task relevance and user answerability, operationalized as RL rewards.
contribution: Train CLARITI module that matches GPT-5's resolution rate while generating 41% fewer questions.

problem: Traditional instrumental variable estimators cannot handle more treatments than instruments, limiting application to high-dimensional clinical data like treatment pathways.
approach: Propose framework that constructs treatment representations by explicitly incorporating instrumental variables into representation learning.
contribution: Ensure identification of optimal outcome-prediction directions with limited instruments, showing significant improvements on large-scale clinical data.

problem: Online continual learning assumes flat label spaces and overlooks hierarchical organization of real-world concepts that evolves both horizontally and vertically.
approach: Propose HALO (Hierarchical Adaptive Learning with Organized Prototypes) combining complementary classification heads regularized by hierarchical prototypes.
contribution: Enable rapid adaptation and hierarchical consistency as taxonomy evolves, outperforming existing methods on hierarchical accuracy and catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Encoding numeric values in transformers for EHR data requires trade-offs between numeric precision, optimization stability, and architectural flexibility.
approach: Systematically compare discrete, continuous, and hybrid encoding strategies using synthetic arithmetic tasks and real-world clinical prediction.
contribution: Show hybrid token-based approaches with binning provide robust defaults with optimal bin count following power-law in dataset size.

problem: Constrained linear best arm identification with multiple performance metrics and covariate selection requires sample-efficient algorithms with tight complexity bounds.
approach: Establish instance-dependent lower bounds via multi-level optimization and prove tightness with an algorithm, then derive computationally efficient duality-based version.
contribution: Achieve both theoretical sample complexity bounds and practical computational efficiency via convex duality.

problem: Mixing synthetic old-class data from frozen generators with real new-class data in generative replay causes domain-shift-driven performance degradation.
approach: Propose DREAM using subspace rectification and orthogonal projection to eliminate domain shortcuts while reinforcing semantic alignment.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art class-incremental learning performance without exemplar replay using training-free generation.

problem: Speculative decoding for long-context LLMs is limited by verification bottleneck where Key-Value cache loading dominates latency.
approach: Propose Dustin, a sparse verification framework integrating lookahead signals and historical attention to identify critical tokens for multi-step verification.
contribution: Achieve 27.85× speedup in self-attention and 9.17× end-to-end speedup at 32k sequence length with negligible accuracy loss.

problem: Contextual bandit algorithms must efficiently explore under function approximation with uncertainty calibration.
approach: Propose Bayesian Forest Thompson Sampling using arm-wise BART models with MCMC posterior sampling for exploration.
contribution: Achieve information-theoretic regret bound of order O-tilde(K sqrt(T)) with competitive empirical results and near-nominal calibration.

problem: PageRank computation must satisfy various group-fairness criteria based on vertex sensitive attributes, but principled algorithms remain lacking.
approach: Propose FairRARI, a unified convex optimization framework solving strongly convex problems with fairness constraints to compute fair PageRank vectors.
contribution: Achieve target fairness levels with same asymptotic time-complexity as original PageRank while maintaining utility.

problem: LLMs fail systematically under meaning-preserving question rewrites due to unstable reasoning processes that diverge across semantically-equivalent inputs.
approach: Identify divergence points in reasoning traces across rewrites, aggregate into graphs pinpointing problematic steps, and train via targeted alternation.
contribution: Improve performance on MMLU-Pro, Big-MATH, and DROP with consistent gains; improve GPT-5.2 from 35.4% to 38.1% on Humanity's Last Exam.

problem: Crowdsourced annotations introduce redundancy when repeated annotation strategies are offline, instance-unaware, and model-centric.
approach: Propose MA³S, a model-agnostic strategy using margin-Beta distribution for uncertainty estimation and nearest-neighbor graphs for redundancy reduction.
contribution: Consistently outperform existing annotation strategies without relying on model feedback.

problem: Autonomous 3D indoor scene synthesis breaks down in non-convex rooms with tightly coupled spatial constraints due to lack of topological priors.
approach: Propose ZoneMaestro shifting from object-centric to Zone-Graph orchestration, with zone-aware group relative policy optimization.
contribution: Resolve density-safety dichotomy with new SCALE benchmark for intricate spatial orchestration, significantly outperforming baselines.

problem: Discrete Flow Matching for graph generation introduces substantial complexity with task-specific heuristics and large hyperparameter spaces, limiting sampling efficiency.
approach: Propose SimGFM simplifying graph DFM by relying only on scheduler and rate matrix, eliminating heuristics while leveraging trajectory patterns.
contribution: Match 500-1000 step baselines with only 10 steps on QM9 and match/surpass performance at 50 steps on most datasets.

problem: Understanding how different tasks shape neural representation geometry and their roles in downstream adaptability remains unclear.
approach: Develop controlled framework with 5,075 city coordinates and 7 geometric tasks to study representation convergence and divergence.
contribution: Show multi-task training drives convergent world representations while some divergent tasks harm new entity integration via fine-tuning.

problem: LLM free-text explanations lack guarantees of sufficiency, making it unclear if they contain enough information to explain output generation.
approach: Generalize sufficiency from feature attributions to arbitrary explanations and use LLM itself to generate alternative inputs conditioned on explanations.
contribution: Introduce self-consistent sufficiency metric (SCSuff) showing LLM explanations are generally insufficient and weakly correlated with model size.

problem: Differentially private optimization suffers from geometric mismatch: deep networks have anisotropic loss landscapes while DP-SGD injects isotropic noise.
approach: Show Fisher Information Matrix decouples into architectural sensitivity (via synthetic noise) and input correlations (via frequency statistics) for preconditioning.
contribution: Propose DP-KFC achieving preconditioner estimates without private or public data, matching private-data baselines in privacy regimes.

problem: Rashomon sets of near-optimal models reshape trustworthiness by introducing robustness-privacy trade-offs governed by diversity.
approach: Analyze how Rashomon set diversity enables reactive robustness against attacks while simultaneously increasing information leakage.
contribution: Show sparse interpretable models preserve privacy but are fragile, while diverse sets enable switching between models for robustness.

problem: Function-guided protein design lacks unified comprehensive evaluation framework with inconsistent metrics preventing fair comparison.
approach: Introduce PDFBench benchmark systematically evaluating eight models on 16 metrics for description-guided and keyword-guided design.
contribution: Enable reliable model comparisons through comprehensive metric analysis and new SwissTest dataset with strict datetime cutoff.

problem: Training neural networks with strong denoising performance and global Lipschitz guarantees is challenging without theoretical guarantees beyond training data.
approach: Exploit permutation symmetry on image lattice to constrain globally nonexpansive neural architecture with Lipschitz bound ≤1.
contribution: Develop provably contractive reconstruction mechanism with global convergence while maintaining competitive denoising performance.

problem: Mechanistic interpretability circuit discovery exhibits high instability as causal mediation analysis scores have intrinsic variance that propagates through discovery pipelines.
approach: Reframe circuit discovery as statistical estimation problem, decompose variance sources, and advocate rigorous MI practices with stability metrics.
contribution: Demonstrate small perturbations yield vastly different circuits, emphasizing need for statistical robustness in mechanistic interpretability.

problem: Long-term memory persistence in conversational LLMs introduces overlooked safety risks including cross-domain leakage and memory-induced sycophancy.
approach: Introduce PersistBench measuring safety risks of long-term memory-specific issues through cross-domain and sycophancy sampling.
contribution: Reveal median failure rates of 53% on cross-domain and 97% on sycophancy samples across frontier LLMs.

problem: Existing discrete function approximators lack efficient optimization while maintaining expressiveness for discrete domains.
approach: Introduce Deep Flow Networks inspired by minimum-cost flow value functions that admit M-convex properties for efficient optimization.
contribution: Prove universal approximation for discrete functions admitting convex extensions and demonstrate strong accuracy with faster optimization.

problem: Offline black-box optimization from limited labeled samples requires capturing bidirectional dependencies in design problems, not left-to-right generation.
approach: Adapt diffusion LLMs to offline BBO with domain adaptation via unified corpus and delimiter tokens, then post-train with SFT and RL.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art results on Design-Bench under small-data settings.

problem: Vision Transformers released on third-party hubs face supply-chain risk where adversaries can implant backdoors via direct weight editing without poisoned data.
approach: Introduce DF-LoGiT exploiting ViT's multi-head architecture to implant logic-gated compositional triggers via data-free weight editing.
contribution: Achieve near-100% attack success with negligible benign accuracy degradation, showing robustness against classical and ViT-specific defenses.

problem: RAG systems recompute query-time adaptations like query expansion for each query, losing cumulative learning and repeatedly incurring inference-time cost.
approach: Propose Evolving Retrieval Memory (ERM) transforming transient query-time gains into persistent improvements via correctness-gated feedback.
contribution: Show query and key expansion are theoretically equivalent and prove convergence of ERM's updates, achieving consistent BEIR/BRIGHT gains at native retrieval speed.

problem: Sparse autoencoders are a proven tool for interpreting autoregressive language models, but mechanistic interpretability methods for the emerging class of diffusion language models remain underdeveloped.
approach: The authors develop DLM-Scope, the first SAE-based interpretability framework for diffusion language models, showing that Top-K SAEs can extract sparse, interpretable features from DLMs and enable effective diffusion-time interventions.
contribution: They demonstrate that SAE insertion in DLMs reduces cross-entropy loss in early layers (unlike autoregressive LLMs where it incurs a penalty) and that SAE features enable more effective DLM steering and decoding order prediction.

problem: Observations in many RL environments are high-dimensional while only a subset of features matter for control, making it unclear how to learn control-relevant representations.
approach: The authors study the empowerment objective, which maximizes an agent's influence over the environment, and analyze how empowerment maximization induces two complementary representations (forward and backward) that capture control-relevant features invariant to irrelevant variations.
contribution: They show that empowerment agents implicitly learn a control-centric model of the world and that learning through interaction aimed at maximizing control is essential for acquiring useful invariance properties.

problem: Inferring vector fields of ODEs from noisy trajectories is challenging because current symbolic regression, GP, and Neural ODE methods require complex training pipelines, domain expertise, or substantial ML expertise.
approach: FIM-ODE is a pretrained foundation inference model that directly predicts ODE vector fields from noisy trajectory data in a single forward pass, using neural operators to represent the target field and pretraining on a distribution of low-degree polynomial ODEs.
contribution: FIM-ODE achieves strong zero-shot performance matching or exceeding ODEFormer, and provides fast, stable adaptation via finetuning without requiring machine learning expertise.

problem: Periodicity misalignment is a persistent challenge in multi-domain time-series generation, and existing attention mechanisms process only individual points or fragmented segments, limiting their ability to capture complex periodic patterns.
approach: Winformer extends the attention processing unit from individual points to sliding windows with adaptive window-alignment kernels derived from frequency decomposition, enabling window-wise attention that captures and transfers complex periodic patterns across domains.
contribution: Winformer achieves an average performance gain of 10.67% over SOTA baselines on 12 real-world time-series generation datasets.

problem: State-of-the-art multimodal LLMs consistently fail on basic visual reasoning tasks that human 3-year-olds solve easily, indicating fragile visual understanding despite linguistic prowess.
approach: BabyVision is a benchmark with 388 items across 22 subclasses and 4 key categories designed to assess core visual abilities independent of linguistic knowledge in MLLMs, including automatic evaluation via generation models.
contribution: Leading MLLMs like Gemini3-Pro-Preview score only 49.7 (vs 94.1 human average), revealing a fundamental gap in visual primitives despite strong performance on knowledge-heavy evaluations.

problem: Existing Decision-Focused Learning methods compute regret gradients via expensive differentiation through solvers or surrogate losses that deviate from the true objective.
approach: Under standard regularity conditions, the regret gradient admits a closed-form geometric characterization equivalent to prediction error projected onto the tangent space of active constraints scaled by local curvature, enabling PEAR to filter decision-irrelevant components from the MSE gradient.
contribution: PEAR (Projected Error As Regret-gradient) achieves superior decision quality among all baselines while being the most computationally efficient, with gains persisting under constraint shifts.

problem: Embodied 3D object detection in egocentric first-person views faces challenges of partial occlusion and temporal discontinuity, which existing benchmarks and methods designed for global scenes do not address.
approach: Embodied-DETR is an end-to-end temporal detection framework combining Scene-aware Feature Aggregation and Instance-aware Query Embedding to model scene-level context and instance-level consistency across sequential egocentric observations.
contribution: Embodied-DETR achieves superior accuracy and temporal consistency compared to existing methods on the new Embodied-Det benchmark, which evaluates detection accuracy, temporal stability, and consistency.

problem: The Bertrand paradox questions why markets sustain high prices when classical theory predicts price wars, motivating investigation of how no-regret learning algorithms affect market equilibria.
approach: The authors analyze a repeated discrete Bertrand pricing game where firms use no-regret learners to set prices, characterizing which no-regret guarantees lead to high-price versus low-price equilibria.
contribution: They demonstrate that no-external-regret learners can converge to high-price outcomes while stronger guarantees like no-swap regret shape more competitive low-price behavior, supported by theoretical analysis and experiments.

problem: Dual-LoRA federated learning designs for personalized model adaptation introduce computational overhead and structural redundancy while data heterogeneity limits personalization.
approach: FedPissa rethinks single-LoRA design via selective aggregation based on aggregation dynamics and subspace decorrelation projection to mitigate heterogeneous update conflicts, reducing cross-client interference.
contribution: FedPissa achieves up to 35% lower communication and computation cost compared to dual-LoRA methods while improving personalized adaptation on textual and visual scenarios.

problem: Transformers are known to struggle with state tracking, particularly failing on out-of-distribution length extrapolation, but the in-distribution implications of this limitation remain unclear.
approach: A large-scale empirical study compares data efficiency of transformers and RNNs across supervision regimes, analyzing weight sharing across sequence lengths and learned state-tracking mechanisms.
contribution: Transformers require substantially more training data than RNNs as state-space size and sequence length grow, learn length-specific solutions with negligible weight sharing, while RNNs exhibit effective amortized learning across lengths.

problem: All-in-one image restoration seeks a single unified model for diverse spatially non-uniform corruptions, but fixed patch partitioning leaves embedding and reconstruction stages insensitive to local degradation variations.
approach: FIT (Flexible Image Transformer) uses a Degradation Encoder to predict global degradation vectors and spatial maps, which jointly condition patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation, plus task-token dropout for robustness.
contribution: FIT achieves state-of-the-art performance on five standard benchmarks with 30.72 dB average PSNR on five-degradation settings, outperforming recent unified methods by 0.5-1.1 dB.

problem: Modern conversational agents condition on growing dialogue history, incurring redundant attention costs, while naive truncation or existing compressors cause information loss and compounding errors in long dialogues.
approach: C-DIC (Context-Driven Incremental Compression) models conversations as interleaved contextual threads with per-thread compression states in a compact memory, using a retrieve-revise-write-back loop to share cross-turn information and adapt truncated backpropagation-through-time.
contribution: C-DIC maintains near-constant inference time and stable perplexity over hundreds of dialogue turns, outperforming existing methods on long-form benchmarks.

problem: Vision-Language Models are vulnerable to adversarial examples, and existing transferable attack methods using simplex interpolation rely on unstable finite random sampling to approximate perturbation distributions.
approach: DDGA (Dirichlet Distributional Gradient Aggregation) models perturbations over the simplex with a learnable Dirichlet policy optimized via policy gradient, replacing heuristic sampling with principled distributional optimization and leveraging closed-form covariance for orthogonal perturbation construction.
contribution: DDGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art transfer-based attacks on image-text retrieval and image captioning across multiple VLM architectures.

problem: Mobile GUI world models face a critical trade-off: text-based models sacrifice visual fidelity while visual models cannot render precise text and depend on slow external pipelines.
approach: gWorld introduces a novel paradigm where a Vision-Language Model predicts the next GUI state as executable web code that renders to pixels, combining linguistic priors for text rendering with pre-training on structured web code for high-fidelity visual generation.
contribution: gWorld-8B and gWorld-32B set a new pareto frontier in accuracy versus model size, outperforming 8 frontier open-weight models over 50.25x larger on 4 in- and 2 out-of-distribution benchmarks.

problem: Generative models persistently memorize training data, creating legal liabilities and eroding diversity, but understanding which samples are memorized and under what conditions remains an open problem.
approach: Training diffusion models on strings from the Random Hierarchy Model, the authors show that samples with common substrings are preferentially memorized, even when training data is entirely unique, and identify an intermediate regime of partial memorization.
contribution: The study reveals that dataset diversity at higher levels of abstraction plays an important role in preventing memorization and that models trained in intermediate regimes exhibit 'slop' (blandness from reversion-to-the-mean).

problem: Vision-and-Language Navigation agents deployed in the wild face non-stationary environment shifts, and existing Test-Time Adaptation methods treat online adaptation as transient updates, leading to catastrophic forgetting.
approach: IDEA (Inter-Domain Bridge with Historical Assets) transforms adaptation into asset accumulation and composition via soft prompts optimized with Fisher-guided weighting, forming a dynamic library augmented with domain coordinates to construct cross-domain bridges.
contribution: IDEA enables training-free adaptation via asset sharing and achieves consistent superiority over existing TTA methods on REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE benchmarks.

problem: Understanding how frozen Transformers can serve as prompt-programmable computers and execute composite programs requires theoretical characterization of in-context universality and compositional generalization.
approach: The authors prove in-context universality via in-context emulation, where a fixed-weight Transformer emulates target computations specified by prompts, and establish one-pass and multi-pass composition theorems for combining prompts.
contribution: The work provides concrete mechanisms by which GPT-style models execute and assemble algorithms in context, supporting a principled view of prompts as programs and frozen Transformers as program interpreters.

problem: Neuromodulation control of neuronal microenvironment dynamics requires high-rate feedback on irregular 3D morphologies with complex unknown biophysics, yet high-fidelity simulators are too slow for real-time control and safety constraints are difficult to enforce.
approach: NeuronCtrl is a modular operator-level framework combining a history-conditioned observer for latent field inference, a morphology-aware neural operator for one-step dynamics prediction, and flow-matching for action proposal, with barrier-based safety enforcement at action and field levels.
contribution: NeuronCtrl demonstrates improved trade-offs among cost, safety, and latency on three high-fidelity 3D neuromodulation benchmarks, with a distilled single-step policy retaining the same safety filter.

problem: Knowledge distillation from powerful reasoning models to small language models assumes that higher-reward traces are more useful, but this assumption often fails for mathematical reasoning.
approach: The authors identify that Oracle refinement couples logical repair with distributional drift from the SLM's native distribution, increasing adaptation cost and introducing the Quality-Utility Paradox, then propose Style-Aligned Refinement to preserve the SLM's trajectory while retaining logical repairs.
contribution: Style-Aligned Refinement restores downstream utility and allows distilled SLMs to match or surpass baselines from the SLMs themselves, showing that distillation should optimize perceived quality alongside learner-data compatibility.

problem: Deep neural networks demonstrate empirical success in high-dimensional regression but their theoretical behavior with infinite-dimensional functional covariates remains largely unexplored.
approach: The authors extend existing DNN theory from finite-dimensional compact sets to infinite-dimensional non-compact functional data settings, establishing minimax-optimal convergence rates for both functional linear and functional generalized linear models.
contribution: DNN estimators attain minimax-optimal polynomial convergence rates for regression with functional covariates, with analysis highlighting fundamental obstacles inherent to nonparametric functional regression.

problem: Inferring continuous probability paths from sparse destructive measurements (e.g., in single-cell biology) is challenging because target objects live on infinite-dimensional Wasserstein space where existing interpolation methods lack uncertainty quantification.
approach: The authors introduce a framework using Linearized Optimal Transport (LOT) to map distributional snapshots into a tangent space amenable to Gaussian Process modeling, enabling probabilistic surrogates for probability paths and uncertainty-driven acquisition policies.
contribution: The approach outperforms uncertainty-agnostic baselines on both synthetic and real-world single-cell biology datasets by strategically selecting measurement times to minimize uncertainty.

problem: Adapting large language models to diverse contexts requires either expensive fine-tuning for each context or effective in-context learning, motivating scalable hypernetworks that map contexts to high-quality LoRA adapters.
approach: SHINE (Scalable Hyper In-context NEtwork) is a hypernetwork reusing the frozen LLM's parameters in an in-context design to generate high-quality LoRA adapters from diverse contexts in a single forward pass, with a pretraining and instruction fine-tuning pipeline.
contribution: SHINE generates LoRA adapters without fine-tuning, enabling complex question-answering tasks by transforming in-context knowledge to in-parameter knowledge in one pass while greatly saving time, computation, and memory.

problem: Reinforcement learning training on Mixture-of-Experts models tends to be unstable and can collapse due to discrepancies in routing behaviors between training and inference phases.
approach: R3 (Rollout Routing Replay) records routing distributions from the inference engine and replays them during training, reducing training-inference policy KL divergence and mitigating extreme discrepancies without compromising training speed.
contribution: R3 successfully stabilizes RL training in MoE models, preventing collapse and outperforming strong baselines, while remaining orthogonal to policy optimization improvements.

problem: Learned iterative optimization often fails to generalize and optimize well because existing approaches struggle with expressiveness and generalization across problem classes.
approach: FlowOptimizer represents each optimization iteration as a velocity field operating on a population of parallel candidate solutions, initially trained simulation-free via displacement matching and then fine-tuned end-to-end via objective value optimization.
contribution: FlowOptimizer consistently outperforms traditional and learning-to-optimize methods often by orders of magnitude on standard benchmarks and real-world problems, generalizing from low-dimensional to substantially higher-dimensional problems.

problem: Model-based representation methods can fail to capture sufficient information about relevant variables and overfit to early replay buffer experiences, causing biased representations and inferior actor-critic learning.
approach: DR.Q (Debiased model-based Representations for Q-learning) maximizes mutual information between current and next state-action representations while minimizing their deviations, and employs faded prioritized experience replay.
contribution: DR.Q matches or surpasses recent strong baselines on numerous continuous control benchmarks with a single set of hyperparameters, sometimes by large margins.

problem: Multimodal Large Language Models fail on implicit text recognition where content is intentionally concealed through deformation, camouflage, or cognitive suggestion, bypassing content moderation systems.
approach: ImpText introduces a benchmark (ImpText-Bench) and a tool-augmented framework (ImpText-Reader) using a three-stage training strategy with capability-boundary data to optimize tool selection and semantic reasoning for hidden text extraction.
contribution: ImpText-Reader achieves state-of-the-art performance on implicit text reasoning, significantly enhancing model robustness while demonstrating that current systems struggle with adversarial text scenarios.

problem: Mixture of Experts for continual learning typically relies on shared parameters that become bottlenecks and explicit task ID predictors, limiting scaling and generalization as the number of tasks increases.
approach: The authors eliminate shared parameters and task ID predictors by enabling dynamic expert knowledge sharing via a multimodal foundation model (CLIP) that provides expert priors, with experts learning calibrated inter-task posteriors guided by multivariate Gaussians.
contribution: The approach consistently outperforms existing methods across diverse continual learning settings without requiring reference datasets or replay memory, with new evaluation benchmarks simulating realistic scenarios.

problem: Classical dynamic programming algorithms for structured combinatorial problems use hard constraints, while soft relaxations rely on hand-tuned hyperparameters like gap penalties that are difficult to optimize.
approach: d2p learns DP algorithm parameters directly from data by treating marginal computation as first-order derivatives, making parameter learning a second-order problem solved via efficient Hessian-vector products implemented as fused CUDA kernels.
contribution: d2p achieves 100-20,000x speedups over PyTorch and demonstrates that learning DP parameters is critical: protein structure alignment improves from 0.32 to 0.75 F1 when jointly learning gap penalties.

problem: Multi-objective combinatorial optimization methods rely exclusively on node-centric representations and fail to capture complementary edge feature representations, resulting in persistent optimality gaps.
approach: The authors propose Preference-Modulated Structural Attention using preference-modulated edge features as explicit structural biases during attention, with dynamic edge feature aggregation incorporating node-specific context.
contribution: The approach achieves superior performance and generalization on classic MOCOP benchmarks by synergizing node and edge features for preference-aware structure perception.

problem: LLMs can generate incorrect yet coherent chain-of-thought reasoning that appears plausible, creating a powerful yet fragile basis for trust that humans and systems struggle to detect.
approach: DecepChain induces deceptive reasoning by fine-tuning on naturally erroneous rollouts from the model itself, then reinforces it via Group Relative Policy Optimization with flipped rewards and format constraints to preserve fluent, benign-looking reasoning.
contribution: DecepChain achieves high deception effectiveness with minimal degradation on benign scenarios, and both LLMs and humans struggle to distinguish deceptive from benign reasoning, underscoring the stealthiness of this failure mode.

problem: Post-hoc text watermarking via LLM rephrasing offers degrees of freedom for both generation and detection but the trade-offs between quality and detectability remain unclear.
approach: The authors investigate how allocating compute through rephrasing model size, beam search, multi-candidate generation, and entropy filtering at detection affects the quality-detectability trade-off for various watermarking schemes.
contribution: Gumbel-max surprisingly outperforms recent alternatives under nucleus sampling with strong detectability on open-ended text, though most approaches struggle with verifiable text like code.

problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer from geometric fragility where visual representations degrade rapidly under viewpoint and viewing distance changes because they remain entangled with the view-dependent pixel grid.
approach: AffIn-Space enforces strict affine invariance via explicit geometric resampling using decomposed affine quantities (from pose features) to spatially align 3D features and affine-invariant constraints via orthogonal projection within the MLLM.
contribution: AffIn-Space achieves state-of-the-art performance on VSI-Bench, ScanQA, SQA3D, Scan2Cap, and EmbodiedScan with superior stability against affine perturbations.

problem: Score-based diffusion models encounter fundamental bottlenecks in inverse problems due to analytical intractability of the time-dependent likelihood score.
approach: PGM (Proximal-Based Generative Modeling) exploits theoretical equivalence between Gaussian convolution and Moreau-Yosida regularization, introducing the Moreau score which admits closed-form expression via proximal operators, with Moreau score matching training.
contribution: PGM eliminates early-stopping bias and achieves non-asymptotic convergence, significantly surpassing state-of-the-art methods in reconstruction quality and sampling time.

problem: Tool-augmented LLM agents struggle to balance planning flexibility with production reliability, and agents that learn from experience suffer from skill library pollution where unverified abstractions degrade performance.
approach: EvoC2F redefines tool orchestration via program compilation to a well-defined intermediate representation with explicit semantic annotations, enabling verified continuous learning where learned skills undergo rigorous testing before library admission.
contribution: EvoC2F outperforms existing methods by reducing latency while establishing soundness guarantees, providing a robust foundation for building reliable, evolving autonomous agents.

problem: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials struggle to make accurate predictions on out-of-distribution data and lack uncertainty estimates, both critical for guiding active learning and ensuring simulation accuracy.
approach: BLIPs proposes a scalable, architecture-agnostic variational Bayesian framework for training or fine-tuning MLIPs via adaptive Variational Dropout, delivering well-calibrated uncertainty estimates with minimal inference overhead.
contribution: BLIPs improves predictive accuracy over standard MLIPs with trustworthy uncertainty estimates, especially in data-scarce and heavy out-of-distribution regimes, with consistent gains from fine-tuning pretrained MLIPs.

problem: Existing GRPO approaches on Flow Matching models propagate outcome-based rewards uniformly to all denoising steps without distinguishing local effects, and ignore within-trajectory dependencies where early actions affect later states.
approach: TP-GRPO (TurningPoint-GRPO) replaces outcome-based rewards with step-level incremental rewards for dense learning signals, and identifies turning points (steps that flip reward trends) to assign aggregated long-term rewards capturing delayed impacts.
contribution: TP-GRPO alleviates reward sparsity and consistently improves text-to-image generation by exploiting reward signals more effectively with hyperparameter-free turning point detection.

problem: Multi-agent systems are increasingly complex with inter-agent coordination, tool use, and long-horizon reasoning making error recognition particularly challenging, while debugging incurs high costs for humans and automated systems.
approach: CORRECT leverages an online cache of distilled error schemata to recognize and transfer knowledge of failure structures across requests, enabling targeted error localization via LLMs without expensive retraining.
contribution: CORRECT improves step-level error localization by up to 19.8% over existing advances while operating at near-zero overhead, with the CORRECT-Error dataset providing 2,000+ annotated trajectories via error-injection pipeline.

problem: Bayesian PINNs lack theoretical guarantees for uncertainty quantification in solving elliptic PDEs, particularly when learning from noisy measurements in both domain and boundary.
approach: The authors prove posterior contraction rates for Bayesian PINNs solving elliptic PDEs with Hölder solutions, showing that a suitably constructed prior enables rate-adaptive posterior concentration without prior knowledge of smoothness.
contribution: Theoretical analysis establishes near-minimax posterior contraction rates and eliminates early-stopping bias, providing statistical guarantees for uncertainty quantification in PDEs via Bayesian PINNs.

problem: External signals like token probabilities and self-evaluations used to rank LLM sample-evaluate-ensemble outputs are poorly calibrated after post-training and low-dimensional projections of internal dynamics.
approach: NAD (Neuron Agreement Decoding) analyzes internal neuron activations and finds that correct responses activate fewer unique neurons with stronger cross-sample agreement while incorrect responses diverge, enabling unsupervised best-of-N selection via activation sparsity.
contribution: NAD matches majority voting on benchmarks with verifiable answers and outperforms Avg@64 on open-ended coding tasks, reducing token usage by 99% with minimal quality loss via early stopping.

problem: Standard majority voting for multi-agent LLM aggregation treats all answers equally, failing to account for latent heterogeneity and correlation across models.
approach: OW (Optimal Weight) and ISP (Inverse Surprising Popularity) leverage first-order and second-order information to design training-free aggregation algorithms that provably mitigate majority voting limitations.
contribution: Both algorithms consistently outperform standard baselines on synthetic data, fine-tuning benchmarks like UltraFeedback and MMLU, and real-world healthcare settings.

approach: Proposes Density-Aware Translation (DAT) that refines image-text similarity scores using a local geometric density term derived from group reference sets

approach: Proposes Immuno-VLM, a bio-inspired framework that adapts the biological principle of Immunological Negative Selection to high-dimensional latent spaces

approach: Proposes a Likelihood Matching approach for training diffusion models by first establishing an equivalence between the likelihood of the target data distribution and a likelihood along the sample path
contribution: Empirical and simulation evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Likelihood Matching and validate the theoretical results

problem: In many applications of LLMs, natural language responses often have an underlying structure such as representing discrete labels, numerical values, or...
approach: Yet, existing decoding and uncertainty estimation methods operate only in language space and largely disregard structural information
contribution: Across different tasks, Bayes-optimal responses consistently outperform standard decoding methods like beam search

problem: Active feature acquisition must adapt feature selection to new tasks using only retrospective data with systematic missingness and limited labels.
approach: L2M introduces reliable uncertainty quantification over unseen tasks via autoregressive pre-training and an uncertainty-guided agent that maximizes conditional mutual information, operating directly on datasets with missingness without per-task retraining.
contribution: L2M matches or surpasses task-specific baselines on synthetic and real-world tabular benchmarks, particularly under scarce labels and high missingness.

problem: One-class audio deepfake detection must establish compact decision boundaries without auxiliary negative samples, as negatives bias toward seen artifacts and degrade generalization to unseen attacks.
approach: CA-SOADD refines the acceptance region by constructing off-manifold boundary probes and uses centroid-anchored tri-objective learning to simultaneously enforce compactness and centroid-referenced margins.
contribution: CA-SOADD consistently outperforms strong baselines on ASVSpoof and MLAAD benchmarks under unseen attack types and domain shifts without explicit negative supervision.

problem: Shampoo optimization requires matrix inversion that is computationally prohibitive, forcing practitioners to use stale preconditioner updates that degrade performance and introduce numerical instability.
approach: FOAM adaptively stabilizes training by dynamically controlling both damping factor and eigendecomposition frequency based on an approximation of staleness-oriented error.
contribution: FOAM reduces wall-clock time compared to standard Shampoo while maintaining robust convergence through stabilized preconditioner updates.

problem: LLMs trained on larger datasets with extended reasoning chains neglect logicality, the rational foundation ensuring valid reasoning steps and reliable conclusions in scientific tasks.
approach: A logicality-enriched methodology extracts scientific problems from academic literature, samples high-quality datasets with strong logicality, and uses assessment criteria and logicality-guided training to improve logical faithfulness.
contribution: Training data constructed with strong logicality effectively improves scientific logicality in LLM reasoning and plays a critical role in solving physics and science problems.

problem: Offline Federated Deep RL aggregates locally-trained models but neglects combined consideration of Q-values and policy inconsistency, causing clients with asymmetric advantages to disproportionately affect global performance.
approach: A novel FL framework weights client models by both policy inconsistency and Q-values with scaling to avoid numerical discrepancies, and reduces impact of weak global models on local training.
contribution: The framework improves offline FDRL performance by considering both Q-values and policy inconsistency for adaptive client weighting during global aggregation.

problem: Ride-hailing platforms must balance passenger waiting times with system efficiency under non-stationary supply-demand conditions and spatio-temporal regime shifts that shallow encoders cannot capture.
approach: RAST-MoE equips RL agents with a self-attention Mixture-of-Experts encoder that lets different experts specialize automatically across operational regimes while maintaining modest per-sample computation.
contribution: On San Francisco TNC data, the 12M-parameter model reduces average matching delay by 10% and pickup delay by 15%, generalizes zero-shot to two additional cities, and exhibits clear expert specialization.

problem: Vision-Language Models for mobile GUI navigation lack systematic evaluation of data scaling effects and reasoning capabilities, limiting rigorous benchmarking across diverse applications.
approach: HyperTrack introduces a large-scale dataset with over 16,000 real-world tasks across 650+ Chinese mobile apps, and GUIEvalKit provides an open-source toolkit for unified benchmarking of VLMs on offline GUI navigation.
contribution: Reinforcement-based finetuning consistently outperforms supervised finetuning, particularly in out-of-domain settings, demonstrating synergy between data scaling and reinforcement learning for GUI navigation.

problem: Knowledge distillation for Vision-Language embedding models focuses on reasoning tasks and overlooks hierarchical feature structure and fine-grained cross-modal interactions, leaving students unable to inherit object-level semantics.
approach: HieRD preserves hierarchical structure via distillation by leveraging clustered visual tokens and multi-granular alignment with phrase-level text across modalities.
contribution: HieRD consistently outperforms strong baselines on multimodal embedding and downstream tasks while enabling compact and efficient embedding models.

problem: Few-shot time series forecasting suffers from data scarcity and severe overfitting risk, requiring targeted data augmentation to identify and address overfitting-prone regions.
approach: ReAugment uses RL to learn transformation policies, maintaining a model zoo to measure prediction diversity and identify overfitting-prone samples as anchors for augmentation decisions.
contribution: ReAugment demonstrates effectiveness across diverse forecasting architectures in both few-shot and standard time series forecasting.

problem: Masked diffusion language models suffer performance degradation when generating multiple tokens simultaneously due to mismatch between token-level training and joint sequence consistency.
approach: ME-DLM augments diffusion generation with lightweight post-editing steps that refine initial responses through minimal edit operations (replacement, deletion, insertion) conditioned on the full sequence.
contribution: ME-DLM improves quality and robustness of multi-token generation with 11.6 points gain on HumanEval and 33.6 points on GSM8K while using one-eighth of total diffusion steps.

problem: Dataset pruning methods rely on either intrinsic signals assessing samples independently or extrinsic signals promoting diversity via pairwise relations, but each captures only one aspect and lacks robustness across pruning ratios.
approach: A unified graph-based DP framework models the dataset as a weighted graph where node weights encode intrinsic value and edge weights encode extrinsic value, casting pruning as a Maximum Weight Clique Problem.
contribution: The method outperforms existing DP approaches and reduces training time by over 40% without sacrificing accuracy on ImageNet-1k with ResNet-50.

problem: LLM serving routing heuristics lack explicit service-level objectives and offer limited control over latency-throughput trade-offs while operating under tight batch-size and KV-cache constraints.
approach: An online linear programming framework formulates routing as an optimization problem with interpretable decision rewards, using bid-price control policy based on shadow prices to admit requests when benefit exceeds cost.
contribution: The router demonstrates substantial improvements over standard baselines across multiple SLO regimes including end-to-end latency, time-to-first-token, throughput, and tail performance.

problem: Spoken Language Models in low-resource languages rely on synthetic data which improves phonetic accuracy but progressively suppresses prosodic variability, causing expressivity collapse (Synthetic Erosion).
approach: Two self-alignment frameworks address this: Disentanglement-Guided Self-Alignment recovers expressivity via prosody-timbre separation, and Temperature-Driven Self-Critique stabilizes generation through automated exploration and filtering.
contribution: The approach outperforms commercial systems including ElevenLabs and Gemini Pro and enables zero-shot voice cloning capability for Lao.

problem: RL for LLM reasoning on hard problems wastes compute because correct on-policy traces are rare and policy gradients vanish, making learning inefficient.
approach: PrefixRL conditions on successful off-policy trace prefixes and runs on-policy RL to complete them, modulating problem difficulty through prefix length and avoiding backpropagation through forecasting models.
contribution: PrefixRL reaches the same training reward 2x faster than the strongest baseline and increases final reward by 3x on hard reasoning problems.

problem: LLM agents rely on fixed cognitive patterns (immediate or uniform deep reasoning) that are inefficient for long-horizon tasks where cognitive demands vary significantly step-to-step.
approach: CogRouter trains agents to dynamically adapt cognitive depth at each step using Cognition-aware Supervised Fine-tuning and Cognition-aware Policy Optimization with confidence-aware advantage reweighting.
contribution: CogRouter achieves state-of-the-art performance on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld with superior efficiency through step-level cognitive adaptation.

problem: Learning rate warm-up is ubiquitous in deep learning but its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood.
approach: The paper provides a principled explanation using a generalization of $(L_0, L_1)$-smoothness that bounds local curvature as a linear function of loss suboptimality and adapting learning rate in response to this condition.
contribution: The resulting one-parameter warm-up schedule yields provably faster convergence guarantees than fixed learning rate and matches tuned linear warm-up on language and vision models.

problem: Deep learning CT reconstruction lacks theoretical confidence estimation and uncertainty guarantees needed for reliable medical imaging.
approach: A framework based on sequential likelihood mixing establishes confidence regions with theoretical coverage guarantees for deep-learning-based CT reconstructions under realistic Beer-Lambert forward models with Poisson noise.
contribution: Deep reconstruction methods yield substantially tighter confidence regions than classical methods while maintaining theoretical coverage guarantees and enable hallucination detection.

problem: Conventional LLMs suffer from corpus heterogeneity and subtle condition changes, with finetuning causing catastrophic forgetting and meta-learning limited by model complexity.
approach: A meta-gating mechanism within SwiGLU blocks adaptively adjusts FFN nonlinearity via a hypernetwork that dynamically produces parameters under textual conditions.
contribution: The method outperforms finetuning and meta-learning baselines across different condition types (task, domain, persona, style) and generalizes reasonably on unseen tasks and instructions.

problem: Bayesian inference for inverse problems requires posterior sampling but exact posterior sampling is expensive; approximate posteriors introduce significant bias.
approach: Proximal-IMH removes bias from approximate posteriors by solving an auxiliary optimization problem that yields local adjustments trading off model adherence against stability around the approximate reference point.
contribution: Proximal-IMH reliably outperforms existing IMH variants across multimodal and data-driven priors, tightening the match between approximate and exact posteriors.

problem: Medical large vision-language models achieve progress in vision-language comprehension and segmentation separately but struggle to unify these capabilities for clinically-grounded reasoning.
approach: MedSIGHT introduces Region Perceiver for pixel-level understanding with region-centric tokens and a medical region codebook in LLM vocabulary enabling end-to-end spatial grounding via progressive training.
contribution: Trained on 72K multimodal instruction pairs, MedSIGHT achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse imaging modalities on both medical comprehension and segmentation tasks.

problem: Agentic software engineering post-training alone does not address distribution mismatch between static pre-training and dynamic deployment environments.
approach: Agent-native mid-training uses contextually-native trajectories preserving complete information flow and environmentally-native trajectories from actual tool invocations and test executions.
contribution: On SWE-Bench Verified, the 56.1% and 58.5% resolution rates for 32B and 72B models match or exceed prior open agentic recipes while using fewer mid-training tokens.

problem: Cross-domain knowledge distillation effectiveness under substantial domain shift between source and target remains theoretically unclear.
approach: A high-dimensional asymptotic analysis of a linear teacher-student model characterizes excess risk accounting for both model and covariate shifts.
contribution: The analysis shows that even with substantial domain differences there exists a regime where the student achieves superior generalization and identifies a crossed double descent phenomenon.

problem: Standard generative models like Flow Matching assume flat Euclidean geometry but fail for Spatial Semantic Pointers on toroidal manifolds where linear interpolants destroy phase and magnitude structure.
approach: Geodesic Flow Matching adapts Riemannian transport dynamics to restrict denoising flow strictly to the SSP manifold.
contribution: In a Spiking Neural SLAM system, manifold-aware cleanup achieves 72% reduction in tracking error and enables 40% increase in neural efficiency compared to classical baselines.

problem: Self-rewarding vision-language agents struggle with visual reasoning verification and suffer from evaluation hallucinations when using purely text-based self-evaluation.
approach: Agent0-VL incorporates tool usage into reasoning, self-evaluation, and self-repair, unifying Solver and Verifier roles through a Self-Evolving Reasoning Cycle with tool-grounded critique and reinforcement learning.
contribution: Through zero-external-reward evolution, Agent0-VL achieves continual self-improvement on chart reasoning, geometric problem solving, and visual science tasks.

problem: Anomaly detection methods treat anomalies as outliers but fail when anomalies are mechanism violations rather than extreme values, especially in tabular data with causal dependencies.
approach: CausalAno trains a causal GAN on normal data and uses its discriminator to learn mechanism-consistent representations, scoring test samples via Mahalanobis distance in this feature space.
contribution: CausalAno shows consistent improvements across 28 tabular datasets (18 continuous-only and 10 mixed-type), comparing against 16 strong baselines.

problem: Existing calibration methods for LLMs overlook behavioral robustness to irrelevant information; a model's true confidence should reflect stability under cognitive pressure.
approach: CaliDist measures how LLM predictions and uncertainty change when prompts are perturbed with semantic distractors, using this stability signal to adaptively scale initial confidence scores.
contribution: Across seven NLU classification benchmarks using six LLMs, CaliDist achieves 70% relative improvement in ECE, reducing it from 23% to 7% on average.

problem: Bayesian additive spanning trees rely on hard partitions that limit ability to represent smoothly varying functions on constrained domains.
approach: PR-BAST replaces hard cuts with probabilistic routing along spanning tree components, representing the regression surface as additive spanning tree-aligned smooth components with sparse tree-structured precision matrices.
contribution: PR-BAST yields strictly faster posterior contraction rates than BAST under graph-smooth truth and consistently improves accuracy on synthetic and real datasets.

problem: Synthesizing authentic phonocardiograms from electrocardiograms requires capturing complex electromechanical coupling but existing models fail to meet dual requirements of temporal precision and physiological fidelity.
approach: A Temporally-Aware VAE-Diffusion model enforces physiological coupling through Enhanced Condition Fusion and explicitly models long-range cardiac dynamics via Temporal Attention Blocks.
contribution: On EPHNOGRAM, the model achieves Pearson correlation of 0.910±0.008, 95.95% S1 detection accuracy, and 12.0 ms timing error with robust cross-dataset transfer.

problem: VMC simulations of quantum many-body systems rely on double precision arithmetic but this limits scalability and energy efficiency despite GPU availability.
approach: The paper investigates mixed-precision arithmetic in neural-network based VMC by deriving analytical bounds on error from reduced precision MCMC and empirically validating on quantum simulations.
contribution: Significant portions of VMC including state sampling can execute in half precision without accuracy loss, enabling more scalable and energy-efficient quantum simulations.

problem: Dirac-Frenkel instantaneous residual minimization for nonlinear PDE parametrizations suffers from ill-conditioning that makes parameter dynamics non-unique.
approach: Interprets non-uniqueness as gauge freedom and introduces a history variable (momentum) injected along nullspace directions, guided by Onsager's minimum-dissipation principle.
contribution: The Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager dynamics preserve instantaneous residual minimization while promoting temporally smooth parameter evolution with increased robustness in singular regimes.

problem: Multimodal Federated Learning faces client selection challenges under compounded modality, distribution, and quantity heterogeneity; reactive methods miss how decisions influence optimization trajectories.
approach: FedSSM reconceptualizes client selection as proactive decision-making via decision-aware state space models predicting training dynamics; surprise signal governs adaptive budgets and exploration-exploitation via counterfactual reasoning.
contribution: FedSSM achieves 2.5-4.5% accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art while reducing communication rounds by over 30%.

problem: Why Graph Prompt Learning remains effective under cross-domain shift from pre-training source to downstream target remains unexplored.
approach: A dual-branch GPL method explicitly instantiates frozen branch retaining pre-trained knowledge and adapted branch with lightweight adapters for task-specific adaptation, fusing adaptively via contrastive and topology-consistent losses.
contribution: GP2F outperforms existing GPL methods on cross-domain few-shot node and graph classification through adaptive fusion under topology constraints.

problem: Black box auditing of language models may miss subtle misalignment and hidden information during pre-deployment evaluation.
approach: Overthinking amplifies reasoning task vectors with a model defined as $O_\alpha = M + \alpha(R - M)$ where $\alpha > 1$; layer-wise attenuation strategies selectively amplify without losing quality.
contribution: Overthinking models reveal hidden information up to 10x more frequently than pure reasoning models across four settings with 2B-32B models.

problem: Which properties of pre-trained representations enable effective class-incremental learning under strict data access constraints remains unclear.
approach: The paper demonstrates that maintaining simple class-wise statistical estimators of features from frozen CLIP representations can recover substantial performance without continual parameter updates.
contribution: Competitive performance on class-incremental learning can be achieved via class-level inference based solely on statistical estimators from frozen features.

problem: Pay-per-token pricing mechanisms create financial incentives for providers to misreport token counts; users cannot prove or know if overcharged.
approach: The paper develops an efficient heuristic algorithm demonstrating optimal overcharging strategies and proposes incentive-compatible pricing based on linear pricing on character count.
contribution: Token-based pricing mechanisms are vulnerable to strategic misreporting; character-based pricing eliminates the financial incentive while allowing providers to maintain average margins.

problem: Evaluating cryptography capabilities of LLMs requires comprehensive benchmarking across diverse skill levels from memorization through vulnerability exploitation to formal reasoning.
approach: AICrypto introduces 135 multiple-choice questions, 150 capture-the-flag challenges, and 30 proof problems reviewed by cryptography experts with detailed scoring rubrics and reference solutions.
contribution: State-of-the-art models match or exceed human experts in memorization and vulnerability exploitation but struggle with abstract mathematical concepts and multi-step dynamic reasoning.

problem: Video object-centric learning maintains temporal consistency through learned dynamics modules that predict future representations, but these predictors function as expensive approximations.
approach: Grounded Correspondence replaces learned transition functions with deterministic bipartite matching on frozen backbone features; slots initialize from salient regions and frame-to-frame identity uses Hungarian matching.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on MOVi-D, MOVi-E, and YouTube-VIS without learnable parameters for temporal modeling.

problem: VLMs exhibit puzzling failures in multi-object visual tasks such as hallucinating elements or failing to identify similar objects; internal mechanisms driving these remain poorly understood.
approach: Analyzes representational geometry by extracting concept vectors encoding visual concepts, validates via steering interventions in simplified and naturalistic tasks.
contribution: Geometric overlap between concept vectors correlates strongly with error patterns, offering a quantitative framework to understand how internal representations shape VLM behavior.

problem: Diffusion Bridge and Flow Matching are two competing approaches for transforming between arbitrary distributions, but their relative merits and practical applicability remain unclear due to different modeling assumptions and implementations.
approach: Unified analysis through Stochastic Optimal Control and Optimal Transport perspectives, with a Transformer-based latent architecture enabling fair empirical comparison across image restoration, translation, and style transfer tasks.
contribution: Proved that Diffusion Bridge has lower cost function for stable trajectories and Flow Matching becomes ineffective at reduced data sizes; comprehensive experiments validate theoretical predictions across varying distributional difficulty and data size.

problem: Existing geometric deep learning methods only exploit certain symmetry structures; richer symmetries in data that could improve performance and efficiency remain unexploited.
approach: Develop order-equivariant neural networks (OENN) generalizing graph message passing and sheaf neural networks through equivariant bundles over face posets, with universal approximation theorems for continuous order-equivariant maps.
contribution: First universal approximation theorem for sheaf neural networks; OENN framework subsumes and extends graph neural networks while enabling leverage of categorical symmetries including non-invertible symmetries with compositional relations.

problem: Softmax attention enforces strict unit-sum normalization that limits flexibility in controlling attention magnitudes and can lead to overly concentrated or unstable attention patterns during training.
approach: Introduce Affine-Scaled Attention adding input-dependent scaling and bias terms to softmax-normalized weights, relaxing normalization constraints while maintaining value aggregation and allowing controlled attention reweighting.
contribution: Large-scale LLM pretraining experiments show consistent improvements in training stability, optimization behavior, and downstream task performance compared to standard softmax attention and attention sink baselines.

problem: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is difficult due to sparse signals and severe experimental noise, with existing methods suffering from mean collapse that produces false positives by predicting global averages.
approach: AdaPert uses differentiable node selection to extract sparse perturbation-specific subgraphs, suppressing spurious variation in non-responsive genes while emphasizing differentially expressed ones.
contribution: Outperforms existing baselines across multiple benchmarks with largest gains on DEG-aware metrics by extracting perturbation-specific knowledge rather than treating biological knowledge graphs as dense static priors.

problem: Text-to-Audio-Video generation evaluation is fragmented, relying on coarse embedding similarity that fails to capture fine-grained joint correctness required for realistic multi-modal prompts.
approach: AVGen-Bench proposes a multi-granular evaluation framework combining specialist models with Multimodal LLMs, assessing audio-video generation across 11 real-world categories from perceptual quality to semantic controllability.
contribution: Benchmark reveals significant gap between strong audio-visual aesthetics and weak semantic reliability, with persistent failures in text rendering, speech coherence, physical reasoning, and universal breakdown in musical pitch control.

problem: Existing LLM-based kernel optimization methods struggle with semantic mismatch between generalized reasoning and low-level system behaviors, suffering from runtime blindness and configuration fragmentation.
approach: QiMeng-PerceptOS shifts to perception-driven tuning integrating: (1) Perception Module aligning telemetry into semantic fingerprints, (2) Bi-level Hierarchical Induction Tree for efficient search, (3) Posterior Enhancement suppressing hallucinations via trajectory synthesis.
contribution: Achieves 296.6% of default Redis throughput and surpasses SOTA by 32.6% within 15 iterations, establishing perception-driven closed-loop for automated system optimization.

problem: Large reasoning models require expensive full-precision inference and suffer from high KV cache footprints; full 4-bit FP4 quantization causes severe reasoning degradation that existing methods cannot recover.
approach: ReQAT proposes reasoning-centric FP4 training with Trace-Aligned QAT revisiting identical reasoning traces, Selective Entropy Minimization reinforcing low-entropy positions, and Q-FIT initialization calibrating RoPE-consistent KV cache.
contribution: Recovers and surpasses BF16 accuracy under same training budget while delivering up to 3.9x throughput speedup on NVIDIA DGX Spark and 3.1x on B200.

problem: While RL algorithm design drives recent reasoning model progress, data scheduling decisions that determine training data over time remain underexplored despite being critical for competitive code generation.
approach: DRIVE pipeline with hardness-prioritized SFT and two-stage RL: first stage uses decreased max sequence length to expand entropy, second stage uses large rollouts per prompt and curriculum design for exploration.
contribution: Achieves sota for 32B models in competitive code generation on LeetCode and Codeforces weekly contests; implementation on Qwen2.5-32B and 389B MoE model demonstrates effectiveness and scalability.

problem: Existing gradient-based sufficient dimension reduction estimators either suffer from curse of dimensionality in ambient space or incur quadratic per-iteration cost when localizing to reduced space.
approach: SMAVE recasts MAVE risk as smooth maximization on Stiefel manifold with closed-form Riemannian gradient, combining sparse projected-space nearest-neighbor localization with Riemannian stochastic gradient ascent.
contribution: Almost-sure convergence with non-asymptotic rate matching standard non-convex first-order scaling; matches or improves synthetic subspace recovery at high dimension and uniformly outperforms OPG with orders of magnitude lower runtime.

problem: The Mountain Car problem, a canonical RL benchmark for 36 years, lacks analytical optimal solution, hindering understanding of why modern RL agents display large gaps to optimality.
approach: Analytically solve Mountain Car to derive optimal control, then introduce Chebyshev policies as universal dense class of RL policies from first principles, trainable as neural net drop-in replacements.
contribution: Chebyshev policies reduce regret by factor of 4.18 while requiring 277 times fewer parameters; consistent improvements on further RL tasks and real-world nonlinear motion control testbed, demonstrating sample efficiency and explainability.

problem: Existing multimodal federated learning methods assume homogeneous models and balanced modality distributions, ill-suited for practical scenarios with heterogeneous client architectures and severe modality imbalance.
approach: MFedPBA framework with dual alignment mechanism: feature-level alignment via projection encoder using contrastive learning and Gromov-Wasserstein distance, and decision-level alignment via entropy-weighted logit prototype aggregation.
contribution: Significantly outperforms sota baselines under model heterogeneity and modality imbalance conditions through joint handling of heterogeneous feature spaces and collective decision aggregation.

problem: The emerging Agentic Web paradigm shifts from centralized information retrieval to decentralized coordination, but how well autonomous agents can synthesize answers by interacting with content-specific agents remains unexplored.
approach: AgentWebBench evaluates user agent synthesis across four information-need tasks (web search, recommendation, QA, deep research) with seven LLMs and three coordination strategies in decentralized settings.
contribution: Multi-agent coordination lags centralized retrieval as expected but gap shrinks with model scale; decentralized access concentrates traffic, test-time scaling improves performance, and strong results require careful planning and sufficient interactions.

problem: Standard LLM-as-a-Judge protocols systematically fail when evaluating upper-undergraduate to early graduate level mathematics proofs, showing significant biases and reasoning disparities.
approach: QEDBench introduces first benchmark systematically measuring alignment with human experts on undergraduate proofs, contrasting course-specific rubrics against expert common knowledge via dual-evaluation matrix (7 judges × 5 solvers) on 1,000+ hours.
contribution: Reveals frontier evaluators like Claude 4.5 Opus exhibit positive bias up to +0.28, while specialized reasoning models like o3-deep-research collapse in discrete domains (42.1% accuracy in Graph Theory vs 0.91 for generalists.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models suffer significant performance drops when encountering unseen real-world visual disturbances absent from training data, limiting practical robustness.
approach: StableVLA proposes Information Bottleneck Adapter (IB-Adapter) module grounded in information theory that selectively filters noise from visual inputs without requiring extra data or augmentation, improves over baseline average 30%.
contribution: With negligible parameter overhead (<10M), achieves robustness competitive with 7B sota VLAs despite using 14x smaller backbone (0.5B) and no Open X-Embodiment pretraining; maintains accuracy on long-horizon tasks and surpasses OpenPi under disturbances.

problem: Existing LMM-based image quality assessment methods support only partial perception dimensions (reasoning or pixel-level grounding), lacking unified frameworks for multi-granularity quality understanding.
approach: IQA-Spider formulates four-task paradigm (global/local description, pixel-level grounding, region-level referring) with scalable automatic annotation and conflict-free two-stage design progressively extending text-level understanding to pixel-level grounding.
contribution: Achieves unified multi-granularity explainable image quality assessment across multiple benchmarks through training-free text-to-point grounding paradigm mapping token logits to spatial coordinates.

problem: Mainstream distributed RL frameworks rely on centralized architecture coupling control dispatch with data transmission, creating significant communication bottlenecks that severely limit scalability and efficiency for LLM post-training.
approach: DistFlow adopts fully distributed multi-controller paradigm decoupling data from control, with parallelism-aware Data Coordinator leveraging local caching and load balancing, plus DAG-based task scheduler for fine-grained independent execution.
contribution: Achieves near-linear scalability up to 512 GPUs with up to 2.63x throughput improvement over sota frameworks for distributed RL at scale.

problem: Omni-modal LLMs relying on long multimodal token sequences suffer substantial computational overhead; token compression methods designed for omni-modals remain limited.
approach: OmniSIFT proposes two-stage compression: (i) spatio-temporal video pruning removing intra-frame and inter-frame redundancy, (ii) vision-guided audio selection filtering tokens, optimized end-to-end via differentiable straight-through estimator.
contribution: With only 25% of original token context and 4.85M added parameters, consistently outperforms compression baselines and surpasses full-token model on several tasks for Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.

problem: Prompt learning for vision-language models suffers fundamental bottleneck: sample-wise optimization within task-specific feature spaces traps models in local optima, hindering global optimality.
approach: AlignedNorm identifies Coupled Prompt Field as shared space where base and new tasks are mutually constrained, enforcing field coupling by dynamically aligning prompt norms to VLM native scale for joint optimization.
contribution: Without complex designs, matches leading decoupled approaches on 15 datasets across 4 settings, offering new perspective and practical solution to local-optima dilemma in prompt learning.
