problem: Building multimodal Transformers on Spiking Neural Networks is hindered by unstable training in deep spiking stacks and mismatch between dense softmax attention and spike-based communication.
approach: SMM Transformer combines: (i) Parallel LIF neuron with Multistage Learnable Parameters and P-STBP algorithm for training stability, (ii) spike-driven attention approximation with lightweight self-compensation, (iii) spiking mixture-of-experts for modality fusion.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracy vs ANN baselines while reducing estimated compute energy of attention module up to 97% under standard MAC/AC cost model on visual and multimodal benchmarks.

problem: GFlowNets for molecular generation must truncate trajectory length in vast chemical space, conflating incomplete fragments with valid molecules and distorting learned distribution.
approach: LeakGFN uses dual-head architecture decomposing flow into: chemical head modeling full space and valid head estimating reachability fraction, with valid head implicitly learning molecular accessibility.
contribution: Proves LeakGFN recovers correct distribution over accessible molecules under mild assumptions; achieves sota on 4 of 5 molecular optimization tasks with plug-and-play integration into existing frameworks.

problem: Existing online change-point detection methods rely on fixed-dimensional Euclidean summaries, obscuring important changes in distributional shape or geometry.
approach: Proposes intrinsic distribution-valued CPD treating streaming batch data as stochastic process on 2-Wasserstein space, mapping distributions to tangent space relative to pre-change Fréchet barycenter for reference-centered linearization.
contribution: Detects complex distributional shifts with reduced detection delay at matched ARL0 compared with moments-based and model-free baselines through sequential detectors on tangent fields.

problem: Multimodal models face two obstacles: collecting large-scale paired datasets is impractical, and existing representations entangle shared and modality-specific information, hindering interpretability.
approach: MultiLoReFT extends low-rank adaptation to multimodal setting with pretrained unimodal models, learning interpretable projection subspaces that decouple shared and modality-specific information.
contribution: Produces multimodal representations supporting prediction while explicitly revealing distributed shared and modality-specific information across modalities on simulated and real-world benchmarks.

problem: Evolutionary multi-view classification assumes noise-free training labels, but label noise introduces fitness evaluation bias that misguides evolutionary search toward local optima.
approach: GFD-EMVC proposes detect-then-calibrate data purification using outlier analysis in gradient space to identify noisy samples and prototype calibration in feature space to correct labels.
contribution: Effectively purifies data and alleviates fitness evaluation bias, improving performance of various multi-view learning paradigms in label noise scenarios.

problem: Continual learning with pre-trained models faces critical challenges like catastrophic forgetting and parameter interference without historical data, with existing methods overlooking loss landscape sharpness and singular value alignment.
approach: SAIM framework with Sharpness-Aware Block Coordinate Descent optimizer guiding toward flatter minima and adaptive isotropic merging balancing singular value spectrum across tasks.
contribution: Achieves 5-10% higher accuracy than existing methods while maintaining robust performance as task count increases, with code available.

problem: Aligning LLMs to heterogeneous and rapidly evolving safety requirements remains critical; existing instruction-tuned models and standalone classifiers fail to generalize to new safety configurations.
approach: CSRM jointly optimizes calibrated safety compliance and reward modeling with configuration-targeted data augmentation enforcing instruction adherence while preserving severity structure.
contribution: Achieves sota on CoSApien (94.6% F1) and DynaBench (75.8% F1) without additional annotation; yields downstream LLMs with improved helpfulness-safety tradeoff when used for safety alignment.

problem: Video predictive models for robotics operate on 2D sequences, inherently lacking 3D geometric understanding necessary for precise spatial reasoning and physical consistency.
approach: Structured 4D Latent Predictive Model predicts evolution of scene 3D structure in structured latent space conditioned on observations and textual instructions, decodable into diverse 3D formats.
contribution: Generates futures with strong visual quality and substantially better 3D consistency and multi-view coherence vs sota video-based planners; achieves superior manipulation performance with robust generalization to novel conditions.

problem: Bridging sim2real gap between inexpensive models and complex physical systems remains central challenge, especially in multi-scale settings where reduced-order models capture only dominant dynamics.
approach: Cheap2Rich combines fast low-fidelity prior with learned interpretable discrepancy corrections via multi-scale data assimilation, demonstrated on rotating detonation engines coupling detonation-front, injector effects, and stiff chemistry.
contribution: Successfully reconstructs high-fidelity RDE states from sparse measurements while isolating physically meaningful discrepancy dynamics, providing general framework for complex multi-scale systems.

problem: While continuous-time RL shows empirical success, its instance-dependent behavior and ability to adapt to varying problem difficulty remain poorly understood.
approach: Develop model-based algorithm built on maximum likelihood estimation estimating state marginal density rather than dynamics directly, with randomized measurement schedule adapting to problem complexity.
contribution: Establishes instance-dependent regret bound scaling with total reward variance and measurement resolution; regret becomes independent of measurement strategy when observation frequency adapts appropriately.

problem: Decentralized optimization requires both resilience against Byzantine attackers and faster convergence on sparse networks, but existing methods fail to achieve both simultaneously.
approach: BRED integrates Byzantine-robust Exact Diffusion within scaled dual ascent framework, mitigating error accumulation; momentum variant BRED-M further reduces complexity.
contribution: Achieves linear speedup with transient complexity O((1-λ)^-2) and Byzantine-affected complexity reduced from O(δ²(1-λ)^-6) to O(δ²(1-λ)^-4), demonstrated on benchmark datasets.

problem: Training transformers that behave like optimization descent algorithms typically uses standard empirical risk minimization without enforcing monotonic loss decrease across layers.
approach: Introduce constrained optimization framework enforcing layerwise descent constraints on objective and replacing ERM with primal-dual training scheme yielding intermediate representations decreasing loss monotonically.
contribution: Constrained transformers achieve stronger robustness to perturbations and maintain higher out-of-distribution generalization while preserving competitive in-distribution performance on video denoising and text classification.

problem: Sparse Autoencoders extract LLM features with hyperparameter L0 (average firing features per token) treated as free parameter, but incorrect L0 causes SAE feature disentanglement failures.
approach: Study L0 effects showing too-low L0 mixes features for reconstruction while too-high L0 finds degenerate mixing solutions; present proxy metric guiding L0 search using toy models and sparse probing.
contribution: Most commonly used SAEs have L0 too low; practitioners must set L0 correctly to train monosemantic SAEs, with proxy metric helping find correct value on given distribution.

problem: Recent work shows vanilla transformer context impact via rank-1 MLP weight patches, but generalization to modern LLM architectures with diverse components remains uncharacterized.
approach: Provide precise analytical solution for Gemma-style blocks mapping entire context effect to rank-1 MLP patches and RMSNorm scale patches, generalizing via framework centered on input/output controllability.
contribution: Proves perfect implicit weight patch possible for any MLP block with input-controllable inner and output-controllable outer functions, extending to gating, norms, mixture of experts, and sequential/parallel blocks.

problem: Point cloud registration faces distinct challenges in rigid vs non-rigid settings due to multi-scale discrepancy between global transformation consistency and local deformation, resisting unified approaches.
approach: RGGT uses generative-prior-guided Transformer with coordinated design across representation, architecture, and supervision: generative priors enrich features, Global-Self-Cross Attention models multi-scale reasoning, dual objective provides consistent supervision.
contribution: Achieves sota accuracy on rigid (ModelNet40, 3DMatch, KITTI) and non-rigid (4DMatch) benchmarks within single unified framework, demonstrating multi-scale geometric-semantic capture.

problem: Offline multi-agent RL with sparse rewards faces brittleness: dense intrinsic rewards alter underlying Markov game while world-model guidance amplifies model bias.
approach: SOLAR proposes simulate-evaluate-shape framework with learned world model enabling low-cost plateau testing; once plateau detected via statistical validation, injects potential-based shaping with uncertainty-aware throttling.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis on policy invariance and plateau decision deviation; consistent gains in stability and final performance across sparse-reward offline MARL benchmarks with varying dataset quality.

problem: Private text generation methods via LLMs are severely inefficient: data-intensive, computationally slow, requiring large private corpora or batch sizes to achieve usable quality.
approach: EPSVec steers LLM generation using dataset vectors—directions in activation space capturing distributional gap—extracted once then used for standard decoding, enabling arbitrarily many samples without additional privacy cost.
contribution: Outperforms baselines in distributional alignment and downstream utility particularly in low-data regimes while significantly reducing computational overhead; differential privacy preserved throughout.

problem: Semantic watermarks embedding information in latent diffusion model noise are vulnerable to black-box forgery attacks, but existing methods lack rigorous theoretical understanding of attack conditions.
approach: Analyze attacks through rate-distortion lens in latent space, identifying irreducible distortion floor from structural proxy-target mismatches; characterize as structured geometric deviations (global drift and local deformation).
contribution: Propose scheme-agnostic detection distinguishing forged samples before verification; demonstrate effectiveness across diverse black-box scenarios while preserving robustness to common distortions.

problem: Discovering analytical solutions to differential equations requires expert intuition or exhaustive combinatorial search; data-driven approaches struggle with requiring large training data.
approach: SIGS uses context-free grammar generating mathematically valid blocks, embeds into topology-regularized continuous latent manifold, searches via structure selection then coefficient refinement against PDE residual and boundary conditions.
contribution: First neuro-symbolic method to recover analytical solutions for coupled nonlinear PDE systems and discover equivalent symbolic forms; improves over existing symbolic methods by orders of magnitude.

problem: Existing low-rank approximation for LLM compression focuses on minimizing individual layer output error without considering Transformer architecture, introducing runtime overhead from decomposed matrices.
approach: A3 splits Transformer layer into QK, OV, and MLP components, providing analytical solutions reducing hidden dimension size while minimizing component functional loss without introducing runtime overheads.
contribution: LLaMA 3.1-70B low-rank approximation achieves 4.69 perplexity on WikiText-2, outperforming sota 7.87; versatile applications in KV cache compression and quantization integration.

problem: Timestep embeddings in diffusion models are underexplored for security risks and malicious information injection despite containing substantial representational capacity.
approach: Shadow Timestep Embedding (STE) investigates temporal space for information injection, analyzing timestep embeddings as position-encoding with mutual coherence evaluation explaining separability of disjoint intervals.
contribution: Reveals timestep as powerful side channel for carrying dedicated information; timestep exhibits distinct representational capabilities encoding side-channel information usable for attack and defense.

problem: Large gap exists between best upper bound O(S^7 A^7) for replicable RL with exploration and O(S^2 A^2) for batch setting, raising questions whether replicable exploration is inherently expensive.
approach: Develop replicable RL algorithm on O(S^2 A) samples for low-horizon tabular MDPs by (nearly) resolving exploration-replicability interaction; complement with O(Ω(S^2)) lower bound.
contribution: Shows exploration is not significant barrier to replicable learning, nearly bridging gap between generative and episodic settings for sample-efficient replicable RL.

problem: Existing sparse matrix-vector multiplication methods perform poorly on the low, unstructured sparsity (30-90%) commonly found in pruned LLMs, making unstructured pruning impractical for real-world deployment.
approach: MACKO-SpMV co-designs a GPU-optimized sparse format and kernel that reduces storage overhead while aligning with GPU execution models, treating memory bandwidth as the primary bottleneck.
contribution: MACKO achieves 1.5× memory reduction and 1.2-1.5× speedup at 50% sparsity compared to dense baselines, making unstructured pruning practical and bridging the gap with structured 2:4 sparsity.

problem: 4-bit quantization severely degrades LLM accuracy because existing decomposition methods minimize real-valued energy rather than post-quantization error.
approach: TwinQuant learns quantization-friendly decomposed subspaces via joint optimization over Stiefel and general linear manifolds, flattening distributions and reducing dynamic-range imbalance, with a fused dual-component kernel to avoid intermediate global-memory traffic.
contribution: TwinQuant preserves near-FP16 accuracy across LLaMA3 and Qwen3 models and delivers up to 1.8× end-to-end speedup over FP16 baseline.

problem: LLM-based automated heuristic design for combinatorial optimization relies on fixed evolutionary rules and static prompts, leading to myopic generation and redundant evaluations.
approach: PathWise formulates heuristic generation as sequential decision-making over an entailment graph (compact memory of search trajectory), using policy, world model, and critic agents to shift from trial-and-error to state-aware planning.
contribution: PathWise converges faster to better heuristics, generalizes across LLM backbones, and scales to larger problem sizes.

problem: It is unclear whether large-scale video encoders rely on factorized physical state variables or task-specific distributed representations for physical reasoning.
approach: First mechanistic interpretability study combining layerwise probing, subspace geometry, patch-level decoding, and targeted attention ablations to map where physical information is organized in video models.
contribution: Identifies Physics Emergence Zone at intermediate depth where physical variables become linearly accessible; shows direction is encoded as circular high-dimensional population code requiring dozens of orthogonal dimensions.

problem: LLMs excel on data-rich platforms like CUDA but suffer catastrophic performance drops (11% accuracy) on data-scarce ecosystems like NPU programming.
approach: EvoKernel formulates kernel synthesis as memory-based reinforcement learning with a value-driven retrieval mechanism that learns stage-specific Q-values, enabling cross-task memory sharing to generalize from simple to complex operators.
contribution: Improves NPU kernel synthesis correctness from 11.0% to 83.0% and achieves median 3.60× speedup through iterative refinement on KernelBench.

problem: All-in-One Image Restoration faces conflicting optimization objectives across heterogeneous degradations; coarse-grained control and fixed mapping schedules yield suboptimal adaptation.
approach: UDBM reformulates image restoration as stochastic transport steered by pixel-wise uncertainty, using a relaxed diffusion bridge to resolve drift singularity and dual modulation (noise and path schedules) to guide diverse degradations into shared latent space.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse restoration tasks within a single inference step.

problem: Continual Offline RL struggles with heterogeneous environment dynamics, reward functions, and behavior policies across tasks; flat knowledge sharing fails to capture task-specific distinctions.
approach: HTAC balances plasticity and stability via dual-level task encoding and soft composition: hierarchical semantic task representation, dual-level expert networks, adaptive knowledge composition, and task adapters.
contribution: HTAC outperforms baselines on Offline Continual World, demonstrating better knowledge reuse and transfer capabilities.

problem: Synthesizing synchronized, high-fidelity long-form audio from silent video requires overcoming audio-visual alignment and generating unconstrained-length sequences efficiently.
approach: SALSA-V uses masked diffusion for audio-conditioned generation and introduces shortcut loss to achieve rapid generation in as few as eight sampling steps.
contribution: SALSA-V significantly outperforms existing methods in audiovisual alignment, synchronization, and enables near-real-time applications without dedicated fine-tuning.

problem: Translating natural language design rules into correct DRC scripts is labor-intensive and requires specialized expertise; existing benchmarks use small evaluation sets and rely on code similarity rather than execution correctness.
approach: Rule2DRC provides a large-scale benchmark (1,000 tasks, 13,921 layouts) with execution-based scoring and proposes SplitTester, a tester agent using execution feedback to generate discriminative test cases.
contribution: Benchmark enables execution-correct evaluation; SplitTester substantially improves Best-of-N selection performance via generated discriminative test cases.

problem: Evaluating and benchmarking GNNs lacks a principled methodology; existing approaches do not capture meaningful structural properties needed for ranking architectures.
approach: Novel benchmarking via graph alignment problem (generalizes graph isomorphism), generating synthetic and real-world datasets with increasing difficulty to rank GNN performance.
contribution: Demonstrates optimal task difficulty for statistically relevant architecture ranking; shows learned node embeddings function as effective positional encodings for transformers with 98% graph reconstruction accuracy.

problem: Repository agents encounter a reasoning disconnect due to fragmented representations that lack semantic depth and rely on isolated API documentation or dependency graphs.
approach: RPG-Encoder generalizes Repository Planning Graph into a unified high-fidelity representation via three mechanisms: encoding raw code into RPG with semantic features, evolving topology incrementally to reduce overhead 95.7%, and operating as unified interface.
contribution: Achieves 93.7% Acc@5 on SWE-bench Verified (10% better than baselines), 98.5% reconstruction coverage on RepoCraft, enabling fine-grained localization in complex codebases.

problem: Neuromorphic event cameras produce asynchronous sparse data that existing methods either densify (losing efficiency) or handle with irregular models incompatible with GPU acceleration.
approach: event2vec, inspired by word-to-vector models, enables Transformers to process events directly with parameter efficiency and GPU compatibility.
contribution: Achieves high accuracy on DVS benchmarks even with extremely low event counts or spatial resolutions; enables sparse asynchronous data integration into high-throughput Transformer architectures.

problem: Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for 3D vision overlook intrinsic geometric and topological information in point cloud data.
approach: TopAdapter leverages algebraic topology (0D, 1D, 2D simplices) via Topology Injection (multi-scale topological features with geometric controller) and Topology Transfer (propagation across Transformer layers).
contribution: TopAdapter outperforms existing PEFT methods and achieves performance comparable to full fine-tuning across point cloud benchmarks.

problem: Text embedding development is exclusionary: prohibitive computational costs, narrow linguistic focus neglecting most languages, and lack of transparency from closed-source models hinder research.
approach: ML-Embed introduces 3-Dimensional Matryoshka Learning combining Matryoshka Representation Learning (storage), Matryoshka Layer Learning (depth), and Matryoshka Embedding Learning (parameter efficiency), trained on massively multilingual dataset.
contribution: ML-Embed sets new records on 9 of 17 MTEB benchmarks with particularly strong results in low-resource languages; releases all models, data, and code.

problem: Grounded Visual Reasoning with MLLMs lacks effective learning signals for intermediate grounding decisions and is prone to shortcut solutions.
approach: CofactGVR decomposes GVR into Evidence Generation and Counterfactual Answer Reasoning via Causal Grounding Graph; uses matched counterfactual intervention to perturb regions while keeping context fixed, yielding principled intermediate bonus.
contribution: Consistent improvements across GVR benchmarks via counterfactual rewards that strengthen evidence-faithful reasoning under controlled interventions.

problem: Fine-grained image-text alignment in CLIP remains challenging despite strong global performance; region- and pixel-level visual grounding is overlooked.
approach: PixCLIP jointly enhances both visual and textual sides via automated annotation pipeline (long-form descriptions with pixel-level localization), LongGRIT dataset (1.5M samples), and three-branch pixel-text alignment framework.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art pixel- and region-level alignment while preserving strong global retrieval performance on arbitrarily-shaped region prompts.

problem: MLLM-powered embodied agents lack explicit mechanisms for identifying hazards and reasoning about action-conditioned risks, leading to missed or over-identified risks.
approach: EMBGuard decouples physical risk reasoning from agent policy by evaluating (observation, action) pairs to identify hazards and provide natural language risk explanations.
contribution: Compact 2B/4B models achieve performance competitive with proprietary MLLMs while significantly reducing false-positive rates for real-time deployment.

problem: RL-based image-editing agents with dense proxy rewards optimize for numerically measurable yet perceptually negligible edits rather than meaningful progress.
approach: B-Spar combines prior-guided trajectory sampling, Bayesian reward modeling to densify sparse binary feedback, and anchor-regularized policy optimization to steer updates toward high-reward regions.
contribution: Improves perceptual quality by 95% over AIGC baselines and ~33.5% over state-of-the-art with stable training.

problem: At high action frequencies (60Hz), action chunking fails to generate temporally smooth and spatially consistent robot actions.
approach: Shifts high-frequency action learning to latent space via VAE; introduces Reuse-then-Refine strategy for smooth chunk-level continuity under asynchronous inference.
contribution: Enables robots to execute complex contact-rich tasks continuously with less pauses and jerky motions compared to action-space baselines.

problem: Attribution robustness is fundamental for reliable explainability yet existing approaches rely on computationally expensive explicit regularization.
approach: Shows attribution robustness arises implicitly from learning dynamics of standard SGD through connections between parameter-space and input-space curvature; proves softmax attention lacks this benefit but kernel-based attention restores it.
contribution: Reveals learning dynamics as principled mechanism for robust explainability with negligible computational overhead; identifies fundamental limitations of softmax attention.

problem: Existing spectral operators decompose higher-order topology into separate ranks, requiring ad-hoc fusion to recover vertex-level information.
approach: Introduces Collapsed Effective Operators that condense higher-order degrees of freedom into single vertex-level operator via Schur complementation of graded Laplacian.
contribution: Operator encodes long-range interactions, preserves positive semi-definiteness with strict spectral upper bound, and improves spectral clustering and signal smoothing.

problem: MLLMs struggle with numerical regression under longtailed distributions due to token-level SFT and point-wise rewards biasing toward high-density regions.
approach: Distribution-aware reinforcement learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization with batch-level comparison supervision using Concordance Correlation Coefficient reward.
contribution: Consistent improvements over SFT and existing methods with particularly strong gains in medium- and few-shot regimes; plug-and-play without architectural modification.

problem: Speculative decoding suffers from draft models poorly approximating target distribution, resulting in shorter acceptance lengths and diminished speedup.
approach: OnlineSPEC leverages verification feedback from speculative decoding as online learning signal, using optimistic online learning for adaptive draft updates and online ensemble for dynamic multi-draft maintenance.
contribution: Achieves up to 24% speedup over seven benchmarks via principled online learning framework with theoretical dynamic regret justification.

problem: Foundation models generate unreliable answers and heuristic uncertainty estimators fail to fully distinguish correct from incorrect outputs without statistical guarantees.
approach: LEC reframes selective prediction via linear expectation constraint over selection and error indicators to control marginal error probability conditioned on selection; extends to two-model routing.
contribution: Maintains prescribed risk level in accepted predictions while substantially improving sample retention compared to baselines across QA and VQA tasks.

problem: Existing multimodal time series forecasting benchmarks suffer from poor generalization due to small scale, synthetic data, limited textual context diversity, and data leakage.
approach: Introduces TimesX, context-enriched benchmark via automated data generation pipeline providing high-quality real-world series with diverse textual contexts.
contribution: Simple ensemble methods leveraging rich textual context outperform strong baselines; reveals many approaches that perform well on existing benchmarks fail on TimesX.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning is computationally efficient but yields inferior generalization compared to RL, primarily due to RL's use of on-policy data.
approach: Distribution Discriminant Theory quantifies alignment between data and model-induced distribution; proposes In-Distribution Finetuning (loss-level) and Hinted Decoding (data-level) to enable On-Policy SFT.
contribution: On-Policy SFT achieves generalization performance on par with prominent offline RL algorithms while maintaining SFT efficiency.

problem: Graph Masked Auto-Encoder methods emphasize reconstruction outcomes without clearly specifying neighborhood context usage, causing performance variations despite similar outcomes.
approach: C2-GMAE ensures consistent neighborhood context use via positional encoding reference, density-partitioned masking for coverage improvement, and heterophilic edge amplification.
contribution: C2-GMAE improves downstream performance over GMAE baselines by ensuring consistent use of structural information.

problem: Test-time scaling via speculative decoding suffers from memory-bound bottleneck and sequential-dependent token selection that limits serving efficiency under high concurrency.
approach: AsyncSpade uses light-weight temporal-regressive module to predict next-token query state and asynchronous disaggregated framework that decouples KV cache selection from auto-regressive loop.
contribution: Overlaps token-level KV selection with inference computation via asynchronism, eliminating sequential dependency while maintaining performance.

problem: Multivariate time series forecasting faces a trade-off: channel-isolation suffers from information fragmentation while channel-interaction introduces spurious dependencies.
approach: Crisp derives spectral priors in frequency domain to construct dynamic resonance topologies; uses adaptive sparse blocking to force attention weights for spectrally-inconsistent neighbors to zero.
contribution: Significantly outperforms 20+ baselines by only modeling interactions between variables with compatible oscillatory patterns.

problem: Clustering-based features rely on a fixed, global resolution parameter; varying resolution produces finite stable partitions (configurations) but most methods choose arbitrarily.
approach: Configuration-Mixed Prediction learns to adaptively weight configurations per sample; MixConfig module extracts configurations and learns energy-aware mixing via selector reasoning about context, assignments, and stability.
contribution: Consistent improvements across tabular, molecular, vision, and text domains with particularly pronounced gains in low-data regimes.

problem: Vision-Language Models inherit social biases from pretraining; test-time debiasing methods rely on point-based corrections that are unstable and weak in multi-class settings.
approach: W4D reframes fairness as distributional alignment (Wasserstein distance) between query and group reference distributions; uses probabilistic prompts for controlled perturbations.
contribution: Improves robustness in multi-class debiasing with stronger fairness-utility trade-off across diverse VLM evaluations.

problem: Conservation laws characterizing implicit bias of gradient descent are well-understood for linear and ReLU networks but remain unexplored for modern architectures.
approach: Develops unified framework to characterize conservation laws for contemporary models including GELU/SiLU/SwiGLU activations, multihead attention with various positional encodings, and Mixture-of-Experts.
contribution: Identifies conservation invariants across modern architectures with experiments validating predicted invariants.

problem: Existing diffusion language model inference relies on local, immediate-step metrics like confidence/entropy that lack broader perspective, leading to suboptimal generation.
approach: Coherent Contextual Decoding bypasses single-context bias by leveraging historical contexts to approximate marginal token prediction distribution; equivalent to modeling consistency via conditional mutual information.
contribution: Achieves simultaneous enhancement in both inference speed and performance with milder degradation under highly parallel decoding.

problem: As AI enters institutional workflows, workers must decide whether to delegate to AI and how to verify outputs; outcome-based evaluation may misalign with worker costs.
approach: Models delegation and verification as rational worker optimization; characterizes optimal workflows and shows AI induces phase transitions.
contribution: Identifies structural mechanism where AI can amplify quality disparities despite improving baseline task success by incentivizing workers with weaker verification to over-delegate.

problem: Actor-critic reinforcement learning methods offer limited interpretability and treat state features equally without accounting for heterogeneous feature impacts.
approach: RSA2C, an RKHS-SHAP-based attribution-aware AC algorithm with Actor/Value/Advantage critics in vector/scalar RKHS with Mahalanobis-weighted kernels; state attributions modulate gradients.
contribution: Achieves efficiency, stability, and interpretability with global non-asymptotic convergence bound under state perturbations.

problem: The volume hypothesis (low-loss basins with good generalization occupy larger weight space) conflicts with random sampling experiments yet is supported by molecular dynamics estimates.
approach: Uses Replica Exchange Wang-Landau algorithm to estimate joint density of states over training and test accuracies in binary networks across different dataset size regimes.
contribution: Shows generalization advantage of gradient learning over random sampling diminishes with larger training data, resolving apparent paradox.

problem: Offline multi-objective optimization suffers from out-of-distribution issue where surrogate models are inaccurate for unseen designs, causing bias toward Pareto front extremes.
approach: DOMOO incorporates accumulative risk control module and nested Pareto set learning to adapt to diverse geometries; uses diversity-driven selection with IGD-offline metric.
contribution: Finds diverse high-quality solution sets in offline MOO setting with improved robustness to surrogate errors.

problem: Evaluating Bayesian imaging models without ground truth is challenging; existing unsupervised methods are computationally expensive and incompatible with machine-learning-based implicit priors.
approach: Combines Bayesian cross-validation and data fission (randomized measurement splitting) for unsupervised model selection and misspecification detection compatible with any Bayesian imaging sampler.
contribution: Achieves excellent selection and detection accuracy with low computational cost across various scoring rules and misspecification types.

problem: LLMs excel at long-context understanding but exhibit significant limitations and volatility in long-form generation, with inconsistent length and content across generations.
approach: VOLTBench benchmark quantifies length volatility; attention trace analysis identifies internal patterns causing volatility; SELB (Structural Enforcement via Logits Boosting) is a lightweight decoding-stage strategy.
contribution: SELB improves mean output length by 148% and reduces volatility by 69% without additional training.

problem: False discovery rate control often fails to guarantee reliability of marginal discoveries at rejection set boundaries; existing methods rely on restrictive assumptions.
approach: Proposes k-bFDR to control error probability of k least significant discoveries; Domino framework guarantees k-bFDR control under arbitrary dependence via closure principle.
contribution: Achieves rigorous k-bFDR control while identifying higher-quality rejection sets with greater practical significance.

problem: Detecting AI-generated videos is difficult because pixel-domain methods overlook generative artifacts encoded in compressed bitstreams.
approach: STREAM operates directly on compressed bitstreams, using I-frames, motion vectors, and residual errors to detect spatiotemporal artifacts through a motion-guided alignment module and gated fusion mechanism.
contribution: Achieves SOTA detection with mAP of 0.965 and 2.5× faster inference than previous baselines.

problem: Evaluating causal claims is hard without ground truth, especially when assessing collections of bivariate statements.
approach: Develops a compatibility score that quantifies plausibility of induced multivariate causal models by measuring implausible additional confounding, without requiring faithfulness.
contribution: Provides theoretical and empirical evidence that compatibility and incompatibility scores distinguish correct from incorrect causal statements, with application to evaluating LLM-generated causal claims.

problem: Low-rank Hankel matrix completion requires balancing first-order algorithmic efficiency with fast convergence independent of condition number.
approach: Uses Jacobi-preconditioned gradient descent with a generator mapping factor-based iterates to matrix space, establishing equivalence with manifold-based methods.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence independent of condition number while maintaining low per-iteration complexity across broad problem settings.

problem: Current LLM agent privacy defenses are static and reactive, failing to support proactive context-aware privacy decisions during multi-step execution.
approach: Proposes Contextualized Defense Instructing (CDI) where an instructor model generates step-specific privacy guidance via reinforcement learning, trained on failure trajectories.
contribution: CDI achieves 94.2% privacy preservation and 80.6% helpfulness with superior robustness to adversarial conditions compared to baseline defenses.

problem: Federated learning under non-IID data suffers from bias toward skewed majority clients when using fixed neighborhood structures for skew estimation.
approach: FedVeer uses self-adaptive kernel density estimation with k-free neighborhoods determined via max-margin learning, plus Kalman filtering for stability.
contribution: Achieves up to 6.36% accuracy improvement and reduces noise-induced degradation by up to 6.01% on real-world datasets.

problem: Graph transport methods fail to generalize across sparse topologies and scale poorly with graph size and time horizon.
approach: GSBoG learns executable controlled continuous-time Markov chain policies on arbitrary graphs via likelihood optimization of trajectory-level behaviors under state cost augmented dynamics.
contribution: Reliably learns accurate, topology-respecting policies optimizing application-specific intermediate state costs on real-world graph topologies.

problem: Continual learning methods that mitigate forgetting often suffer from singular value collapse in gradients, reducing model plasticity.
approach: PAPO augments gradients with polar operators to activate suppressed directions: G ← G + λ·polar(G), approximated via Polar Express using only matrix operations.
contribution: On MiniImageNet, PAPO integrated into ER, MAS, GPM, and TRGP produces accuracy gains of 9.01%, 4.76%, 8.90%, and 9.19% respectively.

problem: Chain-of-thought monitoring for AI agents may be fragile under different training procedures and scaling, yet its reliability is underexplored.
approach: Proposes three evaluation archetypes (intervention, process, outcome-property), studies monitorability across model sizes and reasoning compute, and tests if follow-up questions improve monitoring.
contribution: Shows frontier models are generally monitorable, longer CoTs improve monitorability, and smaller models at higher reasoning effort can achieve better monitoring at greater cost.

problem: AI training carbon emissions lack systematic accounting methods, leaving questions about current and future environmental impact.
approach: Estimates aggregate training emissions of Hugging Face open-source models using metadata with tiered handling of incomplete disclosure, introduces AI Training Carbon Intensity (ATCI) metric.
contribution: Shows training popular open-source models resulted in approximately 6.0×10^4 metric tons of carbon emissions, providing scalable framework for emission estimation.

problem: Statement autoformalization treats formal code as flat sequences, neglecting the hierarchical logic inherent in mathematical statements.
approach: DSR decomposes statements into logical components, maps them to structured operator trees, and uses sub-tree refinement to localize and repair errors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on PRIME benchmark of 156 theorems, consistently outperforming baselines under equivalent computational budgets.

problem: Disentangling memorization from generalization in language models is difficult, making model capacity estimates unreliable.
approach: Proposes method that separates memorization into unintended memorization and generalization by eliminating generalization, enabling total memorization measurement.
contribution: Estimates GPT-style models have capacity of approximately 3.6 bits per parameter; models memorize until capacity fills then transition to generalization.

problem: Model upscaling can be sensitive to hyperparameters at target size, and scaling law extrapolation from smaller models is theoretically unclear.
approach: Introduces principled width-based upscaling using theoretically grounded, width-dependent scalings for perturbation and optimizer hyperparameters based on μP theory.
contribution: Proves upscaled models are functionally equivalent under zero perturbation and establishes hyperparameter transfer enabling efficient tuning with reduced cost.

problem: Converting pretrained Softmax attention to linear-complexity attention causes severe accuracy degradation due to representational gap.
approach: SD3.5-T^5 uses Test-Time Training with structural alignment to Softmax attention and architectural modifications (key instance normalization, locality enhancement) for representational alignment.
contribution: Linearizes Stable Diffusion 3.5 with comparable quality at 1.32× and 1.47× speedup at 1K and 2K resolutions using only 1 hour fine-tuning on 4 H20 GPUs.

problem: Existing adaptive methods like Adam use coordinate-wise adaptation unsuitable for matrix optimization, while spectral methods lack connection to variance adaptation.
approach: DeVA reformulates AdaGrad into decoupled variance adaptation and scale-invariant terms, bridging vector-based and matrix spectral optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Muon and SOAP, reducing token usage by around 6.6% on language modeling and image classification.

problem: Long-horizon interactive agent benchmarks underrepresent global constraints, multi-tool coordination, and adapting to evolving user behavior.
approach: TRIP-Bench offers travel-planning scenarios with real-world data, 18 tools, 40+ requirements, and spans up to 15 user turns with 150+ tool calls; proposes GTPO online RL method.
contribution: Even advanced models achieve at most 50% on easy split; GTPO improves constraint satisfaction and robustness in Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.

problem: Semi-supervised inference in biomedical research struggles with unstructured data and covariate misalignment across datasets.
approach: Integrates LLMs to extract features from unstructured data with systematic pseudo-label calibration via novel prediction-invariance identification strategy.
contribution: Improves parameter estimation efficiency while maintaining full statistical validity despite mismatched covariates between labeled and unlabeled datasets.

problem: Functional equivalence in Transformers is complex due to positional encodings, and their effect on model expressivity and mode connectivity is unclear.
approach: Provides formal analysis of functional equivalence with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings (RoPE), showing RoPE reduces symmetry group.
contribution: Shows sinusoidal encodings preserve vanilla attention equivalence while rotary encodings enhance expressivity, explaining RoPE's growing prominence.

problem: Semi-supervised 3D medical segmentation progress is clouded by confirmation bias in pseudo-labeling and overfitting via test-set validation.
approach: Proposes TCSeg with tri-space calibration decoupling confidence from uncertainty, collaboratively correcting bias across feature, probability, and image spaces.
contribution: Delivers strong performance under existing protocols; advocates for multiple-run reporting to establish more rigorous benchmarks with realistic perspective.

problem: Token-wise temperature scaling in discrete sequence models induces bias in MAP estimates and is not tractable for sequence-level adjustment.
approach: Proposes fine-tuning objectives for sequence-level temperature scaling unified across autoregressive and diffusion models, with metrics based on likelihood ratios.
contribution: Achieves consistent generation with lower perplexity on GPT2 and BD3LM; provides evidence of enhanced reasoning performance.

problem: Lean theorem-proving benchmarks are treated as reliable despite potential dataset defects and evaluation failures that inflate or deflate scores.
approach: Audits five widely used benchmarks with corpus-scale static checkers, surfaces 4,833 findings including 398 mechanically certified issues (counterexamples, vacuous theorems, unsound axioms).
contribution: Proposes fault taxonomy, automated checkers, semantic audit prompts, and standards for formal math dataset creation; releases corrected snapshots.

problem: Quantization hyperparameter effects (bit width, range) on learning dynamics and STE training remain largely unexplored.
approach: Shows STE dynamics converge to a deterministic ODE in high-dimensional limit, with plateau length depending on quantization range.
contribution: Reveals STE training exhibits plateau then sharp drop in error; fixed-point analysis quantifies asymptotic deviation from unquantized models.

problem: Directly sparsifying pretrained dense attention into dilated patterns causes severe accuracy loss, preventing flexible inference-time reuse.
approach: RAT+ trains densely with full-sequence recurrence and active recurrence learning, then switches at inference to dilated or hybrid compositions with minimal adaptation.
contribution: At 1.5B parameters, matches dense accuracy at D=16 and drops 2-3 points at D=64; achieves 64× reduction in attention FLOPs and KV cache at D=64.

problem: Post-Training Quantization for diffusion LLMs is prone to frontier decision flips that are irreversibly locked in, causing cascading errors.
approach: FAIR-Calib uses two-stage PTQ with position prior combining frontier hits and reliability, performing layer-wise calibration on reweighted hidden-state MSE.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on LLaDA and Dream (W4A4), significantly reducing frontier flips and post-commit mismatches.

problem: Separate estimation of multiple dynamic treatment policies prevents information sharing, inducing structurally uncontrolled second-order bias.
approach: PEQ-Net uses policy-aware reparameterization of Q-functions with shared policy encoder trained via kernel mean embeddings, followed by LTMLE correction.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing ICE-based methods with substantial RMSE reductions, particularly when evaluating closely related policies.

problem: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards faces tradeoff between token-level fine-grained credit assignment and sequence-level stability.
approach: TGPO integrates sequence anchors aligning updates with stable reference and trust-based information gates modulating token-level signal contribution.
contribution: Consistently enhances learning efficiency across seven mathematical reasoning datasets, improving gradient utilization while maintaining stable optimization.

problem: Creating editable scientific illustrations remains labor-intensive and existing generative models produce raster outputs lacking vector editability.
approach: LiveFigure uses VLM agents imitating multi-step research workflows: planning from references, generating executable PowerPoint scripts, refining with visual diagnostics.
contribution: Achieves 80% publication-readiness in only 17 manual edits versus 24% for baselines; generates fully vectorized, editable publication-ready figures.

problem: High-quality training datasets for reasoning require costly human annotation, and synthesis methods face tradeoff between structural validity and complexity.
approach: Agentic Proposing models synthesis as goal-driven sequential decision where agents dynamically select and compose modular reasoning skills via internal reflection.
contribution: 30B solver trained on 11,000 synthesized trajectories achieves 91.6% on AIME25, rivaling frontier models and demonstrating synthetic data can substitute for massive human curation.

problem: Hypergraph neural networks suffer from rank collapse and hyperedge semantic dependency in two-stage message passing.
approach: MC-HNN introduces multi-channel message passing maintaining high-rank representations and latent hyperedge type encoding injecting independent degrees of freedom.
contribution: Alleviates rank collapse and semantic dependency bottlenecks, achieving strong empirical performance on hypergraph tasks.

problem: Exact posterior computation is intractable, and existing approximate inference methods are computationally expensive or require costly retraining on prior changes.
approach: Distribution Transformer learns distribution-to-distribution mappings using Gaussian Mixture Models with self and cross-attention, enabling prior-to-posterior transformation.
contribution: Reduces computation from minutes to milliseconds while achieving expected log-likelihood performance on par with or superior to existing methods.

problem: Understanding how auto-regressive models learn latent state representations from partially observed linear systems remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Shows two-layer linear auto-regressive models trained by ERM naturally approximate Kalman filtering, with benign optimization landscape and finite-sample guarantees.
contribution: Demonstrates learned hidden representations coincide with Kalman filter state estimates up to similarity transformation, with theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: Language models in healthcare struggle with trustworthiness across low-resource languages despite global adoption needs.
approach: CLINIC benchmarks LMs across truthfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and privacy through 18 diverse tasks spanning 15 languages and healthcare topics.
contribution: Reveals LMs struggle with factual correctness, demonstrate demographic and linguistic bias, and remain vulnerable to privacy breaches and adversarial attacks.

problem: Sequential recommendation models have limited flexibility responding to immediate user requests without costly retraining or inference overhead.
approach: CRAMER treats user requests as control signals modulating frozen backbone parameters through request-aware masking inspired by control theory.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with minimal overhead; exhibits enhanced controllability and cross-domain adaptability.

problem: Distillation claims about efficiency rarely account for full end-to-end energy costs including teacher-side workloads like data generation and evaluation.
approach: Presents comprehensive energy accounting framework tracking GPU power consumption across distillation phases, constructing energy-quality-throughput Pareto frontiers.
contribution: Reveals previously ignored teacher-side costs and derives practical design rules for selecting distillation methods under energy constraints.

problem: Structure-Based Drug Design mismatch between separate continuous and discrete probability paths ignores underlying statistical manifolds.
approach: EvoEGF-Mol represents molecules via composite exponential-family distributions evolving along exponential geodesics under Fisher-Rao metric with dynamic target distributions.
contribution: Approaches reference PoseBusters passing rate of 93.4% on CrossDock with geometric precision, achieving superior performance on real-world MolGenBench tasks.

problem: Layer pruning in LLMs triggers sudden performance collapse, and representation-based analyses fail to explain the mechanism.
approach: Proposes decision representation framework introducing Decision Margin and Option Frequency metrics, partitioning networks into Silent Phase and Decisive Phase.
contribution: Shows pruning Decisive Phase has minimal impact but Silent Phase pruning triggers immediate collapse, revealing extreme sensitivity of decision transition.

problem: Q-learning is slow as values move from initialization near zero to true values, and algorithms update action-values independently without sharing value structure.
approach: Mean-expansion layer shares values across actions within a state and learns lower-norm representation, accelerating learning as parameter-free addition to Q-networks.
contribution: Improves aggregate performance across 57 Atari games, increases action gaps, and dramatically reduces value overestimation.

problem: Low-precision deep learning suffers instability despite energy efficiency gains, requiring better algorithmic stabilization.
approach: Log-Normal Multiplicative Dynamics (LMD) incorporates biological synaptic properties via variational Bayesian formulation with log-normal posterior over weights.
contribution: Successfully trains Vision Transformers and GPT-2 from scratch with low-precision forward-pass multiplications.

problem: Existing SLAM approaches produce maps lacking geometric fidelity required for reliable downstream perception.
approach: UniMapping constructs persistent neural-descriptor map from multimodal observations using Spatial-Aware Deformable Transformer with explicit geometric inductive bias.
contribution: Achieves competitive SLAM performance; significantly enhances downstream tasks with mAP +3.1% and mIoU +7.1% via accumulated multi-view context.

problem: Zeroth-order optimization for LLM fine-tuning relies on hand-crafted static sampling strategies unadapted to model-specific structures.
approach: ZO-Finetuner learns efficient perturbation strategies through compact memory-efficient design, supporting one-time per-model training with reuse across tasks.
contribution: Outperforms prior zeroth-order baselines in 82.1% of task-model combinations across 4 LLMs and 7 datasets.

problem: Multi-objective RL with reactive preference adversaries needs time-consistent robustness models with tractable weight selection dynamics.
approach: Studies Bellman-Isaacs recursion where opponent chooses weights with switching cost based on Bregman divergence, solving via Bregman-prox updates.
contribution: Develops BR-K evaluation testing policies against independent best-response adversaries, improving WRR under step-wise opponents.

problem: Diffusion Language Models achieve strong text generation but require multi-step sampling that is too slow for practical use.
approach: We extend Inverse Distillation to the discrete setting, address uniqueness and gradient stability issues with theoretical guarantees and gradient-stable relaxations.
contribution: IDLM reduces inference steps 4×-64× while preserving generation quality across multiple DLMs.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLMs during decoding enter a memory-bound regime where latency is governed by the number of activated experts even for moderate batch sizes.
approach: We dynamically re-route token-to-expert mapping using batch-aware routing, where tokens piggyback on experts already loaded due to other tokens in the batch.
contribution: OEA reduces MoE-layer decode latency by 39% on Qwen3-30B and 15% on Qwen3-235B with small or no quality loss.

problem: Standard Bayesian Optimization assumes uniform smoothness across search space, but multi-regime problems like molecular conformation search have distinct energy basins where a single GP either oversmooths or hallucinates noise.
approach: RAMBO uses a Dirichlet Process Mixture of Gaussian Processes that discovers latent regimes during optimization, each with locally-optimized hyperparameters and independent GPs.
contribution: Consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on molecular conformer optimization, virtual screening, and fusion reactor design across multi-regime objectives.

problem: Transformer optimization lacks connection between architectural design, activation scales, and stable learning rates, limiting how aggressively models can be trained.
approach: SimpleNorm stabilizes intermediate activation scales by construction and uses Hessian analysis to show it reduces spectral norm, permitting larger learning rates.
contribution: SimpleGPT tolerates learning rates 3×-10× larger than standard convention and achieves better performance; 7B model reaches 2.208 loss vs 2.290 for Llama2-QKNorm in 60K steps.

problem: Scaling Generative Adversarial Networks remains underexplored; naive scaling exposes failure modes including underutilization of early generator layers and increasing optimization instability.
approach: GAT trains purely transformer-based generators and discriminators in VAE latent space with lightweight intermediate supervision and width-aware learning-rate adjustment.
contribution: GAT-XL achieves state-of-the-art single-step class-conditional generation on ImageNet 256×256 with FID 2.18 in 60 epochs, 4× fewer than strong baselines.

problem: Training language models to generate better research plans is difficult; existing approaches lack a scalable way to leverage diverse training data and evaluation signals from research papers.
approach: Automatically extract research goals and rubrics from papers, train models via RL with a frozen initial policy as grader using rubrics to evaluate plans.
contribution: Finetuned Qwen3-30B-A3B generates plans preferred by experts 70% of the time vs initial model and 59.6% vs Grok-4-Thinking, with 12-22% relative gains and cross-domain generalization.

problem: Existing RL paradigms for uncertainty-aware LLMs suffer from Advantage Bias due to binary decision spaces and static uncertainty rewards, causing excessive conservatism or overconfidence.
approach: UCPO employs Ternary Advantage Decoupling to separate and independently normalize deterministic and uncertain rollouts, with Dynamic Uncertainty Reward Adjustment that adapts weights in real-time.
contribution: UCPO effectively resolves reward imbalance and significantly improves model reliability beyond knowledge boundaries on mathematical reasoning and general tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs excel at broad understanding but struggle with fine-grained perception where decisive evidence is small and overwhelmed by global context; iterative zooming is slow.
approach: Transform zooming from inference-time tool to training-time primitive via Region-to-Image Distillation, distilling zoomed region supervision from teacher models into single-pass student prediction.
contribution: Student model improves fine-grained perception without tool use and achieves leading performance on multiple fine-grained benchmarks while improving visual reasoning and GUI agents.

problem: Protein binder design evaluation lacks standardization; reported metrics are difficult to interpret or compare across studies due to non-standardized protocols and evaluation bias.
approach: ProtDBench defines unified benchmark tasks, evaluation protocols, success criteria, and incorporates throughput-aware metrics based on fixed 24-hour budget plus cluster-level diversity criteria.
contribution: Reveals substantial verifier-dependent bias in structure prediction, systematic differences between filtering rules and success definitions, providing fair reproducible evaluation for protein design.

problem: Multi-turn multi-agent LLM game evaluations exhibit substantial run-to-run variance and instability due to small deviations compounding across turns and being amplified by multi-agent coupling.
approach: MEMO treats inference-time context as optimizable object via retention (distilling self-play trajectories into memory bank) and exploration (tournament-style prompt evolution with prioritized replay).
contribution: Raises mean win rate from 25.1% to 49.5% for GPT-4o-mini and 20.9% to 45.0% for Qwen-2.5-7B while reducing run-to-run dispersion, showing headroom in multi-agent game performance.

problem: Sampling from unnormalized densities in discrete space remains underexplored; discrete diffusion samplers don't leverage techniques used in continuous-space sampling and their application to bridging distributions is limited.
approach: Introduce off-policy training techniques for discrete diffusion samplers and generalize to bridging between distributions via data-to-energy Schrödinger bridge training.
contribution: Improved performance on discrete synthetic benchmarks and data-free posterior sampling in discrete latent spaces of image generative models.

problem: Existing audio-video generation treats human-centric tasks (reference-based generation, video editing, audio-driven animation) as isolated objectives, lacking precise disentangled control over multiple characters and voices.
approach: DreamID-Omni uses Symmetric Conditional Diffusion Transformer with Dual-Level Disentanglement: Synchronized RoPE for signal-level binding and Structured Captions for semantic mappings, trained via Multi-Task Progressive Training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art across video, audio, and audio-visual consistency, outperforming leading proprietary models on controllable human-centric audio-video generation.

problem: Jailbreak attacks on LLMs traditionally target single models, but querying multiple models in a wide-net-casting scenario presents overlooked safety risks.
approach: Develop a novel jailbreak method tailored to the wide-net-casting scenario where an adversary can query a group of LLMs instead of single ones.
contribution: Demonstrates that jailbreak success rate reaches 100% in some experiments targeting large models without additional safeguards, exposing wide-net-casting as a high-risk scenario.

problem: LLMs struggle with spatial reasoning about indoor layouts encoded in structured representations; they fail to respect physical constraints and preserve spatial coherence.
approach: FloorplanQA introduces a diagnostic benchmark grounded in structured JSON/XML representations with core spatial tasks including distance, visibility, path finding, and object placement.
contribution: Reveals inconsistent spatial reasoning: models succeed on shallow queries but fail on constrained spaces; mostly robust to small perturbations.

problem: Classical Estimation-of-Distribution Algorithms rely on learning explicit variable dependency graphs which can be costly and fail to capture complex interactions efficiently.
approach: Parameterize multivariate autoregressive generative model without fixed variable ordering; sample random generation orders during training for order invariance; adapt GRPO for scale-invariant advantages.
contribution: Achieves best performance frequently and consistently avoids catastrophic failures across benchmark problems of varying sizes.

problem: Existing multi-view clustering methods require pre-defined cluster number, limiting flexibility when prior knowledge about the true number of clusters is unavailable.
approach: GROK adapts GRPO (RL strategy for LLM reasoning) to unsupervised clustering with agent orchestrating via state perception, group decision with action space divide-and-conquer, and geometric feedback loop.
contribution: Achieves superior clustering performance in unknown-K scenarios by autonomously exploring cluster structure through reward maximization.

problem: Evolution Strategies is parallelizable but becomes prohibitively expensive at scale on GPUs due to low arithmetic intensity of batched matrix multiplications with unstructured random perturbations.
approach: EGGROLL structures individual perturbations as rank-r matrices to improve arithmetic intensity, achieving hundredfold speedup for billion-parameter models while maintaining ES convergence properties.
contribution: Achieves 91% of pure batch inference throughput, enables stable pretraining of nonlinear recurrent LMs, competitive with GRPO on reasoning tasks, and maintains RL performance in tabula rasa settings.

problem: Large Reasoning Models with extended Chain-of-Thought generation create severe KV cache memory bottlenecks from linearly growing sequence length that exceed GPU capacity for long reasoning traces.
approach: BeaconKV maintains beacon queries (compact representatives of global query clusters) to anticipate which KV pairs will be revisited without storing entire query history, using training-free compression.
contribution: Achieves up to 5.8× memory reduction while nearly preserving full cache accuracy and improving throughput over 4.3×.

problem: Curriculum post-training empirically outperforms non-curriculum approaches for LLM reasoning but lacks principled understanding of effectiveness and limitations.
approach: Develop theoretical framework modeling base model CoT as state-conditioned autoregressive reasoning tree; formalize curriculum as depth-increasing or hint-decreasing strategies; analyze RL finetuning sample complexity.
contribution: Proves RL finetuning with both curriculum strategies achieves high accuracy with polynomial complexity whereas non-curriculum encounters exponential bottleneck; empirical simulations support findings.

problem: Text-guided image-to-video generation struggles with executing text-specified edits requiring substantial changes to reference image due to visual dominance causing attention dispersion.
approach: AlignVid re-calibrates model attention distribution via Attention Scaling Modulation to reduce entropy and concentrate on semantic tokens, plus Guidance Scheduling to maintain stability.
contribution: Effectively enhances semantic fidelity with negligible computational overhead across object addition, deletion, and modification benchmarks.

problem: Open-set anomaly detection in time series fails to preserve sequential nature when generating pseudo anomalies via simple augmentation, resulting in trivial patterns; also plagued by unlabeled anomalies in training data.
approach: IMPACT learns influence function to estimate impact of training samples on modeling, then leverages scores to generate realistic unseen anomalies while repurposing high-influential samples for decontamination.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on open-set time series anomaly detection across varying settings and contamination rates.

problem: Diffusion policies provide stochastic diversity but lack precise behavior steering and efficient generalization to novel constraints without retraining.
approach: PDP learns diffusion policy parameterized in smooth continuous space where latent distances reflect semantic similarity of trajectories, enabling precise steering and smooth interpolation.
contribution: Significantly improves adaptation on complex multimodal benchmarks in simulation and real-robot hardware compared to standard diffusion policy, especially for discovering novel behaviors.

problem: Lifting dense 2D foundation-model embeddings into 3D Gaussian Splatting is challenging; existing methods average normalized embeddings in Euclidean space ignoring hyperspherical geometry and amplifying occlusion noise.
approach: Rh-3DGS uses Visibility-Calibrated Distillation with reliability weights, Visibility-Weighted Fréchet Mean for robust Riemannian aggregation, and Lightweight Consistency Contrast for local regularization.
contribution: Best performance on open-vocabulary segmentation, boundary quality, and view-consistent rendering across three benchmarks.

problem: Graph Neural Networks may lack sufficient expressive power to recover optimal Semidefinite Program solutions despite being natural candidates for sparse optimization problems.
approach: Prove standard GNN architectures fail on recovering linear SDP solutions; identify more expressive architecture that emulates first-order solver updates.
contribution: More expressive architecture achieves consistently lower prediction error and objective gap; warm-starting first-order solver yields practical speedups of up to 80%.

problem: Proxy-based hashing for cross-modal retrieval uses isolated similarity constraints where proxies lack relational interactions, resulting in weakly defined decision regions and limited discriminative structure.
approach: Organize proxies into sample-specific relational structures enabling interactions and competition; contrast positive and negative proxy responses to shape clearer boundaries.
contribution: Consistently improves cross-modal retrieval accuracy and embedding separability across standard benchmarks.

problem: Hard Completion paradigm forces fully concrete code generation even with insufficient context; 61% of suggestions are edited or rejected despite high similarity, indicating erroneous predictions at specific positions.
approach: APC strategically outputs explicit placeholders at high-entropy positions allowing users to fill via IDE navigation; formalize as cost-minimization problem proving existence of entropy threshold where APC lowers cost.
contribution: Reduces expected editing costs from 19% to 50% while preserving standard hard completion performance across 1.5B-14B models.

problem: Small language models significantly underperform on multi-step reasoning compared to larger models; dense reasoning with fewer steps but higher information density per step is more effective.
approach: DenseSteer modulates internal representations at inference-time toward dense reasoning patterns, identifying context-brittle tokens sensitive to perturbations without gradient updates.
contribution: Yields consistent accuracy improvements on reasoning and code benchmarks without increasing token-level negative log-likelihood.

problem: Masked Diffusion Models require many sampling iterations due to factorization errors from simultaneous token updates; standard single-state masks cannot reduce theoretical lower bound on error.
approach: IMDM introduces stochastic infinite-state mask to mitigate theoretical bound while inheriting MDM benefits and compatibility with pre-trained weights.
contribution: Fails on simple synthetic tasks with standard MDMs due to factorization error bound; IMDM finds efficient few-step solutions and surpasses existing distillation methods at small step counts on LM1B.

problem: Graph Contrastive Learning is hindered by random augmentations causing semantic distortion and rigid one-to-one sampling amplifying inter-class entanglement and intra-class dispersion.
approach: CL-GCL uses graph coarsening to preserve structural semantics via community-level representations and manifold learning to capture local geometry without costly pairwise distances.
contribution: Theoretically proven to approximate node-level contrastive loss; demonstrates consistent superiority in accuracy and efficiency over state-of-the-art GCL methods.

problem: Federated Continual Learning assumes synchronous task arrival; asynchronous reality with varying client update timestamps causes task drift corrupting global model and preventing effective learning.
approach: C²-AFCL introduces two-stage orthogonal calibration: intra-client calibration uses task-aware caches for local drift; inter-task interference calibration projects updates orthogonally to remove conflicting components.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in robust and efficient learning in dynamic federated environments with semantic-level task drift handling.

problem: Identifying drivers of causal mechanism shifts and distinguishing functional changes from noise alterations remains underexplored for non-additive, non-linear Structural Causal Models.
approach: FANS framework detects and dissects shifts via independence criterion where function shifts induce dependence between node parents and residual noise; develops two-stage algorithm for efficient detection.
contribution: Extends beyond additive noise models to handle non-additive, non-linear SCMs and addresses simultaneous function-noise shifts with formal identifiability assumptions.

problem: Standard decoding in Masked Diffusion Models suffers from context rigidity where tokens retained by transient confidence ignore lack of full context, creating cascade errors that misguide generation.
approach: CORE uses training-free inference-time revision identifying context-brittle tokens via adversarial perturbation sensitivity, formalizing revision as robust optimization targeting worst-case context shifts.
contribution: Delivers consistent improvements on reasoning and code benchmarks, with code generation (MBPP) improved by up to 9.2%, generalizing to Dream-7B architecture.

problem: Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture feature prediction remains challenging due to inherent visual uncertainty at masked positions, potentially failing to learn semantic representations.
approach: TC-JEPA uses image captions via fine-grained text conditioner computing sparse cross-attention over input tokens to reduce prediction uncertainty and make features semantically meaningful.
contribution: Improves downstream performance and training stability with promising scaling properties; outperforms contrastive methods on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding and reasoning.

problem: DeepSeek-OCR visual tokens remain prone to redundant textual and structural information; token pruning methods for conventional VLMs fail to preserve textual fidelity.
approach: RTPrune uses two-stage pruning motivated by model's distinct two-stage reading trajectory: prioritize high-norm tokens capturing salient information; merge remaining via optimal transport.
contribution: Achieves 99.47% accuracy and 1.23× faster prefill on OmniDocBench with 84.25% token retention for DeepSeek-OCR-Large.

problem: Language generation in the limit framework studies generating unseen strings from unknown target language; noise effects remain incompletely characterized.
approach: Prove single noisy string strictly reduces set of collections generatable for both uniform and non-uniform generation; show generation with single noisy string equivalent to any finite noise.
contribution: Answers open question on noise impact; provides first characterization for non-uniform noise-dependent generatability.

problem: Genomic language models achieve strong performance but internal biological representations remain poorly understood; sparse autoencoder applicability to genomic LMs unexplored.
approach: Systematic study of SAE-based interpretability for genomic LMs using Evo2, introduce genome-tailored metrics, develop graph-based representation organizing semantically related genomic concepts.
contribution: SAE features from intermediate layers are more interpretable than raw embeddings on 76% of genomic concept evaluations with 26/55 having F1 > 0.7.

problem: Subject Customization struggles to achieve effective pose control; existing methods exhibit inaccurate poses or inconsistent cross-pose appearances due to 2D-native backbones lacking volumetric understanding.
approach: Pose-ICL leverages 3D-aware In-Context Learning via Surface-Anchored Position Embedding anchoring image tokens to volumetric bounding box surface coordinates for explicit 3D awareness.
contribution: Significantly outperforms current methods in pose accuracy and identity consistency across 3D assets and real-world subjects.

problem: Survival analysis synthetic data generation faces unique challenges from incomplete event information via censoring; standard tabular generators fail to reproduce event-time distributions and censoring.
approach: SurvDiff is end-to-end diffusion model jointly generating mixed-type covariates, event times, and right-censoring guided by survival-tailored loss encoding time-to-event structure.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on distributional fidelity and survival model evaluation; first end-to-end diffusion for synthetic survival data generation.

problem: SAM despite strong zero-shot performance is unreliable under domain shift due to Mask-level Confidence Confusion where single IoU score fails to reflect pixel-wise reliability near boundaries.
approach: RUAC models out-of-domain variation as appearance shifts and non-rigid deformations; adds lightweight uncertainty head trained with collaborative style-deformation attack and Uncertainty-Error Alignment.
contribution: Improves segmentation quality and yields faithful uncertainty with stronger correlation across 23 zero-shot domains.

problem: Latent reasoning compresses reasoning into compact embeddings for efficiency but renders thinking opaque and non-interpretable; current methods present stark trade-off between efficiency and explainability.
approach: SELR trains single model with multi-task objective: Answer Loss optimizes latent reasoning for accuracy, CoT Loss trains decoding latent representations back to human-understandable steps.
contribution: Achieves superior token efficiency and accuracy on LLMs and VLMs while uniquely providing self-contained explanations without external decoders.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models are vulnerable to backdoor attacks that use fixed textual triggers and single-entity targets, making them susceptible to input defenses and detection methods.
approach: SemBD introduces representation-level triggers based on continuous semantic regions instead of discrete text patterns, implanted via distillation-based editing of cross-attention key-value matrices to enable semantically equivalent but textually diverse prompts to activate the backdoor.
contribution: Achieves 100% attack success rate while maintaining robustness against state-of-the-art input-level defenses through semantic regularization and multi-entity backdoor targets.

problem: LLM serving systems must balance high throughput and low latency across prefill and decode phases, where sharing GPUs causes performance interference while disaggregating wastes resources through model duplication and KV cache transfers.
approach: DuetServe dynamically activates SM-level GPU spatial multiplexing within a single GPU, using an attention-aware roofline model to forecast latency and an interruption-free execution engine to provide phase isolation only when contention threatens SLOs.
contribution: Improves total throughput by up to 1.3x while maintaining low generation latency compared to state-of-the-art frameworks.

problem: Graph neural network potentials like SchNet improve molecular dynamics accuracy but remain slower than classical force fields due to fragmented kernels and memory-bound pipelines that underutilize GPUs.
approach: FlashSchNet redesigns SchNet-style GNN-MD with four IO-aware techniques: flash radial basis fusing distance computation and basis expansion, flash message passing eliminating edge tensor materialization, flash aggregation via CSR segment reduce, and channel-wise 16-bit quantization of MLP weights.
contribution: Achieves 1000 ns/day aggregate simulation throughput over 64 parallel replicas on coarse-grained protein containing 269 beads, a 6.5x improvement.

problem: Learning sparse Gaussian graphical model structure from temporally correlated observations (single Glauber trajectory) is challenging because mixing-time-free guarantees are lacking and polynomial-time structure learning from sublinear samples is suspected computationally hard.
