approach: The algorithm estimates conditional variances to reduce to unit-diagonal case, designs a local edge test extracting adjacency from short update windows by isolating pairwise influence, and aggregates statistics using robust median-based estimation.
contribution: First polynomial-time algorithm recovering conditional-independence graph from single Glauber trajectory with trajectory-length guarantee independent of mixing time.

problem: The Massart noise condition remains under-explored in emerging extensions of PAC learning theory beyond the classical framework, limiting understanding of sample complexity under this important interpolation regime.
approach: The work revisits transductive empirical risk minimization and derives sharper excess error bounds under Massart noise using offset Rademacher techniques and local metric entropy, then leverages this analysis for partial concept class learning.
contribution: Provides new sample complexity bounds for PAC learning with partial concept classes and completes the characterization of universal rates under Massart noise.

problem: Naive expansion of LLM-based multi-agent systems by adding new agents triggers performance collapse as the router cold-starts on heterogeneous and unreliable agents, limiting scalability.
approach: MonoScale proactively generates agent-conditioned familiarization tasks, harvests evidence from successes and failures, distills into natural-language memory to guide routing, and formalizes expansion as contextual bandit with trust-region memory updates.
contribution: Achieves stable performance gains as agent pool grows on GAIA and Humanity's Last Exam benchmarks, outperforming naive scale-up with monotonic non-decreasing performance guarantee under non-interfering expansion.

problem: Sub-bit model compression faces a fundamental one-bit wall because sign matrices resist low-rank approximation and appear random, yet most weights retain their initialization signs suggesting inherited randomness from initialization.
approach: Sign lock-in theory formalizes sign flip behavior under SGD as a stopping-time analysis showing geometric-tail distribution under bounded updates and rare re-entry conditions, enabling low-rank sign-template training from scratch.
contribution: Introduces from-scratch low-rank sign-template training method that prevents emergence of the one-bit wall bottleneck in sub-bit compression.

problem: Reasoning LLMs struggle with factuality in long-form settings, generating substantially more hallucinations than non-reasoning counterparts, while extending online RL for factuality poses challenges due to lack of reliable verification and reward hacking.
approach: Proposes a reward function simultaneously considering factual precision, response detail, and answer relevance, applied via online RL to learn high-quality factual reasoning while avoiding reward hacking pitfalls.
contribution: Achieves average 23.1 percentage points hallucination rate reduction with 23% increase in detail level and no helpfulness degradation across six long-form factuality benchmarks.

problem: Standard attention mechanisms use static token representations across all pair-wise computations, limiting representational alignment with diverse token-pair dynamics especially in multivariate time series with heterogeneous inter-channel dependencies.
approach: Prime attention modulates token representations for each token-pair to optimize each pair-wise interaction for that specific relationship, dynamically adjusting representations based on interaction type.
contribution: Achieves up to 6.5% improvement in forecasting accuracy across benchmarks and comparable performance using up to 40% less sequence length than standard attention.

problem: LLM-based retrieval systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, yet existing methods require known queries and victim model access, limiting validity of attacks in real-world query-agnostic black-box scenarios.
approach: Proposes query-agnostic black-box attack generating transferable injection tokens using zero-shot surrogate LLMs, establishes theoretical framework of LLMR, simulates attack as min-max problem with adversarial learning mechanism.
contribution: Demonstrates effective query-agnostic black-box attacks on benchmark datasets across popular LLM retrievers without victim queries or model knowledge.

problem: Generative VLA policies disregard spatiotemporal scale mismatch between cognition and action, leading to representation inefficiency and weak condition alignment during optimization.
approach: ResVLA shifts from generation-from-noise to refinement-from-intent paradigm, using spectral analysis to decouple control into deterministic low-frequency anchor (global intent) and stochastic high-frequency residual (local dynamics), anchoring generation on predicted intent.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance with strong robustness to language and embodiment perturbations, faster convergence than generative baselines, and strong real-world robot performance.

problem: Text-to-music diffusion models suffer from generation collapse to limited patterns and struggle to balance text alignment with diversity, as inference-time diversity control often harms text alignment by distorting prompt cues.
approach: PADS-TAL perturbs padding-indexed subspace while keeping non-padding conditioning fixed for controlled exploration, and introduces text-aware latent space aligning neighborhoods with text-implied genre structure for genre-consistent diversity.
contribution: Achieves 15.4% higher diversity at comparable text alignment and 71.6% improvement in within-genre diversity compared to prior perturbation methods.

problem: Test-time scaling in VLMs remains brittle because unstructured visual reasoning chains entangle perception and reasoning, leading to cascading errors from small perceptual mistakes and requiring expensive hand-crafted rewards.
approach: SPARC explicitly decouples visual perception from reasoning via two-stage pipeline with visual search localizing question-relevant regions followed by reasoning conditioned on those regions, enabling asymmetric compute allocation.
contribution: Improves Qwen3VL 4B on V* VQA by 6.7 points and surpasses visual-grounding approaches through independent test-time scaling of perception and reasoning stages.

problem: Existing model merging methods rely on fixed or manually tuned coefficients, making unified models sensitive to initial merging strategy and suboptimal for downstream adaptation.
approach: MetaMerging uses meta-learning to adaptively optimize merging coefficients by simulating adapter updates in inner loop and meta-optimizing coefficients in outer loop for task-specific adapter training.
contribution: Produces more balanced and generalizable unified models with strong performance across CV and NLP downstream tasks compared to parameter merging methods.

problem: Model pruning methods lack principled approaches to determine how many scored components can be discarded without sacrificing performance.
approach: EMP derives sparsity directly from importance score distribution using effective sample size (inverse Simpson index) from particle filtering, mapping scores to effective sample size and discarding lowest-scoring components.
contribution: Provides universal adaptive threshold with provable upper bound on loss change relative to original model across MLPs, CNNs, Transformers, LLMs, and KAN architectures.

problem: Formal complexity assessment of slice sampling for Dirichlet process models remains lacking because computational cost is random and potentially unbounded.
approach: Derives high-probability bounds on computational complexity of DP slice samplers showing that overhead from slice variables relative to cluster count is O_P(log n) uniformly across posterior regimes.
contribution: Establishes superlinear blow-ups in per-iteration cost occur with vanishing probability even in worst-case configurations, providing theoretical foundation for assessing DP slice sampler scalability.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models either generate actions autoregressively with poor performance or fragment information pathways through separate diffusion heads outside the backbone, limiting unified scalable architectures.
approach: Discrete Diffusion VLA discretizes action chunks and models them with discrete diffusion inside the unified transformer backbone, enabling adaptive decoding order and secondary re-masking for robust error correction.
contribution: Achieves 96.4% avg success on LIBERO, 71.2% visual matching on SimplerEnv-Fractal, 54.2% on SimplerEnv-Bridge with superior vision-language capability retention in out-of-distribution tests.

problem: Meta-RL typically assumes unobserved confounders can be excluded a priori, but real observational data from heterogeneous environments often contains confounding that violates this assumption.
approach: Employs partial identification methods to generate posterior counterfactual trajectories from candidate environments aligning with confounded observations, using these trajectories to find robust policy initialization.
contribution: Produces solution minimizing generalization loss in future inference tasks under confounded observational data across multiple environments.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action models for autonomous driving struggle with efficient inference and generalization to novel vehicle configurations and driving scenarios.
approach: Reasoning-VLA employs learnable action queries guided by predefined spatial representations and reasoning-enhanced vision-language features to generate continuous action trajectories in parallel, trained on consolidated standardized driving datasets with Chain-of-Thought reasoning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with strong generalization capability and excellent inference speed via parallel decoding across multiple driving benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion language models rely on heuristic random masking for pretraining that fails to target informative tokens, wasting computational effort on redundant or trivial tokens.
approach: InfoDLM reformulates mask selection as active feedback-driven process introducing Trainable Information-Gain signal to quantify masking information gain, develops feedback mechanism adapting masking policy to model state with maturity indicator.
contribution: Achieves up to 13% improvement in reasoning accuracy over LLaDA variant under comparable pretraining budgets through adaptive masking.

problem: Multimodal RAG pipelines treat visual inputs as static and immutable, failing on imperfect queries suffering from geometric distortions, quality degradation, or semantic ambiguity, leading to retrieval failures.
approach: V-QPP-Bench formulates visual query pre-processing as agentic decision-making where MLLMs autonomously diagnose imperfections and deploy perceptual tools to refine queries, enabling supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Reveals critical vulnerabilities to visual imperfections and shows supervised fine-tuning enables compact models to achieve comparable or superior performance to larger proprietary models.

problem: Monocular-to-stereo conversion requires stereo inpainting of disocclusions but training-based methods rely on scarce stereo pairs or synthetic data with domain gaps.
approach: Proposes Geometric Reciprocity Theorem showing disocclusion mask when synthesizing target view equals mask of pixels lost warping from target to source, enabling self-supervised learning from monocular videos via cycle consistency.
contribution: First self-supervised framework for monocular-to-stereo conversion achieving improvements over training-free and supervised state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Dataset pruning remains underexplored for 3D modalities where class imbalance persists across training and test sets, forcing trade-offs between overall accuracy and mean accuracy across different evaluation priors.
approach: Casts pruning as quadrature approximation decomposing error into representation error and prior-mismatch bias, decouples likelihood from prior using distillation with calibrated teacher and geometry-preserving constraints, uses geometric embedding for robust pruning signals.
contribution: Framework elevates performance floor across diverse priors while offering flexibility for different evaluation preferences in 3D dataset pruning.

problem: Existing 4D human-object interaction generation focuses on global whole-body motion but fails to reason about part-level mechanics underlying interactions.
approach: HOI-PAGE explicitly reasons about part-level affordances using LLMs captured in part affordance graph representation, then generates 4D sequences optimizing for reference dynamics while satisfying part-level contact constraints.
contribution: Generates complex multi-object or multi-person interaction sequences with significantly improved realism and text alignment for zero-shot 4D HOI generation.

problem: Learning with sparse datasets and rich domain knowledge (expressed as logical rules and inequalities) requires enforcing hard constraints while existing neuro-symbolic methods only achieve soft penalty enforcement or non-differentiable post-processing.
approach: DisjunctiveNet represents rules as disjunctive constraints and applies hierarchical convex relaxations to obtain convex hull formulations enabling tractable linear constraints as differentiable optimization layers.
contribution: Achieves perfect rule satisfaction and strong predictive performance through end-to-end feasibility enforcement of hard input-dependent mixed-integer linear constraints.

problem: Discovering unknown one-parameter symmetry subgroups from data is challenging as conventional methods assume known symmetries.
approach: Proposes modular data-driven framework learning unknown functional mappings and discovering underlying symmetry subgroup by instantiating architectures with invariant/equivariant layers structured by Lie algebra, learning generator parameters end-to-end.
contribution: Identifies relevant continuous subgroups directly from data with guaranteed symmetry by construction across elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic regimes of matrix Lie groups including SO(n), SL(n), and Lorentz group.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation employs shared low-rank updates across tokens, limiting ability to fully exploit adaptation subspace for tokens from different sequences.
approach: U-LoRA employs conditioned gating generating utilization coefficients along low-rank directions for each token, coordinates them using sequence-level context, and introduces bias-corrected exponential moving average historical prior for training stability.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance under comparable parameter budgets by better utilizing existing low-rank subspace via input-conditioned strategies without expanding it.

problem: Zero-shot imitation learning requires agents to reproduce expert behavior from single demonstrations without environment interaction or gradient updates at test time, making the multi-task inverse RL problem intractable.
approach: CIRL converts multi-task inverse RL into goal-inference problem using contrastive RL for maximum-entropy goal-conditioned policies, automatic goal proposal via GoalKDE, and mean-field variational model for amortized goal inference.
contribution: Consistently recovers demonstrator's intent by accounting for relative difficulty of reaching states, outperforming prior zero-shot imitation methods.

problem: Parallel agentic systems executing multiple teams independently perform overlapping computation on similar sub-problems, resulting in significant computational waste.
approach: LTS introduces global memory bank accessible to all teams and lightweight controller trained via stepwise RL deciding whether intermediate steps should be added, enabling selective cross-team information reuse.
contribution: Significantly reduces overall runtime while matching or improving task performance on AssistantBench and GAIA through learned memory admission.

problem: Cross-view geo-localization fails to generalize to unseen environments because contrastive learning treats all negatives equally, overrepressing semi-positive samples that share semantic cues and causing overfitting.
approach: Proposes uncertainty-aware framework using Deep Evidential Regression modeling Normal-Inverse-Gamma distribution to quantify environmental complexity, enabling adaptive softening of hard negatives in Soft InfoNCE.
contribution: Achieves 18% R@1 average improvement in zero-shot cross-dataset transfer compared to prior methods.

problem: Multimodal LLMs excel at offline understanding but struggle to serve as mobile assistants in continuous real-world audio-visual streams where responding at the right time is critical.
approach: PhoStream benchmarks streaming video, audio, and temporal reasoning with automated generative pipeline and realistic online inference pipeline, using LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation for open-ended responses.
contribution: Reveals temporal asymmetry where models excel on instant/backward tasks but sharply drop on forward tasks due to responding before required visual-audio cues appear.

problem: Sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms leverage random sparsity for computational efficiency but random sparsity leads to irregular memory access patterns that degrade GPU memory bandwidth utilization.
approach: FlashSketch pursues sketch-kernel co-design introducing BlockPerm-SJLT sparse sketches whose structure enables optimized CUDA kernel with tunable parameter trading GPU-efficiency against sketching robustness.
contribution: Achieves global geomean speedup of roughly 1.7x over prior GPU sketches while maintaining theoretical OSE framework guarantees.

problem: LLMs often hallucinate even with reference texts, especially when processing long contexts, as citations remain probabilistic output rather than foundation for generated content.
approach: Guidance builds structured fact pool of Prefix-Tail pairs from documents and uses lookahead strategy during decoding to predict intent, automatically replacing output with verified facts and citations when prefixes match.
contribution: Improves citation F1 score by 11.2% over state-of-the-art baselines with training-free approach pluggable into general or fine-tuned LLMs.

problem: Split federated learning suffers from biased optimization and unstable convergence under non-IID data because client information coordination lacks awareness of split architecture.
approach: BESplit exploits split architecture structure using Evidential Aggregation for fine-grained reweighting, Bias-Compensated Collaboration aligning split-layer representations via complementary pairing, and Dual-Teacher Distillation synchronizing knowledge.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, convergence stability, and computational efficiency under diverse non-IID settings.

problem: Effective data selection for LLM pretraining is essential but existing approaches rely on external pretrained models or estimate importance from fixed model state, failing to capture dynamic data preference evolution.
approach: BLISS operates from scratch without external models using small proxy model and score model estimating importance through multi-step proxy updates, formalizing data selection as bilevel optimization.
contribution: Achieves 1.7x speedup reaching same performance as state-of-the-art method on 1B setting while delivering superior downstream performance on 410M/1B/2.8B models.

problem: Dynamic regret analysis for Follow-the-Regularized-Leader methods is less explored particularly for curved losses and adaptive optimizers like Adam.
approach: Builds on discounted-to-dynamic reduction with modular framework analyzing FTRL-related problems, applies to linear and logistic regression and Adam optimizers.
contribution: Simplifies proofs for optimal dynamic regret of online linear regression and yields new dynamic regret guarantees for online logistic regression and Adam.

problem: Knowledge editing in unified multimodal models shows striking modality gap where text-side efficacy reaches 92% but visual generation VQA accuracy is only 18.5%, suggesting edits fail to transfer cross-modality.
approach: Proposes Reasoning-augmented Parameter Editing explicitly activating edited knowledge before generation, improving VQA accuracy through activation of knowledge pathways for visual synthesis.
contribution: Demonstrates text-level knowledge edits do not guarantee reliable cross-modality transfer, motivates modality-aware editing methods with gains up to 18.6 percentage points.

problem: Stochastic variational inequality algorithms typically assume bounded variance or bounded domain, yet these assumptions are violated in problems like bilinear min-max with unbounded domains.
approach: Analyzes algorithms for solving monotone and structured nonmonotone VIs without bounded variance/domain assumptions, focusing on constrained settings allowing variance growth as squared norm of optimization variable.
contribution: Achieves oracle complexity of O-tilde(epsilon^-4) for making expected residual norm less than epsilon, best-known for constrained VIs.

problem: Reconstruction-based multimodal anomaly detection suffers from one-to-many crossmodal mapping problem where single 3D feature maps to multiple plausible RGB appearances, causing deterministic regression to over-smooth reconstructions.
approach: CFR learns bidirectional cyclic mappings for coarse reconstruction, identifies unreliable reconstructed features and selectively replaces them with high-confidence normal features to correct ambiguity-induced failures.
contribution: In 1-shot setting achieves 92.3 and 82.7 AUPRO at 30% FPR on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies with 74.0 and 75.9 image-level AUROC scores.

problem: Scenario generation for autonomous driving tests either produces visually extreme crashes not physically feasible or overemphasizes controller-dependent aggressive maneuvers, missing the feasibility boundary band where scenarios are physically solvable but cause autonomy failures.
approach: ScenePilot formulates generation as constrained multi-objective RL combining RSS-derived physical-feasibility score with online-learned AV-risk predictor, introduces feasibility-aware shielding maintaining exploration near boundary.
contribution: Yields substantially higher collision rates (+6.2 pp) while preserving physical validity, with adversarial fine-tuning consistently reducing downstream crash rates.

problem: Training Boltzmann generators efficiently is difficult because both simulation data and energy evaluations are costly, limiting practical deployment for sampling from unnormalized probability densities in physical systems.
approach: The paper proposes off-policy log-dispersion regularization (LDR), a regularization framework that acts as a shape regularizer of the energy landscape by leveraging target energy labels without requiring additional on-policy samples during training.
contribution: LDR improves both final performance and data efficiency in Boltzmann generator training, achieving sample efficiency gains of up to one order of magnitude across benchmarks.

problem: Self-supervised learning for physiological time-series struggles to preserve clinical semantics important for downstream transfer while filtering irrelevant noise, as contrastive methods ignore dynamical structure and structural models cannot selectively filter sample-specific noise.
approach: PULSE proposes a pretraining objective that formulates a dynamical systems model to identify transferable and non-transferable information between time-series windows, targeting the former through a novel cross-reconstruction objective.
contribution: PULSE effectively distinguishes clinical semantic classes, increases label efficiency, and improves transfer learning performance on real-world physiological datasets.

problem: Long-term weather forecasting is constrained by catastrophic forgetting, error accumulation, and high training overhead when finetuning models to extend prediction horizons.
approach: EMFormer introduces an efficient multi-scale transformer that extracts multi-scale features through single convolution, combined with accumulative context finetuning and composite loss with sinusoidal weighting to adaptively guide optimization.
contribution: The approach substantially improves long-term forecast accuracy and extreme event prediction, while demonstrating strong generalization on vision benchmarks (ImageNet-1K and ADE20K).

problem: Random shuffling of instruction tuning data overlooks latent structure like domain and reasoning depth, interleaving heterogeneous objectives that induce gradient conflicts and diminish effective optimization progress.
approach: EP-Order operates in representation space by embedding training samples, clustering them, ranking clusters by proximity, and introducing mixed regions that interleave samples from adjacent clusters to stabilize learning across cluster transitions.
contribution: EP-Order achieves broadly consistent improvements over random shuffling across 14 benchmarks spanning vision-language, text-only, and hybrid thinking/no-thinking scenarios.

problem: It remains unclear in a principled sense when finite tests can meaningfully certify broad capabilities of foundation models across task families, without principled evaluation theory.
approach: The paper formalizes evaluation as inference over a task family and analyzes two regimes: stochastic multi-environment evaluation where uniform certification is characterized by χ²-radius, and worst-case rule-like capabilities where impossibility results are established.
contribution: The work provides a principled framework for understanding when finite evaluation can and cannot certify capabilities, with near-optimal evaluation protocols and matching lower bounds under natural overlap conditions.

problem: LLM decomposition introduces approximation errors that propagate and amplify non-linearly through deep transformer layers, progressively distorting internal representations and degrading downstream performance.
approach: Decomper learns to align the output distribution of decomposed transformer blocks with their original counterparts by suppressing error at its source, operating with near-zero inference overhead.
contribution: On LLaMA-3-8B and OPT-13B at 40% compression, perplexity is reduced by more than 70% while reasoning task accuracy improves by over 10%.

problem: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations require scalable and accurate modeling of interatomic interactions, but existing message passing methods are either not scalable or too coarse for full atomic resolution.
approach: The framework stacks message passing neural network layers with dilated star-structured paths that progressively capture distance-dependent interactions, transforming dense interatomic interactions into region-based sparse message passing graphs.
contribution: The approach delivers state-of-the-art performance across MD22, Chignolin, AdK, and MISATO datasets, including systems with up to 40,000 atoms.

problem: Optimization over non-convex constraint sets like star-shaped sets is difficult because they lack efficient projection oracles and existing methods require expensive projection or optimization subroutines.
approach: Hom-PGD+ learns an invertible neural network to map the non-convex constraint set to a unit ball, transforming the original problem into an equivalent ball-constrained optimization where projections are efficient.
contribution: Hom-PGD+ achieves an O(ε⁻²) convergence rate to approximate stationary solutions while maintaining per-iteration complexity of only O(W) for W INN parameters, with speedups up to one order of magnitude.

problem: Causal inference in spatial domains faces unmeasured spatial confounders and treatment interference that violate no-interference assumptions, with existing methods addressing only one by assuming away the other.
approach: Spatial Deconfounder reconstructs a substitute confounder from local treatment vectors using a conditional VAE with spatial prior, then estimates causal effects with a flexible outcome model, leveraging the insight that interference reveals structure in latent confounders.
contribution: The method enables nonparametric identification of direct and spillover effects under weak assumptions, and consistently improves effect estimation across environmental health and social science datasets.

problem: Reinforcement learning on looped language models fails when standard objectives like GRPO only assign credit to the final latent state, creating a mismatch with multi-step internal reasoning computation.
approach: RLTT distributes reward across the full latent reasoning trajectory through trajectory-level credit assignment without relying on external verifiers, designed to directly replace GRPO with negligible overhead.
contribution: RLTT yields +5.8% improvements over GRPO on 1.4B scale and +10.9% on 2.6B scale on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with effective transfer to non-mathematical reasoning.

problem: Vision-Language Models as reward functions for diffusion model alignment introduce domain mismatch through pixel-space rewards and suffer from substantial computational and memory cost.
approach: DiNa-LRM formulates preference learning directly on noisy diffusion states with a noise-calibrated Thurstone likelihood, using a timestep-conditioned reward head on a pretrained latent diffusion backbone and inference-time noise ensembling.
contribution: DiNa-LRM outperforms diffusion-based reward baselines and achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art VLMs while maintaining substantially lower computational cost.

problem: Fine-tuned foundation models for medical image analysis exhibit significant subgroup disparity, and one-shot federated learning can suffer from parameter conflicts when heterogeneous distributions across institutions cause local models to diverge.
approach: Fair-FedMOE uses fairness-aware expert routing with learnable prototypes to route samples to group-specific experts, and prototype-guided differential aggregation to compute personalized weights and filter conflicting updates.
contribution: Fair-FedMOE demonstrates consistent fairness gains without sacrificing accuracy on retinal and chest X-ray datasets with multiple foundation models.

problem: Modern optimizers that aggregate gradients across batches and incorporate historical state can produce parameter updates that increase the loss for individual samples, creating per-sample harm that degrades generalization.
approach: The method formalizes parameter updates as an optimization problem minimizing conflicting impacts of batch averaging and historical state, then introduces a proxy that reduces dimensionality to batch size and restricts optimization to the last linear layer.
contribution: The method reduces per-sample interference and improves generalization on image classification benchmarks with favorable scaling properties as model size or input grows.

problem: Learning Nash equilibria in offline two-player zero-sum Markov games requires handling distribution shift, but existing approaches rely on explicit pessimism which can be conservative.
approach: The paper shows that KL regularization alone suffices to stabilize learning and proposes ROSE, a framework with unilateral concentrability, along with SOS-MD, a model-free algorithm using least-squares value estimation and iterative self-play updates.
contribution: SOS-MD achieves a fast Õ(1/n) convergence rate with unilateral concentrability, improving over standard Õ(1/√n) rates in unregularized settings.

problem: CLIP remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks and prior adversarial fine-tuning overlooks uncertainty calibration, leading to miscalibration where perturbations suppress uncertainty rather than increase it.
approach: The method reparameterizes CLIP outputs as Dirichlet distribution concentration parameters to capture both semantic structure and confidence magnitude, enabling holistic distribution alignment under perturbations.
contribution: The method significantly improves uncertainty calibration and achieves competitive adversarial robustness while preserving clean accuracy across multiple zero-shot benchmarks.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer catastrophic failures in visual counting beyond training distributions, failing to extrapolate to unseen quantities despite success on interpolation tasks.
approach: By deconstructing visual counting into object individuation, abstract magnitude representation, and symbolic decoding on synthetic Go boards, the paper isolates the failure mechanism to symbolic decoding where valid magnitudes fail to project onto discrete tokens.
contribution: The work identifies the Fractured Magnitude Hypothesis—VLMs learn disjoint, modality-specific statistical manifolds preventing cross-modal grounding for unseen pairings—and shows this affects state-of-the-art foundation models.

problem: Existing credal predictors define epistemic uncertainty primarily as disagreement from random training initializations, which mainly reflects optimization sensitivity rather than uncertainty from substantive distribution shifts.
approach: CreDRO learns an ensemble of plausible models via distributionally robust optimization, formulating epistemic uncertainty as disagreement between models trained under different degrees of i.i.d. assumption relaxation.
contribution: CreDRO outperforms state-of-the-art credal approaches on out-of-distribution detection and selective classification in medical settings by capturing uncertainty from train-test distribution shifts.

problem: Converting pretrained dense models into sparse mixture-of-experts is expensive when training from scratch, and existing dense-to-MoE methods break intrinsic activation patterns leading to suboptimal expert construction.
approach: ExpertWeaver leverages Gated Linear Unit activation patterns to reveal inherent MoE structure with consistently activated universal neurons and dynamically activated specialized neurons, partitioning them into shared and routed experts.
contribution: ExpertWeaver outperforms existing methods as both a training-free dynamic structural pruning technique and as a downcycling strategy for MoE initialization.

problem: Stability properties well-understood in control theory for deterministic systems are largely overlooked in stochastic Markov decision processes, lacking a principled framework for synthesizing controllers with prescribed asymptotic stability.
approach: The paper proposes the fast-mixing steady-state (FMSS) problem and derives a tractable surrogate objective that leads to a convex program by controlling spectral properties of the induced Markov chain transition matrix.
contribution: The work provides a tractable convex formulation for FMSS and an offline sample-based algorithm (FMSS-SV) with finite-sample complexity analysis for tabular MDPs.

problem: Watermarking large language models with chain-of-thought capabilities is challenging because existing black-box methods trade robustness for reasoning fidelity by perturbing final answers or relying on fragile trigger patterns.
approach: BiCoT embeds ownership signals into the internal geometry of reasoning traces by aligning high-saliency structural anchors with a private signature subspace, and proposes Robust Subspace Registration for black-box verification.
contribution: BiCoT preserves reasoning fidelity across diverse reasoning tasks while achieving robust detection under fine-tuning, quantization, and adaptive attacks across in-domain and out-of-distribution settings.

problem: Bilinear bandits with partially observable features on both sides suffer from high-dimensional feature spaces when reduced to linear bandits via Kronecker products, losing bilinear structure.
approach: BiRoLF leverages the bilinear structure directly by augmenting observed feature spaces with orthogonal complement bases and using doubly robust estimation to construct matrix-valued pseudo-rewards, with bilinear DR-Lasso for parameter estimation.
contribution: BiRoLF achieves Õ(√((dx+dhx)(dy+dhy)T)) regret bound where dx,dy are observable dimensions and dhx,dhy denote effective orthogonal-complement dimensions.

problem: Diffusion models face misuse concerns for generating harmful content, and existing LoRA-based unlearning methods struggle to balance removing closely related concepts with maintaining generalization and scaling to multiple concepts.
approach: UnHype incorporates hypernetworks into single and multi-concept LoRA training, dynamically generating adaptive LoRA weights based on CLIP embeddings for context-aware, scalable unlearning.
contribution: UnHype demonstrates effectiveness across object erasure, celebrity erasure, and explicit content removal, and is compatible with Stable Diffusion and modern flow-based models.

problem: Current benchmarks for agent-user interactions in tool-use tasks do not capture the diversity of real interactions like clarification questions and confirmations, and operate in small environments with limited APIs.
approach: AppWorld-UL introduces a user-in-the-loop benchmark with 516 tasks on 9 simulated apps, systematically modifying tasks to introduce ambiguities and constraints, with LLM-simulated user behavior using carefully designed knowledge boundaries.
contribution: Evaluation reveals Claude Opus 4.7 achieves only 48.6% success on AppWorld-UL and 21.3% on compositional tasks at scenario-level, demonstrating the benchmark's difficulty.

problem: Understanding cellular phenotypes and how they respond to perturbations is critical for disease biology, but the combinatorial space of conditions makes exhaustive experimental mapping infeasible.
approach: scCBGM adapts concept bottleneck architectures for single-cell data using decoder skip connections and cross-covariance penalties for disentanglement, extended to flow matching models for concept-guided editing.
contribution: scCBGM demonstrates superior performance in combinatorial generalization and counterfactual prediction on real datasets, supported by cell-level validation on synthetic data.

problem: Neural simulators for physics suffer from bottlenecks in generating high-fidelity training data, limiting scalability for industrial applications.
approach: GeoPT augments geometry with synthetic dynamics for dynamics-aware self-supervision without physics labels, pre-trained on over one million samples and enabling improved industrial-fidelity benchmarks.
contribution: GeoPT reduces labeled data requirements by 20-60% and accelerates convergence by 2× across fluid mechanics and solid mechanics benchmarks.

problem: Multi-modal psychiatric diagnosis must integrate cross-modal agreement with modality-specific complementarity, but real multi-site cohorts introduce site and cohort-dependent confounders that enable shortcut-driven predictions.
approach: SMGD explicitly factorizes multi-modal graph representations into four components: shared diagnostic evidence, complementary diagnostic evidence, incidental agreement, and modality-specific non-robust correlations, using geometry-driven structure learning.
contribution: SMGD improves in-domain diagnosis and cross-dataset generalization under modality gaps on large multi-site datasets without relying on expert-crafted diagnostic biomarkers.

problem: Reverse Chain-of-Thought Generation produces post-hoc rationalizations when models see answers during generation, with naive suppression of the answer paradoxically increasing dependence through active monitoring.
approach: Structural Skeleton-guided Reasoning (SSR) replaces answer suppression with structural decoupling by first generating an answer-invariant functional skeleton then using it as a content-neutral target for trace generation.
contribution: SSR consistently mitigates anchoring across open-ended reasoning benchmarks, with Distilled SSR achieving up to 10% improvement over suppression baselines and reduced OOD degradation.

problem: Incomplete multi-view multi-label classification suffers from missing views and labels, but existing methods treat labels solely as supervision signals while overlooking the semantic structure in partial annotations.
approach: LGRL constructs a semantic-informed mixture prior via learnable category prototypes to guide representation extraction, using category-specific conditional posteriors where prototypes act as Bayesian experts.
contribution: LGRL demonstrates effectiveness across benchmark datasets and real-world applications in sports analytics and medical imaging.

problem: Evaluating generative AI models is resource-intensive due to slow inference, expensive raters, and a rapidly growing landscape of models and benchmarks.
approach: ProEval leverages pre-trained Gaussian Processes as surrogates for performance score functions, framing performance estimation as Bayesian quadrature and failure discovery as superlevel set sampling with uncertainty-aware decision strategies.
contribution: ProEval requires 8-65x fewer samples to achieve estimates within ±1% of ground truth while revealing more diverse failure cases under stricter evaluation budgets.

problem: Federated causal discovery for time series faces intervention policy drift and incompatible time scales across clients with heterogeneous sampling frequencies, making local causal graphs naturally heterogeneous.
approach: Fed-CAW defines edge-level credibility scores quantifying per-edge reliability via within-client temporal stability and cross-client consistency after mapping to unified time scale, with differential privacy for aggregation.
contribution: Fed-CAW recovers global causal graphs while preserving personalized local structures and demonstrating effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Graph learning in critical domains requires trustworthiness through robustness and fairness, but these properties are undermined by perturbations inducing distributional uncertainty.
approach: DICT models distributional uncertainty to minimize worst-case risk over an uncertainty set, reformulating as a finite-dimensional min-max problem integrating strong duality and local Lipschitz continuity.
contribution: DICT consistently improves both robustness and fairness across diverse benchmarks and backbones, pioneering unified robustness and fairness within a single optimization framework.

problem: Networks with polysemantic neurons suffer from interference between features that share neurons, but increasing model parameters increases computational cost and memory demands.
approach: The method demonstrates that splitting neurons into sparser sub-neurons without increasing non-zero parameters improves performance by reducing feature interference, with random splits approximating gains from informed splits.
contribution: Widening networks while maintaining constant non-zero parameter count consistently increases accuracy on Boolean tasks, CLIP classifiers, and multilayer networks, matching modern accelerator strengths.

problem: Reinforcement learning produces high-frequency oscillatory control signals that undermine safety and stability for physical deployment, and explicit action chunking scales the policy output dimension with horizon length.
approach: Dual-Window Smoothing (DWS) uses an execution window ensuring physical smoothness through deterministic modulation and a value window aligning temporal-difference targets, with lightweight actor-side temporal regularization.
contribution: DWS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on DeepMind Control Suite and industrial tasks, achieving 100% success rate on vision-based autonomous driving with smoother control and safer behavior.

problem: Memory-based replay methods for continual learning are constrained by limited memory capacity as each stored example represents only a single data instance, making it difficult to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
approach: Data reassembly partitions current task training data into elementary patches and dynamically reassembles them into coherent replay instances through energy-based optimization enforcing semantic compatibility and global consistency.
contribution: Data reassembly consistently outperforms existing memory-based approaches across continual learning benchmarks, achieving stronger retention while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Diffusion models struggle to enforce hard constraints on generated graphs, with existing approaches either failing to guarantee strict satisfaction or limited to narrow constraint types.
approach: NSPSG integrates unconstrained diffusion models with discrete projection operators using SMT-based projectors to ensure strict constraint satisfaction, with supervised neural projectors approximating the symbolic reasoning.
contribution: NSPSG achieves 99%-100% validity rates across heterogeneous constraints and various datasets, improving data validity by up to 43% for complex non-linear constraints.

problem: Constructing efficient multi-agent systems requires labor-intensive manual design, and current automation methods generate templated agents using monolithic optimization while ignoring task complexity gradients.
approach: EvoMAS employs a dynamic repertoire of seven evolutionary strategies (3 exploration, 3 exploitation, 1 domain-specific) with adaptive strategy selection, role-level evolution, and curriculum-guided scheduling, plus a Cyber Creator meta-controller.
contribution: EvoMAS consistently outperforms existing methods across multiple domains while maintaining cost efficiency, with roles evolving from homogeneous actors to specialized reasoning ensembles.

problem: Sparse-reward reinforcement learning typically focuses on exploration, but fails to leverage structural assumptions about reward functions themselves that could accelerate learning.
approach: Policy-Aware Matrix Completion (PAMC) exploits low-rank structure in reward matrices while correcting for policy-induced sampling bias, combining low-rank plus sparse reward model with inverse propensity weighting.
contribution: PAMC achieves 4100±250 return on Montezuma's Revenge (vs 200±50 for DrQ-v2), 78% success on MetaWorld-50 (vs 65%), and 15% improvement over CQL on D4RL datasets.

problem: Synthesizing sleep EEG from respiration signals faces a significant complexity gap between the two physiological modalities.
approach: A waveform-conditional generative framework preserves fine-grained respiratory dynamics while constraining the EEG target space through discrete tokenization, trained on over 28,000 individuals.
contribution: The model achieves 7% Mean Absolute Error in EEG spectrogram reconstruction and supports downstream tasks with performance comparable to ground truth on age estimation, sex detection, and sleep staging.

problem: Clinical brain-to-text interfaces require data-efficient generalization but most pre-training methods use only seconds of neural context, failing to exploit extended neural dynamics available in minutes of recordings.
approach: MEG-XL pre-trains with 2.5 minutes (191k tokens) of MEG context per sample, 5-300× longer than prior work, learning representations that transfer better to word decoding tasks.
contribution: MEG-XL matches supervised performance with a fraction of the training data (e.g., 1hr vs 50hrs) and outperforms brain foundation models on data-efficient word decoding.

problem: Object-centric representations are often argued to support compositional generalization but systematic evidence in visually rich settings is limited, with unclear tradeoffs against dense representations.
approach: The paper introduces a VQA benchmark across three controlled visual worlds carefully controlling for training data diversity, sample size, representation size, downstream capacity, and compute when comparing OC and dense encoders.
contribution: Object-centric approaches are superior in harder compositional generalization settings, more sample efficient, but dense representations catch up with sufficient data and diversity.

problem: Byzantine nodes in decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning for networked service systems can exploit unbounded state spaces to destabilize both learning and queueing processes.
approach: Proposes a resilient consensus-based MARL algorithm where cooperative agents learn control policies via actor-critic with linear function approximation while communicating with neighbors; mitigates adversarial parameter manipulation through robust consensus mechanisms.
contribution: Proves that cooperative agents' policies converge almost surely to a bounded neighborhood of a stationary solution under mild assumptions, and demonstrates the framework's effectiveness on semantic routing, distributed polling, and smart manufacturing logistics.

problem: Cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation fails when vocabulary overlap is low due to severe alignment noise, causing negative transfer compared to supervised fine-tuning.
approach: Introduces Entropy-aware Span-Constrained Optimal Transport (E-SCOT), which treats distillation as a sparse transport problem using vocabulary-agnostic ground metrics and span-anchored lexical alignment to construct a deterministic support set in linear time.
contribution: E-SCOT achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse model families and eliminates negative transfer even in challenging low-overlap scenarios through Rényi-entropy adaptive reweighting.

problem: Existing instance-wise feature selection methods for explaining black-box model predictions suffer from information leakage, lack of differentiability, and slow training.
approach: Presents Hide&Seek, an end-to-end differentiable model that jointly learns feature selection and prediction under a single objective; reformulates feature removal as a differentiable operation by replacing a proportion of each feature rather than discretely removing them.
contribution: Hide&Seek outperforms existing state-of-the-art models across experiments, is fast to train, and achieves stable training via parsimony-weight annealing.

problem: Existing methods for coupling structural and functional connectivity lack principled formulation grounded in neural communication dynamics, limiting quantification of how information is routed between neural regions.
approach: Formulates multi-modal fusion through neural communication dynamics and proposes Adaptive Flow Routing Network (AFR-Net), a physics-informed framework that models how structural constraints give rise to functional communication patterns.
contribution: AFR-Net significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in discovering critical neural pathways and explaining SC-FC coupling and heterogeneity.

problem: Generalizing motion representation across diverse characters is challenging due to significant topological variations in skeletal structures that hinder development of scalable generative models.
approach: Proposes a Semantic-Aware Topology-Agnostic framework that learns a unified latent manifold using semantic modulation to align functional joint correspondences, thereby decoupling motion from topology.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from large-scale unaligned raw BVH data, enables zero-shot cross-species retargeting without paired data, and supports downstream text-to-motion tasks.

problem: Softmax attention in large language models suffers from numerical instability and reduced performance as the number of inference tokens increases, limiting length extrapolation.
approach: Proposes a two-stage attention mechanism: first stage replaces Softmax with Softplus followed by l1-normalisation with dynamic scale based on invariance entropy; second stage introduces a re-weighting mechanism that amplifies significant attentional weights to mitigate attention sink.
contribution: The novel attention maintains nearly constant validation loss at 16× training length, outperforms Softmax and state-of-the-art Softmax-free alternatives on long-context retrieval tasks.

problem: The learnability of test-time adaptation under non-stationary streams lacks a principled theoretical framework that captures both continuously evolving distribution shifts and intrinsic information constraints.
approach: Introduces the first theoretical framework for studying TTA learnability with Recovery Complexity and TTA Learnability metrics; proposes a discrete surrogate for non-stationary test streams enabling unified analysis of gradual and abrupt shifts.
contribution: Derives order-wise matching lower and upper bounds on recovery complexity, revealing fundamental limits of TTA and an intrinsic adaptivity-information trade-off with unified learnability guarantees.

problem: Existing online benchmarks for mobile GUI agents are app-centric and task-homogeneous, failing to reflect diversity and instability of real-world mobile usage and causing performance gaps.
approach: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile with user-intent-driven task design reflecting real mobile usage and capability-oriented annotation scheme for fine-grained agent behavior analysis.
contribution: Reveals large performance gaps relative to prior benchmarks, shows failures dominated by perception and memory deficiencies, and demonstrates agents exhibit near-zero success under environment variations.

problem: Distributed bilevel optimization over time-varying directed networks remains largely unexplored due to compounded challenges of consensus bias in dynamic unbalanced communication and nested optimization structure.
approach: Proposes FAB, a fully first-order distributed gradient-based algorithm integrating Push-Pull communication strategy with value function-based penalty method for distributed bilevel optimization.
contribution: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence properties and resolves an open question about Push-Pull algorithm convergence over time-varying directed graphs; validates effectiveness on hyperparameter tuning, data hyper-cleaning, and RL.

problem: Medical MLLMs struggle with complex clinical tasks requiring dynamic and iterative focusing on fine-grained visual regions rather than just generating step-by-step textual reasoning.
approach: Introduces Ophiuchus, a tool-augmented framework where an MLLM decides when to probe fine-grained visual regions, determines where within the image to probe, and weaves sub-image content into an interleaved multimodal chain of thought.
contribution: Outperforms both closed-source and open-source methods across diverse medical benchmarks including VQA, detection, and reasoning-based segmentation through three-stage training: cold-start SFT, self-reflection fine-tuning, and agentic tool reinforcement learning.

problem: Architectures like CNNs, Transformers, and SSMs are hindered by static or time-domain-exclusive designs, limiting their representational flexibility for DNA modeling with complex local motifs, long-range dependencies, and periodic signals.
approach: Introduces Synergistic Plasticity Unit (SPU) with three synergistic layers: Locus Plasticity Layer for fine-grained local motifs via token-specific convolution, Domain Plasticity Layer for multi-domain global features via sequential and spectral patterns, and Saliency Plasticity Layer for optimized information flow.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on DNA modeling with quasi-linear complexity and provides theoretical analysis supporting the unified design paradigm.

problem: Trajectory inference from snapshot data is non-identifiable from finitely many marginals, leaving held-out marginal prediction as the dominant evaluation protocol, which provides limited assessment of inferred dynamics.
approach: Introduces a general framework for estimating Kullback-Leibler divergence between probability measures on function space through a tractable, data-driven estimator scalable to realistic snapshot datasets.
contribution: Validates functional KL enables coherent comparison of trajectory inference methods and exposes discrepancies in inferred dynamics, especially in sparse or missing data regions; demonstrates path-space KL as a principled criterion for evaluation under partial observability.

problem: Dynamical system identification from a single trajectory becomes intractable when the system exhibits unknown symmetries or equivariances imposed by physical laws.
approach: Studies adaptive symmetry discovery for systems with unknown group symmetries; proposes a method to learn the symmetry group directly from a single trajectory and incorporate it into identification, achieving optimal trajectory length.
contribution: Shows systems with known symmetries can be identified from significantly shorter trajectories than generic settings; provides group representation theory and Cayley graph analysis for symmetry discovery.

problem: Bundle-valued statistics on manifolds require transporting observations to common reference fibers, introducing curvature and holonomy effects absent from classical concentration theory.
approach: Develops non-asymptotic concentration theory for transported empirical means on manifolds, deriving Hoeffding and Bernstein-type bounds via sharp Hilbert-space inequalities; isolates holonomy bias through bundle curvature.
contribution: Establishes minimax optimal rates with dimension-free bounds, separating stochastic fluctuation from curvature-driven error floor; provides robust median-of-means estimator and central limit theorem in reference fiber.

problem: Vision-Language Models predominantly digest high-bitrate compressed images; their ability to interpret low-bitrate compressed images remains largely unexplored.
approach: Introduces the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating VLM performance on compressed images across codecs and tasks with over one million images; categorizes performance gaps into information loss and generalization failure.
contribution: Proposes a universal VLM adaptor that improves performance across varying codecs and bitrates by 10%-30% through identifying that only generalization gap can be mitigated for compressed images.

problem: Recurrent networks struggle to effectively encode information about past inputs in evolving dynamics rather than converging to static attractors, hindered by vanishing and exploding gradients.
approach: Develops a theoretical framework using dynamic mean-field theory and diffusion physics; derives a Fisher information diffusion operator linking network connectivity to time-resolved information propagation; proposes principled initialization balancing stability and sensitivity.
contribution: Reveals that operating near criticality is necessary but insufficient for reliable memory; effective retention requires alignment between input-output structure and stable dynamical subspaces; demonstrates faster convergence and higher accuracy on copy task and sequential MNIST.

problem: Diffusion models excel at generative tasks for continuous and token-based domains but their application to discrete ordinal data remains underdeveloped.
approach: Presents CountsDiff, a diffusion framework designed to model distributions on natural numbers; extends Blackout diffusion with survival probability parameterization and incorporates continuous-time training, classifier-free guidance, and churn reverse dynamics.
contribution: Matches or surpasses state-of-the-art discrete generative models and scRNA-seq imputation methods on single-cell RNA data while leaving substantial headroom for optimization.

problem: Compositional planning with temporally extended actions struggles with compounding errors in long-horizon predictions that make estimating visitation distribution induced by sequencing policies intractable.
approach: Learns jumpy world models capturing state occupancies induced by pre-trained policies across multiple timescales; enhances with consistency objective aligning predictions across timescales; combines generative predictions to estimate value of arbitrary policy sequences.
contribution: Compositional planning significantly improves zero-shot performance on challenging manipulation and navigation tasks, yielding 200% relative improvement on average over planning with primitive actions.

problem: Vision-Language Models like CLIP degrade significantly in cross-domain scenarios with scarce target-domain data due to uniform alignment paradigms causing excessive overfitting.
approach: Proposes Adaptive Tail-Head Alignment (ATHA) that adaptively strengthens alignment for tokens with sufficient semantic information and weakens alignment for low-similarity tail tokens, transforming uniform to adaptive alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on four challenging CDFSL benchmarks by exploiting the counterintuitive finding that pushing away tail tokens from textual embeddings improves target-domain performance.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models for robot manipulation have representations lacking sensitivity to robotic signals such as control actions and proprioceptive information.
approach: Introduces Robot State-aware Contrastive Loss (RS-CL) that aligns representations with robot proprioceptive states by using relative distances between states as soft supervision, complementing action prediction objectives.
contribution: RS-CL substantially improves performance of state-of-the-art VLA models, achieving 69.7% on RoboCasa-Kitchen benchmark and boosting success rates from 45.0% to 58.3% on challenging real-robot manipulation tasks.

problem: Post-training quantization for W4A4 LLMs remains open, and existing methods designed for INT4 formats suffer from incompatibility with emerging MXFP4 format due to its power-of-two block scaling.
approach: Analyzes the fundamental mismatch between MXFP4's power-of-two block scaling and global rotation-based optimization; proposes a simple block rotation strategy adapting rotation-based methods to MXFP4.
contribution: Provides first in-depth analysis of rotation-based quantization incompatibility with MXFP4 and achieves substantial accuracy improvements across diverse LLMs through block rotation adaptation.

problem: Fine-tuned models on small, imbalanced medical datasets often become overconfident due to norm bias, where predictions rely on feature magnitude rather than semantic alignment.
approach: Proposes Spherical Procrustes Alignment (SPA) combining spherical constraints with dynamic Equiangular Tight Frame alignment; uses Spherical branch to eliminate norm bias via normalization and Geometric branch to adapt features via Procrustes alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on medical audio diagnosis datasets (ICBHI 2017, CirCor DigiScope) and transforms pre-trained models into reliable clinical tools without extra inference cost.

problem: Text-to-video generation methods output only final composited video and lack editable layered representations, limiting use in professional workflows.
approach: Proposes LayerT2V, which produces multiple semantically consistent outputs in a single pass: full video, background layer, and multiple foreground RGB layers with alpha mattes; serializes layer representations along temporal dimension using high compression.
contribution: Substantially outperforms prior methods in visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and cross-layer coherence; introduces VidLayer, the first large-scale dataset for multi-layer video generation.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLM compression via SVD overlooks heterogeneous expert utilization where routing frequency and information density vary significantly across experts.
approach: Proposes RFID-MoE combining expert activation frequency with effective rank to measure importance, adaptively allocating ranks; reconstructs compression residuals via sparse projection mechanism.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving perplexity of 16.92 on PTB with Qwen3-30B at 60% compression ratio, reducing perplexity by over 8.0 compared to baselines.

problem: Practical deployment of LLM-based automated assessment faces persistent challenges: heterogeneous reliability across models, substantial latency and token costs, and lack of principled strategies for resource allocation.
approach: Introduces R²Eval, a routing-aware framework formulating evaluation as resource allocation and aggregation; combines difficulty-aware routing with reasoned evaluation signals to dynamically select evaluator models under accuracy, latency, and cost constraints.
contribution: Provides systematic analysis of how reasoning traces correlate with assessment outcomes; develops offline and online routing strategies achieving substantially improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across 19 language models.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle with complex manipulation tasks requiring high dexterity and generalization due to reliance on synthetic data with significant sim-to-real gaps or limited demonstrations.
approach: Leverages human hands as manipulator template and large-scale human video for VLA pretraining; introduces physical instruction tuning combining VLA pretraining, perspective spatial alignment, and post-training adaptation; develops part-level motion tokenization for millimeter-level accuracy.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance in hand motion generation, favorable scaling laws, and promising capabilities in robotic dexterous manipulation, validating effectiveness of bridging human-robot embodiment gap.

problem: Building LLM workflows typically relies on human-crafted pipelines and prompts, presenting a substantial bottleneck in real-world deployment of AI systems.
approach: Proposes FlowBot, a data-driven approach formulating workflow induction as bilevel optimization: outer loop optimizes workflow sketch structure, inner loop optimizes individual LLM calls via backpropagating textual gradients layer-by-layer.
contribution: Discovered workflows perform competitively against strong baselines using human-crafted or generated workflows.

problem: Post-training quantization of LLMs struggles with temporal inconsistency, invalidation of Round-to-Nearest assumptions, and spatially-inconsistent optimization objectives when synergizing learning-based and compensation-based rounding.
approach: Introduces STLA with cluster-wise integrated rounding optimization resolving temporal inconsistency; achieves spatial alignment through unified global objective derived from Schur Complement; employs Hessian-guided clustering.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art for low-bit PTQ while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Continual learning on pretrained models faces practical barriers where pretraining distributions are unavailable and requires access to old-task data.
approach: Develops PLATE exploiting geometric redundancy in pretrained networks; constructs protected update subspaces from pretrained weights; parameterizes each layer with structured low-rank update where frozen components from pretrained weights and trainable component adapts to new task.
contribution: Provides explicit control over plasticity-retention trade-off without past-task data access and maintains worst-case retention guarantees.

problem: Large language models cannot reliably recognize their parametric knowledge boundaries and often hallucinate answers to out-of-boundary questions.
approach: Introduces MASH (Modeling Abstention via Selective Help-seeking) using reinforcement learning with pay-per-search reward, where external search tool use serves as proxy for abstention when penalized.
contribution: Substantially improves selective help-seeking performance on multi-hop datasets by 7.6%, demonstrates strong off-the-shelf abstention performance competitive with prior methods.

problem: Current AI-Generated Image detectors learn entangled forgery representations, conflating content-dependent flaws with content-agnostic artifacts, and are limited by outdated benchmarks.
approach: Proposes OmniAID with decoupled Mixture-of-Experts architecture: Routable Specialized Semantic Experts separate semantic flaws across domains, Fixed Universal Artifact Expert isolates content-agnostic universal artifacts; employs two-stage training with hard-sampling and lightweight gating.
contribution: Surpasses existing detectors with robust generalization across diverse generative models; introduces Mirage dataset with modern training and challenging test sets.

problem: Comparative capabilities of chain of thought versus latent thought reasoning in large language models remain underexplored despite both exploiting iterative computation.
approach: Presents formal analysis showing latent thought admits efficient parallel computation while CoT is inherently sequential; conversely, CoT enables approximate counting via stochastic decoding.
contribution: Provides formal separations suggesting tasks where depth-driven recursion is more suitable, offering practical guidance for choosing between reasoning paradigms.

problem: Flow-based generative models lack diagnostic tools to assess how much effort trajectories require and how this relates to generation quality and memorization.
approach: Introduces Kinetic Path Energy (KPE), an action-like per-sample diagnostic measuring accumulated kinetic effort along ODE trajectory; develops Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS), a training-free two-phase inference strategy.
contribution: Shows KPE exhibits robust correspondences with semantic fidelity and sparse representation regions; demonstrates non-monotonic correlation at high energy (memorization degeneration); KTS reduces memorization and improves generation quality.

problem: Parallel thinking for reasoning imposes significant computational burdens; existing efficiency methods rely on local per-trajectory signals and lack global mechanisms to exploit dynamics across parallel branches.
approach: Introduces 2D probing exposing width-depth dynamics by eliciting intermediate answers from all branches periodically; develops Parallel-Probe controller with consensus-based early stopping and deviation-based branch pruning.
contribution: Establishes superior Pareto frontier for test-time scaling, reducing sequential tokens by up to 35.8% and total token cost by over 25.8% compared to majority voting.

problem: Code transformation tasks rely on implicit representation construction in model weights or rigid compiler-level abstractions rather than constructing high-quality representations explicitly.
approach: Presents SemRep employing semantics-preserving transformations as intermediate representation; serves both as generative mid-training task and guidance for instruction-specific transformations.
contribution: Outperforms extensively finetuned baselines by 6.9% in correctness, 1.1× in performance, 13.9% in generalization, and 6.7% in robustness; with evolutionary agent finds optimizations that 685B larger-weight baselines miss.

problem: GPU kernel optimization by LLM agents remains inefficient due to fundamental mismatch between LLM generation capabilities and vast optimization search space over diverse hardware.
approach: Formulates kernel optimization as Multi-Armed Bandit problem; designs hardware-aware pruning via profiling bounds and runtime-behavior clustering leveraging Lipschitz continuity to navigate infinite arm space.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strongest agent baseline, achieving up to 1.91× geometric mean speedup with 39-140% relative improvement in Fast@1 success rate across three GPU architectures.

problem: Natural language instructions are often underspecified, mapping to multiple valid yet functionally distinct latent intents; LLMs remain limited in interactive disambiguation due to semantic blindness.
approach: Proposes Topological Active Inference (TAI) recasting task disambiguation as intent-manifold contraction; uses Persistent Homology to recover persistent intent clusters; selects clarifying questions with Topological Expected Information Gain.
contribution: Reduces effective hypothesis space from N sampled solutions to K latent intents with logarithmic interaction complexity O(log K); resolves user intent with fewer turns and robustness to noisy feedback.

problem: Text-to-image generation models lack fine-grained control over generated images due to limited understanding of how semantic information is encoded in latent space.
approach: Develops interpretation of color representation in Variational Autoencoder latent space revealing structure reflecting Hue, Saturation, and Lightness; leverages closed-form latent-space manipulation.
contribution: Introduces fully training-free method in FLUX for predicting and explicitly controlling color through Latent Color Subspace interpretation.

problem: Flow map matching for one- and few-step sampling suffers from mismatch between ground-truth training transitions and model-induced flow maps, hindering performance.
approach: Proposes Contrastive Flow Map Matching (CFMM) motivated by joint-KL decomposition on reverse KL; combines average-velocity regression for marginal alignment with sampling-aligned InfoNCE contrastive loss.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements in fidelity and perceptual quality across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and LSUN with only modest additional training cost and no inference-time overhead.

problem: Decentralized online convex optimization with compressed communication suffers from prohibitively high quadratic or quartic dependence on compression quality factor and super-linear dependence on number of learners.
approach: Proposes novel algorithm with two-level blocking update framework incorporating online gossip strategy and error compensation scheme; establishes improved regret bounds and first lower bounds for the problem.
contribution: Achieves improved regret bounds of Õ(ω^{-1/2}ρ^{-1}n√T) and Õ(ω^{-1}ρ^{-2}n ln T) for convex and strongly convex functions, justifying optimality with respect to compression quality and time horizon.

problem: Probabilistic circuits use data-independent mixture weights that fail to capture the local geometry of data manifolds, limiting their expressiveness.
approach: The paper proposes incorporating Voronoi tessellations into PC sum nodes to capture geometric structure, then provides approximate inference with bounds and identifies conditions for exact tractable inference, plus a differentiable relaxation for gradient-based learning.
contribution: Voronoi tessellations enable geometry-aware probabilistic circuits with either bounded approximate inference or exact tractable inference, validated on standard density estimation tasks.

problem: Multi-view classifiers that fuse all views into a single representation become fragile when some views are missing or corrupted.
approach: A prototype-anchored fusion module based on unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) barycenter summarizes each view into atoms matched to a shared prototype support, with a generalized KL penalty that acts as an automatic trimming mechanism.
contribution: The UOT-based approach improves stability under severe missingness on multi-view action recognition benchmarks with modest overhead, with theoretical bounds on discarding arbitrary atom mass.

problem: The attention sink phenomenon in LLMs, where initial tokens monopolize attention scores, lacks a clear mechanistic explanation.
approach: The paper traces attention sinks to value aggregation variance discrepancy amplified by super neurons in FFN layers, causing dimension disparity in first-token representation, validated through controlled interventions on attention masks and token variance.
contribution: A mechanistic explanation of attention sinks as a structural anchor for dimension disparity, with head-wise RMSNorm architectural modification that accelerates convergence by stabilizing value aggregation.

problem: Spiking neural networks and state space models each have advantages (energy efficiency vs. scalability) but existing approaches do not combine both for long-sequence modeling.
approach: A spiking heterogeneous harmonic resonate-and-fire state space model (SH2RFSSM) eliminates matrix multiplications while scaling to ultra-long sequences, with a kernel-based spiking regressor for sequences up to 50k steps.
contribution: SH2RFSSM outperforms transformers and first-order SSMs on average across 17 datasets while eliminating matrix multiplications, suitable for resource-constrained applications.

problem: Solving deep complex problems like Humanity's Last Exam requires both high capability and computational efficiency, which large generalists struggle to balance.
approach: ToolOrchestra trains small 8B orchestrators using reinforcement learning with outcome-, efficiency-, and preference-aware rewards to coordinate diverse tools and models, achieving higher performance at lower cost.
contribution: Orchestrator achieves 37.1% on HLE outperforming GPT-5 at 35.1% while being 2.5x more efficient, and surpasses GPT-5 on tau2-Bench and FRAMES using only 30% of the cost.

problem: Many sampling tasks require evaluating unnormalized target distributions which can be prohibitively costly or infeasible, limiting MCMC algorithm applicability.
approach: The paper unifies disparate MCMC algorithms (exchange, PoissonMH, TunaMH) under a common auxiliary variable procedure and extends it to use estimated gradients for proposal moves.
contribution: New MCMC algorithms that use estimated gradients significantly outperform existing methods on both synthetic and real datasets without requiring target evaluation.

problem: Existing de novo protein design models directly synthesize geometries without reasoning about which residues are functionally essential, limiting interpretability and reusability of biochemical knowledge.
approach: Proteo-R1 uses a dual-expert architecture where an LLM analyzes sequences/structures/text to identify key functional residues, then passes these decisions to a diffusion-based generation expert for conditional co-design.
contribution: Reasoning-guided protein design achieves stable, interpretable, and modular integration of LLM reasoning with geometric generative models for de novo protein design.

problem: Autoregressive language models frequently degrade during long-horizon generation with repetitive text, lost instruction adherence, and unstable entropy, but practitioners lack online diagnostics.
approach: The paper formalizes degradation as cognitive fatigue characterized by attention decay to prompt, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration, introducing Fatigue Index (FI) that aggregates three signals under explicit axioms.
contribution: Fatigue Index is a lightweight model-agnostic diagnostic predicting task degradation (AUROC=0.95) and repetition (rho=0.94), revealing non-monotonic scaling where small instruction-tuned models collapse faster than base models.

problem: Online configuration selection with admission control in LLM serving and resource scheduling requires both upper-bound benchmarking and theoretically-grounded algorithms.
approach: A switching-aware fluid oracle accounts for value of mixing configurations over time, with saddle point formulation solved via SP-UCB-OLP algorithm combining optimistic saddle point solving.
contribution: SP-UCB-OLP algorithm achieves tilde-O(sqrt(KT)) regret with theoretical guarantees, enabling principled online resource scheduling.
