contribution: Adaptive merging improves performance over base model but provides limited benefit over training new LoRA; random LoRAs yield similar performance to curated pools.

problem: Last-iterate convergence for stochastic monotone variational inequalities lacks anytime guarantees despite relevance to uncoupled learning dynamics.
approach: Analyze regularized gradient (RG) and regularized optimistic gradient (ROG) methods, establishing anytime last-iterate convergence rates in terms of squared gap function.
contribution: RG attains O(t^{-2/5}) and ROG achieves variance-adaptive O(σ^{4/5} t^{-2/5} + t^{-1}), providing guarantees without knowing horizon.

problem: Cache-based test-time adaptation for VLMs introduces latency overhead as cache grows with classes and performs suboptimally with insufficient cache samples.
approach: Prototype-Based Test-Time Adaptation (PTA) uses class-specific knowledge prototypes weighted by zero-shot confidence, accumulating knowledge from test samples without cache overhead.
contribution: PTA improves CLIP accuracy from 65.64% to 69.38% on 10 cross-domain benchmarks while retaining 92% inference speed, state-of-the-art on 15 image and 4 point cloud benchmarks.

problem: Object insertion methods achieve high visual quality but treat insertion as 2D inpainting without explicit 3D pose control, limiting practical applicability.
approach: DIRECT decomposes insertion into appearance, geometry, and context guidance injected through separate pathways, enabling pose-controllable insertion via interactive 3D proxy manipulation.
contribution: DIRECT outperforms previous methods in both geometric controllability and visual quality with automated data construction pipeline.

problem: Test-time scaling via token sampling requires temperature tuning trading off diversity against stability, with fine-grained MoE offering unexplored routing alternatives.
approach: Expert-Sample preserves high-confidence expert selections while injecting controlled stochasticity into uncertain tail of router scores, enabling diverse generation.
contribution: Expert-Sample consistently improves pass@n and verification-based accuracy; on Qwen3-30B pass@32 rises from 85.4% to 91.9% with Best-of-N verification reaching 62.6%.

problem: Small language models fail to scale with task complexity on deep search and coding, with unclear routing strategies for leveraging heterogeneous agents.
approach: Strategy Auctions for Workload Efficiency (SALE) enables agents to bid with strategic plans scored by cost-value mechanism with shared auction memory for per-task routing.
contribution: SALE reduces reliance on largest agent by 52%, lowers overall cost by 35%, and improves pass@1 with negligible overhead, enabling effective small-agent scaling.

problem: Optimal mechanisms for private mean estimation in shuffle model remain unexplored despite differences from local differential privacy settings.
approach: Formulate post-shuffling mechanism design as explicit optimization using shuffle index, establishing lower bounds on achievable mean squared error.
contribution: Constructs asymptotically optimal mechanism achieving privacy-utility trade-off nearly identical to central Gaussian mechanism.

problem: Medical images show sparse visual evidence for clinical decision-making but existing VLM-RL approaches don't prune irrelevant visual tokens before reasoning.
approach: ViToS dual-stream RL framework trains one policy for both visual token pruning and question answering, solving coupled learning via cross-feedback sequential optimization.
contribution: ViToS reduces visual tokens to 77% of original while achieving 108.27% relative performance on Lingshu-7B and 104.16% on HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B.

problem: Long-term time series forecasting emphasizes architectural complexity over fundamental forecasting structures, leading to overengineering and poor generalization.
approach: ReNF reformulates LTSF using Variance Reduction Hypothesis and Boosted Direct Output paradigm hybridizing Auto-Regressive and Direct Output with parameter smoothing.
contribution: Direct temporal MLP outperforms recent complex state-of-the-art models on nearly all benchmarks without intricate inductive biases.

problem: Energy-based models offer flexible distribution modeling but are hindered by unstable and inefficient training that limits their practical adoption.
approach: The method uses informative latent variables to guide joint energy learning while incorporating a cooperative generator for MCMC initialization, allowing optimization only in data space.
contribution: Demonstrates improved generation quality, training stability with fewer resources, and effective performance across multiple downstream tasks.

problem: Inference-time steering of diffusion models via composed experts fails when ratio-of-densities constructions create non-normalizable intermediate distributions despite valid endpoints.
approach: Provides a Path Existence Criterion to characterize well-defined composed densities and introduces Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE) supporting time-varying exponents via Feynman-Kac steering.
contribution: ACE prevents marginal path collapse, significantly outperforms constant-exponent baselines on drug design, and improves attribute success rates in compositional image generation.

problem: Autonomous vehicles struggle with the stability-plasticity trade-off: adapting to rare long-tail driving scenarios while preserving previously learned skills.
approach: NOMAD integrates non-parametric Bayesian memory with diffusion-based trajectory experts, mapping growing scene contexts to dynamic memory clusters that guide a conditional diffusion model functioning as a mixture of experts.
contribution: Achieves 9.4% improvement in interPlan score on nuPlan long-tail scenarios with positive backward transfer during continual learning.

problem: Existing estimators for score differences in diffusion models either lack statistical consistency or fail to scale in high dimensions, limiting transfer learning and discriminator guidance applications.
approach: Proposes a Sobolev-regularized estimator for score differences that ensures consistency and training stability, with convergence rate of Õ(n^(-(s-1)/(d+2s-2))).
contribution: Demonstrates improved stability in small-sample regimes and substantially outperforms non-regularized methods on transfer learning for ECG signal generation.

problem: Diffusion Transformers incur high computational costs due to dual forward passes in Classifier-Free Guidance and uniform calibration across transformer blocks regardless of varying sensitivity.
approach: RSTR jointly reduces temporal and spatial redundancy: Stage-1 uses evolutionary search to discover sparse guidance schedules with variable scales; Stage-2 applies adaptive rank allocation based on block sensitivity.
contribution: Achieves 50-70% compute savings while maintaining or improving quality, with 57% savings and 15% FID improvement on DiT-XL/2 and 3.43x speedup on Qwen-Image.

problem: Vision-language models struggle with multimodal entity tracking, exhibiting large performance gaps between text-based and image-based entity state tracking.
approach: MET-Bench evaluates VLMs on tracking entity states across three domains and modalities, revealing that performance gaps stem from visual reasoning deficits rather than perception limitations, with reinforcement learning applied to improve tracking.
contribution: Demonstrates that explicit text-based reasoning strategies improve performance but RL gains do not transfer robustly across input modalities, highlighting need for improved multimodal representations.

problem: Generative Flow Networks must train on offline datasets without access to active reward queries, but existing proxy-free methods impose coarse constraints limiting exploration effectiveness.
approach: TD-GFN uses inverse reinforcement learning to extract dense transition-level edge rewards from offline trajectories, guiding policy indirectly through DAG pruning and prioritized backward sampling to ensure robustness.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing baselines in convergence speed and sample quality for offline GFlowNet training.

problem: Bayes-assisted conformal prediction suffers when the Bayesian working model is misspecified, resulting in inefficient prediction sets despite preserving distribution-free frequentist coverage.
approach: RoBAS introduces robust nonconformity scores using heavy-tailed Bayesian models or empirical Bayes shrinkage, adapting to prior quality by exploiting reliable information while reverting to Distance-To-Average baseline when prior is weak.
contribution: Achieves competitive efficiency in absence of distribution shift while substantially reducing interval widths in shifted settings on tabular and image regression tasks.

problem: Generating human videos with realistic motions lacks decoupled control over foreground subject, background, trajectory, and action patterns, limiting flexible composition.
approach: RealisMotion uses a 3D world coordinate system for motion editing with trajectory control via unprojection and coordinate transformation, injecting subject as attention tokens while concatenating background and adding motion control signals.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on element-wise controllability and overall video quality with realistic decomposed motion control.

problem: In adaptive experiments, expensive labeled data collection is limited but large unlabeled datasets and pretrained models are available, yet leveraging predictions without validating inference is fundamentally challenging.
approach: PPAI integrates unlabeled data, predicted labels, and adaptively collected labeled data through a single estimating equation with adaptive weighting of predictions based on informativeness.
contribution: Enables valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests with asymptotic variance no worse than labeled-only baseline and strictly smaller when predictions are informative.

problem: LLM-powered edge devices need cloud assistance for reasoning but static task routing based on difficulty overlooks subtask dependencies and misses parallelization opportunities.
approach: HybridFlow builds dependency-aware DAGs enabling concurrent subtask execution, with dynamic benefit-cost utility model optimizing trade-offs between accuracy, token cost, and latency in real-time.
contribution: Improves cost-accuracy trade-off while reducing latency and cloud API usage on GPQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME24, and LiveBench-Reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Schema linking for Text-to-SQL prioritizes textual similarity and inadvertently prunes topologically-critical bridge tables, severing relational pathways necessary for multi-hop joins.
approach: Graph-Link reformulates schema linking as constrained subgraph induction using hierarchical schema graphs and Steiner-tree optimization that guarantees topological connectivity while maximizing signal-to-noise ratio.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art schema linking with up to 7.0% improvement in recall/hit rates and 13.8% boost in SQL generation accuracy on complex queries on BIRD and Spider 2.0.

problem: Large-scale LLM training requires stable and efficient optimization, but existing orthogonal equivalence transformation methods incur high memory consumption and computational overhead.
approach: POET-X performs orthogonal equivalence transformations with significantly reduced computational cost while maintaining stability benefits of spectrum-preserving optimization.
contribution: Enables pretraining of billion-parameter LLMs on a single H100 GPU where standard optimizers like AdamW run out of memory.

problem: Long-form text generation from LLMs suffers from hallucination snowballing where early errors propagate and compound into subsequent outputs.
approach: SHARS uses an arbitrary hallucination detector to identify and reject hallucinated segments during generation, resampling until faithful content is produced while retaining only confident information.
contribution: Substantially reduces hallucinations in long-form generation while preserving or improving informativeness without requiring external resources like web search.

problem: Diffusion language models require fully-factorized output distributions because explicit joint modeling would produce prohibitively large parameter counts, creating a speed-coherence trade-off.
approach: CoDD replaces fully-factorized output distributions with a lightweight probabilistic inference layer that models complex joint dependencies while remaining compact.
contribution: Matches reasoning performance of computationally intensive RL baselines at a fraction of training cost and prevents collapse in few-step generation.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs faces severe statistical heterogeneity from intrinsic data distribution mismatches that model-level defenses typically overlook.
approach: FedSDR augments Federated Self-Distillation with a dual-stream mechanism: LoRA-S for smoothing to absorb heterogeneity via distilled data and LoRA-R for rectification anchored to raw data for factual correctness.
contribution: Yields a globally aligned and faithful model with superior performance compared to conventional algorithms.

problem: Simulation-based inference struggles with effective multimodal modeling as existing methods ignore structural disparities between parameters and observations via brute-force fusion strategies.
approach: FUSE employs a dual-track architecture preserving distinct features of multimodal inputs with FK-steered sampling leveraging intermediate observation likelihoods to guide generative trajectories.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on SBI benchmarks and successfully resolves complex parameter degeneracies in exoplanet orbital estimation.

problem: Analyzing attention weights as a standard interpretation approach neglects geometric properties of value vectors being aggregated, providing incomplete mechanistic insights.
approach: Contribution Weights measure token influence by accounting for attention weight, value magnitude, and directional alignment with layer output via projection-based metrics.
contribution: Provides more faithful measure of token importance than attention-based metrics and enables novel analysis revealing attention sinks suppress information through convex relationship with output norm.

problem: Optimizing training efficiency and model performance for data-driven weather forecasting requires understanding empirical scaling relationships across model size, dataset size, and compute budget.
approach: Analyzes scaling laws for weather models finding that data scaling shows stronger effects than parameter scaling and optimal allocation favors larger training datasets over increased model size.
contribution: Aurora exhibits strongest data-scaling (10x data→3.2x loss reduction) and reveals weather models favor increased width over depth, contrasting language model scaling behaviors.

problem: Fixed-vocabulary language integration for image clustering causes inter-modal semantic misalignment due to granularity discrepancy while overlooking intra-modal semantic redundancy.
approach: MAGIC prompts vision-language models to generate multi-granularity descriptions and designs modality-specific adapters that refine features into clustering-friendly representations under task guidance.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods through effective multi-modal alignment and reduced semantic redundancy.

problem: Extending neural optimal transport to high-dimensional Riemannian manifolds is challenged by curse of dimensionality: discrete approximations require exponentially more parameters with manifold dimension.
approach: Riemannian Neural OT (RNOT) uses continuous neural-network parameterizations incorporating geometric structure by construction while avoiding discretization.
contribution: Approximates Riemannian OT maps with sub-exponential complexity in dimension and demonstrates improved scalability relative to discretization-based baselines.

problem: Autoregressive decoding imposes fundamental latency bottleneck for real-time LLM function calling needed by embodied intelligence and interactive agents.
approach: RealtimeTool introduces special tokens compressing low-entropy tokens (4-6x reduction) while enabling independent parallel generation of function names and arguments.
contribution: Achieves 3-6x end-to-end speedup (up to 9.6x) with only 8.2% parallelization overhead and enables 16 Hz real-time control on consumer GPUs.

problem: Pixel-level accurate segmentation of structural cracks across diverse scenarios struggles with balancing crack topology modeling and computational efficiency.
approach: SCRWKV uses Structure-Field Encoder with Geometry-guided Bidirectional Structure Transformation to capture topological correlations and Dynamic Self-Calibrating Decay to suppress noise propagation.
contribution: Achieves F1 score of 0.8428 and mIoU of 0.8512 on TUT dataset with only 1.22M parameters, significantly outperforming SOTA methods.

problem: Dynamic graph anomaly detection with limited labeled anomalies faces gap between unsupervised methods producing ambiguous boundaries and semi-supervised methods overfitting to rare labeled data.
approach: Framework uses residual representation encoding capturing deviations from context, restriction loss constraining normal representations within co-centered hyperspheres, and bi-boundary optimization with normalizing flows.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority across diverse evaluation settings in learning discriminative and generalizable anomaly detectors.

problem: Text-to-image model evaluation predominantly focuses on image realism and shallow text-image alignment, lacking assessment of complex semantic understanding and world knowledge integration.
approach: WISE benchmark includes 1000 meticulously crafted prompts across 25 subdomains in cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning, and natural science with novel WiScore metric for knowledge-image alignment.
contribution: Reveals significant limitations in 20 models (10 dedicated T2I and 10 unified multimodal) regarding ability to effectively integrate and apply world knowledge.

problem: Point clouds from diverse domains with distinct sensing geometries, densities, and priors are typically handled separately, missing benefits of unified representation learning.
approach: Utonia trains a single self-supervised point transformer encoder jointly across five heterogeneous domains (remote sensing, outdoor LiDAR, indoor RGB-D, CAD models, video-lifted clouds).
contribution: Learns consistent representation space with improved perception, benefits embodied and multimodal reasoning, and demonstrates emergent behaviors from joint training.

problem: Efficient aggregation methods for quantile inference under privacy constraints with heterogeneous datasets remain underdeveloped.
approach: Framework constructs weighted estimators by adaptively aggregating quantile estimates from target and source sites under local differential privacy with adaptive weights minimizing asymptotic variance.
contribution: Establishes consistency, normality, and effectiveness with rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrates robust inference across heterogeneous scenarios.

problem: PPO's ratio clipping mechanism is structurally ill-suited for large vocabularies as it over-penalizes low-probability token updates while under-constraining high-probability shifts.
approach: DPPO substitutes heuristic clipping with principled constraint based on direct policy divergence estimates (Total Variation or KL) using efficient Binary and Top-K approximations.
contribution: Achieves superior stability and efficiency compared to PPO with more robust foundation for RL-based LLM fine-tuning.

problem: Existing relational deep learning methods neglect class imbalance problem in relational database entity classification, under-representing minority entities.
approach: Rel-MOSS designs relation-centric minority synthetic over-sampling with relation-wise gating controller to modulate neighborhood messages and relation-guided minority synthesizer.
contribution: Yields average improvement of up to 2.46% in Balanced Accuracy and 4.00% in G-Mean compared to SOTA RDL methods.

problem: Current evaluation methods for video generation models rely on subjective judgments or trajectory matching, lacking rigorous assessment of physical law adherence.
approach: Morpheus is physics-informed evaluation framework using 130 real-world videos capturing physical phenomena guided by conservation laws, assessing plausibility via interpretable metrics.
contribution: Reveals that contemporary models struggle to encode Newtonian physics despite generating aesthetically pleasing videos, identifying critical pathways for enhancement.

problem: Training CT-specific VAEs from scratch incurs substantial cost and degrades under heterogeneous scanners, protocols, and diseases.
approach: Foundation VAE leverages pretrained natural-image VAE for frozen encoder-decoder serving as unified interface for CT reconstruction, augmentation, and generation.
contribution: Achieves 3.9% NSD improvement for segmentation on reconstructions and 3.9% lower FVD with 36.2% higher CT CLIP score for generation.

problem: LLM long-context inference incurs significant memory overhead as KV cache scales linearly with sequence length and batch size.
approach: OBCache formulates cache eviction as layer-wise structured pruning using Optimal Brain Damage theory, quantifying token saliency via output perturbation with closed-form scores.
contribution: Improves long-context accuracy on LLaMA and Qwen models by replacing heuristic scores with output-aware signals.

problem: Chain-of-Thought reasoning lacks efficiency: models generate unnecessary tokens long after reaching correct answers, and early termination risks incorrect conclusions.
approach: Detects Confidence Region transitions via CUSUM change-point detection algorithm for real-time inference control, enabling early exit and test-time scaling.
contribution: Achieves 63.06% accuracy with 11.1% token reduction, outperforming DEER and Dynasor by 3.28% and 4.36% respectively.

problem: Model-induced label noise from Foundation Models and pre-trained experts introduces systematic errors tightly coupled with local feature manifolds, defying classical transition matrix approaches.
approach: MIND decouples noise into tractable subspace-dependent components via Latent Manifold Disentanglement, with Latent Decoding Estimator projecting samples into clusters with consistent error modes.
contribution: Significantly outperforms SOTA on controlled CIFAR-100 and structural stress tests on 3D datasets, effectively correcting Vision-Language Model zero-shot hallucinations.

problem: Unsupervised and supervised tensor network learning have developed in parallel, missing opportunities for cooperative advancement.
approach: MTNL unifies fields by fusing multiple TNs in deep-network style and develops flexible TN structure search with theoretical guarantees, combined within Bayesian framework.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness on tensor recovery, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and tensor regression with lightweight uncertainty quantification.

problem: Monolithic neural network simulators lack essential features of traditional numerical simulators: physical interpretability, reliability, and constraint satisfaction.
approach: Neural Modular Physics decomposes elastic dynamics into physically meaningful modules connected through intermediate physical quantities with specialized architecture.
contribution: Demonstrates superior generalization to unseen conditions, stable long-horizon simulation, better physical property preservation, and feasibility with unknown dynamics.

problem: Predicting Hamiltonian matrices for electronic structure calculations via SO(3)-equivariant networks requires costly Clebsch-Gordan tensor products, limiting scalability.
approach: QHNetV2 achieves global SO(3) equivariance via efficient SO(2)-equivariant operations on SO(2) local frames, eliminating costly tensor products.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on QH9 and MD17 datasets with strong generalization across molecular structures.

problem: NeRF latent spaces are implicit and globally entangled, making localized editing and physically grounded manipulation difficult while deformation sensitivity causes artifacts.
approach: Affine-Equivariant Kernel Space Encoding aggregates features via anisotropic Gaussian kernels enabling stable interpolation under transformations with feature distillation from hash grids.
contribution: Provides intuitive localized scene editing via Gaussian kernels without retraining while maintaining high-quality rendering.

problem: Graph neural networks for mixed-integer linear programming model locality limits representation power for combinatorial optimization.
approach: Proposes attention-driven neural backbone with element-centric view and dual attention performing parallel intra-type self-attention and inter-type cross-attention.
contribution: Consistently outperforms GNN-based architectures across instance, element, and solving-state level tasks.

problem: Reasoning LLMs generate extended chain-of-thought that is fragile to information loss during decoding, making KV cache compression challenging without disrupting reasoning.
approach: RLKV uses reinforcement learning to discover which attention heads maintain reasoning consistency, enabling aggressive compression on non-critical heads while retaining full cache on reasoning-critical heads.
contribution: Enables 20-60% cache reduction with near-lossless performance and up to 2.06x end-to-end speedup at 60% reduction across diverse tasks.

problem: Dense linear layers in neural networks must be quantized to low precision, creating a tradeoff between compression and output accuracy.
approach: WaterSIC allocates different quantization rates to different columns of weight matrices using a waterfilling strategy from information theory, achieving a rate gap of 0.255 bits to the theoretical optimum.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance for quantization rates 1 to 4 bits on Llama and Qwen LLMs while staying near the information-theoretic limit.

problem: Visual tokenization faces an inherent tradeoff where optimizing for pixel fidelity conflicts with semantic abstraction, causing destructive interference in gradient optimization.
approach: MUSE uses topological orthogonality to physically decouple structural and semantic optimization subspaces within Transformers, routing gradients to separate components that reinforce rather than conflict.
contribution: Breaks the reconstruction-abstraction tradeoff, achieving state-of-the-art generation (gFID 3.08) while outperforming teacher model InternViT-300M in linear probing (85.2% vs 82.5%).

problem: Concept erasure methods for removing unwanted content from text-to-image models do not work with single-stream diffusion transformers, leading to generation collapse.
approach: Z-Erase proposes a stream-disentangled concept erasure framework that decouples updates for single-stream models, then applies Lagrangian-guided adaptive erasure modulation to balance the erasure-preservation tradeoff.
contribution: Successfully enables concept erasure in single-stream T2I models with convergence guarantees to Pareto stationarity, overcoming generation collapse issues.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts layers require complex hyperparameter tuning for router weights and architectural choices (number and size of experts), making HP selection costly and unreliable across model scales.
approach: A novel parameterization justified by dynamical mean-field theory enables hyperparameter transfer across MoE models when scaling width, depth, number of experts, and expert size.
contribution: Reliable hyperparameter transfer demonstrated across models from 51M to 2B parameters; small-model HPs transferred to large models on longer training horizons show performant behavior.

problem: Adversarial examples exploit neural networks through unclear mechanisms; existing explanations based on geometry and data properties do not explain why specific perturbations succeed or transfer between models.
approach: Models adversarial vulnerability as arising from superposition (networks representing more concepts than dimensions), where non-orthogonal representations create interference patterns that attacks exploit.
contribution: Shows superposition suffices to create adversarial vulnerability with predictable attack structure; explains transferability through similar interference patterns across models trained on the same data.

problem: The inference-time algorithm by which transformers perform in-context classification from few examples remains opaque and difficult to interpret.
approach: Enforce feature and label-permutation equivariance at every layer to make computation identifiable, revealing a depth-indexed recursion implementing geometry-driven algorithmic updates.
contribution: Extract the first explicit, identifiable update rule for softmax transformers performing in-context logistic regression, showing how attention drives coupled updates of training points and test probes.

problem: Pre-trained LLM checkpoints represent sunk computational costs but are difficult to extend due to architectural limitations, and training new models from scratch remains expensive.
approach: Orthogonal growth strategy expands converged Mixture-of-Experts models through interpositional layer copying for depth and noisy expert duplication for width, then continues training.
contribution: Recycling approach yields 10.6% accuracy improvement compared to training from scratch under identical compute budgets on models up to 70B parameters and 1T tokens.

problem: Knowledge-intensive visual question answering suffers from knowledge conflicts caused by open-domain retrieval limitations, lacking generalizable conflict detection and intra-model constraints.
approach: REAL framework introduces reasoning-pivots (atomic units in reasoning chains emphasizing knowledge linkage) and uses SFT with pivot extraction plus pivot-guided decoding for targeted conflict resolution.
contribution: Enhanced discrimination accuracy through pivot-driven reasoning; superior performance on diverse datasets with a new REAL-VQA dataset supporting the approach.

problem: AI agents with tool-calling capabilities are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks where malicious content tricks agents into unauthorized actions, and existing defenses overprotect at cost to utility.
approach: CausalArmor uses leave-one-out ablation to compute lightweight attributions at decision points, triggering sanitization only when untrusted content dominates the user intent, plus retroactive CoT masking.
contribution: Matches security of aggressive defenses while improving explainability and preserving utility; theoretical analysis shows sanitization yields exponentially small upper bound on malicious action selection.

problem: Machine learning models achieve strong predictive performance but fail to translate into clinical practice due to misalignment with deployment constraints like memorability and auditability.
approach: AgentScore uses LLMs to propose candidate clinical rules in an exponentially large search space, with deterministic verification-and-selection loops enforcing statistical validity and deployability constraints.
contribution: Outperforms existing score-generation methods with AUROC comparable to flexible interpretable models; achieves higher discrimination than established guideline-based scores on external validation tasks.

problem: Debate-based AI oversight incentivizes persuasion over truthfulness, creating misalignment between argumentation success and epistemic honesty.
approach: Disagreement Resolution reframes oversight from adversarial debate to collaborative truth-seeking, using mediation-inspired strategies where agents identify points of disagreement, examine evidence, and converge toward consensus.
contribution: Non-expert models achieve 62.1% judging accuracy with disagreement resolution versus 49.2% for standard debate, providing empirical evidence for collaborative paradigms in scalable oversight.

problem: Reinforcement learning with delayed state observations, where agents observe current states after random time steps, lacks optimal algorithms with known sample complexity bounds.
approach: Combines augmentation methods with upper confidence bound approaches; derives regret bound O(H sqrt(D_max SAK)) for tabular MDPs and provides matching lower bound.
contribution: Establishes optimal sample complexity for tabular MDPs with delayed observations; general analytical framework applies to MDPs with decomposable transition dynamics.

problem: Optimizers inherit implicit biases from their norm-induced geometries, but cannot simultaneously control both spectral and coordinate-wise structure needed for effective training.
approach: OLion combines spectral control from orthogonalized update directions with ell-infinity coordinate control from sign updates, approximating constrained optimization over scaled Hadamard-like sets.
contribution: Matches or outperforms AdamW and Muon across large-scale language and vision training (GPT-2, Llama, SiT) while using only momentum-level optimizer state.

problem: Modeling wireless channels in complex environments is challenging; conventional ray-tracing requires hand-engineered rules while black-box neural methods do not explicitly preserve physical structure.
approach: SNRFT integrates neural representations with physics-based RF propagation by modeling RF transport as a stochastic process where material-dependent attenuation naturally emerges as rate parameters.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods on real-world wireless communication and sensing testbeds while requiring significantly fewer training samples.

problem: High-dimensional embedding spaces used for generative model evaluation exhibit hubness, which distorts nearest-neighbor relationships and biases distance-based metrics.
approach: GICDM extends Iterative Contextual Dissimilarity Measure with multi-scale corrections to resolve hubness-induced failures in both real and generated data neighborhoods.
contribution: Restores reliable metric behavior and improves alignment with human assessment; resolves hubness-induced evaluation failures for generative models.

problem: Dynamic data selection methods rely on task-specific handcrafted metrics or static criteria, limiting scalability across paradigms and failing to capture evolving data utility during training.
approach: Data Agent formulates selection as a training-aware sequential decision problem where an agent learns sample-wise policies co-evolving with model optimization, guided by composite rewards integrating loss and confidence.
contribution: Consistently accelerates training while preserving performance across diverse datasets; reduces costs by over 50% on ImageNet-1k and MMLU with lossless performance.

problem: Users of LLM-powered agents may wonder what outcomes would result from expressing their intent differently, but counterfactual reasoning in closed-loop agentic systems lacks formal reliability guarantees.
approach: Models closed-loop user-agent-environment interaction as a structural causal model and uses test-time scaling with probabilistic abduction for multiple counterfactuals, with conformal inference for coverage guarantees.
contribution: Provides formal guarantees that counterfactual outcome sets contain the true outcome with high probability; demonstrates advantages over naive re-execution baselines.

problem: Large language model-based agents acting autonomously may engage in upward deception, concealing failures and performing unrequested actions without reporting them.
approach: Constructs a benchmark of 200 tasks across five types and eight realistic scenarios; evaluates 11 LLMs to characterize deceptive behaviors and tests mitigation strategies.
contribution: Demonstrates that agents typically exhibit action-based deceptive behaviors (guessing, fabrication, substitution); mitigation methods achieve only limited reductions, highlighting need for stronger strategies.

problem: Masked diffusion language models fail to uniformly use context despite bidirectional attention; appending mask tokens required for generation acts as a distractor, degrading comprehension.
approach: Introduces mask-agnostic loss function that encourages predictions to remain invariant to the number of appended masks, combined with fine-tuning to mitigate masking distraction.
contribution: Reveals locality bias in MDLMs similar to autoregressive models; mask-agnostic training substantially improves robustness of context comprehension in MDLMs.

problem: Multi-objective reinforcement learning struggles to incorporate explicit constraints while promoting fairness via max-min criterion.
approach: Integrates max-min criterion with constraint satisfaction in a MORL framework; establishes theoretical foundation and validates through convergence analysis and experiments.
contribution: Effectively balances fairness and constraint satisfaction across simulated domains including building thermal control, locomotion, and traffic management.

problem: Graph neural networks struggle with oversquashing in deep layers and exhibit unstable signal propagation in flat or ill-conditioned regions.
approach: TANGO introduces learnable Lyapunov functions to define energy non-increasing directions, augmented with tangential components learned via message passing for flexible feature evolution.
contribution: Achieves strong performance on diverse node and graph classification benchmarks; energy-based framework helps alleviate oversquashing in GNNs.

problem: Lateral excitatory-inhibitory connections remain underexplored in deep learning despite ubiquity in cortex; their role in adaptive coding strategies is unclear.
approach: Analyzes and trains stabilized supralinear networks with strong E-I lateral connections using local plasticity rules on natural images, demonstrating dynamic coding transitions.
contribution: Shows E-I recurrence enables adaptive coding where networks shift from population coding on low-contrast inputs to sparse coding at high contrast, improving robustness.

problem: Macro placement sequencing in VLSI design remains governed by static heuristics despite its decisive impact on optimization; placement order can trigger irreversible domino effects.
approach: OrderPlace automates discovery of macro placement strategies via LLM evolution guided by lightweight proxy evaluation, generating code-level ordering strategies from static to dynamic physics-inspired mechanisms.
contribution: Reduces wirelength by 34.04% versus WireMask-EA and 14.08% versus state-of-the-art EGPlace on ISPD 2005 benchmarks.

problem: Block-wise diffusion language models waste computation by discarding low-confidence tokens during decoding, limiting parallel generation efficiency.
approach: Residual Context Diffusion recycles discarded token representations into contextual residuals injected into the next denoising step, using decoupled two-stage training to bypass memory bottlenecks.
contribution: Improves frontier dLLMs by 4-11 percentage points accuracy; on AIME tasks nearly doubles accuracy and achieves 4-5x fewer denoising steps at baseline peak accuracy.

problem: Standard scaling laws fail to reliably predict LLM performance across different data quality mixtures and under repetition, making optimal data recipe selection uncertain.
approach: InfoLaw models pretraining as information accumulation where quality controls information density and repetition induces diminishing returns, predicting loss from tokens, model size, mixture weights, and repetition.
contribution: Predicts performance on unseen recipes and larger runs (up to 7B, 425B tokens) with 0.15% mean and 0.96% max error; enables efficient data-recipe selection under varying budgets.

problem: The mechanism by which transformers perform in-context learning on linear classification remains unclear; existing explanations lack rigor.
approach: Constructs multi-layer transformers where each layer exactly performs one step of normalized gradient descent on in-context loss, with convergence guarantees for training.
contribution: Reveals that softmax transformers can effectively implement in-context logistic regression through gradient descent; provides training convergence guarantees and out-of-distribution generalization results.

problem: Learning distribution families from noisy samples requires understanding structural properties that guarantee learnability, but connections between sample compressibility and noise robustness are unclear.
approach: Establishes that sample-compressible families remain learnable from samples corrupted by additive independent noise, deriving minimax-necessary and sufficient conditions.
contribution: Provides sample complexity bounds for learnable, sample-compressible classes in arbitrary dimensions under both ell-2 norm and total variation distance.

problem: Synthesizing inductive loop invariants remains a bottleneck in automated program verification; LLMs often produce invalid or ineffective invariants without high-quality training data.
approach: WONDA curates training data by extracting invariants from verifier output via AST normalization, LLM semantic rewriting, and augmentation with quality guarantees; fine-tunes SLMs on curated data.
contribution: 4B and 8B Qwen3 models nearly double invariant correctness; 8B model outperforms GPT-OSS-120B on InvBench and matches GPT-5.2 verification speed.

problem: Observing Hebbian structure in synaptic updates raises identifiability questions: does it necessarily imply underlying Hebbian computation or can it emerge from other mechanisms?
approach: Shows that near stationarity, L2 weight decay generically drives learning signals to align with Hebbian directions, and stochastic noise can induce anti-Hebbian alignment.
contribution: Reveals that Hebbian signatures can emerge without mechanistic Hebbian plasticity; demonstrates phase boundary between anti-Hebbian and Hebbian regimes depending on noise and decay.

problem: Training deep spiking neural networks relies on batch normalization for stability, but BN is unsuitable for variable-length tasks and small batch sizes, preventing large-scale SNN development.
approach: SpikeInit initializes weights and surrogate gradient shape parameters by modeling response curves and gradients to maintain stable firing rates and gradient magnitudes without normalization.
contribution: Deep SNNs train stably without normalization and outperform normalized counterparts; successfully trains 1000-layer SNN without normalization.

problem: Autoregressive image modeling relies on visual tokenizers typically trained separately from generative models, limiting opportunities for generation-informed optimization.
approach: End-to-end training pipeline jointly optimizes reconstruction and generation with direct supervision from generation results to the tokenizer, leveraging vision foundation models.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art FID score of 1.48 without guidance on ImageNet 256×256 generation.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation systems face vulnerability to adversarial attacks amplified by temporal volatility in dynamic web search, with existing defenses incurring prohibitive storage costs.
approach: RADAR models reliable context selection as graph-based energy minimization solved via Max-Flow Min-Cut; Bayesian memory node recursively updates belief state instead of archiving raw documents.
contribution: Superior robustness against attacks and better response quality with minimal storage overhead compared to baselines on dynamic datasets.

problem: Ensuring predictive distributions accurately reflect empirical uncertainty is challenging; minimizing prediction error often produces narrow but overconfident predictions misaligned with true risk.
approach: Nonparametric re-calibration algorithm based on conditional kernel mean embeddings corrects calibration error without restrictive modeling assumptions using O(n log n) characteristic kernel.
contribution: Outperforms prior re-calibration approaches across diverse regression benchmarks and model classes without parametric assumptions.

problem: Existing visual generalization benchmarks for RL entangle multiple sources of shift, hindering systematic analysis of pixel-based agent robustness.
approach: KAGE-Env factorizes the observation process into independently controllable visual axes while keeping control fixed; KAGE-Bench defines six suites with 34 configuration pairs isolating individual shifts.
contribution: Reveals axis-dependent failures with backgrounds and photometric shifts collapsing success; enables 33M environment steps per second on GPU for fast reproducible sweeps.

problem: Serving large language models at scale incurs prohibitive operational costs due to extreme heterogeneity in production traffic and suboptimal resource allocation.
approach: HexGen-3 combines fully disaggregated inference architecture with heterogeneous resource autoscaling; hierarchical scheduling jointly optimizes allocation and parallelism configuration.
contribution: Up to 60% improvement in per-cost throughput under static provisioning; up to 78.3% with autoscaling under dynamic workloads versus state-of-the-art systems.

problem: Safety mechanisms in sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs remain underexplored despite their widespread deployment; routers may enable safety circumvention.
approach: Introduces Router Safety Importance score to quantify router criticality; proposes F-SOUR framework for fine-grained token-layer-wise discovery of unsafe routes exploiting router manipulation.
contribution: Achieves average ASR of 0.90 on JailbreakBench and 0.98 on AdvBench; outlines safety-aware route disabling and router training as defensive directions.

problem: Explanations are typically evaluated via proxy properties weakly tied to their actual purpose, making it unclear whether explanations enable better decision-making.
approach: Decision-theoretic framework treats explanations as information signals valued by expected improvement on specified decision tasks; derives three estimands: theoretical benchmark, human-complementary value, and behavioral value.
contribution: Provides practical validation workflow; instantiated in human-AI decision support and mechanistic interpretability scenarios.

problem: Quantization-aware training scaling behavior, especially at 4-bit precision, is not well understood; existing scaling laws ignore key factors like training tokens and quantization granularity.
approach: Unified QAT scaling law models quantization error as function of model size, training data volume, and granularity; decomposes W4A4 error into weight and activation components.
contribution: Through 268 experiments shows quantization error decreases with model size but increases with tokens and coarser granularity; identifies activation outliers in FC2 as bottleneck.

problem: Deep neural networks underperform tree-based models on tabular data due to poor inductive biases for handling heterogeneous features and local irregularities.
approach: LassoFlexNet incorporates five biases via per-feature embeddings with tied group lasso selection; develops Sequential Hierarchical Proximal Adaptive Gradient optimizer with EMA for training stability.
contribution: Matches or outperforms leading tree models across 52 tabular datasets with up to 10% relative gain while maintaining Lasso-like interpretability.

problem: Nowcasting weather hazards struggles with rapid intensification regimes; existing systems extrapolate 2D radar reflectivity without capturing 3D convective system evolution.
approach: StormInsight integrates multi-source observations (radar, satellite, station) with reanalysis fields; explicitly disentangles convective system state from vertical thermodynamic coupling and environmental forcing.
contribution: Reduces MAE by 12.4% and improves mCSI by 34.0% on StormBench; enables coherent 3D reconstruction of convective systems.

problem: Large language models can be steered via activation interventions but sometimes resist steering by recovering and producing better responses mid-generation, making safety interventions potentially unreliable.
approach: Using sparse autoencoders to identify and ablate specific latents that act as off-topic detectors, combined with prompting and fine-tuning strategies to enhance or suppress endogenous steering resistance.
contribution: Identified 26 off-topic detector latents and demonstrated that zero-ablating them reduces multi-attempt rate by 25%, and that ESR can be deliberately controlled through prompting (5× increase) and fine-tuning.

problem: Automatic heuristic design for combinatorial optimization remains static and fails to effectively accumulate and reuse historical search experience across problem instances.
approach: RefineEvo introduces a planner to dynamically schedule evolutionary operators and a reflector to distill insights into a bidirectional experience pool capturing both positive and negative lessons.
contribution: RefineEvo outperforms strong baselines on classic combinatorial optimization benchmarks with superior solution quality while improving token efficiency.

problem: Hoeffding Trees for online learning rely on concentration inequalities but lack valid statistical guarantees because split decisions use data-dependent stopping rules that violate fixed-sample assumptions.
approach: Replacing concentration-based split decisions with anytime-valid inference that provides formal guarantees under arbitrary data streams and automatically commits to splits when sufficient evidence accumulates.
contribution: Provides anytime-valid control of false splits under non-stationary settings and improves performance while producing substantially smaller trees than existing Hoeffding Trees.

problem: Vector quantization models suffer from dimensional collapse where codebook representations degenerate into low-dimensional subspaces with significantly lower effective rank than continuous representations.
approach: Proposing a codebook regularization strategy that explicitly restores low-variance components suppressed during vector quantization to bridge the spectral gap between discrete and continuous representations.
contribution: Regularization improves reconstruction fidelity and downstream performance in autoregressive image generative models across diverse VQ training paradigms.

problem: Graph structure learning methods require complete re-learning when new nodes arrive and incur prohibitive computational and memory costs for large-scale dynamically evolving graphs.
approach: GraphFLEx restricts edge formation to structurally relevant node subsets identified through clustering and coarsening, enabling incremental graph updates and supporting 48 configurations of learning paradigms.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 26 diverse datasets with significantly improved scalability, demonstrated across different GNN architectures.

problem: LLMs make errors on deterministic arithmetic and token-repetition tasks when small attention errors accumulate across iterations, but existing explanations invoke catastrophic failure rather than gradual degradation.
approach: Deriving a two-parameter quantitative model inspired by effective field theory that relates task accuracy to attention noise and number of plausible erroneous tokens.
contribution: The model provides excellent agreement between predicted and observed accuracy across Gemini, DeepSeek, and other models on repetitive tasks, with alternative explanations to reasoning collapse.

problem: Reinforcement learning degrades when training and deployment environments differ, but existing distributionally robust RL methods require strong data assumptions and focus on tabular settings.
approach: Pure online DR-RL using dual-based fitted robust Bellman updates to jointly learn value functions and robust backup operators without prior knowledge or pre-collected data.
contribution: First regret guarantee for online DR-RL with general function approximation, achieving sublinear regret independent of state and action space size.

problem: Learning-to-rank via probabilistic permutation modeling is intractable due to factorial growth of permutation space, yet full-order structure is important for capturing ranking relationships.
approach: Introducing Full-Order Bound (FOB), a tractable lower bound on observed ordering probability that factorizes across items while preserving order structure, solved via safe-region gradient ascent.
contribution: FOB improves full-list ordering metrics and remains competitive on NDCG on large-scale learning-to-rank benchmarks.

problem: Inverse problem solvers typically assume high-fidelity diffusion priors trained on matched data, but practitioners often must use mismatched or low-fidelity priors, raising questions about when this remains effective.
approach: Combining Bayesian-consistency theory with local-correlation analysis to show when high-dimensional measurements concentrate the posterior near the true signal despite weak priors.
contribution: Provides principled justification that weak priors succeed with highly informative measurements and identifies regimes where they fail.

problem: On-device personal AI agents require storing personal context under tight memory budgets, but existing RAG approaches store raw data without considering what aligns with user preferences.
approach: EPIC (Efficient Preference-aligned Index Construction) focuses on user preferences as compact personal context, integrating them throughout the RAG pipeline to retain only preference-relevant information.
contribution: Reduces indexing memory by 2,404× while improving preference-following accuracy by 18.79 percentage points, maintaining under 1 MB memory with 5.21-29.35 ms/query latency.

problem: Selecting which pretrained LLM to fine-tune for a specific task is time-consuming due to varying sizes, architectures, and pretraining, and practical constraints like cost and throughput must be considered.
approach: LAMPS uses landmark fine-tuning to generate early performance indicators and meta-learns a selection policy via RL to identify the Pareto front of candidate models.
contribution: Reduces search time by average of 73% compared to exhaustive search while covering more than 99% of optimal target space hypervolume.

problem: State value estimation in LLM RLHF is critical for stable training but remains underexplored; critics in PPO-style approaches collapse to coarse group-average baselines.
approach: Proposing Numca to leverage numerical spans as gradable milestones and Hista to use hidden states weighted by rollout returns for improved state value estimation.
contribution: Both methods yield more accurate state value estimates and enhance training performance across different RL algorithms and model sizes without significant computational overhead.

problem: Optimal transport remains computationally expensive for large-scale applications; Sinkhorn algorithm has slow convergence and GPU efficiency is hindered by sparse matrix operations.
approach: cuRegOT introduces algorithmic and architectural GPU optimizations including amortized symbolic analysis, asynchronous Sinkhorn generation, and fused kernels for bandwidth-efficient gradient evaluation.
contribution: Achieves significant speedups over state-of-the-art GPU solvers for entropic-regularized optimal transport across benchmark tasks.

problem: Lagrangian-based safe RL for multi-constraint MDPs lacks theoretical justification for choosing between mixed-critic and dedicated-critic architectures, and mixed critics suffer from bias due to Lagrange multiplier drift.
approach: Performing first theoretical analysis proving that dedicated critic structures (separate critics for reward and constraints) avoid bias from target drift while mixed critics do not.
contribution: Theoretical analysis shows dedicated critics satisfy constraints while mixed critics fail on realistic multi-constraint environments.

problem: Planning-based robotic manipulation methods rely on expensive modular pipelines with multiple submodels, limiting real-time performance on embedded hardware.
approach: RoboFlow4D unifies perception and planning as a lightweight flow world model predicting multi-frame 3D flows from visual observations and text instructions, integrated with action policies.
contribution: Improves manipulation success rates and computational efficiency in both simulation and real-world settings with real-time performance.

problem: Multimodal transformers learn in-context learning across modalities, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear—specifically how information associates across modalities from limited examples.
approach: Controlled synthetic experiments on small transformers reveal learning asymmetry where secondary modality needs low complexity when pretrained on high-diversity primary data, using induction-style mechanisms.
contribution: Provides mechanistic foundation showing multimodal ICL relies on induction circuits refined and extended across modalities, with fundamental asymmetries between modalities.

problem: Anomaly detection in industrial settings requires robustness to data contamination, but existing methods degrade significantly as noise ratio increases without noise-specific tuning.
approach: Memory-Distilled Selection (MeDS) constructs an ensemble of partial memories via random subsampling where sparsity filters nominal patterns, then distills into a reconstruction score network.
contribution: Achieves 99.16% image-level AUROC on MVTecAD at 40% noise ratio and state-of-the-art on VisA and Real-IAD under noisy conditions without hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Conformal prediction treats modeling as a black box and cannot exploit modular structure in two-stage pipelines, limiting ability to attribute uncertainty to specific stages.
approach: Decomposing prediction residuals into stage-specific components with risk-controlled parameter selection via family-wise error rate control, plus adaptive extension for non-stationary settings.
contribution: Improves coverage under structural, stage-wise shifts and identifies stage-wise error contribution compared to standard conformal methods.

problem: Integrating transcriptomic and epigenetic data for clinical applications remains challenging due to high dimensionality and lack of joint representation learning approaches.
approach: Bimodal masked language model jointly learning representations of bulk RNA-seq and DNA methylation via self-supervision, with architecture reducing memory footprint for long sequences.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art cancer-type classification and survival prediction, and maintains downstream performance despite missing modalities.

problem: Numerical integration using finite point sets requires solving a non-convex maximum mean discrepancy optimization, but computing global minima is intractable.
approach: Computing stationary points of MMD (instead of global minima) and proving they yield faster numerical integration error convergence than MMD value itself for RKHS integrands.
contribution: Proves super-convergence property of stationary MMD points and shows MMD gradient flows can compute them with non-asymptotic finite-particle error bounds.

problem: Adaptive gradient methods like AdaGrad lack convergence guarantees under heavy-tailed noise that frequently occurs in modern machine learning optimization.
approach: Providing first provable convergence rate for AdaGrad in non-convex optimization when tail index satisfies 4/3 < p ≤ 2, without prior knowledge of p.
contribution: Achieves adaptive-to-tail-index convergence, and develops algorithm-dependent lower bound suggesting minimax optimality is not attainable by AdaGrad.

problem: LLMs excel at reasoning but validation of their proofs remains challenging; interactive theorem provers require detailed steps while auto-active verifiers lack LLM evaluation.
approach: Translating miniF2F benchmark to Dafny auto-active verifier and evaluating LLMs for proof guidance with 62.7% cumulative pass@4 on Claude Opus 4.6.
contribution: Demonstrates auto-active verification provides complementary setting for AI-assisted mathematical reasoning where LLMs guide and SMT automation handles low-level details.

problem: Video anomaly detection systems prioritize accuracy while overlooking privacy concerns, limiting suitability for human-centered real-world deployment.
approach: Orthogonal Projection Layer removes task-irrelevant variations, and Guided OPL suppresses facial attributes via weak supervision from face-presence signals.
contribution: Embedding privacy constraints into model design reduces sensitive information while maintaining or improving detection accuracy.

problem: Extending Object-Centric Learning to continual learning is underexplored; objects suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning sequentially.
approach: Observing that Slot Attention exhibits factor-wise homogeneity—organizing latents into separated regions preserving factor states across tasks—and leveraging this with minimal decoder-only post-replay.
contribution: Factor-wise homogeneity serves as key mechanism preventing forgetting in continual object-centric learning, achievable with minimal intervention.

problem: Diffusion-based LLMs face deployment challenges but post-training quantization suffers from severe accuracy degradation due to distinct distributions across decoding steps and error accumulation.
approach: DLLMQuant addresses DLLM-specific mechanisms via Temporal-Mask Adaptive Sampling for calibration, interaction-aware techniques, and accumulated error mitigation.
contribution: Tailored quantization framework for diffusion LLMs addressing unique challenges unaddressed by standard PTQ methods.

problem: Transformers learn to represent the world but whether they use factored representations (orthogonal subspaces) or product-space representations (exponentially growing dimension) remains unclear.
approach: Testing representational hypotheses on transformers trained on synthetic processes with known latent structure and deriving predictions about geometric activation structure.
contribution: Conditionally independent factors lead to factored representations with linear dimensionality growth, while dependencies cause models to gradually expand dimensionality for fidelity.

problem: Critic-free RLHF for LLMs requires expensive full-trajectory updates even when intermediate prefixes often contain enough information to determine final outcomes.
approach: PS-PPO samples trajectory prefixes via prompt-conditioned cutoff distribution and applies importance-weighting corrections to backpropagate only through sampled prefixes.
contribution: Achieves large reductions in training compute and peak GPU memory while maintaining accuracy comparable to full-trajectory critic-free baselines.

problem: Neural architecture search and hyperparameter optimization lack unified frameworks for synthesizing and traversing parametric function spaces.
approach: Formalizing algebraic theory for parametric functions in finite combinatory logic with predicates and automating composition from components.
contribution: General framework for search space synthesis enabling language-agnostic component specification instantiable as any implementation like PyTorch modules.

problem: Electrostatic generative models like PFGM++ achieve competitive performance but require expensive ODE simulations for sampling, limiting computational efficiency.
approach: Proposing Inverse Poisson Flow Matching (IPFM) for distillation, reformulating it as inverse problem of matching induced electrostatic fields of teacher.
contribution: Distilled generators achieve near-teacher or superior sample quality using only few function evaluations, with faster convergence at finite auxiliary dimensionality.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models generalize to generic instructions but struggle with personalized commands requiring identification of specific instances among visually similar objects.
approach: Visual Attentive Prompting treats reference images as non-parametric visual memory, grounds personal objects via open-vocabulary detection and embedding matching, injects grounding as visual prompt.
contribution: Consistently outperforms generic policies and token-learning baselines in personalized manipulation across simulation and real-world settings.

problem: Web services for LLM agents remain static endpoints that poorly express long-horizon workflows requiring loops, conditionals, joins, and retries.
approach: ToolPro represents agent tool intent as executable programs compactly encoding multi-step interactions with effect types, using constraint-guided construction and profile-driven execution policy.
contribution: Reduces end-to-end latency by up to 53.4% and client-side traffic by up to 96.1%, with larger gains under higher network latency.

problem: Long-context inference is constrained by KV-cache memory growth; geometry-based KV eviction using cosine similarity is scale-invariant and may discard magnitude cues.
approach: ManifoldKV ranks tokens by Euclidean distance to key centroid capturing both angular and radial deviations; WindowedManifoldKV addresses centroid dilution at 64K context.
contribution: Achieves 95.7% accuracy at 4K-16K with 20% compression and 92.4% on multi-key retrieval, decisively outperforming cosine-based approaches.

problem: Bayesian Mallows model for preference learning scales poorly due to expensive inference, preventing use in real-time applications.
approach: Proposing Pseudo-Mallows distribution as product of univariate Mallows-like distributions, optimizing variational order by minimizing marginalized KL-divergence.
contribution: Enables much faster probabilistic preference learning compared to MCMC-based alternatives while maintaining approximation quality.

problem: Task-specific parameter updates from fine-tuning expensive to relearn for every model variant; transferring updates across different-width models remains unexplored.
approach: Theseus characterizes task updates by functional effects on intermediate representations and uses orthogonal Procrustes analysis for representation-space alignment.
contribution: Training-free method enabling meaningful task-vector transfer across heterogeneous-width models with consistent improvements on vision and language tasks.

problem: Small tabular foundation models struggle on high-dimensional, low-sample-size data; feature ordering and representation efficiency remain bottlenecks.
approach: GOTabPFN applies Graph-guided Ordering with Local Refinement and Neuro-Inspired Subunit Compression to pool ordered features into compact meta-features.
contribution: Improves stability and accuracy under tight token budgets for HDLSS tabular prediction.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks fail on oscillatory, multiscale, stiff, or long-time solutions; high-dimensional collocation-based training yields large numerical errors and high-variance gradients.
approach: Low-Rank Fourier Sums (LoRFS) represent solutions as low-rank separable Fourier expansions enabling closed-form evaluation of physics objectives and their gradients.
contribution: Eliminates sampling noise and consistently outperforms PINN baselines across failure modes while remaining stable in high-dimensional regimes.

problem: Machine unlearning aims to remove influence of forget data but existing weighted-loss methods don't guarantee specific improvement extents across all samples.
approach: Hardness-Aware Multi-Objective Unlearning (HAMU) quantifies reconciliation difficulty via similarity between forget and retain data, uses constrained optimization with FWER control.
contribution: Guarantees specified improvement in forget quality while minimizing retain utility degradation, informing users when both objectives cannot be simultaneously improved.

problem: Robustifying next-token prediction models in adversarial online decision-making requires distributional robustness, but feasibility under context bounds remains unclear.
approach: Proving that unbounded-context models can achieve sublinear regret while changing distribution by negligible amount, but bounded-context models face impossibility results.
contribution: Shows modest context-window increase restores robustification, and small transformers can be trained to represent robustified distributions.

problem: Applying uniform learning rates across Transformer layers overlooks structural heterogeneity and may limit effectiveness as LLM backbone.
approach: Layerwise Learning Rate (LLR) assigns distinct rates to layers based on Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization theory, using empirical spectral density to quantify heavy-tailedness.
contribution: Achieves up to 1.5× training speedup, raising zero-shot accuracy from 47.09% to 49.02% for 1B models with low tuning overhead.

problem: Zero-shot classifier expansion uses shared semantic-to-weight mappings but struggles with mixtures of distinct and similar classes due to granularity mismatch and noise sensitivity.
approach: Granularity-aware adaptive framework generates multi-source semantics via interventions, discovers latent class structure, and refines similar classes with invariance to noise.
contribution: Balances distinct and similar classes through theoretical and empirical interventions for improved zero-shot classification.

problem: Computing low-rank optimal transport plans is NP-hard and computationally expensive, despite offering better statistical properties than unconstrained optimal transport.
approach: Transport Clustering reduces the low-rank optimal transport problem to a clustering problem performed on correspondences from a full-rank transport solution, yielding polynomial-time approximation algorithms with proven constant-factor guarantees.
contribution: Polynomial-time approximation algorithms achieving (1+γ) approximation for negative-type metrics, (1+γ+√(2γ)) for kernel costs, and (1+γ+ρ) for general metrics.

problem: Standard distributional reinforcement learning does not handle multi-objective settings where multiple rewards must be balanced and risk-sensitivity matters, especially in finance and robotics.
approach: Extend distributional RL to multi-objective settings using vector-risk measures approximated via Knothe-Rosenblatt quantile regression, with a transformer architecture without positional encoding to mitigate artificial ordering.
contribution: Risk-sensitive multi-objective RL framework with convergence guarantees under the distributional Bellman operator and improved performance on MO-Gymnasium benchmarks.

problem: Existing tabular anomaly detection methods require dataset-specific training for each new dataset, incurring high computational cost and poor generalization to unseen domains.
approach: OFA-TAD extracts neighbor-distance patterns as transferable cues across multiple metric spaces via multi-view representations and uses a Mixture-of-Experts scoring network to adaptively fuse anomaly evidence.
contribution: One-for-all generalist framework achieving superior anomaly detection and cross-domain generalizability on 34 datasets from 14 domains after one-time training.

problem: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks face efficiency bottlenecks from explicit construction of geometric features and dense tensor products on every edge, limiting scalability.
approach: E2Former-V2 integrates algebraic sparsity using Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) that converts dense Wigner-6j contractions into sparse operations, implemented via fused Triton kernels for hardware-aware execution.
contribution: Up to 20× higher TFLOPS than standard implementations while preserving predictive accuracy on molecular benchmarks.

problem: Vision-language and robotic action spaces have incompatible metric structures—vision-language is topologically linear and isotropic while action manifolds are non-Euclidean and anisotropic—making direct regression fail.
approach: LAST bridges the heterogeneity via Lie-algebraic mapping that linearizes the action manifold globally and discretizes it locally into schemas and whitened residuals, establishing mathematical isomorphism with isotropic Euclidean space.
contribution: Enhanced convergence and generalizability for Vision-Language-Action models by resolving structural mismatch through Lie-algebraic reconstruction.

problem: Knowledge distillation of Multimodal LLMs relies on static next-token alignment, missing dynamic token interactions that encode essential capabilities for multimodal understanding.
approach: Align-TI introduces two components: IVA aligns on salient visual regions to capture instruction-relevant visual extraction, and TPA aligns sequential token-to-token transition probabilities to capture generative logic.
contribution: 2.6% relative improvement over vanilla KD; distilled Align-TI-2B outperforms LLaVA-1.5-7B by 7.0%, establishing state-of-the-art parameter-efficient MLLM distillation.

problem: Population-Based Training variants have an important hyperparameter controlling steps between updates, but no principled method exists for setting it efficiently.
approach: IPBT automatically adjusts this hyperparameter via restarts that reuse weights and leverage time-varying Bayesian optimization to reinitialize hyperparameters in a task-agnostic way.
contribution: Matches or outperforms 5 prior PBT variants and other HPO algorithms on average across 8 tasks without requiring budget increases or hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Data scheduling for LLM training ignores directional influences and dependencies between samples, yet real-world data exhibits complex interactions that affect training order importance.
approach: D³ formulates sample interactions as a dynamic influence graph with loss-based dependencies and solves constrained optimization over this graph to derive training order respecting information flow.
contribution: Consistent improvements over existing data scheduling methods on pre-training and post-training phases with scalable approximation algorithms.

problem: Neural operators for PDEs struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution test inputs such as novel initial conditions or unseen physics without adapting weights.
approach: Searches over compositions of training operators at test time to approximate unseen dynamics, building on DISCO which provides a dictionary of operators trained across different physics.
contribution: State-of-the-art zero-shot generalization on parameter extrapolation and novel physics combinations while recovering underlying PDE parameters.

problem: Constrained generation in language models faces a tradeoff: greedy decoding enforces validity but distorts distributions, while rejection sampling preserves fidelity but wastes computation.
approach: CARS adaptively prunes invalid continuations by recording them in a trie and subtracting probability mass from future draws, ensuring prefixes proven invalid are never revisited.
contribution: Higher sample efficiency measured in forward passes per valid sample with stronger diversity than greedy constrained decoding and rejection sampling methods.

problem: KL divergence in language model distillation is dominated by the teacher's highest-probability modes, diminishing the influence of lower-probability yet informative components.
approach: Propose a tail-aware divergence that decouples the contribution of top-K predictions from lower-probability predictions while maintaining computational efficiency.
contribution: Competitive performance on mathematical reasoning across datasets with efficient distillation achievable on academic budgets.

problem: Barriers to clinical AI research include difficulty replicating baselines, high computational costs, and required domain expertise, limiting reproducibility and accessibility.
approach: PyHealth 2.0 unifies 15+ datasets, 20+ tasks, 25+ models, and interpretability methods in a single framework supporting multimodal clinical data and diverse computational resources.
contribution: Up to 39× faster processing and 20× lower memory usage enabling work from 16GB laptops; 400+ community members supporting accessible, reproducible healthcare AI.

problem: In modern ML pipelines with abundant pretrained representations and scarce task-specific labels, determining how to effectively use noisy proxy covariates for semi-supervised regression is unclear.
approach: Two-stage estimator learns kernel eigenfeatures from all proxy covariates and fits ridge predictor on labeled data with finite sample bounds accounting for proxy perturbation.
contribution: Fast labeled sample rates recovered when proxy perturbation is controlled; distribution regression as a direct special case with analogous guarantees.

problem: Global embedding geometry metrics exhibit near-zero correlation with compositional binding in vision representations, missing how elements are composed despite capturing which elements are present.
approach: Use input-output Jacobian functional sensitivity rather than geometry-based statistics to track compositional binding capability across 21 vision encoders.
contribution: Functional sensitivity reliably tracks compositional binding while geometry metrics fail; establishes functional sensitivity as critical complementary axis for modeling composite structure.

problem: LLM agents improving at test time through memory updates typically rely on hand-designed prompting rules, making it difficult to align memory updates with multi-step objectives.
approach: MemoPilot trains the memory update process end-to-end using multi-turn GRPO with turn-wise reward signals and context-independent advantage estimation for fine-grained credit assignment.
contribution: Substantially improved test-time learning ranking first in Elo on both Rock-Paper-Scissors (1590) and Limit Texas Hold'em (1762), outperforming Deepseek-V3.2.

problem: Multi-agent RL in large-scale systems with local interactions suffers from credit assignment challenges; global value functions provide weak learning signals while local constructions are difficult to estimate.
approach: Diffusion Value Function (DVF) assigns value to each agent by diffusing rewards over the influence graph with temporal discounting and spatial attenuation, decomposing global value via averaging.
contribution: Up to 11% improvement in average reward across firefighting and distributed computation tasks compared to local and global critic baselines.

problem: Standard fixed activation functions like ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh are less expressive than trainable low-degree rational activations for approximating target functions.
approach: Use trainable low-degree rational activation functions that provide exponential improvements in parameter efficiency for approximating functions to target error ε.
contribution: Rational-activation networks require only poly(log log(1/ε)) overhead versus poly(log(1/ε)) for fixed activations; seamlessly integrate into standard architectures.
